sentences.en: A Since the 1980s, the term ‘blockbuster’ has become the fashionable word for spectacular, high-profile museum exhibitions that have the ability to attract large crowds.
sentences.zh: 自 1980 年代以来，“blockbuster”（重磅大展）这一术语已成为对那些气势宏大、声誉显赫、有能力吸引大量人流的博物馆展览的时髦称呼。

sentences.en: A blockbuster is a ‘large-scale loan exhibition that people who normally don’t go to museums will stand in line for hours to see’ (Eisen 1984).
sentences.zh: 一场重磅大展指的是“一场大规模的借展，让那些通常不去博物馆的人都愿意排上几个小时的队来看”（Eisen 1984）。

sentences.en: Once the museum that created the exhibition has shown it to its local market, it can be offered to other organizations for a fee.
sentences.zh: 一旦策划该展的博物馆已经向本地市场展出过，它就可以收费提供给其他机构。

sentences.en: This means that you can boost your own door takings and make money from boosting someone else’s door takings.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你既可以提升自家的门票收入，又可以借由提升别人的门票收入而赚钱。

sentences.en: B While partaking of the excitement of the blockbuster, visitors thus lured are likely to stay longer at the museum.
sentences.zh: 在分享重磅大展的兴奋同时，被吸引而来的观众往往会在博物馆停留更长时间。

sentences.en: Betty Churcher, when Director of the Australian National Gallery, summed up the new blockbuster creed as follows: ‘The bonus of the blockbuster exhibitions is that people come to see the blockbuster and they stay to look at the permanent collection, so you are getting broader exposure for your collection.’
sentences.zh: 贝蒂·丘彻（Betty Churcher）担任澳大利亚国家美术馆馆长时，曾这样总结新兴的重磅大展信条：“重磅大展的附加好处在于，人们来看大展，却会留下来观看常设藏品，这样你的藏品就能获得更广泛的曝光。”

sentences.en: C Museums across the UK, USA, Canada and Australia currently operate under a system of plural funding: revenue raised through contributions by federal, state and/or local governments, combined with revenue raised through admission charges and other activities.
sentences.zh: 英国、美国、加拿大和澳大利亚的博物馆当前都在多元资助的体系下运作：收入既来自联邦、州和/或地方政府的拨款，又来自门票及其他活动的收入。

sentences.en: Maintaining and increasing visitor levels is thus paramount and involves not only creating or hiring blockbuster exhibitions, but providing regular exhibition changes and innovations.
sentences.zh: 因此，维持并提升参观人数变得至关重要，这不仅意味着策划或借入重磅大展，还包括定期更换展览和推陈出新。

sentences.en: In addition, the visiting public have become known as customers rather than visitors, and the skills that are valued in museums to keep the new customers coming through the door have changed.
sentences.zh: 此外，参观公众如今被视为顾客而非访客，博物馆所看重的、用以持续吸引新顾客的技能也发生了变化。

sentences.en: Curators are now administrators, and being a museum director no longer requires an Arts degree—but public relations skills are essential if the museum is going to compete with other museums to stage travelling exhibitions which draw huge crowds.
sentences.zh: 策展人如今成了行政管理者，担任博物馆馆长不再必须拥有艺术学位——但若要在与其他博物馆争夺巡回大展、以吸引大批人流的竞争中胜出，公关技能则至关重要。

sentences.en: D The convergence of museums, the heritage industry, tourism, profit-making and pleasure-giving has resulted in the new ‘museology’.
sentences.zh: 博物馆、文化遗产产业、旅游业、营利和娱乐功能的融合，催生了新的“博物馆学”。

sentences.en: This has given rise to much debate about whether it is appropriate to see museums primarily as tourist attractions.
sentences.zh: 这引发了大量讨论：把博物馆主要视为旅游景点是否合适？

sentences.en: In literature from both the UK and USA, the words that are starting to appear in some descriptions of blockbusters are ‘less scholarly’, ‘non-elitist’ and ‘popularist’, while others extol the virtues of encouraging scholars to co-operate on projects, and to provide exhibitions that cater for a broad selection of the community rather than an elite sector.
sentences.zh: 在来自英国和美国的相关文献中，已经开始出现一些用来描述重磅大展的词语，如“学术性较弱”“非精英化”和“民粹化”；与此同时也有人在赞扬鼓励学者合作开展项目、推出面向社区广泛人群而非精英阶层的展览的价值。

sentences.en: Whatever commentators may think, managers of museums worldwide are looking for artful ways to blend culture and commerce, and blockbuster exhibitions are at the top of the list.
sentences.zh: 无论评论家怎么想，世界各地的博物馆管理者都在寻找把文化与商业巧妙融合的途径，而重磅大展正高居首选。

sentences.en: E But do blockbusters held in public institutions really create a surplus to fund other activities?
sentences.zh: 但在公立机构举办的重磅大展真的能产生盈余、用以资助其他活动吗？

sentences.en: If the bottom line is profit, then according to the records of many major museums blockbusters do make money.
sentences.zh: 如果衡量的底线是利润，那么根据许多大型博物馆的记录，重磅大展确实能赚钱。

sentences.en: For museums in some countries, it may be the money that they require to replace parts of their collections or to fix buildings that are in need of attention.
sentences.zh: 对一些国家的博物馆来说，这或许正是他们用以替换部分藏品或维修需要修缮的建筑物所需的资金。

sentences.en: For some museums in Australia, it may be the opportunity to illustrate that they are attempting to pay their way by recovering part of their operating costs.
sentences.zh: 对澳大利亚的一些博物馆来说，这或许是一个机会来证明：它们正通过收回部分运营成本来努力实现自我维持。

sentences.en: Also, creating or hiring a blockbuster has many positive spin-offs: blockbusters mean crowds, and crowds are good for the local economy, providing increased trade for shops, hotels, restaurants, the transport industry and retailers.
sentences.zh: 此外，策办或引进一场重磅大展会带来许多积极的连带效应：大展意味着人潮，而人潮对本地经济有好处——会给商店、酒店、餐馆、交通行业和零售商带来生意。

sentences.en: The argument that the arts provide sustained economic benefits has been well illustrated in impact studies in the USA and UK.
sentences.zh: 关于艺术能带来持续经济效益的论点，已在美国和英国的影响研究中得到很好的印证。

sentences.en: F However, blockbusters require large capital expenditure and draw on resources across all branches of an organization, and the costs don’t end there.
sentences.zh: 然而，重磅大展需要巨额的资金投入，并占用机构各部门的资源，而成本并不止于此。

sentences.en: There is a Human Resource Management cost in addition to a measurable ‘real’ dollar cost.
sentences.zh: 除了可量化的“真实”美元成本之外，还有一项人力资源管理成本。

sentences.en: Receiving a touring exhibition draws resources from across functional management structures in a project-management style.
sentences.zh: 接收一场巡回展会按项目管理的方式调动横跨各职能管理结构的资源。

sentences.en: Everyone—from general labourers to building services, front-of-house, technical, promotional, educational and administrative staff—is required to perform additional tasks.
sentences.zh: 每个人——从普通劳工到楼宇维护、前台、技术、宣传、教育和行政人员——都需要承担额外的工作。

sentences.en: Furthermore, as an increasing number of institutions try their hand at increasing visitor numbers and memberships (and therefore revenue) by staging blockbuster exhibitions, it may be less likely that blockbusters will continue to provide a surplus to subsidize other activities due to the competitive nature of the market.
sentences.zh: 此外，随着越来越多的机构试图通过策办重磅大展来增加参观人数和会员数（从而增加收入），由于市场竞争激烈，重磅大展持续提供盈余以补贴其他活动的可能性或许会下降。

sentences.en: G It has been illustrated in both the UK and USA that the blockbuster ideology has resulted in the false expectation that the momentum required to stage blockbusters can be maintained continually.
sentences.zh: 已有研究在英国和美国证明，重磅大展的意识形态导致了一种错误期待——即认为持续策办重磅大展所需的能量是可以无限维持的。

sentences.en: Creating, mounting or hiring blockbusters is exhausting, with the real costs throughout an institution difficult to calculate.
sentences.zh: 策办、布置或引进重磅大展是非常耗费精力的，机构内部各处的真实成本难以核算。

sentences.en: Secondly, as some analysts have argued, the ‘shopkeeping’ mentality and cost-benefit analysis, and a pure concentration on the bottom line, can squeeze substance out of an exhibition.
sentences.zh: 其次，正如一些分析人士所指出的，那种“小铺老板”心态、成本效益分析以及一味盯着账面盈亏的做法，会让一场展览失去实质内容。

sentences.en: Taking out substance can be a recipe for blockbuster failure and therefore financial failure.
sentences.zh: 把实质内容抽走，可能正是重磅大展失败、进而导致财务失败的根源。

sentences.en: H Perhaps the best pathway to take is one that balances both blockbusters and regular exhibitions.
sentences.zh: 也许最好的路径是在重磅大展与常规展览之间寻求平衡。

sentences.en: However, this easy middle ground may only work if you have enough space, and have alternative sources of funding to continue to support the regular, less exciting fare.
sentences.zh: 然而，这种看似轻松的中庸之道，只有在你有足够空间，并且有其他资金来源持续支持那些常规、不那么轰动的展览时，才行得通。

sentences.en: Perhaps the advice should be to make sure that you find out what your local community wants from you and make sure that your regular activities and exhibitions are more enduring.
sentences.zh: 也许应该给出的建议是：务必弄清楚你所在的本地社区想从你这里得到什么，并确保你的常规活动与展览更具持久性。

records.title: The Development of The Silk Industry

sentences.en: (A) When silk was first discovered in China over 4,500 years ago, it was reserved exclusively for the use of the emperor, his close relations and the very highest of his dignitaries.
sentences.zh: 4500 多年前丝在中国最早被发现时，它专供皇帝、其近亲以及最高级别的权贵使用。

sentences.en: Within the palace, the emperor is believed to have worn a robe of white silk; outside, he, his principal wife, and the heir to the throne wore yellow, the colour of the earth.
sentences.zh: 在宫中，皇帝据信穿白色丝袍；宫外，他、正妻和皇位继承人则身穿黄色——即土地之色。

sentences.en: (B) Gradually silk came into more general use, and the various classes of Chinese society began wearing tunics of silk.
sentences.zh: 渐渐地，丝走向更广泛的使用，中国社会各阶层开始穿丝制衫袍。

sentences.en: As well as being used for clothing and decoration, silk was quite quickly put to industrial use, and rapidly became one of the principal elements of the Chinese economy.
sentences.zh: 丝绸除用于服装和装饰外，很快也被投入工业用途，迅速成为中国经济的主要元素之一。

sentences.en: It was used in the production of musical instruments, as string for fishing, and even as the world’s first luxury paper.
sentences.zh: 它被用于乐器制作、做钓鱼线，甚至成为世上第一种奢华纸。

sentences.en: Eventually even the common people were able to wear garments of silk.
sentences.zh: 最终连普通百姓也得以穿上丝制衣物。

sentences.en: (C) During the Han dynasty (206 BC-220 AD), silk ceased to be a mere fabric and became a form of currency.
sentences.zh: 汉朝（公元前 206 年至公元 220 年）期间，丝绸不再只是一种织物，而成为一种货币形态。

sentences.en: Farmers paid their taxes in grain and silk, and silk was used to pay civil servants and to reward subjects for outstanding services.
sentences.zh: 农民以谷物和丝绸交税，丝绸用以支付官吏俸禄，并用于奖赏功臣。

sentences.en: Values were calculated in lengths of silk as they had previously been calculated in weight of gold.
sentences.zh: 价值的计算单位从过去以黄金重量计算，转为以丝绸长度计算。

sentences.en: Before long, silk became a currency used in trade with foreign countries, which continued into the Tang dynasty (616-907 AD).
sentences.zh: 不久之后，丝绸成为与外国贸易所用的一种货币，这种用法一直延续到唐朝（公元 616 年至 907 年）。

sentences.en: It is possible that this added importance was the result of a major increase in production.
sentences.zh: 这种额外重要性可能是生产量大幅增加的结果。

sentences.en: Silk also found its way so thoroughly into the Chinese language that 230 of the 5,000 most common characters of Mandarin have ‘silk’ as their key component.
sentences.zh: 丝绸也深入到中文语言之中，最常见的 5000 个汉字之中，有 230 个以“丝”为偏旁。

sentences.en: (D) Silk became a precious commodity, highly sought after by other countries from an early date, and it is believed that the silk trade actually existed before the Silk Road was officially opened in the second century BC.
sentences.zh: 丝绸成为一种珍贵的商品，自很早的时代起就受到其他国家追捧；据信丝绸贸易其实早在公元前 2 世纪丝绸之路正式开通之前就已存在。

sentences.en: An Egyptian mummy with a silk thread in her hair, dating from 1070 BC, has been discovered in the village of Deir el Medina near the Valley of the Kings, and is probably the earliest evidence of the silk trade.
sentences.zh: 在帝王谷附近的代尔麦地那（Deir el Medina）村发现的一具公元前 1070 年的埃及木乃伊头发中带有一根丝线，这可能是有关丝绸贸易的最早证据。

sentences.en: During the second century BC, the Chinese emperor Han Wu Di’s ambassadors travelled as far west as Persia and Mesopotamia, bearing gifts including silks.
sentences.zh: 在公元前 2 世纪期间，中国汉武帝的使节远西可至波斯和美索不达米亚，所带礼物之中就包括丝绸。

sentences.en: A range of important finds of Chinese silks have also been made along the Silk Road.
sentences.zh: 沿丝绸之路也发现了一批重要的中国丝绸出土物。

sentences.en: One of the most dramatic of these finds was some Tang silk discovered in 1900.
sentences.zh: 其中最具戏剧性的发现之一，是 1900 年发现的一批唐代丝绸。

sentences.en: It is believed that around 1015 AD Buddhist monks, possibly alarmed by the threat of invasion by Tibetan people, had sealed more than ten thousand manuscripts and silk paintings, silk banners and textiles in caves near Dunhuang, a trading station on the Silk Road in north-west China.
sentences.zh: 据信约公元 1015 年，佛教僧侣或许是出于对吐蕃人入侵威胁的警觉，把一万余件手稿、丝绸绘画、丝绸幡旗和纺织品封存在敦煌附近的洞窟中——敦煌当时是中国西北丝绸之路上的一处贸易站。

sentences.en: (E) Some historians believe the first Europeans to set eyes upon the fabulous fabric were the Roman legions of Marcus Licinius Crassus, Governor of Syria.
sentences.zh: 一些历史学家认为，最早一睹这种神奇织物的欧洲人是叙利亚总督马库斯·李锡尼·克拉苏（Marcus Licinius Crassus）所率领的罗马军团。

sentences.en: According to certain accounts of the period, at an important battle near the Euphrates River in 53 BC, the Roman soldiers were so startled by the bright silken banners of the enemy that they fled in panic.
sentences.zh: 根据当时某些史料的记载，公元前 53 年在幼发拉底河附近一场重要战役中，罗马士兵被敌人鲜艳的丝绸旌旗吓得仓皇逃窜。

sentences.en: Yet, within decades Chinese silks were widely worn by the rich and noble families of Rome.
sentences.zh: 然而，几十年之内，中国丝绸已经被罗马的富裕和贵族家庭广泛穿着。

sentences.en: The Roman Emperor Heliogabalus (218-222 AD) wore nothing but silk.
sentences.zh: 罗马皇帝赫利奥伽巴卢斯（公元 218 年至 222 年）只穿丝绸。

sentences.en: By 380 AD, the Roman historian Ammianus Marcellinus reported that the use of silk, which was once confined to the nobility, had now spread to all classes without distinction—even to the lowest.
sentences.zh: 到公元 380 年，罗马历史学家阿米阿努斯·马尔切利努斯（Ammianus Marcellinus）记录说，丝绸的使用已经从过去仅限于贵族扩展到不分等级的各个阶层——甚至最底层也是如此。

sentences.en: The desire for silk continued to increase over the centuries.
sentences.zh: 对丝绸的渴望在此后几个世纪里持续上升。

sentences.en: Despite this demand, the price of silk remained very high.
sentences.zh: 尽管需求强劲，丝绸的价格仍然非常之高。

sentences.en: (F) In spite of their secrecy about production methods, the Chinese eventually lost their monopoly on silk production.
sentences.zh: 尽管中国对生产方法保密，但中国人最终还是失去了对丝绸生产的垄断。

sentences.en: Knowledge of silk production methods reached Korea around 200 BC, when waves of Chinese immigrants arrived there.
sentences.zh: 约公元前 200 年，丝绸生产方法的知识随着中国移民浪潮到达朝鲜。

sentences.en: Shortly after 300 AD, it travelled westward, and the cultivation of the silkworm was established in India.
sentences.zh: 公元 300 年后不久，知识又西传至印度，蚕的养殖在印度建立起来。

sentences.en: (G) Around 550 AD silk production reached the Middle East.
sentences.zh: 约公元 550 年，丝绸生产到达中东。

sentences.en: Records indicate that two monks from Constantinople (modern-day Istanbul), capital of the Byzantine Empire, appeared at their emperor’s court with silkworm eggs which they had obtained secretly, and hidden in their hollow bamboo walking sticks.
sentences.zh: 记载表明，来自拜占庭帝国都城君士坦丁堡（今伊斯坦布尔）的两名僧侣以暗中获得的蚕卵——藏在其空心竹杖中——出现在皇帝的宫廷。

sentences.en: Under their supervision the eggs hatched into worms, and the worms spun silk threads.
sentences.zh: 在他们的看护下，蚕卵孵化成幼蚕，幼蚕吐出丝线。

sentences.en: Byzantium was in the silk business at last.
sentences.zh: 拜占庭终于跻身丝绸生意。

sentences.en: The Byzantine church and state created imperial workshops, monopolising production and keeping the secret to themselves.
sentences.zh: 拜占庭的教会和国家设立了皇家作坊，把生产垄断在手，并把秘密牢牢保住。

sentences.en: This allowed a silk industry to be established, undercutting the market for ordinary-grade Chinese silk.
sentences.zh: 这使得他们得以建立一项丝绸产业，抢占了普通级别中国丝绸的市场。

sentences.en: However, high quality silk textiles, woven in China especially for the Middle Eastern market, continued to achieve high prices in the West, and trade along the Silk Road continued as before.
sentences.zh: 然而，专为中东市场在中国织造的高质量丝绸织物在西方仍可卖出高价，沿丝绸之路的贸易一如既往地进行。

sentences.en: By the sixth century the Persians, too, had mastered the art of silk weaving, developing their own rich patterns and techniques.
sentences.zh: 到 6 世纪，波斯人也掌握了丝绸织造的技艺，并发展出自己丰富的图案与工艺。

sentences.en: But it wasn’t until the 13th century that Italy began silk production, with the introduction of 2,000 skilled silk weavers from Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 但意大利直到 13 世纪才开始丝绸生产——当时从君士坦丁堡引入了 2000 名熟练的丝绸织工。

sentences.en: Eventually, silk production became widespread throughout Europe.
sentences.zh: 最终，丝绸生产在整个欧洲普及开来。

sentences.en: (H) World silk production has approximately doubled during the last 30 years in spite of manmade fibres replacing certain uses of silk.
sentences.zh: 在过去 30 年里，尽管人造纤维取代了丝绸的某些用途，但世界丝绸产量仍大致翻了一番。

sentences.en: Before this period, China and Japan were the two main producers, together manufacturing more than 50 per cent of world production each year.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，中国和日本是两个主要的生产国，二者合计每年生产超过世界产量的 50%。

sentences.en: After the late 1970s, however, China dramatically increased its silk production, and once again became the world’s leading producer.
sentences.zh: 然而 1970 年代后期之后，中国大幅提高了丝绸产量，再次成为世界最大生产国。

sentences.en: (A) The potato was first cultivated in South America between three and seven thousand years ago, though scientists believe they may have grown wild in the region as long as 13,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 马铃薯最早是在三千到七千年前在南美洲被栽培的，尽管科学家相信它们可能早在 13000 年前就在那一地区野生生长。

sentences.en: The genetic patterns of potato distribution indicate that the potato probably originated in the mountainous west-central region of the continent.
sentences.zh: 马铃薯分布的遗传模式表明，马铃薯可能起源于该大陆中西部山区。

sentences.en: (B) Early Spanish chroniclers who misused the Indian word batata (sweet potato) as the name for the potato noted the importance of the tuber to the Incan Empire.
sentences.zh: 早期的西班牙编年史家误用印第安语 batata（红薯）来称呼马铃薯，记录了这种块茎对印加帝国的重要性。

sentences.en: The Incas had learned to preserve the potato for storage by dehydrating and mashing potatoes into a substance called chuño, which could be stored in a room for up to 10 years, providing excellent insurance against possible crop failures.
sentences.zh: 印加人学会通过脱水捣碎马铃薯做成名为 chuño 的物质来储存马铃薯，这种食物可以在房间中存放长达 10 年，为可能的歉收提供了极好的保险。

sentences.en: As well as using the food as a staple crop, the Incas thought potatoes made childbirth easier and used them to treat injuries.
sentences.zh: 除了把这种食物当作主食外，印加人还认为马铃薯能让分娩更顺利，并用它来治疗伤口。

sentences.en: (C) The Spanish conquistadors first encountered the potato when they arrived in Peru in 1532 in search of gold, and noted Inca miners eating chuño.
sentences.zh: 西班牙征服者于 1532 年到达秘鲁寻找黄金时第一次遇到马铃薯，并注意到印加矿工吃着 chuño。

sentences.en: At the time the Spaniards failed to realize that the potato represented a far more important treasure than either silver or gold, but they did gradually begin to use potatoes as basic rations aboard their ships.
sentences.zh: 当时西班牙人没意识到马铃薯所代表的财富远比金银更重要，但他们确实逐渐开始把马铃薯作为船上的基本口粮。

sentences.en: After the arrival of the potato in Spain in 1570, a few Spanish farmers began to cultivate them on a small scale, mostly as food for livestock.
sentences.zh: 1570 年马铃薯进入西班牙后，少数几位西班牙农户开始小规模种植，主要用作牲畜饲料。

sentences.en: (D) Throughout Europe, potatoes were regarded with suspicion, distaste and fear.
sentences.zh: 在整个欧洲，马铃薯都受到怀疑、厌恶和畏惧。

sentences.en: Generally considered to be unfit for human consumption, they were used only as animal fodder and sustenance for the starving.
sentences.zh: 它们一般被认为不适合人类食用，只被当作动物饲料和饥民的口粮。

sentences.en: In northern Europe, potatoes were primarily grown in botanical gardens as an exotic novelty.
sentences.zh: 在北欧，马铃薯主要作为外来奇珍在植物园中种植。

sentences.en: Even peasants refused to eat from a plant that produced ugly, misshapen tubers and that had come from a heathen civilization.
sentences.zh: 连农民也拒绝吃这种长出难看、畸形块茎、且来自异教文明的植物。

sentences.en: Some felt that the potato plant’s resemblance to plants in the nightshade family hinted that it was the creation of witches or devils.
sentences.zh: 有些人觉得，马铃薯植株与茄科植物的相似暗示它是巫师或魔鬼的造物。

sentences.en: (E) In meat-loving England, farmers and urban workers regarded potatoes with extreme distaste.
sentences.zh: 在喜爱肉食的英格兰，农民和城市工人极度厌恶马铃薯。

sentences.en: In 1662, the Royal Society recommended the cultivation of the tuber to the English government and the nation, but this recommendation had little impact.
sentences.zh: 1662 年，英国皇家学会向英国政府和全国推荐栽培这种块茎，但这一建议影响甚微。

sentences.en: Potatoes did not become a staple until, during the food shortages associated with the Revolutionary Wars, the English government began to officially encourage potato cultivation.
sentences.zh: 直到与革命战争相关的食物短缺期间，英国政府才开始正式鼓励种植马铃薯，马铃薯才成为主食。

sentences.en: In 1795, the Board of Agriculture issued a pamphlet entitled “Hints Respecting the Culture and Use of Potatoes”; this was followed shortly by pro-potato editorials and potato recipes in The Times.
sentences.zh: 1795 年，农业委员会发布了一本名为《关于马铃薯的栽培与使用的提示》（Hints Respecting the Culture and Use of Potatoes）的小册子；不久之后，《泰晤士报》上也出现了赞成马铃薯的社论和马铃薯食谱。

sentences.en: Gradually, the lower classes began to follow the lead of the upper classes.
sentences.zh: 渐渐地，下层阶级也开始跟随上层阶级。

sentences.en: (F) A similar pattern emerged across the English Channel in the Netherlands, Belgium and France.
sentences.zh: 在英吉利海峡对岸的荷兰、比利时和法国，出现了类似的模式。

sentences.en: While the potato slowly gained ground in eastern France (where it was often the only crop remaining after marauding soldiers plundered wheat fields and vineyards), it did not achieve widespread acceptance until the late 1700s.
sentences.zh: 虽然马铃薯在法国东部缓慢推广（在那里，被劫掠的士兵洗劫了麦田和葡萄园之后，它常常是唯一剩下的作物），但直到 1700 年代末才被广泛接受。

sentences.en: The peasants remained suspicious, in spite of a 1771 paper from the Faculté de Paris testifying that the potato was not harmful but beneficial.
sentences.zh: 尽管巴黎学院 1771 年的一篇论文证明马铃薯无害且有益，农民们仍持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: The people began to overcome their distaste when the plant received the royal seal of approval: Louis XVI began to sport a potato flower in his buttonhole, and Marie-Antoinette wore a purple potato blossom in her hair.
sentences.zh: 当这种植物获得王室印章式的认可时，人们才开始克服自己的厌恶：路易十六开始在扣眼上佩戴马铃薯花，玛丽-安托瓦内特则在头发上戴上紫色马铃薯花。

sentences.en: (G) Frederick the Great of Prussia saw the potato’s potential to help feed his nation and lower the price of bread, but faced the challenge of overcoming the people’s prejudice against the plant.
sentences.zh: 普鲁士国王腓特烈大帝（Frederick the Great）看到了马铃薯帮助养活国民并降低面包价格的潜力，但面临着克服人民对这种植物偏见的挑战。

sentences.en: When he issued a 1774 order for his subjects to grow potatoes as protection against famine, the town of Kolberg replied: “The things have neither smell nor taste, not even the dogs will eat them, so what use are they to us?”
sentences.zh: 当他在 1774 年下令臣民种植马铃薯以防饥荒时，科尔贝格镇回应说：“这些东西既无气味也无味道，连狗都不会吃，那它们对我们有什么用呢？”

sentences.en: Trying a less direct approach to encourage his subjects to begin planting potatoes, Frederick used a bit of reverse psychology: he planted a royal field of potato plants and stationed a heavy guard to protect this field from thieves.
sentences.zh: 腓特烈尝试用更间接的方法鼓励臣民开始种马铃薯，借助一点反向心理：他种下了一片皇家马铃薯田，并派重兵保护这片田地不被偷盗。

sentences.en: Nearby peasants naturally assumed that anything worth guarding was worth stealing, and so sneaked into the field and snatched the plants for their home gardens.
sentences.zh: 附近的农民自然认为，值得守卫的东西也值得偷盗，于是溜进田里把植株偷走，种到自家菜园里。

sentences.en: Of course, this was entirely in line with Frederick’s wishes.
sentences.zh: 当然，这完全符合腓特烈的意愿。

sentences.en: (H) Historians debate whether the potato was primarily a cause or an effect of the huge population boom in industrial-era England and Wales.
sentences.zh: 历史学家就马铃薯主要是工业时代英格兰和威尔士人口大爆炸的原因还是结果，存在争论。

sentences.en: Prior to 1800, the English diet had consisted primarily of meat, supplemented by bread, butter and cheese.
sentences.zh: 1800 年以前，英国人的饮食主要是肉，辅以面包、黄油和奶酪。

sentences.en: Few vegetables were consumed, most vegetables being regarded as nutritionally worthless and potentially harmful.
sentences.zh: 很少吃蔬菜——大多数蔬菜被认为营养上毫无价值且可能有害。

sentences.en: This view began to change gradually in the late 1700s.
sentences.zh: 这种看法从 1700 年代末开始逐渐改变。

sentences.en: The Industrial Revolution was drawing an ever-increasing percentage of the populace into crowded cities, where only the richest could afford homes with ovens or coal storage rooms, and people were working 12–16-hour days which left them with little time or energy to prepare food.
sentences.zh: 工业革命把越来越多的人口卷入拥挤的城市，那里只有最富裕的人才负担得起带烤箱或煤储室的住房；人们一天工作 12 至 16 小时，几乎没有时间或精力准备食物。

sentences.en: High-yielding, easily prepared potato crops were the obvious solution to England’s food problems.
sentences.zh: 高产、容易加工的马铃薯庄稼是英格兰食物问题的明显解决办法。

sentences.en: (I) Whereas most of their neighbours regarded the potato with suspicion and had to be persuaded to use it by the upper classes, the Irish peasantry embraced the tuber more passionately than anyone since the Incas.
sentences.zh: 虽然大多数邻邦对马铃薯仍抱怀疑态度，必须由上层阶级劝导才使用它，但爱尔兰农民对这种块茎的拥抱比印加人之后任何人都更热烈。

sentences.en: The potato was well suited to the Irish soil and climate, and its high yield suited the most important concern of most Irish farmers: to feed their families.
sentences.zh: 马铃薯非常适合爱尔兰的土壤和气候，其高产正契合大多数爱尔兰农户最关心的事：养活家人。

sentences.en: (J) The most dramatic example of the potato’s potential to alter population patterns occurred in Ireland, where the potato had become a staple by 1800.
sentences.zh: 马铃薯改变人口格局的潜力最戏剧性的例子发生在爱尔兰，那里到 1800 年马铃薯已成为主食。

sentences.en: The Irish population doubled to eight million between 1780 and 1841, this without any significant expansion of industry or reform of agricultural techniques beyond the widespread cultivation of the potato.
sentences.zh: 1780 至 1841 年间，爱尔兰人口翻倍到 800 万——这并未伴随着工业的显著扩张或除了广泛种植马铃薯之外农业技术的改革。

sentences.en: Though Irish landholding practices were primitive in comparison with those of England, the potato’s high yields allowed even the poorest farmers to produce more healthy food than they needed with scarcely any investment or hard labour.
sentences.zh: 尽管爱尔兰的土地占有方式与英格兰相比较为原始，马铃薯的高产仍让最贫穷的农户也能用几乎没有什么投入或繁重劳动就产出比所需更多的健康食物。

sentences.en: Even children could easily plant, harvest and cook potatoes, which of course required no threshing, curing or grinding.
sentences.zh: 连孩童都能轻松地种、收并烹煮马铃薯，而这些过程当然不需要打谷、腌制或研磨。

sentences.en: The abundance provided by potatoes greatly decreased infant mortality and encouraged early marriage.
sentences.zh: 马铃薯带来的富足极大降低了婴儿死亡率，并鼓励了早婚。

5.stemZh: 西班牙人来到秘鲁的目的是为了寻找土豆。

6.stemZh: 西班牙人认为土豆与其他蔬菜具有相同的营养成分。

sentences.en: (A) The ritual may be universal, but the details of business cards and how they are swapped vary across countries.
sentences.zh: 这种仪式或许是普世的，但名片的细节以及交换的方式因国而异。

sentences.en: Americans throw their cards casually across a table; the Japanese make the exchange of cards a formal ceremony.
sentences.zh: 美国人会随意地把名片扔过桌子；日本人则把交换名片当作一种正式仪式。

sentences.en: While there are cards that are discreet and understated, others are crammed full of details and titles.
sentences.zh: 有些名片低调含蓄，另一些则塞满细节和头衔。

sentences.en: Some businesspeople hand out 24-carat gold cards, and there are kindergarten children who have cards with not only their own contact details, but also with the job descriptions of their parents and even grandparents.
sentences.zh: 一些商人会发放 24 K 金的名片，还有些幼儿园的孩子也有名片——上面不仅有自己的联系方式，还附有父母乃至祖父母的职位描述。

sentences.en: This practice has become so common in parts of New York, for example, that the use of such cards is now prohibited by some of these institutions.
sentences.zh: 这种做法在纽约的一些地区已经常见到，以至于某些机构现在禁止使用这类名片。

sentences.en: (B) Cards have been around a long time in one form or another.
sentences.zh: 名片以某种形式存在已经很久了。

sentences.en: The Chinese invented calling cards in the 15th century to give people notice that they intended to pay them a visit, but these were for social purposes only.
sentences.zh: 中国人在 15 世纪发明了拜帖，用以告知对方有意前往拜访，但这仅用于社交目的。

sentences.en: Then, in the 17th century, European businesspeople invented a new type of card to act as miniature advertisements, signalling the advent of the business card.
sentences.zh: 到了 17 世纪，欧洲商人发明了一种新的卡片，作为微型广告，标志着商务名片的诞生。

sentences.en: In today’s world, business cards can cause people to have strong emotional reactions.
sentences.zh: 在今天的世界里，商务名片可以让人产生强烈的情绪反应。

sentences.en: According to one experienced company director, very few things can provoke more heated discussion at a board meeting than the composition of the company’s business cards.
sentences.zh: 据一位经验丰富的公司总监说，在董事会议上很少有什么事情比公司名片的设计更能引发激烈的讨论。

sentences.en: (C) Lots of companies try to promote themselves by altering the form of the card.
sentences.zh: 许多公司试图通过改变名片形式来推销自己。

sentences.en: Employees at one famous toy company give out little plastic figures with their contact details stamped on them.
sentences.zh: 一家著名玩具公司的员工会发放贴有自己联系方式的小型塑料玩偶。

sentences.en: One fast-food company has business cards which are shaped like a portion of French fries.
sentences.zh: 一家快餐公司的名片形状像一份薯条。

sentences.en: A Canadian divorce lawyer once gave out cards that could be torn in two – one half for each of the spouses.
sentences.zh: 一位加拿大的离婚律师曾发过可以从中间撕成两半的名片——夫妻各得一半。

sentences.en: For many business commentators, such gimmicky business cards prove that the use of a physical business card is nearly at an end.
sentences.zh: 对许多商业评论员而言，这种花样翻新的名片证明，使用实体名片的做法已经接近终结。

sentences.en: After all, why bother exchanging bits of thick paper at all when you can simply swap electronic versions by smartphone?
sentences.zh: 毕竟，当你可以用智能手机直接交换电子版时，为什么还要费劲交换几片厚纸呢？

sentences.en: (D) However, one can just as well argue the opposite: that business cards are here to stay, and, in a business world full of meetings and correspondence, it is more important than ever that your card is unique.
sentences.zh: 然而，人们同样可以提出相反的看法：商务名片将一直存在；在一个充满会议和往来通信的商业世界中，让你的名片独具特色比以往任何时候都更重要。

sentences.en: Attempts to reinvent business cards for the digital age have not been successful.
sentences.zh: 为数字时代重新设计名片的种种尝试都未能取得成功。

sentences.en: Even at the latest technology conferences, people still greet each other by handing out little rectangles made from paper rather than using a digital alternative.
sentences.zh: 即便在最新的科技大会上，人们仍然以彼此递送由纸制成的小长方形相互问候，而不是使用某种数字替代物。

sentences.en: (E) To understand business cards, it is necessary to understand how business works.
sentences.zh: 要理解名片，就有必要理解商业的运作方式。

sentences.en: That business cards are thriving in a digital age is a forceful reminder that there is much about business that is timeless.
sentences.zh: 商务名片在数字时代仍然兴盛，这有力地提醒我们：商业之中有许多东西是不随时间变化的。

sentences.en: According to Kate Jones, a business lecturer, there is one eternal and inescapable issue.
sentences.zh: 商业讲师凯特·琼斯（Kate Jones）认为，有一条永恒、无法回避的议题。

sentences.en: Her 2006 study of more than 200 business executives in North America found that trust was the key element for running a successful business.
sentences.zh: 她 2006 年对北美 200 多位企业高管开展的研究发现，信任是经营一桩成功生意的关键要素。

sentences.en: It is vital to be able to look someone in the eye and decide what sort of person they are.
sentences.zh: 能够直视对方的眼睛、判断对方是什么样的人，至关重要。

sentences.en: In this way, you can transform acquaintanceships into relationships.
sentences.zh: 通过这种方式，你才能把泛泛之交转化为真正的关系。

sentences.en: A good proportion of business life will always be about building social connections – having dinner or playing sport with clients and colleagues – and while computers can deal with administrative tasks, it is still human beings that have to focus on the emotional.
sentences.zh: 商业生活中很大一部分始终在于建立社会关系——与客户和同事共进晚餐、运动——而尽管计算机能处理行政事务，最终仍要由人来关注情感层面。

sentences.en: (F) The rapid advance of globalisation means that this relationship-building process is becoming ever more demanding.
sentences.zh: 全球化的迅速推进意味着，这种关系建立的过程要求越来越高。

sentences.en: Managers have to put more effort in when dealing with international counterparts, especially when there is not a common language, which is so often the case these days.
sentences.zh: 管理者在与国际同行打交道时必须付出更多努力，尤其是没有共同语言时——而如今这种情形非常常见。

sentences.en: A recent UK survey showed that chief executives of global organisations now routinely spend three out of every four weeks on international travel.
sentences.zh: 英国近期的一项调查显示，跨国机构的首席执行官们如今通常每四周中有三周在做国际差旅。

sentences.en: It is in these situations that business cards are doubly useful, as they are a quick way of establishing connections.
sentences.zh: 在这些场合下，商务名片格外有用——它们是建立连接的快捷方式。

sentences.en: Cards can also remind you that you have actually met someone in a face-to-face meeting rather than just searched for them on the Internet.
sentences.zh: 名片也可以提醒你，你确实在面对面会议中见过某个人，而不是只是在网上搜索过他们。

sentences.en: Looking through piles of different cards can enhance your memory in ways that simply looking through uniform electronic lists would never do.
sentences.zh: 翻阅一摞不同的名片，能以单纯翻看千篇一律的电子列表所无法做到的方式增强你的记忆。

sentences.en: (G) Janet McIntyre is a leading expert on business cards in today’s world.
sentences.zh: 珍妮特·麦金太尔（Janet McIntyre）是当今商务名片研究的领军专家。

sentences.en: She maintains that as companies become more complex, cards are essential in determining the exact status of every contact you meet in multinational corporations.
sentences.zh: 她坚持认为，随着公司变得越来越复杂，名片在确定你在跨国公司中接触到的每位联系人的确切身份方面是必不可少的。

sentences.en: Janet also explains how exchanging business cards can be an effective way of initiating a conversation, because it gives people a ritual to follow when they first meet a new business contact.
sentences.zh: 珍妮特还解释说，交换名片可以是开启一段对话的有效方式，因为它在人们初次见到新商业联系人时，提供了一个可遵循的仪式。

sentences.en: (H) The business world is obsessed with the idea of creating and inventing new things that will change the way we do everything, and this does lead to progress.
sentences.zh: 商业界痴迷于创造和发明可以改变我们做事方式的新事物，这确实推动了进步。

sentences.en: But there are lots of things that do not need to be changed and, in Janet McIntyre’s view, tradition also has an equally valuable role to play.
sentences.zh: 但有许多事情并不需要被改变；在珍妮特·麦金太尔看来，传统也扮演着同等重要的角色。

sentences.en: Therefore the practice of exchanging business cards is likely to continue in the business world.
sentences.zh: 因此，交换名片的做法在商业界很可能将继续下去。

records.title: Thomas Young The last man who knew everything
records.titleZh: 托马斯·杨，最后一个知道一切的人

sentences.en: (A) Thomas Young (1773–1829) contributed 63 articles to the great British encyclopaedia, Encyclopaedia Britannica, including 46 biographical entries (mostly on scientists and classical scholars) and substantial essays on ‘Bridge’ (a card game), ‘Egypt’, ‘Languages’ and ‘Tides’.
sentences.zh: 托马斯·扬（Thomas Young，1773—1829）为伟大的英国百科全书《大英百科全书》（Encyclopaedia Britannica）撰写了 63 篇文章，其中包括 46 篇传记条目（主要是科学家和古典学者）以及关于“桥牌”（一种纸牌游戏）、“埃及”“语言”和“潮汐”的重要长文。

sentences.en: Was someone who could write authoritatively about so many subjects a genius, or a dilettante?
sentences.zh: 一个能够就如此众多的主题进行权威撰写的人，究竟是天才，还是好为浅尝者？

sentences.en: In an ambitious biography, Andrew Robinson argues that Young is a good contender to be described as “the last man who knew everything”.
sentences.zh: 在一部雄心勃勃的传记中，安德鲁·罗宾逊（Andrew Robinson）认为扬是“最后一个无所不知的人”这一称谓的有力候选人。

sentences.en: Young has competition, however: the phrase, which Robinson uses as the title of his biography of Young, also serves as the subtitle of two other recent biographies – Leonard Warren’s 1998 life of palaeontologist Joseph Leidy (1823–1891) and Paula Findlen’s 2004 book on Athanasius Kircher (1602–1680).
sentences.zh: 但扬有竞争者：罗宾逊把这句话用作其扬传记的书名，而这句话也用作另两部近年传记的副标题——伦纳德·沃伦（Leonard Warren）1998 年所著古生物学家约瑟夫·莱迪（Joseph Leidy，1823—1891）的传记，以及保拉·芬德兰（Paula Findlen）2004 年出版的关于阿塔纳修斯·基歇尔（Athanasius Kircher，1602—1680）的著作。

sentences.en: (B) Young, of course, did more than write encyclopaedia entries.
sentences.zh: 扬当然不只是撰写百科全书条目。

sentences.en: He presented his first paper, on the human eye, to the prestigious academic institution, the Royal Society of London, at the age of 20 and was elected a Fellow of the Society shortly afterwards.
sentences.zh: 20 岁时，他便向享有盛誉的学术机构——伦敦皇家学会——提交了第一篇论文，论及人眼，并不久后被选为该学会会员。

sentences.en: In the paper, which sought to explain how the eye focuses on objects at varying distances, Young hypothesised that this was achieved by changes in the shape of the lens.
sentences.zh: 在这篇试图解释眼睛如何聚焦于不同距离物体的论文中，扬假设这是通过晶状体形状的变化实现的。

sentences.en: He also theorised that light travels in waves and believed that, to be able to see in colour, there must be three receptors in the eye corresponding to the three principal colours (red, green and violet) to which the retina could respond.
sentences.zh: 他还提出光是以波的形式传播的理论，并相信要能看到色彩，眼睛中必须有对应三种主要颜色（红、绿和紫）的三种感受器，让视网膜对此作出反应。

sentences.en: All these hypotheses were subsequently proved correct.
sentences.zh: 这些假说后来全都被证明是正确的。

sentences.en: (C) Later in his life, when he was in his forties, Young was instrumental in cracking the code that unlocked the unknown script on the Rosetta Stone, a tablet found in Egypt by the Napoleonic army in 1799.
sentences.zh: 在他的后半生——40 多岁时——扬在破译罗塞塔石碑（Rosetta Stone）上未知文字的密码中发挥了关键作用。这块石板是 1799 年拿破仑军队在埃及发现的。

sentences.en: The stone has text in three alphabets: Greek, Egyptian hieroglyphs and another script that was originally unrecognisable.
sentences.zh: 该石碑上有三种字体的文字：希腊文、埃及象形文字以及另一种最初无法识别的字体。

sentences.en: The unrecognisable script is now known as demotic and, as Young deduced, is directly related to Egyptian hieroglyphs.
sentences.zh: 那种无法识别的字体如今被称为通俗体（demotic），而正如扬所推断，它与埃及象形文字直接相关。

sentences.en: His initial work on this appeared in the Britannica entry ‘Egypt’.
sentences.zh: 他在这方面最初的工作出现在《大英百科全书》“埃及”条目中。

sentences.en: In another entry, Young coined the term ‘Indo-European’ to describe the family of languages spoken throughout most of Europe and northern India.
sentences.zh: 在另一个条目里，扬创造了“印欧”（Indo-European）一词，用以描述在大部分欧洲和北印度所使用的语言家族。

sentences.en: These works are landmark achievements for a man who was a child prodigy but who, unlike many remarkable children, did not fade into obscurity as an adult.
sentences.zh: 对一个童年天才——而且不像许多杰出儿童那样在成年后归于沉寂——的人而言，这些工作堪称里程碑式的成就。

sentences.en: (D) Born in 1773 in Somerset, England, Young lived with his maternal grandfather from an early age.
sentences.zh: 扬于 1773 年生于英格兰萨默塞特郡，从年幼时起便与外祖父同住。

sentences.en: He devoured books from the age of two and excelled at Latin, Greek, mathematics and natural philosophy (the 18th-century term for science).
sentences.zh: 他从两岁起就如饥似渴地读书，并在拉丁文、希腊文、数学和自然哲学（natural philosophy，即 18 世纪对“科学”的称呼）方面表现卓越。

sentences.en: After leaving school, he was greatly encouraged by Richard Brocklesby, a physician and Fellow of the Royal Society.
sentences.zh: 离开学校后，他受到内科医生、皇家学会会员理查德·布罗克尔斯比（Richard Brocklesby）极大的鼓励。

sentences.en: Following Brocklesby’s lead, Young decided to pursue a career in medicine.
sentences.zh: 按照布罗克尔斯比的引导，扬决定从医。

sentences.en: He studied in London and then moved on to more formal education in Edinburgh, Göttingen and Cambridge.
sentences.zh: 他先在伦敦学习，随后又前往爱丁堡、哥廷根和剑桥接受更正规的教育。

sentences.en: After completing his medical training at the University of Cambridge in 1808, Young set up practice as a physician in London and, a few years later, was appointed physician at St George’s Hospital.
sentences.zh: 1808 年在剑桥大学完成医学训练后，扬在伦敦开诊行医，几年后被任命为圣乔治医院的医生。

sentences.en: (E) Young’s skill as a physician, however, did not equal his talent as a scholar of natural philosophy or linguistics.
sentences.zh: 然而，扬作为医师的能力并未与他作为自然哲学或语言学者的才华相称。

sentences.en: In 1801, he had been appointed to a professorship of natural philosophy at the Royal Institution, where he delivered as many as 60 lectures a year.
sentences.zh: 1801 年，他被任命为皇家学会的自然哲学教授，每年发表多达 60 场讲座。

sentences.en: His opinions were sought by civic and national authorities on matters such as the introduction of gas lighting to London streets and methods of ship construction.
sentences.zh: 他的意见被市政及全国当局就诸如向伦敦街道引入煤气照明和造船方法等事项征询。

sentences.en: From 1819, he was Superintendent of the Nautical Almanac and Secretary to the Board of Longitude.
sentences.zh: 自 1819 年起，他担任《航海年历》（Nautical Almanac）的主管和经度委员会（Board of Longitude）的秘书。

sentences.en: Between 1816 and 1825, he contributed many entries to the Encyclopaedia Britannica, and throughout his career he authored numerous other essays, papers and books.
sentences.zh: 1816 至 1825 年间，他为《大英百科全书》撰写了许多条目，整个职业生涯中他还写了大量其他文章、论文和著作。

sentences.en: (F) Young is a perfect subject for a biography – perfect, but daunting.
sentences.zh: 扬是写传记的绝佳对象——绝佳，但令人却步。

sentences.en: Few men contributed so much to so many technical fields.
sentences.zh: 很少有人为这么多技术领域贡献过这么多。

sentences.en: Robinson’s aim is to introduce non-scientists to Young’s work and life.
sentences.zh: 罗宾逊的目标是把扬的工作和生活介绍给非科学家。

sentences.en: He succeeds, providing clear expositions of the technical material (especially that on optics and Egyptian hieroglyphs).
sentences.zh: 他成功做到了，并对技术性内容（尤其是关于光学和埃及象形文字的）做出了清晰的阐释。

sentences.en: Some readers of this book will, like Robinson, find Young’s accomplishments impressive; others will see him, as some historians have, as a dilettante.
sentences.zh: 这本书的一些读者会像罗宾逊一样发现扬的成就令人钦佩；另一些读者则会像某些历史学家那样，把他视为一个浅尝辄止者。

sentences.en: Yet despite the rich material presented in this book, readers will not end up knowing Young personally.
sentences.zh: 然而，尽管本书呈现了丰富的素材，读者最终也不会真正认识扬这个人。

sentences.en: We catch glimpses of a playful Young, doodling Greek and Latin phrases in his notes on medical lectures and translating the verses that a young lady had written on the walls of a summerhouse into Greek elegiacs.
sentences.zh: 我们能瞥见一个顽皮的扬——他在医学讲座笔记里涂写希腊文和拉丁文短语，把一位年轻女士写在凉亭墙上的诗句翻译成希腊挽歌体。

sentences.en: Young was introduced into elite society, attended the theatre and learned to dance and play the flute.
sentences.zh: 扬被引入上流社会，参加戏剧，学会跳舞和吹长笛。

sentences.en: In addition, he was an accomplished horseman.
sentences.zh: 此外，他还是个出色的骑手。

sentences.en: However, his personal life looks pale next to his vibrant career and studies.
sentences.zh: 然而，与他活跃的职业生涯和研究相比，他的私生活看起来十分平淡。

sentences.en: (G) Young married Eliza Maxwell in 1804, and according to Robinson, “their marriage was happy and she appreciated his work”.
sentences.zh: 扬于 1804 年与伊莱扎·麦克斯韦（Eliza Maxwell）结婚，按罗宾逊的说法，“他们的婚姻幸福，她欣赏他的工作”。

sentences.en: Almost all we know about her is that she sustained her husband through some acrimonious disputes about optics and that she worried about money when his medical career was slow to take off.
sentences.zh: 我们对她几乎只知道：在关于光学的几场激烈论战中，她支持着丈夫；当他医生生涯起步缓慢时，她为钱而忧虑。

sentences.en: Little evidence survives concerning the complexities of Young’s relationships with his mother and father, and Robinson does not credit them with shaping Young’s extraordinary mind.
sentences.zh: 关于扬与父母关系复杂性的证据所剩无几，罗宾逊并未把扬非凡的心智归功于他们。

sentences.en: Despite the lack of personal detail, anyone interested in what it means to be a genius should read this book.
sentences.zh: 尽管缺乏个人细节，任何对何为天才感兴趣的人都应该读一读这本书。

sentences.en: (A) Triumph of the City, by Edward Glaeser, is a thrilling and very readable hymn of praise to an invention so vast and so effective that it is generally taken for granted.
sentences.zh: 爱德华·格莱泽所著的《城市的胜利》，是一曲激动人心、极为耐读的赞歌，歌颂的是一项如此宏大、如此有效，以致人们普遍视若理所当然的发明。

sentences.en: More than half the global population already live in urban areas and, every month, five million more flood into the cities of the developed and developing worlds.
sentences.zh: 全球已有一半以上的人口居住在城市地区，而且每个月还有五百万人涌入发达世界和发展中世界的城市。

sentences.en: The crowds and poverty of some of these modern cities may horrify us.
sentences.zh: 其中一些现代城市的拥挤与贫困，也许会让我们感到震惊。

sentences.en: They shouldn’t, says Glaeser; they are signs of growth, energy and aspiration.
sentences.zh: 格莱泽说，其实不必如此；它们是增长、活力与抱负的标志。

sentences.en: Cities are our best and brightest hope.
sentences.zh: 城市是我们最美好、最光明的希望。

sentences.en: (B) This idea has had more than two hundred years of resistance.
sentences.zh: 这一观点已经遭遇了两百多年的抵触。

sentences.en: Not long after the Industrial Revolution began in Britain, the Romantic poets turned away from the smoke and factories of their cities to celebrate the air and light of untouched nature.
sentences.zh: 工业革命在英国开始后不久，浪漫主义诗人便背离城市的烟尘与工厂，转而讴歌未经触动的大自然的空气与光亮。

sentences.en: In 19th-century America, the writer Henry David Thoreau retreated to the wilderness of Walden Pond to live the solitary, simple life, and convinced generations of Americans that cities were bad and nature was good.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪的美国，作家亨利·戴维·梭罗退隐到瓦尔登湖的荒野，过起孤独而简朴的生活，并使一代又一代美国人相信，城市是坏的，自然是好的。

sentences.en: (C) They had, Glaeser admits, a point.
sentences.zh: 格莱泽承认，他们的看法不无道理。

sentences.en: The early industrial cities were dirty, since they lacked efficient waste-disposal systems, and disease spread rapidly among the population.
sentences.zh: 早期的工业城市肮脏不堪，因为缺乏有效的废物处理系统，疾病在人群中迅速蔓延。

sentences.en: But more importantly they were profitable, and there were enormous commercial incentives to make them work, as well as political ones.
sentences.zh: 但更重要的是，它们有利可图，让它们良好运转既有巨大的商业动机，也有政治上的动机。

sentences.en: Their transformation could be achieved at a stroke: in the second half of the 19th century, the French Emperor Napoleon III gave Baron Haussmann unrestricted power to turn the slum-infested city of Paris into one of the wonders and delights of the modern world.
sentences.zh: 它们的改造可以一举完成：19世纪下半叶，法国皇帝拿破仑三世赋予奥斯曼男爵不受限制的权力，把贫民窟遍布的巴黎变成了现代世界的奇迹与乐土之一。

sentences.en: Or the transformation could be done by trial and error.
sentences.zh: 这种改造也可以通过反复试错来完成。

sentences.en: Glaeser gives a brilliant account of the stop-start progression of New York to its late 20th-century position as the cultural and economic centre of the world.
sentences.zh: 格莱泽精彩地讲述了纽约如何走走停停地发展，最终在20世纪后期成为世界的文化和经济中心。

sentences.en: Either way, Paris, New York and other cities developed because they were truly effective markets of ideas and innovation.
sentences.zh: 无论以何种方式，巴黎、纽约及其他城市之所以发展起来，是因为它们是真正高效的思想与创新的集市。

sentences.en: (D) For these and many other reasons, we should not be so upset by the spectacle of urban poverty.
sentences.zh: 出于上述以及许多其他原因，我们不应被城市贫困的景象搅得如此心烦意乱。

sentences.en: The poor flock to cities in the hope of becoming richer (which, by and large, they do).
sentences.zh: 穷人成群涌向城市，希望变得更富裕（而大体上他们也确实如愿了）。

sentences.en: They also reinvigorate the economy of the city.
sentences.zh: 他们同时也为城市的经济注入新的活力。

sentences.en: It is folly to drive them away by forcing property prices to soar with unreasonable planning regulations.
sentences.zh: 用不合理的规划法规推高房价，从而把他们赶走，是一种愚蠢之举。

sentences.en: Instead, cities should build more houses and thereby hold property prices in check.
sentences.zh: 相反，城市应当建造更多住房，从而把房价控制住。

sentences.en: (E) It can go wrong, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，事情也可能出岔子。

sentences.en: In Glaeser’s view, this is primarily because municipal authorities fail to understand the principal virtues of their cities.
sentences.zh: 在格莱泽看来，这主要是因为市政当局未能理解自己城市的主要优点。

sentences.en: The heart of Paris, as many Parisians say, is turning into a museum because of the desire to preserve Baron Haussmann’s 19th-century boulevards.
sentences.zh: 正如许多巴黎人所说，由于人们一心想保留奥斯曼男爵19世纪的林荫大道，巴黎的中心区正在变成一座博物馆。

sentences.en: Glaeser defends their preservation, but argues that in the 1950s the French made a mistake in establishing a huge high-rise commercial development — La Défense — on the outskirts of the city.
sentences.zh: 格莱泽为保留这些大道辩护，但认为法国人在1950年代犯了一个错误，在城市的郊外兴建了一片庞大的高层商业开发区——拉德芳斯。

sentences.en: Far better, he says, to have turned the central area of Montparnasse into a new commercial district.
sentences.zh: 他说，远为明智的做法，本应是把蒙帕纳斯的中心地带改造成一个新的商业区。

sentences.en: This would have revitalised much of the city centre without destroying its fabric.
sentences.zh: 这样既能让大部分市中心重焕生机，又不会破坏其原有肌理。

sentences.en: In India, Mumbai could save itself from ever-more inefficient sprawl over the surrounding area simply by relaxing the rules presently imposed on the height of new constructions.
sentences.zh: 在印度，孟买只需放宽目前对新建筑高度的限制，就能使自己免于向周边地区日益低效地蔓延扩张。

sentences.en: (F) In America, it is the suburbs that have proved to be the real disaster.
sentences.zh: 在美国，事实证明真正的灾难恰恰是郊区。

sentences.en: Glaeser is repentant on this subject himself.
sentences.zh: 在这个问题上，格莱泽自己也满怀悔意。

sentences.en: He moved to the suburbs when he had children.
sentences.zh: 他在有了孩子之后搬到了郊区。

sentences.en: His entirely legitimate excuse is that the government made him (and millions like him) do it.
sentences.zh: 他那完全站得住脚的借口是，是政府逼着他（以及数百万像他这样的人）这么做的。

sentences.en: By under-taxing petrol and imposing tight planning restrictions on inner cities that drove up the cost of property, it made flight to the suburbs more or less inevitable for the middle classes.
sentences.zh: 政府对汽油征税过低，又对内城施加严格的规划限制、推高了房产成本，这就使中产阶级逃往郊区或多或少成了必然。

sentences.en: (G) This is a disaster because nothing is more inefficient than a suburb.
sentences.zh: 这是一场灾难，因为没有什么比郊区更低效的了。

sentences.en: Suburbanites mingle less, and lose the face-to-face contact that makes being an urbanite so much more creative.
sentences.zh: 郊区居民彼此往来较少，失去了那种面对面的接触，而正是这种接触让城市居民富有得多的创造力。

sentences.en: Moreover, houses are costlier to heat and cool than flats, and suburbanites drive thousands more miles per year than city dwellers.
sentences.zh: 而且，独栋住宅的取暖和制冷费用比公寓更高，郊区居民每年驾车里程也比城市居民多出数千英里。

sentences.en: Every aspect of life involves more consumption.
sentences.zh: 生活的方方面面都涉及更多的消耗。

sentences.en: This leads to the strongest and newest argument in favour of cities — they are good for the environment.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了支持城市的最有力、也最新的论点——城市有利于环境。

sentences.en: To live in the country or the suburbs is to have a vastly larger carbon footprint than any urbanite.
sentences.zh: 居住在乡村或郊区，意味着碳足迹远远大于任何一个城市居民。

sentences.en: (H) Full of characters and accessible information, this is a tremendous book, not least because, like me, you will find yourself constantly seeking reasons to disagree.
sentences.zh: 这是一本了不起的书，充满了人物和通俗易懂的资讯，尤其是因为，你会像我一样，发现自己不断地在寻找反驳它的理由。

sentences.en: Like the poor in the city, this is a sign of success.
sentences.zh: 就像城市里的穷人一样，这正是成功的标志。

sentences.en: If you hate the city and get moist-eyed at the thought of the country then, one way or another, Glaeser is the man you will have to take on.
sentences.zh: 如果你厌恶城市，一想到乡村就热泪盈眶，那么无论如何，格莱泽都是你不得不去较量的对手。

records.title: Tunnelling under the Thames
records.titleZh: 在泰晤士河下方隧道施工

sentences.en: (A) At the beginning of the 19th century, the port of London was the busiest in the world.
sentences.zh: 19 世纪初，伦敦港是世界上最繁忙的港口。

sentences.en: Cargoes that had travelled thousands of miles and survived all the hazards of the sea were unloaded on the banks of the Thames, only for their owners to discover that the most frustrating portion of their journey lay ahead.
sentences.zh: 在跋涉数千英里、躲过海上各种危险后，货物被卸到泰晤士河岸——它们的主人才发现，行程中最令人沮丧的部分还在前头。

sentences.en: Consignments intended for the southern parts of Britain had to be lifted onto horse carts, pulled through the docks and across London Bridge, built in the 12th century and as impractical as its early date implies.
sentences.zh: 运往英国南部地区的货物必须被搬上马车，从码头上拉出来，穿过 12 世纪建成、像其早期年代所暗示的那样不实用的伦敦桥。

sentences.en: By 1820, London Bridge had become the centre of the world’s largest traffic jam.
sentences.zh: 到 1820 年，伦敦桥已经成为世界上最大堵车的中心。

sentences.en: (B) It was an intolerable situation, and it was clear that if private enterprise could build another crossing closer to the docks, there would be good money to be made in tolls paid by users.
sentences.zh: 情况令人无法忍受，显然，如果私营企业能在更靠近码头的地方建造另一处过河通道，凭借使用者所付的过路费就能赚得不少钱。

sentences.en: Another bridge was out of the question, as this would deny sailing ships access to the city centre, and ambitious men turned their thoughts to tunnelling beneath the Thames instead.
sentences.zh: 再建一座桥根本不可能，因为那样会切断帆船进入市中心的通道，于是那些有抱负的人把心思转向了在泰晤士河底下挖隧道。

sentences.en: This was not such an obvious idea as it might appear.
sentences.zh: 这并不是看上去那样显而易见的想法。

sentences.en: Although increasing demand for coal had meant a great many tunnels had been dug in mines in Britain, working methods remained primitive.
sentences.zh: 尽管对煤需求的增长意味着英国矿山里挖出了大量隧道，但工作方法仍然原始。

sentences.en: Tunnels were dug by men with simple tools, by candlelight.
sentences.zh: 隧道由工人用简单工具在烛光下挖出。

sentences.en: However, in 1807, a group of businessmen got themselves up as the Thames Archway Company.
sentences.zh: 然而，1807 年，一群商人组建了泰晤士拱道公司（Thames Archway Company）。

sentences.en: Their ambition was to tunnel below the Thames, but there was little to guide them as there had been no previous attempt to do this.
sentences.zh: 他们的抱负是在泰晤士河底下挖隧道，但因为此前没有人尝试过，他们几乎没有任何参照。

sentences.en: Their chief engineer was Richard Trevithick, designer of the world’s first high-pressure steam engine.
sentences.zh: 他们的总工程师是理查德·特里维西克（Richard Trevithick）——世界上第一台高压蒸汽机的设计者。

sentences.en: His men made progress at the beginning, but then things began to go disastrously wrong, with muddy soil pouring into the tunnel.
sentences.zh: 他的工人在起初取得了进展，但随后事情开始灾难性地出错，泥泞的土壤涌入隧道。

sentences.en: Eventually the Thames Archway Company had had enough.
sentences.zh: 最终泰晤士拱道公司忍无可忍。

sentences.en: Its funds were exhausted, Trevithick was sick from exposure to the river water, and its efforts had proved only that a passage under the river exceeded the limits of contemporary mining technology.
sentences.zh: 公司资金耗尽，特里维西克因暴露于河水中而生病；他们的努力只证明了：从河底通过的通道超出了当时矿业技术的极限。

sentences.en: (C) At that time, the only machines used in mines were pumps.
sentences.zh: 那时，矿山里所用的机器只有泵。

sentences.en: It took a man of genius to recognise that a different sort of machine was needed, a machine that could prevent the roof and walls of a tunnel from collapsing.
sentences.zh: 需要有天才之人意识到，需要的是一种不同的机器，一种能阻止隧道顶部和侧壁坍塌的机器。

sentences.en: This man was Marc Brunel, a Frenchman who had become one of the most prominent engineers in Britain.
sentences.zh: 这个人就是马克·布鲁内尔（Marc Brunel）——一位已成为英国最杰出工程师之一的法国人。

sentences.en: Not long after the failure of the Thames Archway Company, Brunel saw a rotten piece of wood lying on the river bank.
sentences.zh: 在泰晤士拱道公司失败后不久，布鲁内尔在河岸上看到一块腐烂的木头。

sentences.en: Examining the wood through a magnifying glass, he observed it was infested with something that looked like a worm.
sentences.zh: 用放大镜观察这块木头时，他发现它被一种看起来像虫子的东西蛀了。

sentences.en: Brunel realised that as it tunnelled through the wood, it would push chewed wood into its mouth and digest it, then excrete a hard substance that lined the new tunnel.
sentences.zh: 布鲁内尔意识到，当它从木头里钻过去时，会把咬下的木屑送入口中并消化，再分泌出一种坚硬的物质来给新通道做衬里。

sentences.en: Brunel realised that the worm’s digging technique could be adapted to produce a new way of tunnelling.
sentences.zh: 布鲁内尔意识到，这种虫子的挖掘技术可以被改造，用以产生一种新的挖隧道方式。

sentences.en: His realisation led him to invent a device that has been used in one form or another in most major tunnels built since: the tunnelling shield.
sentences.zh: 这种认识促使他发明了一种装置，此后大多数主要隧道工程都以某种形式使用过这种装置：盾构。

sentences.en: It consisted of a series of iron frames that could be pressed against the tunnel face and supported on a set of horizontal wooden planks that would prevent the face from collapsing.
sentences.zh: 它由一系列可以抵在隧道掌子面上的铁框架组成，并由一组水平木板支撑，以防止掌子面坍塌。

sentences.en: It was a complex machine and not easy to use, but it seemed that it would protect the miners.
sentences.zh: 这是一种复杂的机器，使用起来并不容易，但看起来它能保护矿工。

sentences.en: Brunel’s team examined earth samples taken from beneath the riverbed, and subsequently decided to dig the tunnel close to the muddy river bottom, where he could expect to find clay.
sentences.zh: 布鲁内尔的团队检查了从河床下取来的土样，随后决定靠近河底的泥层中挖隧道，因为他能在那里期望找到黏土。

sentences.en: This would be a more solid and safe substance to dig through than the sand that was found deeper down.
sentences.zh: 与更深处发现的沙子相比，这种黏土是一种更坚实、更安全的挖掘介质。

sentences.en: (D) Brunel began work on his tunnel in 1825, but the problems of such an operation soon became apparent.
sentences.zh: 布鲁内尔于 1825 年开始他的隧道工程，但这种作业的种种问题很快显现。

sentences.en: Although the shield itself worked well, water began to drip into the tunnel.
sentences.zh: 虽然盾构本身工作良好，但水开始滴入隧道。

sentences.en: This was more of an annoyance than a danger while the pump was working, but this machine proved unreliable and sometimes failed altogether, meaning that floods began to occur with increasing regularity.
sentences.zh: 在水泵运转时，这更像是一种烦扰而非危险，但这台机器被证明不可靠，有时甚至完全失灵，意味着洪灾以越来越规律的频率发生。

sentences.en: The miners often had to run for their lives.
sentences.zh: 矿工们时常不得不为活命而奔逃。

sentences.en: Even when Brunel’s men were able to work, they complained of frequent headaches, because the air underground was dirty and contaminated due to the lack of an adequate ventilation system.
sentences.zh: 即便布鲁内尔的工人能开工，他们也抱怨头痛频发，因为由于缺乏适当的通风系统，地下空气污浊而被污染。

sentences.en: There were other problems too.
sentences.zh: 还有其他问题。

sentences.en: Illuminating the tunnels was a constant challenge.
sentences.zh: 为隧道照明是一项持续的挑战。

sentences.en: Lamps gave off only a weak glow, and there were a number of accidents because the miners could not see what they were doing.
sentences.zh: 灯发出的光只是微弱的微光，矿工因看不清自己在干什么而发生了多起事故。

sentences.en: Lastly, a number of Brunel’s miners walked off the job because they could not tolerate the excessive temperatures that developed in the cramped conditions underground.
sentences.zh: 最后，由于无法忍受地下狭窄环境中产生的过高温度，布鲁内尔的多位矿工辞职走人。

sentences.en: (E) Despite all the setbacks, the tunnel finally emerged on the opposite river bank on August 12, 1841.
sentences.zh: 尽管历经种种挫折，隧道最终于 1841 年 8 月 12 日在对岸钻出。

sentences.en: Brunel’s triumph, however, was only partial.
sentences.zh: 然而，布鲁内尔的胜利只是部分性的。

sentences.en: The small payment of a penny per person made by the thousands of visitors hardly paid the interest on the government loan he had required to complete the project.
sentences.zh: 成千上万名访客每人支付的一便士小钱，几乎勉强够支付他完成这一工程所需的政府贷款利息。

sentences.en: As a result, there was never enough funding to make it accessible to horse-drawn vehicles, as intended.
sentences.zh: 结果，资金始终不足以按原计划让它通行马车。

sentences.en: Instead, the passageways were filled with souvenir-sellers by day and the homeless at night, before it was finally closed.
sentences.zh: 反而，通道白天充斥着纪念品贩子，夜里则是无家可归者的容身之所——最后它被关闭。

sentences.en: (F) It was only when the underground railway came to London in the 1860s that the Thames Tunnel achieved a measure of real usefulness.
sentences.zh: 只有当 1860 年代地下铁路来到伦敦时，泰晤士隧道才获得了一定程度的真正实用价值。

sentences.en: It was bought in 1869 by the East London Railway, who found it to be in such excellent condition that it was immediately pressed into service as a route for passenger trains heading east.
sentences.zh: 它在 1869 年被东伦敦铁路公司买下，他们发现它状况极好，于是立即将其投入使用，作为东向客运列车的通道。

sentences.en: The tunnel became, and remains, part of the London Underground network.
sentences.zh: 该隧道成为——并一直是——伦敦地铁网的一部分。

sentences.en: (A) On a Sunday morning in late November 1974, a team of scientists were digging in an isolated spot in the Afar region of Ethiopia.
sentences.zh: 1974年11月下旬的一个星期天早晨，一队科学家正在埃塞俄比亚阿法尔地区一处偏僻的地点进行挖掘。

sentences.en: Surveying the area, palaeoanthropologist Donald Johanson spotted a small piece of bone.
sentences.zh: 在勘查这片区域时，古人类学家唐纳德·约翰森发现了一小块骨头。

sentences.en: Straight away, he recognised that it came from the elbow of a human ancestor.
sentences.zh: 他一眼就认出，这块骨头来自一位人类祖先的肘部。

sentences.en: And there were plenty more.
sentences.zh: 而且还有许多。

sentences.en: “As I looked up the slopes to my left, I saw bits of the skull, a chunk of jaw, a couple of vertebrae,” says Johanson.
sentences.zh: “当我抬头望向左边的斜坡时，我看到了一些头骨碎片、一块下颌骨和几节脊椎骨，”约翰森说。

sentences.en: (B) It was immediately obvious that the skeleton was a significant find, because the sediments at the site were known to be 3.5 million years old.
sentences.zh: 这具骨架显然一眼就能看出是一项重大发现，因为该遗址的沉积层已知有350万年的历史。

sentences.en: “I realised this was part of a skeleton that was older than three million years,” says Johanson.
sentences.zh: “我意识到，这是一具年代超过三百万年的骨架的一部分，”约翰森说。

sentences.en: It was the most ancient early human ever found.
sentences.zh: 它是迄今发现的最古老的早期人类。

sentences.en: Later it became apparent that it was also the most complete – 40% of the skeleton had been preserved.
sentences.zh: 后来人们清楚地认识到，它也是最完整的——骨架的40%得到了保存。

sentences.en: (C) At the group’s campsite that night, Johanson played a Beatles song called “Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds”, and, as the feeling was that the skeleton was female due to its size, someone suggested calling it Lucy.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上，在这支队伍的营地里，约翰森播放了一首名为《缀满钻石天空中的露西》的披头士歌曲，由于从骨架的大小判断它应是女性，于是有人提议把它叫作露西。

sentences.en: The name stuck and Johanson says, “All of a sudden, she became a person.
sentences.zh: 这个名字就此沿用下来。约翰森说：“她一下子就成了一个有血有肉的人。

sentences.en: But the morning after the discovery, the discussion was dominated by questions.
sentences.zh: 但在发现她之后的第二天早晨，讨论被各种问题所主导。

sentences.en: How old was Lucy when she died?
sentences.zh: 露西去世时多大年纪？

sentences.en: Did she have children?
sentences.zh: 她有过孩子吗？

sentences.en: And might she be our direct ancestor?”
sentences.zh: 她会不会是我们的直系祖先？”

sentences.en: Nowadays, we’re starting to get the answers to some of these questions.
sentences.zh: 如今，我们开始能够得到其中一些问题的答案了。

sentences.en: (D) According to Johanson, Lucy had an incredible combination of primitive and derived features, which had not been seen before.
sentences.zh: 据约翰森所说，露西身上有着原始特征与衍生特征令人难以置信的结合，这是前所未见的。

sentences.en: Her skull and jaws were more ape-like than those of other groups of early humans.
sentences.zh: 她的头骨和颌骨比其他类群的早期人类更像猿。

sentences.en: Her braincase was also very small, no bigger than that of a chimpanzee.
sentences.zh: 她的颅腔也非常小，不比黑猩猩的大。

sentences.en: (E) For Johanson, it was immediately apparent that Lucy walked upright.
sentences.zh: 在约翰森看来，露西能够直立行走是一目了然的。

sentences.en: That’s because the shape and positioning of her pelvis reflected a fully upright gait.
sentences.zh: 这是因为她骨盆的形状和位置反映出一种完全直立的步态。

sentences.en: Lucy’s knee and ankle were also preserved and seemed to reflect bipedal walking.
sentences.zh: 露西的膝盖和脚踝也得到了保存，似乎同样反映出两足行走。

sentences.en: Later studies of feet offer even more evidence.
sentences.zh: 后来对足部的研究提供了更多的证据。

sentences.en: As an upright walker, Lucy strengthened the idea that walking was one of the selective pressures driving human evolution forwards.
sentences.zh: 作为一个直立行走者，露西强化了这样一种观点：行走是推动人类进化向前的选择压力之一。

sentences.en: Early humans did not need bigger brains to take defining steps away from apes.
sentences.zh: 早期人类并不需要更大的大脑，就能迈出使自己有别于猿的关键一步。

sentences.en: Extra brainpower only came over a million years later with the arrival of the species Homo erectus, meaning upright man.
sentences.zh: 额外的脑力直到一百多万年后才出现，伴随着直立人这一物种的到来，“直立人”意为直立的人。

sentences.en: Though big brains would clearly be important later, walking remains one of the traits that makes us uniquely human.
sentences.zh: 尽管大脑容量在后来显然会变得重要，但直立行走至今仍是使我们成为独特人类的特征之一。

sentences.en: (F) She may have walked like a human, but Lucy spent at least some of her time up in the trees, as chimpanzees and orangutans still do today.
sentences.zh: 露西也许走起路来像人，但她至少有一部分时间是在树上度过的，就像黑猩猩和红毛猩猩今天仍然如此一样。

sentences.en: It may be that upright walking evolved in the trees, as a way to walk along branches that would otherwise be too flexible.
sentences.zh: 直立行走或许是在树上进化出来的，作为一种沿着原本过于柔软的树枝行走的方式。

sentences.en: It’s not clear why Lucy left the safety of the trees.
sentences.zh: 露西为何离开了树上的安全之所，目前尚不清楚。

sentences.en: It is thought that savannahs were gradually opening up, so trees were spaced further apart.
sentences.zh: 一般认为，当时稀树草原正逐渐扩展开来，因而树木之间的间距越来越大。

sentences.en: But hunting for food may have been the real reason for heading to the ground, says Chris Stringer of the Natural History Museum in London.
sentences.zh: 但伦敦自然历史博物馆的克里斯·斯特林格说，觅食才可能是它们走向地面的真正原因。

sentences.en: In line with this idea, recent evidence suggests that the diet of early humans was changing at that time.
sentences.zh: 与这一观点相一致的是，近来的证据表明，早期人类的饮食在那时正在发生变化。

sentences.en: (G) Studies of the remains of food trapped on preserved human teeth indicate that several species, including Lucy’s, were expanding their diet around 3.5 million years ago.
sentences.zh: 对残留在保存下来的人类牙齿上的食物残余的研究表明，包括露西所属物种在内的若干物种，在约350万年前正在拓宽自己的食谱。

sentences.en: Instead of mostly eating fruit from trees, they began to include grasses and possibly meat.
sentences.zh: 它们不再以树上的果实为主食，而是开始把草类、或许还有肉类纳入食谱。

sentences.en: This change in diet may have allowed them to range more widely, and to travel around more efficiently in a changing environment.
sentences.zh: 这种饮食上的变化，也许使它们得以在更大的范围内活动，并在不断变化的环境中更高效地四处迁移。

sentences.en: Fossilised crocodile and turtle eggs were found near her skeleton, suggesting that Lucy died while foraging for them in a nearby lake.
sentences.zh: 在她的骨架附近发现了鳄鱼蛋和龟蛋的化石，这表明露西是在附近一处湖中觅食这些蛋时死去的。

sentences.en: (H) How did early humans process all these new foods?
sentences.zh: 早期人类是如何处理所有这些新食物的呢？

sentences.en: Later species, like Homo erectus, are known to have used simple stone tools, but no tools have ever been found from this far back.
sentences.zh: 已知像直立人这样较晚的物种使用过简单的石器，但从未发现过年代如此久远的工具。

sentences.en: However, in 2010 archaeologists uncovered animal bones with scratches that seem to have been made by stone tools.
sentences.zh: 然而，2010年考古学家发现了一些动物骨头，上面有似乎是石器留下的划痕。

sentences.en: This suggests that Lucy and her relatives used stone tools to eat meat.
sentences.zh: 这表明，露西和她的同类曾用石器来吃肉。

sentences.en: There have since been heated debates over whether or not the marks were really made by tools.
sentences.zh: 此后，关于这些痕迹是否真的由工具造成，一直存在激烈的争论。

sentences.en: But if they were, it is not surprising, says Fred Spoor of the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology in Leipzig, Germany.
sentences.zh: 但德国莱比锡马克斯·普朗克进化人类学研究所的弗雷德·斯波尔说，如果真是工具造成的，那也不足为奇。

sentences.en: (I) It also seems that Lucy’s childhood was much briefer than ours and that she had to fend for herself from a young age.
sentences.zh: 看来露西的童年也比我们的短得多，她从小就不得不自谋生路。

sentences.en: We know that Lucy was a full-grown adult because she had wisdom teeth and her bones had fused.
sentences.zh: 我们之所以知道露西是个发育完全的成年人，是因为她长有智齿，骨骼也已愈合。

sentences.en: But unlike modern humans, she seems to have grown to full size very quickly, and the time of death was when she was around 12 years old.
sentences.zh: 但与现代人不同，她似乎很快就长到了完全的体型，而去世时她大约只有12岁。

sentences.en: In line with that, a recent study of a 3-year-old early human suggested that their brains matured much earlier than ours do.
sentences.zh: 与此相一致的是，近来对一名3岁早期人类个体的研究表明，他们的大脑成熟得比我们的要早得多。

sentences.en: (A) During the settlement of New Zealand by European immigrants, natural timbers played a major role.
sentences.zh: 在欧洲移民定居新西兰的过程中，天然木材发挥了重要作用。

sentences.en: Wood was easily accessible and relatively cheap.
sentences.zh: 木材容易获取，且相对便宜。

sentences.en: A tradition of wooden houses arose, supported by the recognition that they were less likely to collapse suddenly during earthquakes, a not-infrequent event in this part of the world.
sentences.zh: 由此形成了建造木屋的传统，人们认识到木屋在地震时不易突然倒塌——而地震在世界的这一带并不少见，这种认识也支撑着这一传统。

sentences.en: But in addition to demand from the domestic market, there was also demand for forest products from overseas.
sentences.zh: 但除了国内市场的需求之外，海外对林产品也有需求。

sentences.en: (B) Early explorers recognised the suitability of the tall, straight trunks of the kauri for constructing sailing vessels.
sentences.zh: 早期探险者认识到，贝壳杉高大笔直的树干很适合用来建造帆船。

sentences.en: The kauri is a species of coniferous tree found only in small areas of the southern hemisphere.
sentences.zh: 贝壳杉是一种针叶树，仅分布于南半球的小片区域。

sentences.en: So, from the early 1800s, huge amounts of this type of wood were sold to Australia and the UK for that purpose.
sentences.zh: 因此，从十九世纪初起，大量这种木材为此被售往澳大利亚和英国。

sentences.en: For a period, the forestry industry was the country’s major export earner, but the rate of harvest was unsustainable and, by the beginning of the 20th century, indigenous timber exports were rapidly declining.
sentences.zh: 有一段时期，林业是该国主要的出口创汇行业，但采伐速度难以为继，到20世纪初，本土木材出口已迅速下滑。

sentences.en: (C) From the 1940s, newly established plantations of an imported species of tree called radiata pine supplied timber and other wood products in increasing quantities.
sentences.zh: 从1940年代起，新建立的、种植一种名为辐射松的外来树种的人工林，开始以日益增多的产量供应木材和其他木制品。

sentences.en: By the 1960s, plantation-grown timber was providing most of the country’s sawn-timber needs, especially for construction.
sentences.zh: 到1960年代，人工林木材已能满足该国大部分锯材需求，尤其是建筑用材。

sentences.en: Today, less than two percent of timber is cut from indigenous forests, and almost all of that is used for higher-value end uses such as furniture and fittings.
sentences.zh: 如今，采自原生森林的木材不到2%，且几乎全部用于家具和装修配件等更高价值的终端用途。

sentences.en: As the pine industry developed, it became apparent that this type of wood was also well suited for many uses.
sentences.zh: 随着松木产业的发展，人们逐渐发现这种木材也非常适合多种用途。

sentences.en: It makes excellent pulp*, and is frequently used for posts, poles, furnishings and mouldings, particleboard, fibreboard, and for plywood and ‘engineered’ wood products.
sentences.zh: 它能制成优质纸浆*，并常用于柱子、杆件、家具和线条、刨花板、纤维板，以及胶合板和“工程”木制品。

sentences.en: Pine by-products are used in the chemical and pharmaceutical industries and residues are consumed for fuel.
sentences.zh: 松木副产品被用于化工和制药行业，残余物则被用作燃料。

sentences.en: This amazing versatility has encouraged the development of an integrated forest-products industry which is almost unique in the world.
sentences.zh: 这种惊人的多用途性促成了一个一体化林产品产业的发展，这在世界上几乎是独一无二的。

sentences.en: (D) Exporters of wood products have largely targeted the rapidly growing markets of South and East Asia and Australia.
sentences.zh: 木制品出口商主要瞄准了南亚、东亚和澳大利亚等快速增长的市场。

sentences.en: Eighty percent of exports by value go to only five markets: Japan, Korea, China, the United States and Australia.
sentences.zh: 按价值计算，80%的出口仅流向五个市场：日本、韩国、中国、美国和澳大利亚。

sentences.en: The product mix remains heavily biased towards raw materials, with logs, sawn wood, pulp and paper comprising 75 percent of export value.
sentences.zh: 产品结构仍严重偏向原材料，原木、锯材、纸浆和纸张占出口总值的75%。

sentences.en: However, finished wood products such as panels and furniture components are exported to more than 50 countries.
sentences.zh: 不过，板材和家具部件等成品木制品被出口到50多个国家。

sentences.en: (E) In New Zealand itself, the construction industry is the principal user of solid wood products, servicing around 20,000 new-house starts annually.
sentences.zh: 在新西兰本国，建筑业是实木产品的主要使用者，每年服务于约2万套新房的开工建设。

sentences.en: However, the small size of New Zealand’s population (just over four million), plus its small manufacturing and remanufacturing base, limits the forestry industry’s domestic opportunities.
sentences.zh: 然而，新西兰人口规模偏小（仅四百万出头），加上其制造和再加工基础薄弱，限制了林业在国内的机会。

sentences.en: For the last few years local wood consumption has been around only four million cubic metres.
sentences.zh: 过去几年，本地木材消费量仅在四百万立方米左右。

sentences.en: Accordingly, the development of the export market is the key to the industry’s growth and contribution to the national economy in decades to come.
sentences.zh: 因此，开拓出口市场是该行业在未来数十年实现增长、为国民经济作出贡献的关键。

sentences.en: (F) In 2004, forestry export receipts were about 11 percent of the country’s total export income, their value having increased steadily for ten years, until affected by the exchange fluctuations and shipping costs of recent years.
sentences.zh: 2004年，林业出口收入约占该国出口总收入的11%，其金额已连续十年稳步增长，直到近年受到汇率波动和运输成本的影响。

sentences.en: The forestry industry is New Zealand’s third-largest export sector, generating around $3.3 billion annually from logs and processed wood products.
sentences.zh: 林业是新西兰第三大出口部门，每年从原木和加工木制品中创收约33亿美元。

sentences.en: But it is generally agreed that it is operating well below its capacity and, with the domestic market already at its peak, almost all of the extra wood produced in future will have to be marketed overseas.
sentences.zh: 但人们普遍认为，该行业的运转远未达到其产能，而由于国内市场已达顶峰，未来增产的木材几乎全部都得销往海外。

sentences.en: That presents a major marketing challenge for the industry.
sentences.zh: 这给该行业带来了重大的营销挑战。

sentences.en: (G) Although the export of logs will continue to provide valuable earnings for forest owners, there is broad acceptance that the industry must be based on value-added products in future.
sentences.zh: 尽管原木出口仍将继续为林主带来可观的收入，但人们已广泛接受：该行业未来必须立足于增值产品。

sentences.en: So the industry is investigating various processing, infrastructure and investment strategies with a view to increasing the level of local manufacturing before export.
sentences.zh: 因此，该行业正在研究各种加工、基础设施和投资策略，以期在出口前提高本地加工的水平。

sentences.en: The keys to future success will depend on a variety of factors — better international marketing, product innovation, internationally competitive processing, improved infrastructure and a suitable political, regulatory and investment environment.
sentences.zh: 未来成功的关键将取决于多种因素——更好的国际营销、产品创新、具有国际竞争力的加工、改善的基础设施，以及适宜的政治、监管和投资环境。

sentences.en: The industry claims that, given the right conditions, by 2025 the forestry sector could be the country’s biggest export earner, generating $20 billion a year and employing 60,000 people.
sentences.zh: 该行业声称，在条件具备的情况下，到2025年林业部门有望成为该国最大的出口创汇行业，每年创收200亿美元，雇用6万人。

sentences.en: (H) One competitive advantage that New Zealand has is its ability to source large quantities of softwood from renewable forests.
sentences.zh: 新西兰拥有的一项竞争优势，是它能够从可再生森林中获取大量软木。

sentences.en: Consumers in several key wood markets are becoming more worried about sustainability, and the industry is supporting the development of national standards as well as the recognition of these internationally.
sentences.zh: 几个主要木材市场的消费者越来越关注可持续性问题，该行业正支持制定国家标准并推动这些标准获得国际认可。

sentences.en: However, New Zealand is not the only country with a plantation-style forestry industry; Chile, Brazil, Argentina, South Africa and Australia all have extensive plantings of fast-growing species (hardwood and softwood), and in the northern hemisphere, Scandinavian countries have all expanded their forests or controlled their use in the interests of future production.
sentences.zh: 然而，新西兰并非唯一拥有人工林式林业的国家；智利、巴西、阿根廷、南非和澳大利亚都大面积种植了速生树种（硬木和软木），而在北半球，斯堪的纳维亚各国也都为了未来生产而扩大森林或控制其利用。

sentences.en: (I) Finally, in addition to competition from other wood producers, New Zealand faces competition from goods such as wood substitutes.
sentences.zh: 最后，除了来自其他木材生产国的竞争之外，新西兰还面临着木材替代品等商品的竞争。

sentences.en: These include steel framing for houses.
sentences.zh: 这些替代品包括房屋的钢制框架。

sentences.en: This further underlines the necessity for globally competitive production and marketing strategies.
sentences.zh: 这进一步凸显了制定具有全球竞争力的生产和营销策略的必要性。
