sentences.en: (A) Katherine Mansfield Beauchamp Murry was born in 1888, into a prominent family in Wellington, New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳·曼斯菲尔德·博尚·默里于1888年出生在新西兰惠灵顿的一个名门之家。

sentences.en: She became one of New Zealand's best-known writers, using the pen name of Katherine Mansfield.
sentences.zh: 她以笔名凯瑟琳·曼斯菲尔德成为新西兰最知名的作家之一。

sentences.en: The daughter of a banker, and born into a middle-class family, she was also a first cousin of Countess Elizabeth von Arnim, a distinguished novelist in her time.
sentences.zh: 她是一位银行家的女儿，生于一个中产阶级家庭，还是伊丽莎白·冯·阿尼姆伯爵夫人的堂姐妹，后者是当时一位杰出的小说家。

sentences.en: Mansfield had two older sisters and a younger brother.
sentences.zh: 曼斯菲尔德有两个姐姐和一个弟弟。

sentences.en: Her father, Harold Beauchamp, went on to become the chairman of the Bank of New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 她的父亲哈罗德·博尚后来成为新西兰银行的董事长。

sentences.en: In 1893, the Mansfield family moved to Karori, a suburb of Wellington, where Mansfield would spend the happiest years of her childhood; she later used her memories of this time as an inspiration for her Prelude story.
sentences.zh: 1893年，曼斯菲尔德一家搬到惠灵顿郊区的卡罗里，曼斯菲尔德在那里度过了童年最快乐的时光；后来她把这段时光的回忆当作灵感，写成了短篇小说《序曲》。

sentences.en: (B) Her first published stories appeared in the High School Reporter and the Wellington Girls' High School magazine in 1898 and 1899.
sentences.zh: 她最早发表的小说，于1898年和1899年分别刊登在《中学记者》和惠灵顿女子中学的校刊上。

sentences.en: In 1902, she developed strong feelings for a musician who played the cello, Arnold Trowell, although her feelings were not, for the most part, returned.
sentences.zh: 1902年，她对一位拉大提琴的音乐家阿诺德·特罗韦尔萌生了强烈的爱意，尽管这份感情大多没有得到回应。

sentences.en: Mansfield herself was an accomplished cellist, having received lessons from Trowell's father.
sentences.zh: 曼斯菲尔德本人是一位造诣颇深的大提琴手，曾师从特罗韦尔的父亲。

sentences.en: Mansfield wrote in her journals of feeling isolated to some extent in New Zealand, and, in general terms, of her interest in the Maori people (New Zealand's native people), who were often portrayed in a sympathetic light in her later stories, such as How Pearl Button Was Kidnapped.
sentences.zh: 曼斯菲尔德在日记中写到自己在新西兰多少感到孤立，并大体写到她对毛利人（新西兰的原住民）的兴趣，毛利人在她后来的小说中常以充满同情的笔触加以刻画，例如《珍珠·巴顿是如何被拐走的》。

sentences.en: (C) She moved to London in 1903, where she attended Queen's College, along with her two sisters.
sentences.zh: 1903年，她迁居伦敦，与两个姐姐一同就读于女王学院。

sentences.en: Mansfield recommenced playing the cello, an occupation that she believed, during her time at Queen's, she would take up professionally.
sentences.zh: 曼斯菲尔德重新拉起了大提琴，在女王学院期间，她一度认为自己会以此为职业。

sentences.en: She also began contributing to the college newspaper, with such a dedication to it that she eventually became its editor.
sentences.zh: 她还开始为学院的报纸供稿，由于投入之深，她最终成了这份报纸的编辑。

sentences.en: She was particularly interested in the works of the French writers of this period and in the 19th century British writer, Oscar Wilde, and she was appreciated amongst fellow students at Queen's for her lively and charismatic approach to life and work.
sentences.zh: 她对这一时期法国作家的作品，以及19世纪英国作家奥斯卡·王尔德尤感兴趣，在女王学院的同学中，她因对生活和学业那种活泼而富有魅力的态度而备受赏识。

sentences.en: She met fellow writer Ida Baker, a South African, at the college, and the pair became lifelong friends.
sentences.zh: 她在学院结识了同样从事写作的南非人艾达·贝克，两人成了终生的挚友。

sentences.en: Mansfield did not actively support the suffragette movement in the UK.
sentences.zh: 曼斯菲尔德并未积极支持英国的妇女参政运动。

sentences.en: Women in New Zealand had gained the right to vote in 1893.
sentences.zh: 新西兰的妇女早在1893年就已获得了选举权。

sentences.en: (D) Mansfield first began journeying into other parts of Europe in the period 1903–1906, mainly to Belgium and Germany.
sentences.zh: 1903年至1906年间，曼斯菲尔德开始首次前往欧洲其他地区游历，主要是比利时和德国。

sentences.en: After finishing her schooling in England, she returned to her New Zealand home in 1906, only then beginning to write short stories in a serious way.
sentences.zh: 在英格兰完成学业后，她于1906年返回新西兰的家，直到那时才开始认真地写作短篇小说。

sentences.en: She had several works published in Australia in a magazine called The Native Companion, which was her first paid writing work, and by this time she had her mind set on becoming a professional writer.
sentences.zh: 她有几篇作品在澳大利亚一本名为《本土伙伴》的杂志上发表，这是她第一份有稿酬的写作，到这时她已下定决心要成为一名职业作家。

sentences.en: It was also the first occasion on which she used the pseudonym “K.
sentences.zh: 这也是她第一次使用化名“K.

sentences.en: Mansfield”.
sentences.zh: 曼斯菲尔德”。

sentences.en: Mansfield rapidly grew discontented with the provincial New Zealand lifestyle, and with her family.
sentences.zh: 曼斯菲尔德很快就对新西兰那种偏狭闭塞的生活方式，以及对自己的家庭感到不满。

sentences.en: Two years later she headed again to London.
sentences.zh: 两年后，她再度动身前往伦敦。

sentences.en: Her father sent her an annual subsidy of £100 for the rest of her life.
sentences.zh: 她的父亲在她的余生里每年寄给她100英镑的津贴。

sentences.en: In later years, she would express both admiration and disdain for New Zealand in her journals.
sentences.zh: 在后来的岁月里，她会在日记中既流露出对新西兰的赞赏，又流露出对它的鄙夷。

sentences.en: (E) In 1911, Mansfield met John Middleton Murry, the Oxford scholar and editor of the literary magazine Rhythm.
sentences.zh: 1911年，曼斯菲尔德结识了约翰·米德尔顿·默里，他是牛津学者，也是文学杂志《节奏》的编辑。

sentences.en: They were later to marry in 1918.
sentences.zh: 两人后来于1918年结为夫妻。

sentences.en: Mansfield became a co-editor of Rhythm, which was subsequently called The Blue Review, in which more of her works were published.
sentences.zh: 曼斯菲尔德成了《节奏》的联合编辑，这本杂志后来更名为《蓝色评论》，她有更多作品在上面发表。

sentences.en: She and Murry lived in various houses in England and briefly in Paris.
sentences.zh: 她和默里在英格兰住过多处房子，还曾在巴黎短暂居住。

sentences.en: The Blue Review failed to gain enough readers and was no longer published.
sentences.zh: 《蓝色评论》未能赢得足够的读者，最终停刊。

sentences.en: Their attempt to set up as writers in Paris was cut short by Murry's bankruptcy, which resulted from the failure of this and other journals.
sentences.zh: 他们想在巴黎以写作为生的尝试，因默里破产而中断，而破产正是这本杂志及其他刊物失败所致。

sentences.en: Life back in England meant frequently changed addresses and very limited funds.
sentences.zh: 回到英格兰的生活，意味着频繁地搬家和极为有限的钱财。

sentences.en: (F) Between 1915 and 1918, Mansfield moved between England and Bandol, France.
sentences.zh: 1915年至1918年间，曼斯菲尔德往返于英格兰与法国的邦多勒之间。

sentences.en: She and Murry developed close contact with other well-known writers of the time such as D.
sentences.zh: 她和默里与当时其他知名作家结下了密切的交往，例如D.

sentences.en: H.
sentences.zh: H.

sentences.en: Lawrence, Bertrand Russell and Aldous Huxley.
sentences.zh: 劳伦斯、伯特兰·罗素和奥尔德斯·赫胥黎。

sentences.en: By October 1918 Mansfield had become seriously ill; she had been diagnosed with tuberculosis and was advised to enter a sanatorium.
sentences.zh: 到1918年10月，曼斯菲尔德已病得很重；她被诊断出患有肺结核，并被建议住进疗养院。

sentences.en: She could no longer spend winters in London.
sentences.zh: 她再也无法在伦敦过冬了。

sentences.en: In the autumn of 1918 she was so ill that she decided to go to Ospedaletti in Italy.
sentences.zh: 1918年秋天，她病得很重，于是决定前往意大利的奥斯佩达莱蒂。

sentences.en: It was the publication of Bliss and Other Stories in 1920 that was to solidify Mansfield's reputation as a writer.
sentences.zh: 正是1920年《幸福及其他故事》的出版，奠定了曼斯菲尔德作为作家的声誉。

sentences.en: Mansfield also spent time in Menton, France, as the tenant of her father's cousin at “The Villa Isola Bella”.
sentences.zh: 曼斯菲尔德还在法国芒通住过一段时间，作为父亲堂亲的租客，住在“伊索拉贝拉别墅”里。

sentences.en: There she wrote eight stories including Miss Brill and The Daughters of the Late Colonel, the latter of which she pronounced to be “…the only story that satisfies me to any extent”.
sentences.zh: 她在那里写了八篇小说，包括《布里尔小姐》和《已故上校的女儿们》，后者她称之为“……唯一一篇在某种程度上让我感到满意的小说”。

sentences.en: (G) Mansfield produced a great deal of work in the final years of her life, and much of her prose and poetry remained unpublished at her death in 1923.
sentences.zh: 曼斯菲尔德在生命的最后几年创作了大量作品，到她1923年去世时，她的许多散文和诗歌仍未发表。

sentences.en: After her death, her husband, Murry, took on the task of editing and publishing her works.
sentences.zh: 她去世后，她的丈夫默里担起了编辑和出版她作品的任务。

sentences.en: His efforts resulted in two additional volumes of short stories, The Doves' Nest and Something Childish, published in 1923 and 1924 respectively; the publication of her Poems; as well as a collection of critical writings (Novels and Novelists) and a number of editions of Mansfield's previously unpublished letters and journals.
sentences.zh: 他的努力促成了另外两部短篇小说集《鸽巢》和《稚气未脱》分别于1923年和1924年出版；促成了她的《诗集》问世；还促成了一部评论文集（《小说与小说家》）以及若干版曼斯菲尔德此前未曾发表的书信与日记的出版。

sentences.en: (A) The first plastics were developed as a substitute for natural rubber.
sentences.zh: 最早的塑料是作为天然橡胶的替代品而研制出来的。

sentences.en: Chemically, rubber is a polymer—a compound containing large molecules that are formed by the bonding of many smaller, simpler units, repeated over and over again.
sentences.zh: 从化学角度看，橡胶是一种聚合物——一种含有大分子的化合物，这些大分子由许多更小、更简单的单元一再重复键合而成。

sentences.en: The same bonding principle—polymerization—is the basis of the creation of a huge range of plastics by the chemical industry.
sentences.zh: 同样的键合原理——聚合反应——是化工行业制造种类繁多的塑料的基础。

sentences.en: The first plastic was developed as a result of a competition in the USA.
sentences.zh: 第一种塑料是美国一场竞赛的产物。

sentences.en: In the 1860s, $10,000 was offered to anybody who could replace ivory—supplies of which were declining—with something equally good as a material for making billiard balls.
sentences.zh: 在1860年代，有人悬赏1万美元，奖给任何能用一种同样好的材料替代象牙来制作台球的人——当时象牙的供应正日益减少。

sentences.en: The prize was won by John Wesley Hyatt, with a material called celluloid.
sentences.zh: 这笔奖金被约翰·韦斯利·海厄特凭借一种名为赛璐珞的材料赢得。

sentences.en: Celluloid was made by dissolving cellulose, a carbohydrate obtained from plants, in a solution of camphor dissolved in ethanol.
sentences.zh: 赛璐珞的制法是，把从植物中获得的碳水化合物纤维素，溶解在樟脑溶于乙醇而成的溶液里。

sentences.en: This new material rapidly found other applications in the manufacture of everyday products such as knife handles and detachable collars and cuffs.
sentences.zh: 这种新材料很快在制造刀柄、可拆卸的衣领和袖口等日用品方面找到了其他用途。

sentences.en: But perhaps the best-known celluloid product was photographic film, without which the film industry could never have taken off at the end of the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 但赛璐珞最著名的产品也许要数胶卷，没有它，电影业绝不可能在19世纪末蓬勃兴起。

sentences.en: (B) Celluloid can be repeatedly softened and reshaped by heat, and is known as a thermoplastic.
sentences.zh: 赛璐珞可以被加热反复软化并重新塑形，被称为热塑性塑料。

sentences.en: In 1907, Leo Baekeland (1863–1944), a Belgian chemist working in the USA, invented a different kind of plastic by causing phenol and formaldehyde to react together.
sentences.zh: 1907年，在美国工作的比利时化学家利奥·贝克兰（1863—1944）通过使苯酚和甲醛发生反应，发明了一种不同的塑料。

sentences.en: Baekeland called it Bakelite, and it was the first of the thermosets—plastics that can be cast and moulded while hot, but cannot be softened by heat and reshaped once they have set.
sentences.zh: 贝克兰把它称为酚醛塑料，它是最早的热固性塑料——这类塑料可以在受热时浇铸和模塑，但一旦定型，就无法再用热软化并重新塑形。

sentences.en: Bakelite was a good insulator, and was resistant to water and acid.
sentences.zh: 酚醛塑料是良好的绝缘体，并且耐水耐酸。

sentences.en: With these properties it was soon being used in the manufacture of electrical switches as well as a variety of domestic items.
sentences.zh: 凭借这些特性，它很快被用于制造电气开关以及各种家用物品。

sentences.en: (C) As the century went on, the range of newly developed plastics increased.
sentences.zh: 随着这个世纪的推进，新研制出的塑料种类不断增多。

sentences.en: Chemists began looking for other small molecules that could be strung together to make polymers.
sentences.zh: 化学家们开始寻找其他能够串联起来制成聚合物的小分子。

sentences.en: In the 1930s, chemists in Britain discovered that the gas ethylene would polymerize under heat and pressure to form a thermoplastic they called polythene.
sentences.zh: 在1930年代，英国的化学家发现，乙烯气体在加热加压下会聚合，形成一种他们称为聚乙烯的热塑性塑料。

sentences.en: Polypropylene followed in the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 聚丙烯在1950年代随之问世。

sentences.en: Both are used to make bottles, pipes and plastic bags.
sentences.zh: 两者都被用来制造瓶子、管材和塑料袋。

sentences.en: A small change in the starting material—replacing a hydrogen atom in ethylene with a chlorine atom—produced rigid PVC (polyvinyl chloride), a fireproof plastic suitable for drains and gutters.
sentences.zh: 起始原料上的一个小改动——把乙烯中的一个氢原子换成一个氯原子——制成了硬质PVC（聚氯乙烯），这是一种适用于排水管和檐槽的阻燃塑料。

sentences.en: By adding certain chemicals, a soft form of PVC can be produced, suitable as a substitute for rubber in items such as waterproof clothing.
sentences.zh: 通过添加某些化学品，可以制成一种软质PVC，适合在防水服等物品中替代橡胶。

sentences.en: A closely related plastic is Teflon or PTFE (polytetrafluoroethylene).
sentences.zh: 一种与之密切相关的塑料是特氟龙，即PTFE（聚四氟乙烯）。

sentences.en: It produces very little friction, making it ideal for products such as non-stick frying pans.
sentences.zh: 它产生的摩擦力极小，因此非常适合用于不粘煎锅之类的产品。

sentences.en: (D) Polystyrene, a hard, clear material like glass, was developed during the 1930s in Germany, and its applications included food containers and toys.
sentences.zh: 聚苯乙烯是一种像玻璃一样坚硬、透明的材料，于1930年代在德国研制成功，其用途包括食品容器和玩具。

sentences.en: Expanded polystyrene is rigid and is widely used in packaging and insulation.
sentences.zh: 发泡聚苯乙烯质地坚硬，被广泛用于包装和保温隔热。

sentences.en: Polyurethane, developed in the same country, was commonly produced as a foam, which was very useful in the production of insulating materials.
sentences.zh: 聚氨酯也是在这个国家研制出来的，通常被制成泡沫，在生产保温隔热材料方面非常有用。

sentences.en: (E) In the 1930s, the first of the man-made fibres was created—nylon.
sentences.zh: 在1930年代，第一种人造纤维诞生了——尼龙。

sentences.en: Its inventor was a chemist called Wallace Carothers (1896–1937), who worked for the Du Pont company in the USA.
sentences.zh: 它的发明者是一位名叫华莱士·卡罗瑟斯（1896—1937）的化学家，他在美国的杜邦公司工作。

sentences.en: He found that under the right conditions two particular chemicals would form a polymer that could be pumped out through holes and then stretched to form long glossy threads that could be woven like silk.
sentences.zh: 他发现，在适当条件下，两种特定的化学物质会形成一种聚合物，这种聚合物可以通过小孔挤出，再拉伸成又长又有光泽的丝线，能像蚕丝一样织成织物。

sentences.en: Its first use was to make parachutes for the US armed forces in World War II.
sentences.zh: 它最初的用途是在第二次世界大战中为美军制造降落伞。

sentences.en: In the postwar years, it completely replaced silk in the manufacture of stockings.
sentences.zh: 在战后的岁月里，它在长袜制造中完全取代了蚕丝。

sentences.en: Many other synthetic fibres joined nylon, including Orlon, Acrilan, and Terylene.
sentences.zh: 许多其他合成纤维也加入了尼龙的行列，包括奥纶、阿克利纶和涤纶。

sentences.en: Today most garments are made of a blend of natural fibres, such as cotton and wool, and man-made fibres that make fabrics easier to look after.
sentences.zh: 如今，大多数衣物都由天然纤维（如棉和羊毛）与人造纤维混纺而成，人造纤维使织物更易于打理。

sentences.en: (F) Despite its enormous usefulness, plastic has its drawbacks.
sentences.zh: 尽管塑料用途极广，它也有自身的缺点。

sentences.en: In fact, one of its great strengths—its indestructibility—is its greatest disadvantage.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它的一大优点——坚不可摧——恰恰是它最大的缺点。

sentences.en: Beaches all over the world, even on the remotest island, are littered with plastic bottles that nothing can destroy.
sentences.zh: 世界各地的海滩，乃至最偏远的岛屿，都散落着无法被任何东西毁掉的塑料瓶。

sentences.en: Nor is it very easy to recycle plastics, as different types of plastic are often found in the same items and call for different treatments.
sentences.zh: 回收塑料也并不容易，因为不同类型的塑料常常出现在同一件物品中，需要不同的处理方法。

sentences.en: Plastics can be made biodegradable by incorporating into their structure a material such as starch, which is attacked by bacteria and causes the plastic to fall apart.
sentences.zh: 通过在塑料结构中掺入淀粉之类的材料，可以使塑料具有生物可降解性，淀粉会受到细菌的侵蚀，从而使塑料散碎解体。

sentences.en: Other materials can be incorporated that gradually decay in sunlight—although bottles made of such materials have to be stored in the dark, to ensure they do not disintegrate before they have been used.
sentences.zh: 也可以掺入另一些会在阳光下逐渐分解的材料——不过，用这类材料制成的瓶子必须避光存放，以确保它们在使用之前不会解体。

records.title: The extinction of the cave bear

sentences.en: (A) Hervé Bocherens, an evolutionary biologist at the University of Tübingen, Germany, says his colleagues find his research methods a little 'crude'.
sentences.zh: 德国蒂宾根大学的进化生物学家埃尔韦·博什朗斯（Hervé Bocherens）说，他的同事们觉得他的研究方法有点“粗暴”。

sentences.en: He dissolves 30,000-year-old animal bones in hydrochloric acid, which is strong enough to burn through metal, soaks the bone solution in lye, cooks it at about 200 degrees Fahrenheit and freeze-dries it, until what's left is a speck of powder weighing less than one one-hundredth of an ounce.
sentences.zh: 他把 30000 年前的动物骨头溶解在盐酸里——盐酸的腐蚀性足以烧穿金属——再把骨头溶液浸泡在碱液中、以约 200 华氏度（约 93 摄氏度）烹煮、再冷冻干燥，直到剩下的是一小撮不到 1 盎司百分之一重的粉末。

sentences.en: The method may be harsh, but the yield is precious – the biography of a cave bear as told through its chemical components.
sentences.zh: 方法或许严苛，但所得却很宝贵——通过其化学成分讲述的一头穴熊的生平。

sentences.en: Bocherens is at the forefront of research on the bear, a European species that died out 25,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 博什朗斯处于对这种 25000 年前绝灭的欧洲熊种研究的最前沿。

sentences.en: People have been excavating cave bear remains for hundreds of years— in the Middle Ages, the massive skulls were attributed to dragons — but the past decade has seen a burst of discoveries about how the bears lived and why they became extinct.
sentences.zh: 人们挖掘穴熊遗骸已经几百年了——中世纪时，那些巨大的头骨被认为是龙的——但过去十年里，关于这些熊如何生活、为何灭绝的新发现集中涌现。

sentences.en: An abundance of bones has been found from Spain to Romania in caves where the animals once hibernated.
sentences.zh: 从西班牙到罗马尼亚，在这些动物曾经冬眠的洞穴中已经发现了大量骨骼。

sentences.en: 'Caves are good places to preserve bones, and cave bears had the good sense to die there,' Bocherens says.
sentences.zh: “洞穴是保存骨头的好地方，而穴熊很有自知之明，选择死在那里，”博什朗斯说。

sentences.en: (B) Along with mammoths, lions and woolly rhinos, cave bears (Ursus spelaeus) were once among Europe's most impressive creatures.
sentences.zh: 与猛犸象、狮子和披毛犀一起，穴熊（Ursus spelaeus）曾是欧洲最令人印象深刻的动物之一。

sentences.en: Males weighed up to 1,500 pounds, 50 per cent more than the largest modern grizzly bears.
sentences.zh: 雄性体重可达 1500 磅，比现代最大的灰熊还要重 50%。

sentences.en: Cave bears had wider heads than today's bears, and powerful shoulders and forelimbs.
sentences.zh: 穴熊头部比今天的熊更宽，肩膀和前肢也很强健。

sentences.en: But the relationship between humans and cave bears has been mysterious.
sentences.zh: 但人与穴熊之间的关系一直颇为神秘。

sentences.en: Were humans prey for the bears, or predators?
sentences.zh: 人类是穴熊的猎物，还是它们的猎手？

sentences.en: Were bears the object of worship or fear?
sentences.zh: 熊是崇拜的对象，还是恐惧的对象？

sentences.en: (C) Initially cave bears shared the continent of Europe, more than 100,000 years ago, with Neanderthals, a primitive species of humans.
sentences.zh: 起初，穴熊与一种原始人类——尼安德特人——共同生活在 10 万多年前的欧洲大陆上。

sentences.en: Modern humans arrived in Europe about 40,000 years ago, and were soon aware of the bears.
sentences.zh: 现代人类大约在 4 万年前到达欧洲，很快就意识到了这些熊的存在。

sentences.en: They painted images of the animals on cave walls, and carved their likeness in fragments of mammoth tusk.
sentences.zh: 他们把这些动物的形象画在洞壁上，并在猛犸象牙的碎片上刻出它们的形象。

sentences.en: The walls of France's Chauvet cave are painted with lions, hyenas and bears; dating back 32,000 years, these are perhaps the oldest paintings in the world.
sentences.zh: 法国肖维洞（Chauvet cave）的洞壁上绘有狮、鬣狗和熊；这些画距今 32000 年，或许是世界上最古老的绘画。

sentences.en: The painters weren't the cave's only occupants: the floor is covered with 150 cave bear skeletons, and its soft clay still holds paw prints.
sentences.zh: 画家并不是这座洞穴的唯一居民：洞底铺着 150 具穴熊骨架，柔软的黏土中至今仍留有掌印。

sentences.en: Most dramatically, a cave bear skull was perched on a stone slab in the center of one chamber, placed deliberately by some long-gone cave inhabitant.
sentences.zh: 最具戏剧性的是，一个穴熊的头骨被摆放在洞中一处石板上，显然是由某位早已逝去的洞穴居民有意放置在那里。

sentences.en: 'There's no way to tell if it was just curiosity that made someone put a skull on the rock, or if it had religious significance,' says Bocherens.
sentences.zh: “我们无法判断把头骨摆到石头上的人只是出于好奇，还是这有宗教意义，”博什朗斯说。

sentences.en: (D) Another discovery, hundreds of miles to the east of Chauvet, would shed light on the relationship between cave bears and humans.
sentences.zh: 在肖维洞以东数百英里的另一项发现，将照亮穴熊与人类之间的关系。

sentences.en: The Swabian Jura is a limestone plateau in southwestern Germany that is riddled with caves.
sentences.zh: 施瓦本汝拉（Swabian Jura）是德国西南部一处石灰岩台地，到处是洞穴。

sentences.en: A steel gate guards the Hohle Fels cave from vandals and curiosity-seekers.
sentences.zh: 一道钢制大门把霍勒费尔斯洞（Hohle Fels）与破坏者和好奇人隔开。

sentences.en: Floodlights in the cave's main chamber illuminate the ceiling, vaulted like a cathedral above 5,000 square feet of floor space.
sentences.zh: 洞内主厅的泛光灯照亮了像大教堂穹顶一样的天花板，覆盖着 5000 平方英尺的地面空间。

sentences.en: Long ago, as shown by the bones and tools that archaeologists have found, cave bears and human beings sought shelter here from winter weather.
sentences.zh: 考古学家发现的骨骼和工具表明，很久以前，穴熊和人类都曾在这里躲避冬季的天气。

sentences.en: In 2000, University of Tübingen paleobiologist Susanne Münzel unearthed a bear vertebra with a tiny triangular piece of flint embedded in it.
sentences.zh: 2000 年，蒂宾根大学古生物学家苏珊·明策尔（Susanne Münzel）发掘出一块熊脊椎，其上嵌有一块小小的三角形燧石。

sentences.en: The flint was likely a broken spear point, hard evidence of a successful bear hunt 29,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 这块燧石很可能是一只折断的矛头——一次 29000 年前成功的猎熊行动的硬证据。

sentences.en: Münzel also found bear bones that had clearly been scraped by stone tools.
sentences.zh: 明策尔还发现了一些熊骨，骨上明显有石器刮过的痕迹。

sentences.en: Evidence for bears being a food source for early humans was shown by cut marks on skulls and leg bones where the flesh had been cut away.
sentences.zh: 早期人类把熊作为食物来源的证据，体现在头骨和腿骨上把肉切下来留下的切痕。

sentences.en: Many of the bones were from baby bears, perhaps caught while hibernating.
sentences.zh: 许多骨头来自幼熊——也许是它们在冬眠时被捕获的。

sentences.en: (E) Cave bears disappeared not long after humans spread throughout Europe, and one theory is that hunting led to the bears' extinction.
sentences.zh: 在人类遍布欧洲后不久，穴熊就消失了；一种理论认为，狩猎导致了熊的灭绝。

sentences.en: Hervé Bocherens' test tubes may hold the clues.
sentences.zh: 埃尔韦·博什朗斯的试管里也许藏有线索。

sentences.en: Running his white powder through a mass spectrometer, he identifies different isotopes, or chemical forms, of elements such as carbon and nitrogen that reflect what the bears were eating and how quickly they grew.
sentences.zh: 他把自己手里的白色粉末通过质谱仪，识别出碳、氮等元素的不同同位素，即不同化学形式——这些反映出熊吃什么、长得多快。

sentences.en: After studying hundreds of bones from dozens of sites in Europe, Bocherens has found that cave bears ate mainly plants.
sentences.zh: 在研究了欧洲数十处遗址数百块骨头之后，博什朗斯发现穴熊主要吃植物。

sentences.en: This would have made bears particularly vulnerable to the last Ice Age, which began around 30,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 这会让熊在大约 3 万年前开始的最后一次冰期面前格外脆弱。

sentences.en: This Ice Age shortened or eliminated growing seasons, and altered the distributions of plant species across Europe.
sentences.zh: 这次冰期缩短甚至消除了生长季，并改变了欧洲植物物种的分布。

sentences.en: Cave bears began to move from their old territories, according to a DNA analysis of teeth found near the Danube River.
sentences.zh: 根据多瑙河附近发现的牙齿 DNA 分析，穴熊开始离开它们的旧领地。

sentences.en: The cave bear population there was relatively stable, with the same genetic patterns showing up generation after generation.
sentences.zh: 在那里，穴熊种群相对稳定，同样的遗传谱型在世代间反复出现。

sentences.en: But about 28,000 years ago, newcomers with different DNA patterns arrived — a possible sign of hungry bears suddenly on the move.
sentences.zh: 但大约 28000 年前，带有不同 DNA 谱型的“新来者”出现了——这或许是饥饿的熊突然迁徙的迹象。

sentences.en: (F) But changes in the climate can't be solely to blame for the bears' extinction.
sentences.zh: 但气候变化不能成为穴熊灭绝的唯一责任。

sentences.en: According to the latest study, by Erik Trinkaus and his colleagues at the Max Planck Institute, cave bear populations began a long, slow decline 50,000 years ago — well before the climate began to change.
sentences.zh: 根据马克斯·普朗克研究所（Max Planck Institute）的埃里克·特林考斯（Erik Trinkaus）及其同事的最新研究，穴熊种群在 5 万年前——远在气候开始变化之前——就已开始了长期、缓慢的衰退。

sentences.en: The new study supports a different explanation for the cave bears' demise.
sentences.zh: 这项新研究为穴熊的消亡提供了另一种解释。

sentences.en: As Neanderthals, and then a growing population of modern humans moved into the caves of Europe, cave bears had fewer safe places to hibernate.
sentences.zh: 随着尼安德特人——以及随后日益增长的现代人群——迁入欧洲的洞穴，穴熊可供冬眠的安全场所越来越少。

sentences.en: An acute housing shortage may have been the final blow for these magnificent beasts.
sentences.zh: 严重的“住房短缺”或许就是这些壮丽生灵所遭受的最后一击。

sentences.en: (A) What is today a simple children's toy has a surprisingly rich history.
sentences.zh: 今天的一件简单儿童玩具，却有着出人意料的丰富历史。

sentences.en: Dolls have been a part of humankind for thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 玩偶已经成为人类生活的一部分长达数千年。

sentences.en: Often depicting religious figures, or used as playthings, early dolls were probably made from primitive materials such as clay, fur, or wood.
sentences.zh: 早期玩偶常被用作宗教人物的形象，或作为玩物，多由黏土、皮毛或木头等原始材料制成。

sentences.en: Dolls constructed of flat pieces of wood, painted with various designs, and with 'hair' made of clay, have often been found in Egyptian graves dating back to 2000 BC.
sentences.zh: 由扁平木片拼成、表面绘有各种图案、用黏土做“头发”的玩偶，常在可追溯至公元前 2000 年的埃及墓葬中被发现。

sentences.en: Egyptian tombs of wealthy families have included pottery dolls.
sentences.zh: 富裕家庭的埃及墓葬中也曾出土陶制玩偶。

sentences.en: Dolls being placed in these graves leads some to believe that they were cherished possessions.
sentences.zh: 玩偶被放入这些墓葬，让一些人相信它们是受珍视的物品。

sentences.en: Girls from ancient Greece and Rome offered their wooden dolls to goddesses after they were too 'grown-up' to play with dolls.
sentences.zh: 古希腊和古罗马的女孩当年龄大到不再适合玩玩偶时，会把自己的木制玩偶献给女神。

sentences.en: Most ancient dolls that were found in tombs were very simple creations, often made from such materials as clay, rags, wood, or bone.
sentences.zh: 出土于墓葬的大多数古代玩偶都是非常简单的制品，常用黏土、布头、木头或骨头等材料制成。

sentences.en: Some of the more unique dolls were made with ivory or wax.
sentences.zh: 一些更独特的玩偶则用象牙或蜡制成。

sentences.en: The main goal was to make the doll as lifelike as possible.
sentences.zh: 主要的目标是让玩偶尽可能逼真。

sentences.en: That ideal led to the creation of dolls with movable limbs and removable garments, dating back to 600 BC.
sentences.zh: 这一理念催生了带有可活动肢体和可拆卸服装的玩偶，最早可追溯至公元前 600 年。

sentences.en: (B) Following the era of the ancient dolls, Europe became a major hub for doll production.
sentences.zh: 在古代玩偶时代之后，欧洲成为玩偶生产的重要枢纽。

sentences.en: These dolls were primarily made of wood.
sentences.zh: 这些玩偶主要由木头制成。

sentences.en: Fewer than 30 examples of primitive wooden stump dolls from England survive today.
sentences.zh: 如今英格兰存世的原始木桩玩偶不足 30 件。

sentences.en: The Grodnertal area of Germany produced many peg wooden dolls, a type of doll that has very simple peg joints and resembles a clothespin (a device for hanging washing on a clothesline).
sentences.zh: 德国的格罗德纳尔（Grodnertal）地区生产了大量插销木偶，这类玩偶的关节非常简单，外形类似晾衣夹（一种用以把衣物挂在晒衣绳上的装置）。

sentences.en: An alternative to wood was developed in the 1800s.
sentences.zh: 19 世纪发展出一种替代木头的材料。

sentences.en: 'Composition' is a collective term for mixtures of pulped wood or paper that were used to make doll heads and bodies.
sentences.zh: “composition”（合成料）是一个统称，指用木浆或纸浆混合而成、用来制作玩偶的头部和身体的材料。

sentences.en: These mixtures were moulded under pressure, creating a durable doll that could be mass-produced.
sentences.zh: 这些混合料在压力下模制成型，可制成耐用、可批量生产的玩偶。

sentences.en: Manufacturers closely guarded the recipes for their mixtures, sometimes using strange ingredients like ash or eggshells.
sentences.zh: 制造商对其配方守口如瓶，有时会使用灰烬或蛋壳等奇怪原料。

sentences.en: Papier-mâché, a type of composition, was one of the most popular mixtures.
sentences.zh: 纸浆塑形料（papier-mâché）作为合成料的一种，是当时最受欢迎的混合料之一。

sentences.en: (C) In addition to wooden dolls, wax dolls grew in popularity in the 17th and 18th centuries.
sentences.zh: 除了木制玩偶之外，在 17 和 18 世纪，蜡制玩偶的流行度也在上升。

sentences.en: Munich in Germany was a major manufacturing centre for wax dolls.
sentences.zh: 德国慕尼黑是蜡制玩偶的重要制造中心。

sentences.en: Wax dollmakers would model a doll's head in wax or clay, and then cover it with plaster to create a mould.
sentences.zh: 蜡偶工匠会先用蜡或黏土塑出玩偶的头部模型，然后用石膏覆盖以制成模具。

sentences.en: Then they would pour melted wax into the cast.
sentences.zh: 再把熔化的蜡倒入模具中。

sentences.en: The wax for the head would be very thin, no more than 3 mm.
sentences.zh: 头部用蜡极薄，通常不超过 3 毫米。

sentences.en: Some of the most distinctive wax dolls were created in England between 1850 and 1930.
sentences.zh: 在 1850 年至 1930 年间，英格兰制作了一些最有特色的蜡制玩偶。

sentences.en: One of the first dolls that portrayed a baby was made in England from wax at the beginning of the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 最早一批描绘婴儿形象的玩偶之一，是 19 世纪初在英格兰用蜡制成的。

sentences.en: (D) Around the same time, porcelain became popular.
sentences.zh: 大约在同一时期，瓷器开始流行。

sentences.en: It is made by firing special clays in a kiln at more than 2372 degrees Fahrenheit (1300°C), and only a few clays can withstand firing at such high temperatures.
sentences.zh: 它是把特定的黏土在窑中以 2372 华氏度（1300 °C）以上的高温烧制而成，只有少数几种黏土能承受这种高温烧制。

sentences.en: Porcelain is used generically to refer to both china and bisque dolls; china is glazed, whereas bisque is unglazed.
sentences.zh: 瓷（porcelain）一词被笼统地用来指代上釉瓷偶（china）和素瓷偶（bisque）——china 是上釉的，而 bisque 则未上釉。

sentences.en: Germany, France, and Denmark started creating china heads for dolls in the 1840s.
sentences.zh: 德国、法国和丹麦从 1840 年代开始为玩偶制作上釉瓷头。

sentences.en: These china heads were replaced in the 1860s by ones made of bisque.
sentences.zh: 这些上釉瓷头在 1860 年代被素瓷头所取代。

sentences.en: Bisque, which is porcelain fired twice with colour added to it after the first firing, looked more like skin than china did.
sentences.zh: 素瓷（bisque）是经两次烧制、并在首次烧制后加上颜色的瓷器，看起来比 china 更接近肌肤的质感。

sentences.en: In France, the bébé was popular in the 1880s, and it has become a highly sought-after doll today.
sentences.zh: 在法国，bébé 在 1880 年代非常流行，而它今天已成为一种备受追捧的玩偶。

sentences.en: The bébé, first made in the 1850s, was different from its predecessors because it depicted a younger girl.
sentences.zh: bébé 最早制作于 1850 年代，与前辈玩偶的不同之处在于它呈现的是一个年龄较小的女孩形象。

sentences.en: Until then, most French dolls were representations of adults.
sentences.zh: 在那之前，大多数法国玩偶都是成年人的形象。

sentences.en: Although the French dolls were unrivalled in their artistry, German bisque dolls became quite popular because they were not as expensive.
sentences.zh: 尽管在艺术性上，法国玩偶无与伦比，但德国的素瓷玩偶因价格不那么昂贵而相当受欢迎。

sentences.en: Kammer & Reinhardt introduced a bisque character doll in the 1900s, starting a trend of creating realistic dolls.
sentences.zh: 1900 年代，Kammer & Reinhardt 公司推出了一款素瓷角色玩偶，开启了制作写实风格玩偶的潮流。

sentences.en: (E) For many centuries, rag dolls were made by mothers for their children.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，布偶都是母亲为孩子做的。

sentences.en: The term 'rag doll' refers generically to dolls made of any fabric.
sentences.zh: “布偶”（rag doll）一词泛指任何用织物制成的玩偶。

sentences.en: 'Cloth doll' refers to a subset of rag dolls made of linen or cotton.
sentences.zh: “棉布玩偶”（cloth doll）则指用亚麻布或棉布制成的布偶子集。

sentences.en: Commercially produced rag dolls were first introduced in the 1850s by English and American manufacturers.
sentences.zh: 商业生产的布偶在 1850 年代由英国和美国的制造商首次推出。

sentences.en: Although not as sophisticated as dolls made from other materials, rag dolls were well loved, often as a child's first toy.
sentences.zh: 虽然在精致程度上不及用其他材料制成的玩偶，但布偶深受喜爱，常常是儿童的第一件玩具。

sentences.en: (F) Dollmaking did not become an industry in the United States until after the Civil War in the 1860s.
sentences.zh: 在美国，玩偶制造直到 1860 年代南北战争之后才形成产业。

sentences.en: Doll production was concentrated in the New England region of the United States, with dolls made from a variety of materials such as leather, rubber, papier-mâché, and cloth.
sentences.zh: 玩偶生产集中在美国的新英格兰地区，所用材料多样，例如皮革、橡胶、纸浆塑形料和棉布等。

sentences.en: Celluloid was developed in the state of New Jersey in the late 1860s and was used to manufacture dolls until the mid-1950s.
sentences.zh: 赛璐珞（celluloid）在 1860 年代末在新泽西州被研发出来，并被用来制作玩偶，一直延续到 1950 年代中期。

sentences.en: German, French, American, and Japanese factories churned out cheaply produced celluloid dolls in mass quantities.
sentences.zh: 德国、法国、美国和日本的工厂都以廉价方式大规模生产赛璐珞玩偶。

sentences.en: However, celluloid fell out of favour because of its extreme flammability and propensity to fade in bright light.
sentences.zh: 然而，赛璐珞由于极易燃，并在强光下容易褪色，因而逐渐失宠。

sentences.en: (G) After World War I, dollmakers experimented with plastics.
sentences.zh: 第一次世界大战之后，玩偶制造商开始尝试各种塑料。

sentences.en: Hard plastic dolls were manufactured in the 1940s.
sentences.zh: 硬塑料玩偶在 1940 年代被生产出来。

sentences.en: They resembled composition dolls, but they were much more durable.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来类似合成料玩偶，但耐用性强得多。

sentences.en: Other materials used in doll manufacturing included rubber, foam rubber, and vinyl in the 1950s and 1960s.
sentences.zh: 1950 年代和 1960 年代，用于玩偶制造的其他材料还包括橡胶、泡沫橡胶和乙烯基塑料。

sentences.en: Vinyl changed dollmaking, allowing dollmakers to root hair into the head, rather than using wigs or painting the hair.
sentences.zh: 乙烯基塑料改变了玩偶制造，使得制偶者能够把头发直接植入头部，而不再使用假发或在头部上画头发。

sentences.en: Although most dolls are now mass manufactured using these modern materials, many modern dollmakers are still using the traditional materials of the past to make collectible dolls.
sentences.zh: 尽管如今大多数玩偶都采用这些现代材料批量生产，但仍有许多现代制偶师在使用过去的传统材料来制作收藏级玩偶。

records.title: Sleep Study on Modem-Day Hunter-Gatherers Dispels Popular Notions
records.titleZh: 对现代狩猎采集者的睡眠研究推翻了普遍观念

sentences.en: (A) The sleep troubles common in modern life have long been blamed on our industrial society, from the city lights, long work hours and commutes, to caffeine and the Internet.
sentences.zh: 现代生活中常见的睡眠问题，长期以来一直被归咎于我们的工业社会——从城市的灯光、漫长的工作时间和通勤，到咖啡因和互联网。

sentences.en: Sleep researchers often look back on a time when humans were able to get more rest by sleeping and waking to the rhythms of the sun.
sentences.zh: 睡眠研究者常常追忆这样一个时代：那时人类能够顺应太阳的节律入睡和醒来，从而获得更多的休息。

sentences.en: It turns out that this may not be quite right.
sentences.zh: 然而事实证明，这种看法或许并不完全正确。

sentences.en: In fact, our ancestors may not have been getting the recommended eight hours of sleep, either.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们的祖先也未必睡足了推荐的八个小时。

sentences.en: In a recent study, researchers traveled all over the world to examine sleep in some of the world’s last remaining hunter-gatherer societies – the Hadza of Tanzania, the San of Namibia, and the Tsimane of Bolivia.
sentences.zh: 在最近的一项研究中，研究者走遍世界各地，考察了世界上仅存的几个狩猎采集社会的睡眠——坦桑尼亚的哈扎人、纳米比亚的桑人和玻利维亚的齐曼内人。

sentences.en: Cut off from media, electricity and other distractions, these pre-industrial societies are thought to sleep the way humans did more than 10,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 这些前工业社会与媒体、电力和其他干扰相隔绝，人们认为他们的睡眠方式与一万多年前的人类相同。

sentences.en: Traveling to where they lived, often in humid, remote locations, researchers used medical devices to record the sleeping habits of 94 of these tribespeople and ended up collecting data representing 1,165 days.
sentences.zh: 研究者前往他们的居住地——常常是潮湿偏远的地方——用医疗设备记录了其中94名部落成员的睡眠习惯，最终收集到了相当于1165天的数据。

sentences.en: (B) They found very similar sleep patterns despite their geographic isolation.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，尽管这些人在地理上彼此隔绝，睡眠模式却非常相似。

sentences.en: On average, all three groups sleep a little less than 6.5 hours a night, do not take naps, and don’t go to sleep when it gets dark.
sentences.zh: 平均而言，这三个族群每晚睡眠都略少于6.5小时，不午睡，也不在天黑时就去睡觉。

sentences.en: Like many of us, the Hadza, San, and Tsimane spend more time in bed – from 6.9 to 8.5 hours – than they do actually sleeping.
sentences.zh: 和我们许多人一样，哈扎人、桑人和齐曼内人躺在床上的时间——从6.9到8.5小时——比他们实际睡着的时间要长。

sentences.en: This adds up to a sleep efficiency that is very similar to today’s industrial populations.
sentences.zh: 算下来，这样的睡眠效率与当今工业社会人群非常接近。

sentences.en: (C) According to Jerome Siegel, director of the University of California’s Center for Sleep Research, evidence suggests sleep habits may not be environmental or cultural, but central to the physical makeup of humans.
sentences.zh: 据加州大学睡眠研究中心主任杰罗姆·西格尔所言，有证据表明，睡眠习惯或许并非源于环境或文化，而是人类身体构造的核心组成部分。

sentences.en: These findings question the millions of dollars that have been spent on research that tries to explain why some sleepers get only about six hours of sleep a night.
sentences.zh: 这些发现使人对那些耗资数百万美元、试图解释为何有些人每晚只睡约六小时的研究提出了质疑。

sentences.en: Also, such findings question whether lack of sleep is a cause of obesity, mood disorders, and other physical and mental illnesses which have become so common in recent decades.
sentences.zh: 此外，这类发现还使人质疑，睡眠不足是否真是近几十年来变得如此普遍的肥胖、情绪障碍及其他身心疾病的诱因。

sentences.en: Scientists have documented that people’s energy often falls in the mid afternoon.
sentences.zh: 科学家已记录到，人们的精力往往在下午中段下降。

sentences.en: Some have suggested that it’s because we’ve managed to suppress a natural desire for a nap.
sentences.zh: 有人提出，这是因为我们硬生生压抑了想要午睡的自然欲望。

sentences.en: However, the new study provides evidence that this is unlikely, and that napping was actually rare in hunter-gatherer societies.
sentences.zh: 然而，这项新研究提供的证据表明，这种说法不太可能成立，午睡在狩猎采集社会中其实很少见。

sentences.en: The researchers estimated that naps may have occurred on up to 7 percent of winter days and 22 percent of summer days.
sentences.zh: 研究者估计，午睡在冬季可能至多发生在7%的日子里，在夏季则至多发生在22%的日子里。

sentences.en: They noted that their devices were only good at detecting longer naps, so it is possible that some of the study subjects took naps that were short, perhaps 15 minutes or less.
sentences.zh: 他们指出，所用设备只擅长检测较长时间的午睡，因此有些研究对象可能小睡过较短的时间，或许只有15分钟或更短。

sentences.en: (D) Another fascinating finding from the study had to do with the circadian rhythms, our daily activity cycles related to sunlight.
sentences.zh: 这项研究另一个引人入胜的发现，与昼夜节律有关，即我们与阳光相关的日常活动周期。

sentences.en: Instead of going to sleep right at dusk, tribespeople were staying awake an average of between 2.5 and 4.4 hours after sunset.
sentences.zh: 部落成员并不会在黄昏时就入睡，而是在日落之后平均还要清醒2.5到4.4小时。

sentences.en: All three tribes had fires going, but the light itself was much lower than you might get from a light bulb.
sentences.zh: 这三个部落都生着火，但火光本身要比电灯泡发出的光暗得多。

sentences.en: They did, however, have a tendency to wake up anywhere between an hour before and an hour after sunrise.
sentences.zh: 不过，他们确实倾向于在日出前一小时到日出后一小时之间的某个时刻醒来。

sentences.en: Siegel and his co-authors investigated this further by looking into the significance of temperature.
sentences.zh: 西格尔及其合作者进一步探究了这一点，考察了温度的重要性。

sentences.en: They found that it also played a big role, though it was somewhat less important than light in influencing sleep patterns.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，温度同样起着很大的作用，不过在影响睡眠模式方面，它的重要性略逊于光照。

sentences.en: They wrote that “sleep in both the winter and summer usually occurred during the period of cooling and that waking times usually occurred near the height of the daily warming trend.”
sentences.zh: 他们写道：“无论冬夏，睡眠通常都发生在气温下降的时段，而醒来的时间通常出现在一天升温趋势接近最高点之时。”

sentences.en: (E) The tribespeople that were studied are different from people living in modern conditions in a number of respects.
sentences.zh: 受研究的这些部落成员，在许多方面都与生活在现代条件下的人不同。

sentences.en: Importantly, almost none of them were troubled by sleeplessness.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，他们当中几乎没有人受失眠困扰。

sentences.en: In interviews with the researchers conducted through interpreters, only 1.5 to 2.5 percent of the study subjects said they had severe difficulties sleeping more than once a year.
sentences.zh: 在通过翻译进行的访谈中，只有1.5%到2.5%的研究对象表示，他们一年中有不止一次严重的入睡困难。

sentences.en: This figure is far lower than the 10 to 30 percent recorded in many industrialized countries today.
sentences.zh: 这一比例远低于当今许多工业化国家所记录的10%到30%。

sentences.en: Siegel suggested that “mimicking aspects of the natural environment” may therefore help treat some sleep disorders.
sentences.zh: 西格尔由此提出，“模仿自然环境的某些方面”或许有助于治疗某些睡眠障碍。

sentences.en: The tribespeople are also much healthier.
sentences.zh: 这些部落成员的身体也要健康得多。

sentences.en: Not a single one is overweight, indicating their overall higher levels of physical fitness.
sentences.zh: 没有一个人超重，这表明他们整体的身体素质更高。

sentences.en: They also tended to have healthier hearts.
sentences.zh: 他们的心脏往往也更健康。

sentences.en: Thus comes a critical question.
sentences.zh: 由此引出一个关键的问题。

sentences.en: If we can’t blame our health problems on our lack of sleep, could it be that the reason we feel so unrested is because of poor health?
sentences.zh: 如果我们不能把自己的健康问题归咎于睡眠不足，那么会不会正是因为健康状况不佳，我们才会感到如此疲惫不堪呢？

5.stemZh: 科学家研究狩猎采集社会，是因为人们认为这些社会的睡眠模式与一万多年前人类的睡眠模式更为相似。

6.stemZh: 研究中使用的医疗器械专为潮湿环境设计。

11.stemZh: 杰罗姆·西格尔认为，环境和文化对睡眠模式影响甚微。

sentences.en: (A) Some discoveries are so unusual it takes decades and sometimes even centuries to understand their full significance.
sentences.zh: 有些发现极不寻常，以至于要历经数十年、有时甚至数百年，人们才能领会其全部意义。

sentences.en: One such discovery is the fossil bed known as the Burgess Shale, which contains a record of bizarre creatures that lived 505 million years ago.
sentences.zh: 其中一项发现便是被称为伯吉斯页岩（Burgess Shale）的化石层，它记录了生活在5.05亿年前的各种奇异生物。

sentences.en: It was discovered in the Canadian Rockies over a century ago, and was popularized in 1989 in a book, Wonderful Life, by Stephen Jay Gould, an American paleontologist.
sentences.zh: 它于一个多世纪前在加拿大落基山脉被发现，并在1989年因美国古生物学家斯蒂芬·杰伊·古尔德（Stephen Jay Gould）的著作《奇妙的生命》而广为人知。

sentences.en: The Burgess Shale fossils were created at a time when the future Canadian land mass was situated near the Earth's equator.
sentences.zh: 伯吉斯页岩化石形成之时，日后构成加拿大的那片陆块正位于地球赤道附近。

sentences.en: The creatures were preserved when an entire marine ecosystem was buried in mud that eventually hardened and became exposed hundreds of millions of years later in an outcrop of the Rocky Mountains.
sentences.zh: 当整个海洋生态系统被泥沙掩埋时，这些生物得以保存下来；泥沙最终硬化，并在数亿年后于落基山脉的一处露头中显露出来。

sentences.en: American paleontologist Charles Walcott, following reports of fabulous fossil finds by construction workers on a Canadian railway who were digging in the mountains in the late 19th century, is said to have tripped over a block of shale in 1909 that revealed the area's remarkable supply of specimens.
sentences.zh: 据说，美国古生物学家查尔斯·沃尔科特（Charles Walcott）在听闻19世纪末在山中施工的加拿大铁路工人发现大量绝妙化石的报告后，于1909年被一块页岩绊了一跤，从而揭示出该地区惊人的标本宝藏。

sentences.en: It has long been believed that the curious fauna that lived there vanished in a series of extinctions because the fossil record ends abruptly.
sentences.zh: 由于化石记录戛然而止，人们长期以来一直认为，曾生活在那里的奇特动物群是在一系列灭绝事件中消失的。

sentences.en: But that no longer appears to be the case.
sentences.zh: 但如今看来，情况似乎并非如此。

sentences.en: (B) The Burgess Shale began to form soon after a period known as the Cambrian explosion, when most major groups of complex animals arose over a surprisingly short period.
sentences.zh: 伯吉斯页岩开始形成的时间，紧随被称为寒武纪大爆发的时期之后；在那段短得惊人的时间里，大多数主要的复杂动物类群相继出现。

sentences.en: Before 560 million years ago, most living things were either individual cells or simple colonies of cells.
sentences.zh: 在5.6亿年前之前，大多数生物要么是单个细胞，要么是简单的细胞群体。

sentences.en: Then, and for reasons that remain a mystery, life massively diversified and became ever more complex as the rate of evolution increased.
sentences.zh: 此后，出于至今仍是谜团的原因，随着演化速度加快，生命大规模分化，并变得越来越复杂。

sentences.en: An unusual feature of the Burgess Shale is that it is one of the earliest fossil beds to contain impressions of soft body parts alongside the remains of bones and shells, which is highly unusual.
sentences.zh: 伯吉斯页岩有一个不寻常的特点：它是最早在保存骨骼与外壳遗骸的同时、还留有软体部位印痕的化石层之一，这是极为罕见的。

sentences.en: Although the fossil bed was discovered on a mountain, these animals originally existed below an ocean, the bed of which was later pushed up to create the Rockies.
sentences.zh: 尽管这一化石层是在山上发现的，但这些动物最初却生活在海洋之下，而那片海床后来被抬升，形成了落基山脉。

sentences.en: Nobody knows exactly why they were so well preserved.
sentences.zh: 没有人确切知道它们为何能保存得如此完好。

sentences.en: One possibility is that the creatures were buried quickly and in conditions that were hostile to the bacteria that cause decomposition of soft body parts.
sentences.zh: 一种可能是，这些生物被迅速掩埋，且所处的环境不利于那些会导致软体部位腐烂的细菌生存。

sentences.en: (C) Those who first worked on the Burgess Shale, unearthing 65,000 specimens over a 14-year period up to 1924, assumed that the fossils came from extinct members of groups of animals in existence today.
sentences.zh: 最早研究伯吉斯页岩的人，在截至1924年的14年间发掘出65000件标本，他们认为这些化石来自如今仍存在的动物类群中已灭绝的成员。

sentences.en: This turned out to be misleading because many of the creatures are so unusual that they are still difficult to classify.
sentences.zh: 事实证明这种看法具有误导性，因为其中许多生物极为奇特，至今仍难以归类。

sentences.en: One such example is Opabinia, a creature that grew to about 8 cm (3 inches), had five eyes, a body that was a series of lobes, a tail in the shape of a fan, and that ate using a proboscis.
sentences.zh: 欧巴宾海蝎（Opabinia）便是一例，这种生物可长到约8厘米（3英寸），有五只眼睛，身体由一连串瓣状结构组成，尾巴呈扇形，进食时用一根长吻。

sentences.en: (D) The proboscis had a set of grasping claws on the end, with which it grabbed food and stuffed it into its mouth.
sentences.zh: 这根长吻末端长有一组用于抓取的爪子，它用这些爪子抓住食物并塞进嘴里。

sentences.en: Nectocaris, meanwhile, could be mistaken for a leech, but with fins and tentacles.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，纳克托虾（Nectocaris）则可能被误认为水蛭，只是它长有鳍和触手。

sentences.en: Weirdest of all was Hallucigenia, described by paleontologist Simon Conway Morris, when he re-examined Walcott's specimens in 1979.
sentences.zh: 其中最为怪异的是怪诞虫（Hallucigenia），它是古生物学家西蒙·康威·莫里斯（Simon Conway Morris）在1979年重新检视沃尔科特的标本时描述的。

sentences.en: With its multiplicity of spines and tentacles, little about Hallucigenia made sense, but scientists hypothesized that the spines were legs that helped it move and the tentacles were for feeding.
sentences.zh: 怪诞虫长着众多的棘刺和触手，其身体构造几乎令人无从理解，但科学家推测，那些棘刺是帮助它移动的腿，而触手则用于进食。

sentences.en: Like an abstract painting, its orientation is a mystery at first, making it difficult to work out which way up it went, which hole food went into, and which hole food came out of.
sentences.zh: 它就像一幅抽象画，方向起初是个谜，让人难以判断它哪一面朝上、食物从哪个孔进入、又从哪个孔排出。

sentences.en: (E) Paleontologists had long thought that many of the Burgess Shale animals were examples of experiments in evolution.
sentences.zh: 古生物学家长期以来一直认为，伯吉斯页岩中的许多动物都是演化“试验”的例子。

sentences.en: In other words, entirely new forms of life that did not survive or lead to other groups or species.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，它们是全新的生命形态，既没有存活下来，也没有演化出其他类群或物种。

sentences.en: Hallucigenia, ironically, turned out to be the exception that proved the rule.
sentences.zh: 颇具讽刺意味的是，怪诞虫最终却成了印证这一规律的例外。

sentences.en: It is now thought to be an ancestor of the modern group of arthropods, which includes everything from flies and butterflies to centipedes and crabs.
sentences.zh: 如今人们认为它是现代节肢动物类群的祖先，而节肢动物涵盖了从苍蝇、蝴蝶到蜈蚣、螃蟹等各种生物。

sentences.en: (F) Now another misconception has been quashed.
sentences.zh: 如今，又一种错误观念被推翻了。

sentences.en: Writing in Nature recently, Peter Van Roy of Yale University in the United States and his colleagues suggest that the sudden absence of such crazy soft-bodied fossils does not indicate a mass extinction, but merely an end to the unusual local circumstances that caused the creatures to be preserved.
sentences.zh: 美国耶鲁大学的彼得·范罗伊（Peter Van Roy）及其同事近期在《自然》杂志上撰文指出，此类奇异软体化石的骤然消失并不意味着发生了大规模灭绝，而仅仅表明那些促成这些生物得以保存的特殊局部条件不复存在了。

sentences.en: In an area of the Atlas Mountains of Morocco, Van Roy's team of researchers has found another diverse (and sometimes bizarre) assemblage of soft-bodied organisms from a period after the Burgess Shale was formed.
sentences.zh: 在摩洛哥阿特拉斯山脉的一处区域，范罗伊的研究团队发现了另一批多样（有时也很奇异）的软体生物组合，它们来自伯吉斯页岩形成之后的一个时期。

sentences.en: One discovery includes something that may be a stalked barnacle.
sentences.zh: 其中一项发现包括一种可能是有柄藤壶的生物。

sentences.en: This suggests that the evolution of such complex life went on uninterrupted.
sentences.zh: 这表明此类复杂生命的演化一直未曾中断。

sentences.en: For its part, the Burgess Shale continues to produce an astonishing array of indefinable creatures faster than paleontologists can examine them.
sentences.zh: 至于伯吉斯页岩本身，它仍在源源不断地产出令人惊叹的、难以界定的各种生物，其速度之快超过了古生物学家所能研究的程度。

sentences.en: The world still has plenty to learn about this wonderful life.
sentences.zh: 关于这奇妙的生命，世人仍有许多东西要去了解。

sentences.en: (A) The earliest stringed instruments currently known to archaeologists are bowl harps.
sentences.zh: 目前考古学家所知最早的弦乐器是弓形竖琴。

sentences.en: For millennia, people made bowl harps using, for example, tortoise shells as resonators, with a bent stick for a neck and one or more gut or silk strings.
sentences.zh: 数千年来，人们一直在制作弓形竖琴，例如以龟壳作为共鸣体、以一根弯曲的棍子作琴颈，配上一根或多根羊肠或丝制琴弦。

sentences.en: The world's museums contain many such harps from the ancient Sumerian, Babylonian, and Egyptian civilisations.
sentences.zh: 世界各地的博物馆里都收藏着许多来自古代苏美尔、巴比伦和埃及文明的此类竖琴。

sentences.en: Around 2500-2000 BC, more advanced harps, such as the beautifully carved 11-stringed instrument found in the tomb of Queen Shub-Ad in ancient Mesopotamia, now modern-day Iraq, started to appear.
sentences.zh: 公元前 2500 年至 2000 年前后，更先进的竖琴开始出现，例如在古代美索不达米亚（今伊拉克）舒巴德王后墓中发现的那把雕饰精美的 11 弦乐器。

sentences.en: The tanbur* probably developed from the bowl harp.
sentences.zh: 丹布尔（tanbur）很可能是从弓形竖琴发展而来的。

sentences.en: It was different from the bowl harp in that its neck was straightened out to allow the strings to be pressed down to create more notes.
sentences.zh: 它与弓形竖琴不同之处在于琴颈被拉直，使琴弦可以被按下以产生更多音符。

sentences.en: Tomb paintings and stone carvings in Egypt indicate that harps and tanburs – plus flutes and percussion instruments – were being played together 3,500-4,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 埃及的墓室壁画和石刻表明，竖琴、丹布尔以及笛和打击乐器在 3500 至 4000 年前就被一同演奏。

sentences.en: Archaeologists have also found many similar relics amongst the ruins of the ancient Mesopotamian civilisation.
sentences.zh: 考古学家还在古代美索不达米亚文明的废墟中发现了许多类似的遗物。

sentences.en: Many of these instruments have survived into modern times in almost unchanged form, for example, folk instruments of the region such as the Turkish saz and Afghan panchtar.
sentences.zh: 其中许多乐器以几乎不变的形式延续至今，例如该地区的民间乐器，如土耳其的萨兹（saz）和阿富汗的潘奇塔尔（panchtar）。

sentences.en: At 3,500 years old, the tanbur which belonged to the Egyptian singer Har-Mose is the earliest known example of this instrument.
sentences.zh: 距今 3500 年的、属于埃及歌手哈尔-莫塞（Har-Mose）的丹布尔，是已知最早的此类乐器实例。

sentences.en: Har-Mose's tanbur had three strings and a plectrum suspended from the neck by a cord.
sentences.zh: 哈尔-莫塞的丹布尔有三根弦，琴颈上还以一根绳子悬挂着一片拨片。

sentences.en: The soundbox, which increased the volume, was made of beautifully polished cedarwood and covered in rawhide.
sentences.zh: 用以扩大音量的共鸣箱由打磨精致的雪松木制成，外覆生牛皮。

sentences.en: It can be seen today at the Archaeological Museum in Cairo.
sentences.zh: 它今天仍可以在开罗的考古博物馆中看到。

sentences.en: (B) In order to distinguish guitars from other stringed instruments, it is helpful to have a broad definition of the guitar.
sentences.zh: 为了把吉他与其他弦乐器区分开来，给吉他下一个宽泛的定义会很有帮助。

sentences.en: Music expert Dr Michael Kasha defines a guitar as having 'a long, fretted neck, flat wooden soundboard, ribs, and a flat back, most often with sides that curve inwards'.
sentences.zh: 音乐专家迈克尔·卡沙博士（Dr Michael Kasha）将吉他定义为“具有狭长且带品丝的琴颈、平整的木质共鸣板、琴框，以及一块平整的背板，绝大多数情况下两侧曲线向内凹陷”。

sentences.en: The oldest known visual representation of such an instrument is a stone carving at Alaca Huyuk in Turkey, which shows a 3,300-year-old instrument with a long neck and sides that clearly curve inwards.
sentences.zh: 目前已知最早的此类乐器视觉形象，是土耳其阿拉贾许由克（Alaca Huyuk）的一幅石刻，上面描绘的是一件距今 3300 年的乐器，琴颈狭长，两侧曲线明显向内凹。

sentences.en: The name 'guitar' comes from the ancient Sanskrit word for 'string' – 'tar'.
sentences.zh: “吉他”（guitar）这个名字源自梵语中表示“弦”的古词——“tar”。

sentences.en: Many popular stringed instruments used in Central Asia today have existed in an unchanged form for several thousand years, as shown by archaeological finds in the area.
sentences.zh: 如今在中亚仍流行的许多弦乐器，已以一种几乎未改变的形态存在了数千年，该地区的考古发现可以证明这一点。

sentences.en: Many have names that end in 'tar', with a prefix indicating the number of strings, such as the doter, a two-stringed instrument found in Turkestan, and the Persian three-stringed setar and four-stringed chartar.
sentences.zh: 许多乐器名以“tar”结尾，再以前缀表明弦数，例如土库曼地区发现的两弦乐器多塔尔（doter），以及波斯的三弦塞塔尔（setar）和四弦查尔塔尔（chartar）。

sentences.en: The Indian sitar almost certainly took its name from the setar, but over the centuries it evolved radically, following the Indians' own aesthetic and cultural ideals.
sentences.zh: 印度的西塔尔（sitar）几乎可以肯定是从塞塔尔得名的，但在数百年间，它按照印度自身的审美与文化理念发生了根本性的演变。

sentences.en: (C) Tanburs and harps spread around the ancient world with travellers, merchants and seamen.
sentences.zh: 丹布尔与竖琴随着旅人、商人和水手传播到古代世界各地。

sentences.en: The earliest guitar-like instruments to arrive in Europe had, most often, four strings.
sentences.zh: 传入欧洲的最早的类吉他乐器，最常见的是四弦琴。

sentences.en: Many such instruments, and variations with from three to five strings, can be seen in mediaeval illustrated manuscripts.
sentences.zh: 在中世纪的插图手抄本中可以看到许多此类乐器，以及弦数从三到五不等的各种变体。

sentences.en: They were also carved in stone in European churches and cathedrals, from the first century AD through until the 13th century.
sentences.zh: 从公元 1 世纪至 13 世纪，它们也被刻在欧洲的教堂和大教堂的石雕上。

sentences.en: When the four-stringed Persian chartar arrived in Spain, however, it changed in form and construction, acquiring pairs of strings tuned to the same note instead of single strings.
sentences.zh: 然而，当四弦的波斯查尔塔尔传到西班牙时，其形态和构造发生了变化，开始采用调到同一音高的成对琴弦，而非单根琴弦。

sentences.en: It became known as the chitarra.
sentences.zh: 它因此被称为 chitarra。

sentences.en: By the middle of the 14th century, the chitarra had become dominant, at least in most of Europe.
sentences.zh: 到了 14 世纪中叶，chitarra 至少在欧洲大部分地区已经占据了主导地位。

sentences.en: The earliest known music for the eight-stringed chitarra was written in 16th-century Spain.
sentences.zh: 目前所知最早为八弦 chitarra 谱写的乐曲，出自 16 世纪的西班牙。

sentences.en: The ten-string version first appeared in Italy at the same time, and gradually replaced the eight-stringed instrument.
sentences.zh: 十弦版本同期首先出现在意大利，并逐步取代了八弦乐器。

sentences.en: A further two strings first appeared in the 17th century, an innovation which guitar makers all over Europe quickly took up.
sentences.zh: 另外两根弦于 17 世纪首次出现，欧洲各地的吉他制作师很快采纳了这一创新。

sentences.en: However, this twelve-string arrangement gradually gave way to six single strings across the continent.
sentences.zh: 然而，这种十二弦的设置在整个欧洲大陆又逐渐被六根单弦所取代。

sentences.en: The six-stringed guitar can thus be said to be a development of the twelve-string, rather than vice versa, as was thought previously.
sentences.zh: 因此可以说，六弦吉他是十二弦吉他的发展产物，而不是像此前认为的那样反过来。

sentences.en: (D) At the beginning of the 19th century, the present-day guitar began to take shape, although bodies were still fairly small and narrow-waisted.
sentences.zh: 进入 19 世纪初，今天我们所见的吉他开始成形，尽管那时的琴体仍相当小巧、腰部内收。

sentences.en: The modern classical guitar first appeared in its current form in the mid-19th century, when the Spanish guitar maker Antonio Torres increased the size of the body, altered its proportions, and introduced the revolutionary fan-braced top**.
sentences.zh: 现代古典吉他在 19 世纪中叶才首次以其今天的形态出现，那时西班牙制琴师安东尼奥·托雷斯（Antonio Torres）加大了琴体尺寸，调整了比例，并引入了革命性的扇形支撑面板。

sentences.en: His design radically increased the volume and improved the tone of the instrument, and very soon became the norm.
sentences.zh: 他的设计大幅提升了乐器的音量并改善了音色，很快便成为标准。

sentences.en: This design has remained essentially unchanged to this day.
sentences.zh: 这种设计实质上一直延续到今天。

sentences.en: At the time when Torres made his breakthrough, German immigrants to America – among them Christian Friedrich Martin – began making guitars with X-braced tops.
sentences.zh: 在托雷斯取得突破之时，前往美国的德国移民——其中包括克里斯蒂安·弗里德里希·马丁（Christian Friedrich Martin）——开始制造采用 X 形支撑面板的吉他。

sentences.en: Steel strings, which became widely available several decades later in the early 1900s, offered the promise of a much louder guitar, but the increased tension was too much for the fan-braced top.
sentences.zh: 几十年后，钢弦在 1900 年代初期开始广泛使用，它使吉他有望发出更响亮的声音，但其增大的张力远远超过扇形支撑面板所能承受的范围。

sentences.en: The stronger X-braced top proved equal to the job, and quickly became the industry standard.
sentences.zh: 更结实的 X 形支撑面板被证明能胜任这一任务，并迅速成为行业标准。

sentences.en: (E) At the end of the 19th century, guitar manufacturer Orville Gibson added steel strings to a body constructed like a cello, a combination which produced more volume.
sentences.zh: 19 世纪末，吉他制造师奥维尔·吉布森（Orville Gibson）把钢弦装到了一种构造仿照大提琴的琴体上，这一组合产生了更大的音量。

sentences.en: The electric guitar was born when pickups were fitted to Hawaiian and jazz guitars in the late 1920s, but met with little success until 1936, when Gibson introduced its famous ES150 model.
sentences.zh: 1920 年代末，当人们把拾音器装到夏威夷吉他和爵士吉他上时，电吉他便诞生了，但它一直反响平平，直到 1936 年吉布森推出其著名的 ES150 型号。

records.title: Caral: an ancient South American city
records.titleZh: 卡拉尔：一座古老的南美洲城市

sentences.en: (A) Huge earth and rock mounds rise out of the desert of the Supe Valley near the coast of Peru in South America.
sentences.zh: 在南美洲秘鲁海岸附近的苏佩河谷，巨大的土石丘从沙漠中拔地而起。

sentences.en: These immense mounds appear simply to be part of the geographical landscape in this arid region squeezed between the Pacific Ocean and the Andes mountains.
sentences.zh: 这些庞大的土丘看上去不过是这片夹在太平洋与安第斯山脉之间的干旱地区地貌的一部分。

sentences.en: But looks deceive.
sentences.zh: 但外表具有欺骗性。

sentences.en: These are actually human-made pyramids.
sentences.zh: 它们其实是人工建造的金字塔。

sentences.en: Strong evidence indicates they are the remains of a city known as Caral that flourished nearly 5,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 有力的证据表明，它们是一座名为卡拉尔的城市的遗迹，这座城市在近5000年前曾经繁盛一时。

sentences.en: If true, it would be the oldest known urban center in the Americas and among the most ancient in the world.
sentences.zh: 如果属实，它将是美洲已知最古老的城市中心，也是世界上最古老的城市中心之一。

sentences.en: Research undertaken by Peruvian archaeologist Ruth Shady suggests that the 150-acre complex of pyramids, plazas and residential buildings was a thriving metropolis when Egypt’s great pyramids were still being built.
sentences.zh: 秘鲁考古学家露丝·沙迪所做的研究表明，这片占地150英亩、由金字塔、广场和住宅建筑组成的建筑群，在埃及大金字塔尚在建造之时，已是一座繁华的大都市。

sentences.en: Though discovered in 1905, for years Caral attracted little attention, largely because archaeologists believed the structures were fairly recent.
sentences.zh: 卡拉尔虽然早在1905年就被发现，但多年来一直无人问津，这在很大程度上是因为考古学家认为这些建筑年代相当晚近。

sentences.en: But the monumental scale of the pyramids had long interested Shady, who began excavations at the site in 1996, about 22 kilometers from the coast and 190 kilometers north of Peru’s capital city of Lima.
sentences.zh: 但金字塔那纪念碑般的规模早就令沙迪着迷，她于1996年在该遗址开始发掘，遗址距海岸约22公里，位于秘鲁首都利马以北约190公里处。

sentences.en: (B) Shady and her crew searched for broken remains of the pots and containers that most such sites contain.
sentences.zh: 沙迪和她的团队四处寻找陶罐和容器的残片，大多数此类遗址都会有这些东西。

sentences.en: Not finding any only made her more excited; it meant Caral could be what archaeologists term pre-ceramic, that is, existing before the advent in the area of pot-firing techniques.
sentences.zh: 什么都没找到反而让她更加兴奋；这意味着卡拉尔可能属于考古学家所说的前陶器时期，也就是说，它存在于当地出现烧陶技术之前。

sentences.en: Shady’s team undertook the task of excavating Piramide Mayor, the largest of the pyramids.
sentences.zh: 沙迪的团队承担起发掘大金字塔的任务，那是所有金字塔中最大的一座。

sentences.en: After carefully clearing away many hundreds of years’ worth of rubble and sand, they identified staircases, walls covered with remnants of colored woven bags and brickwork.
sentences.zh: 在小心翼翼地清除了数百年间堆积的瓦砾和沙土之后，他们辨认出了楼梯，以及覆满彩色编织袋残片的墙壁和砖砌结构。

sentences.en: In the foundations, they found the remains of grass-like reeds woven into bags.
sentences.zh: 在地基中，他们发现了编成袋子的草状芦苇的残余。

sentences.en: The original workers, she surmised, must have filled these bags with stones from a nearby quarry and laid them atop one another inside retaining walls, gradually giving rise to the pyramid’s immense structure.
sentences.zh: 她推测，当年的工人一定是把附近采石场的石块装进这些袋子，再在挡土墙内一层层垒叠起来，逐渐建起了金字塔那庞大的结构。

sentences.en: Shady had samples of the reeds subjected to radiocarbon dating and found that the reeds were 4,600 years old.
sentences.zh: 沙迪把芦苇的样本送去做放射性碳定年，发现这些芦苇已有4600年的历史。

sentences.en: This evidence indicated that Caral was, in fact, more than 1,000 years older than what had previously been thought to be the oldest urban center in the Americas.
sentences.zh: 这一证据表明，卡拉尔实际上比此前被认为是美洲最古老城市中心的那座城市还要早1000多年。

sentences.en: (C) What amazed archaeologists was not just the age, but the complexity and scope of Caral.
sentences.zh: 令考古学家惊叹的不仅是年代，还有卡拉尔的复杂程度和规模。

sentences.en: Piramide Mayor alone covers an area nearly the size of four football fields and is 18 meters tall.
sentences.zh: 单单大金字塔就占地近四个足球场大小，高达18米。

sentences.en: A nine-meter-wide staircase rises from a circular plaza at the foot of the pyramid, passing over three terraced levels until it reaches the top.
sentences.zh: 一段九米宽的楼梯从金字塔脚下的圆形广场升起，越过三级台地，直抵塔顶。

sentences.en: Thousands of manual laborers would have been needed to build such a project, not counting the many architects, craftsmen, and managers.
sentences.zh: 建造这样一项工程，需要数以千计的体力劳动者，这还不算众多的建筑师、工匠和管理者。

sentences.en: Shady’s team found the remains of a large amphitheater, containing almost 70 musical instruments made of bird and deer bones.
sentences.zh: 沙迪的团队发现了一座大型圆形剧场的遗迹，里面有近70件用鸟骨和鹿骨制成的乐器。

sentences.en: Clearly, music played an important role in Caral’s society.
sentences.zh: 显然，音乐在卡拉尔的社会中扮演了重要的角色。

sentences.en: Around the perimeter of Caral are a series of smaller mounds and various buildings.
sentences.zh: 在卡拉尔的外围一圈，分布着一系列较小的土丘和各式建筑。

sentences.en: These indicate a hierarchy of living arrangements: large, well-kept rooms atop pyramids for the elite, ground-level quarters for craftsmen, and shabbier outlying dwellings for workers.
sentences.zh: 这些显示出一种等级分明的居住安排：金字塔顶上宽敞整洁的房间属于精英，地面上的住所属于工匠，而外围更为简陋的居所则属于工人。

sentences.en: (D) But why had Caral been built in the first place?
sentences.zh: 但卡拉尔当初究竟为何而建？

sentences.en: Her excavations convinced Shady that Caral once served as a trade center for the region, which extends from the rainforests of the Amazon to the high forests of the Andes.
sentences.zh: 沙迪的发掘使她确信，卡拉尔曾是该地区的一处贸易中心，这一地区从亚马孙的雨林一直延伸到安第斯山的高地森林。

sentences.en: Shady found evidence of a rich trading environment, including seeds of the cocoa bush and necklaces of shells, neither of which was native to the immediate Caral area.
sentences.zh: 沙迪发现了贸易环境繁荣的证据，包括可可灌木的种子和贝壳项链，二者都不是卡拉尔近旁地区的本土之物。

sentences.en: This environment gave rise to people who did not take part in the production of food, allowing them to become priests and planners, builders and designers.
sentences.zh: 这种环境催生出一批不参与食物生产的人，使他们得以成为祭司和规划者、建造者和设计者。

sentences.en: Thus occupational specialization, elemental to an urban society, emerged.
sentences.zh: 于是，作为城市社会基本要素的职业分工应运而生。

sentences.en: (E) But what sustained such a trading center and drew travelers to it?
sentences.zh: 但又是什么维系着这样一个贸易中心，并把旅人吸引到这里？

sentences.en: Was it food?
sentences.zh: 是食物吗？

sentences.en: Shady and her team found the bones of small edible fish, which must have come from the Pacific coast to the west, in the excavations.
sentences.zh: 沙迪和她的团队在发掘中发现了可食用小鱼的骨头，这些鱼一定来自西边的太平洋海岸。

sentences.en: But they also found evidence of squash, sweet potatoes and beans having been grown locally.
sentences.zh: 但他们也发现了当地曾种植南瓜、甘薯和豆类的证据。

sentences.en: Shady theorized that Caral’s early farmers diverted the area’s rivers into canals, which still cross the Supe Valley today, to irrigate their fields.
sentences.zh: 沙迪推断，卡拉尔早期的农人把这一地区的河流引入渠道，用以灌溉田地，而这些渠道至今仍横贯苏佩河谷。

sentences.en: But because she found no traces of maize, which can be traded or stored and used in times of crop failure, she concluded that Caral’s trade leverage was not based on stockpiling food supplies.
sentences.zh: 但由于她没有发现玉米的踪迹——玉米可以用于交易或储存，在歉收时备用——她断定，卡拉尔的贸易筹码并不是建立在囤积粮食之上的。

sentences.en: It was evidence of another crop in the excavations that gave Shady the best clue to Caral’s success.
sentences.zh: 真正为沙迪揭示卡拉尔成功之道的最佳线索，是发掘中另一种作物的证据。

sentences.en: In nearly every excavated building, her team discovered evidence of cotton—seeds, fibers and textiles.
sentences.zh: 几乎在每一座被发掘的建筑里，她的团队都发现了棉花的痕迹——种子、纤维和纺织品。

sentences.en: Her theory fell into place when a large fishing net made of those fibers, unearthed in an unrelated dig on Peru’s coast, turned out to be as old as Caral.
sentences.zh: 当一张用这种纤维织成的大渔网——它出土于秘鲁海岸一处与此无关的发掘——被证实与卡拉尔同样古老时，她的理论便顺理成章了。

sentences.en: “The farmers of Caral grew the cotton that the fishermen needed to make their nets,” Shady speculates.
sentences.zh: “卡拉尔的农人种出了渔民织网所需的棉花，”沙迪推测道。

sentences.en: “And the fishermen gave them shellfish and dried fish in exchange for these nets.”
sentences.zh: “而渔民则以贝类和鱼干来交换这些渔网。”

sentences.en: In essence, the people of Caral enabled fishermen to work with larger and more effective nets, which made the resources of the sea more readily available, and the fishermen probably used dried squash grown by the Caral people as flotation devices for their nets.
sentences.zh: 从本质上说，卡拉尔人让渔民得以使用更大、更高效的渔网，从而更便于获取海洋的资源，而渔民很可能把卡拉尔人种的南瓜晒干，当作渔网的浮子来用。

records.title: The Early History of Olive Oil

sentences.en: (A) Olive oil is produced from the fruit of the olive tree, which is a member of the Oleaceae plant family.
sentences.zh: 橄榄油由橄榄树的果实制成，橄榄树属于木犀科（Oleaceae）植物。

sentences.en: The trees require some cold weather during the year, but also tolerate hot, dry conditions, and do not like moisture when they are flowering.
sentences.zh: 这种树一年中需要一定的冷凉天气，但同时也能耐受炎热干燥的环境，并且在开花时不喜欢潮湿。

sentences.en: They actually produce better when subjected to these stressful conditions, and as a result, olive trees have traditionally been grown on land where little else will survive.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它们在这种胁迫条件下反而结果更佳；正因如此，橄榄树历来都种植在其他植物难以存活的土地上。

sentences.en: (B) Archaeologists today are divided over exactly where the first domestication of the olive occurred: some say it was in the area which is now Iran, Syria, Jordan and Egypt, while others contend it was in mainland Greece or on the island of Crete.
sentences.zh: 如今的考古学家对橄榄最早在何处被驯化看法不一：有人认为是在今天伊朗、叙利亚、约旦和埃及一带，另一些人则坚持认为是在希腊本土或克里特岛。

sentences.en: The one thing that can be said with certainty is that cultivation began at least 6,000 years ago and spread slowly westward across the lands bordering on the Mediterranean Sea.
sentences.zh: 唯一可以确定的是，橄榄的栽培至少始于 6000 年前，并缓慢向西扩散至地中海沿岸各地。

sentences.en: Olive oil was used for a variety of purposes during these early times, including as a pharmacological ointment and in rituals for anointing royalty.
sentences.zh: 在那些早期年代，橄榄油被用于各种用途，包括作为药用油膏，以及用于为王室成员涂抹的仪式。

sentences.en: (C) The ancient Greeks believed the olive tree was a priceless gift from the goddess Athena and used its oil in sacred religious rituals.
sentences.zh: 古希腊人相信橄榄树是雅典娜女神赐予的无价之宝，并在神圣的宗教仪式中使用其油。

sentences.en: In fact, the Greek poet Homer called olive oil ‘liquid gold’, and during the 6th and 7th centuries BC, Greek law forbade the cutting down of olive trees and made it punishable by death.
sentences.zh: 事实上，希腊诗人荷马称橄榄油为“液体黄金”，在公元前 6 世纪和 7 世纪，希腊法律禁止砍伐橄榄树，违者甚至会被判处死刑。

sentences.en: The ancient Middle Eastern ruler King David valued his groves of olive trees and his olive oil warehouses so much that he posted guards around the clock to protect them.
sentences.zh: 古代中东的统治者大卫王对自己的橄榄园和橄榄油仓库极为珍视，甚至安排卫兵昼夜不停地守护。

sentences.en: (D) Over the years, olive oil developed other uses.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，橄榄油又发展出其他用途。

sentences.en: Its employment in cooking dates at least as far back as the 5th century BC, as described by the Greek philosopher Plato.
sentences.zh: 据希腊哲学家柏拉图的记载，橄榄油用于烹饪至少可以追溯到公元前 5 世纪。

sentences.en: Its use as an aid to beauty and health later became ingrained in many Mediterranean cultures.
sentences.zh: 它作为美容和健康辅助手段的用法后来融入了许多地中海文化。

sentences.en: The Romans, for example, are said to have used generous amounts on their bodies to moisturise their skin after bathing.
sentences.zh: 举例来说，据说罗马人在沐浴后会在身上涂抹大量橄榄油来滋润皮肤。

sentences.en: With the spread of the Roman Empire, olive oil became a major commodity, and its trade promoted commerce throughout the ancient world.
sentences.zh: 随着罗马帝国的扩张，橄榄油成为一项重要商品，其贸易促进了整个古代世界的商业往来。

sentences.en: It is generally believed that in the 1st–2nd centuries BC, olive trees were taken to North Africa and then to Spain, which was later to become the world’s largest producer of olive oil.
sentences.zh: 一般认为，公元前 1 至 2 世纪橄榄树被引入北非，随后又传入西班牙——后者后来发展为世界上最大的橄榄油生产国。

sentences.en: Artefacts found at various Mediterranean archaeological sites include olive oil storage vessels with olive plant residue still in them.
sentences.zh: 在地中海多处考古遗址出土的文物中，包括内部仍残留着橄榄植物残渣的橄榄油储存器皿。

sentences.en: Historical evidence still in existence in the form of wall paintings and ancient manuscripts (including the works of the Roman naturalist and philosopher, Pliny the Elder) all record production techniques and the various uses of olive oil.
sentences.zh: 至今仍然留存的壁画和古代手稿（包括罗马博物学家兼哲学家老普林尼的著作）等历史证据，都记录了橄榄油的生产工艺以及它的各种用途。

sentences.en: (E) Making olive oil in those early days was a laborious process accomplished without mechanisation.
sentences.zh: 在那些早期年代，制作橄榄油是一个不借助机械、极其费力的过程。

sentences.en: Processing or milling the fruit involved several distinct stages to extract the liquid.
sentences.zh: 为了榨取油液，对果实的加工或碾磨需要经过几个明确的步骤。

sentences.en: The olives were harvested from the trees by hand or by beating the fruit from the trees with long sticks.
sentences.zh: 工人们用手从树上采下橄榄，或者用长棍敲打树枝把果实击落。

sentences.en: The olives were then rinsed and crushed to separate out the large seed found in the centre of each.
sentences.zh: 随后将橄榄冲洗并压碎，以分离出每颗果实中央的大核。

sentences.en: The remaining seedless flesh was put in woven bags and pressed.
sentences.zh: 剩下的去核果肉被装入编织口袋中并加以压榨。

sentences.en: Hot water was then poured over the bags to separate the oil from the solid bits of olive.
sentences.zh: 然后将热水倒在袋子上，使油与橄榄固体分离开来。

sentences.en: The liquid produced in this process, consisting of oil and water, was drained into stone basins or tanks, where it was allowed to settle and separate.
sentences.zh: 由此产生的液体由油和水组成，被排入石制容器或缸中，让其静置分层。

sentences.en: In cold weather, a bit of salt was added to speed up the process.
sentences.zh: 在寒冷的天气里，会加入少量盐以加快这一过程。

sentences.en: As much oil as possible was drawn off the water, but the result was still not pure oil.
sentences.zh: 尽量将油从水面舀出，但所得仍非纯油。

sentences.en: Therefore, this impure mixture was allowed once more to settle in vats and then separated in order to refine the product.
sentences.zh: 因此，这种不纯的混合物会再次被放入大缸中静置，然后再次分离，以提纯产品。

sentences.en: (F) The waste water from the milling process, which is called amurca, is a bitter-tasting and foul-smelling liquid.
sentences.zh: 压榨过程中产生的废水称为 amurca，是一种味苦、气味难闻的液体。

sentences.en: In many ancient civilisations it was often simply discarded, causing serious pollution because of its acidity and high salt content.
sentences.zh: 在许多古代文明中，这种废水通常被直接丢弃，因其酸性强、盐分高而造成严重污染。

sentences.en: However, in the Roman period it was regarded as a very useful substance.
sentences.zh: 然而，在罗马时期，它却被视为一种非常有用的物质。

sentences.en: When spread on surfaces, amurca forms a hard finish and therefore it was often applied to the floors of grain storage buildings where it hardened, keeping out water, mud and pests.
sentences.zh: amurca 涂抹在表面后会形成坚硬的覆层，因此常被用于谷物仓库的地面——干透后可以挡住水、泥土和虫害。

sentences.en: When boiled down, amurca was applied to leather to soften it so that it was easier to shape into articles of clothing and shoes.
sentences.zh: amurca 被熬煮浓缩后涂在皮革上，可以让皮革变软，便于加工成衣物和鞋类。

sentences.en: It could also be eaten by farm animals and was, in fact, fed to livestock suffering from malnutrition.
sentences.zh: 它也可以被农场动物食用，事实上还被喂给营养不良的牲畜。

sentences.en: According to ancient texts, amurca was also utilised in moderate amounts by farmers as a fertiliser or as a pesticide, helping them to protect their crops from insects and even small rodents.
sentences.zh: 根据古代文献记载，amurca 还被农夫适量用作肥料或杀虫剂，帮助他们保护庄稼不受昆虫甚至小型啮齿动物的侵害。

sentences.en: (A) It was Jacob Hodes's first day at college.
sentences.zh: 那是雅各布·霍兹（Jacob Hodes）上大学的第一天。

sentences.en: He can still recall spending an enjoyable afternoon being shown around campus by a second-year student named Daniel Byrne, who happened to be from his home town.
sentences.zh: 他至今还记得，一位名叫丹尼尔·伯恩（Daniel Byrne）的二年级学生陪他度过了愉快的一下午，带他参观校园，而这个学生恰好与他来自同一座城市。

sentences.en: Jacob then spent the rest of the year ignoring him.
sentences.zh: 可那年余下的时间里，雅各布却把他当成空气，完全不予理睬。

sentences.en: 'I never saw him again,' he says.
sentences.zh: “我再也没见过他，”他说。

sentences.en: 'Well, I'm sure I walked past him plenty of times, but I just didn't see him.'
sentences.zh: “嗯，我肯定从他身边走过很多次，可我就是没看见他。”

sentences.en: This behaviour wasn't intentional.
sentences.zh: 这种行为并非故意。

sentences.en: Jacob just couldn't recollect what his fellow student looked like.
sentences.zh: 雅各布只是想不起那位同学长什么样。

sentences.en: He had had the same trouble all his life.
sentences.zh: 他这辈子一直都有同样的麻烦。

sentences.en: Friends and relatives would greet him and he would have no idea who they were.
sentences.zh: 朋友和亲戚跟他打招呼，他根本不知道对方是谁。

sentences.en: It wasn't until five years ago that it all made sense.
sentences.zh: 直到五年前，这一切才豁然开朗。

sentences.en: That was when Hodes was diagnosed with prosopagnosia, a condition that means he is unable to recognise faces.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，霍兹被诊断患有面孔识别障碍症（prosopagnosia）——一种使他无法辨认人脸的病症。

sentences.en: According to researchers, he is far from alone.
sentences.zh: 据研究人员所说，他绝非个例。

sentences.en: In fact, the condition is not that uncommon, but until a few years ago only a few dozen cases had ever been described, and all of these had been caused by brain injury.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这种症状并不算罕见，但直到几年前，文献中所描述的病例不过几十宗，且都是由脑损伤引起的。

sentences.en: Recently, though, researchers identified a second form of face blindness, developmental prosopagnosia, which is either present from birth or develops very early in life.
sentences.zh: 不过最近研究人员发现了脸盲症的第二种形式——发育型面孔识别障碍症（developmental prosopagnosia），这种症状要么与生俱来，要么在生命早期就已形成。

sentences.en: (B) In May a team from Harvard University in the US and University College London (UCL) announced the results of a web survey of 1,600 people, suggesting that up to 2 per cent of people have some degree of face blindness.
sentences.zh: 5 月，美国哈佛大学和伦敦大学学院（UCL）联合的一支团队公布了一项面向 1600 人的网络调查结果，提示多达 2% 的人在某种程度上存在脸盲症状。

sentences.en: Then in August, Martina Gruter and colleagues at the Institute for Human Genetics in Munster, Germany, similarly reported that 2.5 per cent of 700 secondary-school pupils they had tested had trouble recognising faces.
sentences.zh: 接着 8 月，德国明斯特人类遗传学研究所的玛蒂娜·格鲁特（Martina Gruter）及其同事也发布了类似报告，称在他们所测试的 700 名中学生中，有 2.5% 的人在辨认人脸方面存在困难。

sentences.en: The results of the surveys took everyone by surprise.
sentences.zh: 这些调查结果让所有人都大感意外。

sentences.en: (C) It seems that if you have never known what it is to recognise a face, you don't necessarily know that you are supposed to be able to.
sentences.zh: 看来，如果你从不知道认出一张人脸是怎样的体验，你也未必意识到自己本该能认出。

sentences.en: Prosopagnosics almost always know that they have trouble recognising people, but they often don't realise that other people have better recognition skills than they do, says Brad Duchaine, a researcher at UCL.
sentences.zh: UCL 的研究员布拉德·杜申（Brad Duchaine）表示，脸盲症患者几乎都知道自己在辨认他人方面有困难，但他们往往意识不到别人的辨识能力其实比自己更强。

sentences.en: Despite these issues, the majority of developmental prosopagnosics possess strategies that allow them to get around their difficulty—for instance, by recognising hair, clothing, or a person's way of speaking—so, unless they see a familiar person out of context, with a new hairstyle or in different clothes, they can recognise people just fine.
sentences.zh: 尽管存在这些问题，绝大多数发育型脸盲患者都拥有一些绕开困难的策略——例如靠发型、衣着或说话方式来辨识他人——所以，只要不是在意料之外的场合见到熟人，或对方换了新发型、穿了不同的衣服，他们就能正常地认出别人。

sentences.en: Even so, the discovery of developmental prosopagnosia has attracted attention from neuroscientists keen to discover what is different about the brain of face-blind people.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，发育型脸盲症的发现仍引起了神经科学家的注意，他们渴望弄清脸盲者的大脑究竟有何不同。

sentences.en: This difference, they believe, could help solve the problem of how the brain deals with information in general, not just visual data.
sentences.zh: 他们相信，这种差异有助于解开大脑总体处理信息——而不仅仅是视觉数据——的奥秘。

sentences.en: In other words, it may show whether the brain has specialised parts for specific tasks or is more of a general-purpose information processor.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，它或许能揭示大脑究竟是为特定任务设有专门区域，还是更像一个通用型的信息处理器。

sentences.en: (D) One issue, however, that will present challenges for researchers is that no two prosopagnosics are the same.
sentences.zh: 然而有一个问题会让研究人员颇感棘手，那就是没有两位脸盲患者是完全相同的。

sentences.en: Some have problems only with faces, while others have trouble with ordinary everyday objects and, so it turns out, animals which would normally be familiar as well.
sentences.zh: 有人只是认不出脸，另一些人则连普通日常物品也辨识不清，事实证明，本应熟悉的动物对他们也同样难认。

sentences.en: Some prosopagnosics can train themselves to recognise specific faces; others can't even recognise their own in a mirror.
sentences.zh: 有些脸盲患者能训练自己辨认某些特定面孔；另一些人则连自己在镜中的容貌都认不出来。

sentences.en: When some have been tested they could identify the emotion that was conveyed on another's face, even though the face itself seemed unfamiliar, while for other subjects this was an impossibility.
sentences.zh: 在测试中，有些人即便看一张陌生脸，也能识别其所传递的情绪，而对另一些受试者而言，这是根本无法做到的。

sentences.en: Some cannot recognise the faces of old friends or fellow students but have no trouble telling whether a particular face from such groups would be attractive to most people.
sentences.zh: 有些人认不出老朋友或同学的脸，却毫不费力地判断出这些人中的某张脸是否会让大多数人觉得有吸引力。

sentences.en: Because of this diversity, working out the cause of prosopagnosia will not be easy.
sentences.zh: 正因为存在这种多样性，要弄清脸盲症的成因绝非易事。

sentences.en: (E) In Martina Gruter's study, the prosopagnosics who agreed to have their parents and relatives tested reported at least one relative with the condition.
sentences.zh: 在玛蒂娜·格鲁特的研究中，那些同意让父母和亲属也接受测试的脸盲患者都报告说，至少有一位亲属也有同样的症状。

sentences.en: Having looked at 38 cases in seven families, the German team believe they have good evidence that a single gene could be responsible.
sentences.zh: 在考察了 7 个家族中的 38 个病例之后，这支德国团队认为他们已掌握有力证据，提示这一切可能由单一基因所致。

sentences.en: Duchaine also has some evidence that face blindness could be inherited but thinks other factors might be more significant.
sentences.zh: 杜申也掌握一些证据，表明脸盲症可能会遗传，但他认为还有其他因素或许更为重要。

sentences.en: He refers to studies of babies born with a condition which means the eye's lens is not clear, and when it's the left one, being unable to see through this eye during the first two months of life is a major risk factor for prosopagnosia.
sentences.zh: 他提到有研究关注那些出生时眼球晶状体不清的婴儿，当受影响的是左眼时，出生头两个月里这只眼睛看不清，会成为日后患脸盲症的重要风险因素。

sentences.en: (F) Whatever the cause, what most prosopagnosics want to know is whether they can do anything to improve their face-recognition skills.
sentences.zh: 不论病因为何，大多数脸盲患者最想知道的是：他们能不能做点什么来改善自己的人脸辨识能力。

sentences.en: Joseph DeGutis, a graduate student at the University of California, recently reported successfully training a severe developmental prosopagnosic to recognise faces during tests carried out in the laboratory.
sentences.zh: 加州大学的研究生约瑟夫·德古蒂斯（Joseph DeGutis）近期报告称，他成功训练一位重度发育型脸盲患者，使其在实验室测试中能够辨认人脸。

sentences.en: The subject also reported that recognising faces in everyday life became easier due to the training.
sentences.zh: 这名受试者还反映，经过训练后，在日常生活中辨认人脸也变得更容易了。

sentences.en: Duchaine now plans to attempt to train sufferers to recognise the five people they most need to know—maybe their immediate family, for example, and essential colleagues.
sentences.zh: 杜申现在打算尝试训练患者辨认他们最需要认得的五个人——比如直系亲属和不可或缺的同事。

sentences.en: Thomas Gruter, Martina Gruter's husband, who also works on her team, however, is not convinced it will work.
sentences.zh: 不过，玛蒂娜·格鲁特的丈夫托马斯·格鲁特（Thomas Gruter）——他也是团队成员——并不相信这种训练会奏效。

sentences.en: 'I don't know how you can have more training than you have already had,' he says.
sentences.zh: “我不知道你还能怎么再加训练，毕竟我们已经接受了远远不止这些的训练，”他说。

sentences.en: 'Humans already spend all day looking at faces.'
sentences.zh: “人类本来就整天都在看脸。”

sentences.en: He also points out that cheating is a possibility during tests and provides an example.
sentences.zh: 他还指出，受试者在测试中存在作弊的可能，并举了一个例子。

sentences.en: One person we studied said that when she was doing the face-recognition test, she memorised the distance between nose and upper lip.
sentences.zh: 我们研究过的一位受试者说，在做人脸识别测试时，她记住的是鼻子和上唇之间的距离。

sentences.en: She wasn't the only one.
sentences.zh: 她不是唯一这么做的人。

sentences.en: So you can perform well in the test and not do so well in real life.
sentences.zh: 所以，一个人可能在测试中表现良好，到了现实生活中却未必如此。
