sentences.en: (A) The naturalist and author of On the Origin of Species, Charles Darwin, was fascinated by carnivorous plants.
sentences.zh: 博物学家、《物种起源》的作者查尔斯·达尔文，对食肉植物着迷不已。

sentences.en: In 1860, soon after he came across his first carnivorous plant — the sundew, Drosera — he wrote, ‘I care more about Drosera than the origin of all the species in the world.’
sentences.zh: 1860年，在他初次见到第一种食肉植物——茅膏菜（Drosera）后不久，他写道：“比起世界上所有物种的起源，我更在意茅膏菜。”

sentences.en: He spent months running experiments on the plants.
sentences.zh: 他花了好几个月对这些植物进行实验。

sentences.en: He dropped flies and bits of meat on their leaves and watched them slowly fold their sticky tentacles over their prey.
sentences.zh: 他把苍蝇和小块肉放到它们的叶片上，看着它们缓缓地把黏性的触毛合拢在猎物之上。

sentences.en: He thought it incredible that brushing a leaf with a single strand of human hair was enough to bring about a response.
sentences.zh: 他觉得不可思议的是，用一根人的头发轻拂叶片，竟足以引发反应。

sentences.en: Yet sundews, he observed, ignored raindrops.
sentences.zh: 然而他观察到，茅膏菜对雨滴却无动于衷。

sentences.en: To react to such a false alarm, he reasoned, would obviously be a great evil to the plant.
sentences.zh: 他推断，对这样一个假信号作出反应，对植物来说显然是一种很大的损害。

sentences.en: This was no accident.
sentences.zh: 这绝非偶然。

sentences.en: This was adaptation.
sentences.zh: 这是一种适应。

sentences.en: (B) Darwin expanded his studies from sundews to other species in his book Insectivorous Plants.
sentences.zh: 在《食虫植物》一书中，达尔文把研究从茅膏菜扩展到了其他物种。

sentences.en: He was amazed at the quickness and power of the Venus flytrap.
sentences.zh: 捕蝇草的迅捷与力量令他惊叹。

sentences.en: He showed that when one of its leaves snapped shut, it formed itself into a temporary ‘stomach’, secreting enzymes that could dissolve the prey.
sentences.zh: 他证明，当它的一片叶子猛然合拢时，会把自己变成一个临时的“胃”，分泌能够溶解猎物的酶。

sentences.en: He noted that a leaf took more than a week to reopen after closing, and reasoned that the interlocking spines along the margin of the leaf allowed tiny insects to escape, saving the plant the expense of digesting an insufficient meal.
sentences.zh: 他注意到一片叶子合拢后要花一个多星期才能重新张开，并由此推断，叶缘那一排相互交错的刺能让极小的昆虫逃走，从而省去植物消化一顿不够分量的餐食的代价。

sentences.en: (C) Today, biologists using 21st-century tools to study cells and DNA are beginning to understand how these plants hunt, eat, and digest — and how these strange adaptations came about in the first place.
sentences.zh: 如今，生物学家利用21世纪的工具研究细胞和DNA，开始理解这些植物是如何捕猎、进食和消化的——以及这些奇特的适应性当初究竟是怎样产生的。

sentences.en: Alexander Volkov, a plant physiologist at Oakwood University in Alabama, believes he has figured out the Venus flytrap’s secret.
sentences.zh: 亚拉巴马州橡木大学的植物生理学家亚历山大·沃尔科夫相信，他已经弄清了捕蝇草的秘密。

sentences.en: ‘This,’ Volkov declares, ‘is an electrical plant.’
sentences.zh: “这，”沃尔科夫宣称，“是一种带电的植物。”

sentences.en: When an insect brushes against a hair on the leaf of a Venus flytrap, the movement sets off an electric charge.
sentences.zh: 当昆虫蹭到捕蝇草叶片上的一根感觉毛时，这一动作便会触发一股电荷。

sentences.en: The charge builds up inside the tissue of the leaf but is not enough to stimulate the snap, which keeps the Venus flytrap from reacting to false alarms, such as raindrops.
sentences.zh: 电荷在叶片组织内积聚，但还不足以触发合拢，这使捕蝇草不会对雨滴之类的假信号作出反应。

sentences.en: An insect, however, is likely to brush a second hair, adding enough electric charge for the leaf to close.
sentences.zh: 然而昆虫很可能会蹭到第二根感觉毛，从而补足电荷，使叶片闭合。

sentences.en: (D) Volkov’s experiments reveal that the electric charge travels down fluid-filled tunnels in a leaf, which opens up pores in cell membranes.
sentences.zh: 沃尔科夫的实验揭示，电荷沿着叶片中充满液体的通道传导，从而打开了细胞膜上的孔道。

sentences.en: Water rushes from the cells on the inside of the leaf to those on the outside, causing the leaf to rapidly flip in shape from convex to concave, like a soft contact lens.
sentences.zh: 水分从叶片内侧的细胞涌向外侧的细胞，使叶片的形状迅速由凸翻转为凹，就像一片柔软的隐形眼镜。

sentences.en: As the leaves flip, they snap together, trapping an insect inside.
sentences.zh: 随着叶片翻转，它们猛然合拢，把昆虫困在里面。

sentences.en: (E) The bladderwort plant has an equally sophisticated way of setting its underwater trap.
sentences.zh: 狸藻则有一套同样精巧的方式来布设它的水下陷阱。

sentences.en: It pumps water out of tiny air sacs or bladders, lowering the pressure inside.
sentences.zh: 它把水从微小的气囊或囊泡中抽出，降低内部的压力。

sentences.en: When a water flea or some other small creature swims past, it bends hairs on the bladder, causing a flap to spring apart.
sentences.zh: 当水蚤或其他小生物游过时，会碰弯囊泡上的细毛，使一片活瓣猛然弹开。

sentences.en: The low pressure sucks water in, carrying the creature along with it.
sentences.zh: 低压把水吸入，连带着把那只生物也一起卷了进去。

sentences.en: In one five-hundredth of a second, the flap swings shut again.
sentences.zh: 在五百分之一秒内，活瓣又重新合上。

sentences.en: The cells in the bladder then begin to pump water out again, creating a new vacuum.
sentences.zh: 随后囊泡中的细胞又开始把水抽出，形成新的真空。

sentences.en: Many other species of carnivorous plants act like living flypaper, catching animals on sticky tentacles.
sentences.zh: 许多其他种类的食肉植物则像活的捕蝇纸，用黏性的触毛捕捉动物。

sentences.en: Pitcher plants use yet another strategy, growing long tube-shaped leaves into which insects fall.
sentences.zh: 猪笼草采用的又是另一种策略，它长出长长的管状叶子，昆虫会掉落其中。

sentences.en: Some of the largest have pitchers up to 30cm deep and can consume whole frogs unlucky enough to fall into them.
sentences.zh: 其中最大的一些，捕虫笼深达30厘米，能够吞食那些不幸掉进去的整只青蛙。

sentences.en: Sophisticated chemistry helps make the pitcher a death trap.
sentences.zh: 精妙的化学作用帮助把这种捕虫笼变成了致命的陷阱。

sentences.en: (F) Nicholas Gotelli, of the University of Vermont, is trying to figure out what evolutionary forces pushed these plants towards meat.
sentences.zh: 佛蒙特大学的尼古拉斯·戈泰利正试图弄清，是什么样的进化力量把这些植物推向了食肉。

sentences.en: Carnivorous plants clearly benefit from eating animals; when scientists feed pitcher plants extra bugs, the plants get bigger.
sentences.zh: 食肉植物显然能从吃动物中获益；当科学家给猪笼草多喂一些虫子时，植株会长得更大。

sentences.en: But the benefits of eating flesh are not the ones you might expect.
sentences.zh: 但吃肉带来的好处，并不是你可能以为的那种。

sentences.en: Carnivorous animals, like ourselves, use the carbon in protein and the fat in meat to build muscles and store energy.
sentences.zh: 像我们人类这样的食肉动物，利用蛋白质中的碳和肉中的脂肪来构建肌肉、储存能量。

sentences.en: Carnivorous plants, however, take nitrogen and phosphorus from the flesh in order to build light-harvesting enzymes.
sentences.zh: 然而食肉植物却是从肉中摄取氮和磷，用以构建采集光能的酶。

sentences.en: Eating animals, in other words, lets carnivorous plants do what all plants do: grow by taking energy directly from the sun.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，吃动物让食肉植物得以做所有植物都做的事：直接从太阳获取能量来生长。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, they do a really bad job of it.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，它们在这件事上做得非常糟糕。

sentences.en: That’s because they have to use a lot of energy to make the equipment they need to catch animals — the enzymes, the pumps, the sticky tentacles, and so on.
sentences.zh: 这是因为它们必须耗费大量能量来制造捕捉动物所需的“装备”——那些酶、泵和黏性触毛等等。

sentences.en: A pitcher or a flytrap is not very good at photosynthesis because, unlike plants with ordinary leaves, it does not have flat solar panels that can absorb lots of sunlight.
sentences.zh: 猪笼草或捕蝇草并不擅长光合作用，因为与长着普通叶子的植物不同，它没有能够吸收大量阳光的平展“太阳能板”。

sentences.en: Gotelli suspects that only under special conditions are the benefits of being carnivorous greater than the costs.
sentences.zh: 戈泰利推测，只有在特殊条件下，食肉的好处才会大于代价。

sentences.en: The poor soil of bogs and swamps, where many carnivorous plants grow, offers little nitrogen and phosphorus, so carnivorous plants enjoy an advantage there over ‘conventional’ plants.
sentences.zh: 许多食肉植物生长的沼泽和湿地土壤贫瘠，几乎提供不了多少氮和磷，因此食肉植物在那里比“普通”植物更占优势。

sentences.en: Also, bogs are often flooded with sunshine, so even an inefficient carnivorous plant can carry out enough photosynthesis to survive.
sentences.zh: 此外，沼泽常常阳光充沛，因此即便是一株效率不高的食肉植物，也能进行足够的光合作用以维持生存。

sentences.en: ‘They’re stuck, and they’re making the best of it,’ says Aaron Ellison of Harvard University.
sentences.zh: “它们被困在这样的环境里，只能尽量利用现有条件，”哈佛大学的亚伦·埃利森说。

sentences.en: (G) Unfortunately, the adaptations that enable carnivorous plants to survive in harsh habitats also make them extremely sensitive to environmental changes.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，使食肉植物得以在严酷生境中生存的那些适应性，也让它们对环境变化极为敏感。

sentences.en: Chemical fertilizers used in agriculture and pollution from power plants are adding extra nitrogen to many bogs in North America.
sentences.zh: 农业中使用的化肥和发电厂造成的污染，正给北美许多沼泽增添额外的氮。

sentences.en: Carnivorous plants are so finely adapted to low levels of nitrogen that this extra fertilizer is overloading their systems.
sentences.zh: 食肉植物对低氮环境的适应如此精细，以致这些额外的养分正使它们的系统不堪重负。

sentences.en: Humans also threaten carnivorous plants in other ways.
sentences.zh: 人类还以其他方式威胁着食肉植物。

sentences.en: The black market trade in exotic carnivorous plants is strong, but even if this can be prevented, carnivorous plants will continue to suffer from other dangers.
sentences.zh: 奇异食肉植物的黑市交易十分活跃，但即便能加以遏制，食肉植物仍将继续遭受其他危险的侵害。

sentences.en: Their habitat is disappearing, to be replaced by shopping centers and houses.
sentences.zh: 它们的栖息地正在消失，取而代之的是购物中心和住宅。

sentences.en: The suppression of wildfires by government agencies allows other plants to grow quickly and outcompete the Venus flytraps.
sentences.zh: 政府机构对野火的扑灭，使得其他植物得以迅速生长，并在竞争中压过捕蝇草。

sentences.en: Good news, perhaps, for flies.
sentences.zh: 这或许对苍蝇来说是个好消息。

sentences.en: But a loss for all who delight in the inventiveness of evolution.
sentences.zh: 但对所有醉心于进化之巧思的人而言，却是一种损失。

records.title: A Brief History of Humans and Food

sentences.en: (A) During the journey from our hunter-gatherer ancestors to the present day, there have been three seismic changes that have impacted the food we eat: the discovery of cooking, the emergence of agriculture, and the invention of methods of preserving food.
sentences.zh: 从我们的狩猎采集祖先到今天的历程中，有三次撼动性的变化影响了我们所吃的食物：烹饪的发现、农业的出现，以及保存食物方法的发明。

sentences.en: The 19th-century scientist Charles Darwin thought that cooking, after language, was the greatest discovery made by man.
sentences.zh: 19 世纪科学家查尔斯·达尔文（Charles Darwin）认为，烹饪是人类继语言之后所做的最伟大的发现。

sentences.en: All of us eat some raw food, such as fruit and vegetables, but the great majority of food we consume is cooked.
sentences.zh: 我们都吃一些生食，例如水果和蔬菜，但我们所食用的绝大部分食物是煮过的。

sentences.en: Cooking can turn plants that are inedible into edible food by destroying toxic chemicals that plants often manufacture to protect themselves against attack by insects or other herbivorous animals.
sentences.zh: 烹饪可以通过破坏植物常为保护自己免受昆虫或其他食草动物攻击而合成的有毒化学物质，把不可食用的植物变成可食用的食物。

sentences.en: These toxic chemicals are referred to as “plant secondary compounds” because they are not directly involved in the plant's normal growth, development, and reproduction, and are produced purely as chemical defenses.
sentences.zh: 这些有毒化学物质被称为“植物次生化合物”，因为它们不直接参与植物的正常生长、发育和繁殖，纯粹是作为化学防御被产生的。

sentences.en: They give many of the plants we consume, such as coffee or Brussels sprouts, their bitter taste.
sentences.zh: 它们给我们食用的许多植物——比如咖啡或抱子甘蓝——带来苦味。

sentences.en: (B) Cooked food is often more digestible because heat breaks down tough cellulose cell walls in plants or tough connective tissue in animals.
sentences.zh: 煮过的食物常常更易消化，因为热量分解了植物中坚韧的纤维素细胞壁或动物中坚韧的结缔组织。

sentences.en: Chewing raw turnip, a plate of uncooked rice, or a raw leg of lamb is much harder work than eating the cooked equivalent.
sentences.zh: 嚼生芜菁、一盘未煮过的米饭或一条生羊腿，比吃同样的煮过版本要费劲得多。

sentences.en: The energy expended in chewing to break down the tough material is replaced by energy from the fuel used in cooking the food, so the ratio of energy gained to energy expended by the body is greater when food is cooked.
sentences.zh: 用以咀嚼、分解坚韧物质所消耗的能量被烹饪食物所使用的燃料能量取代，所以食物被煮过时，身体获得的能量与消耗的能量之比更高。

sentences.en: (C) Until the development of agriculture, hunter-gatherers spent up to seven hours a day gathering food.
sentences.zh: 在农业发展之前，狩猎采集者每天要花长达 7 小时来采集食物。

sentences.en: This all began to change around 10,500 years ago with the advent of farming, which led to dramatic changes in human societies.
sentences.zh: 这一切大约在 10500 年前随着农耕的出现开始改变，农耕给人类社会带来了戏剧性的变化。

sentences.en: People began to create a variety of new tools to aid survival, and in turn, populations increased in size.
sentences.zh: 人们开始制造各种新工具以帮助生存，反过来人口规模也增加了。

sentences.en: These changes led to the possibility of specialization of different tasks within society.
sentences.zh: 这些变化使社会内部不同任务的专业化成为可能。

sentences.en: Around this time, writing became more sophisticated and allowed people to maintain records of the harvest and taxes.
sentences.zh: 大约在这一时期，文字变得更复杂，让人们得以保存收成和税收的记录。

sentences.en: Eventually, formalized structures of government were established as people settled in one area.
sentences.zh: 最终，随着人们在一个地方定居，正式的政府结构得以建立。

sentences.en: (D) The arrival of agriculture meant that, for the first time, our ancestors had more food than they could eat immediately.
sentences.zh: 农业的到来意味着，我们的祖先第一次拥有了超过他们能立即吃掉的食物。

sentences.en: This, combined with the seasonality of production, led them to discover methods of preserving food: smoking, drying, adding acid by fermentation, or adding salt.
sentences.zh: 这一点与生产的季节性相结合，促使他们发现了保存食物的方法：熏制、晾干、通过发酵增酸或加盐。

sentences.en: These four methods all share one feature in common—they make the food a more hostile environment for bacteria that can cause it to spoil.
sentences.zh: 这四种方法都有一个共同特征——它们让食物对可能导致腐败的细菌而言成为更不友好的环境。

sentences.en: They also tend to slow down natural chemical reactions in the food that would cause decay.
sentences.zh: 它们也会减慢食物中导致腐烂的自然化学反应。

sentences.en: (E) Although foods today are still preserved in these ancient ways, two more recent methods of preserving food have become more common: canning and freezing.
sentences.zh: 尽管今天仍以这些古老方法保存食物，但两种较新的食品保存方法已经更为常见：罐装和冷冻。

sentences.en: Canning was invented by a Frenchman, Nicolas Appert, in the early 19th century.
sentences.zh: 罐装由一位法国人尼古拉·阿佩尔（Nicolas Appert）于 19 世纪初发明。

sentences.en: He sealed food in bottles fabricated from glass and then heated them in boiling water to cook the contents.
sentences.zh: 他把食物封在玻璃瓶中，然后在沸水中加热以煮熟瓶内的食物。

sentences.en: Appert's method had great advantages over older methods of food preservation: it could be applied to a wide range of foods, and the flavor and texture were similar to freshly cooked products.
sentences.zh: 阿佩尔的方法相比此前的食物保存方法具有巨大优势：它可以应用于多种食物，且风味和口感与新鲜烹制的产品相似。

sentences.en: His idea was soon copied by an Englishman, Peter Durand.
sentences.zh: 他的想法很快被一位英国人彼得·杜兰德（Peter Durand）效仿。

sentences.en: Until this point, containers had been too heavy to be widely used, but Durand produced the first ones which were lightweight and resistant to damage.
sentences.zh: 在那之前，容器太重以至于无法被广泛使用，但杜兰德首次生产出轻便、不易损坏的容器。

sentences.en: Two years later, in 1812, two Englishmen, Bryan Donkin and John Hall, started the commercial canning of food, although the real rise in popularity of canning had to wait until the invention of the can opener in 1855.
sentences.zh: 两年后，即 1812 年，两位英国人布莱恩·东金（Bryan Donkin）和约翰·霍尔（John Hall）开始了食品罐头的商业化生产，尽管罐装真正的流行兴起要等到 1855 年开罐器的发明。

sentences.en: Until then, cans were opened with a chisel and hammer.
sentences.zh: 在那之前，罐头是用凿子和锤子打开的。

sentences.en: Canning is an extremely effective way of preserving food: one can containing meat, dating back to 1824, was opened in 1939, and the contents were still in good condition.
sentences.zh: 罐装是一种极其有效的食物保存方法：一罐 1824 年的肉罐头在 1939 年被打开，里面的食物仍处于良好状态。

sentences.en: (F) In the 21st century, the dominance of canning as a method of food preservation has been overtaken by freezing.
sentences.zh: 到了 21 世纪，罐装作为食物保存方法的主导地位已被冷冻所取代。

sentences.en: Chilling food to keep it fresh is an old idea.
sentences.zh: 为保鲜而冷藏食物的想法由来已久。

sentences.en: The earliest mentions of icehouses, thick-walled buildings, half underground, date back to 1700 BC in northwest Iran.
sentences.zh: 最早提到冰窖——一种厚壁的、半地下的建筑——可以追溯到公元前 1700 年的伊朗西北部。

sentences.en: In early 16th-century Italy, water was mixed with chemicals to lower its freezing point to -18 degrees Celsius.
sentences.zh: 在 16 世纪初的意大利，水被与化学物质混合以把冻结温度降至零下 18 摄氏度。

sentences.en: Several centuries later, frozen fish and other goods were transported by ship from Australia to England.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪后，冷冻的鱼和其他货物开始用船从澳大利亚运到英格兰。

sentences.en: However, the modern frozen food industry was started in the 1920s by an American, Clarence Birdseye.
sentences.zh: 然而，现代冷冻食品产业是 1920 年代由美国人克拉伦斯·伯德赛（Clarence Birdseye）开创的。

sentences.en: While on a fishing trip with the Inuit in the Canadian Arctic, Birdseye observed that rapid freezing creates smaller ice crystals and therefore causes less damage to food—a discovery he had not expected.
sentences.zh: 在加拿大北极地区与因纽特人一起垂钓时，伯德赛观察到快速冷冻形成的冰晶更小，因此对食物造成的损害更小——这是他没有预料到的发现。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the major growth in demand for frozen food came with the arrival of freezers in ordinary people's homes.
sentences.zh: 但是，对冷冻食物需求的真正大增是随着冷冻柜进入普通家庭而出现的。

sentences.en: The advantages of frozen over canned food include the fact that the flavor and consistency are often identical to the fresh product, and freezing can be used to preserve a wide variety of foods.
sentences.zh: 冷冻食品相比罐装食品的优势包括：其风味和口感往往与新鲜产品相同，并且冷冻可以用来保存各种各样的食物。

sentences.en: (A) Cuneiform, the world's first known system of handwriting, originated some 6,000 years ago in Sumer in what is now southern Iraq.
sentences.zh: 楔形文字是世界已知最早的手写系统，约 6000 年前起源于今天伊拉克南部的苏美尔（Sumer）。

sentences.en: It was most often inscribed on palm-sized, rectangular clay tablets measuring several centimetres across, although occasionally larger tablets or cylinders were used.
sentences.zh: 它最常被刻在巴掌大的、几厘米见方的矩形泥板上，偶尔也使用更大的泥板或圆柱。

sentences.en: Clay was an excellent medium for writing.
sentences.zh: 黏土是一种极佳的书写介质。

sentences.en: Other surfaces which have been employed—for example, parchment, papyrus and paper—are not long lasting and are easily destroyed by fire and water.
sentences.zh: 曾被使用的其他表面——例如羊皮纸、纸莎草和纸——并不耐久，且容易被火和水毁坏。

sentences.en: But clay has proved to be resistant to those particular kinds of damage.
sentences.zh: 但黏土被证明能抵抗那几种特别的破坏。

sentences.en: The word 'cuneiform' actually refers to the marks or signs inscribed in the clay.
sentences.zh: “楔形文字”（cuneiform）一词实际上指的是刻在泥土上的痕迹或符号。

sentences.en: The original cuneiform signs consisted of a series of lines—triangular, vertical, diagonal, and horizontal.
sentences.zh: 最初的楔形符号由一连串线条构成——三角形的、垂直的、斜的和水平的。

sentences.en: Sumerian writers would impress these lines into the wet clay with a stylus—a long, thin, pointed instrument which looked somewhat like a pen.
sentences.zh: 苏美尔的书写者会用一种叫做尖笔（stylus）——一种细长、有尖头、外形有点像笔的工具——把这些线条压入湿黏土中。

sentences.en: Oddly, the signs were often almost too small to see with the naked eye.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，这些符号往往小到几乎肉眼难以辨认。

sentences.en: Cuneiform signs were used for the writing of at least a dozen languages.
sentences.zh: 楔形符号被用来书写至少十几种语言。

sentences.en: This is similar to how the Latin alphabet is used today for writing English, French, Spanish and German, for example.
sentences.zh: 这类似于拉丁字母如今被用来书写英语、法语、西班牙语和德语等。

sentences.en: (B) Before the development of cuneiform, tokens were used by the Sumerians to record certain information.
sentences.zh: 在楔形文字发展之前，苏美尔人使用代币来记录某些信息。

sentences.en: For example, they might take small stones and use them as tokens or representations of something else, like a goat.
sentences.zh: 例如，他们可能取小石子用作代币或某物——比如一只山羊——的代表。

sentences.en: A number of tokens, then, might mean a herd of goats.
sentences.zh: 一定数量的代币就可能意味着一群山羊。

sentences.en: These tokens might then be placed in a cloth container and provided to a buyer as a receipt for a transaction, perhaps five tokens for five animals.
sentences.zh: 这些代币随后可能被放入一个布袋容器中，作为交易凭证交给买方——也许是用 5 个代币代表 5 只动物。

sentences.en: It was not that different from what we do today when we buy some bread and the clerk gives us back a piece of paper with numbers on it to confirm the exchange.
sentences.zh: 这与今天我们买面包时店员给我们一张写着数字的纸来确认交易的做法没什么不同。

sentences.en: By the 4th century BCE, the Sumerians had adapted this system to a form of writing.
sentences.zh: 到公元前 4 世纪，苏美尔人把这一体系改造成了一种文字。

sentences.en: They began putting tokens in a container resembling an envelope, one made of clay instead of cloth.
sentences.zh: 他们开始把代币放在一种类似信封的容器中——用黏土而非布制成。

sentences.en: They then stamped the outside to indicate the number and type of tokens inside.
sentences.zh: 然后他们在外面盖上印记，标明里面代币的数量和种类。

sentences.en: A person could then 'read' what was stamped on the container and know what was inside.
sentences.zh: 一个人于是可以“读”容器外面所盖的印记，知道里面装的是什么。

sentences.en: (C) Gradually, Sumerians developed symbols for words.
sentences.zh: 渐渐地，苏美尔人发展出了表示词语的符号。

sentences.en: When first developed, each symbol looked like the concrete thing it represented.
sentences.zh: 最初被创造出来时，每个符号看起来都像它所代表的具体事物。

sentences.en: For example, an image which resembled the drawing of a sheep meant just that.
sentences.zh: 例如，一个看起来像绵羊图样的图像，意思就是绵羊。

sentences.en: Then another level of abstraction was introduced when symbols were developed for intangible ideas such as 'female' or 'hot' or 'God'.
sentences.zh: 随后又引入了另一层抽象——人们为“女性”“热”或“神”等无形概念创造符号。

sentences.en: Cuneiform, in other words, evolved from a way used primarily to track and store information into a way to represent the world symbolically.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，楔形文字从主要用于跟踪和储存信息的方式，演化为以符号表达世界的方式。

sentences.en: Over the centuries, the marks became ever more abstract, finally evolving into signs that looked nothing like what they referred to, just as the letters 'h-o-u-s-e' have no visual connection to the place we live in.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，这些标记变得越来越抽象，最终演化为与所指事物毫无相像的符号——正如字母“h-o-u-s-e”与我们居住的地方没有视觉上的联系一样。

sentences.en: At this last stage in the evolution of cuneiform, the signs took the form of triangles, which became common cuneiform signs.
sentences.zh: 在楔形文字演化的这最后阶段，符号呈现出三角形的形态，成为常见的楔形符号。

sentences.en: As the marks became more abstract, the system became more efficient because there were fewer marks for a 'reader' to learn.
sentences.zh: 随着标记越来越抽象，体系变得越来越高效，因为“读者”要学的符号变少了。

sentences.en: But cuneiform also became more complex because society itself was becoming more complex, so there were more ideas and concepts that needed to be expressed.
sentences.zh: 但楔形文字也变得越来越复杂，因为社会本身在变得越来越复杂，需要表达的思想和概念越来越多。

sentences.en: However, most linguists and historians agree cuneiform developed primarily as a tool for accounting.
sentences.zh: 然而，多数语言学家和历史学家都同意，楔形文字主要是作为一种会计工具发展起来的。

sentences.en: Of the cuneiform tablets that have been discovered, excavated and translated, about 75 percent contain this type of practical information, rather than artistic or imaginative work.
sentences.zh: 在已被发现、发掘并翻译出的楔形泥板中，约 75% 包含这类实用性信息，而非艺术或想象性的作品。

sentences.en: (D) Cuneiform writing was used for thousands of years, but it eventually ceased to be used in everyday life.
sentences.zh: 楔形文字被使用了数千年，但最终在日常生活中不再使用。

sentences.en: In fact, it died out and remained unintelligible for almost 2,000 years.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它消亡了，并在近 2000 年间一直无法被解读。

sentences.en: In the late 19th century, a British army officer, Henry Rawlinson, discovered cuneiform inscriptions which had been carved into the surface of rocks in the Behistun Mountains in what is present-day Iran.
sentences.zh: 在 19 世纪后期，英国陆军军官亨利·罗林森（Henry Rawlinson）发现了刻在今伊朗贝希斯敦山岩石表面的楔形铭文。

sentences.en: Rawlinson made impressions of the marks on large pieces of paper as he balanced dangerously on the surrounding rocks.
sentences.zh: 罗林森在周围岩石上危险地保持平衡，用大张的纸把这些标记的拓印取了下来。

sentences.en: Rawlinson took his copies home to Britain and studied them for years to determine what each line stood for, and what each group of symbols meant.
sentences.zh: 罗林森把抄件带回英国，研究了多年来判定每一行代表什么、每一组符号意味着什么。

sentences.en: He found that, in the writing on those particular rocks, every word was repeated three times in three languages: Old Persian, Elamite and Babylonian.
sentences.zh: 他发现，在那些特定岩石上的文字中，每个词都用三种语言重复了三次：古波斯语、埃兰语和巴比伦语。

sentences.en: Since the meanings in these languages were already known to linguists, he could thus translate the cuneiform.
sentences.zh: 由于语言学家已经知道这些语言的意思，他因此可以翻译楔形文字。

sentences.en: Eventually, he fully decoded the cuneiform marks and discovered that they described the life of Darius, a king of the Persian Empire in the 5th century BCE.
sentences.zh: 最终，他完全破译了楔形标记，并发现它们描述的是公元前 5 世纪波斯帝国国王大流士（Darius）的生平。

1.stemZh: 楔形文字泥板有各种不同的形状和尺寸。

7.stemZh: 当苏美尔文人刻写泥板时，这些泥板是干燥的。

8.stemZh: 楔形文字由于字形较大，通常难以阅读。

9.stemZh: 许多语言采用了楔形文字。

10.stemZh: 楔形文字符号可以在一些现代字母中找到。

sentences.en: (A) TF became a retail success in the 1970s when it succeeded in spotting homeware trends and meeting the needs of its then trendy young customers.
sentences.zh: TF在1970年代成为零售业的成功典范，当时它成功捕捉到家居用品的潮流，满足了其当时时尚的年轻顾客的需求。

sentences.en: However, by 2004, the TF stores were failing and a rethink was clearly necessary.
sentences.zh: 然而到2004年，TF门店经营每况愈下，显然有必要重新思考。

sentences.en: Tibal Fisher, TF's founder and CEO, decided to change its focus under a new brand name, TF's Nextstage.
sentences.zh: TF的创始人兼首席执行官蒂巴尔·费舍尔决定以新品牌名TF’s Nextstage来转变其经营重点。

sentences.en: His aim was to recapture the now ageing customers that had given him his early success and target consumers aged 60+ with devices and gadgets specifically designed to assist them with the problems associated with ageing: mobile phones with screens that were easy to read; kitchen gadgets with comfortable grips; electronic devices that were easy to set and adjust.
sentences.zh: 他的目标是重新赢回那些曾助他早年成功、如今已步入老年的顾客，并以专为帮助应对衰老相关问题而设计的器具和小装置来瞄准60岁以上的消费者：屏幕易于阅读的手机、握感舒适的厨房小工具、易于设置和调节的电子设备。

sentences.en: TF's market research proved to be very positive, showing strong consumer support for the products.
sentences.zh: TF的市场调研结果非常乐观，显示消费者对这些产品有强烈的支持。

sentences.en: In 2007, the stores were remodelled at a cost of US $40 million, and the new brand was launched.
sentences.zh: 2007年，门店以4000万美元的成本进行了改造，新品牌随之推出。

sentences.en: Each store was made more comfortable and featured a coffee shop to help increase traffic — Tibal had predicted that if they could get customers into the stores, then the products would sell themselves.
sentences.zh: 每家门店都被改造得更加舒适，并设有咖啡馆以帮助提升客流——蒂巴尔曾预测，只要能把顾客吸引进店，产品自然就会畅销。

sentences.en: However, by 2009 it was clear that the idea was a failure, and the stores consistently remained empty.
sentences.zh: 然而到2009年，事实清楚地表明这一构想失败了，门店始终冷冷清清。

sentences.en: Customers complained that the new stores felt like a senior center and reminded them that they were growing old.
sentences.zh: 顾客抱怨新门店让人感觉像老年活动中心，提醒着他们自己正在变老。

sentences.en: Feedback from experts
sentences.zh: 专家反馈

sentences.en: Expert 1: Donna Sturgess, global head of innovation, GlaxoSmithKline
sentences.zh: 专家一：葛兰素史克全球创新主管唐娜·斯特吉斯

sentences.en: (B) The team's customer research efforts are a classic case of missing the subconscious associations at work in consumers' minds.
sentences.zh: 该团队的顾客调研是一个典型的例子，忽视了在消费者心中起作用的潜意识联想。

sentences.en: Tibal and his executives looked only at surface attitudes.
sentences.zh: 蒂巴尔和他的高管们只看到了表层的态度。

sentences.en: Since those attitudes make up a relatively small part of the total consumer response, the executives are clueless about the reason for the poor sales.
sentences.zh: 由于这些态度只占消费者全部反应中相对很小的一部分，这些高管对销售惨淡的原因毫无头绪。

sentences.en: It's critical for companies to understand that every customer relates to a brand emotionally, and it's those emotions that trigger — or block — purchases.
sentences.zh: 企业必须明白，每一位顾客都是在情感上与品牌建立联系的，而正是这些情感触发——或阻止——购买行为。

sentences.en: That's why we've focused on using emotional strategies behind branding for a number of years now.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们多年来一直专注于在品牌塑造背后运用情感策略的原因。

sentences.en: A great example is Alli (pronounced 'ally'), a drug to aid weight loss.
sentences.zh: 一个很好的例子是Alli（读音同“ally”），一种帮助减肥的药物。

sentences.en: The product deals with a highly emotional issue, so in marketing it, we faced the same challenge that the new TF stores are facing: the very thought of buying the product reminds customers that they have problems they feel negatively about.
sentences.zh: 该产品涉及一个高度情感化的问题，因此在营销它时，我们面临着与新TF门店相同的挑战：仅仅是想到购买这种产品，就会提醒顾客他们有着令自己心生反感的问题。

sentences.en: In the case of TF's Nextstage, the problems are age and infirmity.
sentences.zh: 就TF’s Nextstage而言，这些问题是年龄和体弱。

sentences.en: In the case of Alli, the problems are excessive weight and its consequences.
sentences.zh: 就Alli而言，这些问题是超重及其后果。

sentences.en: There's always a risk that consumers' negative feelings will discourage them from starting or staying on a diet.
sentences.zh: 始终存在这样一种风险：消费者的负面情绪会使他们不愿开始或坚持节食。

sentences.en: So, after extensive market research, we took a number of steps to inject emotions into the whole process of using the product.
sentences.zh: 因此，在大量市场调研之后，我们采取了一系列措施，把情感注入使用该产品的整个过程。

sentences.en: (C) First, we came up with a name that sounds like a helpful partner.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们想出了一个听起来像贴心伙伴的名字。

sentences.en: We also aimed to make the container both beautiful and functional — something that didn't just hold pills but could later be used to store diet guides and recipes.
sentences.zh: 我们还力求让容器既美观又实用——它不仅用来装药片，日后还能用来存放饮食指南和食谱。

sentences.en: Traditional market research is unlikely to uncover ideas like this, so we use a wide variety of techniques.
sentences.zh: 传统的市场调研不太可能发掘出这样的点子，因此我们采用了多种多样的方法。

sentences.en: Even simple techniques, such as one-on-one interviews, or ethnographic observation that involves going into people's houses to examine their behaviour, can provide valuable data.
sentences.zh: 即便是简单的方法，比如一对一访谈，或是进入人们家中考察其行为的人种志观察，也能提供宝贵的数据。

sentences.en: Expert 2: Alex Lee, president of OXO International, maker of OXO Good Grips household products
sentences.zh: 专家二：OXO Good Grips家居用品制造商OXO International总裁亚历克斯·李

sentences.en: (D) This retailer can get back on track by remembering a principle that applies to consumers in general, and those aged 60+ in particular: they're attracted by brands they associate with the type of people they'd like to be — not the type they really are.
sentences.zh: 这家零售商若想重回正轨，需要记住一条对消费者普遍适用、尤其适用于60岁以上人群的原则：吸引他们的品牌，是那些让他们联想到自己想成为的那类人的品牌——而不是他们真实所属的那类人。

sentences.en: That's why marketing campaigns for surf gear feature surfers, not the city dwellers who will wear the products while doing their shopping.
sentences.zh: 这正是冲浪装备的营销活动以冲浪者为主角的原因，而不是那些买来在购物时穿的城市居民。

sentences.en: (E) I was reminded of this principle a few years ago when we wanted to find out how far we could apply our design philosophy of making things easier to use in order to move from our core business, kitchen tools, into other products.
sentences.zh: 几年前，当我们想弄清能在多大程度上推广“让产品更易使用”的设计理念，以便从厨房用具这一核心业务拓展到其他产品时，我又一次想起了这条原则。

sentences.en: We conducted what are known as focus groups, where participants were asked to look at photos of people and pick those they perceived to be users and non-users of our products.
sentences.zh: 我们开展了所谓的焦点小组，请参与者看一些人物照片，挑出他们认为是我们产品使用者和非使用者的人。

sentences.en: Consistently, they picked people who looked fit as the sort who would use our products, and people who looked old and boring as the sort who wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 他们无一例外地把看起来健康的人挑为会使用我们产品的那类人，而把看起来年老、乏味的人挑为不会使用的那类人。

sentences.en: Yet the participants, all owners of our products, looked a lot more like the latter than the former.
sentences.zh: 然而这些参与者全都是我们产品的拥有者，他们的样子更像后者而非前者。

sentences.en: (F) Although the needs of elderly users and those with deteriorating vision or dexterity are very much taken into consideration when we develop new designs, we try to offer products that appeal to 20- and 30-year-olds.
sentences.zh: 尽管在开发新设计时，我们非常充分地考虑了老年使用者以及视力或灵活性日渐衰退者的需求，但我们仍力求提供能吸引二三十岁年轻人的产品。

sentences.en: We believe that referring to these products as helping tools would serve only to harm the brand in our customers' eyes.
sentences.zh: 我们相信，把这些产品称作“辅助工具”只会在顾客眼中损害品牌形象。

sentences.en: That's why our philosophy of universal design, which involves creating products that are comfortably useable by the largest possible range of people, is never explicitly stated as part of our marketing position.
sentences.zh: 这正是为什么我们的通用设计理念——即创造能让尽可能多的人舒适使用的产品——从不被明确地纳入我们的营销定位之中。

sentences.en: We've found that market research does not need to be very sophisticated.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，市场调研并不需要非常复杂精深。

sentences.en: For instance, we have conducted simple surveys in the lobby of our building, offering free products in exchange for people's opinions.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们曾在公司大楼的门厅里做过简单的问卷调查，以免费产品换取人们的意见。

sentences.en: Some may call this unscientific, but we have uncovered great insights this way.
sentences.zh: 有人或许会说这不科学，但我们正是通过这种方式获得了极好的洞见。

sentences.en: Sometimes the most important signals come from an executive's own instincts.
sentences.zh: 有时，最重要的信号来自高管自身的直觉。

sentences.en: In Tibal Fisher's case, this could have told him what his surveys and focus groups didn't: 60-plus-year-olds won't support a business that expects them to act their age.
sentences.zh: 就蒂巴尔·费舍尔而言，直觉本可以告诉他那些问卷和焦点小组没能告诉他的东西：60多岁的人不会去支持一家期望他们“活出符合自己年纪的样子”的企业。

3.stemZh: TF Nextstage商店计划销售产品，以方便老年人的生活。

4.stemZh: TF的市场调研显示，人们喜欢这些产品。

5.stemZh: 翻新TF门店的费用比预期更高。

6.stemZh: TF Nextstage咖啡店销售自有品牌的食品和饮料。

8.stemZh: TF Nextstage的顾客喜欢新店的氛围。

records.title: The history of the British wool industry

sentences.en: (A) Wool is part of Britain's history and heritage, more so than any other commodity ever produced in that country.
sentences.zh: 羊毛是英国历史与遗产的一部分，其重要性超过该国出产过的任何其他商品。

sentences.en: It was made into cloth there in the Bronze Age, which began about 1900 BC.
sentences.zh: 早在约公元前1900年开始的青铜时代，英国就已把羊毛织成布料。

sentences.en: By the time the Romans invaded in 55 BC the Britons had developed a wool industry, and this was encouraged by their new masters.
sentences.zh: 到公元前55年罗马人入侵时，不列颠人已发展出羊毛业，而这受到了新统治者的鼓励。

sentences.en: Roman emperors appreciated the fineness of British woollen cloth.
sentences.zh: 罗马皇帝们赏识不列颠羊毛布料的精细。

sentences.en: Although Saxon invasions in the fifth century nearly destroyed the industry, it is known that in the eighth century Britain was exporting woollen fabrics to continental Europe, and after the arrival of the Norman conquerors in 1066 the industry expanded.
sentences.zh: 尽管五世纪的撒克逊人入侵几乎摧毁了这一行业，但据知八世纪时不列颠已在向欧洲大陆出口羊毛织物，而1066年诺曼征服者到来后，该行业进一步扩张。

sentences.en: By the twelfth century, wool was becoming England's greatest national asset.
sentences.zh: 到十二世纪，羊毛逐渐成为英格兰最大的国家财富。

sentences.en: Cloth making was widespread, particularly in the large towns of southern and eastern England, nearest to France.
sentences.zh: 织布业十分普遍，尤其在距离法国最近的英格兰南部和东部的大城镇。

sentences.en: But the greatest wealth came from exports of raw wool.
sentences.zh: 但最大的财富来自原毛的出口。

sentences.en: (B) Kings and their ministers welcomed the revenue that resulted from exports and export taxes – and also the power it gave to the king, who could grant or withdraw permits for the wool towns and for the industry.
sentences.zh: 国王及其大臣乐见出口和出口税带来的收入——也乐见它赋予国王的权力，国王可以授予或撤销羊毛城镇及该行业的经营许可。

sentences.en: Trade associations, known as 'guilds', were founded to guarantee good work by experienced weavers (people who produce cloth from woollen threads), and were powerful for hundreds of years.
sentences.zh: 人们成立了称为“行会”的同业组织，以保证有经验的织工（用毛线织布的人）做出优质的活计，这些行会在数百年间都颇有势力。

sentences.en: The peak of cloth production was reached in the thirteenth century.
sentences.zh: 织布业的产量在十三世纪达到顶峰。

sentences.en: Then the wool trade declined for a long period because of political conflict.
sentences.zh: 此后由于政治冲突，羊毛贸易经历了长期的衰落。

sentences.en: (C) In 1331, King Edward III encouraged master weavers from Flanders (an area of present day Belgium) to settle in England.
sentences.zh: 1331年，国王爱德华三世鼓励来自佛兰德斯（即今比利时的一片地区）的织布师傅到英格兰定居。

sentences.en: These Flemish weavers and their descendants were to play a part in the final development of English cloth.
sentences.zh: 这些佛兰德斯织工及其后代日后将在英格兰布料的最终发展中发挥作用。

sentences.en: The export trade in raw wool recovered and the first half of the fourteenth century was a time of prosperity for English wool farmers.
sentences.zh: 原毛出口贸易得以复苏，十四世纪上半叶是英格兰养羊农户的繁荣时期。

sentences.en: But it was overshadowed by a long war with France (export taxes on wool were one of the principal means of financing the war) and by bubonic plague (the Black Death), which in 1349 caused devastation: in many villages as much as three-quarters of the population died.
sentences.zh: 但这一繁荣被一场与法国的长期战争（羊毛出口税是为战争筹资的主要手段之一）和鼠疫（黑死病）所笼罩，1349年的黑死病造成了浩劫：许多村庄多达四分之三的人口死亡。

sentences.en: This led to an increase of the sheep flocks, for there were not enough people left to cultivate the land for arable crops.
sentences.zh: 这反而使羊群增多，因为剩下的人手已不足以耕种田地、种植农作物。

sentences.en: (D) Despite setbacks, raw wool exporting expanded, and so also did manufacturing of wool fabrics.
sentences.zh: 尽管遭遇挫折，原毛出口仍在扩大，羊毛织物的生产也同样如此。

sentences.en: This was becoming both specialised and localised.
sentences.zh: 这种生产正变得既专业化又地方化。

sentences.en: The area of England known as the West Country had three advantages – extensive sheep pastures, a supply of soft water for washing, scouring and dyeing wool, and water-power to drive machinery.
sentences.zh: 英格兰被称为西部地区的一带拥有三大优势——广阔的牧羊草场、可用于洗涤、脱脂和染色羊毛的软水供应，以及驱动机械的水力。

sentences.en: Similarly, the hills of Yorkshire and Lancashire in the north of England had soft water and fast running streams.
sentences.zh: 同样，英格兰北部约克郡和兰开夏郡的丘陵也有软水和湍急的溪流。

sentences.en: Water from the latter could be used to drive mills for 'fulling', a shrinking process which makes the fabric firmer and its surface more compact.
sentences.zh: 后者的水流可用来驱动“缩绒”作坊的机械，缩绒是一种使织物更结实、表面更紧密的收缩工艺。

sentences.en: In East Anglia there was soft water, but no hills or fast-running streams to provide power for fulling mills.
sentences.zh: 东安格利亚有软水，却没有丘陵或湍急的溪流来为缩绒作坊提供动力。

sentences.en: Instead, East Anglia used the long, fine wool from its native sheep breeds to produce a cloth which did not require the fulling process.
sentences.zh: 于是，东安格利亚利用本地绵羊品种产出的细长羊毛，生产出一种无需缩绒工艺的布料。

sentences.en: This was the type of cloth which is now called 'worsted', after the village of Worstead.
sentences.zh: 这种布料如今称为“精纺毛呢”，得名于伍斯特德村。

sentences.en: For four hundred years East Anglia dominated the worsted trade, with skills inherited from the Flemish settlers of 1331.
sentences.zh: 在四百年间，东安格利亚凭借1331年佛兰德斯移民传下的技艺，主导了精纺毛呢贸易。

sentences.en: (E) English cloth quickly achieved an international reputation.
sentences.zh: 英格兰布料很快赢得了国际声誉。

sentences.en: From being primarily a raw wool exporter, the country became in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries a manufacturer and exporter of cloth.
sentences.zh: 该国从主要的原毛出口国，在十四和十五世纪转变为布料的制造国和出口国。

sentences.en: At the end of the fifteenth century, it was said that England was largely a nation of sheep farmers and cloth manufacturers.
sentences.zh: 十五世纪末，有人说英格兰基本上是一个养羊人和布料制造商的国度。

sentences.en: The next two centuries saw continued expansion of the industry despite conflicts at home and abroad.
sentences.zh: 尽管国内外冲突不断，此后两个世纪里该行业仍持续扩张。

sentences.en: In the sixteenth century, French weavers, persecuted for their Protestant religion, sought refuge in England and took their skills with them.
sentences.zh: 十六世纪，因信奉新教而遭迫害的法国织工到英格兰避难，并带去了他们的技艺。

sentences.en: England began to surpass Flanders in woollen manufacture; by the end of the seventeenth century it comprised two-thirds of the value of its exports.
sentences.zh: 英格兰在羊毛制造业上开始超越佛兰德斯；到十七世纪末，羊毛制品已占其出口总值的三分之二。

sentences.en: Radical changes lay ahead, in the geographical location of the industry, in labour use and in manufacturing processes.
sentences.zh: 巨大的变革还在后头，涉及该行业的地理布局、劳动力使用和生产工艺。

sentences.en: By 1770, output of worsted from Yorkshire equalled that of East Anglia, and its cloth manufacturing district began to take shape with the expansion of major towns: Leeds, Bradford, Halifax, Huddersfield, and Wakefield.
sentences.zh: 到1770年，约克郡的精纺毛呢产量已与东安格利亚相当，随着利兹、布拉德福德、哈利法克斯、哈德斯菲尔德和韦克菲尔德等主要城镇的扩张，其织布业产区开始成形。

sentences.en: (F) The Industrial Revolution of 1750–1850 also brought change.
sentences.zh: 1750年至1850年的工业革命也带来了变革。

sentences.en: It led the way for new inventions stemming from the Lancashire cotton industry, to mechanize and speed dramatically the processes of spinning and weaving.
sentences.zh: 它为源自兰开夏棉纺业的新发明开辟了道路，使纺纱和织布的工序大幅机械化、提速。

sentences.en: Manufacturing methods, unchanged since the revival of the trade in the fourteenth century, were now superseded.
sentences.zh: 自十四世纪该行业复兴以来一直未变的生产方法，如今被取而代之。

sentences.en: Mechanization had been opposed in the past and it was again.
sentences.zh: 机械化过去曾遭到反对，此时再度受到抵制。

sentences.en: The widespread unrest of 1812 led to the destruction of equipment by bands of rioters, who feared they would lose employment.
sentences.zh: 1812年蔓延各地的骚乱，导致成群的暴动者捣毁设备，他们担心自己会失去工作。

sentences.en: But machinery won the day.
sentences.zh: 但机器最终占了上风。

sentences.en: (G) Over the course of the nineteenth century, the older industries in areas such as East Anglia, where opposition had been most bitter, permanently declined.
sentences.zh: 在整个十九世纪，像东安格利亚这类抵制最为激烈地区的传统行业，永久性地衰落了。

sentences.en: They were overtaken by Yorkshire, where machinery was more readily accepted.
sentences.zh: 它们被更乐于接受机器的约克郡所超越。

sentences.en: The younger industry jumped ahead and never lost its lead, supported by abundant supplies of inexpensive coal to generate steam and, later, electrical power.
sentences.zh: 这一较年轻的产业一跃领先，并始终未失去领先地位，背后有大量廉价煤炭支撑，用以产生蒸汽，后来又用于发电。

sentences.en: Other specialised types of manufacturing developed in Scotland, famed for its tweeds (a range of coloured woollen cloth with characteristic designs), and in the West Country, which focused on the production of high quality, woven carpets.
sentences.zh: 其他专门的制造类型则在苏格兰和西部地区发展起来，苏格兰以粗花呢（一系列带有独特花纹的彩色毛呢）闻名，而西部地区则专注于生产高品质的机织地毯。

sentences.en: (A) Australians living or travelling in rural and remote areas can face particular difficulties when they need medical care.
sentences.zh: 居住在或往来于乡村和偏远地区的澳大利亚人，在需要医疗护理时可能面临特殊的困难。

sentences.en: Hundreds of kilometres from major cities and many hours by road from the closest hospital or clinic, some rural Australians do not have easy access to doctors, nurses and dentists.
sentences.zh: 一些乡村的澳大利亚人距大城市数百公里，距最近的医院或诊所也有数小时车程，他们很难方便地看上医生、护士和牙医。

sentences.en: Organisations such as the Royal Flying Doctor Service (RFDS) have been established to bring health services to outback Australian communities.
sentences.zh: 皇家飞行医生服务（RFDS）等组织应运而生，把医疗服务送到澳大利亚内陆的社区。

sentences.en: The RFDS provides free medical care to people who live, work or travel in remote and regional parts of Australia.
sentences.zh: RFDS为在澳大利亚偏远和边远地区生活、工作或旅行的人提供免费的医疗护理。

sentences.en: This non-profit organisation is the oldest and largest airborne health service of its kind in the world, and since 1928 it has used small aircraft to send doctors and nurses to some of Australia's most far-away communities.
sentences.zh: 这个非营利组织是世界上同类空中医疗服务中历史最悠久、规模最大的，自1928年以来，它一直用小型飞机把医生和护士送往澳大利亚一些最为偏远的社区。

sentences.en: (B) In recent years, the RFDS has also started to fly dentists to regional Australia.
sentences.zh: 近年来，RFDS还开始用飞机把牙医送往澳大利亚的边远地区。

sentences.en: As well as offering mobile dental clinics, the RFDS offers a range of preventative and educational services.
sentences.zh: 除了提供流动牙科诊所之外，RFDS还提供一系列预防性和教育性的服务。

sentences.en: Looking after the teeth of people in remote areas presents special challenges.
sentences.zh: 照顾偏远地区人们的牙齿，带来了特殊的挑战。

sentences.en: These include providing care to disparate communities with no established dental facilities, and dealing with higher incidences of other diseases which are linked to, or caused by poor dental health.
sentences.zh: 这些挑战包括：要为各处没有现成牙科设施的零散社区提供护理，以及要应对其他疾病更高的发病率，而这些疾病与口腔健康不佳相关，或由其引起。

sentences.en: (C) People in remote areas have very infrequent visits by health staff.
sentences.zh: 偏远地区的人们极少有医疗人员来访。

sentences.en: RFDS dentists might only visit a community once every few months, or sometimes once per year.
sentences.zh: RFDS的牙医可能每隔几个月才到一个社区一次，有时甚至一年才一次。

sentences.en: Because of infrequent dentist visits, patients in these areas often need to put up with their dental problems before they can get treatment.
sentences.zh: 由于牙医来访稀少，这些地区的患者往往得忍着牙病，才能等到接受治疗。

sentences.en: Consequently, people in remote areas are more likely to have tooth decay (the blackening and deterioration of teeth) and develop gum and other mouth diseases.
sentences.zh: 因此，偏远地区的人更容易患上龋齿（牙齿发黑、变坏），也更容易得牙龈病和其他口腔疾病。

sentences.en: (D) In some locations that the RFDS visits, there are no suitable dental facilities, so dentists have to bring everything with them.
sentences.zh: 在RFDS到访的某些地方，没有合适的牙科设施，因此牙医不得不把一切都随身带去。

sentences.en: This includes drills, dentists' chairs, portable X-ray machines, and computers for keeping track of patients' treatments.
sentences.zh: 这包括牙钻、牙科椅、便携式X光机，以及用来记录患者治疗情况的电脑。

sentences.en: Equipment can weigh up to 100 kilograms, and since the small planes that transport dentists have limited space, dentists cannot always bring everything that they need.
sentences.zh: 这些设备的重量可达100千克，而由于运送牙医的小飞机空间有限，牙医并不总能把所需的一切都带上。

sentences.en: (E) While dentists in town or city centres can specialise in certain types of treatment, RFDS dentists need to be 'all-rounders'.
sentences.zh: 城镇或市中心的牙医可以专攻某些类型的治疗，而RFDS的牙医却需要成为“全能型”医生。

sentences.en: They need to be able to do all kinds of dental procedures, as they don't have the ability to refer patients to more specialised dentists.
sentences.zh: 他们必须能够进行各种牙科操作，因为他们没有办法把患者转诊给更专业的牙医。

sentences.en: Even with their broad experience, there are some services that are particularly challenging for RFDS dentists.
sentences.zh: 即便拥有广博的经验，对RFDS的牙医来说，仍有一些服务格外棘手。

sentences.en: For example, dentures (or artificial teeth) can be very difficult to provide, as they need to be the right shape and size for the patient, and this requires many visits over a long period of time.
sentences.zh: 例如，假牙（即人造牙齿）就很难提供，因为它们的形状和大小必须与患者相吻合，而这需要在很长一段时间里多次就诊。

sentences.en: As a result, it is not practical to make dentures available.
sentences.zh: 因此，提供假牙并不切合实际。

sentences.en: (F) Some chronic illnesses are more common in remote communities than in the rest of Australia.
sentences.zh: 某些慢性疾病在偏远社区比在澳大利亚其他地方更为常见。

sentences.en: These illnesses can in turn lead to a lowered resistance to infection, including gum and other oral infections.
sentences.zh: 这些疾病又会反过来导致人体对感染的抵抗力下降，包括牙龈感染和其他口腔感染。

sentences.en: As a result, people in outback Australian communities are more likely to experience oral health problems than city folk, and this poses extra challenges for both the dentists and the doctors of the RFDS.
sentences.zh: 因此，澳大利亚内陆社区的人比城里人更容易出现口腔健康问题，这给RFDS的牙医和医生都带来了额外的挑战。

sentences.en: (G) Because there aren't a lot of dental services in remote areas, people living in these areas also receive less education about good dental hygiene than their city counterparts do.
sentences.zh: 由于偏远地区的牙科服务不多，生活在这些地区的人在良好口腔卫生方面所受的教育，也比城里的同胞要少。

sentences.en: Australians in very remote communities might not be aware of things that people in cities take for granted, such as the importance of daily tooth brushing.
sentences.zh: 生活在极偏远社区的澳大利亚人，可能并不知道城里人习以为常的一些事情，比如每天刷牙的重要性。

sentences.en: Also, basic dental hygiene items such as toothpaste and toothbrushes can be more expensive in outback areas.
sentences.zh: 此外，牙膏和牙刷等基本的口腔卫生用品，在内陆地区可能更贵。

sentences.en: Many people are on low incomes, meaning they have extra difficulty affording these products.
sentences.zh: 许多人收入微薄，这意味着他们要负担这些产品格外吃力。

sentences.en: If this is the case, the RFDS supplies these.
sentences.zh: 遇到这种情况，RFDS便会提供这些用品。

sentences.en: (H) As well as treating patients, RFDS dentists try to focus on preventative oral health and educate their patients on good oral hygiene, such as tooth brushing and flossing.
sentences.zh: 除了为患者诊治之外，RFDS的牙医还力求把重点放在预防性口腔健康上，并教导患者养成良好的口腔卫生习惯，比如刷牙和用牙线。

sentences.en: The RFDS also provides mouthguards for young sports players.
sentences.zh: RFDS还为年轻的运动员提供护齿套。

sentences.en: Playing contact sports, such as rugby league or Australian rules football, can damage young people's teeth, so mouthguards provide protection which prevents accidental injuries.
sentences.zh: 从事橄榄球联盟赛或澳式足球之类的身体接触类运动，可能会损伤年轻人的牙齿，因此护齿套能提供防护，防止意外受伤。

sentences.en: (I) Adding fluoride to water supplies has been proven to reduce the incidence of tooth decay in many parts of the world.
sentences.zh: 在世界许多地方，往供水中添加氟化物已被证明能降低龋齿的发病率。

sentences.en: City dwellers in Australia use water supplies that have been fluoridated, and their rates of tooth decay are lower because of this.
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚的城市居民使用的是经过加氟处理的供水，正因如此，他们的龋齿发生率较低。

sentences.en: In remote areas, it is not practical to fluoridate drinking water supplies, and so people living in these areas are more subject to tooth decay.
sentences.zh: 在偏远地区，对饮用水供应加氟并不切合实际，因此生活在这些地区的人更容易患龋齿。

sentences.en: As a result, it is particularly important that people living in areas without fluoridated water pay special attention to regular brushing of their teeth with fluoridated toothpaste.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于生活在没有加氟用水地区的人来说，特别注意用含氟牙膏定期刷牙就显得尤为重要。

sentences.en: (J) Despite many challenges, the RFDS continues to offer much needed dental and medical support.
sentences.zh: 尽管面临诸多挑战，RFDS仍在持续提供亟需的牙科和医疗支持。

sentences.en: Its presence in isolated communities greatly improves the quality of dental health, and supports important oral hygiene and health initiatives.
sentences.zh: 它在偏远社区的存在，极大地改善了口腔健康的状况，并支持着各项重要的口腔卫生和健康行动。

sentences.en: A The oceans cover more than 70 per cent of the planet's surface, yet until quite recently we knew less about their depths than about the surface of the Moon.
sentences.zh: 海洋覆盖了地球表面的 70% 以上，然而直到不久之前，我们对其深处的了解还不如对月球表面的了解。

sentences.en: The Moon has been far more accessible to study because astronomers have long been able to look at its surface, first with the naked eye and then with the telescope, both instruments that focus light.
sentences.zh: 月球远比海洋更易研究，因为天文学家长期以来就能观察其表面，先是用肉眼，后来用望远镜——这两者都是聚焦光线的工具。

sentences.en: Until the twentieth century, however, no instruments were available for the study of Earth's oceans: light, which can travel trillions of kilometres through the vast vacuum of space, cannot penetrate very far in seawater.
sentences.zh: 然而，直到 20 世纪以前，人们还没有可用来研究地球海洋的仪器：光可以穿越广阔真空的空间传播几万亿公里，却无法在海水中传播太远。

sentences.en: B It turns out that for penetrating water the best instrument is sound.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，穿透水体的最佳工具是声音。

sentences.en: Curious investigators have long been fascinated by sound and the way it travels in water.
sentences.zh: 好奇的探究者长期以来一直被声音及其在水中的传播方式所吸引。

sentences.en: As early as 1490, the artist and scientist Leonardo da Vinci observed: 'If you cause your ship to stop and place the head of a long tube in the water and place the outer extremity to your ear, you will hear ships at a great distance from you.'
sentences.zh: 早在 1490 年，艺术家兼科学家莱昂纳多·达·芬奇（Leonardo da Vinci）就观察到：“如果你让自己的船停下来，把一根长管的一端放入水中，把另一端贴在耳朵上，你就会听到远处船只的动静。”

sentences.en: It was not until 1826 that two scientists, Colladon and Sturm, accurately measured the speed of sound in water.
sentences.zh: 直到 1826 年，两位科学家科拉东（Colladon）和施图姆（Sturm）才精确测量了声音在水中的传播速度。

sentences.en: Using a long tube to listen under water (as da Vinci had suggested), they recorded how fast the sound of a submerged bell travelled across Lake Geneva in Switzerland.
sentences.zh: 他们采用一根长管在水下倾听（正如达·芬奇所建议的那样），记录了一只浸没的钟所发出的声音穿越瑞士日内瓦湖的速度。

sentences.en: What these investigators demonstrated was that water is an excellent medium for sound, transmitting it almost five times faster than its speed in air.
sentences.zh: 这些研究者所证明的是：水是声音的极佳介质，声音在水中的传播速度几乎是其在空气中的 5 倍。

sentences.en: C A number of factors influence how far sound travels under water and how long it lasts, including particles, salinity, temperature and pressure.
sentences.zh: 影响声音在水下能传多远以及持续多久的因素有很多，包括颗粒、盐度、温度和压力。

sentences.en: Particles in seawater can reflect, scatter and absorb certain frequencies of sound, just as certain wavelengths of light may be reflected, scattered and absorbed by specific types of particles in the atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 海水中的颗粒可以反射、散射和吸收特定频率的声音，正如某些波长的光可能被大气中特定类型的颗粒反射、散射和吸收一样。

sentences.en: In 1943, Maurice Ewing and J.
sentences.zh: 1943 年，莫里斯·尤因（Maurice Ewing）和 J.

sentences.en: L.
sentences.zh: L.

sentences.en: Worzel conducted an experiment to test the theory that low-frequency waves, which are less vulnerable than higher frequencies to scattering and absorption, should be able to travel great distances, if the sound source is placed correctly.
sentences.zh: 沃泽尔（Worzel）进行了一项实验，以检验如下理论：低频声波相比高频声波更不易被散射和吸收，因此若声源放置得当，应能传播很远的距离。

sentences.en: The researchers set off an underwater explosion and learned that it was detected easily by receivers 3,200 kilometres away.
sentences.zh: 研究者引爆了一次水下爆炸，发现 3200 公里以外的接收器都能轻易探测到它。

sentences.en: In analysing the results of this test, they discovered a kind of 'sound pipeline', known as the 'deep sound channel'.
sentences.zh: 在分析这次实验结果时，他们发现了一种“声学管道”，被称为“深海声道”。

sentences.en: Sound introduced into this channel of water could travel thousands of kilometres with minimal loss of signal.
sentences.zh: 导入这条水中通道的声音，可以传播数千公里而信号衰减极小。

sentences.en: D The US Navy was quick to appreciate the usefulness of low-frequency sound and the deep sound channel.
sentences.zh: 美国海军迅速认识到低频声音和深海声道的用处。

sentences.en: They developed the Sound Surveillance System (SOSUS), which involved underwater microphones, called hydrophones, that were placed on the ocean bottom and connected by cables to on-shore processing centres.
sentences.zh: 他们研发出“声学监视系统”（Sound Surveillance System，简称 SOSUS），其中包括布设在海底、被称为水听器的水下麦克风，并通过电缆与岸上的处理中心相连。

sentences.en: It was Christopher Clark of Cornell University who soon realised that SOSUS could be used to listen to whales.
sentences.zh: 正是康奈尔大学的克里斯托弗·克拉克（Christopher Clark）很快意识到，SOSUS 可以用来倾听鲸鱼。

sentences.en: Using a SOSUS receiver in the West Indies, he could hear whales that were 1,770 kilometres away.
sentences.zh: 他用一台位于西印度群岛的 SOSUS 接收器，能听到 1770 公里之外的鲸鱼。

sentences.en: E Whales are the biggest of Earth's creatures, yet these animals are also remarkably elusive.
sentences.zh: 鲸是地球上最大的生物，然而这些动物也异常难以捉摸。

sentences.en: Scientists wishing to observe blue whales must simply wait in their ships for the whales to surface.
sentences.zh: 希望观察蓝鲸的科学家只能在船上等候鲸浮出水面。

sentences.en: A few whales have been tracked briefly in the wild in this way but not for very great distances, and much about them remains unknown.
sentences.zh: 用这种方式仅能在野外短暂追踪到少数几头鲸，且距离也不算很远，关于它们仍有许多未知。

sentences.en: But by using SOSUS, scientists can track the whales and position them on a map.
sentences.zh: 但借助 SOSUS，科学家可以跟踪鲸并在地图上为它们定位。

sentences.en: Moreover, they can track not just one whale at a time, but many creatures simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 而且，他们一次可以跟踪的不只是一头鲸，而是同时跟踪许多头。

sentences.en: They can also learn to distinguish whale calls; researchers have detected changes in the calls of finback whales as the seasons change, and have found that blue whales in different regions of the Pacific Ocean have different calls.
sentences.zh: 他们也可以学会分辨不同的鲸鸣；研究者发现，长须鲸的叫声随季节变化而发生变化，并发现太平洋不同海域的蓝鲸有着不同的叫声。

sentences.en: F SOSUS has also proved instrumental in obtaining information crucial to our understanding of climate.
sentences.zh: SOSUS 在获取对理解气候至关重要的资料方面也发挥了重要作用。

sentences.en: The system has enabled researchers to begin making ocean temperature measurements on a global scale, measurements that are key to understanding the workings of heat transfer between the ocean and the atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 该系统使研究人员得以开始在全球尺度上测量海洋温度，这些测量对于理解海洋与大气之间的热量传递机制至关重要。

sentences.en: The ocean plays an enormous role in determining air temperature — the heat capacity in only the upper few metres of ocean is thought to be equal to all of the heat in the entire atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 海洋在决定气温方面发挥着巨大作用——单单海洋上层几米水体的热容量，据信就相当于整个大气中蕴含的所有热量。

sentences.en: For sound waves travelling horizontally in the ocean, speed is largely a function of temperature.
sentences.zh: 对于在海洋中水平传播的声波，其速度在很大程度上是温度的函数。

sentences.en: Thus, the travel time of a wave of sound between two points is a sensitive indicator of the average temperature along its path.
sentences.zh: 因此，一段声波在两点之间的传播时间，是这条路径上平均温度的灵敏指标。

sentences.en: Transmitting sound in numerous directions through the deep sound channel can give scientists measurements spanning vast areas of the globe.
sentences.zh: 通过深海声道在多个方向上发送声音，科学家可以获得覆盖全球广大区域的测量数据。

sentences.en: Thousands of sound paths in the ocean can be pieced together into a map of global ocean temperatures, and by repeating measurements along the same paths over time, scientists can track changes in temperature over months or years.
sentences.zh: 海洋中成千上万条声路径可以拼接成一张全球海洋温度图，并通过沿相同路径反复测量，科学家可以追踪几个月乃至几年间温度的变化。

sentences.en: G Researchers are also using other acoustic techniques to monitor climate.
sentences.zh: 研究人员还在使用其他声学技术来监测气候。

sentences.en: Oceanographer Jeff Nystuen, for example, has explored the use of sound to measure rainfall over the ocean.
sentences.zh: 例如海洋学家杰夫·尼斯滕（Jeff Nystuen）已经探索用声音来测量海面上的降雨量。

sentences.en: Monitoring changing global rainfall patterns will contribute to understanding major climate change as well as the weather phenomenon known as El Niño.
sentences.zh: 监测全球降雨格局的变化，将有助于理解重大气候变化以及被称为厄尔尼诺的天气现象。

sentences.en: Since 1985, Nystuen has used hydrophones to listen to rain over the ocean, acoustically measuring not only the rainfall rate but also the rainfall type, ranging from drizzle to thunderstorms.
sentences.zh: 自 1985 年以来，尼斯滕一直在使用水听器倾听海面上的降雨，并以声学方式不仅测量降雨速率，还测量降雨类型——从毛毛雨到雷暴。

sentences.en: By using the sound of rain under water as a 'natural' rain gauge, the measurement of rainfall over the oceans will become available to climatologists.
sentences.zh: 通过把水下雨声当作一种“天然”的雨量计，对海洋降雨量的测量将可以为气候学家所用。

sentences.en: In this way, modern society continues to benefit from the investigations of those who, like Leonardo da Vinci, pursued the answers to some basic questions of nature.
sentences.zh: 通过这种方式，现代社会得以继续从那些像达·芬奇一样追问自然界一些基本问题的探究者身上受益。

sentences.en: (A) During the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, the British East India Company had the monopoly on trade with China and India.
sentences.zh: 在 17 和 18 世纪期间，英国东印度公司垄断了与中国和印度的贸易。

sentences.en: This meant that because no rival could legally import tea or other goods from these countries at this time, the company was rarely in a hurry to transport its merchandise.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，由于此时没有竞争对手能合法地从这些国家进口茶叶或其他商品，公司很少有动力急于运输货物。

sentences.en: Instead, its priority was to minimise costs by carrying as much as possible on each ship.
sentences.zh: 相反，它优先考虑的是通过每艘船多装货来压低成本。

sentences.en: This meant that its ships – known as East Indiamen – were enormous, strong and very slow.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它的船只——被称为“东印度商船”——巨大、坚固但非常缓慢。

sentences.en: (B) By 1800, the average East Indiaman could carry 1,200 tons of merchandise.
sentences.zh: 到 1800 年，平均一艘东印度商船能运载 1200 吨货物。

sentences.en: The trading pattern for China tea usually meant the East Indiamen set sail from Britain in January, sailed round the Cape of Good Hope at the southernmost tip of Africa, and arrived in China in September.
sentences.zh: 中国茶叶的贸易格局通常是：东印度商船 1 月从英国启航，绕过非洲最南端的好望角，9 月抵达中国。

sentences.en: There they would load up that year's tea harvest, set off again and, depending on the wind and weather, aim to arrive back by the following September, so even with favourable sailing conditions, the round trip lasted almost two years, and if anything went wrong it could take a lot longer.
sentences.zh: 在那里它们装上当年的茶叶收成，再次启航；视风和天气情况，目标是在第二年 9 月之前回到英国，所以即便航行条件顺利，往返一次也几乎需要两年；如果出任何差错，可能会拖得更久。

sentences.en: (C) However, by 1834 the company had lost its trading monopolies, and tea had become a freely traded item.
sentences.zh: 然而，到 1834 年，公司失去了贸易垄断权，茶叶也成为可以自由交易的商品。

sentences.en: Having no more use for its great ships, the company sold them off, and many were bought by merchants or their captains, who continued to plough the seas between Britain and China.
sentences.zh: 由于不再需要那些大船，公司把它们卖掉，许多船被商人或船长买下，继续往返于英国和中国之间。

sentences.en: But now that tea could be traded freely, a few smart sailors began to realise that whoever brought each new harvest of tea to Britain first stood to make the most money.
sentences.zh: 但现在既然茶叶可以自由交易，一些聪明的水手开始意识到：谁能把每一季新茶最早送回英国，谁就能赚最多的钱。

sentences.en: (D) This was partly because if you were home first, you could sell your shipment of tea before your competitors even arrived, and partly because consumers in Britain in the nineteenth century believed that the fresher and earlier-picked the tea, the better the resulting drink.
sentences.zh: 这部分原因是：如果你最早回到家，你可以在竞争对手还没到达前就卖掉茶叶；部分原因是 19 世纪英国的消费者认为茶叶越新鲜、采摘越早，泡出来就越好喝。

sentences.en: Tea traders now needed faster, sleeker ships to bring their precious cargo back.
sentences.zh: 如今，茶商需要更快、更纤细的船把宝贵的货物运回。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, in Britain this idea only caught on slowly, and while the 1840s saw a few faster ships launched, for the time being many merchants remained satisfied with the slow but reliable East Indiamen.
sentences.zh: 然而，在英国这一理念只是慢慢流行起来；尽管 1840 年代有几艘更快的船下水，但当时许多商人仍满足于慢却可靠的东印度商船。

sentences.en: (E) In fact it was the Americans who pioneered the first clipper ships.
sentences.zh: 事实上，是美国人率先制造了第一批飞剪船。

sentences.en: These vessels were fast and slender, with a narrow hull that was deeper at the back than at the front, and masses of sails on tall masts.
sentences.zh: 这些船迅速而修长，船身狭窄、后部比前部更深，高桅杆上挂满风帆。

sentences.en: They earned their name from the way that they 'clipped off' journey time.
sentences.zh: 它们的名字“clipper”来自其“剪短”（clip off）行程的方式。

sentences.en: British merchants resolved to build their own clippers to rival the Americans, and the first British tea clipper, Stornaway, was built in Aberdeen in 1850.
sentences.zh: 英国商人下决心打造自己的飞剪船与美国人抗衡，第一艘英国茶叶飞剪船 Stornaway 于 1850 年在阿伯丁建造。

sentences.en: More tea clippers were designed and built in Britain throughout the 1850s and 1860s; they had a narrower beam than their American equivalents, making them less powerful during storms but faster in calmer weather.
sentences.zh: 在整个 1850 年代和 1860 年代，英国设计并建造了更多茶叶飞剪船；它们的船梁比美国同行更窄，使其在风暴中威力较小，但在风平浪静时更快。

sentences.en: (F) There was a great spirit of competition between the British and American ships plying the tea trade, but to begin with the Americans had the edge.
sentences.zh: 在英国船与美国船角逐茶叶贸易之间存在着浓厚的竞争氛围，但起初美国人占据优势。

sentences.en: Then in 1851 a British shipowner, Richard Green, built the aptly named clipper Challenger with the stated intention of beating the American ships.
sentences.zh: 然后在 1851 年，英国船东理查德·格林（Richard Green）建造了恰如其名的飞剪船 Challenger，公开宣称要打败美国船。

sentences.en: Loaded with tea, Challenger left China for London in 1852 at the same time as the American clipper Challenge, a much larger, older ship already greatly admired for its speed.
sentences.zh: 载着茶叶的 Challenger 于 1852 年与美国飞剪船 Challenge 同时从中国驶往伦敦——后者是一艘更大、更老、且因速度已享盛誉的船。

sentences.en: Large sums were bet on which would complete the journey first.
sentences.zh: 人们押下大笔赌注，赌哪艘船会先完成航程。

sentences.en: In the event, the British ship beat its rival to London by two days, amid much jubilation.
sentences.zh: 结果，英国船比对手提前两天抵达伦敦，在一片欢腾中获胜。

sentences.en: From then on, such international races grew in popularity.
sentences.zh: 自此之后，此类国际竞速越来越受欢迎。

sentences.en: (G) After 1855, American participation in the British tea trade gradually stopped.
sentences.zh: 1855 年后，美国对英国茶叶贸易的参与逐渐停止。

sentences.en: But even without the Anglo-American rivalry, the competitive spirit continued.
sentences.zh: 但即便没有了英美对抗，竞争精神仍在延续。

sentences.en: It was really ignited when new ports were opened up for trade in China.
sentences.zh: 当中国开放新的通商口岸时，这种竞争真正被点燃。

sentences.en: These included Foochow, which was much closer to the tea-producing areas than Canton, the port used previously.
sentences.zh: 这些口岸包括福州，它比此前使用的广州港更靠近茶产区。

sentences.en: As a result, tea could be loaded on board earlier and fresher, and the clippers could set off in late May or early June – sometimes not even taking time to fill out the official paperwork – racing back to Britain whatever the difficulties.
sentences.zh: 因此，茶叶可以更早被装船、更新鲜，飞剪船可以在五月底或六月初出发——有时甚至来不及填写官方手续文件——不管遇到何种困难都向英国疾驰而去。

sentences.en: (H) They sped down through the South China Sea and into the Indian Ocean, then raced to get round the southernmost tip of Africa at the Cape of Good Hope.
sentences.zh: 它们一路向南穿过南海，进入印度洋，再竞相绕过非洲最南端的好望角。

sentences.en: Then it was north across the vast Atlantic, past the Azores, through the English Channel and into the estuary of the River Thames.
sentences.zh: 然后向北横渡浩瀚的大西洋，经过亚速尔群岛，穿过英吉利海峡，进入泰晤士河口。

sentences.en: Once there, they would be towed by tugs up the river and into the docks.
sentences.zh: 一旦抵达，它们会被拖船拖上河、进入码头。

sentences.en: (I) The cargo of the winning ship could earn a premium of up to sixpence per pound – and so the captain and crew were rewarded by the owners of the cargo.
sentences.zh: 获胜船只的货物每磅可获得高达 6 便士的溢价——所以船长和船员会被货主以丰厚回报。

sentences.en: But the races were about more than just money: the crews, about 40 men on each clipper, were expert sailors, proud of their ships, and they delighted in competing against each other.
sentences.zh: 但这些赛事关乎的不只是钱：每艘飞剪船上约 40 名船员都是经验丰富的水手，以自己的船为荣，并乐于互相竞争。

sentences.en: Without their enthusiasm, the races would never have happened, since getting home as fast as possible required the crew to be totally dedicated and to sacrifice much of their rest for the duration of the race.
sentences.zh: 没有他们的热情，赛事就根本不会发生，因为要尽快回家，船员必须全心投入、并在比赛期间牺牲大量休息时间。

sentences.en: (A) Beatrix Potter is one of the best-selling children's authors of all time.
sentences.zh: 比阿特丽克斯·波特是有史以来最畅销的儿童文学作家之一。

sentences.en: Her popular series of books that includes The Tale of Peter Rabbit was first published over one hundred years ago and has never been out of print.
sentences.zh: 她那套广受欢迎、包含《彼得兔的故事》在内的系列图书，初版于一百多年前，此后从未绝版。

sentences.en: Generations of children have enjoyed her many stories and illustrations, all of which celebrate the English way of life and rural landscape through the adventures of animals.
sentences.zh: 一代又一代的孩子都喜爱她众多的故事和插画，这些作品都借由动物的冒险，礼赞了英格兰的生活方式与乡村风光。

sentences.en: (B) Born into a comfortable middle-class family in London in 1866, Potter spent much of her early life in her own company.
sentences.zh: 波特于1866年出生在伦敦一个家境舒适的中产阶级家庭，早年大部分时光都是独自一人度过的。

sentences.en: She was educated at home by a governess and rarely saw her brother, Bertram, who was sent to boarding school.
sentences.zh: 她在家由家庭教师授课，很少见到自己的哥哥伯特伦（Bertram），因为他被送去了寄宿学校。

sentences.en: Having little social contact with children of her own age, Potter was drawn into a private world of writing.
sentences.zh: 由于与同龄孩子几乎没有社交往来，波特被引入了一个属于自己的写作世界。

sentences.en: When she was 15, she began to keep a diary written in a secret code of her own invention.
sentences.zh: 15 岁时，她开始用自己发明的密码写日记。

sentences.en: Even Beatrix herself, when she read back over it in later life, found it difficult to understand.
sentences.zh: 甚至连比阿特丽克斯本人在晚年重读时，也觉得难以读懂。

sentences.en: It was not until 15 years after her death that the code was cracked.
sentences.zh: 直到她去世 15 年之后，这套密码才被破解。

sentences.en: To the outside world Beatrix seemed shy and reserved, but in her diary she expressed herself freely and was critical of the work of several contemporary artists.
sentences.zh: 在外界看来，比阿特丽克斯似乎害羞而内敛，但在日记中她畅所欲言，并对若干同时代艺术家的作品提出批评。

sentences.en: (C) Potter was a naturally gifted artist, and with the aid of some art lessons she also learned the technical side of drawing.
sentences.zh: 波特天生具有艺术天赋，并在几次美术课的帮助下也掌握了绘画的技术层面。

sentences.en: Throughout her childhood she looked after many animals—rabbits, frogs and even bats—and sketched them constantly, gradually improving her work by sketching in museums.
sentences.zh: 整个童年时期，她都在照看许多动物——兔子、青蛙乃至蝙蝠——并不断地为它们写生，又通过在博物馆中临摹来逐步提升画技。

sentences.en: She was also interested in natural history.
sentences.zh: 她也对博物学很感兴趣。

sentences.en: She would spend many hours drawing wildlife such as fungi and flowers, and at one time she had an ambition to develop this scientific interest.
sentences.zh: 她会花上许多时间描绘真菌、花卉等野生生物，一度还立志将这种科学兴趣发展为事业。

sentences.en: An uncle tried to help her enrol at the Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew in London, but she was rejected because of her gender.
sentences.zh: 一位舅父曾试图帮她进入伦敦邱园皇家植物园（Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew），但她因性别而被拒之门外。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, she won respect from the scientific establishment for her illustrations and her contribution to mycology, the study of fungi.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，她仍凭借自己的插画以及对真菌学（即对真菌的研究）的贡献，赢得了科学界的尊重。

sentences.en: (D) When Potter was in her early twenties, her parents tried to arrange a husband for her.
sentences.zh: 在波特二十出头时，她的父母试图为她安排一桩婚事。

sentences.en: Many suitable suitors were found; however, Potter turned them all down.
sentences.zh: 他们物色了不少合适的求婚者；然而，波特一一回绝了他们。

sentences.en: Fiercely independent, she disliked the idea of being tied to a domestic life that, at that time, consisted mostly of staying at home and raising children.
sentences.zh: 她极其独立，反感被束缚于一种当时主要由待在家里、抚养孩子构成的居家生活。

sentences.en: Thus—unusually for British women of the period—she remained single and lived in her parents' home.
sentences.zh: 于是——这在当时的英国女性中并不常见——她一直未婚，住在父母家中。

sentences.en: (E) For several years Potter tried to get her first children's book, The Tale of Peter Rabbit, published.
sentences.zh: 有好几年时间，波特一直在尝试出版她的第一本儿童读物《比得兔的故事》（The Tale of Peter Rabbit）。

sentences.en: Her initial attempts were unsuccessful, but she persevered, and eventually Frederick Warne & Co.
sentences.zh: 她最初的尝试均未成功，但她坚持了下来，最终弗雷德里克·沃恩公司（Frederick Warne & Co.）

sentences.en: accepted the book.
sentences.zh: 接受了这本书。

sentences.en: It was finally published in 1902, when Potter was 36, though the publishers did not expect it to sell many copies.
sentences.zh: 它最终于 1902 年正式出版，那年波特 36 岁，尽管出版方并不预期它会畅销。

sentences.en: The project was given to the youngest brother in the firm, Norman Warne, as his first assignment—essentially a test.
sentences.zh: 这一项目交给了公司里最年轻的弟弟诺曼·沃恩（Norman Warne），算是他接手的第一份工作——本质上是一次试用。

sentences.en: Luckily, he warmed to both the book and its author.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，他对这本书和作者都倾注了热情。

sentences.en: Determined to make it a success, he worked closely with Potter, poring over every detail.
sentences.zh: 他下定决心要让此书获得成功，并与波特紧密合作，逐一推敲每一处细节。

sentences.en: It was Norman who insisted that each illustration should be in colour, while Potter insisted the book remain small enough for children to hold easily.
sentences.zh: 正是诺曼坚持要求每一幅插图都用彩色印刷，而波特则坚持要让这本书保持小巧，以便孩子们容易拿在手中。

sentences.en: By the end of the year, 28,000 copies were in print.
sentences.zh: 到了那年年底，已有 28000 册付印。

sentences.en: (F) The relationship between Warne and Potter blossomed, and they eventually became engaged.
sentences.zh: 沃恩与波特之间的感情逐渐发展，最终订下婚约。

sentences.en: However, Potter's parents disapproved because of his occupation.
sentences.zh: 然而，波特的父母因为他的职业身份而表示反对。

sentences.en: They relented only on condition that the couple live apart for six months to give Potter time to reconsider.
sentences.zh: 他们只是有条件地让步：要求这对未婚情侣分开生活六个月，给波特时间重新考虑。

sentences.en: Tragically, before the wedding could take place, Warne developed pernicious anaemia, a blood disease, and passed away.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，在婚礼能够举行之前，沃恩患上了恶性贫血（一种血液疾病）并去世了。

sentences.en: Potter was devastated and wrote to his sister, Millie, “He did not live long, but he fulfilled a useful, happy life.
sentences.zh: 波特悲痛欲绝，给他的妹妹米莉（Millie）写信道：“他没能活很久，但他过完了一段有意义、快乐的人生。

sentences.en: I must try to make a fresh beginning next year.”
sentences.zh: 我必须努力在明年开始新的生活。”

sentences.en: (G) After Warne's death, Potter moved to the Lake District in northern England.
sentences.zh: 在沃恩去世后，波特搬到了英格兰北部的湖区。

sentences.en: In 1905 she bought a small farm there, and for the next eight years she busied herself writing more books, some set in or around the area.
sentences.zh: 1905 年，她在那里买下了一座小农场，在接下来的八年里忙于写作更多的书，其中一些故事就设定在这一带。

sentences.en: She remained there for the rest of her life, but failing eyesight eventually forced her to stop writing children's books.
sentences.zh: 她在那里度过了余生，但视力日渐衰退，最终迫使她停止写作儿童读物。

sentences.en: Instead, she devoted herself to breeding sheep and helping to conserve farms in the district.
sentences.zh: 于是，她转而投身于养羊事业，并帮助保护当地的农场。

sentences.en: Thanks to the proceeds from her successful books and a later inheritance, Potter was able to buy many working farms.
sentences.zh: 凭借其畅销著作的版税收入以及后来的一笔遗产，波特得以买下许多在营的农场。

sentences.en: On her death she left more than 4,000 acres to the National Trust, an organisation that protects historic buildings and countryside in England.
sentences.zh: 她去世时，将 4000 多英亩土地遗赠给了国民信托——一家在英格兰负责保护历史建筑与乡村景观的机构。

sentences.en: As a result, her beloved landscape is now accessible to countless visitors.
sentences.zh: 因此，她所深爱的这片土地如今得以向无数游客开放。

诺曼·沃恩建议波特在她的第一本书中加入黑白插图。

40.stemZh: 波特向国家信托基金会的捐赠是近年来最大的一笔。

sentences.en: (A) The word paper derives from the Greek term for the ancient Egyptian writing material called papyrus.
sentences.zh: paper（纸）一词源自希腊语中对古埃及书写材料“莎草纸”（papyrus）的称谓。

sentences.en: In about 2400 BC, the Egyptians discovered how to make a writing surface out of papyrus, a type of reed that grows along waterways in southern Europe and North Africa.
sentences.zh: 大约在公元前2400年，埃及人发现了如何用莎草（papyrus，一种生长在南欧和北非水道沿岸的芦苇）制作书写面。

sentences.en: The Egyptians cut the plant into strips which they softened in water.
sentences.zh: 埃及人把这种植物切成细条，并在水中将其软化。

sentences.en: Papyrus was cross-woven into a mat and then pounded into a hard, thin sheet.
sentences.zh: 莎草被交叉编织成一张席状物，然后捶打成坚硬而轻薄的薄片。

sentences.en: (B) As the papyrus plant requires subtropical conditions to grow, papyrus was not much used in Europe at that time; instead, the main material used for writing was parchment.
sentences.zh: 由于莎草需要亚热带环境才能生长，当时莎草纸在欧洲并不多用；取而代之，主要的书写材料是羊皮纸。

sentences.en: This was made from animal skin and was extremely expensive.
sentences.zh: 羊皮纸由动物皮制成，价格极其昂贵。

sentences.en: In fact, it has been estimated that a single book written on parchment required the skins of 300 sheep.
sentences.zh: 事实上，据估计，一本用羊皮纸书写的书需要用到300只羊的皮。

sentences.en: The skins had to be specially prepared by drying them and they were then stretched on a special frame.
sentences.zh: 这些皮需要经过特别处理，先将其晾干，然后绷在一个专门的框架上。

sentences.en: It is not known when parchment was first introduced, but it was the main writing material in Europe for hundreds of years.
sentences.zh: 羊皮纸最初是何时出现的尚不可知，但它在数百年间一直是欧洲主要的书写材料。

sentences.en: (C) Paper—made from pulp, rags and fibres of plants—seems to have been invented in China and is considered to be one of the Four Great Inventions of Ancient China.
sentences.zh: 纸——由纸浆、破布和植物纤维制成——似乎是在中国发明的，并被视为中国古代四大发明之一。

sentences.en: In 105 AD, under the Han-Dynasty emperor Ho-Ti, a government official in China named Ts'ai Lun was the first to start a papermaking industry.
sentences.zh: 公元105年，在汉代和帝在位期间，一位名叫蔡伦的中国官员率先创办了造纸业。

sentences.en: Ts'ai Lun seems to have made his paper by mixing finely chopped mulberry bark and hemp rags with water, mashing the mixture flat with a stone mortar, and then pressing out the water and letting it dry in the sun.
sentences.zh: 蔡伦造纸的方法似乎是：把切碎的桑树皮和麻布碎屑与水混合，用石臼将混合物捣烂压平，然后挤出水分，置于阳光下晾干。

sentences.en: He may have based his idea on bark cloth, which was very common in China and also made from mulberry.
sentences.zh: 他的这一构想可能源自树皮布，这种布在中国很常见，同样以桑树为原料制成。

sentences.en: (D) Previously, during the Shang (1600-1050 BC) and Zhou (1050-256 BC) dynasties of Ancient China, documents were ordinarily written on bone or bamboo (on tablets or bamboo strips bound and rolled together into scrolls), making them very heavy and awkward to transport.
sentences.zh: 此前，在中国古代的商朝（公元前1600年至前1050年）和周朝（公元前1050年至前256年），文献通常书写在骨头或竹子上（写在简牍上，或写在用绳编连、卷成卷轴的竹简上），这使得它们十分沉重，搬运起来很不方便。

sentences.en: The light material of silk was sometimes used, but was normally too expensive to consider.
sentences.zh: 有时也会使用轻便的丝帛，但它通常太过昂贵，难以考虑使用。

sentences.en: When paper was first invented, it was used for purposes of wrapping or padding protection for delicate bronze mirrors.
sentences.zh: 纸刚发明时，被用于包裹或衬垫，以保护易损的青铜镜。

sentences.en: Although paper for writing became popular by the 3rd century AD, it continued to be used for wrapping and other purposes.
sentences.zh: 尽管到公元3世纪书写用纸已经普及，但纸仍继续被用于包装等其他用途。

sentences.en: During the Tang Dynasty (618-907 AD) paper was folded and sewn into square bags to preserve the flavour of tea.
sentences.zh: 在唐朝（公元618年至907年），人们将纸折叠并缝成方形的袋子，用以保存茶叶的香味。

sentences.en: During the same period, according to a written account, tea was served from baskets with multi-coloured paper cups and paper napkins of different sizes and shapes.
sentences.zh: 据一份文字记载，同一时期，人们用篮子盛茶，并配以彩色纸杯和形状、大小各异的纸巾。

sentences.en: During the Chinese Song Dynasty (960-1279 AD) not only did the government produce the world's first known printed paper money, or banknote, but paper money bestowed as gifts was wrapped in special paper envelopes.
sentences.zh: 在中国宋朝（公元960年至1279年），政府不仅发行了世界上已知最早的印刷纸币（即钞票），而且作为礼物馈赠的纸币还会用特制的纸信封包好。

sentences.en: (E) Paper spread widely outside China; other Asian cultures, even after seeing paper, could not make it themselves.
sentences.zh: 纸在中国以外广为传播；其他亚洲文化即便见到了纸，自己也造不出来。

sentences.en: Instruction in the manufacturing process was required, and the Chinese were reluctant to share their secrets.
sentences.zh: 这需要有人传授制造工艺，而中国人却不愿分享自己的秘密。

sentences.en: It made its true push westward in 751 AD when the Tang Dynasty was at war with the Islamic world.
sentences.zh: 纸真正向西传播是在公元751年，当时唐朝正与伊斯兰世界交战。

sentences.en: During a battle on the banks of the Talas River, a Chinese caravan was captured which happened to include several papermakers.
sentences.zh: 在怛罗斯河畔的一场战役中，一支中国商队被俘，其中恰好包括几名造纸工匠。

sentences.en: They were taken away to Samarkand, which was a good place to make paper because it had an abundant supply of hemp and flax.
sentences.zh: 他们被带往撒马尔罕，那里因麻和亚麻供应充足，是造纸的好地方。

sentences.en: Samarkanders changed the technology of manufacturing paper.
sentences.zh: 撒马尔罕人改变了造纸的工艺。

sentences.en: They began to prepare it in stone mills and Samarkand became an important papermaking centre.
sentences.zh: 他们开始用石磨来制浆，撒马尔罕也由此成为重要的造纸中心。

sentences.en: The rudimentary and laborious process of papermaking was refined, and bulk manufacturing of paper began in Iran, where they invented a method to make a thicker sheet of paper, which helped transform papermaking from an art into an important business.
sentences.zh: 原本粗陋而费力的造纸工序得到了改进，纸张的批量生产在伊朗兴起；在那里，人们发明了一种制造更厚纸张的方法，这有助于把造纸从一门技艺转变为一项重要的生意。

sentences.en: Gradually papermakers made their way further west through the Arab world—to Baghdad, Damascus and Cairo.
sentences.zh: 造纸工匠们逐渐穿过阿拉伯世界，进一步向西迁移——到达巴格达、大马士革和开罗。

sentences.en: Finally, when the Moors from North Africa invaded Spain and Portugal, they brought the technology with them and so it was that papermaking entered Europe in the 12th century.
sentences.zh: 最终，来自北非的摩尔人入侵西班牙和葡萄牙时，把这项技术一并带去，造纸术便由此在12世纪传入欧洲。

sentences.en: (F) In Europe, the preferred medium for the artists and literati of the time was still the smooth and lustrous parchment.
sentences.zh: 在欧洲，当时艺术家和文人偏爱的书写媒介仍是光滑而有光泽的羊皮纸。

sentences.en: The notion of paper being used as a practical everyday item did not occur until the 15th century, when Johannes Gutenberg perfected movable-type printing, which included the use of metal moulds and alloys, a special press, and oil-based inks, allowing the mass production of printed books.
sentences.zh: 直到15世纪，把纸当作实用的日常物品的观念才出现，当时约翰内斯·古腾堡（Johannes Gutenberg）完善了活字印刷术，其中包括使用金属模具与合金、专门的印刷机以及油性墨水，从而使印刷书籍得以大批量生产。

sentences.en: The birth of the modern paper and printing industry is commonly marked from this date.
sentences.zh: 现代造纸与印刷业的诞生通常便以这一时期为标志。

sentences.en: Printing technology rapidly developed and created an ever-increasing demand for paper.
sentences.zh: 印刷技术迅速发展，催生了对纸张不断增长的需求。

sentences.en: The early European papers were made from recycled cotton and linen—and a huge trade quickly developed around the trading of old rags.
sentences.zh: 早期的欧洲纸张由回收的棉布和亚麻布制成——围绕旧破布的买卖，很快发展出一桩规模庞大的生意。

sentences.en: It is said that the disease known as the Black Death entered England from Europe on these old rags.
sentences.zh: 据说，被称为黑死病的疾病正是借由这些旧破布从欧洲大陆传入英格兰的。

sentences.en: Yet soon this source became insufficient and some curious attempts were made to find new materials.
sentences.zh: 然而这一来源很快便供不应求，于是人们做了一些奇特的尝试，以寻找新的原料。

sentences.en: Experiments with fibres such as straw, cabbage, wasp nests and finally wood resulted in inexpensive—and replaceable—materials for papermaking.
sentences.zh: 人们对稻草、卷心菜、马蜂窝乃至最终木材等纤维进行了试验，得到了廉价且可再生的造纸原料。

sentences.en: Today, the long, soft fibres of softwoods such as spruce have become the most suitable source of pulp for the mass production of paper.
sentences.zh: 如今，云杉等针叶木又长又软的纤维，已成为最适合用于大批量造纸的纸浆来源。
