sentences.en: A The 16th and 17th centuries saw two great pioneers of modern science: Galileo and Gilbert.
sentences.zh: 16世纪和17世纪出现了两位伟大的现代科学先驱：伽利略和吉尔伯特。

sentences.en: The impact of their findings is eminent.
sentences.zh: 他们的发现影响卓著。

sentences.en: Gilbert was the first modern scientist, the accredited father of the science of electricity and magnetism, an Englishman of learning and a physician at the court of Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 吉尔伯特是第一位现代科学家，被公认为电磁学之父，是一位博学的英格兰人，也是伊丽莎白宫廷的御医。

sentences.en: Prior to him, all that was known of electricity and magnetism was what the ancients knew: nothing more than that the lodestone possessed magnetic properties and that amber and jet, when rubbed, would attract bits of paper or other substances of small specific gravity.
sentences.zh: 在他之前，人们对电和磁的全部认识不过是古人所知的那些：仅仅知道天然磁石具有磁性，以及琥珀和煤玉经摩擦后能吸引碎纸片或其他比重很小的物质。

sentences.en: However, he is less well known than he deserves.
sentences.zh: 然而，他的知名度却不及他应得的那样高。

sentences.en: B Gilbert's birth predated Galileo's.
sentences.zh: 吉尔伯特的出生早于伽利略。

sentences.en: Born into an eminent local family in Colchester, Essex, on 24 May 1544, he went to grammar school and then studied medicine at St John's College, Cambridge, graduating in 1573.
sentences.zh: 1544年5月24日，他生于埃塞克斯郡科尔切斯特的一个当地名门，先就读于文法学校，后在剑桥圣约翰学院学医，于1573年毕业。

sentences.en: Later he travelled on the Continent and eventually settled in London.
sentences.zh: 后来他游历欧洲大陆，最终在伦敦定居。

sentences.en: C He was a very successful and eminent doctor.
sentences.zh: 他是一位非常成功、声名显赫的医生。

sentences.en: All this culminated in his election as president of the Royal Society.
sentences.zh: 这一切的顶峰是他当选为皇家学会会长。

sentences.en: He was also appointed personal physician to Queen Elizabeth I and was later knighted by her.
sentences.zh: 他还被任命为伊丽莎白一世女王的御医，后来获她册封为爵士。

sentences.en: He faithfully served her until her death.
sentences.zh: 他忠心耿耿地侍奉女王，直至她去世。

sentences.en: However, he did not outlive the Queen for long and died on 30 November 1603, only a few months after his appointment as personal physician to King James.
sentences.zh: 然而，他并未比女王多活多久，于1603年11月30日去世，距他被任命为詹姆斯国王的御医仅仅几个月。

sentences.en: D Gilbert was first interested in chemistry but later changed his focus because alchemy contained too great a portion of mysticism (such as the transmutation of metals).
sentences.zh: 吉尔伯特起初对化学感兴趣，但后来改变了研究方向，因为炼金术中含有过多的神秘主义成分（例如金属的嬗变）。

sentences.en: He gradually developed an interest in physics, inspired by the great minds of the ancients, particularly the knowledge the ancient Greeks had about lodestones—strange minerals with the power to attract iron.
sentences.zh: 他逐渐对物理学产生了兴趣，这受到了古代伟大思想家的启发，尤其是古希腊人关于天然磁石的知识——那是一种能够吸引铁的奇异矿物。

sentences.en: In the meantime, Britain became a major seafaring nation in 1588 when the Spanish Armada was defeated, opening the way to British settlement of America.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，1588年西班牙无敌舰队被击败，英国成为一个海上大国，为英国人在美洲的殖民开辟了道路。

sentences.en: British ships depended on the magnetic compass, yet no one understood why it worked.
sentences.zh: 英国船只依赖磁罗盘，却无人明白它为何能起作用。

sentences.en: Did the Pole Star attract it, as Columbus once speculated; or was there a magnetic mountain at the pole, as described in the Odyssey, which ships would never approach because the sailors thought its pull would yank out all their iron nails and fittings?
sentences.zh: 是北极星在吸引它，如哥伦布曾经猜测的那样；还是极地有一座磁山，如《奥德赛》中所描述的，船只永远不敢靠近，因为水手们认为它的引力会把船上所有的铁钉和铁件都拽出来？

sentences.en: For nearly 20 years, William Gilbert conducted ingenious experiments to understand magnetism.
sentences.zh: 在将近20年的时间里，威廉·吉尔伯特做了一系列巧妙的实验来理解磁现象。

sentences.en: His works include On the Magnet, Magnetic Bodies, and The Great Magnet of the Earth.
sentences.zh: 他的著作包括《论磁石、磁体以及地球这块大磁体》。

sentences.en: E Gilbert's discoveries were of great importance to modern physics.
sentences.zh: 吉尔伯特的发现对现代物理学具有重大意义。

sentences.en: He investigated the nature of magnetism and electricity, and he even coined the word “electric”.
sentences.zh: 他研究了磁与电的本质，甚至创造了“electric（电的）”这个词。

sentences.en: Early beliefs about magnetism were largely entangled with superstitions—for instance, sailors believed that rubbing garlic on a lodestone could neutralise its magnetism and that even the smell of garlic would interfere with the action of a compass, which is why helmsmen were forbidden to eat it near a ship's compass.
sentences.zh: 早期关于磁的观念大多与迷信纠缠在一起——例如，水手们相信在磁石上擦大蒜可以中和它的磁性，甚至连大蒜的气味都会干扰罗盘的运转，这正是舵手被禁止在船上罗盘附近吃大蒜的原因。

sentences.en: Gilbert also found that metals can be magnetised by rubbing materials such as fur on them.
sentences.zh: 吉尔伯特还发现，用毛皮之类的材料摩擦金属，可以使金属磁化。

sentences.en: He named the ends of a magnet the “north pole” and “south pole”.
sentences.zh: 他把磁体的两端命名为“北极”和“南极”。

sentences.en: The magnetic poles can attract or repel, depending on polarity; ordinary iron, however, is always attracted to a magnet.
sentences.zh: 磁极可以相互吸引或排斥，这取决于极性；然而普通的铁总是被磁体吸引。

sentences.en: Though he began to study the relationship between magnetism and electricity, he did not complete this work.
sentences.zh: 尽管他着手研究磁与电之间的关系，却未能完成这项工作。

sentences.en: His research into static electricity using amber and jet only demonstrated that objects with electrical charges can attract small pieces of paper and the like.
sentences.zh: 他用琥珀和煤玉对静电所做的研究，只证明了带电的物体能够吸引碎纸片之类的东西。

sentences.en: It was a French scientist named du Fay who later discovered that there are actually two electrical charges—positive and negative.
sentences.zh: 后来正是一位名叫迪费的法国科学家发现，电荷实际上有两种——正电荷和负电荷。

sentences.en: F He also questioned traditional astronomical beliefs.
sentences.zh: 他还对传统的天文学观念提出了质疑。

sentences.en: Though a Copernican, he did not state explicitly whether the Earth is at the centre of the universe or in orbit around the Sun.
sentences.zh: 尽管他是哥白尼学说的信奉者，却没有明确表态地球究竟是处于宇宙的中心，还是围绕太阳运行。

sentences.en: However, he believed that stars are not equidistant from the Earth but have their own Earth-like planets orbiting around them.
sentences.zh: 不过，他相信恒星与地球的距离并不相等，而是各自有着类似地球的行星围绕它们运转。

sentences.en: The Earth itself is like a giant magnet, which is also why compasses always point north: they align with the planet's polarity.
sentences.zh: 地球本身就像一块巨大的磁体，这也是罗盘总是指向北方的原因：它们与地球的极性保持一致。

sentences.en: He likened the polarity of a magnet to the polarity of the Earth and built an entire magnetic philosophy on this analogy.
sentences.zh: 他把磁体的极性比作地球的极性，并在这一类比之上构建起一整套磁学理论。

sentences.en: In his explanation, magnetism is the soul of the Earth.
sentences.zh: 按照他的解释，磁性就是地球的灵魂。

sentences.en: Thus a perfectly spherical lodestone, when aligned with the Earth's poles, would wobble all by itself in 24 hours.
sentences.zh: 因此，一块完美的球形磁石，当它与地球的两极对齐时，会在24小时内自行摆动。

sentences.en: Further, he believed that the Sun and other stars wobble just as the Earth does around a crystal core, and he speculated that the Moon might also be a magnet caused to orbit by its magnetic attraction to the Earth.
sentences.zh: 进一步地，他相信太阳和其他恒星会像地球一样围绕一个水晶核心摆动，并推测月球或许也是一块磁体，因受到地球的磁力吸引而被迫绕地运行。

sentences.en: This was perhaps the first proposal that a force might cause a heavenly orbit.
sentences.zh: 这或许是关于某种力可能导致天体轨道运动的最早设想。

sentences.en: G His research method was revolutionary in that he used experiments rather than pure logic and reasoning, as the ancient Greek philosophers had done.
sentences.zh: 他的研究方法具有革命性，因为他采用实验，而不是像古希腊哲学家那样仅凭纯粹的逻辑与推理。

sentences.en: This represented a new attitude towards scientific investigation; until then, systematic experiments were not in fashion.
sentences.zh: 这代表了一种对待科学研究的新态度；在那之前，系统的实验并不流行。

sentences.en: Because of this scientific attitude, together with his contribution to our knowledge of magnetism, a unit of magnetomotive force—also known as magnetic potential—was named the gilbert in his honour.
sentences.zh: 由于这种科学态度，再加上他对人类磁学知识的贡献，磁动势——又称磁位——的一个单位便以他的名字命名为吉伯（gilbert）。

sentences.en: His approach of careful observation and experimentation, rather than reliance on authoritative opinion or deductive philosophy, laid the very foundation for modern science.
sentences.zh: 他这种依靠细致观察和实验、而非依赖权威观点或演绎哲学的研究方式，为现代科学奠定了真正的基石。

sentences.en: (A) Everybody knows that the dinosaurs became extinct as a result of a large asteroid; something big hit the Earth 65 million years ago and, when the dust had fallen, so had the great reptiles.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，恐龙是因为一颗大型小行星撞击地球而灭绝的；6500 万年前，有一个庞然大物砸向地球，等到尘埃落定时，那些庞大的爬行动物也随之倒下。

sentences.en: There is thus a nice, if ironic, symmetry in the idea that a similar impact brought about the dinosaurs' rise.
sentences.zh: 因此，认为恐龙的崛起也是由一次类似撞击带来的，这种看法虽然带点反讽，却有一种漂亮的对称感。

sentences.en: That is the thesis proposed by Paul Olsen of Columbia University.
sentences.zh: 这正是哥伦比亚大学的保罗·奥尔森（Paul Olsen）所提出的论点。

sentences.en: (B) Dinosaurs first appear in the fossil record 230 million years ago, during the Triassic period.
sentences.zh: 恐龙最早出现在 2.3 亿年前的化石记录中，那是三叠纪。

sentences.en: But they were mostly small, and they shared the Earth with lots of other sorts of reptile.
sentences.zh: 但它们大多体型偏小，与许多其他类别的爬行动物共享着地球。

sentences.en: It was in the subsequent Jurassic period, which began 202 million years ago, that they overran the planet and turned into the monsters realistically depicted in modern books and movies.
sentences.zh: 正是在随后开始于 2.02 亿年前的侏罗纪，它们才横扫地球，变成了如今在书籍和电影中被栩栩如生地描绘的那些庞然大物。

sentences.en: Dr Olsen and his colleagues are not the first to suggest that the dinosaurs inherited the Earth as the result of an asteroid strike.
sentences.zh: 奥尔森博士及其同事并不是第一个提出恐龙因一次小行星撞击而占据地球的人。

sentences.en: But they are the first to show that the takeover did, indeed, happen in a geological eye-blink.
sentences.zh: 但他们是第一个证明这种取代过程的确发生在地质学意义上一眨眼之间的人。

sentences.en: (C) Dinosaur skeletons are rare.
sentences.zh: 恐龙骨架很罕见。

sentences.en: Dinosaur footprints are, however, surprisingly abundant.
sentences.zh: 然而，恐龙脚印却出乎意料地丰富。

sentences.en: And the size of the prints is as good an indication of the size of the beasts as are the skeletons themselves.
sentences.zh: 脚印的大小同骨架本身一样，是反映动物体型的良好指标。

sentences.en: Dr Olsen and his colleagues therefore concentrated on prints, not bones.
sentences.zh: 因此，奥尔森博士与同事把研究重心放在脚印而不是骨头上。

sentences.en: The prints in question were made in Eastern North America, a part of the world then full of rift valleys similar to those in East Africa today.
sentences.zh: 所关注的这些脚印形成于北美东部，那里当时遍布着与今日东非裂谷类似的裂谷。

sentences.en: Like the modern African rift valleys, the Triassic/Jurassic American ones contained lakes, and these lakes grew and shrank at regular intervals because of climatic changes.
sentences.zh: 和今天的非洲裂谷一样，三叠纪/侏罗纪时期的美洲裂谷中也有湖泊，这些湖泊由于气候变化而以规律的间隔涨落。

sentences.en: Rocks from this place and period can be dated to within a few thousand years.
sentences.zh: 这一地区、这一时期的岩石可以被精确到几千年内进行定年。

sentences.en: As a bonus, squishy lake-edge sediments are just the things for recording the tracks of passing animals.
sentences.zh: 更妙的是，湖边那些软泥沉积物，正是记录路过动物足迹的绝佳介质。

sentences.en: (D) By dividing the labour between them, the research team were able to study such tracks at 80 sites and look at 18 so-called ‘ichnotaxa'.
sentences.zh: 研究团队通过分工合作，得以在 80 个地点研究这类足迹，并查看了所谓的 18 个“ichnotaxa”（足迹分类单元）。

sentences.en: These are recognisable types of footprint that cannot be matched precisely within the species of animal that left them.
sentences.zh: 这些是可被辨识的脚印类型，无法精确对应到留下它们的具体动物物种。

sentences.en: But they can be matched with a general sort of animal, and thus act as an indicator of the fate of that group, even when there are no bones to tell the story.
sentences.zh: 但它们可以对应到大致的动物类别，因而即便没有骨骼来佐证，也能作为该类群命运的指示器。

sentences.en: (E) Their findings show that five of the ichnotaxa disappear before the end of the Triassic, and four march confidently across the boundary into the Jurassic.
sentences.zh: 他们的发现表明，其中有五种足迹类型在三叠纪结束之前就消失了，另有四种则信心十足地跨过界线进入了侏罗纪。

sentences.en: Six, however, vanish at the boundary, or only just splutter across it; and three appear from nowhere, almost as soon as the Jurassic begins.
sentences.zh: 另外六种则在界线处消失，或者只是勉强跨过去；还有三种几乎是在侏罗纪刚开始就突然冒了出来。

sentences.en: That boundary itself is suggestive.
sentences.zh: 这条界线本身就很耐人寻味。

sentences.en: The first geological indication of the impact that killed the dinosaurs was an unusually high level of iridium in rocks at the end of the Cretaceous period, when the beasts disappear from the fossil record.
sentences.zh: 灭杀恐龙的那次撞击的第一项地质学证据，是白垩纪末期岩石中异常高的铱含量——那时这些动物从化石记录中消失。

sentences.en: Iridium is normally rare at the Earth's surface, but it is more abundant in meteorites.
sentences.zh: 铱通常在地表很罕见，但在陨石中含量更高。

sentences.en: When people began to believe the impact theory, they started looking for other Cretaceous-end anomalies.
sentences.zh: 当人们开始相信撞击理论时，便着手寻找白垩纪末期的其他异常现象。

sentences.en: One that turned up was a surprising abundance of fern spores in rocks just above the boundary layer – a phenomenon known as the ‘fern spike'.
sentences.zh: 其中一个被发现的是界线层之上岩石中蕨类孢子的惊人富集——这种现象被称为“蕨类孢子峰”。

sentences.en: (F) That matched the theory nicely.
sentences.zh: 这一点与该理论吻合得很好。

sentences.en: Many modern ferns are opportunists.
sentences.zh: 许多现代蕨类植物是机会主义者。

sentences.en: They cannot compete against plants with leaves, but if a piece of land is cleared by, say, a volcanic eruption, they are often the first things to set up shop there.
sentences.zh: 它们无法与有叶植物竞争，但如果一块土地被——比如说——火山喷发清空，它们往往是最先在那里安家落户的。

sentences.en: An asteroid strike would have scoured much of the Earth of its vegetable cover, and provided a paradise for ferns.
sentences.zh: 一次小行星撞击会把地球上的植被大面积清除掉，为蕨类提供一个天堂。

sentences.en: A fern spike in the rocks is thus a good indication that something terrible has happened.
sentences.zh: 因此，岩石中出现蕨类孢子峰，是某种可怕事件发生的良好线索。

sentences.en: (G) The surprises are how rapidly the new ichnotaxa appeared and how quickly they increased in size.
sentences.zh: 令人吃惊的是新出现的足迹类型出现得如此之快，且体型增长得如此之迅速。

sentences.en: Dr Olsen and his colleagues suggest that the explanation for this may be a phenomenon called ecological release.
sentences.zh: 奥尔森博士及其同事认为，这或许可以用一种被称为“生态释放”的现象来解释。

sentences.en: This is seen today when reptiles (which in modern times tend to be small creatures) reach islands where they face no competitors.
sentences.zh: 如今当爬行动物（在现代多为小型生物）抵达没有竞争者的岛屿时，便能见到这种现象。

sentences.en: The most spectacular example is on the Indonesian island of Komodo, where local lizards have grown so large that they are often referred to as dragons.
sentences.zh: 最壮观的例子出现在印度尼西亚的科莫多岛，那里当地的蜥蜴长得非常大，人们常常把它们称为“龙”。

sentences.en: The dinosaurs, in other words, could flourish only when the competition had been knocked out.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，恐龙只有在竞争对手被清除掉之后才能繁盛起来。

sentences.en: (H) That leaves the question of where the impact happened.
sentences.zh: 剩下的问题是，那次撞击发生在哪里。

sentences.en: No large hole in the Earth's crust seems to be 202 million years old.
sentences.zh: 地球壳上似乎没有哪一个大型坑洞的年龄是 2.02 亿年。

sentences.en: It may, of course, have been overlooked.
sentences.zh: 当然，它有可能被忽略了。

sentences.en: Old craters are eroded and buried, and not always easy to find.
sentences.zh: 古老的撞击坑会被侵蚀和掩埋，并不总是容易找到。

sentences.en: Alternatively, it may have vanished.
sentences.zh: 也可能它已经消失了。

sentences.en: Although continental crust is more or less permanent, the ocean floor is constantly recycled by the tectonic processes that bring about continental drift.
sentences.zh: 尽管大陆地壳大致是永久存在的，但海底却因带动大陆漂移的板块运动而不断被回收利用。

sentences.en: There is no ocean floor left that is more than 200 million years old, so a crater that formed in the ocean would have been swallowed up by now.
sentences.zh: 如今没有任何超过 2 亿年的洋底残留，所以一个形成于海洋中的撞击坑到现在早已被吞没。

sentences.en: (I) There is a third possibility, however.
sentences.zh: 不过，还有第三种可能性。

sentences.en: This is that the crater is known, but has been misdated.
sentences.zh: 那就是这个撞击坑是已知的，只是它的年代被定错了。

sentences.en: The Manicouagan ‘structure', a crater in Quebec, is thought to be 214 million years old.
sentences.zh: 位于魁北克的马尼夸根（Manicouagan）“结构”——一个撞击坑——目前被认为有 2.14 亿年的历史。

sentences.en: It is huge – some 100 kilometres across – and seems to be the largest of between three and five craters that formed within a few hours of each other as the lumps of disintegrated comet hit the Earth one by one.
sentences.zh: 它非常大——直径约 100 公里——而且似乎是 3 到 5 个撞击坑中最大的一个，这些撞击坑是在解体的彗星碎块逐一撞击地球的几小时内相继形成的。

sentences.en: Such an impact would surely have had a perceptible effect on the world, but the rocks from 214 million years ago do not record one.
sentences.zh: 这样一次撞击对世界肯定会产生明显的影响，但 2.14 亿年前的岩石却并未记录到这种影响。

sentences.en: It is possible, therefore, that Manicouagan has been misdated.
sentences.zh: 因此，马尼夸根有可能被定错了年代。

sentences.en: That will be the next thing to check.
sentences.zh: 这将是下一步要核实的事情。

sentences.en: (A)  Though Rome draws tourists from around the world to its many impressive sites, one notable monument there has never attracted nearly as much interest: the Pyramid of Cestius.
sentences.zh: 尽管罗马以众多令人叹为观止的名胜吸引着世界各地的游客，那里却有一座引人注目的古迹从未引起过同样多的关注：塞斯提乌斯金字塔。

sentences.en: But why would there be a pyramid in Italy?
sentences.zh: 可是，意大利怎么会有一座金字塔呢？

sentences.en: After the Roman conquest of Egypt in 30 B.C., Egyptian architectural style became the fashion in Rome.
sentences.zh: 公元前30年罗马征服埃及之后，埃及的建筑风格在罗马蔚然成风。

sentences.en: (B) Though obelisks and other monuments inspired by Egypt's great pyramids sprang up around the city, only two actual pyramids are known to have been built.
sentences.zh: 尽管受埃及大金字塔启发而建的方尖碑和其他纪念性建筑在城中纷纷涌现，但据知真正建成的金字塔只有两座。

sentences.en: The only one left standing, the Pyramid of Cestius, was designed as the burial pyramid for a Roman politician named Caius Cestius, who ordered that the building work be completed within a period of 330 days.
sentences.zh: 如今唯一留存的塞斯提乌斯金字塔，是为一位名叫盖乌斯·塞斯提乌斯的罗马政客设计的陵墓金字塔，他下令工程必须在330天之内完工。

sentences.en: Construction took place at some point between 18 B.C. and 12 B.C.
sentences.zh: 建造工程是在公元前18年至前12年之间的某个时候进行的。

sentences.en: Cestius' pyramid had a layer of white Carrara marble on the outside, and was constructed from brick held together by a basic kind of cement on the inside.
sentences.zh: 塞斯提乌斯的金字塔外覆一层白色的卡拉拉大理石，内部则由砖块砌成，用一种最基本的水泥黏合。

sentences.en: One of the things that strikes you when you look at the pyramid is how steep it is, so that the shape of Cestius' pyramid is quite unlike that of typical Egyptian ones.
sentences.zh: 当你望着这座金字塔时，令你印象深刻的一点是它有多么陡峭，以致塞斯提乌斯金字塔的外形与典型的埃及金字塔颇为不同。

sentences.en: This is a difference that could have been the result of inaccurate information sent back to Rome by soldiers who saw the pyramids in person in Egypt.
sentences.zh: 这种差异可能是由于那些在埃及亲眼见过金字塔的士兵把不准确的信息传回了罗马所致。

sentences.en: Alternatively, Roman builders could have drawn inspiration from the pyramids in Nubia, a region located in what is today northern Sudan and southern Egypt.
sentences.zh: 或者，罗马的建造者也可能是从努比亚的金字塔中获得了灵感，努比亚这一地区位于今天苏丹北部和埃及南部一带。

sentences.en: (C) At the time of its construction, since there was a strict Roman law prohibiting the placement of tombs within the city itself, the Pyramid of Cestius would have stood in the countryside.
sentences.zh: 在它建造之时，由于罗马有一条严格的法律禁止在城内安置坟墓，塞斯提乌斯金字塔当时应是矗立在乡野之中。

sentences.en: Rome grew enormously during the next two centuries, and, by the 3rd century A.D., the pyramid would have been surrounded by buildings.
sentences.zh: 在随后的两个世纪里，罗马急剧扩张，到公元3世纪，这座金字塔想必已被建筑物所环绕。

sentences.en: We also know that in the 3rd century A.D., the Pyramid of Cestius was hidden behind a high wall on the orders of Emperor Aurelian; this probably helped it survive throughout the centuries to come, even as other ancient monuments disappeared.
sentences.zh: 我们还知道，公元3世纪，塞斯提乌斯金字塔奉奥勒良皇帝之命被隐没在一道高墙之后；这或许帮助它在此后的数百年间得以存留，即便其他古代遗迹纷纷消失。

sentences.en: By the Middle Ages, the pyramid was covered in vegetation and thick dirt, and popular myth had developed that it might be a tomb for one of the twin brothers Romulus and Remus, who were regarded as the men who had established the city of Rome.
sentences.zh: 到中世纪时，金字塔已覆满植被和厚厚的尘土，民间还流传起一种说法，说它可能是罗慕路斯和雷穆斯这对孪生兄弟之一的陵墓，这两人被视为建立罗马城的人。

sentences.en: Cestius' actual tomb within the pyramid and the inscription identifying the pyramid as his weren't rediscovered until the 1660s, when the pyramid underwent restoration.
sentences.zh: 金字塔内塞斯提乌斯真正的墓室，以及确认金字塔属于他的那处铭文，直到17世纪60年代金字塔进行修复时才被重新发现。

sentences.en: During excavations, when trees and plants were cleared away, two marble bases were found in front of the pyramid, as well as fragments of bronze statues that had once stood on them, on either side of the pyramid.
sentences.zh: 在发掘过程中，当树木和植物被清除之后，人们在金字塔前面、金字塔两侧发现了两座大理石基座，以及曾经立于其上的青铜雕像的残片。

sentences.en: The people employed to excavate the pyramid did not find the urn that would have contained Cestius' remains, but they did come across a tunnel.
sentences.zh: 受雇发掘金字塔的人没有找到本应盛放塞斯提乌斯遗骸的骨灰瓮，却发现了一条隧道。

sentences.en: It was quite possible, therefore, that robbers had at some earlier time removed the contents of the tomb.
sentences.zh: 因此很有可能，盗墓者早在更早的时候就已把墓中的东西洗劫一空。

sentences.en: But while some of the features of Cestius' tomb no longer exist, at least the pyramid itself has survived.
sentences.zh: 但是，尽管塞斯提乌斯墓的某些构件已不复存在，至少金字塔本身保留了下来。

sentences.en: (D) Today, the foundations of Cestius' pyramid rest below street level near an intersection with heavy traffic, so that passing tourists and residents could easily fail to notice its full height of 119 feet.
sentences.zh: 如今，塞斯提乌斯金字塔的地基位于一处车流繁忙的十字路口附近的街面之下，以致路过的游客和居民很容易忽略它高达119英尺的全貌。

sentences.en: Across the intersection is the Piramide station, located on Line B of the Rome Metro.
sentences.zh: 十字路口对面是金字塔地铁站，位于罗马地铁B线上。

sentences.en: In 2011, the Japanese clothing-company entrepreneur Yuzo Yagi, president of Yagi Tsusho Ltd, announced his intention to help the Italian government pay for an ambitious renovation of the Pyramid of Cestius.
sentences.zh: 2011年，日本服装公司企业家、八木通商株式会社社长八木雄三宣布，他有意帮助意大利政府出资，对塞斯提乌斯金字塔进行一次雄心勃勃的修缮。

sentences.en: 'It's an act of gratitude,' he later told journalists.
sentences.zh: “这是一种感恩之举，”他后来对记者说。

sentences.en: 'Our company has grown thanks to Italy.'
sentences.zh: “我们公司的发展要归功于意大利。”

sentences.en: Work began at the site shortly after Yagi signed an official agreement with the Special Superintendency for the Archaeological Heritage of Rome, and was completed ahead of schedule thanks to his 2-million-euro contribution.
sentences.zh: 在八木与罗马考古遗产特别管理署签署正式协议后不久，工地便动工了，并得益于他200万欧元的捐助而提前完工。

sentences.en: (E) As archaeologist Leonardo Guarnieri explained to journalists, officials are now conducting tours of the newly renovated pyramid twice a month by reservation.
sentences.zh: 正如考古学家莱昂纳多·瓜尔涅里向记者解释的那样，官方如今每月两次、以预约方式组织参观这座新近修缮的金字塔。

sentences.en: Visitors who take advantage of the tour can make their way through a narrow corridor in order to enter the burial chamber itself.
sentences.zh: 参加这种参观的访客，可以穿过一条狭窄的走廊，进入墓室本身。

sentences.en: It is within these walls that they can admire the frescoes: watercolour paintings typical of the time.
sentences.zh: 正是在这些墙壁之内，他们得以欣赏壁画：那是当时典型的水彩画。

sentences.en: In the chamber, it is possible to make out four frescoes of the winged Roman goddess of war, Victoria, a figure from Roman legend, as well as a series of vases, the type that would have been used for special rituals and purification purposes.
sentences.zh: 在墓室中，可以辨认出四幅长着翅膀的罗马战争女神维多利亚的壁画，她是罗马传说中的人物，此外还有一系列花瓶，正是当年用于特殊仪式和净化用途的那种。

sentences.en: We know from the writings of earlier visitors that there used to be more here, but the majority have disappeared over time.
sentences.zh: 我们从早先访客的记述中得知，这里原本还有更多壁画，但大多数都已随时间消失。

sentences.en: Only one problem remains now that the restoration is complete.
sentences.zh: 如今修复已经完成，只剩下一个问题。

sentences.en: The white exterior of the Pyramid of Cestius will have to be cleaned every few months to remove the layer of urban pollution.
sentences.zh: 塞斯提乌斯金字塔白色的外表面将不得不每隔几个月清洗一次，以除去那层城市污垢。

sentences.en: A team of free-climbers will be employed to do the job, in order to avoid placing builders' scaffolding around the newly welcoming monument.
sentences.zh: 这项工作将雇用一支徒手攀岩队来完成，以免在这座新近向公众开放的古迹周围搭建施工脚手架。

sentences.en: (A) Slow Food began when Carlo Petrini, an Italian journalist, was dismayed by the opening of a fast food restaurant on the famous Piazza di Spagna in Rome.
sentences.zh: 慢食运动始于意大利记者卡洛·佩特里尼对一家快餐店在罗马著名的西班牙广场开张的失望。

sentences.en: He decided it was time to celebrate the fast-disappearing virtues of the slow production, preparation and eating of food.
sentences.zh: 他认定，是时候去颂扬那些正在迅速消失的美德了——慢慢地生产、烹制和享用食物。

sentences.en: What he had in mind when he began the Slow Food organization were local foods which were prepared in their traditional manner and eaten at leisurely meals with family and friends.
sentences.zh: 他创立慢食组织时心中所想的，是那些以传统方式烹制、在与家人朋友悠闲共餐时享用的本地食物。

sentences.en: Slow Food is the antithesis of everything fast food stands for, and it is now a thriving international organization with members in 45 countries, a successful publishing operation and a biannual trade show.
sentences.zh: 慢食运动是快餐所代表的一切的对立面，如今它已是一个蓬勃发展的国际组织，在45个国家拥有会员，经营着成功的出版业务，并举办一年两次的贸易展。

sentences.en: In addition, Slow Food has launched a project called the 'Ark of Taste' and a concept called 'virtuous globalization'.
sentences.zh: 此外，慢食运动还发起了一个名为“味觉方舟”的项目，提出了一个称为“良性全球化”的理念。

sentences.en: (B)  The Ark of Taste is the catalog of endangered food plant and animal species that Slow Food has resolved to protect against the rising global tide of fast food.
sentences.zh: 味觉方舟是一份濒危食用动植物物种的名录，慢食运动决心保护这些物种，使其免遭日益高涨的全球快餐浪潮的冲击。

sentences.en: Some examples of the biodiversity promoted by the Ark of Taste include Iroquois white corn and the Narragansett turkey, both of which are old, or heritage, foods in North America.
sentences.zh: 味觉方舟所倡导的生物多样性中，有易洛魁白玉米和纳拉甘西特火鸡，二者都是北美古老的、即传承下来的食物。

sentences.en: Biodiversity is a term commonly associated with discussions of threats to wild species, but according to Slow Food the biodiversity of the domesticated species people have depended on for centuries is no less important.
sentences.zh: 生物多样性是一个通常与野生物种受威胁的讨论联系在一起的术语，但慢食运动认为，人类数百年来赖以为生的驯化物种的多样性同样重要。

sentences.en: For example, when the latest patented hybrid variety of plant proves unable to withstand fungal or bacterial disease, plant breeders will need the disease-resistant genes which can be obtained from heritage plant varieties.
sentences.zh: 例如，当最新的专利杂交植物品种被证明无法抵御真菌或细菌病害时，植物育种者就会需要那些可从传承品种中获得的抗病基因。

sentences.en: If Iroquois white corn had fallen out of production, as it very nearly did two decades ago due to the commercial launch of a new hybrid corn, irreplaceable and possibly crucial sets of corn genes would have been lost forever.
sentences.zh: 假如易洛魁白玉米停产——二十年前由于一种新杂交玉米的商业推出，它险些就停产了——那么一批无可替代、或许至关重要的玉米基因就将永远消失。

sentences.en: (C) For some time, plant-saver groups have been preserving heritage plant varieties, but Slow Food takes that project a step further.
sentences.zh: 一段时间以来，植物保种团体一直在保存传承植物品种，而慢食运动则把这项事业又推进了一步。

sentences.en: The movement understands that all the food and plant species in its Ark of Taste carry not only information about genetic traits but they also embody a set of social practices, and in some cases even a way of life of previous generations.
sentences.zh: 这场运动明白，其味觉方舟中所有的食物和植物物种，不仅携带着遗传性状的信息，还承载着一整套社会习俗，某些情况下甚至承载着前几代人的一种生活方式。

sentences.en: Slow Food teaches that when a variety of food or breed of animal disappears, something greater also disappears: a specific, irreplaceable mode of life that a particular people have devised for living in a particular part of the Earth.
sentences.zh: 慢食运动告诉人们，当一种食物或一个动物品种消失时，某种更重要的东西也随之消失：那是某个特定民族为在地球上某个特定地方生活而创造出的、无可替代的独特生活方式。

sentences.en: An example of this is the Iroquois white corn.
sentences.zh: 易洛魁白玉米就是一个例子。

sentences.en: By working to find new markets for this ancient variety of corn, Slow Food is ensuring a source of income for the Native Americans who grow, roast, and grind this corn and, at the same time, helping to preserve the specific cookery and religious uses that the corn has been selected to support over hundreds of years.
sentences.zh: 通过努力为这一古老的玉米品种开拓新市场，慢食运动既为种植、烘烤和研磨这种玉米的美洲原住民确保了收入来源，同时也帮助保留了数百年来这种玉米被选育以支撑的特定烹饪和宗教用途。

sentences.en: (D) Slow Food has moved away from the traditional locations for preserving rare animal and plant species.
sentences.zh: 慢食运动已不再依赖那些保存珍稀动植物物种的传统场所。

sentences.en: For example, instead of zoos for rare animals and botanic gardens for rare plants, Slow Food maintains that its plants and animals are best preserved on the dishes and plates of discerning customers.
sentences.zh: 例如，慢食运动主张，比起把珍稀动物关进动物园、把珍稀植物种进植物园，它的动植物最好是被保存在有鉴赏力的顾客的餐盘之中。

sentences.en: To this end, Slow Food has introduced the concept of virtuous globalization, which recognizes that the best way to ensure a safe future for distinctive local products and practices is to find a global market for them.
sentences.zh: 为此，慢食运动提出了良性全球化的理念，它认识到，为独具特色的本地产品和习俗确保安全未来的最佳途径，就是为它们找到一个全球市场。

sentences.en: In this way, local producers will be able to continue producing the food which for many years has been a defining factor of their cultural identity.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，本地生产者就能继续生产那些多年来一直是其文化认同决定性因素的食物。

sentences.en: The characteristics of the virtuous globalization of Slow Foods show how different the concept is from the globalization of fast foods.
sentences.zh: 慢食良性全球化的特点，显示出这一理念与快餐全球化有多么不同。

sentences.en: Whereas global fast food companies aim to sell food that has an unchanging taste wherever in the world it is eaten, the taste of a recognized Slow Food is unique to that food.
sentences.zh: 全球快餐公司力求出售一种无论在世界何处食用都口味不变的食物，而一种公认的慢食，其味道则是该食物所独有的。

sentences.en: Another aspect is the quantities sold of these two types of food.
sentences.zh: 另一个方面是这两类食物的销售数量。

sentences.en: In the case of fast food, these are enormous, but the quantities of Slow Food products which are available for selling are limited, due to the rarity of the plants or animals.
sentences.zh: 就快餐而言，销量极为庞大，而可供出售的慢食产品数量却很有限，原因在于相关动植物的稀有。

sentences.en: The customers of virtuous globalization Slow Foods are affluent people who value novelty and are undeterred by the costs, which are high when compared to fast food.
sentences.zh: 良性全球化慢食的顾客是富裕人群，他们看重新奇，也不会被价格吓退——相比快餐，这些慢食的价格是偏高的。

sentences.en: (E) Some years ago, a network of farmers in the USA volunteered to take part in a national Slow Food project.
sentences.zh: 几年前，美国的一个农户网络自愿参加了一个全国性的慢食项目。

sentences.en: The project was for the farmers to raise a total of 5,000 turkeys from eggs which had been selected from four varieties of endangered turkey.
sentences.zh: 该项目要求这些农户用从四个濒危火鸡品种中选出的火鸡蛋，共饲养出5000只火鸡。

sentences.en: The farmers had to begin by hatching the eggs they had been supplied with, then raising the young turkeys to adults.
sentences.zh: 农户们得先把分到的火鸡蛋孵化出来，再把雏火鸡养到成年。

sentences.en: They were promised a guaranteed price per pound for the adult turkeys.
sentences.zh: 他们获得承诺，成年火鸡可按每磅保证价收购。

sentences.en: The object of the enterprise was to raise heritage turkeys for the North American holiday of Thanksgiving.
sentences.zh: 这项事业的目的，是为北美的感恩节饲养传承火鸡。

sentences.en: Although chefs in some restaurants where the turkeys were on the menu complained that the Slow Food turkeys were smaller than industrially produced turkeys, the distinctive flavors were very well received by consumers.
sentences.zh: 尽管在一些把这种火鸡列入菜单的餐厅里，厨师们抱怨慢食火鸡比工业化养殖的火鸡个头小，但其独特的风味很受消费者欢迎。

sentences.en: By the following year, the world population of these turkeys had nearly doubled.
sentences.zh: 到第二年，这些火鸡的全球数量已几乎翻了一番。

sentences.en: (F) It may seem strange that taking pleasure in eating could be a strategy for preserving biodiversity because pleasure is not normally associated with environmentalism.
sentences.zh: 把从饮食中获得乐趣当作保护生物多样性的一种策略，这听起来或许有些奇怪，因为乐趣通常并不与环保主义联系在一起。

sentences.en: However, pleasure is part of what Slow Food aims to bring back, by demonstrating that, at least when it comes to the politics of food, the best choice is often the one that provides the most enjoyment.
sentences.zh: 然而，乐趣正是慢食运动力图找回的东西之一，它要表明：至少在食物的政治这件事上，最好的选择往往就是那个带来最多享受的选择。

8.stemZh: 传统植物的基因对现代育种者可能具有至关重要的意义。

11.stemZh: 慢食组织认为，食物与文化是相互独立的。

14.stemZh: 一些美洲原住民现在正在开设烹饪课程，教授使用易洛魁白玉米的烹饪方法。

sentences.en: (A) When primitive people began using their hands to be creative, they began to add color to their lives.
sentences.zh: 当原始人开始用双手进行创造时，他们便开始为自己的生活增添色彩。

sentences.en: They used natural materials like ochre to stain animal hides, decorate shells and feathers, and paint on the walls of caves.
sentences.zh: 他们用赭石之类的天然材料给兽皮染色、装饰贝壳和羽毛，并在洞穴的岩壁上作画。

sentences.en: Ochre is a naturally occurring brownish-yellow earth containing iron oxide.
sentences.zh: 赭石是一种天然存在的、含有氧化铁的棕黄色泥土。

sentences.en: Scientists have been able to date the black, white, yellow and reddish pigments made from ochre, used in cave paintings, to over 15,000 BCE.
sentences.zh: 科学家已能将洞穴壁画中所用的、由赭石制成的黑、白、黄和偏红色颜料，追溯到公元前15000年以前。

sentences.en: With the development of fixed settlements and agriculture, around 7,000 to 2,000 BCE, people began to produce fabrics, and used natural substances such as ochre to color them.
sentences.zh: 随着固定聚落和农业的发展，大约在公元前7000至前2000年间，人们开始生产织物，并用赭石等天然物质给它们上色。

sentences.en: (B) Natural dyes, or dyes made from substances found in nature, can be broken down into two categories: substantive and adjective.
sentences.zh: 天然染料，即由自然界中的物质制成的染料，可分为两类：直接染料和媒染染料。

sentences.en: Substantive, or direct dyes, become fixed to fibers without the aid of any other chemicals or additives.
sentences.zh: 直接染料，又称直接性染料，无需任何其他化学品或添加剂的帮助，就能固着在纤维上。

sentences.en: Adjective dyes require a mordant (usually a metal salt), which acts as a fixative and prevents the color from washing out or being bleached by sunlight.
sentences.zh: 媒染染料则需要一种媒染剂（通常是某种金属盐），它起到固色的作用，防止颜色被洗掉或被阳光漂淡。

sentences.en: Most natural dyes are adjective dyes, and require the application of a mordant solution to the fibers at some point in the dyeing process.
sentences.zh: 大多数天然染料都是媒染染料，需要在染色过程的某个环节给纤维施加媒染剂溶液。

sentences.en: (C) Historically, three natural fibers were used in making fabrics: wool, silk and cotton.
sentences.zh: 历史上，制作织物所用的天然纤维有三种：羊毛、丝绸和棉花。

sentences.en: Wool fabric remains have been found in Europe dating back to 2,000 BCE.
sentences.zh: 在欧洲已发现可追溯到公元前2000年的羊毛织物残片。

sentences.en: It was a common medieval fabric worn in both dyed and natural colors and was processed by both professional manufacturers and by people in their own homes.
sentences.zh: 羊毛是中世纪常见的织物，染色的和本色的都有人穿，既由专业的制造商加工，也由人们在自己家中加工。

sentences.en: Silk was imported from China to Europe, and in the 14th to 16th centuries major silk manufacturing centers were set up in France, Spain and Italy.
sentences.zh: 丝绸由中国进口到欧洲，14至16世纪，法国、西班牙和意大利建立起了主要的丝绸制造中心。

sentences.en: These silk production centers also became centers of dye technology, as most silk was dyed and required the highest quality dyes available.
sentences.zh: 这些丝绸生产中心也成了染色技术的中心，因为大多数丝绸都要染色，需要当时能买到的最高品质的染料。

sentences.en: Cotton was considered a luxury fabric in Europe, as it was imported all the way from India and was dyed before it was shipped.
sentences.zh: 棉布在欧洲被视为奢侈织物，因为它要从遥远的印度进口，而且在运出之前就已染好色。

sentences.en: Cotton was also valued because of the brightness and colorfastness of the dyes used to color it.
sentences.zh: 棉布之所以受重视，还因为给它染色所用染料色泽鲜艳、不易褪色。

sentences.en: (D)  Dyes that gave fabrics a good bright color and were able to withstand washing and exposure to sunlight without losing their color were highly prized.
sentences.zh: 那些能让织物呈现鲜亮色彩、又能经受洗涤和日晒而不褪色的染料，备受珍视。

sentences.en: The names of some of these valued and traded colors are still familiar today.
sentences.zh: 其中一些珍贵且用于贸易的颜色的名称，至今仍为人们所熟悉。

sentences.en: The color known as Tyrian purple, for example, originated in the Mediterranean 2,000 years ago, and cochineal is the name given to the red dye from Latin America.
sentences.zh: 例如，被称为推罗紫的颜色，两千年前起源于地中海地区，而胭脂虫红则是对来自拉丁美洲的那种红色染料的称呼。

sentences.en: Both of these colors came from animals; the mucus found in certain species of shellfish produced the deep, rich Tyrian purple and cochineal was extracted from insects.
sentences.zh: 这两种颜色都来自动物；某些贝类体内的黏液产生了浓郁深沉的推罗紫，而胭脂虫红则是从昆虫中提取的。

sentences.en: Two other natural sources of color were saffron and indigo.
sentences.zh: 另外两种天然的颜色来源是藏红花和靛蓝。

sentences.en: Saffron, the base of yellow dyes, comes from the flowers of a particular kind of crocus which is thought to have first been cultivated on Crete in the eastern Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 藏红花是黄色染料的基础，来自一种番红花的花朵，人们认为这种番红花最早是在地中海东部的克里特岛上栽培的。

sentences.en: The leaves of a plant native to India were used to produce indigo, which was the main source of the color blue.
sentences.zh: 一种原产于印度的植物的叶子被用来制取靛蓝，而靛蓝是蓝色的主要来源。

sentences.en: (E) As societies developed over the centuries, the demand for dyes and dyed fabric grew, and by the 17th century a worldwide shipping and trading network was in place, allowing dyestuffs from all parts of the world to be brought to Europe.
sentences.zh: 随着各个社会在数百年间的发展，对染料和染色织物的需求不断增长，到17世纪，一个全球性的航运和贸易网络已经形成，使来自世界各地的染料得以运往欧洲。

sentences.en: This meant that numerous dyestuffs could be blended to create a variety of colors for the rich and powerful.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，可以把众多染料调配起来，为富有而有权势的人创造出各种各样的颜色。

sentences.en: Fiber dyeing in the lower classes was a bit more restrictive.
sentences.zh: 下层阶级的纤维染色则要受到更多限制。

sentences.en: Without the money to buy exotic imported dyes, clothing in the countryside tended to be black, brown, grey and tan.
sentences.zh: 由于没有钱购买进口的异域染料，乡间的衣物往往是黑色、棕色、灰色和黄褐色。

sentences.en: Country people had some resources they could use to get a wider range of colors.
sentences.zh: 乡下人也有一些可资利用的资源，能调出范围更广的颜色。

sentences.en: They had always used local plants as food, and many of these plants were also used as medicines and in some cases as sources of dyes.
sentences.zh: 他们一向把本地植物当作食物，其中许多植物也被用作药物，某些情况下还被用作染料的来源。

sentences.en: Home dyers used any plants they could find that would give a good color.
sentences.zh: 在家染色的人会用上任何他们能找到、能染出好颜色的植物。

sentences.en: People who picked blackberries to make jam soon recognized this wild fruit as a source for a blue dye.
sentences.zh: 采摘黑莓做果酱的人很快就认识到，这种野果是一种蓝色染料的来源。

sentences.en: Washing beehives in preparation for making mead (a popular drink containing honey) yielded a liquid that could be used as a yellow dye.
sentences.zh: 为酿造蜂蜜酒（一种含有蜂蜜的流行饮品）而清洗蜂巢时，会产生一种可用作黄色染料的液体。

sentences.en: The mosses which grow in many parts of Europe were used to produce green dye.
sentences.zh: 生长在欧洲许多地方的苔藓被用来制取绿色染料。

sentences.en: (F)  With the tremendous rise of interest in chemistry in the mid-19th century, several important innovations in dyeing came about.
sentences.zh: 19世纪中叶，随着人们对化学的兴趣急剧高涨，染色方面出现了几项重要的革新。

sentences.en: Perkin, a student of celebrated European scientist Wilhelm von Hofmann, accidentally discovered the first synthetic dye, later called mauve.
sentences.zh: 珀金是著名欧洲科学家威廉·冯·霍夫曼的学生，他偶然发现了第一种合成染料，后来被称为苯胺紫。

sentences.en: The color was so popular that Perkin was able to open a factory of his own and went on to develop more synthetic dye colors.
sentences.zh: 这种颜色大受欢迎，使珀金得以开办起自己的工厂，并继续研制出更多合成染料色彩。

sentences.en: Synthetic dye production grew in Europe, and hardly a year passed until the end of the century without a new synthetic dye being patented.
sentences.zh: 合成染料的生产在欧洲不断发展，直到世纪末，几乎没有哪一年不出现一种新合成染料获得专利。

sentences.en: (G) Eventually, the old natural dyes lost popularity in favor of the newer synthetic ones, and now the use of natural dyes on a commercial scale only exists in a few remote areas where people have either little access to synthetic dyes or a vested interest in retaining their ancient dyeing customs.
sentences.zh: 最终，古老的天然染料失宠，让位给较新的合成染料，如今天然染料的商业化使用只存在于少数偏远地区，那里的人们要么很难获得合成染料，要么对保留自己古老的染色习俗有着切身的利益。

sentences.en: (A) Nico Michiels is an ecologist from the University of Tübingen in Germany who spends part of each year in Egypt, where he dives in the Red Sea, observing fish life and gathering data on its coral reefs.
sentences.zh: 尼科·米希尔斯是德国蒂宾根大学的一位生态学家，他每年都有一部分时间在埃及度过，在那里潜入红海，观察鱼类的生活，并收集珊瑚礁的数据。

sentences.en: In September 2007 he decided to find out how far red light could penetrate the ocean depths.
sentences.zh: 2007年9月，他决定弄清红光究竟能穿透到多深的海底。

sentences.en: Seawater absorbs different colours at different depths, and as an experienced diver, Michiels was aware that red light is extinguished not far below the surface whereas blue-green light penetrates deeper.
sentences.zh: 海水在不同深度吸收不同的颜色，作为一名经验丰富的潜水员，米希尔斯知道红光在水面下不深处就会消失，而蓝绿光则能穿透得更深。

sentences.en: To find out the depth at which red disappeared in this particular ocean, however, he attached a special plastic filter to his dive mask, which was designed to block out all colours except red.
sentences.zh: 然而，为了弄清在这片特定的海域里红色会在多深处消失，他在潜水镜上加装了一片特制的塑料滤光片，这种滤片专门用来滤掉除红色以外的所有颜色。

sentences.en: Then he began to descend.
sentences.zh: 随后他开始下潜。

sentences.en: (B) In theory, once he reached about 15 metres, he should have been plunged into darkness.
sentences.zh: 按理说，一旦下潜到约15米深，他本应陷入一片黑暗。

sentences.en: Instead, something totally unexpected happened.
sentences.zh: 然而，发生的却是完全出乎意料的事。

sentences.en: Sure enough, 20 metres down it was as dark as night.
sentences.zh: 果然，下到20米深时，四周漆黑如夜。

sentences.en: 'All the fish disappeared.
sentences.zh: “所有的鱼都消失了。

sentences.en: With no light from the surface, they were effectively black and had become invisible,' he says.
sentences.zh: 由于没有来自水面的光，它们实际上一片漆黑，已变得无法看见，”他说。

sentences.en: 'But it didn't stay black for long.
sentences.zh: “但黑暗并没有持续太久。

sentences.en: Then I saw a group of goby fish with bright red eyes lit up against the background.
sentences.zh: 接着，我看到一群虾虎鱼，它们鲜红的眼睛在背景中亮了起来。

sentences.en: After that, red spots began to show up all over the reef.'
sentences.zh: 在那之后，红色的斑点开始遍布整片珊瑚礁。”

sentences.en: (C) Even with the red filter removed, Michiels could pick them out without much trouble once his eyes grew accustomed to the gloom.
sentences.zh: 即便取下红色滤片，只要眼睛适应了昏暗，米希尔斯也能毫不费力地把它们分辨出来。

sentences.en: It seems strange that no diver or researcher had spotted all this red before, but as Michiels points out, no one saw it because no one expected to see it.
sentences.zh: 此前竟没有哪位潜水员或研究者注意到这么多红色，这似乎有些奇怪，但正如米希尔斯所指出的，之所以没人看到，是因为没人料想会看到。

sentences.en: On that one dive, Michiels discovered three fish species with prominent red markings, and has found many others since.
sentences.zh: 仅那一次下潜，米希尔斯就发现了三种带有醒目红色斑纹的鱼，此后又陆续发现了许多其他种类。

sentences.en: (D) But how can fish appear red where there's no red light?
sentences.zh: 但是，在没有红光的地方，鱼怎么会显出红色呢？

sentences.en: Ordinary red pigments* look red because they reflect red light while absorbing all other wavelengths.
sentences.zh: 普通的红色色素*之所以看起来是红的，是因为它们反射红光，同时吸收所有其他波长的光。

sentences.en: At 20 metres down, there had to be some other explanation for the red Michiels was seeing.
sentences.zh: 在20米深的水下，米希尔斯所看到的红色一定另有缘故。

sentences.en: He suspected fluorescence.
sentences.zh: 他怀疑是荧光。

sentences.en: Fluorescent pigments behave differently from ordinary ones: they receive incoming light of one wavelength, for example blue, and emit light of a longer wavelength, in this case red.
sentences.zh: 荧光色素的表现与普通色素不同：它们接收某一波长的入射光，例如蓝光，再发出波长更长的光，在这里就是红光。

sentences.en: On the reef in the Red Sea during daytime, the most likely explanation was that the predominantly blue and green wavelengths at depth triggered the emission of fluorescent red in the fish.
sentences.zh: 在红海的珊瑚礁上，白天最有可能的解释是，深处占主导的蓝绿波长激发了鱼体发出红色荧光。

sentences.en: (E) With only a week left in Egypt, and lacking the equipment to confirm that the fish were fluorescent, Michiels photographed as many of them as he could.
sentences.zh: 在埃及只剩下一周时间、又缺乏设备来证实这些鱼会发荧光的情况下，米希尔斯尽其所能地给它们拍了照。

sentences.en: Then, once back in Germany, he bought an assortment of tropical fish and installed them in his lab.
sentences.zh: 随后，回到德国后，他买来各式各样的热带鱼，安置在自己的实验室里。

sentences.en: Here he confirmed that the fish did indeed fluoresce.
sentences.zh: 在这里，他证实了这些鱼确实会发出荧光。

sentences.en: In most of the fish he looked at, the fluorescence could be traced to specialised pigment cells that lie in the skin beneath the scales.
sentences.zh: 在他所观察的大多数鱼身上，荧光都可以追溯到位于鳞片之下皮肤里的特化色素细胞。

sentences.en: These cells contain 'guanine crystals', which scatter light to give fish their silvery sheen.
sentences.zh: 这些细胞含有“鸟嘌呤晶体”，它们散射光线，使鱼呈现出银亮的光泽。

sentences.en: However, Michiels says they are still not sure exactly what is fluorescing.
sentences.zh: 不过，米希尔斯说，他们仍不确定究竟是什么在发荧光。

sentences.en: 'It's not the crystals themselves.
sentences.zh: “并不是晶体本身。

sentences.en: It's probably a fluorescent protein built into the crystals, and we have a suspicion that it might be made by bacteria.'
sentences.zh: 很可能是嵌在晶体里的一种荧光蛋白，而我们怀疑它或许是由细菌产生的。”

sentences.en: (F) Intrigued, Michiels began a systematic search for red fluorescence in reef fish.
sentences.zh: 出于好奇，米希尔斯开始系统地搜寻珊瑚礁鱼类身上的红色荧光。

sentences.en: He and his colleagues, Nils Anthes and Dennis Sprenger, have identified some 50 species with red fluorescence.
sentences.zh: 他和同事尼尔斯·安特斯、丹尼斯·施普伦格已鉴定出约50种带有红色荧光的鱼。

sentences.en: The most common markings tend to be on the body towards the head and to a lesser extent around the eyes, and then the fins.
sentences.zh: 最常见的斑纹往往位于身体靠近头部的部位，其次是眼睛周围，再次是鱼鳍。

sentences.en: To Michiels, the distribution of these markings is one of the strongest indications that red fluorescence has a very particular function: communication with other members of the species.
sentences.zh: 在米希尔斯看来，这些斑纹的分布是最有力的迹象之一，表明红色荧光有着一种非常特定的功能：与同种的其他成员进行交流。

sentences.en: According to several recent studies, a whole range of animals employ fluorescence as a natural highlighter to boost the visibility of body parts they use to signal, for example to ward off enemies.
sentences.zh: 据近来几项研究，一大批动物都把荧光当作一种天然的“荧光笔”，用以提高它们用来发信号的身体部位的可见度，例如用来吓退敌人。

sentences.en: In reef fish, the red tends to be confined to parts of the body used to signal, suggesting these markings serve a similar function.
sentences.zh: 在珊瑚礁鱼类身上，红色往往局限于用来发信号的身体部位，这表明这些斑纹起着类似的作用。

sentences.en: But instead of highlighting an existing colour, the fluorescence gives the fish a colour that otherwise wouldn't exist.
sentences.zh: 但荧光并不是去凸显一种已有的颜色，而是赋予鱼一种本来并不存在的颜色。

sentences.en: For example, fish commonly use eye rings to signal that they are present and their direction of gaze, and Michiels suspects that red-eyed gobies use signals to indicate their location and keep their group together.
sentences.zh: 例如，鱼类常用眼圈来示意自己的存在和注视的方向，米希尔斯猜测，红眼的虾虎鱼会用信号来表明自己的位置，使群体聚拢在一起。

sentences.en: (G) Red light, whatever its source, doesn't travel far through water, which suggests signals are intended to be private, seen only by nearby fish of the right species.
sentences.zh: 红光无论来自何处，在水中都传不远，这表明这种信号是有意保持私密的，只让附近同种的鱼看到。

sentences.en: There are several lines of evidence to support this, says Michiels.
sentences.zh: 米希尔斯说，有好几方面的证据支持这一点。

sentences.en: And closely related species do not have completely identical markings, which suggests they might be important in species recognition.
sentences.zh: 而且亲缘关系相近的物种，其斑纹并不完全相同，这表明它们在物种识别中可能很重要。

sentences.en: (H) Michiels suspects red fluorescence has another important role for some reef fish: helping them blend in.
sentences.zh: 米希尔斯猜测，对某些珊瑚礁鱼类来说，红色荧光还有另一个重要作用：帮助它们隐身于环境之中。

sentences.en: During his first dive with the red filter, he noticed corals glow a dark but faint red too.
sentences.zh: 在他第一次戴着红色滤片下潜时，他注意到珊瑚也会发出一种暗淡而微弱的红光。

sentences.en: Against this irregular red background, a fish that glows red all over would be hard to distinguish.
sentences.zh: 在这种斑驳不规则的红色背景下，一条通体泛红的鱼会很难被辨认出来。

sentences.en: More compelling for Michiels is the case of the scorpionfish, which lies perfectly still until food swims past, which it then sucks in.
sentences.zh: 对米希尔斯来说更有说服力的，是鲉鱼的例子，它一动不动地潜伏着，直到食物游过，便一口把它吸进去。

sentences.en: (I) Yet if red plays any part in a fish's life, then it must be able to see it.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果红色在鱼的生活中起着任何作用，那么它就必须能够看见红色。

sentences.en: Fish that live in a world dominated by blue-green light are assumed to have eyes tuned to those wavelengths, and most marine fish that have been studied are thought incapable of seeing red.
sentences.zh: 人们假定，生活在蓝绿光主导的世界里的鱼，眼睛是与那些波长相适应的，而已被研究过的大多数海洋鱼类被认为无法看见红色。

sentences.en: One exception is the seahorse, whose eyes are sensitive to red.
sentences.zh: 一个例外是海马，它的眼睛对红色敏感。

sentences.en: As for the other fish, it remains to be seen.
sentences.zh: 至于其他的鱼，那就有待观察了。

sentences.en: (A) Traditionally, smell has not been at the forefront of sensory research, pushed aside in favour of the seemingly more vital senses of vision and hearing.
sentences.zh: 传统上，嗅觉一直不处于感官研究的前沿，而是被搁在一边，让位于视觉和听觉这两种看似更为重要的感官。

sentences.en: There has been a strong belief that people, especially compared to other mammals, are not that influenced by smells.
sentences.zh: 人们一直坚信，相比其他哺乳动物，人类受气味的影响并不那么大。

sentences.en: (B) One of the first to assert the relative unimportance of the human sense of smell was Pierre Paul Broca, an influential 19th-century anatomist.
sentences.zh: 最早断言人类嗅觉相对无足轻重的人之一，是19世纪颇有影响力的解剖学家皮埃尔·保罗·布罗卡。

sentences.en: After comparing the proportion of the brain devoted to smell in different animals, he suggested that mammals can be classed into two broad groups: macrosmatic mammals, such as dogs, have a finely tuned sense of smell which they rely on to perceive the world, while marine mammals and primates, including humans, are microsmatic – the organ with which they smell is small and functionally redundant.
sentences.zh: 在比较了不同动物大脑中用于嗅觉的比例之后，他提出哺乳动物可以大致分为两类：像狗这样的强嗅觉哺乳动物，拥有极为灵敏的嗅觉，并依赖它来感知世界；而包括人类在内的海洋哺乳动物和灵长类则属于弱嗅觉动物——它们用来嗅闻的器官又小、在功能上又多余。

sentences.en: (C) That idea seemed to fit with more recent studies in genetics, which found that the majority of mammals have about one thousand different types of smell receptor.
sentences.zh: 这一观点似乎与较晚近的遗传学研究相吻合，那些研究发现，大多数哺乳动物拥有约一千种不同类型的嗅觉受体。

sentences.en: Most of these aren't present in humans, who only possess four hundred or so different types.
sentences.zh: 其中大多数在人类身上并不存在，人类只拥有四百来种不同类型。

sentences.en: (D)  Yet these findings may have been misleading.
sentences.zh: 然而，这些发现可能具有误导性。

sentences.en: Brain scans show that more of the human brain is devoted to smell processing than Broca's anatomical studies suggested.
sentences.zh: 脑部扫描显示，人脑中用于处理嗅觉的部分，比布罗卡的解剖学研究所暗示的要多。

sentences.en: And although we may have fewer types of receptor than other mammals, research has shown that the human nose and brain are unusually well connected, with each group of receptors linking to many more neural regions than is the case in other animals.
sentences.zh: 而且，尽管我们的受体类型也许比其他哺乳动物少，研究却表明人的鼻子和大脑之间的连接异常紧密，每一组受体所连接的神经区域，都比其他动物多得多。

sentences.en: That should give us a good ability to process incoming scents.
sentences.zh: 这应当赋予我们处理传入气味的良好能力。

sentences.en: (E) Once researchers began looking, they found the nose to be far more sensitive than its reputation suggested.
sentences.zh: 研究者一旦着手探究，便发现鼻子远比它的名声所暗示的要灵敏得多。

sentences.en: One study, for example, found that we can pick out a particular substance even when heavily diluted.
sentences.zh: 例如，一项研究发现，即便某种物质被高度稀释，我们也能把它分辨出来。

sentences.en: In fact, a person can smell just one drop of a chemical in a large swimming pool.
sentences.zh: 事实上，一个人能闻出一大泳池水中仅仅一滴化学物质的气味。

sentences.en: (F) What's more, with the latest findings, it is becoming clear that the brain's smelling centres are intimately linked to its system for controlling emotion, fear and memory.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，随着最新的研究发现，越来越清楚的是，大脑的嗅觉中枢与它控制情绪、恐惧和记忆的系统有着密切的联系。

sentences.en: That suggests a link between smell and the way we think.
sentences.zh: 这表明，气味与我们思考的方式之间存在某种关联。

sentences.en: One Dutch academic, for example, found that when the smell of orange, seawater or peppermint was pumped through a nightclub, those inside partied harder – they danced more, laughed more, and even thought the music was better than when there was no added scent.
sentences.zh: 例如，一位荷兰学者发现，当橙子、海水或薄荷的气味被注入一家夜店时，里面的人玩得更尽兴了——他们跳得更多、笑得更多，甚至觉得音乐都比没有额外气味时更动听。

sentences.en: (G) Other work has found that scent can influence our cognitive skills.
sentences.zh: 另有研究发现，气味能够影响我们的认知能力。

sentences.en: A study found that when men were subjected to a novel smell – either good or bad – during a task used to test decision-making skills, they performed significantly worse than normal.
sentences.zh: 一项研究发现，当男性在一项用于测试决策能力的任务中闻到一种新奇的气味——无论是好闻的还是难闻的——他们的表现都明显比平常差。

sentences.en: The researchers concluded that the scent stimulated brain areas connected with emotion, making their decisions emotional rather than rational.
sentences.zh: 研究者由此得出结论，这种气味刺激了与情绪相关的大脑区域，使他们的决策变得情绪化而非理性。

sentences.en: (H) The surprising thing about such studies is that up to 95% of subjects altered their behaviour, despite only 5% of them being aware of the introduced smells that they were facing.
sentences.zh: 这类研究令人惊讶之处在于，多达95%的受试者改变了自己的行为，尽管其中只有5%的人意识到自己正面对着被引入的气味。

sentences.en: The question, then, is why do we pay so little conscious attention to our noses unless we smell something really strong?
sentences.zh: 那么问题来了：除非闻到某种特别浓烈的气味，我们为什么对自己的鼻子如此缺乏有意识的关注呢？

sentences.en: (I) One vital factor is that our noses just aren't equipped to locate the source of an odour.
sentences.zh: 一个关键的因素在于，我们的鼻子根本不具备定位气味来源的能力。

sentences.en: This makes the sense of smell fundamentally different to vision or hearing, which are built to identify sights and sounds with precision.
sentences.zh: 这使嗅觉从根本上有别于视觉或听觉，后两者天生就能精确地辨识景象和声音。

sentences.en: Apparently, we become aware of something when the brain focuses on a single location, after which it picks out the details, like a familiar face, from the scene.
sentences.zh: 显然，当大脑聚焦于某个单一的位置时，我们才会意识到某样东西，随后大脑再从场景中把细节挑出来，比如一张熟悉的面孔。

sentences.en: With smell, though, the brain does not focus in the same way, and so is not able to make us aware of the details relating to one particular area.
sentences.zh: 然而对于气味，大脑并不会以同样的方式聚焦，因此无法让我们觉察到与某一特定区域相关的细节。

sentences.en: It's for this reason that we can only ever pick out around four smells from a complex mixture.
sentences.zh: 正是由于这个原因，我们从一种复杂的混合气味中至多只能分辨出大约四种气味。

sentences.en: (J) Nevertheless, we all have the capacity to train our sense of smell, but it needs to be worked at.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，我们每个人都有训练自己嗅觉的能力，但这需要下功夫。

sentences.en: Master perfumers, for instance, learn to recognise, name and imagine an extraordinary range of smells through years of practice.
sentences.zh: 例如，调香大师通过多年的练习，学会去辨认、命名并想象出种类繁多得惊人的气味。

sentences.en: This is accompanied by a significant reorganisation of the olfactory areas in the brain that helps them to process the scents more efficiently.
sentences.zh: 与此相伴的是大脑嗅觉区域的一次显著重组，这帮助他们更高效地处理各种气味。

sentences.en: (K) Smells are also especially good memory evokers, but it's actually a myth that odours trigger more complete memories than other stimuli.
sentences.zh: 气味还特别善于唤起记忆，但要说气味比其他刺激能触发更完整的记忆，其实是一种误解。

sentences.en: These memories are neither more accurate nor more detailed, but they are unique in that they are more emotional.
sentences.zh: 这些记忆既不更准确，也不更详尽，但它们的独特之处在于更富有情感。

sentences.en: This isn't surprising when you consider that both emotion and smell are processed by the same areas of the brain, and there is a strong link between emotion and memory.
sentences.zh: 一旦你想到情绪和气味都由大脑的同一区域处理，而情绪与记忆之间又有着紧密的联系，这就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: (L) That said, not all smell memories are equal.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，并非所有的气味记忆都一样。

sentences.en: The link between a memory and a smell is stronger if the smell is an unpleasant rather than a pleasant one, which makes sense from an evolutionary perspective.
sentences.zh: 如果气味是令人不快的而非令人愉悦的，那么记忆与气味之间的联系就会更强，这从进化的角度看是说得通的。

sentences.en: In addition, the very first time we associate a smell with an object, it evokes a much greater response in our brains than for any encounter with the smell or object in later life, laying down stronger foundations for the memory.
sentences.zh: 此外，我们第一次把某种气味与某个事物联系起来时，它在我们大脑中所唤起的反应，要远大于日后任何一次与该气味或事物的相遇，从而为记忆打下了更牢固的基础。

sentences.en: That doesn't happen with any other sense.
sentences.zh: 这种情况在其他任何感官上都不会发生。

sentences.en: Since most first encounters with a smell happen at a young age, this might explain why smells often carry us back to our childhood.
sentences.zh: 由于与某种气味的初次相遇大多发生在年幼时，这或许能解释为什么气味常常把我们带回童年。

sentences.en: (A) The new US headquarters of Izon are situated in Cambridge, Massachusetts, one of the most important global centres of scientific research and technology.
sentences.zh: 伊宗公司新的美国总部坐落在马萨诸塞州的剑桥市，那里是全球最重要的科学研究与技术中心之一。

sentences.en: Half the other offices in the building Izon shares have scientific names like Stemgent, or the word 'pharmaceutical' in the name.
sentences.zh: 在伊宗公司共用的这栋楼里，其他办公室有一半都取着像Stemgent这样带科学色彩的名字，或是名称中含有“pharmaceutical（制药）”一词。

sentences.en: In the past three years, Izon has expanded to 17 times its previous size.
sentences.zh: 在过去三年里，伊宗公司已扩张到原先规模的17倍。

sentences.en: It's done so selling only one product that it's been developing since 2004, the qNano.
sentences.zh: 它实现这一扩张，靠的只是销售一款自2004年以来一直在研发的产品——qNano。

sentences.en: This is an adjustable tool for the measurement and analysis of tiny particles in scientific research, which comes with a $27,000 price tag.
sentences.zh: 这是一种可调节的工具，用于在科学研究中测量和分析微小颗粒，售价标签为27000美元。

sentences.en: Izon's success results from the fact that the qNano machine provides precise measurements, while similar machines of the same price only offer averaging techniques.
sentences.zh: 伊宗公司的成功源于这样一个事实：qNano仪器能提供精确的测量，而同等价位的同类仪器只能提供求平均值的技术。

sentences.en: In effect, researchers using the qNano are able to gather information about very small things, and it has many possible applications from drug delivery analysis through to environmental research.
sentences.zh: 实际上，使用qNano的研究者能够收集关于极微小事物的信息，它有许多可能的应用，从药物递送分析直到环境研究。

sentences.en: (B) Kristoffer Bolen is Izon's US head of sales.
sentences.zh: 克里斯托弗·博伦是伊宗公司美国区的销售主管。

sentences.en: Alongside his full-time role with the company, he's just finished the fifth semester of six for his High-Tech Master of Business Administration at Northeastern University, which will be his second master's degree, alongside a Master of Science.
sentences.zh: 在公司担任全职工作的同时，他刚刚读完东北大学高科技工商管理硕士六个学期中的第五个学期，这将是他的第二个硕士学位，此外他还拥有一个理学硕士学位。

sentences.en: These soon-to-be twin master's degrees provide Bolen with the perfect combination of skills for his job, which depends on him being able to manage the sales process and also comprehend in depth a very complicated piece of technology.
sentences.zh: 这两个即将到手的硕士学位，为博伦的工作提供了堪称完美的技能组合，因为这份工作既要求他能够管理销售流程，又要求他能深入理解一项非常复杂的技术。

sentences.en: When a customer buys a qNano device, an Izon representative will fly anywhere in America to train them how to use the instrument.
sentences.zh: 当客户购买一台qNano设备时，伊宗公司的代表会飞往美国任何地方，培训他们如何使用这台仪器。

sentences.en: The representative then checks in with the client on an ongoing basis to be completely informed about how each qNano is being used, and then liaises with technicians back in New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 此后，这位代表会持续与客户保持联系，以便完全掌握每台qNano的使用情况，再与远在新西兰的技术人员沟通协调。

sentences.en: (C) The Izon story started 8 years ago in New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 伊宗公司的故事始于8年前的新西兰。

sentences.en: Hans van der Voorn was aimless, having sold his own company, and was looking for something more taxing to set his mind to.
sentences.zh: 汉斯·范德沃恩卖掉了自己的公司后一时无所事事，正想找一件更费心力的事来投入。

sentences.en: Van der Voorn was introduced to three scientists with an idea that involved simply a small plastic membrane with a tiny adjustable hole to measure a range of very small particles.
sentences.zh: 有人把范德沃恩引荐给三位科学家，他们有一个构想，无非是用一片带有可调节微孔的小塑料膜来测量一系列非常微小的颗粒。

sentences.en: Initially he put up an investment of $1.5 million to move the process forward to the development of a prototype, and this led to the founding of Izon and the production of the qNano.
sentences.zh: 起初，他投入了150万美元的资金，把这一进程推进到原型机的开发，由此催生了伊宗公司的成立和qNano的生产。

sentences.en: Van der Voorn believes that the worlds of science and business sometimes don't understand each other very well.
sentences.zh: 范德沃恩认为，科学界与商界有时彼此并不十分了解。

sentences.en: However, he thinks that engineering can be a bridge between the two, and his long experience in that field has been crucial to the company's success.
sentences.zh: 然而，他认为工程学可以成为两者之间的桥梁，而他在该领域的长期经验，对公司的成功至关重要。

sentences.en: He soon realised that Izon was going to need people on the ground overseas if it was going to grow, so the US office was opened.
sentences.zh: 他很快意识到，伊宗公司若想发展壮大，就需要在海外有当地的人手，于是美国办事处便开设了起来。

sentences.en: For now Izon trades in the US as a foreign company, so avoids the high level of compliance that comes with being an American-registered company.
sentences.zh: 目前，伊宗公司是以一家外国公司的身份在美国经营，因而避开了在美国注册的公司所要承担的高度合规要求。

sentences.en: But he sees that one day soon this will change, as Izon's current position disallows it from entering into partnerships locally.
sentences.zh: 但他预见，这种状况不久之后就会改变，因为伊宗公司目前的身份使它无法在当地结成合作伙伴关系。

sentences.en: (D) Marketing the qNano is complicated.
sentences.zh: 为qNano做营销是件复杂的事。

sentences.en: Izon needs scientists both to buy and advertise the product.
sentences.zh: 伊宗公司既需要科学家来购买产品，也需要他们来为产品做宣传。

sentences.en: The science world may seem like a big playing field, but it's actually a small group.
sentences.zh: 科学界看上去或许像一个广阔的天地，实际上却是一个不大的圈子。

sentences.en: As a result, the critical part of the company's marketing is articles that clients publish describing work they have performed with the qNano.
sentences.zh: 因此，该公司营销中最关键的部分，是客户发表的、描述他们用qNano所做工作的文章。

sentences.en: So for Izon the sale isn't enough in itself; it also has a stake in how customers are using the qNano.
sentences.zh: 所以对伊宗公司而言，单单卖出产品本身还不够；它还与客户如何使用qNano利害攸关。

sentences.en: That's where Yaniv Gaynor comes in.
sentences.zh: 这正是雅尼夫·盖纳发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: As development and training manager, he's involved throughout the sales process and manages most of the customer's post-sale experience.
sentences.zh: 作为开发与培训经理，他参与整个销售流程，并负责管理客户售后体验的大部分环节。

sentences.en: The sales process is new for Gaynor, who shifted cities and switched from a role as teacher at the University of Minnesota to his first private sector role with Izon.
sentences.zh: 销售流程对盖纳来说是个全新的领域，他更换了所在城市，从明尼苏达大学的教师一职转到了伊宗公司，这是他在私营部门的第一份工作。

sentences.en: 'It's tricky, it's challenging, and it's not in my comfort zone,' he concedes.
sentences.zh: “这很棘手，很有挑战性，也不在我的舒适区里，”他坦言。

sentences.en: But nine out of ten times, if there's an unhappy customer, he's able to turn their experience around.
sentences.zh: 但十有八九，如果遇到不满意的客户，他都能扭转他们的体验。

sentences.en: And there's another part to this, because sitting with customers as they learn about the qNano, Gaynor gets to see how they are using the product.
sentences.zh: 这其中还有另一层意义，因为在陪伴客户了解qNano的过程中，盖纳得以看到他们是如何使用这款产品的。

sentences.en: 'People ask very good questions, and these are great triggers for future development,' he says.
sentences.zh: “人们会提出非常好的问题，而这些都是推动未来开发的绝佳契机，”他说。

sentences.en: (E) 'Our business is selling research tools,' van der Voorn says.
sentences.zh: “我们的业务是销售研究工具，”范德沃恩说。

sentences.en: But he knows that the application range of this tool is wide.
sentences.zh: 但他知道，这种工具的应用范围很广。

sentences.en: For instance, Izon is engaged in a project with Harvard University, looking for a particular type of particle of blood that is a symptom of the medical condition of thrombosis.
sentences.zh: 例如，伊宗公司正与哈佛大学合作开展一个项目，寻找血液中一种特定类型的颗粒，这种颗粒是血栓这一病症的征兆。

sentences.en: If in the future they can identify this particle, they can design a simple test for it.
sentences.zh: 如果将来他们能够鉴别出这种颗粒，就能为它设计一种简便的检测方法。

sentences.en: This would make it easier for doctors to diagnose thrombosis.
sentences.zh: 这将使医生更容易诊断血栓。

sentences.en: Another planned development is eventually to shift the US base to more spacious offices on the other side of town.
sentences.zh: 另一项计划中的发展，是最终把美国基地迁到城另一头更为宽敞的办公场所。

sentences.en: With larger headquarters, the company will be able to bring clients into the Izon building for training with its product, rather than travelling to them, which will hopefully result in an even closer relationship between the company and its customers.
sentences.zh: 有了更大的总部，公司就能把客户请到伊宗大楼里来接受产品培训，而不必前往客户所在地，这有望使公司与客户之间的关系变得更加紧密。

sentences.en: (A) Images of deserts in the United States show dusty, barren landscapes, but the land may not always have been this way.
sentences.zh: 美国沙漠的照片显示出尘土飞扬、荒凉的景观，但这片土地或许并非一直如此。

sentences.en: Ever since settlers moved west across the US, there has been dust, clouds of it, everywhere.
sentences.zh: 自从开拓者向西穿越美国以来，到处都是尘土，那是一团团的尘云。

sentences.en: It was part of the landscape, or so it seemed to them.
sentences.zh: 在他们看来，那是这片地貌的一部分。

sentences.en: But there were no records of the landscape of the West until the settlers arrived.
sentences.zh: 但是，在拓荒者到来之前，没有人对西部的地貌留下记录。

sentences.en: Now, evidence is starting to emerge which suggests that before the settlers, there was very little dust.
sentences.zh: 如今，正在出现的证据表明：在拓荒者到来之前，这里的尘土其实很少。

sentences.en: The evidence comes from the San Juan Mountains of southwest Colorado, downwind of Arizona and New Mexico.
sentences.zh: 证据来自科罗拉多州西南部的圣胡安山脉，那里位于亚利桑那州和新墨西哥州的下风向。

sentences.en: There, Jason Neff, a geochemist from the University of Colorado, has been analyzing sediments, the sand, stones and mud, laid down over the past 5,000 years.
sentences.zh: 在那里，科罗拉多大学的地球化学家杰森·内夫（Jason Neff）一直在分析过去 5000 年间沉积下来的沙、石和泥等沉积物。

sentences.en: Atmospheric dust was minimal throughout those five millennia until the mid-19th century, he says, but then, 'from about 1860 to 1900, dust deposition rates shot up.'
sentences.zh: 他说，在那 5000 年间，大气中的尘土一直很少，直到 19 世纪中叶——但接下来，“从大约 1860 年到 1900 年，尘土沉积速率猛增”。

sentences.en: (B) This is surprising because usually dry means dusty, and the American West has almost always been dry, often drier than today.
sentences.zh: 这令人惊讶，因为通常情况下，干燥意味着尘土飞扬，而美国西部几乎一直很干燥，往往比今天还要干燥。

sentences.en: There was a near-permanent drought between 900 and 1300 which was so intense that it destroyed a series of Native American civilizations, including the Anasazi, whose cliff homes are now US national treasures.
sentences.zh: 在公元 900 年至 1300 年间曾出现一场几乎是持续性的旱灾，干旱之严重摧毁了一系列美洲原住民文明，包括阿纳萨齐人——他们的悬崖民居如今已是美国的国宝。

sentences.en: Yet the evidence from the San Juan lakes is that it was not dusty.
sentences.zh: 然而圣胡安湖泊的证据却表明，那个时期并不多尘。

sentences.en: Even as their civilization was collapsing, the Anasazi seem to have protected their soils from erosion.
sentences.zh: 即便他们的文明正在崩溃，阿纳萨齐人似乎也保护了他们的土壤免遭侵蚀。

sentences.en: (C) This was not the case with the European settlers once they brought their cows.
sentences.zh: 欧洲拓荒者带来牛之后，情况就不同了。

sentences.en: The landscape the cattle were introduced to was remarkably ill-equipped to cope with grazing animals, says Neff.
sentences.zh: 内夫说，引入牛群所到达的这片地貌，对放牧动物的应对能力极差。

sentences.en: 'Unlike most other parts of the US, there were few grazers in the American Southwest until the Europeans came.
sentences.zh: “与美国大多数其他地区不同，在欧洲人到来之前，美国西南部的食草动物很少。

sentences.en: No bison and few antelope or deer.'
sentences.zh: 没有美洲野牛，羚羊和鹿也很少。”

sentences.en: (D) In the Great Plains to the east and north, bison roamed in vast herds.
sentences.zh: 在东边和北边的大平原上，美洲野牛成群结队地漫游。

sentences.en: Their regular grazing had created tough grass, while the herds manured the soil.
sentences.zh: 它们规律的啃食造就了坚韧的草本，野牛群的粪便也为土壤施肥。

sentences.en: In the Southwest, the land had few defenses against a sudden invasion of millions of livestock, whose teeth stripped the grass and whose hooves punctured the hard crust of desert soils that protected them from the wind.
sentences.zh: 而在美国西南部，这片土地几乎没有什么防御能力，就承受了数百万头牲畜突如其来的入侵：它们的牙齿啃光了草，蹄子戳穿了沙漠土壤上那层硬壳——而正是这层硬壳保护土壤不被风吹走。

sentences.en: The invasion was sudden, funded by a bubble of speculative investment, much of it from Britain.
sentences.zh: 这场入侵来得很突然，背后是投机性投资形成的泡沫资金，其中很大一部分来自英国。

sentences.en: The money went into railroads and herds of cattle and sheep that rode the rails to the wide open pastures.
sentences.zh: 这些资金流向了铁路以及牛羊群——它们坐着铁路一路驶向辽阔开放的牧场。

sentences.en: By 1900, when sedimentation rates peaked, there were 20 million cattle and 25 million sheep in the West.
sentences.zh: 到 1900 年沉积速率达到峰值时，美国西部已经有 2000 万头牛和 2500 万头羊。

sentences.en: (E) One of the biggest ranches was owned by the Aztec Land and Cattle Company, which owned a million acres of land by 1884.
sentences.zh: 最大的牧场之一归阿兹特克土地与畜牧公司（Aztec Land and Cattle Company）所有，到 1884 年时该公司已拥有 100 万英亩的土地。

sentences.en: Each acre had cost the company a mere 50 cents, and like many other speculators, it was only interested in quick profits and had little incentive to protect the soils from overgrazing.
sentences.zh: 公司为每英亩仅花费 50 美分；与许多其他投机者一样，它只关心快速获利，对保护土壤不被过度放牧几乎没有动力。

sentences.en: By the time Aztec sold the ranch in 1901, it was barren, with cattle carcasses scattered across the exhausted land.
sentences.zh: 等到阿兹特克公司在 1901 年把这家牧场卖出时，土地已变得寸草不生，牛的尸骸散落在这片被透支的土地上。

sentences.en: Such was the damage to the grasslands that even now few of the pastures have recovered.
sentences.zh: 对草地的破坏如此严重，以至于即使到今天，这些牧场也少有恢复过来。

sentences.en: The parched and exposed soil simply blew away.
sentences.zh: 干裂裸露的土壤就这样被风吹散了。

sentences.en: The 1862 Homestead Act was passed in order to encourage the populating of the West.
sentences.zh: 1862 年的《宅地法》是为了鼓励向西部移民而通过的。

sentences.en: Any family willing to make the journey was entitled to claim 160 acres and farm it.
sentences.zh: 任何愿意踏上这段旅程的家庭都有权获得 160 英亩土地进行耕种。

sentences.en: Yet by the time people moved west in large numbers, the cattle companies had taken most of the land and surrounded it with barbed wire.
sentences.zh: 然而，等到人们开始大规模西迁时，牧牛公司已经占据了大部分土地，并用带刺铁丝网把它们圈了起来。

sentences.en: The water sources were therefore cut off, and were aggressively guarded.
sentences.zh: 水源因此被切断，并由人严密守护。

sentences.en: It was only in the 1930s, with the passage of the Taylor Grazing Act, that federal authorities finally sought to limit cattle herds.
sentences.zh: 直到 1930 年代《泰勒放牧法》通过后，联邦当局才终于试图对牛群规模加以限制。

sentences.en: (F) Soil scientists have known for a while about the importance of the hard crust that forms on arid soils.
sentences.zh: 土壤科学家很久以前就知道在干旱土壤上形成的坚硬硬壳的重要性。

sentences.en: 'These crusts can survive winds of up to a hundred miles an hour, but cattle hooves break the crust,' says Jayne Belnap, a soil ecologist at the US Geological Survey, Utah.
sentences.zh: “这些硬壳可以承受时速高达 100 英里的风，但牛蹄会把硬壳踩碎。”位于犹他州的美国地质调查局土壤生态学家杰恩·贝尔纳普（Jayne Belnap）说。

sentences.en: The scale of the dust clouds created by the livestock invasion has until now been largely unknown.
sentences.zh: 由牲畜入侵造成的尘云规模，迄今为止在很大程度上还未为人所知。

sentences.en: When Neff first discovered dust in Colorado lake sediments laid down in the 19th century, he was initially unsure where it came from.
sentences.zh: 当内夫第一次在 19 世纪沉积的科罗拉多湖底沉积物中发现尘土时，他起初并不确定它们来自何处。

sentences.en: Maybe it had crossed the Pacific from China's Gobi Desert.
sentences.zh: 也许它们越过太平洋来自中国的戈壁沙漠。

sentences.en: (G) But after investigating the size and chemical composition of the dust, Neff was clear that it mostly came from the American Southwest, mainly Arizona and New Mexico.
sentences.zh: 但在分析了这些尘土的颗粒大小和化学成分之后，内夫清楚地认定，它们大多来自美国西南部，主要来自亚利桑那州和新墨西哥州。

sentences.en: Now, with the soil crusts gone, dust clouds still head north and are having significant ecological effects in the Colorado mountains.
sentences.zh: 如今，由于土壤硬壳已经消失，尘云仍向北飘移，对科罗拉多山区产生了重大的生态影响。

sentences.en: They carry nutrients with them into areas which previously evolved and survived without them.
sentences.zh: 它们将养分带入此前在没有这些养分的情况下演化并生存的地区。

sentences.en: But perhaps the most dramatic impact of the dust has been on snowfields in the Rocky Mountain Range.
sentences.zh: 但尘土最戏剧性的影响也许是对落基山脉中雪原产生的影响。

sentences.en: Even a thin sprinkling of dark material means snow absorbs more solar radiation, meaning that snowmelt occurs far more rapidly during springtime.
sentences.zh: 哪怕只洒上一层薄薄的深色物质，雪就会吸收更多的太阳辐射，意味着春季雪融的速度会大大加快。

sentences.en: The impact on the ski tourism industry is obvious.
sentences.zh: 对滑雪旅游业的影响是显而易见的。

sentences.en: (H) The loss of snow and the shrinking of glaciers across the American West in the past century have been dramatic.
sentences.zh: 过去一个世纪，美国西部雪量减少和冰川萎缩的程度十分惊人。

sentences.en: Glacier National Park in Montana, for example, has lost three quarters of its snow cover since 1910.
sentences.zh: 例如，蒙大拿州的冰川国家公园（Glacier National Park）自 1910 年以来已经失去了四分之三的雪盖。

sentences.en: All this is frequently attributed to global warming.
sentences.zh: 这一切常被归因于全球变暖。

sentences.en: While this almost certainly plays a role, Neff's findings suggest that dust may also contribute.
sentences.zh: 虽然全球变暖几乎肯定也起着作用，但内夫的发现表明，尘土可能也是一个促因。

records.title: A new look for Talbot Park
records.titleZh: 塔尔博特公园焕然一新

sentences.en: A  The new Talbot Park is immediately eye-catching because the buildings look quite different to other state-housing projects in Auckland.
sentences.zh: 新Talbot Park一眼就引人注目，因为这些建筑看起来和奥克兰其他公屋项目很不一样。

sentences.en: ‘There is no reason why state housing should look cheap in my view,’ says architect Neil Cotton, one of the design team.
sentences.zh: “在我看来，公屋没有理由看起来廉价，”设计团队成员之一、建筑师Neil Cotton说。

sentences.en: ‘In fact, I was anticipating a backlash by those who objected to the quality of what is provided with government money.’
sentences.zh: “事实上，我曾预料会遭到那些反对用政府的钱所提供之物的质量的人的反弹。”

sentences.en: The tidy brick and wood apartments and townhouses would not look out of place in some of the city’s most affluent suburbs, and this is a central theme of the Talbot Park philosophy.
sentences.zh: 这些整洁的砖木公寓和联排别墅，放在这座城市一些最富裕的郊区也不会显得格格不入，而这正是Talbot Park理念的一个核心主题。

sentences.en: B  Talbot Park is a triangle of government-owned land, which in the early 1960s was developed for state housing built around a linear garden that ran through the middle.
sentences.zh: Talbot Park是一块政府所有的三角形土地，20世纪60年代初被开发为公屋，围绕一座贯穿中间的带状花园而建。

sentences.en: Initially, there was a strong sense of neighbourliness.
sentences.zh: 最初，那里有很强的邻里感。

sentences.en: Former residents recall how the garden played a big part in their childhoods — a place where kids came together to play softball, cricket and bullrush.
sentences.zh: 昔日的居民回忆起那座花园在他们童年中扮演了多大的角色——一个孩子们聚在一起打垒球、板球和玩抓人游戏的地方。

sentences.en: ‘We had respect for our neighbours and addressed them by title — Mr and Mrs so-and-so,’ recalls Georgie Thompson, who grew up there in the 1960s.
sentences.zh: “我们尊重邻居，用尊称称呼他们——某某先生和某某夫人，”20世纪60年代在那里长大的Georgie Thompson回忆道。

sentences.en: C  Exactly what went wrong with Talbot Park is unclear.
sentences.zh: Talbot Park究竟出了什么问题尚不清楚。

sentences.en: The community began to change in the late 1970s as more immigrants moved in.
sentences.zh: 这个社区在20世纪70年代末开始变化，因为更多移民迁入。

sentences.en: The new arrivals didn’t always integrate with the community and a ‘them and us’ mentality developed.
sentences.zh: 新来者并不总能融入社区，一种“他们与我们”的心态滋生出来。

sentences.en: In the process, standards dropped and the neighbourhood began to look shabbier.
sentences.zh: 在这个过程中，标准下降，街区开始显得更破败。

sentences.en: The buildings themselves were also deteriorating and becoming run-down, petty crime was on the rise and the garden was considered unsafe.
sentences.zh: 建筑本身也在恶化、变得破旧，轻微犯罪在上升，那座花园被认为不安全。

sentences.en: In 2002, Housing New Zealand decided the properties needed upgrading.
sentences.zh: 2002年，新西兰住房局决定这些房产需要升级改造。

sentences.en: The question was, how to avoid repeating the mistakes of the past?
sentences.zh: 问题是，如何避免重蹈过去的覆辙？

sentences.en: D  One controversial aspect of the upgrade is that the new development has actually made the density of housing in Talbot Park greater, putting 52 more homes on the same site.
sentences.zh: 这次升级改造一个有争议的方面是，新开发实际上让Talbot Park的住房密度更大了，在同一块地上多放了52套住宅。

sentences.en: Doing this required a fresh approach that can be summed up as ‘mix and match’.
sentences.zh: 做到这一点需要一种全新的思路，可以概括为“混搭”。

sentences.en: The first priority was to mix up the housing by employing a variety of plans by different architects: some of the accommodation is free-standing houses, some semi-detached, some low-level, multi- apartment blocks.
sentences.zh: 首要任务是通过采用不同建筑师的多种方案来把住房混合起来，有些住宅是独栋房屋，有些是半独立的，有些是低层、多套公寓的楼房。

sentences.en: By doing this, the development avoids the uniform appearance of so many state-housing projects, which residents complain denies them any sense of individual identity.
sentences.zh: 这样做，该开发避免了许多公屋项目那种千篇一律的外观，居民抱怨那种外观剥夺了他们任何个体身份感。

sentences.en: The next goal was to prevent overspending by using efficient designs to maximise the sense of space from minimum room sizes.
sentences.zh: 下一个目标是通过用高效的设计、从最小的房间尺寸中最大化空间感，来防止超支。

sentences.en: There was also a no-frills, industrial approach to kitchens, bathrooms and flooring, to optimise durability and ensure the project did not go over budget.
sentences.zh: 对厨房、浴室和地面也采取了一种朴实、工业化的做法，以优化耐用性并确保项目不超预算。

sentences.en: Architecturally, the buildings are relatively conservative: fairly plain houses standing in a small garden.
sentences.zh: 在建筑上，这些楼房相对保守，是立在小花园里相当朴素的房子。

sentences.en: There’s a slight reflection of the traditional Pacific beach house (a fale) but it’s not over-played.
sentences.zh: 略微反映了传统的太平洋海滨屋（一种fale），但没有过度发挥。

sentences.en: ‘It seems to us that low-cost housing is about getting as much amenity as you can for the money,’ says architect Michael Thompson.
sentences.zh: “在我们看来，低成本住房就是用这笔钱尽可能多地换取便利设施，”建筑师Michael Thompson说。

sentences.en: Another key aspect of the ‘mix and match’ approach is openness: one that not only lets residents see what is going on but also lets them know they are seen.
sentences.zh: “混搭”做法的另一个关键方面是开放，一种既让居民看到正在发生什么、也让他们知道自己被看到的开放。

sentences.en: The plan ensures there are no cul-de-sacs or properties hidden from view, that the gardens are not enclosed by trees and that most boundary fences are see- through — a community contained but without walls.
sentences.zh: 这个方案确保没有死胡同或隐于视线之外的房产，确保花园不被树木围闭，并确保大多数边界围栏是透视的——一个有边界却没有围墙的社区。

sentences.en: E  The population today is cosmopolitan: 50% Pacific Islanders, 20% Māori, 15% Asian, 10% New Zealand European and the rest composed of immigrants from Russia, Ukraine and Iran.
sentences.zh: 如今的人口很国际化，50%是太平洋岛民、20%是毛利人、15%是亚裔、10%是新西兰欧裔，其余由来自俄罗斯、乌克兰和伊朗的移民构成。

sentences.en: ‘It was important that the buildings were sufficiently flexible to cater for the needs of people from a wide variety of cultural backgrounds,’ explains designer James Lundy.
sentences.zh: “重要的是这些建筑要足够灵活，以满足来自各种各样文化背景的人的需求，”设计师James Lundy解释道。

sentences.en: F  Despite the quality of the buildings, however, there should be no doubt that Talbot Park and its surrounding suburb of Tāmaki are low socio-economic areas.
sentences.zh: 然而，尽管建筑质量很高，毋庸置疑的是，Talbot Park及其周边的Tāmaki郊区是社会经济地位较低的地区。

sentences.en: Of the 5,000 houses there, 55% are state houses, 28% privately owned (compared to about 65% nationally) and 17% private rental.
sentences.zh: 那里的5000套房子中，55%是公屋，28%是私人拥有（相比之下全国约为65%），17%是私人租赁。

sentences.en: The area has a high density of households with incomes in the $5,000 to $15,000 range and very few with an income over $70,000.
sentences.zh: 这一地区有很高密度的家庭收入在5000到15000美元之间，而收入超过70000美元的极少。

sentences.en: That’s in sharp contrast to the more affluent suburbs in Auckland.
sentences.zh: 那与奥克兰更富裕的郊区形成鲜明对比。

sentences.en: G  Another important part of the new development is what Housing New Zealand calls ‘intensive tenancy management’.
sentences.zh: 新开发另一个重要的部分是新西兰住房局所谓的“集约化租户管理”。

sentences.en: Opponents of the project call it social control.
sentences.zh: 该项目的反对者称它为社会控制。

sentences.en: ‘The focus is on frequent inspections and setting clear guidelines and boundaries regarding the sort of behaviour we expect from tenants,’ says Graham Bodman, Housing New Zealand’s regional manager.
sentences.zh: “重点是频繁的检查，以及就我们对租户行为的期望设定清晰的准则和界线，”新西兰住房局区域经理Graham Bodman说。

sentences.en: The result is a code of sometimes strict rules: no loud parties after 10 pm; no washing hung over balcony rails; and a requirement to mow lawns and keep the property tidy.
sentences.zh: 结果是一套有时很严格的规则，晚上10点后不许大声开派对；不许在阳台栏杆上晾衣服；并要求修剪草坪、保持房产整洁。

sentences.en: The Tenancy Manager walks the site every day, knows everyone by name and deals with problems quickly.
sentences.zh: 租户经理每天巡视场地，叫得出每个人的名字，并迅速处理问题。

sentences.en: ‘It’s all based on the intensification,’ says project manager Stuart Bracey.
sentences.zh: “这一切都基于集约化，”项目经理Stuart Bracey说。

sentences.en: ‘We acknowledge that if you are going to ask people to live in these quite tightly-packed communities, you have to actually help them to get to know each other by organising morning teas and street barbecues.’
sentences.zh: “我们承认，如果你要请人住在这些相当紧凑的社区里，你就得通过组织早茶和街头烧烤，真正帮他们彼此认识。”

sentences.en: So far it seems to be working and many involved in the project believe Talbot Park represents the way forward for state housing.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止它似乎奏效了，参与该项目的许多人相信Talbot Park代表了公屋前进的方向。
