sentences.en: (A) How busy is too busy?
sentences.zh: 多忙才算太忙？

sentences.en: For some it means sometimes having to have a short lunch; for others it may mean missing lunch altogether.
sentences.zh: 对一些人来说，它意味着有时不得不匆匆吃顿午饭；对另一些人来说，它可能意味着完全错过午饭。

sentences.en: For a few, it is not being able to take a day off once a month.
sentences.zh: 对少数人来说，它是一个月连一天假都休不了。

sentences.en: Then there is a group of people for whom working every evening and weekend is normal, and feeling stressed is taken for granted.
sentences.zh: 然后有这样一群人，对他们来说每个晚上和周末都工作是常态，感到压力被视为理所当然。

sentences.en: For most senior executives, workloads swing between extremely busy and frenzied.
sentences.zh: 对大多数高级管理人员来说，工作量在极其繁忙和忙到发狂之间摆动。

sentences.en: Neil Plumridge, vice-president of a management consultancy company, says that his weeks vary from a ‘manageable’ 45 hours to 80 hours, but average 60 hours.
sentences.zh: 一家管理咨询公司的副总裁Neil Plumridge说，他的周工作时间在“可控的”45小时到80小时之间变化，但平均为60小时。

sentences.en: (B) Three signs warn Plumridge about his workload: sleep, scheduling and family.
sentences.zh: 三个迹象警示Plumridge注意他的工作量，睡眠、日程安排和家庭。

sentences.en: He knows he is doing too much when he gets less than six hours’ sleep for three consecutive nights, when he is constantly having to reschedule appointments, and when he misses a family birthday or anniversary.
sentences.zh: 当他连续三晚睡眠不足六小时、不得不不断重新安排约会、错过家人的生日或纪念日时，他就知道自己做得太多了。

sentences.en: ‘Then,’ he says, ‘I know things are out of control.’
sentences.zh: “那时，”他说，“我就知道事情失控了。”

sentences.en: Plumridge states that stress is often caused by his having unrealistic expectations of himself.
sentences.zh: Plumridge表示，压力常常是由他对自己有不切实际的期望造成的。

sentences.en: ‘I’ll promise a client that I’ll do something tomorrow, and then I’ll promise another client that I’ll do the same thing, when I know it’s not going to happen.
sentences.zh: “我会答应一个客户明天做某件事，然后又答应另一个客户做同样的事，而我明知那不会实现。

sentences.en: I could have said: “Why don’t I give that to you in 48 hours?”
sentences.zh: 我本可以说，‘我何不在48小时内给你？’

sentences.en: The client wouldn’t care.’
sentences.zh: 客户不会在意。”

sentences.en: (C) Over-committing is something people experience as an individual problem.
sentences.zh: 过度承诺是人们作为个人问题来体验的东西。

sentences.en: However, new research indicates that people may be designed to over-commit.
sentences.zh: 然而，新的研究表明，人也许天生就会过度承诺。

sentences.en: A study in the Journal of Experimental Psychology shows that people always believe that they will be less busy in the future.
sentences.zh: 《Journal of Experimental Psychology》上的一项研究表明，人们总相信自己将来会不那么忙。

sentences.en: This is a misapprehension according to the authors of the report, Gal Zauberman of the University of North Carolina and John Lynch of Duke University.
sentences.zh: 据该报告的作者、北卡罗来纳大学的Gal Zauberman和杜克大学的John Lynch说，这是一种误解。

sentences.en: ‘On average, an individual will be just as busy two weeks or a month from now as he or she is today.
sentences.zh: “平均而言，一个人两周后或一个月后会和今天一样忙。

sentences.en: But that is not how it appears in everyday life,’ they say.
sentences.zh: 但在日常生活中看起来并非如此，”他们说。

sentences.en: ‘People make commitments long in advance that they would never make if the same commitments required immediate action.
sentences.zh: “人们提前很久作出承诺，而如果同样的承诺需要立即行动，他们绝不会作出。

sentences.en: They discount future time investments relatively steeply.’
sentences.zh: 他们对未来的时间投入打了相当大的折扣。”

sentences.en: (D) Being ‘too busy’ is highly subjective, but for any individual there are some concrete signs of stress: disturbed sleep and declining mental and physical health are the most common examples.
sentences.zh: “太忙”是高度主观的，但对任何个人来说，都有一些压力的具体迹象，睡眠受扰以及身心健康下降是最常见的例子。

sentences.en: Figures for National Workers’ Compensation (insurance against injury caused by work) show that stress causes the most loss of time of any workplace injury: employees suffering stress are absent from work for an average of 16.6 weeks.
sentences.zh: 国家工伤赔偿（针对工作所致伤害的保险）的数据显示，压力造成的时间损失比任何工作场所伤害都多，遭受压力的员工平均缺勤16.6周。

sentences.en: The effects of stress are also expensive.
sentences.zh: 压力的影响也很昂贵。

sentences.en: The Australian Government insurer reports that, in 2003–2004, claims for stress-related psychological injury accounted for 7% of insurance claims, but almost 27% of the amount paid out in claim payments.
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚政府保险机构报告说，在2003到2004年，与压力相关的心理伤害索赔占保险索赔的7%，却占赔付总额的近27%。

sentences.en: (E) Experts say the key to dealing with stress is not to focus on relief — a game of golf or a massage — but to reassess workloads.
sentences.zh: 专家说，应对压力的关键不是聚焦于缓解——打一场高尔夫或做一次按摩——而是重新评估工作量。

sentences.en: Neil Plumridge says he makes it a priority to work out what has to change: that might mean allocating extra staff to a job, allowing more time, or changing expectations.
sentences.zh: Neil Plumridge说，他把弄清什么必须改变作为优先事项，那可能意味着给一项工作多分配人手、留出更多时间，或改变期望。

sentences.en: He also relies on the advice of colleagues, saying that his peers coach each other on business problems: ‘Just a fresh pair of eyes over an issue can help,’ he states.
sentences.zh: 他还依靠同事的建议，说他的同侪在业务问题上互相指点，“仅仅是对一个问题换一双新的眼睛看就能有帮助，”他表示。

sentences.en: (F) Executive stress is not confined to big organisations.
sentences.zh: 高管的压力并不局限于大机构。

sentences.en: Vanessa Stoykov has been running her own advertising agency and public relations business for seven years.
sentences.zh: Vanessa Stoykov经营自己的广告公司和公关业务已有七年。

sentences.en: Her company has grown so fast that it appeared on the Business Review Weekly ‘Fast 100’ list of fastest- growing small enterprises in 2004, just after Stoykov had her first child.
sentences.zh: 她的公司增长得如此之快，以至于在2004年登上了《Business Review Weekly》增长最快小企业的“百强”榜单，那正好在Stoykov生第一个孩子之后。

sentences.en: In 2005, revenue was projected to double to $2.4 million.
sentences.zh: 2005年，营收预计将翻倍到240万美元。

sentences.en: She had just had her second child.
sentences.zh: 她刚生了第二个孩子。

sentences.en: With a fast- growing business and two small children, Stoykov says she has mastered the art of caring for children, typing, and talking on the phone at the same time.
sentences.zh: 带着一项快速增长的业务和两个小孩，Stoykov说她已经掌握了同时照看孩子、打字和打电话的本领。

sentences.en: But, unlike many others, she appears to thrive on the mental stimulation of running her own business, despite the stress.
sentences.zh: 但与许多其他人不同，尽管有压力，她似乎在经营自己的业务这种脑力刺激中如鱼得水。

sentences.en: (G) Jan Elsner, a psychologist who specialises in executive coaching, says that doing well on a demanding workload is typical of senior executives.
sentences.zh: 专攻高管辅导的心理学家Jan Elsner说，在繁重的工作量上表现出色是高级管理人员的典型特征。

sentences.en: Some people work best with high- adrenaline periods followed by quieter times, while others thrive under sustained pressure.
sentences.zh: 有些人在高肾上腺素时期之后跟着较安静的时期会工作得最好，而另一些人在持续的压力下如鱼得水。

sentences.en: Elsner’s practice is based on a movement known as positive psychology, a school of thought that argues that positive experiences — feeling engaged and challenged, for example — do not balance out negative experiences such as stress; instead they help people increase their resilience over time.
sentences.zh: Elsner的实践基于一种叫积极心理学的运动，这一学派主张，积极的体验——比如感到投入和受到挑战——并不会抵消压力等消极体验；相反，它们会帮助人们随时间增强复原力。

sentences.en: Elsner says that many of the senior business people she coaches are increasingly relying more on regulating stress through methods such as meditation.
sentences.zh: Elsner说，她辅导的许多高级商界人士越来越多地依靠冥想等方法来调节压力。

sentences.en: She points to research showing that meditation can alter the biochemistry of the brain and the way that brains and bodies react to stress.
sentences.zh: 她指出有研究表明，冥想能改变大脑的生化机制以及大脑和身体对压力的反应方式。

sentences.en: (H) Some experts believe there is too much emphasis on treating job stress as an individual problem.
sentences.zh: 有些专家认为，把工作压力当作个人问题来处理被过分强调了。

sentences.en: Tony LaMontagne, of the University of Melbourne, says that while personality traits do have some effect on stress, it is systemic stressors — qualities of job roles and organisations themselves — that have a far greater effect.
sentences.zh: 墨尔本大学的Tony LaMontagne说，虽然人格特质确实对压力有一定影响，但产生远为更大影响的是系统性的压力源——工作角色和组织本身的特质。

sentences.en: His recent research shows that the major predictor of stress is the level of job control a person has.
sentences.zh: 他最近的研究表明，压力的主要预测因素是一个人所拥有的工作控制权水平。

sentences.en: The best type of job combines challenging work with high autonomy.
sentences.zh: 最好的那类工作把有挑战性的工作与高度自主结合起来。

sentences.en: The worst jobs combine challenging work and low control.
sentences.zh: 最糟的工作把有挑战性的工作和低控制权结合起来。

sentences.en: People with demanding jobs but little autonomy have up to four times the probability of depression and more than double the risk of heart attack.
sentences.zh: 工作要求高但自主权少的人，患抑郁症的概率高达四倍，心脏病发作的风险高出两倍以上。

records.title: The Constant Evolution of the Humble Tomato

sentences.en: (A) Famous for their taste, color, and organic appearance, heirloom tomatoes are favorites of gardeners and advocates of locally grown foods.
sentences.zh: 传家宝番茄以其味道、色泽和天然的外观而闻名，是园艺爱好者和本地食材倡导者的最爱。

sentences.en: The tomato enthusiast might conclude that, given the immense varieties, heirlooms must have a more diverse and superior set of genes than the tomatoes available in grocery stores, those ordinary hybrid varieties such as cherry and plum.
sentences.zh: 番茄爱好者也许会得出结论：鉴于其品种繁多，传家宝番茄想必拥有比杂货店里那些普通杂交品种（如樱桃番茄和李形番茄）更为多样、更为优良的基因。

sentences.en: However, their seeming diversity is only skin- deep: heirlooms are actually feeble and inbred—the defective product of breeding experiments that began hundreds of years ago, and exploded thanks to enthusiastic backyard gardeners.
sentences.zh: 然而，它们看似的多样性只是表皮上的：传家宝番茄实际上孱弱而近亲繁殖——它们是几百年前开始、又因热心的后院园丁而激增的育种试验的有缺陷的产物。

sentences.en: “The irony of all this,” says Steven Tanksley, a geneticist at Cornell University, “is that all that diversity of heirlooms can be accounted for by a handful of genes.
sentences.zh: “这一切的讽刺之处，”康奈尔大学的遗传学家史蒂文·坦克斯利说，“在于传家宝番茄的全部多样性，都可以由屈指可数的几个基因来解释。

sentences.en: There are probably no more than 10 mutant genes that create the diversity of heirlooms you see.”
sentences.zh: 造就你所见到的那种传家宝番茄多样性的突变基因，很可能不超过10个。”

sentences.en: But rather than simply proving that the myth about the heirlooms’ diversity is wrong, Tanksley’s deconstruction of the tomato genome, along with work by others, is showing how a small berry-like fruit from the Andes became one of the world’s top crops.
sentences.zh: 但坦克斯利对番茄基因组的解构，连同其他人的研究，所做的不仅仅是证明关于传家宝番茄多样性的那个说法是错误的，它还在揭示一种源自安第斯山、形似浆果的小果子是如何成为世界顶级作物之一的。

sentences.en: (B) The cultivated tomato is a member of the nightshade family that includes New World crops such as the potato, which spread around the globe after Christopher Columbus brought them back to Spain in the 15th century.
sentences.zh: 栽培番茄是茄科的一员，茄科包括马铃薯等新大陆作物，15世纪克里斯托弗·哥伦布把它们带回西班牙之后，它们便传遍了全球。

sentences.en: But whereas scientists have uncovered a wealth of archaeological evidence on early farming practices in the New World, the record is blank when it comes to the tomato.
sentences.zh: 但是，尽管科学家已发掘出关于新大陆早期农耕方式的大量考古证据，在番茄这件事上记录却是一片空白。

sentences.en: The modern tomato seems to have its origins in the Andes in South America and may have been domesticated in Veracruz, Mexico.
sentences.zh: 现代番茄的起源似乎在南美洲的安第斯山，并可能是在墨西哥的韦拉克鲁斯被驯化的。

sentences.en: Primitive varieties still grow throughout the Americas.
sentences.zh: 原始的品种至今仍遍布美洲各地。

sentences.en: All told, botanists call as many as 13 species “tomatoes” and consider an additional four to be closely related.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，植物学家把多达13个物种称为“番茄”，并认为另有四个物种与之关系密切。

sentences.en: (C) One might assume that one of these known wild species became today’s cultivated crop, but that’s not the case: the Mother Tomato has never been found.
sentences.zh: 人们也许会以为，这些已知的野生物种之一变成了今天的栽培作物，但事实并非如此：番茄之母从未被找到过。

sentences.en: The closest relative is the currant tomato, which, based on genetic comparisons, split from today’s tomato some 1.4 million years ago.
sentences.zh: 与之最接近的近亲是醋栗番茄，根据基因比较，它在约140万年前与今天的番茄分道扬镳。

sentences.en: So researchers like Tanksley have to work backward, crossing tomato varieties and species in order to understand how various genes influence shape and size.
sentences.zh: 因此，像坦克斯利这样的研究者只能逆向推演，把番茄的不同品种和物种杂交，以理解各种基因是如何影响形状和大小的。

sentences.en: Once isolated, Tanksley later inserts those genes into other tomato varieties to make his case with a dramatic transformation.
sentences.zh: 一旦把那些基因分离出来，坦克斯利随后会把它们插入其他番茄品种，以一种戏剧性的转变来证明自己的观点。

sentences.en: (D) Tanksley concludes from his analyses that in their effort to make bigger, tastier, and faster-growing fruit, our ancestors ultimately exploited just 30 mutations out of the tomato’s 35,000 genes.
sentences.zh: 坦克斯利从他的分析中得出结论：我们的祖先在努力培育更大、更可口、长得更快的果实的过程中，最终只利用了番茄35000个基因中的30个突变。

sentences.en: Most of these genes have only small effects on tomato size and shape, but recently Tanksley and his colleagues reported that they found a gene that increases fruit size by 50 percent.
sentences.zh: 这些基因中的大多数对番茄的大小和形状只有微小的影响，但最近坦克斯利和他的同事报告说，他们发现了一个能使果实增大50%的基因。

sentences.en: It was probably the most important event in domestication.
sentences.zh: 这很可能是驯化过程中最重要的事件。

sentences.en: The first written record of tomatoes—from Spain in the 1500s—confirms that this mutation, which enlarges tomatoes by producing compartments known as locules, existed back in the same yellow tomatoes that gave Italians the word pomodoro, or golden apple.
sentences.zh: 关于番茄的第一份文字记载——来自16世纪的西班牙——证实，这个通过产生被称为心室的小室来使番茄增大的突变，早就存在于那种黄色番茄之中，正是这种番茄让意大利人有了pomodoro一词，意即金苹果。

sentences.en: Besides size, tomato farmers also selected for shape.
sentences.zh: 除了大小之外，番茄种植者还对形状进行了选育。

sentences.en: To discover those genes, Esther van der Knaap, a Tanksley alumna now at The Ohio State University, took a gene from one heirloom tomato and inserted it into a wild relative.
sentences.zh: 为了找出那些基因，坦克斯利曾经的学生、如今在俄亥俄州立大学任职的埃丝特·范德克纳普，从一种传家宝番茄中取出一个基因，把它插入一个野生近缘种。

sentences.en: She observed that, as a result, the tiny fruits became shaped like pears.
sentences.zh: 她观察到，结果那些细小的果实变成了梨的形状。

sentences.en: (E) The selection of these traits has, however, affected the heirlooms’ hardiness.
sentences.zh: 然而，对这些性状的选育，影响了传家宝番茄的强健程度。

sentences.en: They often suffer from infections that cause the fruit to crack, split, and otherwise rot quickly.
sentences.zh: 它们常常遭受感染，致使果实开裂、裂口，并以其他方式迅速腐烂。

sentences.en: Wild plants must continuously evolve to fend off such infections, points out Roger Chetelat of the Tomato Genetics Resource Center at the University of California.
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚大学番茄遗传资源中心的罗杰·切特拉指出，野生植物必须不断进化，以抵御此类感染。

sentences.en: But in their quest for size, shape, and flavor, humans have inadvertently eliminated defensive genes.
sentences.zh: 但在追求大小、形状和风味的过程中，人类无意中淘汰了那些防御性基因。

sentences.en: As a result, most possess only a single disease-resistant gene.
sentences.zh: 其结果是，大多数传家宝番茄只拥有一个抗病基因。

sentences.en: Chetelat elaborates that heirlooms’ taste may have less to do with their genes than with the productivity of the plant and the growing environment.
sentences.zh: 切特拉进一步解释说，传家宝番茄的味道，与其说取决于它们的基因，不如说更取决于植株的产量和生长环境。

sentences.en: Any plant that produces only two fruits, as heirlooms sometimes do, is highly likely to produce juicier, sweeter, and more flavorful fruit than varieties that produce 100, as commercial types do.
sentences.zh: 任何只结两个果实的植株——传家宝番茄有时就是如此——结出的果实，极有可能比那些像商业品种一样结100个果实的品种更多汁、更甜、更有风味。

sentences.en: In addition, heirlooms are sold ripened on the vine, a certain way to get tastier results than allowing them to mature on the shelf.
sentences.zh: 此外，传家宝番茄是在藤上成熟后才出售的，这无疑比让它们在货架上成熟更能得到可口的结果。

sentences.en: This means breeders feel confident that getting germ-beating genes back into heirlooms won’t harm the desirable aspects of the fruit.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，育种者有信心：把抗菌基因重新引入传家宝番茄，并不会损害果实那些令人称道的方面。

sentences.en: Modern breeding has resuscitated grocery-store tomatoes with an influx of wild genes; in the past 50 years, as many as 40 disease-resistant genes have been bred back into commercial crops.
sentences.zh: 现代育种已通过注入大量野生基因，让杂货店里的番茄重焕生机；在过去50年里，多达40个抗病基因已被重新培育进商业作物之中。

sentences.en: (F) In 1996, a tomato breeder and former Tanksley student named Doug Heath began a favorite project.
sentences.zh: 1996年，一位番茄育种家、坦克斯利曾经的学生道格·希思开始了一个他钟爱的项目。

sentences.en: After 12 years of traditional breeding with the help of molecular markers, he created a new multi-colored tomato less prone to cracking and also endowed with 12 disease-resistant genes.
sentences.zh: 在借助分子标记进行了12年的传统育种之后，他培育出一种不易开裂、并被赋予了12个抗病基因的新型多色番茄。

sentences.en: The original heirloom plant, Heath explains, had defective flowers, which is one reason why it produced only two fruits compared with the 30 he gets from his new variety.
sentences.zh: 希思解释说，最初那株传家宝番茄的花有缺陷，这正是它只结两个果实的原因之一，而他的新品种能结30个。

sentences.en: He claims he is also able to maintain a comparable flavor and sugar profile even on productive plants.
sentences.zh: 他声称，即便在高产的植株上，他也能保持相当的风味和糖分构成。

sentences.en: The heirloom’s defects are, after all, just an accident of a narrow breeding strategy left over from the very beginning of genetic modification.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，传家宝番茄的缺陷，不过是一种狭隘育种策略的偶然产物，而这种策略是从基因改造最初阶段遗留下来的。

records.title: Will Eating Less Make You Live Longer

sentences.en: A Calorie restriction, or 'semi-starvation' as some refer to it, has been proven to extend lifespan in many living organisms from yeast to mice, but the picture for primates, including humans, is not so clear.
sentences.zh: 热量限制，或者像有些人所说的“半饥饿”，已被证明能延长从酵母到小鼠等许多生物的寿命，但对包括人类在内的灵长类来说，情况就不那么清楚了。

sentences.en: Research published by a team at the University of Wisconsin in the United States shows that rhesus monkeys also live longer on a calorie-restricted diet.
sentences.zh: 美国威斯康星大学一个团队发表的研究表明，恒河猴在热量限制饮食下也活得更久。

sentences.en: But those findings disagree with research by the National Institute on Aging (NIA) in Maryland, also in the United States.
sentences.zh: 但那些发现与美国马里兰州国家老龄研究所的研究不一致。

sentences.en: Rozalyn Anderson, of the Wisconsin team, says the research is not intended as a recommendation of calorie restriction.
sentences.zh: 威斯康星团队的罗莎琳·安德森说，这项研究并不打算作为对热量限制的推荐。

sentences.en: 'I find the idea monumentally unattractive!'
sentences.zh: “我觉得这个想法极其没有吸引力！”

sentences.en: she says.
sentences.zh: 她说。

sentences.en: 'We study it because it is so effective at delaying ageing and the onset of age-related disease.
sentences.zh: “我们研究它，是因为它在延缓衰老和与年龄相关疾病的发作方面如此有效。

sentences.en: It's a way to tease out what it is that creates increased disease vulnerability as a function of age.'
sentences.zh: 它是一种厘清究竟是什么随年龄增长造成疾病易感性增加的办法。”

sentences.en: B Both groups started long-term trials on rhesus monkeys in the late 1980s to determine whether calorie restriction would extend the lifespan of primates.
sentences.zh: 两个团队都在20世纪80年代末开始了对恒河猴的长期试验，以确定热量限制是否会延长灵长类的寿命。

sentences.en: In mice, many experiments had come to the same finding: feed them a diet with 30% fewer calories and see a lifespan extension of 40%.
sentences.zh: 在小鼠身上，许多实验都得出了相同的发现：给它们喂热量少30%的饮食，会看到寿命延长40%。

sentences.en: The monkey trials were set up in a similar way: researchers took the calorie content of a standard monkey diet, cut it by 30% (while continuing to supply all essential nutrients) and monitored whether those monkeys lived longer, healthier lives than those on the standard diet.
sentences.zh: 猴子的试验也以类似的方式设置：研究人员取一份标准猴子饮食的热量含量，把它削减30%（同时继续供应所有必需的营养），并监测那些猴子是否比吃标准饮食的猴子活得更久、更健康。

sentences.en: C In 2009, with the monkeys approaching old age, preliminary findings of the two trials started coming in.
sentences.zh: 在2009年，随着这些猴子接近老年，两项试验的初步发现开始出来了。

sentences.en: For the Wisconsin monkeys, calorie restriction seemed to be working.
sentences.zh: 对威斯康星的猴子来说，热量限制似乎在起作用。

sentences.en: Compared to well-fed control animals, the lean monkeys were living longer and suffering less from the diseases of ageing: diabetes, heart disease and brain diseases.
sentences.zh: 与吃得好的对照动物相比，这些精瘦的猴子活得更久，也较少受衰老疾病的折磨：糖尿病、心脏病和脑部疾病。

sentences.en: However, in 2012 the NIA results emerged with a dramatically different conclusion: their monkeys were not living any longer than the controls, although they were healthier.
sentences.zh: 然而，在2012年，国家老龄研究所的结果以一个截然不同的结论出现：它们的猴子并没有比对照组活得更久，尽管它们更健康。

sentences.en: D The Wisconsin group's latest results confirm that their calorie-restricted monkeys are living longer than the controls.
sentences.zh: 威斯康星团队最新的结果证实，它们做了热量限制的猴子比对照组活得更久。

sentences.en: They also offer a possible explanation of why the two groups' findings don't agree, and that lies in the treatment of the control group.
sentences.zh: 它们还为两个团队的发现为何不一致提供了一种可能的解释，而那在于对照组的处理方式。

sentences.en: The Wisconsin study began with monkeys in early adulthood.
sentences.zh: 威斯康星的研究始于处于成年早期的猴子。

sentences.en: Initially, all the monkeys were allowed to eat as much as they liked.
sentences.zh: 起初，所有猴子都被允许想吃多少吃多少。

sentences.en: A few months into the trial, the monkeys were placed into one of two groups: the controls (who continued to be fed as much as they wished) and the calorie-restricted monkeys (who were given an individualised diet of 30% less than they were previously eating).
sentences.zh: 试验开始几个月后，这些猴子被分入两组之一：对照组（继续想吃多少喂多少）和热量限制组（被给予一份比它们之前所吃少30%的个性化饮食）。

sentences.en: E The NIA study differed in two ways.
sentences.zh: 国家老龄研究所的研究在两个方面有所不同。

sentences.en: First, the control group of monkeys were not allowed to eat as much as they wished.
sentences.zh: 首先，对照组的猴子不被允许想吃多少吃多少。

sentences.en: They were given a diet considered to represent a normal calorie count, while the calorie-restricted monkeys were fed 30% less than that.
sentences.zh: 它们被给予一份被认为代表正常热量摄入的饮食，而热量限制组的猴子则被喂以比那少30%的量。

sentences.en: Second, whereas the Wisconsin monkeys were given highly processed food high in sucrose, making it easy to standardise, the NIA diet was based on whole grains, fish oils, and was very low in sugar.
sentences.zh: 其次，威斯康星的猴子被给予高蔗糖的高度加工食物、以便容易标准化，而国家老龄研究所的饮食以全谷物、鱼油为基础，含糖极低。

sentences.en: These different settings for the normal control diet may provide an explanation of why the two groups showed different results.
sentences.zh: 正常对照饮食的这些不同设定，可能为两个团队为何显示出不同结果提供了一种解释。

sentences.en: F The Wisconsin group may in effect have studied the effects of 'overeating'.
sentences.zh: 威斯康星团队实际上可能研究的是“过量进食”的影响。

sentences.en: Their control animals weighed up to 10% more than average for their age and gender.
sentences.zh: 它们的对照动物体重比同年龄、同性别的平均值高出多达10%。

sentences.en: Compared to them, the calorie-restricted animals not only suffered fewer diseases, they lived longer.
sentences.zh: 与它们相比，热量限制的动物不仅患的疾病更少，还活得更久。

sentences.en: Julie Mattison, head of the NIA study, observes that an overweight person who goes to a fast food restaurant every day will obviously benefit if their calories are cut back by 30%.
sentences.zh: 国家老龄研究所研究的负责人朱莉·马蒂森指出，一个每天去快餐店的超重者，如果他们的热量被削减30%，显然会受益。

sentences.en: G The NIA study fed their control monkeys what they considered a 'standard' caloric intake and saw that longevity for monkeys that were fed 30% less was the same.
sentences.zh: 国家老龄研究所给它们的对照猴喂以它们认为“标准”的热量摄入，并发现被喂以少30%的猴子寿命是一样的。

sentences.en: But in Anderson's view, the NIA control monkeys were not fed enough; the NIA was calorie restricting both groups of animals.
sentences.zh: 但在安德森看来，国家老龄研究所的对照猴喂得不够；该所对两组动物都做了热量限制。

sentences.en: Their older female control monkeys, for example, weighed nearly 20% less than the national average.
sentences.zh: 比如，它们较年长的雌性对照猴体重比全国平均值轻了近20%。

sentences.en: Indeed, Anderson points out that several of the NIA control monkeys have lived past the age of 40, far exceeding the 27- year average lifespan for captive rhesus monkeys.
sentences.zh: 实际上，安德森指出，国家老龄研究所的几只对照猴活过了40岁，远远超过圈养恒河猴27年的平均寿命。

sentences.en: 'That's the maximum lifespan ever detected for the species, so the idea that their intervention is doing nothing is really at odds with the data,' says Anderson.
sentences.zh: 安德森说：“那是这个物种有史以来探测到的最长寿命，所以认为它们的干预什么都没做的看法，真的与数据相悖。”

sentences.en: H However, neither group had the right notion of a standard diet according to Leonie Heilbronn, who researches calorie restriction and healthy ageing at the University of Adelaide in Australia.
sentences.zh: 然而，据在澳大利亚阿德莱德大学研究热量限制与健康衰老的莱奥妮·海尔布隆说，两个团队对标准饮食都没有正确的概念。

sentences.en: Heilbronn points out that the NIA controls were a very healthy set of monkeys and leaner than a control monkey should be.
sentences.zh: 海尔布隆指出，国家老龄研究所的对照猴是一群非常健康的猴子，比一只对照猴应有的样子更精瘦。

sentences.en: On the other hand, she notes, the Wisconsin controls were a little bigger than they had to be.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，她指出，威斯康星的对照猴比它们本该有的样子稍大了一点。

sentences.en: On balance, Heilbronn agrees with the Wisconsin researcher's argument.
sentences.zh: 权衡来看，海尔布隆同意威斯康星研究者的论点。

sentences.en: 'I think these studies suggest calorie restriction definitely will increase lifespan,' she says.
sentences.zh: 她说：“我认为这些研究表明，热量限制肯定会延长寿命。”

sentences.en: I Both studies agree that cutting calories is beneficial to health — in both cases the calorie-restricted monkeys had fewer diseases related to ageing.
sentences.zh: 两项研究都同意削减热量有益于健康——在两种情况下，热量限制的猴子患与衰老相关的疾病都更少。

sentences.en: As to the question of whether calorie restriction extends lifespan in primates, Anderson and Mattison are currently working together to compare the two studies' raw data.
sentences.zh: 至于热量限制是否延长灵长类寿命的问题，安德森和马蒂森目前正在合作比较两项研究的原始数据。

sentences.en: They plan to co-publish a joint analysis.
sentences.zh: 他们计划共同发表一份联合分析。

sentences.en: The current data conflict will ultimately provide deeper insights into ageing, Anderson predicts.
sentences.zh: 安德森预测，目前的数据冲突最终将为衰老提供更深刻的洞见。

sentences.en: 'The fact the two studies were set up differently, asking the same question in different ways — I think we will gain maximally from that.'
sentences.zh: “这两项研究设置不同、以不同的方式问同一个问题这一事实——我认为我们将从中获益最大。”

sentences.en: A Recently, winter floods on the rivers of central Europe have been among the worst for 600 to 700 years, and dams and dykes (protective sea walls) have failed to solve the problem.
sentences.zh: 近来，中欧河流的冬季洪水是600到700年来最严重的之一，大坝和堤坝（防护海墙）都未能解决这个问题。

sentences.en: Traditionally, river engineers have tried to get rid of the water quickly, draining it off the land and down to the sea in rivers reengineered as high-performance drains.
sentences.zh: 传统上，河流工程师们试图迅速排走洪水，把它从陆地排掉、经由被改造成高性能排水道的河流流入大海。

sentences.en: But however high they build the artificial riverbanks, the floods keep coming back.
sentences.zh: 但无论他们把人工河岸筑得多高，洪水还是不断回来。

sentences.en: And when they come, they seem to be worse than ever.
sentences.zh: 而且当洪水来时，它们似乎比以往任何时候都更严重。

sentences.en: B Engineers are now turning to a different plan: to sap the water's destructive strength by dispersing it into fields, forgotten lakes and flood plains.
sentences.zh: 工程师们现在转向一个不同的方案，通过把水分散到田野、被遗忘的湖泊和泛滥平原中来削弱水的破坏力。

sentences.en: They are reviving river bends and marshes to curb the flow, and even plugging city drains to encourage floodwater to use other means to go underground.
sentences.zh: 他们正在恢复河湾和沼泽以遏制水流，甚至堵住城市排水道，促使洪水用其他方式渗入地下。

sentences.en: Back in the days when rivers took a winding path to the sea, floodwaters lost force and volume while meandering across flood plains and inland deltas, but today the water tends to have a direct passage to the sea.
sentences.zh: 在过去河流蜿蜒入海的年代，洪水在泛滥平原和内陆三角洲上迂回时会失去力量和水量，但如今水往往有一条直通大海的通道。

sentences.en: This means that, when it rains in the uplands, the water comes down all at once.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，当高地下雨时，水会一下子全部涌下来。

sentences.en: C Worse, when the flood plains are closed off, the river's flow downstream becomes more violent and uncontrollable; by turning complex river systems into the simple mechanics of a water pipe, engineers have often created danger where they promised safety.
sentences.zh: 更糟的是，当泛滥平原被封闭，河流下游的水流会变得更猛烈、更难控制；通过把复杂的河流系统变成水管那样简单的机械，工程师们往往在他们承诺安全的地方制造了危险。

sentences.en: The Rhine, Europe's most engineered river, is a good example.
sentences.zh: 莱茵河，欧洲被改造得最多的河流，就是个很好的例子。

sentences.en: For a long time engineers have erased its backwaters and cut it off from its plain.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，工程师们抹去了它的回水区，把它和它的平原隔开。

sentences.en: The aim was partly to improve navigation, and partly to speed floodwaters out of the Alps and down to the North Sea.
sentences.zh: 目的一部分是改善通航，一部分是让洪水更快地流出阿尔卑斯山、流入北海。

sentences.en: Now, when it rains in the Alps, the peak flows from several branches of the Rhine coincide where once they arrived separately, and with four-fifths of the Lower Rhine's flood plain barricaded off, the waters rise.
sentences.zh: 如今，当阿尔卑斯山下雨时，莱茵河几条支流的洪峰会在曾经各自分开到达的地方汇合，而由于下莱茵河五分之四的泛滥平原被封堵，水位便上涨。

sentences.en: The result is more frequent flooding and greater damage.
sentences.zh: 结果是更频繁的洪水和更大的损害。

sentences.en: The same thing has happened in the US on the Mississippi River, which drains the world's second-largest river catchment into the Gulf of Mexico.
sentences.zh: 同样的事也发生在美国的密西西比河上，它把世界第二大流域的水排入墨西哥湾。

sentences.en: Despite some $7 billion spent over the last century on levees (embankments), the situation is growing worse.
sentences.zh: 尽管上个世纪在堤坝（路堤）上花了约70亿美元，情况却越来越糟。

sentences.en: D Specialists in water control now say that a new approach is needed — one which takes the whole landscape into consideration.
sentences.zh: 水利控制方面的专家现在说，需要一种新方法——一种把整个地貌都纳入考量的方法。

sentences.en: To help keep London's feet dry, the UK Environment Agency is reflooding 10 square kilometres of the ancient flood plain of the River Thames outside Oxford.
sentences.zh: 为帮助伦敦免遭水患，英国环境署正在把牛津城外泰晤士河古老泛滥平原的10平方公里重新淹没。

sentences.en: Nearer to London, it has spent £100 million creating new wetlands and a relief channel across 16 kilometres of flood plain.
sentences.zh: 在更靠近伦敦的地方，它已花费1亿英镑，在16公里的泛滥平原上开辟新的湿地和一条泄洪渠。

sentences.en: Similar ideas are being tested in Austria, in one of Europe's largest river restorations to date.
sentences.zh: 类似的想法正在奥地利接受检验，那是迄今欧洲最大的河流修复之一。

sentences.en: The engineers calculate that the restored flood plain of the Drava River can now store up to 10 million cubic metres of floodwater, and slow down storm surges coming out of the Alps by more than an hour, protecting towns not only in Austria, but as far downstream as Slovenia and Croatia.
sentences.zh: 工程师们计算，德拉瓦河修复后的泛滥平原现在能储存多达1000万立方米的洪水，并把来自阿尔卑斯山的风暴潮减缓一个多小时，不仅保护奥地利的城镇，还保护远至下游斯洛文尼亚和克罗地亚的城镇。

sentences.en: E The Dutch, for whom preventing floods is a matter of survival, have gone furthest.
sentences.zh: 对荷兰人来说，防洪关乎生存，他们走得最远。

sentences.en: This nation, built largely on drained marshes and seabed, has had several severe shocks in the last two decades, when very large numbers of people have had to be evacuated.
sentences.zh: 这个主要建在排干的沼泽和海床上的国家，在过去二十年里经历了几次严重的冲击，当时不得不疏散大量的人。

sentences.en: Since that time, the Dutch have broken one of their most enduring national stereotypes by allowing engineers to punch holes in dykes.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，荷兰人打破了他们最根深蒂固的民族成见之一，允许工程师在堤坝上打洞。

sentences.en: They plan to return up to a sixth of the country to its former waterlogged state in order to better protect the rest.
sentences.zh: 他们计划把多达六分之一的国土恢复到以前的水浸状态，以便更好地保护其余部分。

sentences.en: F Water use in cities also needs to change.
sentences.zh: 城市的用水方式也需要改变。

sentences.en: At the moment, cities seem to create floods; they are concreted and paved so that rains flow quickly into rivers.
sentences.zh: 目前，城市似乎在制造洪水；它们被混凝土和路面覆盖，使雨水迅速流入河流。

sentences.en: A new breed of 'soft engineers' wants cities to be porous; Berlin is one place where this is being done.
sentences.zh: 一类新的“软工程师”希望城市能透水；柏林就是正在这么做的一个地方。

sentences.en: Tough new rules for new developments mean that drains will be prevented from becoming overloaded after heavy rains.
sentences.zh: 针对新开发项目的严格新规意味着，排水道在大雨后将被防止超负荷。

sentences.en: Architects of new urban buildings are diverting rainwater from the roofs for use in toilets and the irrigation of roof gardens, while water falling onto the ground is collected in ponds, or passes underground through porous paving.
sentences.zh: 新城市建筑的设计师们正把屋顶的雨水引去用于冲厕和灌溉屋顶花园，而落到地面的水则被收集到池塘里，或通过透水路面渗入地下。

sentences.en: One high-tech urban development can store a sixth of its annual rainfall, and reuse most of the rest.
sentences.zh: 一个高科技城市开发项目能储存其年降雨量的六分之一，并重复利用其余大部分。

sentences.en: G Could this be expanded to protect a whole city?
sentences.zh: 这能否扩大到保护整座城市？

sentences.en: The test case could be Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 试验案例可能是洛杉矶。

sentences.en: With non-porous surfaces covering 70% of the city, drainage is a huge challenge.
sentences.zh: 由于不透水的地面覆盖了这座城市的70%，排水是个巨大的挑战。

sentences.en: Billions of dollars have been spent digging huge drains and concreting riverbeds, but many communities still flood regularly.
sentences.zh: 已经花了数十亿美元挖巨大的排水道、用混凝土浇筑河床，但许多社区仍然定期被淹。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, this desert city ships water from hundreds of kilometres away to fill its taps and swimming pool.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，这座沙漠城市从数百公里外运水来充满它的水龙头和游泳池。

sentences.en: Los Angeles has recently launched a new scheme to utilise floodwater in the Sun Valley section of the city.
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶最近启动了一个新方案，在该市Sun Valley区利用洪水。

sentences.en: The plan is to catch the rain that falls on thousands of driveways, parking lots and rooftops in the valley.
sentences.zh: 这个计划是收集落在该谷地成千上万条车道、停车场和屋顶上的雨水。

sentences.en: Trees will soak up water from parking lots; houses and public buildings will capture roof water to irrigate gardens and parks, and road drains will empty into old gravel pits to recharge the city's underground water reserves.
sentences.zh: 树木将吸走停车场的水；房屋和公共建筑将收集屋顶水来灌溉花园和公园，道路排水道则会排入旧砾石坑，给这座城市的地下水储备补给。

sentences.en: Result: less flooding and more water for the city.
sentences.zh: 结果是，洪水更少，城市的水更多。

sentences.en: It may sound expensive, until we realise how much is spent trying to drain cities and protect areas from flooding, and how little this method achieves.
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能很贵，直到我们意识到为给城市排水、保护地区免遭洪水花了多少钱，而那种方法的成效又多么微小。

sentences.en: A A psychiatrist Tony Fernando was walking down the street when he saw a group of young homeless men sitting on the footpath.
sentences.zh: 精神病学家Tony Fernando走在街上时，看到一群无家可归的年轻男子坐在人行道上。

sentences.en: As Fernando handed out gifts of food, he tried to video the men's reactions in his mind, recording how their gratitude lifted him in return.
sentences.zh: Fernando分发食物礼物时，试图在脑海里录下这些人的反应，记录他们的感激如何反过来让他振奋。

sentences.en: 'I felt warm, content, meaningful,' he says.
sentences.zh: “我感到温暖、满足、有意义，”他说。

sentences.en: Fernando believes the brain can be trained to make us happy and that his 'video method' is one way to achieve this.
sentences.zh: Fernando相信大脑可以被训练来让我们快乐，而他的“录像法”是实现这一点的一种方式。

sentences.en: In fact, a growing body of scientific research internationally is showing how we can learn happiness in the same way we can learn to play the piano.
sentences.zh: 事实上，国际上越来越多的科学研究正表明，我们可以像学弹钢琴一样学会快乐。

sentences.en: In the soft tissue that forms the brain, there are approximately ten trillion synapses connecting roughly a hundred billion neurons.
sentences.zh: 在构成大脑的软组织里，大约有十万亿个突触连接着约一千亿个神经元。

sentences.en: Active synapses become more sensitive; less active synapses die, but new ones grow quickly.
sentences.zh: 活跃的突触会变得更敏感；不那么活跃的突触会死去，但新的会迅速生长。

sentences.en: This is relatively new thinking – just 30 years ago, neuroscientists believed that adult brain cells couldn't regenerate.
sentences.zh: 这是相对较新的看法——就在30年前，神经科学家还相信成年人的脑细胞无法再生。

sentences.en: One of the pioneers in this field is University of Wisconsin professor Richard Davidson.
sentences.zh: 这个领域的先驱之一是威斯康星大学教授Richard Davidson。

sentences.en: He studied Buddhist monks using brain scans in his research facility, and found that those trained in meditation had higher levels of activity in the left prefrontal cortex – the area associated with happiness.
sentences.zh: 他在研究机构里用脑部扫描研究佛教僧侣，发现那些受过冥想训练的人，左前额叶皮层的活动水平更高——这一区域与快乐相关。

sentences.en: Davidson believes that the trained brain is physically different from the untrained one.
sentences.zh: Davidson相信，受过训练的大脑在生理上与未受训练的大脑不同。

sentences.en: B The idea that we can train our brains to find more happiness has been called 'mindfulness' by neuropsychologist Rick Hanson, author of Hardwiring Happiness.
sentences.zh: 我们可以训练大脑去寻得更多快乐这个想法，被神经心理学家、《Hardwiring Happiness》的作者Rick Hanson称为“正念”。

sentences.en: It was in college that Hanson, quite unintentionally, first recognised the importance of something that would become his life's work.
sentences.zh: 正是在大学里，Hanson相当无意间第一次认识到某种后来会成为他毕生事业的东西的重要性。

sentences.en: As an unconfident teenager, he discovered he could turn a small event, 'a young woman smiling at me', into a good feeling he could hold on to.
sentences.zh: 作为一个不自信的少年，他发现自己能把一件小事，“一位年轻女子对我微笑”，变成一种他能抓住不放的好感觉。

sentences.en: To do this, Hanson employs exactly the same imaginary 'video method' as psychiatrist Tony Fernando.
sentences.zh: 为做到这一点，Hanson采用了和精神病学家Tony Fernando完全相同的想象“录像法”。

sentences.en: 'The brain takes its shape from what the mind rests upon,' says Hanson.
sentences.zh: “大脑会从心念所栖之处取得它的形状，”Hanson说。

sentences.en: If you keep resting your mind on self-criticism and worries, he argues, your brain will be shaped by that.
sentences.zh: 他认为，如果你不断把心念停在自我批评和忧虑上，你的大脑就会被那塑造。

sentences.en: Hanson explains that resting it on pleasant feelings and the things you have accomplished means that over time your brain will take on a different shape, with strength and optimism hard-wired into it.
sentences.zh: Hanson解释说，把它停在愉快的感觉和你已经取得的成就上，意味着随着时间推移，你的大脑会呈现出不同的形状，把力量和乐观固化其中。

sentences.en: C In New Zealand, the Mental Health Foundation runs mindfulness programmes in 14 schools.
sentences.zh: 在新西兰，心理健康基金会在14所学校开展正念项目。

sentences.en: Foundation CEO Judi Clements says, 'It's a valuable approach because children are told to pay attention, but aren't told how to pay attention.'
sentences.zh: 基金会首席执行官Judi Clements说：“这是一种有价值的方法，因为孩子被告知要专注，却没被告知如何专注。”

sentences.en: Preliminary results on the outcomes found that children had sustained increases in well-being.
sentences.zh: 关于成效的初步结果发现，孩子们在幸福感上有持续的提升。

sentences.en: The Foundation recognises five pathways to happiness – being active, connecting with others, taking notice, learning and giving.
sentences.zh: 该基金会认可通向快乐的五条途径——保持活跃、与他人联系、留心觉察、学习和给予。

sentences.en: And, says Clements, 'We're detecting a hunger for it from different organisations and professions as well, so the Foundation is soon going to pilot an online “well-being game” in several workplaces.'
sentences.zh: 而且，Clements说：“我们也察觉到不同的组织和职业对它的渴求，所以基金会很快会在几个工作场所试点一个在线的‘幸福游戏’。”

sentences.en: The project leader is psychologist Carsten Grimm, who is interested in whether some pathways to happiness are more effective than others.
sentences.zh: 项目负责人是心理学家Carsten Grimm，他感兴趣的是某些通向快乐的途径是否比其他的更有效。

sentences.en: In a study, Grimm recorded the activities and corresponding happiness scores of 173 people.
sentences.zh: 在一项研究中，Grimm记录了173个人的活动及相应的幸福分数。

sentences.en: What he found was that people who used several pathways to happiness achieved the best results, suggesting it's better to have a balance than concentrate on the single pathway you most identify with.
sentences.zh: 他发现，使用多条通向快乐途径的人取得了最好的结果，这表明保持平衡比专注于你最认同的单一途径更好。

sentences.en: D However, Associate Professor of Psychological Medicine Nathan Consedine greets our relentless search for the secrets to happiness with a tired sigh.
sentences.zh: 然而，心理医学副教授Nathan Consedine对我们不懈追寻快乐秘诀的做法报以一声疲惫的叹息。

sentences.en: 'The more you chase it, the less you get it,' he says, quoting studies showing those who value contentment and well-being are, in fact, less happy.
sentences.zh: “你越追逐它，越得不到它，”他说，并引用研究表明那些看重满足和幸福感的人其实更不快乐。

sentences.en: The big question, he says, is whether there's any benefit in actively seeking happiness.
sentences.zh: 他说，重大的问题是，主动寻求快乐是否有任何益处。

sentences.en: He cites a study, for example, which showed that people who were happier were less inclined to show sympathy.
sentences.zh: 比如，他引用一项研究，表明更快乐的人更不倾向于表现出同情。

sentences.en: Consedine says that's probably because happy people are strongly motivated to stay happy, but engaging sympathetically with others typically involves engaging with their distress, and that's going to reduce their own happiness.
sentences.zh: Consedine说，那大概是因为快乐的人有很强的动机保持快乐，但与他人有同情心地互动通常意味着要触及他们的痛苦，而那会降低他们自己的快乐。

sentences.en: Consedine's not disagreeing with the theory of mindfulness, but believes there's more work to be done.
sentences.zh: Consedine并不反对正念理论，但他相信还有更多工作要做。

sentences.en: E Some of that work is being conducted at Auckland University's Centre for Brain Research.
sentences.zh: 其中一些工作正在奥克兰大学的脑研究中心进行。

sentences.en: Associate Professor Johanna Montgomery has been studying Hanson's theory – that altering our brain activity at a synaptic level affects our behaviour.
sentences.zh: 副教授Johanna Montgomery一直在研究Hanson的理论——在突触层面改变我们的大脑活动会影响我们的行为。

sentences.en: She accepts that it's a logical explanation based on studies from animals, but we haven't yet got the technology to prove it scientifically in humans.
sentences.zh: 她接受这是个基于动物研究的合乎逻辑的解释，但我们还没有技术在人身上科学地证明它。

sentences.en: It's true that MRI scans certainly do indicate an increased flow of blood to different areas of the brain which are experiencing positive stimuli.
sentences.zh: 确实，MRI扫描的确显示，正在经历积极刺激的大脑不同区域血流量增加。

sentences.en: However, she warns that this is a long way from confirming that the brain itself is developing or strengthening.
sentences.zh: 不过，她警告说，这离确认大脑本身正在发育或增强还差得很远。

sentences.en: F Nonetheless, Montgomery believes she is making progress.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，Montgomery相信她正在取得进展。

sentences.en: In the laboratory, when scientists want to experiment with synaptic connections, they stimulate the brain with electricity, as this copies the high-frequency firings that happen normally in the brain every second.
sentences.zh: 在实验室里，当科学家想对突触连接做实验时，他们用电刺激大脑，因为这模仿了大脑里每秒正常发生的高频放电。

sentences.en: Using this technique, Montgomery has made a number of findings.
sentences.zh: 利用这种技术，Montgomery有了一些发现。

sentences.en: For example, the hormones that are released routinely in response to good or bad situations – such as adrenaline – act to regulate the brain, in the same way that weather has a regulating effect on human activity more generally.
sentences.zh: 比如，那些为回应好或坏的情境而例行释放的激素——比如肾上腺素——起到调节大脑的作用，就像天气对更广泛的人类活动有调节作用一样。

sentences.en: But scientists understand some of these stimuli better than others.
sentences.zh: 但科学家对其中一些刺激比对另一些了解得更多。

sentences.en: More is known about the impact on brain activity of prolonged periods of fear than the effects of 'happiness' hormones that are released by positive events in life.
sentences.zh: 相比由生活中积极事件释放的“快乐”激素的效果，人们对长时间恐惧对大脑活动的影响了解得更多。

sentences.en: This is one potentially important area that she hopes to investigate further in future.
sentences.zh: 这是她希望未来进一步研究的一个潜在重要领域。

sentences.en: A It has long been held that decisions made collectively by large groups of people are more likely to turn out to be accurate than decisions made by individuals.
sentences.zh: 长期以来人们一直认为，由大群人集体做出的决定比个人做出的决定更可能准确。

sentences.en: The idea goes back to the 'jury theorem' of Nicolas de Condorcet, an 18th-century French philosopher who was one of the first to apply mathematics to the social sciences.
sentences.zh: 这个想法可以追溯到18世纪法国哲学家Nicolas de Condorcet的“陪审团定理”，他是最早把数学应用于社会科学的人之一。

sentences.en: Condorcet's theory describes collective decisions, outlining how democratic decisions tend to outperform dictatorial ones.
sentences.zh: Condorcet的理论描述了集体决策，阐述了民主决策往往如何优于独裁决策。

sentences.en: If, for example, each member of a jury has only partial information, the majority decision is more likely to be correct than a decision arrived at by a single juror.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果陪审团的每名成员只有部分信息，那么多数人的决定比单个陪审员得出的决定更可能正确。

sentences.en: Moreover, the probability of a correct decision increases with the size of the jury.
sentences.zh: 而且，正确决定的概率会随陪审团规模的增大而提高。

sentences.en: B Now it is becoming clear that group decisions are also extremely valuable for the success of social animals, such as ants, bees, birds and dolphins.
sentences.zh: 如今越来越清楚的是，集体决策对蚂蚁、蜜蜂、鸟和海豚等群居动物的成功也极其宝贵。

sentences.en: Bees make collective decisions, and they do it rather well, according to Christian List of the London School of Economics, who has studied group decision-making in humans and animals.
sentences.zh: 据研究过人类和动物群体决策的伦敦政治经济学院的Christian List说，蜜蜂会做集体决定，而且做得相当好。

sentences.en: Researchers led by Dr List looked at colonies once the original colony reached a certain size.
sentences.zh: List博士带领的研究人员观察了原蜂群达到一定规模后的蜂群。

sentences.en: The queen goes off with about two-thirds of the worker bees to live in a new home or nest, leaving a daughter queen in the old nest with the remaining workers.
sentences.zh: 蜂王带着约三分之二的工蜂离开，去新家或新巢生活，把一只女儿蜂王和其余工蜂留在旧巢。

sentences.en: Among the bees that depart are some that have searched for and found some new nest sites, and reported back using a characteristic body movement known as a 'waggle dance' to indicate to the other bees the suitable places they have located.
sentences.zh: 在离开的蜜蜂中，有些已经搜寻并找到了一些新的筑巢地点，并用一种叫“摆尾舞”的特征性身体动作报告回来，向其他蜜蜂指明它们找到的合适地点。

sentences.en: The longer the dance, the better the site.
sentences.zh: 舞跳得越久，地点越好。

sentences.en: After a while, other bees start to visit the sites signalled by their companions to see for themselves and, on their return, also perform more waggle dances.
sentences.zh: 过一会儿，其他蜜蜂开始去访问同伴示意的那些地点，亲自查看，回来后也表演更多的摆尾舞。

sentences.en: The process eventually leads to a consensus on the best site and the breakaway swarm migrates.
sentences.zh: 这个过程最终导向对最佳地点的共识，分出来的蜂群随之迁徙。

sentences.en: The decision is remarkably reliable, with the bees choosing the best site even when there are only small differences between alternative sites.
sentences.zh: 这个决定可靠得惊人，即使备选地点之间只有微小差别，蜜蜂也会选出最佳地点。

sentences.en: C But exactly how do bees reach such a robust consensus?
sentences.zh: 但蜜蜂究竟如何达成如此稳健的共识？

sentences.en: To find out, Dr List and his colleagues used a computer-generated model of the decision-making process.
sentences.zh: 为弄清这一点，List博士和同事用了一个计算机生成的决策过程模型。

sentences.en: By experimenting with it, they found that, when bees in the model were very good at finding nesting sites but did not share their information, this dramatically slowed down the migration, leaving the swarm homeless and vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 通过对它做实验，他们发现，当模型中的蜜蜂很擅长找筑巢点却不分享信息时，这会大大减慢迁徙，使蜂群无家可归、容易受伤害。

sentences.en: Conversely, bees in the model blindly followed the waggle dances of others without first checking.
sentences.zh: 反过来，模型中的蜜蜂不先核实就盲目跟随别的蜜蜂的摆尾舞。

sentences.en: The researchers concluded that the ability of bees to identify successfully and quickly the best site depends on both the bees' interdependence in communicating the whereabouts of the best site, and their independence in confirming this information for themselves.
sentences.zh: 研究人员的结论是，蜜蜂成功而迅速地识别最佳地点的能力，既取决于蜜蜂在传达最佳地点位置上的相互依赖，也取决于它们亲自确认这一信息上的独立性。

sentences.en: D Another situation in which collective decisions are taken occurs when animals are either isolated from crucial sources of information or dominated by other members of the group.
sentences.zh: 另一种做出集体决定的情形，发生在动物要么与关键信息源隔绝、要么被群体中其他成员支配时。

sentences.en: Jose Halloy of the Free University of Brussels in Belgium used robotic cockroaches to subvert the behaviour of living cockroaches and control their decision-making process.
sentences.zh: 比利时布鲁塞尔自由大学的Jose Halloy用机器蟑螂来颠覆活蟑螂的行为，控制它们的决策过程。

sentences.en: In his experiment, the artificial bugs were introduced to the live ones and soon became sufficiently socially integrated that they were perceived by the real cockroaches as equals.
sentences.zh: 在他的实验里，这些人造虫子被引入活虫子中，很快就在社交上融入得足够好，被真蟑螂视为同类。

sentences.en: By manipulating the robots, which were in the minority, Halloy was able to persuade the living cockroaches to choose an inappropriate shelter—even one which they had rejected before being infiltrated by the robots.
sentences.zh: 通过操纵处于少数的机器人，Halloy得以说服活蟑螂选择一个不合适的庇护所——甚至是一个它们在被机器人渗透之前曾拒绝的庇护所。

sentences.en: E The way insects put into effect collective decisions can be complex and as important as the decisions themselves.
sentences.zh: 昆虫付诸实施集体决定的方式可以很复杂，并和决定本身一样重要。

sentences.en: At the University of Bristol, in the UK, Nigel Franks and his colleagues studied how a species of ant establishes a new nest.
sentences.zh: 在英国布里斯托大学，Nigel Franks及其同事研究了一种蚂蚁如何建立新巢。

sentences.en: Franks and his associates reported how the insects reduce the problems associated with making a necessarily swift choice.
sentences.zh: Franks和他的同事报告了这些昆虫如何减少与做出必然迅速的选择相关的问题。

sentences.en: If the ants' existing nest becomes suddenly threatened, the insects choose certain ants to act as scouts to find a new nest.
sentences.zh: 如果蚂蚁现有的巢突然受到威胁，这些昆虫会选出某些蚂蚁充当侦察兵去寻找新巢。

sentences.en: How quickly they accomplish the transfer to a new home depends not only on how soon the best available site is found, but also on how quickly the migration there can be achieved.
sentences.zh: 它们多快完成向新家的转移，不仅取决于多快找到现有最佳地点，也取决于多快能完成向那里的迁移。

sentences.en: F Once the suitable new nest is identified, the chosen ants begin to lead others, which have made it to the new site or which may simply be in the vicinity, back to the original threatened nest.
sentences.zh: 一旦合适的新巢被确定，被选中的蚂蚁便开始带领其他蚂蚁——那些已到达新址或可能只是在附近的蚂蚁——返回原先受威胁的巢。

sentences.en: In this way, those ants which are familiar with the route can help transport, for example, the queen and young ants to the new site, and simultaneously show the way to those ants which have been left behind to guard the old nest.
sentences.zh: 这样，熟悉路线的蚂蚁就能帮忙运送比如蜂王和幼蚁到新址，同时给那些被留下守卫旧巢的蚂蚁指路。

sentences.en: In this way, moving processes are accomplished faster and more efficiently.
sentences.zh: 这样，迁移过程完成得更快、更高效。

sentences.en: Thus, the dynamics of collective decision-making are closely related to the efficient implementation of those decisions.
sentences.zh: 因此，集体决策的动态与那些决定的高效实施密切相关。

sentences.en: How this might apply to choices that humans make is, as yet, unclear.
sentences.zh: 这如何适用于人类做出的选择，目前还不清楚。

sentences.en: But it does suggest, even for humans, the importance of recruiting dynamic leaders to a cause, because the most important thing about collective decision-making, as shown by these insect experiments, is to get others to follow.

sentences.en: A Dogs' noses are renowned for sensitivity to smells, while human noses are thought to be poor by comparison, yet that might be a misconception.
sentences.zh: 狗的鼻子以对气味的敏感而闻名，而人的鼻子相比之下被认为很差，但那也许是一种误解。

sentences.en: According to recent studies, our noses are in fact acutely sensitive instruments that guide our everyday lives to a surprising extent.
sentences.zh: 根据近来的研究，我们的鼻子其实是高度敏感的仪器，在出人意料的程度上引导着我们的日常生活。

sentences.en: Subtle smells can change your mood, behaviour and the choices you make, often without you realising it.
sentences.zh: 微妙的气味能改变你的情绪、行为和你做出的选择，往往在你没意识到的情况下。

sentences.en: Our own odours, meanwhile, indicate emotional states such as fear or sadness to those around us.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，我们自身的气味向周围的人显示出诸如恐惧或悲伤之类的情绪状态。

sentences.en: The big mystery is why we aren't more aware of our nasal activity.
sentences.zh: 最大的谜团是，我们为什么没有更多地意识到自己鼻子的活动。

sentences.en: Noses have certainly never been at the forefront of sensory research, and were pushed aside until recently in favour of the seemingly more vital senses of vision and hearing.
sentences.zh: 鼻子当然从未处在感官研究的前沿，直到最近还一直被搁在一边，让位于看似更重要的视觉和听觉。

sentences.en: 'There has been a lot of prejudice that people are not that influenced by olfactory stimuli, especially compared to other mammals,' says Lilianne Mujica-Parodi, who studies the neurobiology of human stress at Stony Brook University in New York, in the United States.
sentences.zh: “一直有很多偏见，认为人不那么受嗅觉刺激的影响，尤其是和其他哺乳动物相比，”Lilianne Mujica-Parodi说，她在美国纽约的石溪大学研究人类压力的神经生物学。

sentences.en: B One of the first people to assert the relative unimportance of human smelling was Pierre Paul Broca, an influential 19th-century anatomist.
sentences.zh: 最早断言人类嗅觉相对不重要的人之一，是Pierre Paul Broca，一位有影响力的19世纪解剖学家。

sentences.en: After comparing the proportion of the brain devoted to smell in different animals, he suggested that mammals can be classed into two broad groups: macrosmatic mammals, such as dogs, have a finely tuned sense of smell which they rely on to perceive the world, while we, along with other primates and the marine mammals, are microsmatic – we have small olfactory organs that we only rely on to a small extent.
sentences.zh: 在比较了不同动物大脑中专司嗅觉的比例之后，他提出哺乳动物可以分成两大类，像狗这样的大嗅觉哺乳动物有着精细调校的嗅觉，它们依靠它来感知世界，而我们，连同其他灵长类和海洋哺乳动物，是小嗅觉的——我们有小小的嗅觉器官，只在很小的程度上依赖它。

sentences.en: That idea seemed to fit with more recent studies which found that the majority of mammals have genes coding for about 1000 different types of smell receptor.
sentences.zh: 那个想法似乎与更近期的研究吻合，那些研究发现大多数哺乳动物拥有编码约1000种不同嗅觉受体的基因。

sentences.en: Most of these genes aren't expressed in humans, giving our noses just 400 different types of receptor.
sentences.zh: 这些基因大多数在人类身上不表达，使我们的鼻子只有400种不同的受体。

sentences.en: C Yet these findings may have been misleading.
sentences.zh: 然而这些发现可能一直是误导性的。

sentences.en: Brain scans now show that more of the brain is devoted to smell processing than Broca's anatomical studies suggested.
sentences.zh: 脑部扫描现在表明，专司嗅觉处理的大脑比Broca的解剖研究所暗示的要多。

sentences.en: And although we may have fewer types of receptor than other mammals, Charles Greer at Yale University in the United States has shown that the human nose and brain are unusually well connected, with each group of receptors linking to many more neural regions than is the case in other animals.
sentences.zh: 而且尽管我们的受体种类可能比其他哺乳动物少，但美国耶鲁大学的Charles Greer已证明，人的鼻子和大脑异乎寻常地连接良好，每一组受体连接到的神经区域都比其他动物多得多。

sentences.en: That should give us a good ability to process incoming scents.
sentences.zh: 那应该让我们有很好的能力来处理传入的气味。

sentences.en: Once researchers began looking, they found the nose to be far more sensitive than its reputation suggested.
sentences.zh: 研究人员一开始着手研究，就发现鼻子远比它的名声所暗示的更敏感。

sentences.en: One study, for example, found that we can detect certain chemicals diluted in water to less than one part per billion.
sentences.zh: 比如，一项研究发现，我们能察觉到在水中稀释到不足十亿分之一的某些化学物质。

sentences.en: That means that a person can detect just a few drops of a strong smell like ethyl mercaptan in an Olympic-sized pool.
sentences.zh: 那意味着，一个人能在一个奥林匹克标准的泳池里察觉到仅仅几滴像乙硫醇这样强烈气味的东西。

sentences.en: D 'We are also exceptionally gifted at telling smells apart, even in the case of two molecules whose only difference is that their structures are mirror images of one another.
sentences.zh: “我们还异常擅长分辨气味，即使是两个唯一区别在于其结构互为镜像的分子也不例外。

sentences.en: That is fantastic sensitivity,' says George Dodd, a perfumer and researcher at the olfaction group of the University of Warwick, in the United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 那是了不起的敏感度，”英国华威大学嗅觉研究组的香水师和研究员George Dodd说。

sentences.en: What's more, it's becoming clear that the brain's olfactory centres are intimately linked to its limbic system, which is involved in emotion, fear and memory.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，越来越清楚的是，大脑的嗅觉中枢与其边缘系统密切相连，后者与情绪、恐惧和记忆有关。

sentences.en: That suggests a link between smell and the way we think.
sentences.zh: 那暗示了气味与我们思考方式之间的联系。

sentences.en: E The power of smell will be no news to estate agents, who often advocate the smell of baking bread or brewing coffee to promote the sale of a house.
sentences.zh: 气味的力量对房产中介来说不会是新闻，他们常常提倡用烤面包或煮咖啡的气味来促进房子的销售。

sentences.en: But there are more subtle and surprising effects too.
sentences.zh: 但也有更微妙、更出人意料的效果。

sentences.en: When Hendrik Schifferstein and colleagues, from Delft University of Technology in the Netherlands, pumped the smell of orange, seawater or peppermint into a nightclub, the revellers danced more, rated their night as more enjoyable, and even thought the music was better than when there was no added scent.
sentences.zh: 当荷兰代尔夫特理工大学的Hendrik Schifferstein及其同事把橙子、海水或薄荷的气味泵入一家夜店时，狂欢者跳得更多，把自己的夜晚评得更尽兴，甚至觉得音乐比没有添加气味时更好。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Rob Holland, of the University of Utrecht in the Netherlands, found that the hint of aroma wafting out of a hidden bucket of citrus-scented cleaner was enough to persuade students in a hostel to clean up after themselves.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，荷兰乌得勒支大学的Rob Holland发现，从一个藏起来的柑橘味清洁剂桶里飘出的一丝香气，就足以说服一座宿舍里的学生收拾好自己的东西。

sentences.en: F Other work has found that scent can influence our cognitive skills.
sentences.zh: 其他研究发现，气味能影响我们的认知能力。

sentences.en: A study by William Overman and colleagues at the University of North Carolina in the United States found that when men were subjected to a novel smell – either good or bad – during a task used to test decision-making skills, they performed significantly worse than normal.
sentences.zh: 美国北卡罗来纳大学的William Overman及其同事所做的一项研究发现，当男性在一项用来测试决策能力的任务中接触到一种新奇的气味——无论是好是坏——时，他们的表现明显比正常时差。

sentences.en: The researchers conclude the scent stimulated brain areas connected with emotion, making their decisions emotional rather than rational.
sentences.zh: 研究人员的结论是，那种气味刺激了与情绪相连的大脑区域，使他们的决定变得情绪化而非理性。

sentences.en: G Smells are especially good memory evokers, but it is actually a myth that odours trigger more detailed memories than other stimuli.
sentences.zh: 气味尤其善于唤起记忆，但气味比其他刺激触发更详细记忆这一点其实是个谬误。

sentences.en: 'The memory is not more accurate and you don't remember more details,' says Yaara Yeshurun at the Weizmann Institute of Science in Rehovot, Israel, 'but it is unique in that it is more emotional.'
sentences.zh: “记忆并不更准确，你也不会记得更多细节，”以色列雷霍沃特魏茨曼科学研究所的Yaara Yeshurun说，“但它的独特之处在于它更情绪化。”

sentences.en: This isn't surprising when you consider that there are certain brain areas dedicated to both emotion and olfaction, such as the amygdala, and there is a strong link between emotion and memory.
sentences.zh: 当你想到有某些大脑区域同时专司情绪和嗅觉、比如杏仁核，而且情绪和记忆之间有很强的联系时，这就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: In 2009, Yeshurun found that the link between a memory and a smell is stronger if the smell is unpleasant rather than pleasant.
sentences.zh: 2009年，Yeshurun发现，如果气味是令人不快的而非令人愉快的，那么记忆和气味之间的联系会更强。

sentences.en: She also discovered that the very first time we attach a smell to an object, it evokes a much greater response in our brains than for any subsequent encounter with the smell or object, laying down stronger foundations for the memory.
sentences.zh: 她还发现，我们第一次把一种气味和一个物体联系起来时，它在我们大脑中唤起的反应比之后任何一次遇到这种气味或物体都大得多，为记忆打下了更牢固的基础。

sentences.en: That doesn't happen with any other sense.
sentences.zh: 任何其他感官都不会发生这种情况。

sentences.en: Since those first encounters with a smell would have happened at a young age, this explains why smells often transport us back to our childhood.
sentences.zh: 由于与一种气味的那些初次相遇本会发生在年幼时，这解释了为什么气味常把我们带回童年。

sentences.en: (A) Although it's hard to imagine in this age of urban sprawl and automobiles, North America once belonged to huge, elephant-like mammoths, camels, bear-sized beavers and other giant beasts, collectively known as 'megafauna'.
sentences.zh: 尽管在这个城市扩张和汽车的时代很难想象，但北美曾经属于巨大的、象一样的猛犸象、骆驼、熊一般大的河狸和其他巨兽，它们统称为“巨型动物群”。

sentences.en: Some 11,000 years ago, however, these large-bodied mammals—about 70 species in all—disappeared.
sentences.zh: 然而大约11000年前，这些大体型哺乳动物——总共约70个物种——消失了。

sentences.en: Their demise coincided roughly with the arrival of humans on the continent and dramatic climate change—factors that have inspired several theories about the die-off.
sentences.zh: 它们的消亡大致与人类到达这片大陆以及剧烈的气候变化同时——这些因素激发了关于这场灭绝的几种理论。

sentences.en: Yet despite decades of scientific investigation, the exact cause remains a mystery.
sentences.zh: 然而尽管经过几十年的科学调查，确切的原因仍是个谜。

sentences.en: Now new findings offer support to one of these controversial hypotheses: that human hunting drove these huge megafauna species to extinction.
sentences.zh: 现在，新的发现为这些有争议的假说之一提供了支持，即人类的狩猎把这些庞大的巨型动物物种逼向灭绝。

sentences.en: (B) This belief resulted in the overkill model which emerged in the 1960s, when it was put forth by Paul S.
sentences.zh: 这一信念产生了过度捕杀模型，该模型在20世纪60年代出现，当时由Paul S.

sentences.en: Martin of the University of Arizona.
sentences.zh: 亚利桑那大学的Martin提出。

sentences.en: Since then, critics have charged that no archaeological remains exist to support the idea that the first Americans hunted to the extent necessary to cause these extinctions, but at the annual meeting of the Society of Vertebrate Paleontology in Mexico City in October 1999, specialist John Alroy of the University of California at Santa Barbara argued that, in fact, hunting-driven extinction is not only plausible, it was unavoidable.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，批评者指责说，没有考古遗存支持最早的美洲人狩猎到了足以造成这些灭绝所必需程度的观点，但在1999年10月墨西哥城举行的脊椎动物古生物学会年会上，加州大学圣巴巴拉分校的专家John Alroy论证说，事实上，狩猎驱动的灭绝不仅说得通，而且是不可避免的。

sentences.en: He has determined, using a computer simulation, that even a very modest amount of hunting would have wiped out these animals.
sentences.zh: 他用一个计算机模拟确定，即便非常适度的狩猎量也会把这些动物灭绝。

sentences.en: Assuming an initial human population of 100 people that grew no more than two per cent annually, Alroy determined that, if each band of, say, 50 people killed 15 to 20 large animals a year, humans could have eliminated the animal populations within 1,000 years.
sentences.zh: 假设最初有100人的人口、每年增长不超过百分之二，Alroy确定，如果比方说每群50人每年杀死15到20只大型动物，人类就能在1000年内消灭这些动物种群。

sentences.en: Large mammals in particular would have been vulnerable to the pressure because they have longer gestation periods than smaller mammals and their young require extended care.
sentences.zh: 大型哺乳动物尤其会易受这种压力影响，因为它们的妊娠期比较小的哺乳动物长，它们的幼崽也需要长时间的照料。

sentences.en: (C) However, not everyone agrees with Alroy's assessment.

sentences.en: For one thing, the results depend on population-size estimates for the extinct animals—estimates that are not necessarily reliable.

sentences.en: But a more specific criticism comes from mammal expert Ross D.

sentences.en: MacPhee of the American Museum of Natural History in New York City, who points out that the relevant archaeological record contains barely a dozen examples of stone points embedded in mammoth bones (and none, it should be noted, are known from other megafaunal remains)—hardly what one might expect if hunting drove these animals to extinction.
sentences.zh: 纽约市美国自然历史博物馆的MacPhee，他指出，相关的考古记录里嵌在猛犸象骨头里的石尖几乎只有十来个例子（而且应当指出，其他巨型动物群遗存中一个都不为人所知）——如果狩猎把这些动物逼向灭绝，这很难是人们可能预期的情形。

sentences.en: Furthermore, some of these species had a vast range, covering the whole continent—the Jefferson's ground sloth, for example, lived as far north as the Yukon and as far south as Mexico—which would have made hunting them in numbers sufficient to cause their extinction rather unlikely, he says.

sentences.en: (D) MacPhee agrees that humans most likely brought about these extinctions (as well as others around the world that coincided with human arrival), but not directly.

sentences.en: Repeated outbreaks of a deadly disease could thus quickly drive them to the point of no return.

sentences.en: So far, MacPhee does not have empirical evidence for this theory, and it will not be easy to come by: such disease would kill far too quickly to leave its signature on the bones themselves.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，MacPhee还没有这个理论的经验证据，而要得到它并不容易，这样的疾病杀得太快，不会在骨头本身上留下它的印记。

sentences.en: But he hopes that analyses of tissue and DNA from the most recent animal remains will eventually reveal the microbes responsible.
sentences.zh: 但他希望，对最近的动物遗存的组织和DNA的分析，最终会揭示出负有责任的微生物。

sentences.en: (E) The third explanation for what brought on this North American extinction does not involve human beings.

sentences.en: Instead, its proponents blame the loss on the climate.

sentences.en: The Pleistocene epoch in question witnessed considerable climate instability, explains Russell W.

sentences.en: For some animals, this brought opportunity.

sentences.en: Although these creatures managed to maintain viable populations through most of the Pleistocene period, the final major climate fluctuation pushed them over the edge, Graham says.

sentences.en: (A) Just over a kilometer south of Berlin's Potsdamer Platz, near the left bank of the Landwehr Canal, an extensive, triangular-shaped area of waste ground once separated the neighbourhoods of Kreuzberg to the east and Schöneberg to the west.
sentences.zh: 在柏林波茨坦广场以南仅一公里多、靠近兰德韦尔运河左岸的地方，曾有一片广阔的三角形荒地，把东边的十字山区和西边的舍内贝格区隔开。

sentences.en: Known as Gleisdreieck, meaning 'triangle of rails', it was formed by the intersection of different railway lines built in the mid-nineteenth century that entered Berlin from the south.
sentences.zh: 这片地被称为格莱斯德赖埃克，意为“铁轨三角”，它是由19世纪中叶修建、从南面进入柏林的几条不同铁路线交汇而成的。

sentences.en: Tracks, sheds and warehouses belonging to three old railway stations – Dresdner Bahnhof (1875-1882), Potsdamer Bahnhof (1838-1944) and Anhalter Bahnhof (1839- 1952) – are situated on a raised area some twenty hectares in size, at a height of four metres above the surrounding ground level.
sentences.zh: 属于三座旧火车站——德累斯顿火车站（1875—1882）、波茨坦火车站（1838—1944）和安哈尔特火车站（1839—1952）——的轨道、车棚和仓库，坐落在一片约二十公顷大、高出周围地面四米的高地上。

sentences.en: (B) As the railway infrastructure gradually ceased to be used, the whole area of Gleisdreieck became increasingly run down and abandoned, to the point of being used as a rubbish tip after 1945.
sentences.zh: 随着这些铁路设施逐渐停止使用，整片格莱斯德赖埃克地区日益破败、被人遗弃，到1945年以后甚至被当作垃圾场。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, vegetation took over, turning it into a surprising, natural haven in the middle of built-up areas.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，植被占据了这里，把它变成了一处令人意想不到、夹在建筑密集区中央的自然乐园。

sentences.en: The closeness of the wall which divided the city of Berlin between 1961 and 1990 also contributed to the fact that Gleisdreieck was for decades clearly identified as no-man's-land.
sentences.zh: 1961年至1990年间分隔柏林城的那道墙近在咫尺，这也使得格莱斯德赖埃克在数十年里被明确地视为无人地带。

sentences.en: Only a station of the same name in Berlin's underground railway system testified to its existence.
sentences.zh: 唯有柏林地铁系统中一座同名的车站，证明着它的存在。

sentences.en: Shortly before the fall of the Berlin Wall, however, the German Museum of Technology was established there, attracting large numbers of visitors and giving visibility to the site.
sentences.zh: 然而，就在柏林墙倒塌前不久，德国技术博物馆在这里建成，吸引了大批参观者，让这片场地显露于人前。

sentences.en: More importantly, the unification of the formerly divided city gave the zone more centrality, at which point it became imperative to identify a purpose for it.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，这座一度被分隔的城市重归统一，使这片地带更具中心地位，到这时，为它确定一个用途就成了当务之急。

sentences.en: (C) After 2006, the State of Berlin put forward the proposal of converting Gleisdreieck into a large urban park that would integrate the different urban zones which converged there.
sentences.zh: 2006年之后，柏林州提出了一项提案，要把格莱斯德赖埃克改造成一座大型城市公园，把在此交会的不同城区整合起来。

sentences.en: The decades-long isolation of the site, which had formerly presented a problem, now represented an opportunity for joining the southern area of Potsdamer Platz with Kreuzberg and Schöneberg.
sentences.zh: 这片场地长达数十年的与世隔绝，从前是个难题，如今却成了把波茨坦广场南区与十字山区、舍内贝格区连接起来的契机。

sentences.en: The creation of the park would trigger one of the biggest urban expansions inside Berlin, all within a framework of multiple uses and social characteristics.
sentences.zh: 这座公园的建成，将引发柏林内部规模最大的城市扩展之一，而这一切都处在一个多种用途、多元社会特征并存的框架之内。

sentences.en: It was necessary to stimulate the development of sixteen new hectares of local amenities that would be capable of integrating different generations and social groups in a sustainable way, and in harmony with nature.
sentences.zh: 有必要推动十六公顷新增本地公共设施的建设，使其能够以可持续的方式、在与自然和谐相处的前提下，把不同世代和社会群体融合起来。

sentences.en: Following intense discussion with local proprietors and residents, the need to reconcile these goals with the conservation of railway heritage also emerged.
sentences.zh: 在与当地业主和居民进行了激烈的讨论之后，把这些目标与铁路遗产的保护相协调的需求也随之浮现。

sentences.en: (D) Once the area had been subjected to a process of undergrowth clearance and decontamination, it was then organized around a combination of existing and added elements.
sentences.zh: 在这片地区经过一番清除灌木丛和净化处理之后，它便围绕现有元素与新增元素的组合加以布置。

sentences.en: The project as a whole was planned around a large central meadow, intersected from east to west by a concrete footpath, and from north to south by a pair of railway lines.
sentences.zh: 整个项目是围绕一片巨大的中央草坪来规划的，草坪自东向西被一条混凝土步道贯穿，自北向南则被一对铁轨贯穿。

sentences.en: Once a month, a train slowly travels along these lines from its parking shed to the German Museum of Technology.
sentences.zh: 每月一次，一列火车会沿着这两条铁轨，从它的停放车棚缓缓驶向德国技术博物馆。

sentences.en: The concrete footpath, which is a continuation of one of the main Kreuzberg boulevards, starts in the east, bridges the four-metre difference in ground level by means of a stairway, and suddenly ends in the west on reaching the underground lines.
sentences.zh: 这条混凝土步道是十字山区一条主要大道的延伸，它起于东端，借助一段楼梯跨越四米的地面高差，又在西端抵达地铁线时戛然而止。

sentences.en: (E) North of the meadow, there is a large concrete slab with rounded edges.
sentences.zh: 草坪的北面，有一大块边缘呈圆角的混凝土板。

sentences.en: Being south-facing, this functions as a big sunny terrace, full of benches complete with footrests.
sentences.zh: 由于朝南，它充当了一个阳光充足的大露台，上面满是带搁脚处的长椅。

sentences.en: In the south, the meadow overlooks Yorckstrasse, an underpass crossed by more than fifteen former railway bridges.
sentences.zh: 在南面，草坪俯瞰着约克大街，那是一处由十五座以上旧铁路桥跨越的地下通道。

sentences.en: To the east of the meadow there is quite a dense forest of pre-existing maples, oaks and birches, as well as newly planted trees of the same species.
sentences.zh: 草坪的东面是一片相当茂密的树林，既有原先就有的枫树、橡树和桦树，也有新栽的同种树木。

sentences.en: In this area, a couple of large metal frames each hold two swings.
sentences.zh: 在这片区域，几个大型金属框架各自挂着两副秋千。

sentences.en: The edges of the park are finished with a collection of distinctive, functional spaces, for example a nursery, sports fields, concave surfaces for skateboards, stages for dancing, community gardens, or simply areas covered in gravel obtained from the site itself.
sentences.zh: 公园的边缘以一系列别具特色、各有用途的空间收尾，例如一座苗圃、运动场、供滑板使用的凹面、跳舞用的台子、社区花园，或仅仅是覆盖着取自这片场地本身的砾石的区域。

sentences.en: (F) Although initially the regeneration of Gleisdreieck Park was the subject of disagreement between those who were in favour of safeguarding the railway heritage and those who wanted to regenerate the adjacent neighbourhoods, it was opened to the public in September 2011.
sentences.zh: 尽管格莱斯德赖埃克公园的再生工程起初在主张保护铁路遗产者与希望重振邻近社区者之间引发了分歧，它仍于2011年9月向公众开放。

sentences.en: The heart of Berlin now has a new green lung, in which the atmosphere of various small, very different corners fits neatly into a large-scale, wide-ranging and robust general order.
sentences.zh: 柏林的心脏地带如今有了一片新的绿肺，其中各个细小而又迥然不同的角落所呈现的氛围，恰到好处地融入了一种大尺度、覆盖面广而又稳固的总体秩序之中。

sentences.en: This has been possible precisely because the intervention was not limited to conserving industrial remains in order to promote railway history.
sentences.zh: 这之所以能够实现，恰恰是因为这次改造并不局限于为弘扬铁路史而保存工业遗存。

sentences.en: And as a reminder of the six decades of human absence, during which nature took over, the park has been able to conserve to some extent the spirit of the non-place that preceded it.
sentences.zh: 而作为对那六十年人迹罕至、任由自然接管的岁月的纪念，这座公园在某种程度上得以保留了先前那处“非场所”的精神气质。

sentences.en: (A) New Zealand’s contribution to International Polar Year was a 52-day voyage by the ship Tangaroa in order to conduct research in Antarctica’s Ross Sea.
sentences.zh: 新西兰对国际极地年的贡献，是由“坦加罗阿”号科考船进行的一次为期52天的航行，目的是在南极洲的罗斯海开展研究。

sentences.en: Lead scientist Mary Livingston emphasises just what a multi-faceted expedition this was, bringing together zoologists, oceanographers, meteorologists and other scientists from the Ministry of Fisheries, the National Institute for Water and Atmospheric Research, the National Museum and various universities, to study life beneath the seas of Antarctica.
sentences.zh: 首席科学家玛丽·利文斯顿强调，这是一次多么多元的考察，它把来自渔业部、国家水与大气研究所、国家博物馆及各所大学的动物学家、海洋学家、气象学家和其他科学家汇聚到一起，去研究南极洲海底之下的生命。

sentences.en: Competition for berths – the ship can carry 44 people, including 13 crew – was fierce.
sentences.zh: 对铺位的争夺——这艘船可载44人，包括13名船员——异常激烈。

sentences.en: Voyage leader Stu Hanchet says, ‘We could have filled the science positions four times over …
sentences.zh: 航行负责人斯图·汉切特说：“我们本可以把这些科学岗位填满四次……

sentences.en: we had so many people requesting a berth …
sentences.zh: 申请铺位的人实在太多了……

sentences.en: We ended up with a really strong team.’
sentences.zh: 我们最终组成了一支非常强的团队。”

sentences.en: (B) It would be hard to overstate how hostile the Antarctic environment is for scientists.
sentences.zh: 要说南极环境对科学家有多么恶劣，怎么形容都不为过。

sentences.en: The Tangaroa’s captain, Graham Leachman, explains that the Ross Sea is subject to katabatic winds* that sweep down off the Antarctic continent to create rough seas.
sentences.zh: “坦加罗阿”号的船长格雷厄姆·利奇曼解释说，罗斯海会受到从南极大陆倾泻而下、卷起惊涛骇浪的下降风的影响。

sentences.en: Another danger is the possibility of the ship colliding with floating ice.
sentences.zh: 另一重危险是船只可能与浮冰相撞。

sentences.en: ‘Even though the ship’s officers use all sorts of high-tech equipment …
sentences.zh: “尽管船上的高级船员使用各种高科技设备……

sentences.en: none of it can tell you how thick the ice is,’ says Leachman, ‘and you still can’t beat looking out of the window.’
sentences.zh: 却没有一样能告诉你冰有多厚，”利奇曼说，“而你仍然没有比往窗外看更好的办法。”

sentences.en: In the dark, he says, you can’t tell how thick the ice is, but if you can see its colour, it’s possible to estimate.
sentences.zh: 他说，在黑暗中，你无法判断冰有多厚，但如果你能看见它的颜色，就有可能估算出来。

sentences.en: This is why he prefers sailing in summer, when the hours of daylight in these high latitudes are longest, even though this plays tricks with his passengers’ body clocks.
sentences.zh: 这正是他偏爱在夏季航行的原因，因为在这些高纬度地区，夏季的白昼时数最长，尽管这会捉弄他乘客们的生物钟。

sentences.en: (C) Analysis of what the expedition found continues, but it’s likely that several new species have been discovered and numerous other secrets revealed about life 3,000 metres below the surface.
sentences.zh: 对这次考察发现的分析仍在继续，但很可能已经发现了好几个新物种，并揭示出关于水面以下3000米处生命的许多其他秘密。

sentences.en: ‘We have collected huge worms and strange crustaceans,’ says Livingston, ‘but most impressive of all were the starfish that measured more than half a metre across – that’s most abnormal for creatures belonging to this species.’
sentences.zh: “我们采集到了巨大的蠕虫和奇异的甲壳类动物，”利文斯顿说，“但最令人惊叹的还是那些直径超过半米的海星——这对属于这一物种的生物来说极不正常。”

sentences.en: This phenomenon of Antarctic seas is called ‘gigantism’ – the fact that some species grow to unusually large sizes.
sentences.zh: 南极海域的这种现象被称为“巨型化”——即某些物种会长到异常大的体型。

sentences.en: Livingston suggests various possible causes for gigantism, including the extreme cold, few predators and high levels of oxygen in the seawater, but as yet, no final determination can be made.
sentences.zh: 利文斯顿提出了巨型化的几种可能成因，包括极度的寒冷、捕食者稀少以及海水中含氧量高，但目前还无法做出最终的定论。

sentences.en: Another interesting discovery was that in some places every inch of the sea floor was covered with life, whereas elsewhere icebergs have scoured out deep scars and ravines in the sea floor as they go by.
sentences.zh: 另一个有趣的发现是，在有些地方，海底每一寸都覆盖着生命，而在另一些地方，冰山在经过时则在海底刮出了深深的疤痕和沟壑。

sentences.en: (D) By using deep-sea trawl nets, high-definition cameras and water samplers, the team has revealed that many of the creatures that live at extreme depths have a bizarre appearance.
sentences.zh: 通过使用深海拖网、高清摄像机和取水器，该团队揭示出，许多生活在极深处的生物外形怪异。

sentences.en: Among them were spotted tunicates, plankton-eating animals that are slender structures that appear to be fashioned from glass.
sentences.zh: 其中有带斑点的被囊动物，那是一些以浮游生物为食的动物，呈细长的结构，看上去就像是用玻璃做成的。

sentences.en: The most fearsome-looking fish was the Southern Ocean daggertooth, a species that is ‘monocyclic’, meaning the fish die after the first spawning.
sentences.zh: 样子最凶恶的鱼是南大洋匕牙鱼，这一物种是“单周期”的，意思是这种鱼在第一次产卵后就会死去。

sentences.en: They are also unusual for being capable of shedding their teeth and growing a new set.
sentences.zh: 它们还有一个不寻常之处，就是能够脱落牙齿，再长出一副新的。

sentences.en: Another predatory fish brought to the surface was the stareater, an extraordinary species that has an appendage like a piece of cord hanging from its chin.
sentences.zh: 另一种被带到水面的掠食性鱼类是吞星鱼，这是一种非凡的物种，下巴上垂着一条像绳子一样的附器。

sentences.en: In these deep, dark waters, this glows red and attracts prey to swim within striking distance.
sentences.zh: 在这些幽深漆黑的水域里，这条附器会发出红光，引诱猎物游到攻击范围之内。

sentences.en: Just as impressive and much more beautiful were the basket stars, a species related to starfish that lives on the seabed.
sentences.zh: 同样令人惊叹、却美丽得多的是筐蛇尾，这是一种与海星有亲缘关系、生活在海床上的物种。

sentences.en: The basket stars’ five arms branch out numerous times to form a spectacular fan-like structure which they turn to face into the current so that food is brought into their embrace.
sentences.zh: 筐蛇尾的五条腕多次分叉，形成一个壮观的扇状结构，它们把这个结构转向迎着水流，好让食物被送入自己的怀抱。

sentences.en: (E) But whatever exciting discoveries were made, everyday life onboard ship in the Ross Sea is unrelenting.
sentences.zh: 但无论有什么激动人心的发现，在罗斯海的船上，日常生活都丝毫不会松懈。

sentences.en: Most people share a cabin with one other person – they’re allocated so that as one person begins their 12 hours off duty, the other occupant is starting work on deck.
sentences.zh: 大多数人与另一个人合住一间舱室——这样安排是为了让一个人开始他12小时的休班时，另一名同舱者正要上甲板开始工作。

sentences.en: The fresh food runs out in a few days and after that, most provisions are frozen, canned or dried.
sentences.zh: 新鲜食物几天就吃完了，在那之后，大多数补给都是冷冻、罐装或脱水的。

sentences.en: Expedition general manager Fred Smits recognises that the cook has an essential role in ensuring the well-being of those onboard.
sentences.zh: 考察队总经理弗雷德·斯米茨认识到，厨师在确保船上人员的身心安康方面起着至关重要的作用。

sentences.en: ‘When you are at sea for so long,’ he says, ‘you think a lot about your next meal.’
sentences.zh: “当你在海上待这么久时，”他说，“你会非常惦记自己的下一顿饭。”

sentences.en: (F) Perhaps most controversially, one of the precious berths on the Tangaroa was taken up by cameraman Max Quinn, who filmed a documentary about the voyage.
sentences.zh: 也许最具争议的是，“坦加罗阿”号上一个宝贵的铺位被摄影师马克斯·奎因占去了，他拍摄了一部关于此次航行的纪录片。

sentences.en: Quinn’s inclusion wasn’t welcomed at first.
sentences.zh: 奎因的加入起初并不受欢迎。

sentences.en: ‘Scientists by nature,’ Livingston says, ‘tend to be camera-shy and quiet.
sentences.zh: “科学家天生，”利文斯顿说，“往往羞于面对镜头、不爱说话。

sentences.en: They’re not into having cameras there, so it was difficult getting everyone’s permission and agreement.’
sentences.zh: 他们不喜欢有镜头在场，所以要取得每个人的许可和同意很难。”

sentences.en: But in the end Quinn fitted in very well.
sentences.zh: 但奎因最终融入得非常好。

sentences.en: ‘The trick,’ he says, ‘is to mostly film the scientists at work, in their professional roles …
sentences.zh: “诀窍，”他说，“在于大多拍摄科学家工作时、处于其专业角色中的样子……

sentences.en: rather than eating their breakfast.’
sentences.zh: 而不是拍他们吃早饭。”

sentences.en: He knows when not to intrude.
sentences.zh: 他知道什么时候不该打扰。

sentences.en: The documentary is a window on a trip few people get to make and also a peek into what research really looks like.
sentences.zh: 这部纪录片是一扇窗，让人得以窥见一趟少有人能成行的旅程，也让人得以一瞥科研真正的样子。

sentences.en: ‘Science,’ says Livingston, ‘is intrepid, more so than people realise.
sentences.zh: “科学，”利文斯顿说，“是无畏的，比人们意识到的更加无畏。

sentences.en: It’s not necessarily examining dry samples in the laboratory, but can also mean braving the elements on deck.
sentences.zh: 它未必是在实验室里检查干燥的样本，也可能意味着在甲板上勇敢面对风雨。

sentences.en: That’s what the documentary captures, the sense of real people with real lives.’
sentences.zh: 这正是这部纪录片所捕捉到的，那种有着真实生活的真实的人的感觉。”
