sentences.en: A While it has long been recognized that play affords benefits that last through adulthood, psychologists in the US are now becoming concerned that lack of play could actually be harming their country's kids.
sentences.zh: 虽然人们早已认识到玩耍带来的好处会延续到成年，但美国的心理学家如今开始担心，缺乏玩耍实际上可能正在伤害他们国家的孩子。

sentences.en: In the past, few children grew up without ample free-play time.
sentences.zh: 过去，很少有孩子在成长中没有充裕的自由玩耍时间。

sentences.en: But youngsters' leisure hours are now filled with structured activities such as music lessons and sports.
sentences.zh: 但年轻人的闲暇时间如今被音乐课和运动等有组织的活动填满。

sentences.en: Kids play soccer, Scrabble and saxophone – so why are experts worried that these activities are eating into free play?
sentences.zh: 孩子们踢足球、玩拼字游戏、吹萨克斯——那么专家为什么担心这些活动正在蚕食自由玩耍？

sentences.en: Most games are fun and sources of learning experiences – fostering group cohesion, for instance, says educational psychologist Anthony Pellegrini.
sentences.zh: 大多数游戏既好玩又是学习经验的来源——比如培养群体凝聚力，教育心理学家Anthony Pellegrini说。

sentences.en: But, Pellegrini explains, “games have predetermined rules – set up in advance and followed.
sentences.zh: 但是，Pellegrini解释说，“游戏有预先设定的规则——事先制定并遵守。

sentences.en: Play, on the other hand, does not have rules, so affords more creative responses.
sentences.zh: 而玩耍则没有规则，因此带来更具创造性的反应。

sentences.en: Children initiate and create free play, and use their imagination to try out new activities and roles.”
sentences.zh: 孩子们发起并创造自由玩耍，运用他们的想象去尝试新的活动和角色。”

sentences.en: B Perhaps most crucially, play helps us develop strong social skills.
sentences.zh: 也许最关键的是，玩耍帮助我们发展强大的社交技能。

sentences.en: “You don't become socially competent via teachers telling you how to behave,” Pellegrini says.
sentences.zh: “你不会因为老师告诉你该如何举止就变得善于社交，”Pellegrini说。

sentences.en: “Kids learn those skills by interacting with peers, learning what is and isn't acceptable.
sentences.zh: “孩子们通过与同龄人互动、了解什么可以接受什么不可以来学会那些技能。

sentences.en: They want this thing to keep going, so they're willing to ‘go the extra mile' to accommodate their playmates' desires.
sentences.zh: 他们想让这件事继续下去，所以他们愿意‘多付出一些’来迁就玩伴的愿望。

sentences.en: Keeping things friendly requires communication – arguably the most valuable social skill of all.
sentences.zh: 维持友好需要沟通——可以说是所有社交技能中最有价值的。

sentences.en: Play among peers is the most important in this regard.”
sentences.zh: 在这方面，同龄人之间的玩耍最为重要。”

sentences.en: Studies show that children use more sophisticated language when playing with other children than when playing with adults.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，孩子和其他孩子玩耍时，比和成年人玩耍时使用更复杂的语言。

sentences.en: In pretend play, for instance, they have to communicate about something that's not physically present, so they have to use complicated language to communicate what it is that they're trying to say,” Pellegrini explains.
sentences.zh: 比如在假装游戏中，他们必须就一件实际不在场的东西进行交流，所以他们得用复杂的语言来传达他们想说的究竟是什么，”Pellegrini解释道。

sentences.en: C If play helps children become socialized, then lack of play should impede social development – and research suggests that it does.
sentences.zh: 如果玩耍帮助孩子社会化，那么缺乏玩耍就应该阻碍社会发展——而研究表明确实如此。

sentences.en: A study of children in Michigan revealed that kids who enrolled in play-oriented preschools were more socially adjusted later in life – and less likely to commit a felony or be suspended from work – than kids who attended play-free preschools where they were constantly instructed by teachers.
sentences.zh: 一项对密歇根州儿童的研究显示，相比那些上以玩耍为导向幼儿园的孩子比那些上不玩耍、被老师不断指导的幼儿园的孩子，前者日后社会适应更好——也更不容易犯重罪或被停职。

sentences.en: D A 2003 study even suggests that play promotes emotional and social development in animals.
sentences.zh: 2003年的一项研究甚至表明，玩耍能促进动物的情感和社会发展。

sentences.en: Researchers allowed thirteen rats to play freely with companions for three and a half days, and kept fourteen others isolated for the same period.
sentences.zh: 研究人员让十三只大鼠和同伴自由玩耍三天半，并把另外十四只隔离同样长的时间。

sentences.en: Examination revealed that the brains of the rats which had played contained much higher levels of BDNF – a protein that stimulates the growth of new neurons – than those of the animals that had not.
sentences.zh: 检查显示，玩耍过的大鼠大脑里所含的BDNF——一种刺激新神经元生长的蛋白质——水平比没玩耍过的动物高得多。

sentences.en: “I think play is the major mechanism whereby higher regions of the brain get socialized,” says neuroscientist Jaak Panksepp, who co-authored the study.
sentences.zh: “我觉得玩耍是大脑较高区域得以社会化的主要机制，”共同撰写该研究的神经科学家Jaak Panksepp说。

sentences.en: E Research also suggests that imaginative play is critical for children's emotional health, as it enables them to work through anxiety.
sentences.zh: 研究还表明，富有想象力的玩耍对孩子的情感健康至关重要，因为它使他们能够化解焦虑。

sentences.en: In a 1984 study, researchers assessed the anxiety levels of seventy-four children on their first day of preschool.
sentences.zh: 在1984年的一项研究中，研究人员评估了七十四名儿童入园第一天的焦虑水平。

sentences.en: They labeled each child as either “anxious” or “not anxious”, then randomly split the kids into groups.
sentences.zh: 他们把每个孩子标为“焦虑”或“不焦虑”，然后把孩子随机分组。

sentences.en: Half were escorted to rooms full of toys, where they played for 15 minutes; the other half listened to a teacher tell a story for 15 minutes.
sentences.zh: 一半被带到满是玩具的房间，在那里玩15分钟；另一半听老师讲15分钟故事。

sentences.en: Afterward, their levels were assessed again.
sentences.zh: 之后，再次评估他们的水平。

sentences.en: The anxiety levels of the anxious kids who had played had dropped by more than twice as much compared with the anxious kids who had listened to the story.
sentences.zh: 玩耍过的焦虑孩子的焦虑水平，相比听故事的焦虑孩子，下降幅度超过两倍。

sentences.en: F Results of animal studies support these views.
sentences.zh: 动物研究的结果支持这些观点。

sentences.en: In 2008, neuroscientist Stephen Siviy put rats into a chamber and exposed them to a collar previously worn by a cat, making them visibly anxious.
sentences.zh: 2008年，神经科学家Stephen Siviy把大鼠放进一个箱子，让它们接触一只之前被猫戴过的颈圈，使它们明显焦虑。

sentences.en: Later, the chamber was cleaned to remove the cat odor, and the rats were put back without the collar.
sentences.zh: 后来，箱子被清洗以去除猫的气味，大鼠在没有颈圈的情况下被放回去。

sentences.en: They immediately became anxious again, probably because they associated the space with the cat.
sentences.zh: 它们立刻又变得焦虑，大概是因为它们把这个空间和猫联系了起来。

sentences.en: The researchers then introduced another rat – one that had never been exposed to the collar and was not afraid – and it began playing with one of the rats.
sentences.zh: 然后研究人员引入另一只大鼠——一只从未接触过颈圈、不害怕的大鼠——它开始和其中一只大鼠玩耍。

sentences.en: “Shortly thereafter, the first rat relaxed and became calm,” says Siviy, “suggesting that play helped lessen its anxiety.”
sentences.zh: “此后不久，第一只大鼠就放松下来、平静了，”Siviy说，“这表明玩耍有助于减轻它的焦虑。”

sentences.en: G Play even appears to make kids smarter.
sentences.zh: 玩耍甚至似乎让孩子更聪明。

sentences.en: In a classic study, researchers told a group of preschool children to play freely with some common objects such as paper towels, a screwdriver, a wooden board and paper clips.
sentences.zh: 在一项经典研究中，研究人员让一组学龄前儿童自由玩耍一些常见物品，比如纸巾、螺丝刀、一块木板和回形针。

sentences.en: Another group was asked to imitate an experimenter using the objects in common ways.
sentences.zh: 另一组被要求模仿一名实验人员以常见方式使用这些物品。

sentences.en: A third set was told to sit and draw whatever they wanted, without seeing the objects.
sentences.zh: 第三组被告知坐下随便画他们想画的，不看那些物品。

sentences.en: After 10 minutes, the researchers asked the children to come up with ideas for how one of the objects could be used.
sentences.zh: 10分钟后，研究人员请孩子们想出其中一件物品可以怎么用的点子。

sentences.en: The kids who had played with the objects named, on average, three times as many nonstandard, creative uses for the objects as those in either of the other two groups did, suggesting that play fosters imaginative thinking.
sentences.zh: 玩过这些物品的孩子平均说出的非标准、创造性用法是另外两组中任一组的三倍，这表明玩耍能培养富有想象力的思维。

sentences.en: H A later animal study produced similar results.
sentences.zh: 后来一项动物研究产生了类似的结果。

sentences.en: Experimenters isolated young rats during the development period when they would have most frequently played.
sentences.zh: 实验人员在幼鼠本会最频繁玩耍的发育期把它们隔离。

sentences.en: The researchers taught these rats, and a group that had been allowed to play without constraints, to pull a rubber ball out of the way to get a food treat.
sentences.zh: 研究人员教这些大鼠、以及一组被允许不受约束玩耍的大鼠，把一个橡皮球拉开以得到一份食物奖励。

sentences.en: A few days later they switched the setup so the rats would have to push the same ball to get the treat.
sentences.zh: 几天后，他们调换了设置，使大鼠必须推同一个球才能得到奖励。

sentences.en: Compared with the isolated rats, the ones which had played proved to be far more adept at solving problems.
sentences.zh: 与被隔离的大鼠相比，玩耍过的大鼠被证明在解决问题上要熟练得多。

sentences.en: “Play is like a kaleidoscope,” says evolutionary biologist Marc Bekoff, “in that it is random and creative.
sentences.zh: “玩耍就像万花筒，”进化生物学家Marc Bekoff说，“因为它既随机又有创造性。

sentences.en: It encourages flexibility and creativity that may, in the future, be advantageous in unexpected situations or new environments.
sentences.zh: 它鼓励灵活性和创造力，这在未来意外的情形或新环境中可能是有利的。

sentences.en: And in the absence of play, children miss vital learning experiences.”
sentences.zh: 而在没有玩耍的情况下，孩子会错过至关重要的学习经验。”

records.title: Should we stop eating meat
records.titleZh: 我们是否应该停止吃肉

sentences.en: A The call for people to eat less meat to save the planet is growing louder, so if less is good, wouldn't none be better?
sentences.zh: 要人们为拯救地球而少吃肉的呼声越来越高，那么，如果少吃是好事，一点不吃岂不更好？

sentences.en: To find out, let's imagine what would happen if the world eliminated meat, milk and eggs from its diet, then trace the effects.
sentences.zh: 为了弄清这一点，让我们设想一下，如果全世界把肉、奶和蛋从饮食中剔除会发生什么，然后追溯由此产生的影响。

sentences.en: Last year the world consumed 289 million tonnes of meat, 700 million tonnes of milk and 1.2 billion eggs.
sentences.zh: 去年，全世界消费了2.89亿吨肉、7亿吨奶和12亿枚蛋。

sentences.en: Environmentally speaking, this came at an enormous cost.
sentences.zh: 从环境角度说，这付出了极其高昂的代价。

sentences.en: B All agriculture damages the environment.
sentences.zh: 一切农业都会损害环境。

sentences.en: Take for example the felled forests and the common use of irrigation systems.
sentences.zh: 以被砍伐的森林和灌溉系统的普遍使用为例。

sentences.en: And it may surprise you to know that agriculture creates more greenhouse gases than all methods of transport put together.
sentences.zh: 而且你也许会惊讶地得知，农业所产生的温室气体，比所有交通方式加在一起还要多。

sentences.en: Livestock farming does the most damage.
sentences.zh: 畜牧养殖造成的损害最大。

sentences.en: In part, that is because most livestock eat grain that could be used to feed human populations, and farmers are forced to grow more than we would otherwise need to meet the demand.
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于，大多数牲畜吃的谷物本可以用来养活人类，而农民为满足需求，被迫种出比我们本来所需更多的粮食。

sentences.en: Altogether, if we switched to a vegan diet, meaning no meat, dairy or eggs, the land currently required for crops would drop by an estimated 21 per cent, about 3.4 million hectares, roughly the size of India.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，如果我们改吃纯素，即不吃肉、奶制品或蛋，目前种植作物所需的土地估计会减少21%，约340万公顷，大致相当于印度那么大。

sentences.en: C One environmental impact that would also lessen through a reduction in animal farming would be that of the nitrogen emitted from agricultural processes, which spreads into both waterways and land.
sentences.zh: 通过减少畜牧养殖也会减轻的一项环境影响，是农业生产过程中排放的氮，它会扩散到水道和土地之中。

sentences.en: According to environmental scientist Allison Leach, if everyone eliminated dairy products and eggs, this kind of pollution would fall by 60%.
sentences.zh: 据环境科学家艾莉森·利奇所言，如果人人都不吃奶制品和蛋，这类污染将下降60%。

sentences.en: Livestock production has another serious environmental impact.
sentences.zh: 畜牧业生产还有另一项严重的环境影响。

sentences.en: Global statistics are hard to come by, but in the US at least, livestock account for 55% of erosion, mostly from forests being cut down to make way for grazing land.
sentences.zh: 全球数据很难获得，但至少在美国，水土流失的55%要归因于牲畜，这主要是由于森林被砍伐以腾出放牧用地。

sentences.en: On top of this, half of all antibiotics manufactured are fed to livestock as part of their normal diet, a practice that is leading to drug-resistant bacteria.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，所生产的全部抗生素中有一半作为牲畜日常饮食的一部分被喂给了它们，这种做法正在导致耐药细菌的出现。

sentences.en: D A meat-free world, then would be greener in many ways.
sentences.zh: 那么，一个无肉的世界在许多方面都会更环保。

sentences.en: However, if everyone opted to give up meat there would be significant costs too.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果人人都选择放弃吃肉，也会有可观的代价。

sentences.en: For most of human history, livestock grazed on land that wasn't suitable for ploughing, and in doing so they converted inedible grass into edible meat and milk.
sentences.zh: 在人类历史的大部分时间里，牲畜在不适宜耕作的土地上吃草，并在这一过程中把不可食用的草转化为可食用的肉和奶。

sentences.en: Even today, a flock of sheep or goats can be the most efficient way to get food from marginal land.
sentences.zh: 即便在今天，一群绵羊或山羊也可能是从贫瘠土地上获取食物的最高效方式。

sentences.en: In a world in which over a billion people do not have enough to eat, using this land for crop production would contribute to food insecurity.
sentences.zh: 在一个有十多亿人吃不饱饭的世界里，把这类土地用于种植作物会加剧粮食不安全。

sentences.en: E In some parts of the world today, livestock like chickens, for instance, can subsist on leftovers and whatever they find.
sentences.zh: 如今在世界的某些地方，像鸡这样的牲畜可以靠残羹剩饭以及它们找到的任何东西维生。

sentences.en: Tara Garnett, who heads the Food Climate Research Network at the University of Surrey, points out the usefulness of these animals.
sentences.zh: 执掌萨里大学食物气候研究网络的塔拉·加内特，指出了这些动物的有用之处。

sentences.en: By giving them your leftovers, she says, they deal with your rubbish, and you get meat.
sentences.zh: 她说，把你的剩饭剩菜喂给它们，它们就帮你处理了垃圾，而你也得到了肉。

sentences.en: Garnett admits, though, that if this kind of approach were generally adopted, it would require a major adjustment in food preferences; people would have to get used to chicken, for example, with less fat.
sentences.zh: 不过加内特承认，如果这种做法被普遍采用，将需要食物偏好的一次重大调整；比方说，人们将不得不习惯脂肪更少的鸡肉。

sentences.en: F Another downside to a meat-free world would be the disappearance of animal by- products.
sentences.zh: 一个无肉世界的另一个弊端，是动物副产品的消失。

sentences.en: Such a world would have to replace the 11 million tonnes of leather and 2 million tonnes of wool that come annually from livestock farming and which are turned into clothing.
sentences.zh: 这样一个世界将不得不替代每年来自畜牧养殖、被加工成衣物的1100万吨皮革和200万吨羊毛。

sentences.en: Furthermore, even ardent vegetarians acknowledge that dairy products and meat may be a good thing in poorer countries.
sentences.zh: 此外，就连最坚定的素食者也承认，在较贫穷的国家，奶制品和肉也许是件好事。

sentences.en: 'Whilst there's no doubt that considerable reduction of meat consumption would have an environmental benefit, we do have to be careful about saying it would be the best solution if the whole world went vegetarian,' says Annette Pinner, chief executive of the UK Vegetarian Society.
sentences.zh: “尽管毫无疑问，大幅减少肉类消费会带来环境上的好处，但我们确实必须谨慎，不要说如果全世界都吃素就会是最佳解决方案，”英国素食协会的首席执行官安妮特·平纳说。

sentences.en: For many of the world's poorest rural residents, an animal may represent their only realistic hope for a little extra income, and a little animal protein can make a big difference to a marginal diet.
sentences.zh: 对世界上许多最贫穷的农村居民来说，一头牲畜也许代表着他们获得一点额外收入的唯一现实指望，而一点点动物蛋白，就能让一份勉强糊口的饮食大不相同。

sentences.en: G What if we decided on a no-meat vegetarian diet, rather than a vegan diet?
sentences.zh: 如果我们决定采用无肉的素食、而非纯素饮食，又会怎样呢？

sentences.en: After all, milk and eggs are very efficient ways of producing animal calories.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，奶和蛋是生产动物热量非常高效的方式。

sentences.en: 'It's difficult to switch to a no-meat-but-milk diet,' says Helmut Haberl, a social ecologist.
sentences.zh: “要改为一种不吃肉但喝奶的饮食是很难的，”社会生态学家赫尔穆特·哈伯尔说。

sentences.en: 'Dairy cows must calve every year to keep producing milk, and only half their offspring will be female.
sentences.zh: “奶牛必须每年产犊才能持续产奶，而它们的后代只有一半是雌性。

sentences.en: While many vegetarians see moral reasons not to kill and eat the males, there is surely no practical reason to waste so much meat.'
sentences.zh: 尽管许多素食者出于道德理由不愿宰杀和食用雄性，但要浪费这么多肉，肯定没有什么实际的道理。”

sentences.en: Similar arguments apply to chickens kept for eggs.
sentences.zh: 类似的论点也适用于为产蛋而饲养的鸡。

sentences.en: H So even though a meat-free world sounds good on paper, it is likely that a utopian future will still have some animal products in it.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管一个无肉的世界在纸面上听起来不错，但一个乌托邦式的未来很可能仍会含有一些动物产品。

sentences.en: The real questions, then, are how much meat do we want, and how will we produce it?
sentences.zh: 那么，真正的问题是：我们想要多少肉，以及我们将如何生产它？

sentences.en: The answers depend on how you approach these questions.
sentences.zh: 答案取决于你如何看待这些问题。

sentences.en: The most straightforward approach is to assume that the world will continue to want evermore meat.
sentences.zh: 最直截了当的看法是假定，世界将继续想要越来越多的肉。

sentences.en: The United Nations' best guess is that by 2050, the world will need to more than double its production of meat, an increase that would be environmentally disastrous.
sentences.zh: 联合国最乐观的预测是，到2050年，世界肉类产量将需要增加一倍以上，而这样的增长在环境上将是灾难性的。

sentences.en: I Under this scenario the goal will have to be producing the most meat at the lowest environmental cost.
sentences.zh: 在这种情形下，目标将不得不是以最低的环境代价生产出最多的肉。

sentences.en: According to Walter Falcon, an agricultural economist, this means fewer free range cattle and sheep in green fields.
sentences.zh: 据农业经济学家沃尔特·法尔孔所言，这意味着绿色田野里散养的牛羊会更少。

sentences.en: 'If you're going to keep some livestock systems, I think the ones you'll want to keep are the intensive ones,' he says.
sentences.zh: “如果你打算保留一些畜牧体系，我认为你会想保留的是集约化的那些，”他说。

sentences.en: Of course this does not take into account animal welfare issues, as intensive farming usually means poor living conditions and the use of growth hormones.
sentences.zh: 当然，这并没有把动物福利问题考虑在内，因为集约化养殖通常意味着恶劣的生存条件和生长激素的使用。

sentences.en: (A) Do you think you're a master of multi-tasking?
sentences.zh: 你觉得自己是多任务处理的高手吗？

sentences.en: Think again.
sentences.zh: 再想想吧。

sentences.en: Unless you are one of the three percent of super-taskers in the population, research shows that your brain isn't capable of paying close attention to more than one complex task at a time.
sentences.zh: 除非你是人群中那百分之三的超级任务者，否则研究表明，你的大脑无法在同一时间密切关注一个以上的复杂任务。

sentences.en: Researchers who study attention say that effective multi-tasking is beyond most of us.
sentences.zh: 研究注意力的研究人员说，有效的多任务处理是我们大多数人做不到的。

sentences.en: Psychiatrist Edward M Hallowell even describes multi-tasking as 'a mythical activity in which people believe they can perform two or more tasks simultaneously as effectively as they can perform one'.
sentences.zh: 精神病学家Edward M Hallowell甚至把多任务处理描述为“一种虚构的活动，人们在其中相信自己能像处理一项任务那样有效地同时处理两项或更多任务”。

sentences.en: (B) It is true that you can check your email while eating your lunch, or listen to music while walking.
sentences.zh: 你确实可以一边吃午饭一边查邮件，或一边听音乐一边走路。

sentences.en: But innate activities like walking, chewing, and breathing do not require you to pay attention, whereas activities such as reading, tapping out a text message, or driving a car do require attention.
sentences.zh: 但走路、咀嚼和呼吸等与生俱来的活动不需要你去注意，而阅读、敲打短信或开车之类的活动则确实需要注意。

sentences.en: Why is paying attention to two things at once difficult?
sentences.zh: 为什么同时注意两件事很难？

sentences.en: 'The brain can perform simultaneous tasks, but attention has capacity limitations,' says Associate Professor Paul E Dux, a cognitive neuroscientist at the University of Queensland in Australia.
sentences.zh: “大脑能执行同时进行的任务，但注意力有容量上的限制，”澳大利亚昆士兰大学的认知神经科学家、副教授Paul E Dux说。

sentences.en: When you do only one thing at a time, you're better at that task than when you're doing multiple things concurrently.
sentences.zh: 当你一次只做一件事时，你在那件任务上做得比你同时做多件事时更好。

sentences.en: Take the classic multi-tasking scenario of talking on a mobile phone while driving - an ill-advised activity that many people believe they have mastered.
sentences.zh: 以一边开车一边用手机通话这个经典的多任务情景为例——许多人相信自己已经掌握的一种不明智的活动。

sentences.en: When David Strayer, Professor of Psychology at the University of Utah in the US, and his team observed 56,000 drivers as they approached an intersection, the majority of drivers who were talking on their phone failed to stop in accordance with traffic laws.
sentences.zh: 当美国犹他大学的心理学教授David Strayer和他的团队观察56000名司机驶近一个路口时，大多数正在通话的司机没能按交通法规停车。

sentences.en: And it did not matter if the driver was using a handheld or hands-free device.
sentences.zh: 而且司机用的是手持还是免提设备都没有区别。

sentences.en: Even with both eyes on the road and both hands on the wheel, drivers' performance was impaired.
sentences.zh: 即便双眼都盯着路、双手都握着方向盘，司机的表现也受到了损害。

sentences.en: Strayer's research shows that performance deteriorates drastically when attention is split between tasks: more mistakes are made and it takes longer to complete each activity.
sentences.zh: Strayer的研究表明，当注意力被分到多个任务之间时，表现会急剧恶化，会犯更多错误，完成每项活动也要花更长时间。

sentences.en: (C) The prefrontal cortex is the brain region responsible for choosing what to pay attention to, and for coordinating inputs from other brain areas.
sentences.zh: 前额叶皮层是负责选择注意什么、并协调来自大脑其他区域输入的脑区。

sentences.en: By scanning the prefrontal cortex of people while they multi-tasked, scientists at the French Institute of Health and Medical Research in Paris (INSERM) found that when people focused on a single thing, the right and left sides of the prefrontal cortex work together.
sentences.zh: 通过扫描人们在多任务处理时的前额叶皮层，巴黎法国健康与医学研究所（INSERM）的科学家发现，当人们专注于单一一件事时，前额叶皮层的左右两侧协同工作。

sentences.en: But when people attempt to perform two things at once, the sides work independently.
sentences.zh: 但当人们试图同时做两件事时，两侧会各自独立工作。

sentences.en: Neuroscientist Etienne Koechlin says his study demonstrates that while the brain can switch back and forth between two tasks, we might be in great trouble when we try to juggle more than two tasks, simply because we have only two frontal lobes'.
sentences.zh: 神经科学家Etienne Koechlin说，他的研究表明，虽然大脑能在两个任务之间来回切换，但当我们试图同时应付两个以上的任务时，我们可能会陷入大麻烦，原因很简单，因为我们只有两个额叶。

sentences.en: (D) To the question of whether there is a difference between the sexes, Koechlin's imaging studies uncovered no differences in the ability to switch between tasks in the prefrontal cortices of men or women.
sentences.zh: 关于两性之间是否有差异这个问题，Koechlin的成像研究没有发现男性或女性前额叶皮层在任务间切换能力上的差异。

sentences.en: But other researchers studying real life scenarios such as finding lost keys, believe there might be some truth to the claim that women are superior multi-taskers.
sentences.zh: 但其他研究现实生活情景（比如找丢失的钥匙）的研究人员相信，女性是更出色的多任务者这一说法可能有一定道理。

sentences.en: Women have a much better strategy for finding the keys, whereas men tend to jump to it and be far less organised and thorough.
sentences.zh: 女性有一套好得多的找钥匙策略，而男性往往一下子就上手，远不那么有条理、不那么周到。

sentences.en: 'It's as if they don't stop to reflect and plan for a moment,' says Professor Keith Laws from the University of Hertfordshire in England.
sentences.zh: “就好像他们不停下来反思和片刻规划一样，”英格兰赫特福德大学的Keith Laws教授说。

sentences.en: But while the ability to develop strategies for coping with the numerous tasks in everyday life could give women an advantage, 'nobody can juggle two, never mind three, "complex" tasks at the same time.'
sentences.zh: 但是，尽管制定策略来应付日常生活中众多任务的能力可能给女性带来优势，“没有人能同时应付两个、更别说三个‘复杂’任务。”

sentences.en: (E) However, David Strayer's research uncovered that some rare people possess extraordinary multi-tasking ability.
sentences.zh: 然而，David Strayer的研究发现，有些罕见的人拥有非凡的多任务能力。

sentences.en: These so-called 'super-taskers' exhibit different patterns of brain activity when multi-tasking compared to ordinary people: they show less activity in the prefrontal cortex during multi-tasking, suggesting their brains are functioning with a high level of efficiency.
sentences.zh: 这些所谓的“超级任务者”在多任务处理时表现出与普通人不同的大脑活动模式，他们在多任务处理期间前额叶皮层的活动更少，这表明他们的大脑正以很高的效率运转。

sentences.en: Strayer thinks that pilots of high-performance aircraft, high-end chefs who can cook several meals at the same time to perfection, and elite doctors in hospital emergency rooms might all be more likely to be super-taskers.
sentences.zh: Strayer认为，高性能飞机的飞行员、能同时把好几道菜都做到完美的高端厨师，以及医院急诊室里的精英医生，可能都更有可能是超级任务者。

sentences.en: "All other things being equal, we suspect that super-taskers will rise to a top position in any occupation that places a high demand on juggling various tasks that demand attention at the same time.'
sentences.zh: “在其他条件相同的情况下，我们推测在任何对同时应付各种需要注意的任务要求很高的职业里，超级任务者都会上升到顶尖位置。”

sentences.en: (F) The ability to multi-task probably comes down to the DNA you inherit from your parents to a large extent, says Strayer.
sentences.zh: 多任务的能力很大程度上大概取决于你从父母那里遗传的DNA，Strayer说。

sentences.en: 'You are either born with the neural structure that allows you to overcome the usual multi-tasking challenges, or you aren't.
sentences.zh: “你要么生来就有让你能克服通常多任务挑战的神经结构，要么没有。

sentences.en: Super-taskers' brains are doing something we can't do.'
sentences.zh: 超级任务者的大脑正在做我们做不到的事。”

sentences.en: All in all, these findings may have very real consequences on our lives.
sentences.zh: 总而言之，这些发现可能对我们的生活有非常实际的影响。

records.title: The conquest of malaria in Italy
records.titleZh: 意大利战胜疟疾的历程

sentences.en: A The word 'malaria' means 'bad air' in Italian, and this terrible disease marked the life of the people of that country for thousands of years.
sentences.zh: “malaria”一词在意大利语中意为“坏空气”，这种可怕的疾病数千年来在那个国家人民的生活上留下了印记。

sentences.en: Yet by 1962, Italy was officially declared malaria-free, and it has remained so ever since.
sentences.zh: 然而到1962年，意大利被正式宣布无疟疾，并从此一直如此。

sentences.en: Frank Snowden's study of this successful endeavour is a remarkable piece of historical work.
sentences.zh: Frank Snowden对这一成功努力的研究是一部了不起的历史著作。

sentences.en: Original, crystal clear, analytical and passionate, Snowden takes us to areas historians have rarely visited before.
sentences.zh: 这部著作原创、清澈、富于分析又饱含热情，Snowden带我们去到历史学家此前很少涉足的领域。

sentences.en: B Everybody now knows that malaria is carried by mosquitoes.
sentences.zh: 现在每个人都知道疟疾是由蚊子传播的。

sentences.en: But in the 19th century most experts subscribed to the theory of 'miasma' or 'poisoning of the air'.
sentences.zh: 但在19世纪，大多数专家都赞同“瘴气”或“空气中毒”的理论。

sentences.en: Others made a link between swamps, water and malaria, but did not make the further leap towards insects.
sentences.zh: 另一些人把沼泽、水和疟疾联系起来，但没有进一步跳跃到昆虫上。

sentences.en: The consequence of these theories was that little was done to combat the disease before the end of that century.
sentences.zh: 这些理论的后果是，在那个世纪末之前几乎没有采取什么措施来对抗这种疾病。

sentences.en: The situation was so serious that from a total population of 25m Italians, 11m were 'permanently at risk'.
sentences.zh: 情况如此严重，以至于在意大利总共2500万人口中，有1100万人“长期处于风险中”。

sentences.en: In warm, damp, malarial zones, the life expectancy of land workers was a terrifying 22.5 years.
sentences.zh: 在温暖、潮湿的疟疾区，土地劳作者的预期寿命是骇人的22.5岁。

sentences.en: The economic impact of the disease was immense.
sentences.zh: 这种疾病的经济影响是巨大的。

sentences.en: Epidemics were blamed on people who originated from the hotter parts of Italy, given the widespread belief that malaria was hereditary.
sentences.zh: 鉴于疟疾会遗传这一普遍信念，疫情被归咎于来自意大利较热地区的人。

sentences.en: C One of the first breakthroughs in the war against malaria came in 1898 when the zoologist Giovanni Battista Grassi demonstrated that the micro-organisms causing the disease were carried in the digestive tract of the mosquito.
sentences.zh: 抗击疟疾战争中最早的突破之一发生在1898年，当时动物学家Giovanni Battista Grassi证明，引起这种疾病的微生物携带在蚊子的消化道里。

sentences.en: By releasing mosquitoes into rooms to drink the blood of healthy human volunteers, Grassi was able to make the direct link between the insects and the disease.
sentences.zh: 通过把蚊子放进房间去吸健康人类志愿者的血，Grassi得以在昆虫与疾病之间建立直接的联系。

sentences.en: Definitive proof of this theory was obtained after an extraordinary series of experiments in Italy, where healthy people were introduced into malarial zones but kept free of mosquito bites – and remained well.
sentences.zh: 在意大利进行了一系列非凡的实验之后，这一理论得到了确凿的证明，实验中健康的人被带入疟疾区，但不被蚊子叮咬——结果都保持健康。

sentences.en: The recently formed Italian state at last had the necessary information to begin tackling the disease.
sentences.zh: 新近成立的意大利国家终于有了开始着手对付这种疾病所需的信息。

sentences.en: D A complicated approach was adopted, which made use of quinine – a drug obtained from tree bark which had long been used to combat fever, but was now seen as a crucial part of the war on malaria.
sentences.zh: 人们采取了一种复杂的方法，利用奎宁——一种从树皮中获得、长期用来对抗发热的药物，如今被视为抗疟战争的关键部分。

sentences.en: Italy introduced a quinine law and a quinine tax in 1904, and the drug was administered to large numbers of rural workers.
sentences.zh: 意大利在1904年推出了奎宁法和奎宁税，这种药被发放给大量的农村劳作者。

sentences.en: Despite its often terrible side effects, the drug was successful in limiting the spread of the disease, and in breaking cycles of infection.
sentences.zh: 尽管常有可怕的副作用，这种药在限制疾病传播、打破感染循环上是成功的。

sentences.en: In addition, Italy set up rural health centres and invested heavily in education programmes.
sentences.zh: 此外，意大利建立了农村卫生中心，并在教育项目上大量投资。

sentences.en: Malaria, as Snowden shows, was not just a medical problem, but a social and regional issue, and could only be defeated through multi-layered strategies.
sentences.zh: 正如Snowden所示，疟疾不只是个医学问题，而是个社会和地区性问题，只能通过多层次的策略来战胜。

sentences.en: E It was originally decided to give quinine to all those in vulnerable regions – even healthy people.
sentences.zh: 最初决定给易感地区的所有人——甚至健康的人——发奎宁。

sentences.en: However, peasants were often suspicious of medicine being forced upon them, and doctors were frequently met with hostility and stubborn refusal to accept the treatment offered.
sentences.zh: 然而，农民往往对被强加的药物心存疑虑，医生常常遭遇敌意和对所提供治疗顽固的拒绝。

sentences.en: But despite the refusals, the strategy as a whole was hugely successful.
sentences.zh: 但尽管有这些拒绝，整体策略仍极为成功。

sentences.en: Deaths from malaria fell by some 80% in the first decade of the 20th century and some areas escaped altogether from the scourge of the disease.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪头十年，疟疾死亡人数下降了约80%，一些地区彻底摆脱了这种疾病的祸害。

sentences.en: F The 1915-18 war delayed the campaign, as funds were diverted to the battlefields.
sentences.zh: 1915到1918年的战争延误了这场运动，因为资金被转向了战场。

sentences.en: In the 1920s and 1930s the draining of the damp, unhealthy marshlands around Rome had a certain impact on the spread of malaria.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪20和30年代，排干罗马周围潮湿、不卫生的沼泽地对疟疾的传播有一定影响。

sentences.en: However, as war swept through the drained lands in the 1940s, the disease returned with a vengeance.
sentences.zh: 然而，随着战争在20世纪40年代席卷这些被排干的土地，这种疾病卷土重来、来势汹汹。

sentences.en: Yet the country's leading malariologist Alberto Missiroli refused to order the distribution of quinine, so allowing the epidemic to spread unchecked.
sentences.zh: 然而，该国首席疟疾学家Alberto Missiroli拒绝下令发放奎宁，从而任由疫情不受遏制地蔓延。

sentences.en: According to Snowden, he did this in order to create the ideal conditions for a new strategy, supported by the US Rockefeller Foundation – a massive experiment involving the extermination of mosquitoes with the chemical DDT.
sentences.zh: 据Snowden说，他这么做是为了给一项由美国洛克菲勒基金会支持的新策略创造理想条件——一项用化学品DDT灭蚊的大规模实验。

sentences.en: It is estimated that more than a third of the inhabitants in the affected area contracted malaria and countless thousands died.
sentences.zh: 据估计，受影响地区超过三分之一的居民感染了疟疾，无数千计的人死亡。

sentences.en: G With the end of the war in 1945, the US government and the Rockefeller Foundation were free to experiment.
sentences.zh: 随着1945年战争结束，美国政府和洛克菲勒基金会可以自由地做实验了。

sentences.en: DDT was sprayed from the air, and 3m Italians had their bodies covered with the chemical.
sentences.zh: DDT从空中喷洒，300万意大利人的身体被这种化学品覆盖。

sentences.en: The effects were immense, and by 1962 malaria was more or less gone from the whole country.
sentences.zh: 效果是巨大的，到1962年疟疾或多或少已从整个国家消失。

sentences.en: One of the final victims to die of the disease in Italy was the popular cyclist, Fausto Coppi.
sentences.zh: 意大利死于这种疾病的最后受害者之一是受欢迎的自行车手Fausto Coppi。

sentences.en: He had contracted malaria in Africa in 1960, and the failure of doctors in Italy to spot the disease was a sign of the times.
sentences.zh: 他于1960年在非洲感染了疟疾，意大利的医生未能发现这种疾病，是时代的一个标志。

sentences.en: A few decades earlier, they would have immediately noticed the telltale signs; it was later claimed that a small dose of quinine would have saved his life.
sentences.zh: 几十年前，他们本会立刻注意到那些显露的迹象；后来有人声称，一小剂量奎宁本可以救他的命。

sentences.en: H As there are still more than 1m deaths every year from malaria worldwide, Snowden's book also has contemporary relevance.
sentences.zh: 由于全世界每年仍有超过100万人死于疟疾，Snowden的书也有当代意义。

sentences.en: This is a disease that affects every level of the societies where it is rampant.
sentences.zh: 这是一种影响其肆虐社会各个阶层的疾病。

sentences.en: The economic miracle of the 1950s and 1960s which made Italy into a modern industrial nation would not have been possible without the eradication of malaria.
sentences.zh: 使意大利成为现代工业国家的20世纪50和60年代的经济奇迹，若没有疟疾的根除是不可能实现的。

sentences.en: Moreover, this book convincingly argues that the disease was 'an integral part of the big picture of modern Italian history'.
sentences.zh: 而且，这本书有力地论证了这种疾病“是现代意大利历史大局不可分割的一部分”。

sentences.en: This magnificent study, beautifully written and impeccably documented, deserves an audience beyond specialists in history, or in Italy.
sentences.zh: 这部宏大的研究文笔优美、考据无可挑剔，理应拥有历史专家或意大利专家之外的读者。

sentences.en: A A plane flies a slow pattern over Carlton Hill station, a 3,600 square kilometre ranch in the Kimberley region in northwest Australia.
sentences.zh: 一架飞机在Carlton Hill牧场上空缓慢地盘旋，这是澳大利亚西北部金伯利地区一座3600平方公里的牧场。

sentences.en: As the plane circles, those aboard drop 1,000 small pieces of meat, one by one, onto the scrubland below, each piece laced with poison; this practice is known as baiting.
sentences.zh: 当飞机盘旋时，机上的人把1000小块肉一块块地投到下面的灌木丛地上，每块肉都掺了毒药；这种做法被称为投饵。

sentences.en: Besides 50,000 head of cattle, Carlton Hill is home to the dingo, Australia's largest mammalian predator and the bane of a grazier's (cattle farmer's) life.
sentences.zh: 除了50000头牛，Carlton Hill还是澳大利亚野犬的家园，澳大利亚野犬是澳大利亚最大的哺乳类捕食者，也是牧牛人生活的祸根。

sentences.en: Stuart McKechnie, manager of Carlton Hill, complains that graziers' livelihoods are threatened when dingoes prey on cattle.
sentences.zh: Carlton Hill的经理Stuart McKechnie抱怨说，当野犬捕食牛时，牧牛人的生计就受到威胁。

sentences.en: But one man wants the baiting to end, and for dingoes to once again roam Australia's wide-open spaces.
sentences.zh: 但有一个人希望投饵停止、希望野犬再次漫游澳大利亚广阔的开阔地。

sentences.en: According to Chris Johnson of James Cook University, “Australia needs more dingoes to protect our biodiversity.”
sentences.zh: 据詹姆斯库克大学的Chris Johnson说，“澳大利亚需要更多野犬来保护我们的生物多样性。”

sentences.en: B About 4,000 years ago, Asian sailors introduced dingoes to Australia.
sentences.zh: 大约4000年前，亚洲的水手把野犬引入澳大利亚。

sentences.en: Throughout the ensuing millennia, these descendants of the wolf spread across the continent and, as the Tasmanian tiger disappeared completely from Australia, dingoes became Australia's top predators.
sentences.zh: 在随后的数千年里，这些狼的后代扩散到整个大陆，而随着袋狼从澳大利亚彻底消失，野犬成了澳大利亚的顶级捕食者。

sentences.en: As agricultural development took place, the European settlers found that they could not safely keep their livestock where dingoes roamed.
sentences.zh: 随着农业开发的进行，欧洲定居者发现，在野犬出没的地方无法安全地饲养牲畜。

sentences.en: So began one of the most sustained efforts at pest control in Australia's history.
sentences.zh: 于是开始了澳大利亚历史上最持久的害兽控制行动之一。

sentences.en: Over the last 150 years, dingoes have been shot and poisoned, and fences have been used in an attempt to keep them away from livestock.
sentences.zh: 在过去150年里，野犬被枪杀、被毒杀，人们还用围栏试图把它们挡在牲畜之外。

sentences.en: But at the same time, as the European settlers tried to eliminate one native pest from Australia, they introduced more of their own.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，欧洲定居者在试图从澳大利亚消灭一种本土害兽的同时，引入了更多他们自己的害兽。

sentences.en: C In 1860, the rabbit was unleashed on Australia by a wealthy landowner and by 1980 rabbits had covered most of the mainland.
sentences.zh: 1860年，一位富有的地主把兔子放到了澳大利亚，到1980年兔子已覆盖了大陆的大部分。

sentences.en: Rabbits provide huge prey base for two other introduced species: the feral (wild) cat and the red fox.
sentences.zh: 兔子为另外两种引进物种提供了巨大的猎物基础，野猫和赤狐。

sentences.en: The interaction between foxes, cats and rabbits is a huge problem for native mammals.
sentences.zh: 狐狸、猫和兔子之间的相互作用对本土哺乳动物是个巨大的问题。

sentences.en: In good years, rabbit numbers increase dramatically, and fox and cat populations grow quickly in response to the abundance of this prey.
sentences.zh: 在丰年，兔子数量急剧增加，狐狸和猫的种群随着这种猎物的丰富而迅速增长。

sentences.en: When bad seasons follow, rabbit numbers are significantly reduced – and the dwindling but still large fox and cat populations are left with little to eat besides native mammals.
sentences.zh: 当歉年随之而来，兔子数量大幅减少——而数量在减少但仍然庞大的狐狸和猫种群，除了本土哺乳动物就没什么可吃的了。

sentences.en: D Australian mammals generally reproduce much more slowly than rabbits, cats and foxes – an adaption to prevent overpopulation in the arid environment, where food can be scarce and unreliable – and populations decline because they can't grow fast enough to replace animals killed by the predators.
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚的哺乳动物繁殖速度通常比兔子、猫和狐狸慢得多——这是为防止在食物可能稀缺且不稳定的干旱环境中过度繁殖的一种适应——种群数量下降，因为它们无法快到足以替补被捕食者杀死的动物。

sentences.en: Johnson says dingoes are the solution to this problem because they keep cat and fox populations under control.
sentences.zh: Johnson说，野犬是这个问题的解决办法，因为它们能控制猫和狐狸的种群。

sentences.en: Besides regularly eating the smaller predators, dingoes will kill them simply to lessen competition.
sentences.zh: 除了经常吃掉这些较小的捕食者，野犬还会单纯为减少竞争而杀死它们。

sentences.en: Dingo packs live in large, stable territories and generally have only one fertile female, which limits their rate of increase.
sentences.zh: 野犬群生活在大而稳定的领地里，通常只有一只有繁殖力的雌性，这限制了它们的增长速度。

sentences.en: In the 4,000 years that dingoes have been Australia, they have contributed to few, if any, extinctions, Johnson says.
sentences.zh: 在野犬待在澳大利亚的4000年里，它们造成的灭绝即便有也很少，Johnson说。

sentences.en: E Reaching out from a desolate spot where three states meet, for 2,500 km in either direction, is the world's longest fence, two meters high and stretching from the coast in Queensland to the Great Australian Bight in South Australia; it is there to keep dingoes out of southeast, the fence separates the main types of livestock found in Australia.
sentences.zh: 从三个州交会的一个荒凉地点伸出，向两个方向各延伸2500公里，是世界上最长的围栏，两米高，从昆士兰的海岸一直延伸到南澳大利亚的大澳大利亚湾；它在那里是为把野犬挡在东南之外，这道围栏隔开了澳大利亚的主要牲畜类型。

sentences.en: To the northwest of the fence, cattle predominate; to the southwest, sheep fill the landscape.
sentences.zh: 围栏西北以牛为主；西南则是羊布满了大地。

sentences.en: In fact, Australia is a land dominated by these animals – 25 million cattle, 100 million sheep and just over 20 million people.
sentences.zh: 事实上，澳大利亚是一片由这些动物主导的土地——2500万头牛、1亿只羊，而人只有刚过2000万。

sentences.en: F While there is no argument that dingoes will prey on sheep if given the chance, they don't hunt cattle once the calves are much past two or three weeks old, according to McKechnie.
sentences.zh: 虽然毫无争议野犬一有机会就会捕食羊，但据McKechnie说，一旦牛犊长到过了两三周大很多，它们就不再猎牛。

sentences.en: And a study in Queensland suggests that dingoes don't even prey heavily on the newborn calves unless their staple prey disappears due to deteriorating conditions like drought.
sentences.zh: 而昆士兰的一项研究表明，除非野犬主要的猎物因干旱等恶化的条件而消失，否则它们甚至不会大量捕食新生的牛犊。

sentences.en: This study, co-authored by Lee Allen of the Robert Wicks Research Centre in Queensland, suggests that the aggressive baiting programs used against dingoes may actually be counter-productive for graziers.
sentences.zh: 这项由昆士兰Robert Wicks研究中心的Lee Allen共同撰写的研究表明，针对野犬使用的激进投饵项目，对牧牛人实际上可能适得其反。

sentences.en: When dingoes are removed from an area by baiting, the area is recolonized by younger, more solitary dingoes.
sentences.zh: 当野犬通过投饵从一个区域被清除时，这个区域会被更年轻、更独居的野犬重新占据。

sentences.en: These animals aren't capable of going after large prey like kangaroos, so they turn to calves.
sentences.zh: 这些动物没有能力去追捕袋鼠之类的大型猎物，所以它们转向牛犊。

sentences.en: In their study, some of the highest rates of calf predation occurred in areas that had been baited.
sentences.zh: 在他们的研究中，一些最高的牛犊被捕食率出现在曾被投饵的区域。

sentences.en: G Mark Clifford, general manager of a firm that manages over 200,000 head of cattle, is not convinced by Allen's assertion.
sentences.zh: 一家管理着超过200000头牛的公司的总经理Mark Clifford，并不认同Allen的论断。

sentences.en: Clifford says, “It's obvious if we drop or loosen control on dingoes, we are going to lose more calves.”
sentences.zh: Clifford说，“很明显，如果我们放弃或放松对野犬的控制，我们就会损失更多牛犊。”

sentences.en: He doesn't believe that dingoes will go after kangaroos when calves are around.
sentences.zh: 他不相信牛犊在场时野犬会去追袋鼠。

sentences.en: Nor is he persuaded of dingoes' supposed ecological benefits, saying he is not convinced that they manage to catch cats that often, believing they are more likely to catch small native animals instead.
sentences.zh: 他也不被野犬所谓的生态益处所说服，说他不相信它们那么经常能抓到猫，相信它们更可能抓到的反而是本土小动物。

sentences.en: H McKechnie agrees that dingoes kill the wallabies (small native animals) that compete with his cattle for food, but points out that in parts of Western Australia, there are no foxes, and not very many cats.
sentences.zh: McKechnie同意野犬会杀死那些与他的牛争食的小袋鼠（本土小动物），但指出在西澳大利亚的部分地区没有狐狸，猫也不太多。

sentences.en: He doesn't see how relaxing controls on dingoes in his area will improve the ecological balance.
sentences.zh: 他看不出在他那个地区放松对野犬的控制将如何改善生态平衡。

sentences.en: Johnson sees a need for a change in philosophy on the part of graziers.
sentences.zh: Johnson认为牧牛人需要在理念上有所改变。

sentences.en: “There might be a number of different ways of thinking through dingo management in cattle country,” he says.
sentences.zh: “在养牛地区，也许有若干种不同的方式来通盘考虑野犬管理，”他说。

sentences.en: “At the moment, though, that hasn't got through to graziers.
sentences.zh: “不过目前，那还没有传达给牧牛人。

sentences.en: There's still just one prescription, and that is to bait as widely as possible.”
sentences.zh: 仍然只有一个处方，那就是尽可能广泛地投饵。”

sentences.en: (A) Hacienda La Pacifica, a remote working cattle ranch in Guanacaste Province of northern Costa Rica, has for decades been home to a community of mantled howler monkeys.
sentences.zh: 哈西恩达拉帕西菲卡是哥斯达黎加北部瓜纳卡斯特省一处偏远的肉牛养殖牧场，数十年来一直是一群披风吼猴的家园。

sentences.en: Other native primates—white-faced capuchin monkeys and spider monkeys—were once common in this area too, but vanished after the Pan-American Highway was built nearby in the 1950s and most of the surrounding land was cleared for cattle-raising.
sentences.zh: 其他本地灵长类动物——白脸卷尾猴和蜘蛛猴——一度在这一带也很常见，但在20世纪50年代泛美公路在附近修建、周围大部分土地被清理出来用于养牛之后，它们便消失了。

sentences.en: At Hacienda La Pacifica, however, an enlightened ranch owner chose to leave some strips of native trees growing.
sentences.zh: 然而，在哈西恩达拉帕西菲卡，一位开明的牧场主选择留下了几条原生树木组成的林带。

sentences.en: He used these as windbreaks to protect both cattle and their food crops from dry-season winds.
sentences.zh: 他把这些林带用作防风林，保护肉牛及其饲料作物免受旱季大风的侵袭。

sentences.en: In the process, the farmer unwittingly founded a unique laboratory for the study of monkeys.
sentences.zh: 在这一过程中，这位农场主无意间为研究猴子创建了一个独特的实验室。

sentences.en: (B) Ken Glander, a primatologist from Duke University in the USA, is studying La Pacifica's monkeys in an effort to understand the relationship between howlers and regenerating forests at the edges of grazing lands.
sentences.zh: 美国杜克大学的灵长类动物学家肯·格兰德正在研究拉帕西菲卡的猴子，力图理解吼猴与放牧地边缘正在再生的森林之间的关系。

sentences.en: Studying such disturbed woodlands is increasingly important because throughout much of the New World Tropics, these are the only forests left.
sentences.zh: 研究这类受过扰动的林地越来越重要，因为在新大陆热带的大部分地区，这些已是仅存的森林。

sentences.en: In the 18th century, tropical dry forests once covered most of Central America, but by the 1980s less than two percent remained undisturbed, and less than one percent was protected.
sentences.zh: 在18世纪，热带干旱森林曾覆盖中美洲的大部分地区，但到20世纪80年代，未受扰动的不到百分之二，受到保护的不到百分之一。

sentences.en: (C) Howlers persist at La Pacifica, Glander explains, because they are leaf-eaters.
sentences.zh: 格兰德解释说，吼猴之所以能在拉帕西菲卡存续下来，是因为它们以树叶为食。

sentences.en: They eat fruit when it is available but, unlike capuchin and spider monkeys, do not depend on large areas of fruiting trees.
sentences.zh: 有果子时它们也吃果子，但与卷尾猴和蜘蛛猴不同，它们并不依赖大片的结果树木。

sentences.en: Glander is particularly interested in howlers' ability to thrive on leaves loaded with toxins—poisonous substances designed to protect the plants.
sentences.zh: 格兰德特别感兴趣的是吼猴在满是毒素——为保护植物而生的有毒物质——的树叶上茁壮生长的能力。

sentences.en: For leaf-eaters, long-term exposure to a specific plant toxin can increase their ability to neutralise the poisonous substances and absorb the leaf nutrients.
sentences.zh: 对于食叶动物来说，长期接触某种特定的植物毒素，能够增强它们中和有毒物质、吸收叶片养分的能力。

sentences.en: Watching generations of howlers at La Pacifica has shown Glander that the monkeys keep their systems primed by sampling a variety of plants and then focusing on a small number of the most nutritious food items.
sentences.zh: 观察拉帕西菲卡一代又一代的吼猴，让格兰德看到，这些猴子通过广泛尝试各种植物、然后专注于少数几种最有营养的食物，来让自己的消化系统时刻处于备战状态。

sentences.en: The leaves that grow in regenerating forests, like those at La Pacifica, are actually more howler-friendly than those produced by the centuries- old trees that survive farther south.
sentences.zh: 在像拉帕西菲卡这样正在再生的森林里生长的树叶，实际上比更南面那些存活下来的数百年老树所长出的叶子更适合吼猴食用。

sentences.en: In younger forests, trees put most of their limited energy into growing wood, leaves and fruit, so they produce much lower levels of toxin than do well-established, old-growth trees.
sentences.zh: 在较年轻的森林里，树木把有限的能量大多用于生长木质、叶片和果实，因此它们产生的毒素水平远低于那些根基稳固的原始老树。

sentences.en: (D) The value of maturing forests to primates is also a subject of study at Santa Rosa National Park, about 35 miles northwest of La Pacifica.
sentences.zh: 正在成熟的森林对灵长类动物的价值，也是圣罗莎国家公园的一个研究课题，该公园在拉帕西菲卡西北约35英里处。

sentences.en: Large areas of Santa Rosa's forests had at one time been burnt to make space for cattle ranching and coffee farming, thereby devastating local monkey habitat.
sentences.zh: 圣罗莎的大片森林曾一度被烧毁，以腾出空间用于养牛和种植咖啡，从而严重破坏了当地猴子的栖息地。

sentences.en: But in 1971 the government protected the area by designating it a national park, and species of indigenous trees which had been absent for decades began to invade the abandoned pastures.
sentences.zh: 但1971年，政府把这一地区指定为国家公园加以保护，几十年来一直绝迹的本土树种开始侵入那些被废弃的牧场。

sentences.en: Capuchins were the first to begin using the reborn forests, followed by howlers.
sentences.zh: 卷尾猴最先开始利用这些重生的森林，吼猴紧随其后。

sentences.en: Eventually, even spider monkeys, fruit-eaters that need large areas of continuous forest, returned.
sentences.zh: 最终，就连需要大片连绵森林的食果动物蜘蛛猴也回来了。

sentences.en: In the first 28 years following protection of the area, the capuchin population doubled, while the number of howlers increased seven-fold.
sentences.zh: 在该地区受保护后的头28年里，卷尾猴的数量翻了一番，而吼猴的数量则增加到原来的七倍。

sentences.en: (E) Some of the same traits that allow howlers to survive at La Pacifica also explain their population boom in Santa Rosa.
sentences.zh: 使吼猴得以在拉帕西菲卡存活下来的某些特性，同样可以解释它们在圣罗莎的数量激增。

sentences.en: Howler reproduction is faster than that of other native monkey species.
sentences.zh: 吼猴的繁殖速度比其他本地猴种都快。

sentences.en: They give birth for the first time at about 3.5 years of age, compared with seven years for capuchins, and eight or more for spider monkeys.
sentences.zh: 它们大约在3.5岁时首次产崽，相比之下，卷尾猴要到七岁，蜘蛛猴则要到八岁甚至更晚。

sentences.en: Also, while a female spider monkey will have a baby about once every four years, well-fed howlers can produce an infant every two years.
sentences.zh: 此外，雌性蜘蛛猴大约每四年才产一崽，而吃得饱的吼猴每两年就能产下一只幼崽。

sentences.en: Another factor is diet.
sentences.zh: 另一个因素是食物。

sentences.en: Howlers are very adaptable feeders and need only a comparatively small home range.
sentences.zh: 吼猴的取食适应性很强，只需要相对较小的活动范围。

sentences.en: Spider monkeys, on the other hand, need to occupy a huge home range.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，蜘蛛猴则需要占据巨大的活动范围。

sentences.en: Also crucial is the fact that the leaves howlers eat hold plenty of water, so the monkeys can survive away from open streams and water-holes.
sentences.zh: 同样关键的是这样一个事实：吼猴所吃的树叶含有大量水分，因此这些猴子即便远离开阔的溪流和水洼也能存活。

sentences.en: This ability gives them a real advantage over capuchin and spider monkeys, which have suffered during the long, ongoing drought in the area.
sentences.zh: 这种能力使它们相比卷尾猴和蜘蛛猴占据真正的优势，后两者在该地区长期持续的干旱中遭了殃。

sentences.en: (F) Alejandro Estrada, an ecologist at Estación de Biología Los Tuxtlas in Veracruz, Mexico, has been studying the ecology of a group of howler monkeys that thrive in a habitat totally altered by humans: a cacao plantation in Tabasco State, Mexico.
sentences.zh: 墨西哥韦拉克鲁斯洛斯图斯特拉斯生物站的生态学家亚历杭德罗·埃斯特拉达，一直在研究一群吼猴的生态，这群吼猴在一处被人类彻底改变的栖息地中茁壮生长：墨西哥塔巴斯科州的一处可可种植园。

sentences.en: Cacao plants need shade to grow, so 40 years ago the owners of Cholula Cacao Farm planted figs, monkey-pod and other tall trees to form a protective canopy over their crop.
sentences.zh: 可可植株需要遮阴才能生长，因此40年前，乔卢拉可可农场的主人种下了无花果、雨树和其他高大的树木，为自己的作物形成一层保护性的树冠。

sentences.en: The howlers moved in about 25 years ago after nearby forests were cut.
sentences.zh: 在附近的森林被砍伐之后，吼猴大约在25年前迁了进来。

sentences.en: This strange habitat seems to support about as many monkeys as would a same-sized patch of wild forest.
sentences.zh: 这片奇特的栖息地所能养活的猴子数量，似乎和一片同等大小的野生森林差不多。

sentences.en: The howlers eat the leaves and fruit of the shade trees, leaving the valuable cacao pods alone.
sentences.zh: 吼猴吃这些遮阴树的叶子和果实，而对珍贵的可可豆荚则不加触碰。

sentences.en: (G) Estrada believes the monkeys bring under-appreciated benefits to such plantations, dispersing the seeds of fruits such as fig and other shade trees, and fertilising the soil.
sentences.zh: 埃斯特拉达相信，这些猴子给这类种植园带来了未被充分认识的益处，它们传播无花果及其他遮阴树果实的种子，并使土壤肥沃。

sentences.en: Spider monkeys also forage for fruit here, though they need nearby areas of forest to survive in the long term.
sentences.zh: 蜘蛛猴也在这里觅食果子，不过从长远来看，它们需要附近有森林区域才能存活。

sentences.en: He hopes that farmers will begin to see the advantages of associating with wild monkeys, which could include potential ecotourism projects.
sentences.zh: 他希望农场主们会开始看到与野生猴子相伴的好处，其中可能包括潜在的生态旅游项目。

sentences.en: 'Conservation is usually viewed as a conflict between farming practices and the need to preserve nature,' Estrada says.
sentences.zh: “保护通常被看作农耕方式与保护自然的需求之间的一种冲突，”埃斯特拉达说。

sentences.en: 'We're moving away from that vision and beginning to consider ways in which commercial activities may become a tool for the conservation of primates in human-modified landscapes.'
sentences.zh: “我们正在摆脱那种观念，开始思考在被人类改造过的地貌中，商业活动能以何种方式成为保护灵长类动物的一种工具。”

sentences.en: A Velcro, now commonly used instead of buttons and zippers, is probably the most famous example of 'biomimicry', where technologists turn to nature for inspiration.
sentences.zh: 维可牢（Velcro），如今常用来代替纽扣和拉链，大概是“仿生学”最著名的例子，技术专家在仿生学中向自然寻求灵感。

sentences.en: In 1948, scientist Georges de Mestral was walking through long grass when he noticed that dozens of seeds had attached themselves to his trousers.
sentences.zh: 1948年，科学家Georges de Mestral穿过长草时，注意到几十颗种子附着在他的裤子上。

sentences.en: Under a microscope, de Mestral noted the hook-and-loop system the seed cases used to stick so firmly, and was inspired.
sentences.zh: 在显微镜下，de Mestral注意到种子壳用来如此牢牢附着的钩环系统，受到了启发。

sentences.en: B US biologist Janine Benyus wrote a book on the subject called Biomimicry: Innovation Inspired by Nature.
sentences.zh: 美国生物学家Janine Benyus就这个主题写了一本书，叫《Biomimicry：Innovation Inspired by Nature》。

sentences.en: Published in 1997, the book set off the current wave of technology modelled on nature.
sentences.zh: 这本书于1997年出版，掀起了当前这股以自然为蓝本的技术浪潮。

sentences.en: According to Benyus, our ancestors were practised in the art of biomimicry.
sentences.zh: 据Benyus说，我们的祖先精于仿生这门技艺。

sentences.en: 'I think it's an old impulse for humans to take their cues from other organisms,' she says, referring to African tribes that found edible plants by observing the dining habits of chimpanzees.
sentences.zh: “我想，从其他生物身上获取线索是人类一种古老的本能，”她说，指的是那些通过观察黑猩猩的进食习惯来寻找可食用植物的非洲部落。

sentences.en: But lately we've become more focused on what we can make ourselves.
sentences.zh: 但近来我们变得更专注于我们自己能制造什么。

sentences.en: Benyus thinks our drift away from nature started with the advent of agriculture: 'When we broke free from the challenges of hunting and gathering and learnt to stock our cupboards, we fooled ourselves into believing that we didn't need other organisms at all,' she says.
sentences.zh: Benyus认为，我们偏离自然始于农业的出现，“当我们摆脱了狩猎和采集的挑战、学会储满我们的橱柜时，我们自欺欺人地相信我们根本不需要其他生物了，”她说。

sentences.en: C The scientific, industrial, petrochemical and genetic engineering revolutions have repeatedly reinforced the idea that we are liberated from biological constraints.
sentences.zh: 科学、工业、石化和基因工程革命一再强化了我们已从生物约束中解放出来这个观念。

sentences.en: In recent years, however, the illusion that we are independent of nature has been shattered by the spectre of global warming and the looming end to fossil fuel supplies.
sentences.zh: 然而近年来，我们独立于自然的幻觉，已被全球变暖的阴影和化石燃料供应迫近的终结所击碎。

sentences.en: Since few of us would be willing to forgo the products and services we've grown accustomed to – food, water, shelter, the conveniences that modern technology brings – the challenge is to meet the complex demands of civilisation within the bounds of sustainability.
sentences.zh: 由于我们当中很少有人愿意放弃我们已习惯的产品和服务——食物、水、住所、现代技术带来的便利——挑战在于在可持续的范围内满足文明的复杂需求。

sentences.en: 'Nature has learnt to fly, live in the depths of the ocean and craft miracle materials,' writes Benyus.
sentences.zh: “自然已学会飞翔、生活在海洋深处并打造奇迹般的材料，”Benyus写道。

sentences.en: 'Living creatures have done everything we want to do, without guzzling fossil fuel or polluting the planet.
sentences.zh: “生物已经做到了我们想做的一切，却没有大量消耗化石燃料或污染地球。

sentences.en: What better models could there be?'
sentences.zh: 还能有什么更好的范本呢？”

sentences.en: D There are no better models, according to Tim Finnigan, a marine engineer at the University of Sydney.
sentences.zh: 没有更好的范本，悉尼大学的海洋工程师Tim Finnigan如是说。

sentences.en: In his quest to harness the world's waves and tides for renewable energy more efficiently, Finnigan has taken his cues from aquatic life.
sentences.zh: 在他更高效地利用世界的海浪和潮汐来获取可再生能源的探索中，Finnigan从水生生物那里获取了线索。

sentences.en: With their streamlined bodies and stiff, high tail fins, sharks convert up to 90 per cent of their body energy into forward thrust.
sentences.zh: 凭着流线型的身体和坚硬、高耸的尾鳍，鲨鱼能把多达90%的身体能量转化为向前的推力。

sentences.en: Inspired by such efficient hydrodynamics, but turning the theory on its head, Finnigan designed his tidal stream generator: an 18-metre-long biomimetic shark tail with a fin spanning 15 metres.
sentences.zh: 受这种高效流体动力学的启发，但又把理论反转过来，Finnigan设计了他的潮流发电机，一条18米长的仿生鲨鱼尾，鳍展15米。

sentences.en: 'Rather than have a body moving through a stationary fluid, we have fluid that's moving past a stationary body,' says Finnigan.
sentences.zh: “我们不是让一个身体在静止的流体中移动，而是让流体流过一个静止的身体，”Finnigan说。

sentences.en: E Then there's Finnigan's biomimetic forest of giant seaweed.
sentences.zh: 然后是Finnigan仿生的巨型海藻林。

sentences.en: 'As a diver I've looked at the way motions occur under water in the presence of waves,' he says.
sentences.zh: “作为潜水员，我观察过水下在波浪存在时运动是怎么发生的，”他说。

sentences.en: 'I see plants that move quite dramatically and yet they never seem to be pulled out, even in the most dramatic waves.'
sentences.zh: “我看到植物动得相当剧烈，可即使在最剧烈的波浪中，它们似乎也从未被拔出来。”

sentences.en: The trouble with conventional designs, according to Finnigan, is that they're made to stand rigidly against the power of the ocean.
sentences.zh: 据Finnigan说，传统设计的麻烦在于，它们被造得僵硬地对抗海洋的力量。

sentences.en: 'The structures we try to build in the ocean just never end up being strong enough to survive out there,' says Finnigan.
sentences.zh: “我们试图在海洋里建造的结构，最后就是从来不够结实到能在那里存活下去，”Finnigan说。

sentences.en: In the manner of aquatic plants and animals, Finnigan's designs respond to changing current or wave conditions by reorienting to maximise energy capture.
sentences.zh: 像水生动植物那样，Finnigan的设计通过重新定向以最大化能量捕获，来响应不断变化的水流或波浪条件。

sentences.en: And in severe weather, to avoid a battering, his wave energy generator will lie flat against the ocean floor.
sentences.zh: 而在恶劣天气里，为避免被拍打，他的波浪能发电机会平贴在海床上。

sentences.en: F While conventional architects were designing buildings dependent on expensive air conditioning systems, when Mick Pearce tried to do the same, he struck a problem.
sentences.zh: 当传统建筑师在设计依赖昂贵空调系统的建筑时，Mick Pearce试图做同样的事，却遇到了一个问题。

sentences.en: 'We were building office blocks for a client in Zimbabwe and we ran out of funds.
sentences.zh: “我们在为津巴布韦的一位客户建造办公楼，结果资金用光了。

sentences.en: So we looked for ways to make a building without traditional air conditioning.'
sentences.zh: 所以我们寻找在没有传统空调的情况下建一栋楼的办法。”

sentences.en: One day, driving through the grasslands, he saw a large mound created by termites, the ant-like insect common in Africa.
sentences.zh: 一天，开车穿过草原时，他看到一个由白蚁——非洲常见的那种蚂蚁状昆虫——堆成的大土丘。

sentences.en: He noticed that air entering at the base of the mound was mixed with water drawn from subterranean levels by the termites, causing evaporative cooling.
sentences.zh: 他注意到，从土丘底部进入的空气和白蚁从地下层抽上来的水混合，造成蒸发冷却。

sentences.en: Pearce wanted to reproduce this principle but he needed an alternative system, and in his building massive fans were employed at the base of the structure to lower the temperature of the circulating air.
sentences.zh: Pearce想复制这个原理，但他需要一个替代系统，在他的楼里，巨型风扇被用在结构底部来降低循环空气的温度。

sentences.en: Pearce's termite-inspired cooling system cut energy use to 10 per cent of a similar air-conditioned building.
sentences.zh: Pearce受白蚁启发的冷却系统，把能耗降到了类似空调建筑的10%。

sentences.en: G Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use energy from the sun to convert water and carbon dioxide into carbohydrates and oxygen.
sentences.zh: 光合作用是绿色植物利用太阳能把水和二氧化碳转化为碳水化合物和氧气的过程。

sentences.en: Plants can manage it with humbling ease.
sentences.zh: 植物能做到这一点，轻松得令人汗颜。

sentences.en: But, as the 40 researchers from 11 institutes who have collaborated to form the Australian Artificial Photosynthesis Network have realised, it is very complex.
sentences.zh: 但是，正如来自11家机构、合作组成澳大利亚人工光合作用网络的40名研究人员所认识到的，它非常复杂。

sentences.en: However, there is one aspect working in our favour.
sentences.zh: 不过，有一个方面对我们有利。

sentences.en: In nature, environmental variables like temperature, carbon dioxide and light availability limit the rate of photosynthesis.
sentences.zh: 在自然界，温度、二氧化碳和光照可得性等环境变量限制了光合作用的速率。

sentences.en: In a laboratory, these variables can be optimized.
sentences.zh: 在实验室里，这些变量可以被优化。

sentences.en: 'We don't have to cope with drought or frost.
sentences.zh: “我们不必应付干旱或霜冻。

sentences.en: We can work with a highly controlled, specified set of conditions,' says Tom Collings, the group's spokesman.
sentences.zh: 我们可以在一组高度受控、明确指定的条件下工作，”小组发言人Tom Collings说。

records.title: Should space be explored by robots or by humans
records.titleZh: 太空应由机器人还是人类来探索

sentences.en: A The advisability of humans participating directly in space travel continues to cause many debates.
sentences.zh: 人类直接参与太空旅行是否明智，继续引发许多争论。

sentences.en: There is no doubt that the presence of people on board a space vehicle makes its design much more complex and challenging, and produces a large increase in costs, since safety requirements are greatly increased, and the performance of the technology providing necessities for human passengers such as oxygen, food and water must be guaranteed.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，人在航天器上的存在会让其设计复杂和具挑战得多，并造成成本的大幅增加，因为安全要求大大提高，而且为人类乘客提供氧气、食物和水等必需品的技术，其性能必须得到保证。

sentences.en: Moreover, the systems required are bulky and costly, and their complexity increases for long-duration missions.
sentences.zh: 而且，所需的系统既笨重又昂贵，对长时间任务来说其复杂性还会增加。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, advances in electronics and computer science allow increasingly complex tasks to be entrusted to robots, and unmanned space probes are becoming lighter, smaller and more convenient.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，电子学和计算机科学的进步使得越来越复杂的任务可以托付给机器人，无人太空探测器正变得更轻、更小、更便利。

sentences.en: B However, experience has shown that the idea of humans in space is popular with the public.
sentences.zh: 然而，经验表明，人在太空这个想法很受公众欢迎。

sentences.en: Humans can also be useful; there are many cases when only direct intervention by an astronaut or cosmonaut can correct the malfunction of an automatic device.
sentences.zh: 人也可以是有用的；有许多情况是只有宇航员的直接干预才能纠正某个自动装置的故障。

sentences.en: Astronauts and cosmonauts have proved that they can adapt to conditions of weightlessness and work in space without encountering too many problems, as was seen in the operations to repair and to upgrade the Hubble Space Telescope.
sentences.zh: 宇航员们已经证明，他们能适应失重的条件、在太空中工作而不会遇到太多问题，正如在修理和升级哈勃太空望远镜的操作中所见到的。

sentences.en: One human characteristic which is particularly precious in space missions, and which so far is lacking in robots, is the ability to perform a great variety of tasks.
sentences.zh: 在太空任务中尤其宝贵、而机器人迄今仍欠缺的一项人类特征，是执行种类繁多任务的能力。

sentences.en: In addition, robots are not good at reacting to situations they have not been specifically prepared for.
sentences.zh: 此外，机器人不善于对它们没有专门准备过的情况作出反应。

sentences.en: This is especially important in the case of deep space missions.
sentences.zh: 这在深空任务的情况下尤其重要。

sentences.en: While in the case of the Moon it is possible for someone on Earth to 'tele-operate' a robotic device such as a probe, as the two-way link time is only a couple of seconds, on Mars the two-way link time is several minutes, so sending instructions from Earth is more difficult.
sentences.zh: 就月球而言，地球上的人有可能“遥控操作”一台探测器之类的机器人装置，因为双向链接时间只有几秒，而在火星上，双向链接时间是好几分钟，所以从地球发送指令更困难。

sentences.en: C Many of the promises of artificial intelligence are still far from being fulfilled.
sentences.zh: 人工智能的许多承诺仍远未实现。

sentences.en: The construction of machines simulating human logical reasoning moves towards ever more distant dates.
sentences.zh: 模拟人类逻辑推理的机器的制造，正朝着越来越遥远的日期推移。

sentences.en: The more the performance of computers improves, the more we realise how difficult it is to build machines which display logical abilities.
sentences.zh: 计算机的性能越是提高，我们越是意识到造出能展现逻辑能力的机器有多难。

sentences.en: In the past it was confidently predicted that we would soon have fully automated factories in which all operations were performed without any human intervention, and forecasts of the complete substitution of workers by robots in many production areas were made.
sentences.zh: 过去人们曾自信地预言，我们很快就会有全自动化的工厂，所有操作都无需任何人工干预，并作出了在许多生产领域以机器人完全取代工人的预测。

sentences.en: Today, these perspectives are being revised.
sentences.zh: 今天，这些前景正被修正。

sentences.en: It seems that all machines, even the smartest ones, must cooperate with humans.
sentences.zh: 看来所有机器，即便是最聪明的，也必须和人类合作。

sentences.en: Rather than replacing humans, the present need appears to be for an intelligent machine capable of helping a human operator without replacing him or her.
sentences.zh: 当前的需求似乎不是取代人类，而是要一台能帮助人类操作员而不取代他或她的智能机器。

sentences.en: The word 'cobot', from 'collaborative robot', has been invented to designate this type of robot.
sentences.zh: “协作机器人”这个词，来自“collaborative robot”，被造出来指代这类机器人。

sentences.en: D A similar trend is also apparent in the field of space exploration.
sentences.zh: 在太空探索领域也有类似的趋势。

sentences.en: Tasks which were in the past entrusted only to machines are now performed by human beings, sometimes with the aim of using simpler and less costly devices, sometimes to obtain better performance.
sentences.zh: 过去只托付给机器的任务现在由人类执行，有时是为了使用更简单、更便宜的装置，有时是为了获得更好的性能。

sentences.en: In many cases, to involve a person in the control loop is a welcome simplification which may lower the cost of a mission without compromising safety.
sentences.zh: 在许多情况下，让一个人进入控制回路是一种受欢迎的简化，它可能在不损害安全的前提下降低一项任务的成本。

sentences.en: Many operations originally designed to be performed under completely automatic control can be performed more efficiently by astronauts, perhaps helped by their 'cobots'.
sentences.zh: 许多原本设计为在完全自动控制下执行的操作，可以由宇航员更高效地执行，或许还有他们的“协作机器人”帮忙。

sentences.en: The human-machine relationship must evolve towards a closer collaboration.
sentences.zh: 人机关系必须朝着更紧密的协作演变。

sentences.en: E One way this could happen is by adopting the Mars Outposts approach, proposed by the Planetary Society.
sentences.zh: 实现这一点的一种方式，是采用行星协会提出的火星前哨方法。

sentences.en: This would involve sending a number of robotic research stations to Mars, equipped with permanent communications and navigational systems.
sentences.zh: 这将涉及向火星发送若干配有永久通信和导航系统的机器人研究站。

sentences.en: They would perform research, and establish the infrastructure needed to prepare future landing sites for the exploration of Mars by humans.
sentences.zh: 它们会开展研究，并建立所需的基础设施，为人类探索火星的未来着陆点做准备。

sentences.en: It has also been suggested that in the most difficult environments, as on Venus or Jupiter, robots could be controlled by human beings located in spaceships which remain in orbit around the planet.
sentences.zh: 也有人提出，在最艰难的环境里，比如在金星或木星上，机器人可以由处在环绕该行星轨道飞船里的人类来控制。

sentences.en: In this case, the link time for communication between humans and robots would be far less than it would be from Earth.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，人与机器人之间通信的链接时间会远小于从地球通信的链接时间。

sentences.en: F But if space is to be more than a place to build automatic laboratories or set up industrial enterprises in the vicinity of our planet, the presence of humans is essential.
sentences.zh: 但是，如果太空不只是个在我们星球附近建造自动实验室或建立工业企业的地方，那么人的存在就必不可少。

sentences.en: They must learn how to voyage through space towards destinations which will be not only scientific bases but also places to live.
sentences.zh: 他们必须学会如何穿越太空、前往那些不仅是科学基地、也是居住地的目的地。

sentences.en: If space is a frontier, that frontier must see the presence of people.
sentences.zh: 如果太空是一道边疆，那道边疆就必须见到人的存在。

sentences.en: So the aim for humankind in the future will be not just the exploration of space, but its colonisation.
sentences.zh: 所以人类未来的目标将不只是探索太空，而是殖民太空。

sentences.en: The result of exploring and living in space may be a deep change in the views which humankind has of itself.
sentences.zh: 探索太空和在太空中生活的结果，可能是人类对自身看法的一种深刻改变。

sentences.en: And this process is already under way.
sentences.zh: 而这个过程已经在进行中。

sentences.en: The images of Earth taken from the Moon in the Apollo programme have given humankind a new consciousness of its fragility, its smallness, and its unity.
sentences.zh: 阿波罗计划中从月球拍摄的地球图像，已经给了人类对其脆弱、渺小和统一的一种新意识。

sentences.en: These impressions have triggered a realisation of the need to protect and preserve it, for it is the place in the solar system most suitable for us and above all it is the only place we have, at least for now.
sentences.zh: 这些印象触发了一种认识，即需要保护和保存它，因为它是太阳系中最适合我们的地方，而且最重要的是，至少就目前而言，它是我们唯一拥有的地方。

sentences.en: A For people confined to bed for long periods of time, or for astronauts in microgravity, muscle wasting is a serious problem.
sentences.zh: 对于需要长期卧床的人，或是处于微重力环境中的宇航员来说，肌肉萎缩是一个严重的问题。

sentences.en: Wasting, or atrophy, is a symptom not only of disuse and injury, but of many diseases, including kidney failure, cancer and AIDS.
sentences.zh: 消瘦，或者说萎缩，不仅是废用和损伤的症状，也是许多疾病的症状，包括肾衰竭、癌症和艾滋病。

sentences.en: Once enough muscle has been lost, a vicious cycle sets in as exercise becomes increasingly difficult, which in turn leads to disuse and further atrophy.
sentences.zh: 一旦失去了足够多的肌肉，恶性循环便随之形成：运动变得越来越困难，这反过来又导致废用和进一步的萎缩。

sentences.en: B Despite more than three decades of research into alternatives, the only way to stop such patients losing muscle is a long course of physiotherapy involving weight-bearing exercise, but this is of little use to the weakest and sickest—and in most cases, starts only after wasting has already set in.
sentences.zh: 尽管对替代方法的研究已经持续了三十多年，阻止这类患者肌肉流失的唯一方法仍然是包含负重运动的长期理疗，但这对最虚弱、病情最重的患者几乎没有用处——而且在大多数情况下，只有当萎缩已经开始之后才会进行。

sentences.en: The use of anabolic steroids is being explored for some conditions.
sentences.zh: 目前人们正在探索将合成代谢类固醇用于某些病症。

sentences.en: But these compounds have a huge range of effects on the body besides promoting muscle growth, some of them undesirable, and only appear to work well in conjunction with exercise.
sentences.zh: 但这些化合物除了促进肌肉生长之外，还会对身体产生大范围的影响，其中一些是不良影响，而且它们似乎只有与运动相结合才能发挥良好效果。

sentences.en: C Alfred Goldberg, a cell biologist at Harvard University, began studying muscle atrophy in the late 1960s.
sentences.zh: 哈佛大学的细胞生物学家Alfred Goldberg于20世纪60年代末开始研究肌肉萎缩。

sentences.en: What he and others discovered was that, rather than being a passive side effect of disuse or disease, muscle wasting is an active process controlled by a complex genetic pathway.
sentences.zh: 他和其他人发现，肌肉萎缩并不是废用或疾病的被动副作用，而是一个由复杂基因通路控制的主动过程。

sentences.en: So, if someone found out how it was turned on, it ought to be possible to turn it off.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果有人弄清了它是如何被开启的，就应该有可能把它关掉。

sentences.en: “Back then we didn't know the pathway for muscle breakdown,” says Goldberg, “but about five years ago our work showed that no matter what the trigger—disuse, metabolic disease or fasting—the same biochemical programme is responsible.”
sentences.zh: “那时候我们还不知道肌肉分解的通路，”Goldberg说，“但大约五年前，我们的工作表明，无论触发因素是什么——废用、代谢疾病还是禁食——起作用的都是同一套生化程序。”

sentences.en: D The process involves the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway (UPP), the disposal machinery used to break down unwanted proteins in the cell (New Scientist, 17 December 2005, p.
sentences.zh: 该过程涉及泛素-蛋白酶体通路（UPP），即细胞中用来分解不需要的蛋白质的处理机制（New Scientist，2005年12月17日，第

sentences.en: Once the system has been activated, ubiquitin “destroy me” labels are added to muscle proteins.
sentences.zh: 一旦该系统被激活，泛素“销毁我”标签便会被加到肌肉蛋白质上。

sentences.en: This breaks down the muscle filaments within cells, but does not change the number of muscle cells.
sentences.zh: 这会分解细胞内的肌丝，但不会改变肌肉细胞的数量。

sentences.en: Instead, they become thinner and weaker.
sentences.zh: 相反，它们会变得更细、更弱。

sentences.en: Further studies showed that at least 90 genes are involved in atrophy; Goldberg calls them “atrogenes.”
sentences.zh: 进一步的研究表明，至少有90个基因参与了萎缩过程；Goldberg将它们称为“atrogenes”。

sentences.en: Although it is still unknown which of these genes triggers atrophy, it soon became clear that two of them are essential to the process.
sentences.zh: 尽管这些基因中是哪一个触发了萎缩仍不得而知，但人们很快就清楚了，其中有两个基因对这一过程至关重要。

sentences.en: Atrogin1 and muRF1 were first described in 2001 and are the only two atrogenes active only during muscle atrophy.
sentences.zh: Atrogin1和muRF1于2001年首次得到描述，是仅有的两个只在肌肉萎缩期间才有活性的atrogenes。

sentences.en: They code for ubiquitin ligases, the enzymes that attach the “destroy me” labels to proteins.
sentences.zh: 它们编码泛素连接酶，也就是把“销毁我”标签附着到蛋白质上的酶。

sentences.en: The genes are barely active in normal muscle, but expression levels shoot up in sick animals.
sentences.zh: 这些基因在正常肌肉中几乎没有活性，但在患病动物体内，它们的表达水平会急剧飙升。

sentences.en: Knock out either, and muscle wasting all but stops.
sentences.zh: 只要敲除其中任何一个，肌肉萎缩就几乎完全停止。

sentences.en: E An experiment was conducted on a “superboy” who was normal at birth, lacking fat; by the age of five, he was excellent at weightlifting, lifting as much as three kilograms.
sentences.zh: 一项实验以一名“超级男孩”为对象，他出生时正常，缺乏脂肪；到五岁时，他的举重表现出色，能举起多达3公斤的重量。

sentences.en: The scientists found that this is closely related to his mother, who is a professional runner, and that his extended family has unusually strong abilities.
sentences.zh: 科学家发现，这与他的母亲密切相关——她是一名职业赛跑运动员——而且他的整个大家族都拥有异乎寻常的强大能力。

sentences.en: The boy's condition is caused by a lack of myostatin, a protein that normally limits muscle growth.
sentences.zh: 男孩的这种状况是由缺乏myostatin引起的，这是一种通常会限制肌肉生长的蛋白质。

sentences.en: Without it, muscles grow far larger and stronger than usual.
sentences.zh: 没有它，肌肉会长得比通常情况大得多、也强壮得多。

sentences.en: But the drug can have a temporary effect.
sentences.zh: 但这种药物可能只具有暂时性的效果。

sentences.en: F There are still many gaps to be filled in, but those in the field agree that the question is no longer if we can develop anti-wasting treatments, but when.
sentences.zh: 仍有许多空白有待填补，但该领域的专家一致认为，问题已不再是我们能否开发出抗萎缩疗法，而是何时能开发出来。

sentences.en: As researchers close in on this target, excitement is mounting about exactly what such treatments could achieve.
sentences.zh: 随着研究人员逐步逼近这一目标，人们对这类疗法究竟能实现什么的期待日益高涨。

sentences.en: Patients due to be confined to bed for more than a few days could be given the drug as soon as they begin bed rest to prevent muscle loss that would otherwise slow their recovery.
sentences.zh: 对于即将卧床超过几天的患者，可以在他们一开始卧床休息时就给予这种药物，以防止肌肉流失——否则这种流失会拖慢他们的康复。

sentences.en: Weaning patients off respirators would become easier as doctors could prevent wasting of the diaphragm.
sentences.zh: 让患者脱离呼吸机将变得更加容易，因为医生可以防止横膈膜发生萎缩。

sentences.en: Disease need no longer lead to weakness, and broken bones would not mean long and painful physiotherapy sessions to rebuild muscle strength.
sentences.zh: 疾病将不再导致虚弱，骨折也将不意味着要经历漫长而痛苦的理疗来重建肌肉力量。

sentences.en: And since loss of muscle mass is a major reason why we grow frail with age, an anti-wasting drug could keep older people on their feet and living independently for longer.
sentences.zh: 而且由于肌肉量的流失是我们随年龄增长而变得衰弱的一个主要原因，一种抗萎缩药物可以让老年人更长久地保持行动能力和独立生活。

sentences.en: G The prospect of preventing atrophy is also of great interest to NASA, particularly in view of its much talked-about mission to Mars.
sentences.zh: 防止萎缩的前景也令NASA极感兴趣，尤其是考虑到其备受热议的火星任务。

sentences.en: By the time astronauts reach the Red Planet, they can expect to lose up to 25 per cent of their muscle mass and be too weak to walk, let alone put on a space suit and carry out repairs.
sentences.zh: 等到宇航员抵达这颗红色星球时，他们预计会流失多达25%的肌肉量，并且虚弱得无法行走，更不用说穿上航天服并进行维修了。

sentences.en: That is why Goldberg's work is funded by the National Space Biomedical Research Institute in Houston, Texas, set up by NASA.
sentences.zh: 这正是Goldberg的工作由位于得克萨斯州休斯敦、由NASA设立的国家航天生物医学研究所资助的原因。

sentences.en: H While there are valid medical and space applications for anti-wasting drugs, as a safer alternative to steroids they will inevitably be hugely tempting for athletes too, not to mention the lazy as well.
sentences.zh: 尽管抗萎缩药物有着正当的医疗和航天用途，但作为比类固醇更安全的替代品，它们对运动员也必然具有巨大的诱惑力，更不用说那些懒惰的人了。

sentences.en: Although Goldberg is keen to point out that helping cheats and couch potatoes is not the focus of his work, he admits that it will undoubtedly happen sooner or later.
sentences.zh: 尽管Goldberg极力指出，帮助作弊者和终日懒散的人并不是他工作的重点，但他承认，这种情况无疑迟早都会发生。
