sentences.en: A Beneath the flat, impassive surface of Australia lie hidden mountains, valleys and gorges – ancient traps and channels for the deadly salt that is stealthily killing so much of the Australian landscape.
sentences.zh: 在澳大利亚平坦、看似无动于衷的地表之下，隐藏着群山、峡谷和深沟——这些古老的陷阱与通道，承载着如今正悄然侵蚀大片澳大利亚景观的致命盐分。

sentences.en: The war on salt is calling forth new weapons.
sentences.zh: 这场对盐的战争正在召唤新的武器。

sentences.en: A suite of high technologies used by geologists to see underground and prospect for gold and minerals is now being used to pinpoint the presence of salt beneath the landscape, and to predict where it might move.
sentences.zh: 地质学家用来“看穿”地下、勘探金矿和矿物的一整套高技术，如今正被用来精确定位地表之下盐分的分布，并预测它可能向何处移动。

sentences.en: B Unless this process is clearly understood, warns Chief of Exploration and Mining Dr Neil Phillips, the hard work now underway of planning and tree-planting on the surface may be rendered ineffective: salt can still sneak past and erupt, following one of the ancient river channels formed millions of years ago.
sentences.zh: 探矿与采矿首席科学家尼尔·菲利普斯博士（Dr Neil Phillips）警告说，除非这一过程被清楚地理解，否则地表上正在进行的规划与种树等艰苦工作可能会失效——盐分仍可能溜过去爆发，沿着数百万年前形成的某条古河道前进。

sentences.en: The use of airborne electromagnetics to detect salt hidden beneath the landscape has been around for a decade, but the past two years have seen a major development in its precision and powers of detection.
sentences.zh: 利用机载电磁勘测探测隐藏于地表之下的盐分，已经存在了十年；而过去两年里，其精度和探测能力有了重大提升。

sentences.en: Like the use of radar in battles, it has the potential to turn the tide of the struggle in favour of the defence by helping to pinpoint, plot and predict the movements of the foe.
sentences.zh: 就像战斗中使用雷达一样，它有潜力把这场斗争的形势扭转到防御方有利的一边——帮助精确定位、绘制和预测对手的动向。

sentences.en: C Angus Howell, who farms near Warrenbayne, in Southeast Australia, saw his first outbreak of salt in 1948.
sentences.zh: 安格斯·豪厄尔（Angus Howell）在澳大利亚东南部沃伦贝恩附近务农，他在 1948 年第一次看到盐分爆发。

sentences.en: Over the ensuing decades the patches spread and multiplied until they consumed almost 100 hectares.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的数十年里，那些斑块扩散并增多，直到几乎吞没了 100 公顷土地。

sentences.en: By the late 1970s, Howell and his fellow farmers had decided it was time for action and established a government-funded “Landcare” group in a bid to save Australia's farmland.
sentences.zh: 到 1970 年代末，豪厄尔和他的农民伙伴们决定该行动了，他们成立了一个由政府资助的“土地照护”（Landcare）小组，以挽救澳大利亚的农田。

sentences.en: But despite a mounting effort by scientists, farmers and governments, the “white death” continued to encroach.
sentences.zh: 但尽管科学家、农民和政府的努力不断累积，“白色死亡”仍在步步进逼。

sentences.en: Small successes were eclipsed by larger defeats and fresh outbreaks.
sentences.zh: 小的胜利被更大的失败和新的爆发掩盖。

sentences.en: D “The technical solutions just aren't there yet for dealing with broadacre salinity, nor are the social and economic solutions.
sentences.zh: “技术上的解决方案目前还不足以应对大田规模的盐渍化，社会和经济上的解决方案也是如此。

sentences.en: How do you introduce the land-use changes that are needed when people still need to make a living?”
sentences.zh: 当人们仍然必须谋生时，你如何引入所需的土地用途变化呢？“

sentences.en: Howell asks.
sentences.zh: 豪厄尔问道。

sentences.en: There is no satisfactory solution yet.
sentences.zh: 目前还没有令人满意的解决方案。

sentences.en: Part of the problem has lain in salt's ability to mount ambushes, emerging somewhere new, sometimes unexpected and unexplained, beating plans to intercept it.
sentences.zh: 问题的一部分在于盐分有能力发动伏击，从某个新地方冒出来——有时令人意外、无法解释——挫败拦截它的计划。

sentences.en: Only now are scientists starting to really disclose its secret subterranean stores and passages.
sentences.zh: 只有现在，科学家们才真正开始揭示其隐秘的地下储库和通道。

sentences.en: E The need for such knowledge is pressing.
sentences.zh: 对这种知识的需求十分紧迫。

sentences.en: Salt has already afflicted six million hectares of once-productive country.
sentences.zh: 盐分已经侵害了 600 万公顷曾经富饶的土地。

sentences.en: At present rates, it is predicted that, by 2050, it will have sterilised a total of 17 million hectares and the waters of Australia's Murray River will regularly exceed the World Health Organisation's salt limits for drinking water.
sentences.zh: 按目前的速度，预计到 2050 年，它将使总共 1700 万公顷土地失去生产力，澳大利亚墨累河的水将经常超过世界卫生组织对饮用水的盐分上限。

sentences.en: Defeating this assault may take centuries, not decades.
sentences.zh: 击败这场侵袭可能需要数个世纪，而非数十年。

sentences.en: F Electromagnetic surveys measure the electrical conductivity of soil to reveal the distribution of salt and the nature and variability of the regolith – the weathered rock and sediment that may lie above the bedrock.
sentences.zh: 电磁勘测测量土壤的电导率，以揭示盐分的分布以及风化层（即可能位于基岩之上的风化岩石和沉积物）的性质与可变性。

sentences.en: Magnetic surveys measure small differences in the Earth's magnetic field, enabling scientists to probe the deep past and reconstruct ancient landscapes – rivers, basins and faults now buried under tens of metres of sediment.
sentences.zh: 磁力勘测测量地球磁场的微小差异，使科学家能够探索遥远的过去，重建古老的地貌——河流、盆地和断层，如今被埋在数十米厚的沉积物之下。

sentences.en: These features help to reveal where groundwater is stored, dictate the direction of groundwater movement, and are critical to predicting or ruling out salinity hot-spots.
sentences.zh: 这些特征有助于揭示地下水储存于何处、决定地下水移动的方向，并且对预测或排除盐渍化高发点至关重要。

sentences.en: G Radiometric analysis is based on the detection of radiation emitted by elements contained in rocks and soils, allowing scientists to delineate landforms.
sentences.zh: 放射性测量基于检测岩石和土壤中元素所放出的辐射，使科学家能够勾画出地形。

sentences.en: These factors influence the mobility of salt through the soil profile and help determine where to plant particular crop species to tackle the problem.
sentences.zh: 这些因素影响盐分在土壤剖面中的可移动性，有助于决定在哪里种植特定作物以应对这一问题。

sentences.en: Using data from the Murray River region, scientists have revealed a network of ancient drainage systems that channelled water beneath the current land-surface.
sentences.zh: 利用墨累河流域的数据，科学家揭示了一个由古代排水系统构成的网络，这些系统在当前地表之下输送过水。

sentences.en: These buried channels may carry salt and sometimes run at right angles to channels on the surface.
sentences.zh: 这些埋藏的河道可能携带盐分，有时其走向与地表河道呈直角。

sentences.en: This implies that the salt could move underground in quite a different direction to what one would expect by looking at surface slope and drainage.
sentences.zh: 这意味着盐分可能在地下沿着完全不同于人们仅看地表坡度与排水所预期的方向移动。

sentences.en: H One of the biggest advances in detection, says Professor Neil Phillips, has come with the integration of different techniques such as magnetics, electromagnetics and radiometrics, and ground mapping.
sentences.zh: 尼尔·菲利普斯教授说，检测技术最大的进步之一来自把磁力、电磁、放射性测量以及地面填图等不同技术加以整合。

sentences.en: Individually, these technologies only gave clues to what was going on underground.
sentences.zh: 单独使用时，这些技术只对地下情况给出了一些线索。

sentences.en: Together they provide a far more revealing picture of the subsurface landscape, several hundred metres deep.
sentences.zh: 合用时，它们对地表以下数百米深的景观提供了远为清晰的图像。

sentences.en: Advanced airborne electromagnetics, in particular, enables scientists to take “slices” of the landscape at depths of five metres, ten metres, fifteen metres and so on, to determine where salt may be stored at depth.
sentences.zh: 特别是先进的机载电磁技术，使科学家能够在 5 米、10 米、15 米等深度对景观进行“切片”，以确定盐分可能在何深度被储存。

sentences.en: This is building up a four-dimensional picture of the subsurface landscape, enabling researchers to understand movements of salt in length, breadth, depth and time.
sentences.zh: 这正在为地下景观构建一幅四维图像，使研究者得以在长度、宽度、深度和时间上理解盐分的移动。

sentences.en: From such technologies it will be possible to locate salt stores, identify how saline they are, look at man-made and natural changes to the landscape that may cause it to mobilise, and then predict where it will head to and over what time span.
sentences.zh: 借助这些技术，人们将能够定位盐分储库、识别其盐分含量、查看可能促使其活动的人为和自然景观变化，进而预测它将朝何处去、在多长时间跨度内移动。

sentences.en: This in turn will give the salt warriors time to model various ways of containing or curbing the menace, see what works best and then try it out on the ground.
sentences.zh: 这反过来将为对抗盐分的“战士”们赢得时间，让他们建模出多种遏制或抑制这一威胁的方式，看看哪种方式效果最佳，然后在实地试用。

sentences.en: A A Londoner with a sudden urge for giant African snails could do worse than head to the bustling marketplace in Brixton, a part of south London that is home to many people from Africa.
sentences.zh: 一个突然渴望吃巨型非洲蜗牛的伦敦人，去布里克斯顿熙熙攘攘的市场就不会错，布里克斯顿是南伦敦一处许多来自非洲的人聚居的地方。

sentences.en: Markets like Brixton Market that cater to migrants are a testament to the fact that people often retain very strong preferences for the kinds of food they grew up eating.
sentences.zh: 像布里克斯顿市场这样迎合移民的市场，证明了人们往往对自己从小吃到大的那类食物保有非常强烈的偏好。

sentences.en: Just ask the expatriate Britons who flock to 'Tea and Sympathy' in New York's Greenwich Village for pots of Marmite, a yeast-based spread whose delights baffle other nationalities (and many of their own compatriots).
sentences.zh: 只要问问那些蜂拥到纽约格林威治村“Tea and Sympathy”去买一罐罐Marmite的旅居英国人就知道了，Marmite是一种酵母制成的酱，它的妙处让其他国家的人（以及他们自己许多同胞）困惑不解。

sentences.en: B Past research has shown that people are often willing to pay much more for a favoured brand than for seemingly identical alternatives.
sentences.zh: 过去的研究表明，人们往往愿意为一个偏爱的品牌付出比看似相同的替代品多得多的钱。

sentences.en: It is not always obvious why.
sentences.zh: 原因并不总是显而易见。

sentences.en: However, there is ample evidence to support the theory that certain food preferences form in childhood.
sentences.zh: 然而，有充分的证据支持某些食物偏好在童年时期形成的理论。

sentences.en: Children have a predisposition to fear new foods, which is only overcome when they are repeatedly presented with, and encouraged to consume, a particular food.
sentences.zh: 孩子天生倾向于害怕新食物，这只有在他们被反复呈上、并被鼓励食用某种食物时才会被克服。

sentences.en: Evidence shows that children's instinctive wariness of new foods dates back to the times when humans had to forage for food, and it was important that they learnt which foods were safe to eat.
sentences.zh: 证据表明，孩子对新食物本能的警惕可追溯到人类不得不觅食的时代，当时他们学会哪些食物可以安全食用很重要。

sentences.en: In the modern world, people routinely express a strong liking for a brand even though they are unable to tell the brand apart from rival brands in blind tests, and many studies have found that advertising alone cannot explain the strength of brand loyalty.
sentences.zh: 在现代世界，人们经常表达对某个品牌的强烈喜爱，即便他们在盲测中无法把这个品牌与对手品牌区分开来，而许多研究发现，单靠广告无法解释品牌忠诚度的强度。

sentences.en: C A new study by economists from the universities of Tilburg and Chicago tracks the consumption patterns of 38,000 US households over two years, and confirms the theory that such brand loyalty is widespread, deep and long-lasting.
sentences.zh: 蒂尔堡大学和芝加哥大学经济学家的一项新研究，追踪了38000个美国家庭两年的消费模式，证实了这种品牌忠诚广泛、深厚而持久的理论。

sentences.en: There were clear local patterns in consumption, although the same brands were available everywhere.
sentences.zh: 消费中有明显的地方模式，尽管同样的品牌到处都能买到。

sentences.en: But 16% of people studied were migrants: they had grown up in one state and moved to another.
sentences.zh: 但被研究者中有16%是移民：他们在一个州长大、搬到了另一个州。

sentences.en: These migrants had the same options, in terms of what was on offer and at what price, as everyone else in their adopted home, but although they consumed local favourites, they bought fewer than longtime residents.
sentences.zh: 这些移民在供应什么、什么价格方面，和他们新家里的其他人有同样的选择，但尽管他们也消费当地的最爱，他们买得比长期居民少。

sentences.en: This gap between purchases of migrants and those of the locally born was quite stubborn: although it faded the longer a person lived in their new state, it still took 20 years to halve in magnitude.
sentences.zh: 移民的购买与本地出生者购买之间的这种差距相当顽固：尽管一个人在新州住得越久它就越淡，但它仍要花20年才减半。

sentences.en: Even 50 years on, it was still large enough to show up in the data.
sentences.zh: 即便50年后，它仍然大到足以在数据中显现出来。

sentences.en: This could mean that the benefits of being the first brand into a market could last longer than might be assumed.
sentences.zh: 这可能意味着，作为第一个进入某个市场的品牌，其好处可能比人们可能假定的持续得更久。

sentences.en: D David Atkin of Yale University has identified some important implications of local food favourites.
sentences.zh: 耶鲁大学的大卫·阿特金已经辨认出本地食物偏爱的一些重要含义。

sentences.en: He suggests in a recent paper that the effects of people being loyal to known brands may also lead economists to rethink the way they calculate the benefits resulting from trade.
sentences.zh: 他在最近一篇论文中提出，人们忠于已知品牌的效应，可能还会让经济学家重新思考他们计算贸易所产生收益的方式。

sentences.en: This is because opening up to trade is in some ways very similar to migrating, as it changes the composition and prices of the foods that are available to a person.
sentences.zh: 这是因为对外开放贸易在某些方面与移民非常相似，因为它改变了一个人可获得食物的构成和价格。

sentences.en: In particular, trade can cause local foods to become relatively more expensive.
sentences.zh: 尤其是，贸易可能导致本地食物变得相对更贵。

sentences.en: Atkin's data show something many economists do not take into account: when a traditional food has to compete with imported foods, it may no longer be the cheapest food available for people to choose to eat.
sentences.zh: 阿特金的数据显示出许多经济学家没有考虑到的东西：当一种传统食物不得不与进口食物竞争时，它可能不再是人们可以选择吃的最便宜食物。

sentences.en: Atkin decided to look at this situation in the context of developing countries.
sentences.zh: 阿特金决定在发展中国家的背景下来看这种情况。

sentences.en: E To illustrate his point, Atkin uses detailed data about people's food choices in India.
sentences.zh: 为了说明他的观点，阿特金使用了关于印度人食物选择的详细数据。

sentences.en: India is a good choice because it covers a large number of climatic zones where different specialised crops are grown.
sentences.zh: 印度是个好选择，因为它涵盖了大量种植不同专门作物的气候带。

sentences.en: Despite being part of the same country, the prevalence of internal barriers to trade means that its regions are best thought of as being only partially open to trade.
sentences.zh: 尽管同属一个国家，但内部贸易壁垒的普遍存在意味着它的各地区最好被看作只是部分地对贸易开放。

sentences.en: Atkin's data show that the foods a region specialises in producing are instead cheaper in that region.
sentences.zh: 阿特金的数据显示，一个地区专门生产的食物在那个地区反而更便宜。

sentences.en: F However, there has been some opening up of internal trade in India in recent years, and this has revealed that for every rupee spent on food, people's intake of calories declined most in regions where prices of local favourite foods had risen.
sentences.zh: 然而，近年来印度的内部贸易有了一些开放，而这揭示出，每花一卢比在食物上，在本地最爱食物价格上涨的地区，人们的热量摄入下降得最多。

sentences.en: In theory, when there is a greater choice of types of food, people should adjust their food habits and purchase the cheapest option so that they boost their calorie intake.
sentences.zh: 理论上，当食物种类的选择更多时，人们应该调整自己的饮食习惯、购买最便宜的选项，从而提高他们的热量摄入。

sentences.en: However, in practice, food habits mean that consumers keep buying the things they know and like even though these foods have become relatively expensive.
sentences.zh: 然而，在实践中，饮食习惯意味着消费者继续购买他们熟悉和喜爱的东西，即便这些食物已经变得相对昂贵。

sentences.en: Atkin calculates that if all barriers to internal trade in India were abolished, the average Indian household would have to generate a rise of 3.3 percent in income to maintain their calorie intake.
sentences.zh: 阿特金计算出，如果印度所有的内部贸易壁垒都被取消，普通印度家庭将不得不让收入增长百分之三点三，才能维持他们的热量摄入。

sentences.en: G In developing countries where there is a high prevalence of undernutrition, such as in sub-Saharan Africa, the habit of continuing to eat favourite foods could have a serious effect on development.
sentences.zh: 在营养不良高发的发展中国家，比如撒哈拉以南非洲，继续吃最爱食物的习惯可能对发展产生严重影响。

sentences.en: There is clear evidence that nutritional shortfalls in children can affect their ability to work and earn as adults, and also have detrimental effects on their long-term health.
sentences.zh: 有明确的证据表明，儿童营养不足会影响他们成年后工作和挣钱的能力，也会对他们的长期健康产生有害影响。

sentences.en: Consequently, the nutritional declines that can occur as a result of the opening up of trade are of serious concern, because an entire generation that is malnourished as children will continue to suffer irreversible consequences for the rest of their lives, which could hinder the development of their country due to a lack of a quality workforce.
sentences.zh: 因此，可能由于开放贸易而发生的营养下降是严重的关切，因为整整一代在儿童时期营养不良的人将在余生中继续承受不可逆的后果，这可能由于缺乏优质劳动力而阻碍其国家的发展。

records.title: Looking at daily life in ancient Rome
records.titleZh: 观察古罗马的日常生活

sentences.en: A If our ideas on Roman life are not to become lost in confusion, we must study it within a strictly defined time.
sentences.zh: 若不想让我们对罗马生活的认识陷入混乱，就必须在严格限定的时间范围内加以研究。

sentences.en: Nothing changes more rapidly than human customs.
sentences.zh: 没有什么比人类的风俗习惯变化得更快。

sentences.en: Looking at our own more familiar world, apart from the great scientific discoveries of recent centuries which have turned it upside down—steam, electricity, railways, motor cars and aeroplanes, for example—it is clear that the elementary forms of everyday life have been subject to increasing change.
sentences.zh: 看看我们更为熟悉的当今世界，除了近几个世纪那些把它彻底颠覆的重大科学发现——例如蒸汽机、电力、铁路、汽车和飞机——之外，显而易见，日常生活的种种基本形态也在经历着日益加剧的变化。

sentences.en: Potatoes, for example, were not introduced into Europe until the sixteenth century, coffee was first drunk there in the late sixteenth or early seventeenth, and the banana was used in desserts in Europe at the beginning of the twentieth.
sentences.zh: 例如，马铃薯直到16世纪才传入欧洲，咖啡在那里最早被饮用是在16世纪末或17世纪初，而香蕉用于欧洲的甜点则要到20世纪初。

sentences.en: The law of change was not less operative in antiquity.
sentences.zh: 变化的法则在古代同样发挥着作用。

sentences.en: It was a commonplace of Roman rhetoric to contrast the crude simplicity of the Republic (509BC–27BC) with the luxury and refinement of the imperial times which followed.
sentences.zh: 把共和国时期（公元前509年至前27年）的粗陋质朴，与其后帝国时代的奢华精致相对照，是罗马修辞中司空见惯的做法。

sentences.en: There is no common measure, whether of home, or house, or furniture, between ages which are so different.
sentences.zh: 在如此迥异的时代之间，无论是家庭、房屋还是家具，都没有共同的衡量标准。

sentences.en: B Since a choice of time must necessarily be made, this history will confine itself to studying the generation which was born about the middle of the first century AD, toward the end of the reign of Claudius (41–54AD) or the beginning of the reign of Nero (54–68AD), and which lived on into the reign of Trajan (98–117AD) or of Hadrian (117–138AD).
sentences.zh: 既然时间的选取势在必行，本书便仅限于研究这样一代人：他们大约生于公元1世纪中叶，即克劳狄乌斯（公元41至54年在位）统治末期或尼禄（公元54至68年在位）统治初期，并一直活到图拉真（公元98至117年在位）或哈德良（公元117至138年在位）统治之时。

sentences.en: This generation saw the Roman Empire at its most powerful and prosperous.
sentences.zh: 这一代人见证了罗马帝国最为强盛繁荣的时期。

sentences.en: It was witness to the last conquests of the Caesars: the conquest of Dacia, in modern-day eastern Europe, which brought vast mineral wealth into the Empire, and the conquest of Arabia, which helped to bring the riches of India and East Asia flooding into Rome.
sentences.zh: 它见证了历代凯撒最后的征服：对达契亚（位于今日东欧）的征服，为帝国带来了巨量的矿产财富；以及对阿拉伯的征服，使印度和东亚的财富源源不断地涌入罗马。

sentences.en: In the material domain, this generation attained the pinnacle of ancient civilisation.
sentences.zh: 在物质领域，这一代人达到了古代文明的巅峰。

sentences.en: C By a fortunate coincidence—all the more fortunate in that Latin literature was soon to run nearly dry—this generation is the one whose records combine to offer us the most complete picture of Roman life that we possess.
sentences.zh: 出于一种幸运的巧合——拉丁文学不久便几近枯竭，这就更显其幸运——正是这一代人留下的种种记载汇集在一起，为我们提供了所能拥有的、有关罗马生活最完整的图景。

sentences.en: We have a profusion of vivid and picturesque descriptions, precise and colourful, in such works as the Epigrams of Martial, the Satires of Juvenal and the Letters of Pliny.
sentences.zh: 在马提亚尔的《警句集》、尤维纳利斯的《讽刺诗集》以及普林尼的《书信集》等作品中，我们拥有大量生动如画、精确而多彩的描写。

sentences.en: In addition, the Forum of Trajan in Rome itself and the ruins of Herculaneum and Pompeii, the two prosperous resorts buried by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79AD, supply an immense fund of archaeological evidence.
sentences.zh: 此外，罗马城内的图拉真广场，以及赫库兰尼姆和庞贝——这两座在公元79年维苏威火山喷发中被掩埋的繁华胜地——的遗址，提供了浩如烟海的考古证据。

sentences.en: Later excavations have also restored to us the ruins of the city of Ostia, which date in the main from the time when the Emperor Hadrian created this great commercial city as a realisation of his town planning ideas.
sentences.zh: 后来的发掘还使我们重新得见奥斯蒂亚城的遗址，这些遗址大体可追溯到哈德良皇帝将这座宏大的商业城市建成、以实现其城市规划构想的时代。

sentences.en: Fortune has favoured the historian of this time.
sentences.zh: 命运眷顾了研究这一时代的历史学家。

sentences.en: D It is not enough to focus our study of Roman life only on a fixed time.
sentences.zh: 仅把我们对罗马生活的研究聚焦于某个固定的时间，是不够的。

sentences.en: It would lack foundation and consistency if we did not also focus it in space—in the country or in the town.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不同时在空间上加以聚焦——即聚焦于乡村还是城镇——研究就会缺乏根基与连贯性。

sentences.en: Even today when the facilities for communication bring something of the city into the smallest and most isolated country cottage, there remains a significant difference between rural existence and the excitement of city life: a much greater gulf separated the peasant from the townsman of antiquity.
sentences.zh: 即便在今天，通讯设施已把城市的某些气息带进了最偏小、最孤立的乡间小屋，乡村生活与城市生活的喧闹之间仍存在显著差别；而在古代，农民与城里人之间隔着大得多的鸿沟。

sentences.en: So large was the inequality between them that, according to the historian Rostovtzeff, it pitted one against the other in a fierce and silent struggle which pierced the wall protecting the Roman privileged classes from the barbarian flood from the north.
sentences.zh: 据历史学家罗斯托夫采夫所言，他们之间的不平等如此之大，以致使双方陷入一场激烈而无声的斗争，这场斗争冲破了那道把罗马特权阶层与来自北方的蛮族洪流隔开的壁垒。

sentences.en: When the barbarian forces began to invade Roman territory, the peasants decided to fight alongside them.
sentences.zh: 当蛮族军队开始入侵罗马疆土时，农民们决定与之并肩作战。

sentences.en: E The townsman, in fact, enjoyed all the goods and resources of the earth.
sentences.zh: 事实上，城里人享有大地上一切的物产与资源。

sentences.en: The peasant knew nothing but unending labour without profit, and was unable to enjoy the activities available in even the poorest of cities: the liveliness of the sports field, the warmth of the public baths and the magnificence of public spectacles.
sentences.zh: 农民所知的只有无休无止、毫无收益的劳作，连最贫穷的城市里都能享有的活动也无从享受：运动场的热闹、公共浴场的温暖，以及公共演出的盛大。

sentences.en: In a work on the history of everyday life, we must give up any attempt to blend two such dissimilar pictures into one, and must choose between them.
sentences.zh: 在一部关于日常生活史的著作中，我们必须放弃将两幅如此迥异的图景糅合为一的任何企图，而必须在二者之间作出取舍。

sentences.en: The time which we have chosen to describe day by day is that of those Roman subjects who spent their time exclusively in the town, or rather in The City, Rome, which they regarded as the hub and centre of the universe, proud and wealthy ruler of a world which seemed at that time to have been pacified for ever.
sentences.zh: 我们选择逐日加以描述的，是那些完全生活在城镇——或者不如说生活在“那座城”，即罗马——之中的罗马臣民的时代；他们把罗马视为宇宙的枢纽与中心，视为一个当时仿佛已被永远平定的世界中那位骄傲而富有的统治者。

sentences.en: F To perform our task well, we must first try to form an adequate picture of the surroundings in which our subjects lived, and by which their lives were coloured, freeing ourselves from any misconceptions concerning it.
sentences.zh: 要出色地完成我们的任务，就必须首先努力对我们所研究的对象赖以生活、并为其生活染上色彩的环境形成一幅恰当的图景，同时摆脱关于它的任何误解。

sentences.en: We must seek to reconstruct the physical nature of the great city and the social milieu of the various classes of the hierarchy by which it was governed.
sentences.zh: 我们必须设法重建这座伟大城市的物质面貌，以及统治它的等级制度中各个阶层的社会环境。

sentences.en: We must also investigate the moral background of thought and sentiment which can help explain both its strength and its weaknesses.
sentences.zh: 我们还必须考察其思想与情感的道德背景，这有助于解释它的强大之处与弱点所在。

sentences.en: The way in which the Romans of Rome employed their time can only be studied satisfactorily after we have plotted out the main lines of the framework within which they lived and outside of which the routine of their daily life would be more or less unintelligible.
sentences.zh: 只有在我们勾勒出他们赖以生活的框架的主要脉络之后，才能令人满意地研究罗马城的罗马人是如何利用其时间的；离开了这一框架，他们日常生活的种种常规便或多或少令人费解。

sentences.en: A Two of the great British men of the 17th century, the philosopher John Locke and the physicist Isaac Newton, were both aware that objects are not coloured, and that against all appearances light is not coloured either.
sentences.zh: 17 世纪英国的两位伟人——哲学家约翰·洛克（John Locke）和物理学家艾萨克·牛顿——都知道物体并不是有颜色的，与表象相反，光也不是有颜色的。

sentences.en: This is still not generally recognised even now, 400 years later, because it seems so implausible.
sentences.zh: 即便在 400 年后的今天，这一点也并不被普遍承认，因为它看上去太不可信。

sentences.en: Yet it tells us something very important — that perceptions are not identical with what we perceive, and may be very different.
sentences.zh: 然而它告诉我们一件非常重要的事——知觉与我们所感知到的东西并不相同，可能差异很大。

sentences.en: The most accurate historical account of perception is that of the 19th-century German scientist Hermann von Helmholtz.
sentences.zh: 最准确的知觉历史阐述出自 19 世纪德国科学家赫尔曼·冯·亥姆霍兹（Hermann von Helmholtz）。

sentences.en: However, it was ridiculed at the time.
sentences.zh: 然而他的观点在当时被嘲笑。

sentences.en: Von Helmholtz thought that perceptions are unconscious inferences we make based on a combination of clues provided by the eyes and other senses, and knowledge of the world.
sentences.zh: 冯·亥姆霍兹认为，知觉是我们基于眼睛和其他感官所提供的线索与对世界的知识，作出的无意识推断。

sentences.en: This idea of unconscious inference for perception preceded, by several years, the psychoanalyst Freud's notion of the unconscious, which was also initially treated with derision because it undermined the notion of humans as pre-eminently rational beings who could be held responsible for their actions and awarded blame or praise accordingly.
sentences.zh: 这种“知觉是无意识推断”的想法比精神分析学家弗洛伊德的“无意识”概念早了好几年，而后者最初也曾被嘲笑——因为它动摇了“人类是出类拔萃的理性存在、能为自己的行为负责并因之获罪或受赞”的观念。

sentences.en: B Crucially, perception of the present depends on rich, though of course not always correct or appropriate, knowledge from the past.
sentences.zh: 关键在于，对当下的感知依赖于丰富的、当然也未必总是正确或恰当的来自过去的知识。

sentences.en: We interpret sense data (what we hear, touch, taste, see and smell) from the present according to what we already know.
sentences.zh: 我们根据已知的内容来诠释当前的感官数据（我们听到、触到、尝到、看到和闻到的东西）。

sentences.en: This raises the question: if we see the present through memory, why aren't past and present confused?
sentences.zh: 这就引出一个问题：如果我们透过记忆看当下，为什么过去与当下不会被混淆？

sentences.en: The pioneering Russian neurologist Alexander Luria described the case of Mr S, who had a remarkable memory.
sentences.zh: 开创性的俄罗斯神经学家亚历山大·卢里亚（Alexander Luria）描述过一位记忆力非凡的 S 先生。

sentences.en: However, it was prone to just such confusions, for example mistaking seeing his clock for remembering it, and so failing to get up in the morning.
sentences.zh: 然而这种记忆容易引发那种混淆——例如把“看到自己的钟”和“记得这个钟”弄混，因而早上起不来。

sentences.en: This suggests that perhaps an important function of perception is to underline the present.
sentences.zh: 这表明知觉的一个重要功能或许就是凸显当下。

sentences.en: Individual perceptions have a vividness that is rare for memories, which might be how we are able to separate them.
sentences.zh: 个别的知觉具有一种生动性，这种生动性对于记忆而言是罕见的；这或许是我们能把它们区分开的方式。

sentences.en: Try this: look at something for a few seconds, and then shut your eyes and visualise it in memory.
sentences.zh: 试一下：盯着某物看几秒，然后闭上眼睛在记忆中可视化它。

sentences.en: You will almost certainly find that the memory is pale by comparison with the perception.
sentences.zh: 你几乎肯定会发现，与知觉相比，记忆是苍白的。

sentences.en: Perhaps this is why past and present are not normally confused.
sentences.zh: 这或许是为什么过去与当下通常不会被混淆。

sentences.en: Luria's Mr S had exceptionally vivid memories, and rich synaesthesia (experiencing perceptions from another sense as well as the one being stimulated, such as musical notes experienced as colours), which may be why he confused seeing with having seen.
sentences.zh: 卢里亚的 S 先生有特别生动的记忆，还有丰富的联觉（在受刺激的感官之外还体验到来自另一种感官的知觉，例如把音符体验为色彩）——这或许是他把“看见”与“曾经看见”弄混的原因。

sentences.en: C The complexity of processes involved in how we see first impressed itself on me 45 years ago.
sentences.zh: 我们如何看见——其中所涉及过程的复杂性——在 45 年前第一次给我留下了深刻印象。

sentences.en: With my colleague Jean Wallace, I studied the rare case of Sydney Bradford, a man who had been born blind but, through a corneal graft at the age of 52, suddenly found himself able to see.
sentences.zh: 我与同事让·华莱士（Jean Wallace）一起研究了西德尼·布拉德福德（Sydney Bradford）这一罕见病例——这位男士天生失明，但在 52 岁时通过角膜移植，突然发现自己能看见了。

sentences.en: Almost immediately after the operation he was able to 'see' but he could only see those things that he already knew about, having experienced them through touch.
sentences.zh: 手术后几乎是立刻，他就能“看到”，但他只能看到那些他已经通过触摸经验过、因而已经知道的事物。

sentences.en: It was his touch memories that enabled him to perceive them with his eyes.
sentences.zh: 正是他的触觉记忆让他能够用眼睛感知它们。

sentences.en: When Bradford was first taken to the zoo, he proved utterly unable to see an elephant as he had no knowledge to make sense of his perceptions.
sentences.zh: 布拉德福德第一次被带去动物园时，他完全无法“看见”一头大象——因为他没有可以让他对自己的知觉作出意义化解释的知识。

sentences.en: The more recent case in California of Mike May, who was also born blind, is similar.
sentences.zh: 加州迈克·梅（Mike May）的一个更近的病例也类似——他也是天生失明的。

sentences.en: Since his operation, his sight has gradually improved as he learns to see, for example, by understanding how shadows represent depth and tell us about the shape of things.
sentences.zh: 自手术以来，他的视力随着学习“看见”而逐渐改善——例如，通过理解阴影如何代表深度并告诉我们物体的形状。

sentences.en: Some of the consequences of May's new-found vision were less happy.
sentences.zh: 梅新获得的视力带来的某些后果并不那么愉快。

sentences.en: He had been a champion blind skier, but following the operation, he would have to shut his eyes while skiing to block out what he now found was a terrifying sight.
sentences.zh: 他曾是盲人滑雪冠军，但手术之后，他在滑雪时不得不闭上眼睛，以屏蔽他现在所发现的令人恐惧的景象。

sentences.en: D But acceptance of this intimate connection between memory and perception, even though it was first noticed in the 17th century, has been slow in brain science.
sentences.zh: 但对“记忆与知觉之间这种紧密联系”的接受——尽管 17 世纪就已被注意到——在脑科学中一直进展缓慢。

sentences.en: Despite the fact that state-of-the-art brain imaging shows that perception animates parts of the brain associated with both present information and memory, most research on memory and perception is still undertaken as if these were separate processes.
sentences.zh: 尽管最先进的脑成像显示，知觉激活了大脑中既与当前信息相关、也与记忆相关的部位，但大多数关于记忆与知觉的研究仍把它们视为独立过程来开展。

sentences.en: Seeing used to be thought of as taking place only in the eyes, and in quite specialised brain regions; but now it seems that half the brain is occupied with seeing, requiring a lot of energy.
sentences.zh: 过去人们认为“看见”只发生在眼睛里，以及大脑中相当专门的区域；但现在看来，大脑的一半都被“看见”所占据，并需要大量能量。

sentences.en: Perhaps this is why we shut our eyes for a rest.
sentences.zh: 这或许正是为什么我们要闭上眼睛休息一下。

sentences.en: It is not just extreme cases like Mike May, but also much more common errors of seeing — illusions — that can reveal the crucial role of memory in governing what we (think we) see.
sentences.zh: 不仅是迈克·梅这样的极端病例，还有更常见得多的“看见”的失误——错觉——也能揭示记忆在支配我们（自以为）看到什么这一点上的关键作用。

sentences.en: Perception depends on specific knowledge and probabilities.
sentences.zh: 知觉依赖于具体的知识与概率。

sentences.en: Our brains calculate the likelihood of what is out there, and when too far-fetched, perceptions are rejected.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑计算外界事物的可能性；当太离谱时，知觉就被拒绝。

sentences.en: A dramatic and discomforting example is looking at the two sides of a face-mask.
sentences.zh: 一个戏剧性而令人不适的例子是观察面具的两侧。

sentences.en: From the front it is a convex shape with the nose sticking out.
sentences.zh: 从正面看，它是一个凸出的形状，鼻子是突出的。

sentences.en: Then if the mask is rotated, the back of the mask will be seen as convex, though we know that it must be concave.
sentences.zh: 然后如果把面具旋转过去，面具的背面也会被看成凸的——尽管我们知道它必定是凹的。

sentences.en: It is almost, if not quite, impossible to sketch the back of a hollow mask to look as it is — hollow.
sentences.zh: 要把一个空心面具的背面照其实际样子（凹的）画出来，几乎——如果不是完全——不可能。

sentences.en: Science often learns from what does not happen: people not seeing a hollow face as hollow is the most revealing experiment on perception.
sentences.zh: 科学常常从“未发生之事”中学习：人们把空心的脸看成不空心的——这就是关于知觉的最具揭示性的实验。

sentences.en: The unsettling truth from brain science is that even people with no visual impairment see what, at some level, they expect to see, and often miss things as they really are.
sentences.zh: 脑科学给出的不安真相是：即使是视力没有任何损伤的人，在某种层面上也是看到他们所预期看到的东西，而常常错过事物的真实面貌。

records.title: Petrol power an eco-revolution
records.titleZh: 石油动力，一场生态革命

sentences.en: A Laura Ingalls Wilder's semi-autobiographical novel The Long Winter describes how the inhabitants of a small town called De Smet in the American Midwest narrowly avoided starvation during the severe winter of 1880–1881.
sentences.zh: 劳拉·英格尔斯·怀尔德的半自传体小说《漫长的冬天》描述了美国中西部一个叫德斯梅特的小镇的居民，如何在1880到1881年那个严酷的冬天勉强避免了饿死。

sentences.en: Over three metres of snow fell on the northern plains, immobilising the railways and cutting off the settlers from the rest of the world.
sentences.zh: 三米多的雪落在北部平原上，使铁路瘫痪，把定居者与世界其余部分隔绝开来。

sentences.en: Laura and her neighbours were only saved when her fiancé and his friend trudged 30 kilometres through the snow to fetch food, risking their lives in the process.
sentences.zh: 劳拉和她的邻居们只有在她的未婚夫和他的朋友冒着生命危险、在雪中跋涉30公里去取食物时才得救。

sentences.en: The story is a reminder of how lethal geographical isolation and crop failures could be before the advent of modern farming and transportation technologies.
sentences.zh: 这个故事提醒人们，在现代农业和运输技术出现之前，地理上的孤立和庄稼歉收可能有多么致命。

sentences.en: Not long ago, subsistence farmers in many countries had to cope with the 'lean season' – the period of greatest scarcity before new crops became available.
sentences.zh: 不久之前，许多国家自给自足的农民还不得不应对“青黄不接的季节”——新庄稼上市前最匮乏的时期。

sentences.en: In England, late spring was once referred to as the 'hungry gap'.
sentences.zh: 在英格兰，晚春曾经被称为“饥饿的缺口”。

sentences.en: The situation was made worse by the cost of moving heavy things over muddy dirt roads; three centuries ago, moving goods 50 kilometres on land between, say, Liverpool and Manchester was as expensive as shipping them across the North Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 在泥泞土路上搬运重物的成本使情况更糟；三个世纪前，在陆地上、比如利物浦和曼彻斯特之间搬运货物50公里，和把它们横跨北大西洋运送一样昂贵。

sentences.en: B The development of coal-powered railways and steamships in the 19th century revolutionized the lives of farmers.
sentences.zh: 十九世纪燃煤铁路和蒸汽船的发展彻底改变了农民的生活。

sentences.en: Instead of having to grow everything they needed, they could now specialise in what they did best and rely on other producers for their remaining needs.
sentences.zh: 他们不必再种植自己需要的一切，现在可以专注于自己最擅长的、并依靠其他生产者来满足其余的需求。

sentences.en: The result was not only food and ever-cheaper prices, but the end of widespread famine and starvation, as the surplus from regions with good harvests could now be transported to those that had experienced mediocre ones.
sentences.zh: 其结果不仅是食物以及越来越便宜的价格，还有大范围饥荒和饥饿的终结，因为收成好的地区的余粮现在可以被运送到那些收成平平的地区。

sentences.en: Since then, petroleum-derived fuels have largely displaced coal because of their higher energy density, cleaner combustion and greater ease of extraction, further improving road and rail transportation systems.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，石油衍生燃料因其更高的能量密度、更清洁的燃烧和更易于开采，已在很大程度上取代了煤，进一步改善了公路和铁路运输系统。

sentences.en: C While the convenience of modern methods of transportation is obvious, few people grasp their historical significance in terms of their beneficial impact on large cities and the health of residents.
sentences.zh: 虽然现代运输方式的便利显而易见，但很少有人就其对大城市和居民健康的有益影响而把握它们的历史意义。

sentences.en: In 1898, delegates gathered in New York City for the world's first international urban-planning conference.
sentences.zh: 在1898年，代表们聚集在纽约市参加世界上第一次国际城市规划会议。

sentences.en: The topic that dominated discussions was not infrastructure or housing, but horse manure.
sentences.zh: 主导讨论的话题不是基础设施或住房，而是马粪。

sentences.en: The problem was that as the populations of cities like New York and London grew, the number of horses there also grew, and in New York these produced nearly two million kilograms of manure each day.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，随着纽约和伦敦这样城市的人口增长，那里的马的数量也增长，而在纽约这些马每天产出近两百万千克的粪便。

sentences.en: If this problem continued, it was estimated that by 1950 every street in London would be buried three metres deep in horse manure.
sentences.zh: 据估计，如果这个问题继续下去，到1950年伦敦的每一条街道都会被三米深的马粪埋住。

sentences.en: Unable to think of any solution, the delegates concluded that urban living was inherently unsustainable.
sentences.zh: 想不出任何解决办法，代表们得出结论说，城市生活本质上是不可持续的。

sentences.en: D Paradoxically, much of the urban manure problem was related to the growth of the railways.
sentences.zh: 矛盾的是，城市马粪问题的很大一部分与铁路的增长有关。

sentences.en: The ability to deliver perishable goods, such as meat and dairy products, from locations that benefited from better soil and climate, put many farms located near cities out of business.
sentences.zh: 从土壤和气候更好的地方运送肉类和乳制品等易腐货物的能力，使许多位于城市附近的农场倒闭。

sentences.en: As these had relied on manure from city workhorses for fertiliser, the demand for this was greatly reduced.
sentences.zh: 由于这些农场曾依赖城市役马的粪便作肥料，对这种肥料的需求大大减少了。

sentences.en: The impact of urban workhorses was felt both in the cities and in the countryside.
sentences.zh: 城市役马的影响在城市和乡村都被感受到。

sentences.en: In cities, apart from their overpowering stench, the manure piles were prime breeding grounds for house flies, perhaps three billion of which hatched each day in US cities in the early 20th century.
sentences.zh: 在城市里，除了它们刺鼻的恶臭之外，粪堆还是家蝇绝佳的繁殖地，在二十世纪初的美国城市里，也许每天有三十亿只家蝇在那里孵化。

sentences.en: With flies came outbreaks of typhoid, cholera and diphtheria.
sentences.zh: 随苍蝇而来的是伤寒、霍乱和白喉的暴发。

sentences.en: Workhorses sometimes panicked in heavy traffic and kicked or bit bystanders.
sentences.zh: 役马有时在繁忙的交通中惊慌，踢伤或咬伤旁观者。

sentences.en: The clatter of wagon wheels on cobblestone pavement could be deafening, and since a horse and wagon occupied more street space than a modern truck, they also created significant traffic congestion, while a horse that collapsed on the road created an obstruction that was difficult to remove.
sentences.zh: 马车车轮在鹅卵石路面上的咔嗒声可能震耳欲聋，而由于一匹马加一辆马车占用的街道空间比一辆现代卡车更多，它们还造成了严重的交通拥堵，而一匹倒在路上的马则造成一个难以清除的障碍。

sentences.en: The countryside also suffered.
sentences.zh: 乡村也受了苦。

sentences.en: To supply the workhorses with oats and hay, additional land had to be cleared of its natural animal life and vegetation, and sometimes water had to be diverted to irrigate it, with considerable negative effects on the whole area.
sentences.zh: 为了给役马供应燕麦和干草，不得不清除更多土地上的天然动物和植被，有时还不得不引水来灌溉它，对整个地区造成相当大的负面影响。

sentences.en: E So, while the trains, cars and trucks of the early 20th century were noisy and polluting by today's standards, they were regarded as a significant improvement on what had gone before.
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管二十世纪初的火车、汽车和卡车以今天的标准看是嘈杂而污染的，但它们被视为对此前之物的一个重大改进。

sentences.en: Before they were available, poor soils often meant that a large amount of land was required to sustain a household, and much environmental damage, primarily in the form of soil erosion, was caused by trying to farm these soils.
sentences.zh: 在它们可用之前，贫瘠的土壤往往意味着需要大量土地来维持一个家庭，而试图耕种这些土壤造成了许多环境破坏，主要是以水土流失的形式。

sentences.en: It could be argued that modern transportation allowed the development of remote regions like the Canadian Prairies and allowed more suitable crops to be grown in the poorer soils in Europe before being sold elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 可以认为，现代运输使加拿大草原这样的偏远地区得以开发，并使更合适的作物得以在欧洲较贫瘠的土壤里种植、然后销往别处。

sentences.en: F Over time, the concentration of food production in the world's best locations allowed some agricultural land to revert to a wild state.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，食物生产向世界最佳地点的集中，使一些农业用地得以恢复到野生状态。

sentences.en: For instance, France benefited from an expansion of its forest area by one third between 1830 and 1960.
sentences.zh: 比如，法国在1830到1960年间受益于其森林面积扩大了三分之一。

sentences.en: This so-called 'forest transition' occurred in the context of a doubling of the French population and a dramatic increase in standards of living.
sentences.zh: 这种所谓的“森林转型”发生在法国人口翻倍、生活水平急剧提高的背景下。

sentences.en: Improvements in logistics also allowed the production and export of food from locations where water was abundant to regions where it was scarce, thus preventing the depletion of water resources there.
sentences.zh: 物流的改善还使食物得以从水资源丰富的地方生产并出口到水资源稀缺的地区，从而防止了那里水资源的枯竭。

sentences.en: It also made possible a drastic increase in the size of our cities.
sentences.zh: 它还使我们城市规模的急剧扩大成为可能。

sentences.en: Contrary to what most people believe, the growth in cities is a positive development.
sentences.zh: 与大多数人所相信的相反，城市的增长是一种积极的发展。

sentences.en: In the words of economist Ed Glaeser: 'Residing in a forest might seem to be a good way of showing one's love of nature, but living in a concrete jungle is actually far more ecologically friendly...
sentences.zh: 用经济学家埃德·格莱泽的话说：“住在森林里也许看起来是表达一个人对自然之爱的好办法，但住在钢筋水泥丛林里实际上要环保得多……

sentences.en: If you love nature, stay away from it.'
sentences.zh: 如果你热爱自然，就离它远点。”

sentences.en: It could be argued that modern transportation technologies have been a major contributor to a wealthier, cleaner and more sustainable world.
sentences.zh: 可以认为，现代运输技术一直是一个更富裕、更清洁、更可持续世界的主要贡献者。

records.title: Australia's Megafauna Controversy
records.titleZh: 澳大利亚大型动物争议

sentences.en: A Over the past 50 millennia, Australia has witnessed the extinction of many species of large animals, including a rhinoceros-sized wombat and goannas the size of crocodiles.
sentences.zh: 在过去五万年里，澳大利亚见证了许多大型动物物种的灭绝，包括一种犀牛大小的袋熊和鳄鱼大小的巨蜥。

sentences.en: Debate about the possible cause of these extinctions has continued for more than 150 years, and one of the crucial questions raised is how long humans and megafauna coexisted in Australia.
sentences.zh: 关于这些灭绝可能原因的争论已持续了150多年，而提出的关键问题之一是，人类和巨型动物群在澳大利亚共存了多久。

sentences.en: We need to know the overlap of time to make an informed choice between the two main theories regarding the causes of these extinctions.
sentences.zh: 我们需要知道时间上的重叠，才能在关于这些灭绝原因的两种主要理论之间做出明智的选择。

sentences.en: If humans and megafauna coexisted for a protracted period, then climate change is the more likely cause.
sentences.zh: 如果人类和巨型动物群共存了一段漫长的时期，那么气候变化是更可能的原因。

sentences.en: However, if the megafauna became extinct shortly after the arrival of humans, then humans are the likely culprits.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果巨型动物群在人类到来后不久就灭绝了，那么人类就是可能的罪魁祸首。

sentences.en: B The archaeological site at Cuddie Springs in eastern Australia appears to be well preserved.
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚东部卡迪泉的考古遗址似乎保存完好。

sentences.en: This dusty claypan holds within its sediments a rich cache of flaked stone and seed-grinding tools, and side by side with these clear signals of human culture are the bones of a dozen or more species of megafauna.
sentences.zh: 这片尘土飞扬的黏土盘地在其沉积物中藏着丰富的一批打制石器和磨种子工具，而与这些清晰的人类文化信号并排的是十几种或更多巨型动物群的骨头。

sentences.en: Drs Judith Field and Stephen Wroe of the University of Sydney, who excavated the site, claim that it provides unequivocal evidence of a long overlap of humans and megafauna, and conclude that aridity leading up to the last Ice Age brought about their eventual demise.
sentences.zh: 发掘这处遗址的悉尼大学的朱迪思·菲尔德博士和斯蒂芬·罗博士声称，它提供了人类和巨型动物群长期重叠的明确证据，并得出结论说，导向上一次冰期的干旱带来了它们最终的消亡。

sentences.en: In the long-standing explanation of this site, artefacts such as stone tools and extinct animal remains were deposited over many thousands of years in an ephemeral lake – a body of water existing for a relatively short time – and remained in place and undisturbed until the present day.
sentences.zh: 在对这处遗址长期以来的解释中，石器等人工制品和已灭绝动物遗骸在数千年里沉积于一个短暂的湖泊——一片存在时间相对较短的水体——中，并保持原位、未受扰动直到今日。

sentences.en: C There is no disputing the close association of bones and stones at Cuddie Springs, as both are found 1 to 1.7 metres below the modern surface.
sentences.zh: 卡迪泉骨头与石头的紧密关联是无可争辩的，因为两者都在现代地表以下1到1.7米处被发现。

sentences.en: The dating of these layers is accurate: ages for the sediments were obtained through radiocarbon dating of charcoal fragments and luminescence dating of sand grains from the same levels (revealing when a sample was last exposed to sunlight).
sentences.zh: 这些层位的年代测定是准确的：沉积物的年代是通过对木炭碎片进行放射性碳测年、以及对同一层位沙粒进行光释光测年（揭示样本上次暴露于阳光是什么时候）而获得的。

sentences.en: Intriguingly, some of the stone tools show surface features indicating their use for processing plants, and a few even have well-preserved blood and hair residues suggesting they were used in butchering animals.
sentences.zh: 耐人寻味的是，一些石器表现出表明其被用于加工植物的表面特征，而少数几件甚至有保存完好的血液和毛发残留，表明它们被用于宰杀动物。

sentences.en: D But is the case proposed by Field and Wroe clear-cut?
sentences.zh: 但菲尔德和罗所提出的论点是确凿无疑的吗？

sentences.en: We carried out a reanalysis of the scientific data from Cuddie Springs that brings into question their conclusions.
sentences.zh: 我们对来自卡迪泉的科学数据进行了重新分析，这让他们的结论受到质疑。

sentences.en: The amount of anthropological evidence found at the site is remarkable: we estimate there are more than 3 tonnes of charcoal and more than 300 tonnes of stone buried there.
sentences.zh: 该遗址发现的人类学证据数量惊人：我们估计那里埋着3吨多的木炭和300吨多的石头。

sentences.en: Field and Wroe estimate that there are approximately 20 million artefacts.
sentences.zh: 菲尔德和罗估计大约有两千万件人工制品。

sentences.en: This plethora of tools is hard to reconcile with a site that was only available for occupation when the lake was dry.
sentences.zh: 这么多的工具难以与一个只在湖干涸时才能被占用的遗址相调和。

sentences.en: Furthermore, no cultural features such as oven pits have been discovered.
sentences.zh: 此外，没有发现灶坑之类的文化特征。

sentences.en: If the sediment layers have remained undisturbed since being laid down, as Field and Wroe contend, then the ages of those sediments should increase with depth.
sentences.zh: 如果这些沉积层自沉积以来一直未受扰动，正如菲尔德和罗所主张的，那么这些沉积物的年代应该随深度增加。

sentences.en: However, our analysis revealed a number of inconsistencies.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们的分析揭示出若干不一致之处。

sentences.en: E First, the charcoal samples are all roughly 36,000 years old.
sentences.zh: 第一，木炭样本全都大约36000年之久。

sentences.en: Second, sand in the two upper levels is considerably younger than charcoal from the same levels.
sentences.zh: 第二，上面两层中的沙比同一层位的木炭年轻得多。

sentences.en: Third, Field and Wroe say that the tools and seed-grinding stones used for plant and animal processing are ancient, yet they are very similar to implements found elsewhere that were in use only a few thousand years ago.
sentences.zh: 第三，菲尔德和罗说用于加工植物和动物的工具及磨种子石很古老，然而它们与别处发现的、仅在几千年前还在使用的器具非常相似。

sentences.en: Also of interest is the fact that a deep drill core made a mere 60 metres from the site recovered no stone artefacts or fossil bones whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 同样有意思的是这样一个事实，即在离遗址仅仅60米处所做的一个深钻芯，没有取出任何石器或化石骨头。

sentences.en: These points suggest strongly that the sediments have been moved about and some of the old charcoal has been re-deposited in younger layers.
sentences.zh: 这些点有力地表明，这些沉积物曾被移动过，而一些古老的木炭被重新沉积到了更年轻的层位里。

sentences.en: Indeed, one sample of cow bone found 1 metre below the surface came from sediments where charcoal dated at 6,000 and 23,000 years old is mixed with 17,000-year-old sand.
sentences.zh: 的确，在地表以下1米处发现的一块牛骨，来自一处6000年和23000年之久的木炭与17000年之久的沙混在一起的沉积层。

sentences.en: The megafauna bones themselves have not yet been dated, although new technological developments make this a possibility in the near future.
sentences.zh: 巨型动物群的骨头本身尚未被测年，尽管新的技术发展使这在不久的将来成为一种可能。

sentences.en: F We propose that the archaeologists have actually been sampling the debris carried by ancient flood channels beneath the site, including charcoal transported from bushfires that intermittently occurred within the catchment.
sentences.zh: 我们认为，考古学家实际上一直在采样的是遗址下方古老洪水河道所携带的碎屑，包括从间歇性发生于集水区内丛林大火处运来的木炭。

sentences.en: Flood events more likely explain the accumulation of megafauna remains, and could have mixed old bones with fresh deposits.
sentences.zh: 洪水事件更可能解释巨型动物群遗骸的堆积，而且可能把古老的骨头与新鲜的沉积物混在了一起。

sentences.en: European graziers also disturbed the site in 1876 by constructing a well to provide water for their cattle.
sentences.zh: 欧洲牧场主在1876年也曾扰动这处遗址，他们建了一口井来为牛供水。

sentences.en: Given the expense of well-digging, we speculate that the graziers made sure it was protected from the damage caused by cattle hooves by lining the surface with small stones collected from further afield, including prehistoric quarries.
sentences.zh: 鉴于挖井的花费，我们推测牧场主确保它免受牛蹄造成的损害，办法是用从更远处、包括史前采石场收集来的小石头铺在表面。

sentences.en: This idea is consistent with the thin layer of stones spread over a large area, with cattle occasionally breaking through the gravel surface and forcing the stone and even cattle bones deeper into the waterlogged soil.
sentences.zh: 这一想法与铺在大片区域上的薄薄一层石头相符，牛偶尔会踩穿这层砾石表面、把石头乃至牛骨压进浸水的土壤更深处。

sentences.en: G The lack of conclusive evidence that humans and megafauna coexisted for a lengthy period casts doubt on Field and Wroe's assertion that climate change was responsible for the extinction of Australia's megafauna.
sentences.zh: 缺乏人类与巨型动物群长期共存的确凿证据，使菲尔德和罗关于气候变化导致澳大利亚巨型动物群灭绝的断言受到质疑。

sentences.en: However, we do not suggest that newly arrived, well-armed hunters systematically slaughtered all the large beasts they encountered.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们并不是说新到来的、武装精良的猎人系统性地屠杀了他们遇到的所有大型野兽。

sentences.en: Recent studies based on the biology of modern-day large mammals, combined with observations of people who still practise a traditional hunter-gatherer lifestyle, reveal an unexpected paradox and suggest a further possible explanation as to what happened.
sentences.zh: 最近基于现代大型哺乳动物生物学、并结合对仍在实行传统狩猎采集生活方式者的观察的研究，揭示出一个意想不到的悖论，并就所发生之事提出了一种进一步可能的解释。

sentences.en: Using a mathematical model, it was found that a group of 10 people killing only one juvenile Diprotodon each year would be sufficient to bring about the extinction of that species within 1,000 years.
sentences.zh: 利用一个数学模型，人们发现，一群10个人每年只杀一头幼年双门齿兽，就足以在1000年内使该物种灭绝。

sentences.en: This suggests that here, as in other parts of the world, the arrival of humans in lands previously inhabited only by animals created a volatile combination in which large animals fared badly.
sentences.zh: 这表明，在这里，正如在世界其他地方一样，人类到来到此前只有动物栖居的土地上，造就了一种不稳定的组合，而在其中大型动物处境很糟。

records.title: Child's Play in Medieval England
records.titleZh: 中世纪英格兰的儿童游戏

sentences.en: A 'Play up!
sentences.zh: “加油！

sentences.en: Play up!
sentences.zh: 加油！

sentences.en: And play the game!'
sentences.zh: 投入比赛！“

sentences.en: The ringing chorus of Sir Henry Newbolt's celebrated cricket poem 'Vitai Lampada' (1908) sums up views about play in 19th- and early 20th-century Britain.
sentences.zh: 亨利·纽博尔特爵士（Sir Henry Newbolt）著名板球诗《Vitai Lampada》（1908 年）中铿锵作响的合唱，概括了 19 世纪和 20 世纪初英国对游戏的看法。

sentences.en: Children's play was important, and adults should regulate and direct it.
sentences.zh: 儿童的玩耍很重要，而成年人应当对其加以规制和引导。

sentences.en: Games promoted endurance, self-discipline and team spirit – qualities needed for the health of society and government.
sentences.zh: 游戏培养耐力、自律和团队精神——社会与政府健康所需的品质。

sentences.en: Newbolt was one in a long line of people who thought in this way.
sentences.zh: 纽博尔特只是这种想法的长长队列中的一员。

sentences.en: The notion that children's play should be used for educational and social purposes goes back at least to the ancient Greeks and the toys and games of medieval England tell us much about how adults then saw childhood.
sentences.zh: 应把儿童的玩耍用于教育和社会目的的观念，至少可追溯到古希腊，而中世纪英格兰的玩具与游戏告诉我们很多当时成年人如何看待童年。

sentences.en: But they also reveal a good deal about children themselves, and cast light on what has recently become a controversial issue.
sentences.zh: 但这些玩具与游戏也大量揭示了儿童本身，并照亮了一个近来变得有争议的议题。

sentences.en: B Forty years ago, the French historian Philippe Aries argued, in Centuries of Childhood, that childhood in the Middle Ages did not exist in its modern sense.
sentences.zh: 四十年前，法国历史学家菲利普·阿利埃斯（Philippe Aries）在《童年的世纪》（Centuries of Childhood）中提出，中世纪的童年在现代意义上并不存在。

sentences.en: Children were regarded by adults with relatively little affection and followed a way of life not very different from that of their elders.
sentences.zh: 成人对儿童的关爱相对较少，儿童的生活方式与长辈相差不大。

sentences.en: More recent historians have disputed this, pointing to plentiful signs of parental affection and arguing that childhood, by its very nature, must always have been much the same.
sentences.zh: 更晚近的历史学家对此提出异议，指出父母关爱有大量迹象，并主张童年就其本质而言始终大致相同。

sentences.en: C In this debate play is crucial.
sentences.zh: 在这场争论中，玩耍至关重要。

sentences.en: Did adults encourage it?
sentences.zh: 成人鼓励它吗？

sentences.en: If so, did they see it as recreational (by providing toys, for example) or as educational (making children play in particular ways)?
sentences.zh: 如果鼓励，他们是把它视为娱乐性的（例如，提供玩具），还是教育性的（让孩子按特定方式玩）？

sentences.en: Did children play as their elders told them, or did they invent their own games, away from adults and even against their wishes?
sentences.zh: 儿童是按长辈所言去玩，还是发明自己的游戏，远离成人甚至违背他们的意愿？

sentences.en: These questions can be answered from a rich body of evidence including actual toys of the period, pictures of children's activities in contemporary manuscripts and literary sources such as religious works and dictionaries.
sentences.zh: 这些问题可以从一大批证据中得到解答，包括当时的实际玩具、当时手稿中描绘儿童活动的图画，以及宗教作品和词典等文学资料。

sentences.en: We know not only how medieval English children played but what their elders thought on the subject.
sentences.zh: 我们不仅了解中世纪英格兰儿童如何玩耍，还了解长辈对此的看法。

sentences.en: D We know, for example, that adults gave children toys from infancy onwards.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们知道成人从婴儿期起就给儿童玩具。

sentences.en: In 1398 the writer John Trevisa describes babies playing with 'a child's brooch', an object similar in function to the bright plastic toys given to babies today to bite and handle.
sentences.zh: 1398 年，作家约翰·特里维萨（John Trevisa）描述婴儿玩“a child’s brooch”——一种与今天给婴儿啃咬和抓握的彩色塑料玩具功能相似的物件。

sentences.en: William Horman, 16th-century author of a Latin textbook, talks of buying a rattle to stop a baby crying.
sentences.zh: 16 世纪一本拉丁文教材的作者威廉·霍尔曼（William Horman）谈到，会买一个拨浪鼓来止住婴儿的哭声。

sentences.en: Indeed, by 1300 it appears there was a toy industry in England.
sentences.zh: 事实上，到了 1300 年，英格兰似乎已有玩具产业。

sentences.en: Boys' toys often took military forms, such as the two metal soldiers of that date, found in London, and made from a mould.
sentences.zh: 男孩的玩具常呈军事形态，比如那个年代在伦敦发现的两个用模具铸造的金属士兵。

sentences.en: Girls had dolls, known before the 17th century as 'poppets' or puppets, commercially manufactured, imported and, in 1582, taxed at a halfpenny each.
sentences.zh: 女孩则有玩偶，17 世纪以前被称为“poppets”或木偶，由商业制造、进口而来；1582 年每件被征收半便士的税。

sentences.en: Not that children were by any means dependent on things that were bought for them.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着孩子完全依赖大人买给他们的东西。

sentences.en: Gerald of Wales recalls how he and his brothers built towns, palaces, churches and monasteries from sand at Manorbier Castle in about 1150 (perhaps on the nearby beach).
sentences.zh: 威尔士人吉拉尔德（Gerald of Wales）回忆说，约 1150 年他和兄弟们在玛诺比尔城堡（Manorbier Castle）用沙子搭建小镇、宫殿、教堂和修道院（也许是在附近的海滩上）。

sentences.en: E Active games were universal.
sentences.zh: 活动性游戏是普遍存在的。

sentences.en: In his English-to-Latin dictionary of 1440, a mysterious recluse known as Geoffrey mentions children playing 'tennis' and swinging on what he calls a 'totter' or 'merrytotter'.
sentences.zh: 在 1440 年的一本英语—拉丁语词典里，一位神秘的隐士杰弗里（Geoffrey）提到儿童玩“网球”，并在他称之为“totter”或“merrytotter”的器具上荡来荡去。

sentences.en: Children chased each other, swam and played ball games.
sentences.zh: 儿童彼此追逐、游泳并玩球类游戏。

sentences.en: Boys in the later Middle Ages shot arrows with bows, and archery is an example of a sport encouraged by adults, who wanted boys to grow up to play their part in what was, for most men, a warrior society.
sentences.zh: 中世纪后期的男孩用弓射箭，箭术就是一项被成人鼓励的运动——成人希望男孩长大后能在大多数男人都属于的尚武社会中担当其角色。

sentences.en: F However, by no means all children's military activity was directed by adults.
sentences.zh: 然而，并非所有儿童的军事活动都由成人指挥。

sentences.en: In 1400, six months after King Richard II had been overthrown by Henry IV, the children of London gathered together and chose themselves kings.
sentences.zh: 1400 年，国王理查二世被亨利四世推翻六个月后，伦敦的孩子们聚集起来，自行选出了“国王”。

sentences.en: Adam of Usk tells us they congregated 'in thousands ...
sentences.zh: 亚当·乌斯克（Adam of Usk）告诉我们，他们成千上万地聚在一起……

sentences.en: and made war upon each other ...
sentences.zh: 彼此交战……

sentences.en: whereby many died'.
sentences.zh: 由此许多人丧命“。

sentences.en: The new king had to order their parents and masters to stop them.
sentences.zh: 新国王不得不下令他们的父母和师傅们制止他们。

sentences.en: G This willingness of children to take the initiative in play, not just to wait for adults to direct them, is evident in the way they observed the calendar.
sentences.zh: 孩子在玩耍中愿意主动出击、而不只是等成人来指挥，这一点在他们观察日历的方式中显而易见。

sentences.en: Medieval life was regulated by light, weather, crops and the Church's cycle of fasts and festivals.
sentences.zh: 中世纪生活由光线、天气、庄稼和教会的斋戒与节日周期所调节。

sentences.en: Children shared in the adult round of religious festivals, but had their own observances as well, semi-detached from their elders.
sentences.zh: 儿童与成人共享宗教节日的轮回，但也有自己的庆典——半独立于长辈。

sentences.en: In the 1200s, the priest Thomas Docking remarked that in spring a child 'follows the ploughman; in autumn he accompanies the grape- gatherers'.
sentences.zh: 在 13 世纪，教士托马斯·多金（Thomas Docking）指出，春天里孩子“跟着犁地的人；秋天里他陪着采葡萄的人”。

sentences.en: In 1518, the poet Alexander Barclay records children playing with tops in March, looking for fruit in summer and making footballs by filling pigs' bladders with dried peas in autumn.
sentences.zh: 1518 年，诗人亚历山大·巴克利（Alexander Barclay）记录儿童 3 月玩陀螺、夏天找水果、秋天用猪膀胱装入晒干的豌豆做成足球。

sentences.en: H It is clear from this evidence that the relationship between adults and children in medieval society was, in major respects, a modern one.
sentences.zh: 从这些证据可以清楚地看出，中世纪社会中成人与儿童的关系在主要方面是一种现代的关系。

sentences.en: Parents took an indulgent interest in their children, providing them with toys and giving them time to play.
sentences.zh: 父母对孩子怀着宽厚的兴趣，给他们提供玩具，给他们玩耍的时间。

sentences.en: Children played in a wide variety of ways – imaginatively, skilfully, athletically and violently – developing their minds, bodies and social skills.
sentences.zh: 儿童以各种方式玩耍——富有想象力地、技巧地、富有体力地、也带有暴力性地——发展他们的心智、身体和社交技能。

sentences.en: Adults tried at times to direct play – partly to keep children in order, partly to give them skills for adult life – but children gravitated to one another and formed a culture of their own.
sentences.zh: 成人有时会试图引导玩耍——一方面是为了让儿童守规矩，一方面是为了让他们获得成人生活所需的技能——但儿童总会互相靠拢，形成属于自己的文化。

sentences.en: We can answer Aries's thesis, then, with a resounding 'No!'.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们可以对阿利埃斯的论点给出一个响亮的“不！”作为回答。

sentences.en: Childhood has always been much the same.
sentences.zh: 童年一直大致相同。

records.title: When people are 'deaf' to music
records.titleZh: 当人们对音乐“听而不闻”时

sentences.en: (A) Music has long been considered a uniquely human concept.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，音乐被视为人类独有的概念。

sentences.en: In fact, most psychologists agree that music is a universal human instinct.
sentences.zh: 事实上，多数心理学家同意：音乐是一种普世的人类本能。

sentences.en: Like any ability, however, there is great variation in people's musical competence.
sentences.zh: 然而，像任何能力一样，人们的音乐能力差异巨大。

sentences.en: For every brilliant pianist in the world, there are several people we refer to as 'tone deaf'.
sentences.zh: 世上每出现一位才华横溢的钢琴家，就有好几个我们称之为“五音不全”的人。

sentences.en: It is not simply that people with tone deafness (or 'amusia') are unable to sing in tune, they are also unable to discriminate between tones or recognize familiar melodies.
sentences.zh: 五音不全（或称 amusia）的人不仅唱歌跑调，他们还无法分辨音调或识别熟悉的旋律。

sentences.en: Such a 'disorder' can occur after some sort of brain damage, but recently research has been undertaken in an attempt to discover the cause of congenital amusia (when people are born with the condition), which is not associated with any brain damage, hearing problems, or lack of exposure to music.
sentences.zh: 这种“障碍”可能在某种脑损伤之后发生，但近来已经开展研究，试图弄清先天性 amusia（即出生时就有这种情况）的原因——它并不与任何脑损伤、听力问题或缺乏音乐接触相关。

sentences.en: (B) According to the research of Dr. Isabelle Peretz of the University of Montreal, amusia is more complicated than the inability to distinguish pitches.
sentences.zh: 根据蒙特利尔大学伊莎贝尔·佩雷茨博士（Dr. Isabelle Peretz）的研究，amusia 比单纯无法分辨音高复杂得多。

sentences.en: An amusic (a person who has the condition of amusia) can distinguish between two pitches that are far apart, but cannot tell the difference between intervals smaller than a half step on the Western diatonic scale, while most people can easily distinguish differences smaller than that.
sentences.zh: 一名 amusic（即患有 amusia 的人）可以分辨两个相距很远的音高，但无法分辨小于西方自然大音阶上半音的音程；而大多数人能轻松分辨更小的差异。

sentences.en: When listening to melodies which have had a single note altered so that it is out of key with the rest of the melody, they do not notice a problem.
sentences.zh: 在听到把其中一个音改得与旋律其余部分不在同一调上的旋律时，他们也不会觉察出问题。

sentences.en: As would be expected, amusics perform significantly worse at singing and tapping a rhythm along with a melody than do non-amusics.
sentences.zh: 正如所料，amusic 在与旋律同步歌唱和打节拍方面，表现明显不如非 amusic。

sentences.en: (C) The most fascinating aspect of amusia is how specific to music it is.
sentences.zh: amusia 最引人入胜的方面是它对音乐之特定。

sentences.en: Because of music's close ties to language, it might be expected that a musical impairment may be caused by a language impairment.
sentences.zh: 由于音乐与语言的紧密联系，人们会预期音乐上的缺陷可能由语言缺陷引起。

sentences.en: Studies suggest, however, that language and music ability are independent of one another.
sentences.zh: 然而研究表明，语言能力与音乐能力彼此独立。

sentences.en: People with brain damage in areas critical to language are often still able to sing, despite being unable to communicate through speech.
sentences.zh: 在语言关键区域有脑损伤的人通常仍能唱歌，尽管他们无法通过言语交流。

sentences.en: Moreover, while amusics show deficiencies in their recognition of pitch differences in melodies, they show no such deficiencies in tonal languages.
sentences.zh: 此外，虽然 amusic 在识别旋律的音高差异方面表现欠佳，但他们在声调语言上并没有这样的缺陷。

sentences.en: Amusics who speak tonal languages, such as Chinese, do not report having any difficulty discriminating between words that differ only in their intonation.
sentences.zh: 讲汉语等声调语言的 amusic 报告说，他们在仅靠语调不同的词之间分辨上没有困难。

sentences.en: The linguistic cues inherent in speech make discrimination of meaning much easier for amusics.
sentences.zh: 言语本身固有的语言线索使得 amusic 在分辨语义时容易得多。

sentences.en: Amusics are also successful most of the time at detecting the mood of a melody, can identify a speaker based on his or her voice and can discriminate and identify environmental sounds.
sentences.zh: amusic 也大多能成功识别一段旋律的情绪、能根据声音识别说话者，并且能分辨和识别环境声音。

sentences.en: (D) Recent work has been focused on locating the part of the brain that is responsible for amusia.
sentences.zh: 近期的工作集中在定位大脑中负责 amusia 的部分。

sentences.en: The temporal lobes of the brain, the location of the primary auditory cortex, have been considered.
sentences.zh: 大脑的颞叶——主要听觉皮层所在地——曾被考虑过。

sentences.en: It has long been believed that the temporal lobes, especially the right temporal lobe, are most active when engaged in musical activity, so any musical disability should logically stem from here as well.
sentences.zh: 长期以来人们认为，颞叶——尤其是右颞叶——在参与音乐活动时最活跃，因此任何音乐障碍按理也应源自这里。

sentences.en: Because it has been shown that there is no hearing deficit in amusia, researchers moved on to the temporal neocortex, which is where more sophisticated processing of musical cues was thought to take place.
sentences.zh: 由于已经证明 amusia 中没有听力缺陷，研究者转向颞新皮层——那里被认为发生着对音乐线索更复杂的加工。

sentences.en: New studies, however, have suggested that the deficits in amusics are located outside the auditory cortex.
sentences.zh: 然而新的研究表明，amusic 的缺陷位于听觉皮层之外。

sentences.en: Brain scans of amusics do not show any reaction at all to differences smaller than a half step.
sentences.zh: 对 amusic 的脑扫描显示，他们对小于半音的差异完全没有反应。

sentences.en: When changes in tones are large, their brains overreact, showing twice as much activity on the right side of the brain as a normal brain hearing the same thing.
sentences.zh: 当音调变化较大时，他们的大脑反应过度——右脑表现出的活动是正常大脑听到相同声音时的两倍。

sentences.en: These differences do not occur in the auditory cortex, indicating again that the deficits of amusia lie not in hearing impairment, but in higher processing of melodies.
sentences.zh: 这些差异不发生在听觉皮层中，再次表明 amusia 的缺陷不在于听力损伤，而在于对旋律的更高级加工。

sentences.en: (E) So what does this all mean?
sentences.zh: 那么，这一切意味着什么？

sentences.en: Looking only at the research of Peretz in the field of neuropsychology of music, it would appear that amusia is some sort of disorder.
sentences.zh: 如果只看佩雷茨在音乐神经心理学领域的研究，amusia 看起来确实像某种障碍。

sentences.en: As a student of neurobiology, however, I am skeptical.
sentences.zh: 但作为一名神经生物学专业的学生，我持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: Certainly the studies by Peretz that have found significant differences between the brains of so-called amusics and normal brains are legitimate.
sentences.zh: 佩雷茨发现 amusic 大脑与正常大脑之间存在显著差异的研究当然是有依据的。

sentences.en: The more important question now becomes one of normality.
sentences.zh: 现在更重要的问题是关于“何为正常”。

sentences.en: Every trait from skin color to intelligence to mood exists on a continuum—there is a great deal of variation from one extreme to the other.
sentences.zh: 从肤色到智力到情绪，每一种特质都处于一条连续谱上——从一端到另一端存在极大变化。

sentences.en: Just because we recognize that basic musical ability is something that the vast majority of people have, this doesn't mean that the lack of it is abnormal.
sentences.zh: 只是因为我们承认绝大多数人都具备基本的音乐能力，并不意味着缺乏这种能力就是不正常。

sentences.en: (F) What makes an amusic worse off than a musical prodigy?
sentences.zh: 是什么让 amusic 比音乐神童更糟糕呢？

sentences.en: Musical ability is culturally valued, and may have been a factor in survival at one point in human history, but it does not seem likely that it is being selected for on an evolutionary scale any longer.
sentences.zh: 音乐能力在文化上受到重视，且在人类历史的某一时刻可能是生存因素之一，但似乎在进化层面上它并未继续被选择。

sentences.en: Darwin believed that music was adaptive as a way of finding a mate, but who needs to be able to sing to find a partner in an age when it is possible to express your emotions through a song on your iPod?
sentences.zh: 达尔文认为音乐作为寻找配偶的方式是适应性的，但在一个可以通过 iPod 上的一首歌来表达情感的时代，谁还需要会唱歌才能找伴侣？

sentences.en: While the idea of amusia is interesting, it seems to be just one end of the continuum of innate musical ability.
sentences.zh: 虽然 amusia 这个想法很有趣，但它似乎只是先天音乐能力这条连续谱的一端而已。

sentences.en: Comparing this 'disorder' to learning disorders like a specific language impairment seems to be going too far.
sentences.zh: 把这种“障碍”比作特定语言障碍等学习障碍，似乎走得太远了。

sentences.en: Before amusia can be declared a disability, further research must be done to determine whether lack of musical ability is actually detrimental in any way.
sentences.zh: 在 amusia 可以被宣告为残疾之前，必须开展进一步研究以确定缺乏音乐能力是否真的在任何方面造成不利。

sentences.en: If no disadvantages can be found of having amusia, then it is no more a disability than having poor fashion sense or bad handwriting.
sentences.zh: 如果发现 amusia 没有任何劣势，那么它就并不比时尚感差或字迹潦草更应被视为残疾。

records.title: 200 Years of Australian Landscapes at the Royal Academy in London
records.titleZh: 伦敦皇家艺术学院举办的“澳大利亚景观200年”展览

sentences.en: A For the casual viewer, the exhibition of landscapes, Australia, selected by the Royal Academy of Art, will be a spectacular guide through Australian art history.
sentences.zh: 对于随意的观众来说，由皇家艺术学院策划的风景展《澳大利亚》将是一份穿越澳大利亚艺术史的壮观指南。

sentences.en: Included in the exhibition are a range of artists and styles, dating from the earliest days of colonial art and progressing through expressionism and modernism to the greats of the 20th century, culminating with the current generation of Australian artists.
sentences.zh: 展览中包括各种艺术家和风格，年代从殖民艺术最早的日子起，历经表现主义和现代主义、直到二十世纪的大师，并以当代一代澳大利亚艺术家收尾。

sentences.en: It is hardly surprising, then, that this results in a flexible, wide-ranging notion of landscape.
sentences.zh: 那么，这导致一种灵活、宽泛的风景概念，就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: B But this landmark exhibition gives rise to some questions, and perhaps problems, regarding Britain's relationship with its former colony.
sentences.zh: 但这个里程碑式的展览引出了一些关于英国与其前殖民地关系的问题、也许还有难题。

sentences.en: By choosing a style of painting at which British artists excel, the Academy could be seen as inviting criticism that hints at a telling attitude towards Australian art by comparison.
sentences.zh: 通过选择一种英国艺术家擅长的绘画风格，该学院可能会被视为在招致一种批评，这种批评暗示出一种相比之下对澳大利亚艺术耐人寻味的态度。

sentences.en: But it is the very theme of landscape that provides the strongest connection to Australian art from Britain.
sentences.zh: 但正是风景这一主题本身，提供了澳大利亚艺术与英国之间最强的联系。

sentences.en: To consider it condescending is perhaps too strong, but for Joanna Mendelssohn, an Australian critic and Associate Professor at the University of NSW's College of Fine Arts (COFA), there is a suggestion that British artistic values have directed this exhibition, rather than allowing Australia the freedom to demonstrate its maturity.
sentences.zh: 认为它居高临下也许言重了，但对于澳大利亚评论家、新南威尔士大学美术学院副教授乔安娜·门德尔松来说，有一种暗示，即是英国的艺术价值观主导了这个展览，而不是让澳大利亚自由地展示它的成熟。

sentences.en: What Mendelssohn found surprising about this exhibition was that the underlying rules for the selection of works seemed to have been so conservative.
sentences.zh: 门德尔松觉得这个展览令人惊讶的是，作品选择背后的潜在准则似乎如此保守。

sentences.en: Since the landscape is a very strong British artistic theme, it appeared to her that when the British looked to the art of a former colony, there was a tendency for them to think that those colonies would continue to be like the British themselves.
sentences.zh: 由于风景是一个非常强的英国艺术主题，在她看来，当英国人审视一个前殖民地的艺术时，他们往往会认为那些殖民地会继续像英国人自己一样。

sentences.en: In reviewing Australia, the British insisted on looking at the genre of landscape painting.
sentences.zh: 在评介《澳大利亚》时，英国人坚持去看风景画这一体裁。

sentences.en: C Because of colonial ties, it was inevitable during Australian art's formative years that it would reflect Britain's devotion to the beloved landscape before its own character and idiosyncrasies took shape.
sentences.zh: 由于殖民纽带，在澳大利亚艺术的形成时期，它不可避免地会在自身的特质和个性成形之前，反映出英国对其钟爱风景的痴迷。

sentences.en: And while Mendelssohn's concern over the exhibition's conventional selection is valid, the Academy is nevertheless embracing the peculiarities of Australian art from the mid-19th century onward, albeit within the boundaries of landscape.
sentences.zh: 而尽管门德尔松对展览传统的选择所抱的担忧是站得住脚的，但该学院毕竟在拥抱从十九世纪中叶往后澳大利亚艺术的独特之处，尽管是在风景的范围之内。

sentences.en: Australia is curated by Kathleen Soriano, director of exhibitions at the Royal Academy.
sentences.zh: 《澳大利亚》由皇家艺术学院的展览总监凯瑟琳·索里亚诺策划。

sentences.en: “Certainly the influence of English, French, or German art is much more evident in the early periods, in the early 1800s to mid-1800s,” she says.
sentences.zh: 她说：“当然，英国、法国或德国艺术的影响在早期、在19世纪初到19世纪中叶要明显得多。

sentences.en: “What I wanted to show was how Australian art develops a real distinctiveness, associated with the landscape and the light.”
sentences.zh: 我想展示的是澳大利亚艺术如何发展出一种与风景和光线相关联的真正独特性。”

sentences.en: D The fusion of tradition of the European kind with something more specifically Australian, and often personal, is crucial to the exhibition, and extends particularly to some of the more contemporary artists involved.
sentences.zh: 欧洲式传统与某种更具体地属于澳大利亚、且往往是个人化的东西的融合，对这个展览至关重要，并尤其延伸到一些参与其中的更当代的艺术家。

sentences.en: Sydney-born video artist Shaun Gladwell is a good example of this.
sentences.zh: 悉尼出生的视频艺术家肖恩·格拉德威尔就是这方面的一个好例子。

sentences.en: Gladwell's most famous piece, which is featured in the exhibition, is Storm Sequence (2000), a video of Gladwell skateboarding on the Bondi seafront as one of Sydney's signature brutal storms lingers offshore.
sentences.zh: 格拉德威尔最著名的作品、即展览中所展出的，是《风暴序列》（2000），一段格拉德威尔在邦迪海滨滑板的视频，其时悉尼标志性的猛烈风暴之一正在海面上空徘徊。

sentences.en: It is his acknowledgment of landscape (or seascape) tradition, colored by Gladwell's own individualism.
sentences.zh: 这是他对风景（或海景）传统的致敬，染上了格拉德威尔自己的个人主义色彩。

sentences.en: “To exhibit my work in this show might make some sense because I was interested in Turner and the idea of atmosphere affecting vision, something I was really interested in around the time of Storm Sequence.
sentences.zh: “在这次展览中展出我的作品也许说得通，因为我当时对透纳、以及氛围影响视觉这个想法很感兴趣，那是我在创作《风暴序列》前后真正感兴趣的东西。

sentences.en: I was thinking about this tradition of Romantic landscape, but I wanted to make it personal,” says Gladwell.
sentences.zh: 格拉德威尔说：“我当时在思考浪漫主义风景这一传统，但我想让它变得个人化。”

sentences.en: But he didn't want to just embark on borrowing imagery from elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 但他不想只是着手从别处借用意象。

sentences.en: He wanted to bring it to his experience and his world through skateboarding and beach culture.
sentences.zh: 他想通过滑板和海滩文化，把它带到他的体验和他的世界里。

sentences.en: E So while it may seem narrow for Britain to reduce Australian art to the genre of landscape, there can be little denying that British landscape painting is still relevant to a current generation of Australian practitioners, however indirectly.
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管英国把澳大利亚艺术缩减为风景这一体裁可能显得狭隘，但几乎无法否认，英国风景画对当代一代澳大利亚从业者仍然相关，无论多么间接。

sentences.en: Visitors to the exhibition encounter Australian Aboriginal art first, the idea being that these works warrant a prominent position because they were 'first'.
sentences.zh: 展览的参观者首先会遇到澳大利亚原住民艺术，其用意是这些作品因为是“最早的”而值得占据一个显要的位置。

sentences.en: Over the last couple of decades, London has hosted many successful exhibitions of Aboriginal art in smaller spaces, but for Soriano, Australia represents an opportunity to place such art in a broader context, with new relationships to the art of the settlers and white Australia.
sentences.zh: 在过去几十年里，伦敦在较小的空间里举办过许多成功的原住民艺术展，但对索里亚诺来说，《澳大利亚》代表着一个把这种艺术置于更广阔背景中的机会，使其与移民及白人澳大利亚的艺术建立起新的关系。

sentences.en: 'One of the reasons landscape makes sense as being the right theme was because Aboriginal art started in and on the landscape,' she says.
sentences.zh: 她说：“风景作为正确主题之所以说得通，原因之一是原住民艺术起源于风景之中、之上。

sentences.en: '[The exhibition] is a beautiful meshing of the two different kinds of art, that allowed me to bring them together comfortably and honestly within this theme.
sentences.zh: 这个展览是两种不同艺术的一次美丽交融，让我能够在这个主题内舒适而诚实地把它们结合在一起。

sentences.en: It was important for me to present Indigenous art to audiences, and I felt it was most authentic that it was seen as part of Australian art history, rather than a separate area with a world of its own.'
sentences.zh: 对我来说，把原住民艺术呈现给观众很重要，而我觉得最真实的做法是把它当作澳大利亚艺术史的一部分来看待，而不是当作一个有着自己天地的独立领域。”

sentences.en: F Meanwhile, Australian critic Mendelssohn also points out that London is increasingly less important to today's generation of artists, and this somewhat weakens the ceremony surrounding the exhibition in London.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，澳大利亚评论家门德尔松还指出，伦敦对今天这一代艺术家来说越来越不重要，而这在某种程度上削弱了围绕这个伦敦展览的盛大仪式。

sentences.en: 'China is the most important art market in the world,' she says.
sentences.zh: 她说：“中国是世界上最重要的艺术市场。

sentences.en: 'If you've made it in Shanghai, you've made it.
sentences.zh: 如果你在上海成功了，你就成功了。

sentences.en: The world has changed.
sentences.zh: 世界已经变了。

sentences.en: My students in Australia, who come from all over the world, really want to see Venice Biennale and Art Basel, but they're less interested in going to London.
sentences.zh: 我在澳大利亚的学生，他们来自世界各地，真正想看的是威尼斯双年展和巴塞尔艺术展，但他们对去伦敦不那么感兴趣。

sentences.en: When I was growing up, London was the destination, and then when I was at university all the smart young things wanted to go to New York,' she added.
sentences.zh: 她补充说：“在我成长的时候，伦敦是目的地，而后来我上大学时，所有聪明的年轻人都想去纽约。

sentences.en: 'Now they want to go everywhere.
sentences.zh: 现在他们哪里都想去。

sentences.en: There's no such thing as the centre and the periphery like there used to be.
sentences.zh: 不再有像过去那样的中心与边缘之分。

sentences.en: It's much more complicated.'
sentences.zh: 情况要复杂得多。”
