records.title: Australia's cane toad problem
records.titleZh: 澳大利亚的 cane toad（ cane toad）问题

sentences.en: (A) In the north of Australia there are many sugar cane plantations, which early in the 20th century were being damaged by a particular pest.
sentences.zh: 在澳大利亚北部有许多甘蔗种植园，在 20 世纪初它们曾被一种特定的害虫毁坏。

sentences.en: This was a species of beetle whose larvae, the infant form of the beetle, lived underground in the soil in the sugar cane fields.
sentences.zh: 这是一种甲虫，其幼虫——即甲虫的幼期形态——生活在甘蔗田里的地下土壤中。

sentences.en: The sugar cane plants were weakened or died because their roots were eaten by the larvae.
sentences.zh: 甘蔗植株因根部被这些幼虫吃掉而衰弱或死亡。

sentences.en: This had serious economic consequences for sugar cane farmers.
sentences.zh: 这给蔗农带来了严重的经济后果。

sentences.en: Modern pesticides were not developed until the 1940s, so farmers had to use what was available at the time.
sentences.zh: 现代杀虫剂直到 1940 年代才被研发出来，所以农户当时只能使用手头能找到的东西。

sentences.en: Chemicals like arsenic and copper were used, but these were not only expensive but also stayed in the environment and were poisonous to people, plants and animals.
sentences.zh: 砷和铜等化学品被使用，但它们不仅昂贵，还会残留在环境中并对人、植物和动物有毒。

sentences.en: It was generally acknowledged by government, farmers and scientists that cheaper and safer methods of pest control had to be found.
sentences.zh: 政府、农户和科学家普遍认识到，必须找到更便宜、更安全的害虫防治方法。

sentences.en: (B) A promising replacement for copper and arsenic was the use of biological control.
sentences.zh: 取代铜和砷的一个有前景的方案是使用生物防治。

sentences.en: Farmers already used some forms of biological pest control in the form of predatory and parasitic wasps and flies, insect-eating birds, and plants from different regions or countries to control pests.
sentences.zh: 农户已经在使用某些形式的生物害虫防治，包括捕食性和寄生性的胡蜂和蝇、食虫鸟，以及来自不同地区或国家的植物，用以控制害虫。

sentences.en: Common practice was to release these introduced agents into new environments, the expectation being that they would destroy resident pests.
sentences.zh: 常见做法是把这些引入的“代理人”释放到新环境中，期望它们能够消灭当地的害虫。

sentences.en: Some species of toad already had successful records as agents of biological control in gardens.
sentences.zh: 某些种类的蟾蜍在花园生物防治方面已经有过成功记录。

sentences.en: For example, in 19th century France toads were sold to gardeners at markets in Paris to eat insect pests in their gardens.
sentences.zh: 例如，在 19 世纪的法国，蟾蜍被卖给巴黎集市上的园丁，用来吃掉他们花园里的昆虫害虫。

sentences.en: In the early 20th century French sugar cane farmers first took giant toads from South America to control pests in their Caribbean sugar cane plantations.
sentences.zh: 在 20 世纪初，法国蔗农首次把南美大蟾蜍带到加勒比地区的甘蔗种植园来防治害虫。

sentences.en: Although there is no evidence that these toads did help to control pests, sugar cane scientists then carried some of these toads from Jamaica and Barbados to Puerto Rico and from there to Hawaii.
sentences.zh: 尽管没有证据表明这些蟾蜍真的帮助防治了害虫，但甘蔗业的科学家随后把其中一些蟾蜍从牙买加和巴巴多斯带到波多黎各，再从那里带到夏威夷。

sentences.en: (C) The idea of biological control of pests was not new to Australia.
sentences.zh: 对澳大利亚而言，害虫的生物防治理念并不新鲜。

sentences.en: For example, in 1926 there had been a highly successful prevention of the increase of the exotic prickly-pear cactus by the introduction of a moth from Argentina.
sentences.zh: 例如，在 1926 年，通过引入一种来自阿根廷的蛾，曾极为成功地阻止了外来物种刺梨仙人掌的扩散。

sentences.en: This success added strength to the argument that biological control was the answer to the sugar cane industry’s pest problems.
sentences.zh: 这一成功为如下观点提供了支持：生物防治是解决甘蔗业害虫问题的答案。

sentences.en: Accordingly, in the early 1930s a decision was taken to introduce the giant South American toads, which in Australia are now commonly called cane toads, into Australian sugar cane plantations.
sentences.zh: 因此，在 1930 年代初，澳大利亚作出决定，把南美大蟾蜍——在澳大利亚通常称为“甘蔗蟾蜍”——引入到甘蔗种植园中。

sentences.en: (D) In 1935, an Australian entomologist brought 101 cane toads from Hawaii and released them in sugar cane plantations in the north of Australia.
sentences.zh: 1935 年，一位澳大利亚昆虫学家从夏威夷带回了 101 只甘蔗蟾蜍，把它们释放到澳大利亚北部的甘蔗种植园中。

sentences.en: However, over the following years it became clear that the cane toads were a failure.
sentences.zh: 然而，在随后几年里，事实清楚地表明甘蔗蟾蜍是个失败。

sentences.en: There was a fatal flaw in the plan to use them as a form of biological control.
sentences.zh: 把它们作为一种生物防治手段使用的计划存在一个致命缺陷。

sentences.en: This was that earthbound cane toads were expected to eat the mostly flying adult beetles in order to eliminate the soil-dwelling beetle larvae that ate the roots of the cane sugar plants.
sentences.zh: 那就是，人们指望被困于地面的甘蔗蟾蜍去吃掉大多数会飞的成虫，从而消灭吃甘蔗根的、生活在土壤里的甲虫幼虫。

sentences.en: This, of course, cane toads could not do.
sentences.zh: 这件事，甘蔗蟾蜍当然办不到。

sentences.en: (E) Prior to their introduction in Australia, there had been very few opponents and only one made his views public.
sentences.zh: 在它们被引入澳大利亚之前，反对者非常少，公开表达观点的只有一个人。

sentences.en: He was a retired former Chief Entomologist from the state government of New South Wales named Walter Froggatt.
sentences.zh: 他是新南威尔士州政府退休的前首席昆虫学家沃尔特·弗罗加特（Walter Froggatt）。

sentences.en: He forecast that cane toads might become as great a pest in Australia as rabbits.
sentences.zh: 他预言，甘蔗蟾蜍在澳大利亚的危害可能会和兔子一样大。

sentences.en: However, Froggatt’s peers rebuked him and eminent scientists branded his views ‘decidedly pessimistic’.
sentences.zh: 然而，弗罗加特的同行们批评了他，知名科学家把他的观点斥为“极其悲观”。

sentences.en: It is estimated that today as many as a hundred million cane toads form a toxic infestation which is slowly spreading throughout the land.
sentences.zh: 据估计，今天多达一亿只甘蔗蟾蜍构成了一种有毒的入侵潮，正在缓慢地遍布整个国土。

sentences.en: (F) Cane toads are large, heavily built amphibians.
sentences.zh: 甘蔗蟾蜍是一种身躯庞大、体格健壮的两栖动物。

sentences.en: Average-sized adults are 10-15 cm long and weigh more than a kilo.
sentences.zh: 成体平均身长 10—15 厘米，体重超过 1 公斤。

sentences.en: They have large swellings on each shoulder from which they squirt poison when they are threatened.
sentences.zh: 它们每侧肩部都有大鼓包，受到威胁时会从那里喷出毒液。

sentences.en: This venom contains 14 different chemicals, but they do not appear to be harmful to humans as no-one has died in Australia from cane toad poison.
sentences.zh: 这种毒液含有 14 种不同的化学物质，但似乎对人类无害——在澳大利亚没有人因甘蔗蟾蜍中毒而死亡。

sentences.en: Until recently there was no understanding of the toxicity of cane toad poison, but it is now clear that freshwater crocodiles, goannas (large lizards) and dingoes (wild dogs) have died after eating cane toads.
sentences.zh: 直到最近，人们对甘蔗蟾蜍毒液的毒性都还没有清楚的认识，但现在已经清楚：淡水鳄、巨蜥（goanna，大型蜥蜴）和澳洲野犬（dingo，野生犬）都曾因吃了甘蔗蟾蜍而死亡。

sentences.en: Cane toads compete with native Australian fauna for food, and eat the eggs and young of ground-nesting birds.
sentences.zh: 甘蔗蟾蜍还与澳大利亚本土动物争抢食物，并吃掉在地面筑巢的鸟类的蛋和雏鸟。

sentences.en: As their numbers increase, they are taking over more and more of the land where native Australian fauna live.
sentences.zh: 随着它们数量增加，它们正在接管澳大利亚本土动物所栖息的越来越多的土地。

sentences.en: (G) The lesson that can be learned from the introduction of cane toads is important.
sentences.zh: 从引入甘蔗蟾蜍这件事中可以汲取的教训非常重要。

sentences.en: It is wrong to think that such an awful biological event could not be repeated.
sentences.zh: 认为这种可怕的生物事件不可能再次发生，是一种错误想法。

sentences.en: In this instance, the catalyst was the overwhelming consensus of support for introducing cane toads to Australia.
sentences.zh: 在那次事件中，催化剂是支持把甘蔗蟾蜍引入澳大利亚的压倒性共识。

sentences.en: The error was that there was little or no testing of these biological agents before they were introduced to see what unplanned effects they might have on the environment.
sentences.zh: 错误在于：这些生物代理人在被引入之前，几乎没有任何对其可能对环境产生的意外影响所做的测试。

19.stemZh: 引入 cane toads 的后果立刻显现出来。

25.stemZh: 兔子被引入澳大利亚是为了控制杂草。

26.stemZh: 沃尔特·弗罗加特因试图阻止将食蚁兽引入澳大利亚而受到批评。

29.stemZh: 自引入以来，牛蛙的平均体型有所增大。

32.stemZh: 澳大利亚的动物可以安全地食用食蚁兽。

34.stemZh: 在许多地方，食人花蟾正逐渐占据澳大利亚动物栖息地。

records.title: The history of the bar code V1

sentences.en: (A) The first step toward today’s bar codes came in 1948, when Bernard Silver, a graduate student in the USA, overheard a conversation in the halls of Philadelphia’s Drexel Institute of Technology.
sentences.zh: 通向今天条形码的第一步出现在 1948 年——当时美国一位研究生伯纳德·西尔弗（Bernard Silver）在费城德雷塞尔理工学院（Drexel Institute of Technology）的走廊里无意听到了一段对话。

sentences.en: The president of a food chain was pleading with a professor to undertake research on a method of capturing product information automatically at store checkouts.
sentences.zh: 一家食品连锁的总裁正在恳请一位教授开展研究，以找出一种在商店结账时自动获取商品信息的方法。

sentences.en: The professor turned down the request, but Bernard Silver mentioned the conversation to his friend Norman Woodland, a twenty-seven-year-old teacher at Drexel.
sentences.zh: 教授拒绝了这一请求，但伯纳德·西尔弗把这段对话告诉了他的朋友诺曼·伍德兰（Norman Woodland）——德雷塞尔的一位 27 岁的教师。

sentences.en: The problem fascinated the two friends, and they set about thinking of a solution.
sentences.zh: 这个问题让两位朋友着迷起来，他们便着手思考解决方案。

sentences.en: Their first idea was to use patterns printed with an ink that would glow under ultraviolet light, and they built a device to test the concept.
sentences.zh: 他们最初的想法是使用一种在紫外光下会发光的油墨印制图案，并搭建了一个装置来验证这个概念。

sentences.en: It worked, but the printing costs were high and the patterns faded over time.
sentences.zh: 装置奏效，但印刷成本过高，图案也会随时间褪色。

sentences.en: Nonetheless, they were convinced they had a workable idea.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，他们仍坚信自己有一个可行的思路。

sentences.en: After several months of work they came up with the linear bar code, using elements from two established technologies: Morse code, in which letters and numbers are coded into a system of dots and dashes, and the method used to record soundtracks in movies.
sentences.zh: 经过数月研究，他们提出了线性条形码——借鉴了两种现有技术的元素：将字母和数字编码为点和划体系的摩尔斯电码，以及电影录制配乐时使用的方法。

sentences.en: Silver and Woodland patented the idea in 1952, describing their invention as ‘article classification…
sentences.zh: 西尔弗和伍德兰在 1952 年为该想法申请了专利，把他们的发明描述为“通过识别图案……

sentences.en: through the medium of identifying patterns’.
sentences.zh: 作为媒介对物品进行分类“。

sentences.en: But the cost, together with the fact that their scanning equipment was rather unreliable, made the idea a non-starter at that time.
sentences.zh: 但成本加之他们的扫描设备相当不可靠，使得这一想法在当时根本无法起步。

sentences.en: (B) Scanning systems made little progress until the 1970s, when lasers became affordable.
sentences.zh: 扫描系统在 1970 年代才有所进展，当时激光开始变得负担得起。

sentences.en: Following this, various systems came into use around the world in stores, libraries, factories, and the like, each with its own proprietary code, but there was no standardization.
sentences.zh: 随后，世界各地的商店、图书馆、工厂等地纷纷投入使用各种系统，每个系统都有自己的专有编码，但缺乏标准化。

sentences.en: A consortium of grocery manufacturers and retailers therefore set up a committee to look into bar codes, and to standardize what became known formally as the Universal Product Code (UPC).
sentences.zh: 因此，由杂货生产商和零售商组成的联盟成立了一个委员会，专门研究条形码，并对后来正式称为“通用产品代码”（UPC）的东西进行标准化。

sentences.en: At the heart of the committee’s guidelines were a few basic principles.
sentences.zh: 该委员会指导方针的核心是几条基本原则。

sentences.en: To make life easier for the cashier, bar codes would have to be readable from almost any angle and at a range of distances.
sentences.zh: 为了便于收银员的工作，条形码必须能在几乎任何角度、不同距离下被读取。

sentences.en: Because they would be reproduced by the million, the labels would have to be cheap and easy to print.
sentences.zh: 因为标签将以百万计地被复制，必须做到便宜且易于印刷。

sentences.en: And to be affordable, automated checkout systems would have to pay for themselves in two and a half years.
sentences.zh: 为了让人负担得起，自动结账系统必须能在两年半内收回成本。

sentences.en: The committee considered more than a dozen versions of bar codes, including one based on multi-colored dots and another using a circular bull’s-eye design with lines radiating from a central point.
sentences.zh: 委员会研究了十多种条形码版本，包括一种基于多彩色点的版本，还有一种采用从中心点向外辐射线条的圆形“靶心”设计。

sentences.en: On April 1, 1973, they unanimously agreed on a standardized UPC, a combination of black and white lines and numbers, based on Woodland and Silver’s idea but developed by George Laurer at IBM.
sentences.zh: 1973 年 4 月 1 日，他们一致通过了一种标准化的 UPC——由黑白线条和数字组成，基于伍德兰和西尔弗的想法，由 IBM 的乔治·劳雷尔（George Laurer）研发完成。

sentences.en: Alan Haberman, who headed the subcommittee as president of First National Stores, described the bar code as a kind of world language that worked for everyone.
sentences.zh: 作为第一国家商店（First National Stores）总裁的艾伦·哈伯曼（Alan Haberman）当时领导这个分委员会，他把条形码形容为一种适用于所有人的世界语言。

sentences.en: He recalls proudly, ‘We showed that it could be done on a massive scale, that cooperation…
sentences.zh: 他自豪地回忆说：“我们证明，这件事可以在大规模上完成，证明合作……

sentences.en: was possible for the common good, and that business didn’t need the government to shove them in the right direction.’
sentences.zh: 是可能的，能服务于公共利益；也证明商界并不需要政府推着才能走对方向。“

sentences.en: (C) The investment involved in the bar-code revolution was huge.
sentences.zh: 条形码革命所涉及的投资非常巨大。

sentences.en: Each of the tens of thousands of grocery outlets in the US had to spend at least $200,000 on new scanning equipment.
sentences.zh: 美国数万家杂货零售点中的每一家，都不得不在新扫描设备上投入至少 20 万美元。

sentences.en: Chains had to install new data processing centers and retrain their employees.
sentences.zh: 连锁公司必须建立新的数据处理中心并对员工进行再培训。

sentences.en: Printers had to develop the new types of ink, plates, and other technology to reproduce the code with the exact tolerances it requires, and manufacturers had to spend millions of dollars a year on the labels.
sentences.zh: 印刷商必须研发新的油墨、印版和其他技术，按所需的极小公差再现条形码；制造商每年也必须为标签花费数百万美元。

sentences.en: On June 26, 1974, all the tests were done, all the proposals were complete, all the standards were set, and at a supermarket in Ohio, a single pack of Juicy Fruit chewing gum became the first retail product sold with the help of a bar code scanner.
sentences.zh: 1974 年 6 月 26 日，所有测试完成、所有方案就绪、所有标准制定完毕；在俄亥俄州的一家超市里，一包 Juicy Fruit 口香糖借助条形码扫描器成为第一件以这种方式售出的零售商品。

sentences.en: Decades of schemes and billions of dollars in investment now became a practical reality.
sentences.zh: 几十年的构想和数十亿美元的投资，至此变成了实实在在的现实。

sentences.en: The bar code on any product could be read and understood in every suitably equipped store.
sentences.zh: 任何商品的条形码都能在每一家装备齐全的商店被读取并理解。

sentences.en: (D) The advantages of the system were not clear immediately, as wholesalers, retailers and customers remained suspicious.
sentences.zh: 这一系统的优势并未立即显现，因为批发商、零售商和顾客都仍持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: Some customers believed bar codes were a form of surveillance.
sentences.zh: 一些顾客认为条形码是一种监视手段。

sentences.en: During the early weeks, Business Week magazine ran the headline ‘The Supermarket Scanner That Failed’.
sentences.zh: 在最初几周里，《Business Week》（《商业周刊》）杂志曾用过这样一句标题：“The Supermarket Scanner That Failed”（《失败的超市扫描器》）。

sentences.en: However, the benefits eventually became apparent.
sentences.zh: 然而，益处最终还是显现了出来。

sentences.en: ‘It turns out there were massive savings in labor and other areas,’ Haberman says.
sentences.zh: “结果发现，在人力以及其他方面都有大量的节省，”哈伯曼说。

sentences.en: These included checking out items at twice the speed compared to using traditional equipment, which meant shorter lines.
sentences.zh: 这些益处包括：与使用传统设备相比，结账速度提高一倍，意味着排队更短。

sentences.en: And it did not take supermarkets too long to see that, as well as vastly improving customer service, the bar code could hugely reduce the amount of time spent checking inventory.
sentences.zh: 超市们也很快意识到，除了极大改善顾客体验之外，条形码还能大幅减少盘点存货所花的时间。

sentences.en: (E) Now, every day more than 5 billion bar codes are scanned in retail outlets throughout the world.
sentences.zh: 如今，全球零售门店每天扫描超过 50 亿次条形码。

sentences.en: Passengers’ luggage is tagged with bar codes by airlines.
sentences.zh: 航空公司为乘客的行李贴上条形码标签。

sentences.en: Staff attach them to babies to ensure the right babies go home from hospitals with the right mothers.
sentences.zh: 医院员工把条形码贴在婴儿身上，以确保正确的婴儿与正确的母亲一同回家。

sentences.en: Runners in major marathons set off with bar codes on their vests, and librarians rely on them.
sentences.zh: 大型马拉松的参赛者出发时背心上贴着条形码，图书管理员也依赖条形码。

sentences.en: Tiny bar codes have even been mounted on bees by researchers to track their movements.
sentences.zh: 研究人员甚至给蜜蜂装上了微型条形码，以追踪它们的飞行轨迹。

sentences.en: As for that original pack of Juicy Fruit, it is now, unchewed and unopened, in the Smithsonian Institution National Museum of American History in Washington.
sentences.zh: 至于那包最早的 Juicy Fruit 口香糖，它现在仍未被嚼过、未被打开过，陈列在华盛顿的史密森学会美国国家历史博物馆中。

sentences.en: (A) In the ancient world, the waxy grey substance we now refer to as ambergris was highly prized for its medicinal properties, and was widely used as a spice, which was believed to be an aphrodisiac when added to food or wine.
sentences.zh: 在古代世界，我们如今称为龙涎香的这种灰色蜡状物质，因其药用价值而备受珍视，并被广泛用作香料，人们相信把它加进食物或酒中能起到催情的作用。

sentences.en: Ambergris itself is pleasantly aromatic, especially when warmed, and it was also highly valued as a fixing agent in the making of perfume, since it enabled a scent to retain its fragrance for much longer than might otherwise have been possible.
sentences.zh: 龙涎香本身气味芬芳宜人，尤其在受热之后，它在制作香水时还作为定香剂而备受看重，因为它能让一种香味比本来可能维持的时间长得多。

sentences.en: Most ambergris was found in the form of lumps floating on the surface of the sea, or washed up on the shores of tropical and temperate oceans.
sentences.zh: 大多数龙涎香都是以块状被发现的，它们漂浮在海面上，或被冲上热带和温带海域的岸边。

sentences.en: At one time, ambergris was worth its weight in gold, but there was much confusion about its origins.
sentences.zh: 龙涎香一度价比黄金，但人们对它的来源却有诸多困惑。

sentences.en: (B) Ambergris was known to the Arabs as 'ambar' and was originally called amber in the West in the Middle Ages.
sentences.zh: 龙涎香在阿拉伯人那里被称为“ambar”，在中世纪的西方最初也被称为amber。

sentences.en: This eventually led to further confusion in the popular mind between ambergris and true amber, the mineral known to mineralogists as succinite, which is actually fossilised tree resin, and generally yellow in colour.
sentences.zh: 这最终在大众心中造成了龙涎香与真正的琥珀之间更深的混淆，琥珀在矿物学家那里被称为琥珀石，实际上是树脂的化石，通常呈黄色。

sentences.en: Both substances were rare and costly, and both were associated with the sea, largely because for Europeans the most common source of amber was the shores of the Baltic.
sentences.zh: 这两种物质都既稀有又昂贵，而且都与海洋相关联，这在很大程度上是因为对欧洲人来说，琥珀最常见的来源是波罗的海沿岸。

sentences.en: In Chapter 92 of Moby Dick, the American writer Herman Melville pours scorn on those who believed the two substances to be the same: 'Though the word ambergris is but the French compound for grey amber, yet the two substances are quite distinct.
sentences.zh: 在《白鲸》第92章中，美国作家赫尔曼·麦尔维尔对那些认为这两种物质是同一种东西的人大加嘲讽：“尽管ambergris一词不过是法语中表示灰琥珀的合成词，但这两种物质却截然不同。

sentences.en: For amber, though at times found on the sea-coast, is also dug up in some far-inland soils, whereas ambergris is never found except upon the sea.
sentences.zh: 因为琥珀虽然有时见于海岸，却也能从一些远离海洋的内陆土壤中挖出，而龙涎香除了在海上之外从不会被发现。

sentences.en: Besides, amber is a hard, transparent, brittle, odourless substance, used for mouth-pieces to pipes, for beads and ornaments; but ambergris is soft, waxy, and so highly fragrant that it is largely used in perfumery.'
sentences.zh: 此外，琥珀是一种坚硬、透明、易碎、没有气味的物质，用于制作烟斗的吸嘴、珠子和饰物；而龙涎香则柔软、呈蜡状，香气浓郁，因而大量用于香水制造。”

sentences.en: (C) Moby Dick was published in 1851, by which time the mystery of the origins of ambergris had been resolved by the scientific community.
sentences.zh: 《白鲸》于1851年出版，到那时，龙涎香来源之谜已被科学界解开。

sentences.en: In 1783, the botanist Joseph Banks, who had accompanied Captain James Cook on his voyages of discovery in the Pacific, presented a paper to the Royal Society of London by the German physician Dr Franz Xavier Schwediawer in which it was conclusively proved that ambergris came from sperm whales.
sentences.zh: 1783年，曾随詹姆斯·库克船长在太平洋进行发现之旅的植物学家约瑟夫·班克斯，向伦敦皇家学会提交了一篇德国医生弗朗茨·克扎维尔·施韦迪亚韦尔博士所写的论文，文中确凿地证明了龙涎香来自抹香鲸。

sentences.en: In this, he was confirming an observation made in the 13ᵗʰ century by the great Venetian traveller Marco Polo who, while on the island of Socotra in the Indian Ocean, had witnessed a sperm whale vomiting up ambergris.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，他证实的是13世纪伟大的威尼斯旅行家马可·波罗所做的一项观察，马可·波罗在印度洋的索科特拉岛上，曾目睹一头抹香鲸吐出龙涎香。

sentences.en: But whereas Marco Polo imagined that the whale had swallowed the lump in the depths of the sea, Schwediawer showed that the origin of the material was inside the whale itself.
sentences.zh: 但马可·波罗以为是鲸鱼在深海里吞下了这块东西，施韦迪亚韦尔却表明，这种物质的源头就在鲸鱼体内。

sentences.en: (D) The sperm whale is the largest of the odontocetes, or toothed whales.
sentences.zh: 抹香鲸是齿鲸中体型最大的一种。

sentences.en: Males can grow up to 20 metres in length.
sentences.zh: 雄性体长可达20米。

sentences.en: Melville described the sperm whale as 'the king of whales', and his novel Moby Dick is based on the pursuit of one such creature.
sentences.zh: 麦尔维尔把抹香鲸称为“鲸中之王”，他的小说《白鲸》正是以追捕这样一头巨兽为题材。

sentences.en: Sperm whales are renowned for their ability to dive to great depths, possibly as far as 3 000 metres below the surface, and for remaining underwater for periods of two hours or more in pursuit of their favourite prey, the giant squid.
sentences.zh: 抹香鲸以能够潜入极深的水下而著称，下潜深度或许可达水面以下3000米，并能在水下连续停留两小时或更久，去追捕它们最爱的猎物——大王乌贼。

sentences.en: It is from the problems the whales have in digesting the beaks of such creatures that ambergris has its origins.
sentences.zh: 龙涎香的由来，正是源于鲸鱼在消化这类生物的喙时所遇到的困难。

sentences.en: The beak is sharp and irritates the whale's lower intestine, which responds by producing a black, foul-smelling liquid.
sentences.zh: 这种喙十分锋利，会刺激鲸鱼的下肠道，肠道则以分泌一种黑色、恶臭的液体作为反应。

sentences.en: It is not clear to scientists whether this secretion should be considered a normal response by the whale's digestive system or a pathological one, but from time to time large quantities of the liquid are vomited up by the whale.
sentences.zh: 科学家尚不清楚这种分泌究竟应被视为鲸鱼消化系统的正常反应还是一种病理反应，但鲸鱼时不时会把大量这种液体吐出来。

sentences.en: Once outside the whale's body and exposed to air, the substance hardens, acquiring the waxy, greyish and pleasantly aromatic characteristics of ambergris.
sentences.zh: 这种物质一旦离开鲸鱼体外、接触到空气，便会硬化，呈现出龙涎香那种蜡质、灰白而又芬芳宜人的特征。

sentences.en: Often the beaks of squid are still found embedded in lumps of ambergris, some of which can weigh several hundred kilograms.
sentences.zh: 人们常常发现乌贼的喙仍嵌在龙涎香块中，其中有些龙涎香块重达数百千克。

sentences.en: Melville took some delight in contrasting the origins of ambergris with the high value placed upon it by refined society: 'Who would think, then, that such fine ladies and gentlemen should regale themselves with an essence found in the inglorious bowels of a sick whale!'
sentences.zh: 麦尔维尔颇为得意地把龙涎香的来源与上流社会赋予它的高昂价值加以对照：“那么，谁能想到，这般高贵的淑女绅士，竟会用一种取自病鲸不光彩的肠肚里的香精来款待自己呢！”

sentences.en: (E) Sperm whales were ruthlessly pursued by commercial whalers in the 19ᵗʰ and 20ᵗʰ centuries.
sentences.zh: 19世纪和20世纪，抹香鲸遭到商业捕鲸者的无情猎捕。

sentences.en: In 1963-64 alone, almost 30 000 individuals were killed, and only the imposition of a ban on the hunting of sperm whales in 1984 saved the species from extinction.
sentences.zh: 仅1963至1964年间，就有近3万头抹香鲸被杀，直到1984年颁布捕杀抹香鲸的禁令，才使这一物种免于灭绝。

sentences.en: Ambergris was by far the most valuable product to be extracted during the processing of the whales' carcasses, and over 90 per cent of the annual worldwide total was acquired in this way, as a by-product of commercial whaling.
sentences.zh: 在处理鲸鱼尸体的过程中提取出的产品里，龙涎香是迄今最有价值的，全球每年总量的90%以上都是以这种方式获得的，作为商业捕鲸的副产品。

sentences.en: However, even before the ban on hunting sperm whales was imposed, the 1972 Marine Mammal Protection Act had prohibited trade in ambergris.
sentences.zh: 然而，早在猎捕抹香鲸的禁令颁布之前，1972年的《海洋哺乳动物保护法》就已禁止龙涎香的交易。

sentences.en: Just as petroleum and plastic products were replacing other natural products of whaling, so ambergris was supplanted in the making of perfume by other materials, some natural and some synthetic in origin.
sentences.zh: 正如石油和塑料制品正在取代捕鲸所得的其他天然产物一样，在香水制造中，龙涎香也被其他材料所取代，这些材料有的源于天然，有的源于合成。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, it is possible that, as sperm-whale populations recover to their former numbers in the wild, so the sight of lumps of ambergris washed ashore along the tide-line will once again become a familiar one to beachcombers the world over.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，有可能随着抹香鲸的野生种群恢复到从前的数量，一块块龙涎香被冲上潮线岸边的景象，会再次为世界各地在海滩上拾荒的人所熟悉。

records.title: The Myth of the Eight-hour Sleep

sentences.en: (A) We often worry about lying awake in the middle of the night—but it could be good for you.
sentences.zh: 我们常常因为半夜醒着躺在床上而焦虑——可这其实可能对你有好处。

sentences.en: Indications from both science and history suggest that the eight-hour sleep may not be a natural or inborn pattern for humans.
sentences.zh: 来自科学和历史两方面的迹象都表明，八小时连续睡眠未必是人类天然或与生俱来的睡眠模式。

sentences.en: In the early 1990s, psychiatrist Thomas Wehr conducted research which implies just that.
sentences.zh: 20 世纪 90 年代初，精神病学家托马斯·韦尔（Thomas Wehr）开展的一项研究正暗示了这一点。

sentences.en: Wehr kept a group of people in a darkened room for 14 hours a day for a month.
sentences.zh: 韦尔让一组受试者每天在一间黑暗的房间里待 14 小时，持续了一个月。

sentences.en: It took some time for their sleep to regulate, but by the fourth week the subjects had settled into a very distinct sleeping pattern.
sentences.zh: 他们的睡眠花了一段时间才稳定下来，但到了第四周，受试者们已形成一种非常明显的睡眠模式。

sentences.en: First, they slept for four hours, then woke for one or two hours before falling into a second four-hour sleep.
sentences.zh: 他们先睡四小时，然后醒来一到两个小时，接着再进入第二段四小时的睡眠。

sentences.en: Though sleep scientists were impressed by the implications of the study, the idea that we must sleep for eight consecutive hours persists amongst the general public.
sentences.zh: 虽然睡眠科学家对这项研究的含义印象深刻，但“必须连续睡足八小时”的观念仍在普通大众中根深蒂固。

sentences.en: (B) In 2001, historian Roger Ekirch of Virginia Tech University in the US published a paper drawn from 16 years of research, revealing historical evidence that humans used to sleep in two distinct periods of time each night.
sentences.zh: 2001 年，美国弗吉尼亚理工大学的历史学家罗杰·埃基奇（Roger Ekirch）发表了一篇基于 16 年研究的论文，揭示了人类过去每晚分两段截然不同的时间段睡觉的历史证据。

sentences.en: Ekirch’s research found more than 500 references to a segmented sleeping pattern—in diaries, court records, medical books and literature, from the ancient Greeks to tribes in Nigeria.
sentences.zh: 埃基奇的研究在日记、法庭记录、医书和文学作品中发现了 500 多处有关分段睡眠模式的记载——从古希腊一直延伸到尼日利亚的部落。

sentences.en: Much like Wehr’s findings, these references describe a first sleep which began not long following sunset.
sentences.zh: 与韦尔的研究发现颇为相似，这些资料都描述了一段在日落后不久就开始的“第一觉”。

sentences.en: Then there was a waking period of one or two hours and after that a second sleep.
sentences.zh: 随后是一到两个小时的清醒期，之后再进入第二觉。

sentences.en: During the waking period, people could be quite active.
sentences.zh: 在清醒期间，人们可以相当活跃。

sentences.en: They sometimes got up and moved around the house, although most people stayed in bed, and perhaps read or wrote if they had enough money for candles.
sentences.zh: 他们有时会起身在屋里走动，不过大多数人仍待在床上，或者——如果有钱点蜡烛——便会读书写字。

sentences.en: In many historic accounts, Ekirch found that people used the time that they were awake between periods of sleep to think about and attempt to analyse their dreams.
sentences.zh: 在许多历史记载中，埃基奇发现人们会利用两段睡眠之间的清醒时间，思考并试图解析他们做过的梦。

sentences.en: In his book, Evening’s Empire, historian Craig Koslofsky suggests an explanation for this divided sleep pattern in Europe.
sentences.zh: 历史学家克雷格·科斯洛夫斯基（Craig Koslofsky）在其著作《夜的帝国》（Evening's Empire）中，为欧洲这种分段睡眠模式提出了一种解释。

sentences.en: ‘Associations with night before the 17th century were not good,’ he writes.
sentences.zh: “在 17 世纪以前，人们对夜晚的联想并不美好，”他写道。

sentences.en: He goes on to explain that the streets of the cities and towns at night were often populated by thieves or worse.
sentences.zh: 他接着解释说，城镇的街道在夜间常常充斥着窃贼，甚至更糟糕的人。

sentences.en: The streets at night consequently scared many people.
sentences.zh: 因此，夜晚的街道令许多人感到恐惧。

sentences.en: Even the wealthy, who could afford to light their way, had better things to spend their nights on.
sentences.zh: 即便是付得起照明费用的富人，也有更值得在夜里做的事情。

sentences.en: (C) Ekirch found that references to the first and second sleep started to disappear during the late 17th century.
sentences.zh: 埃基奇发现，关于第一觉和第二觉的记载从 17 世纪末开始逐渐消失。

sentences.en: The pattern began to alter first among the upper classes in northern Europe and, over the course of the next 200 years, began changing amongst the rest of Western society.
sentences.zh: 这种模式最先在北欧的上层阶级中发生变化，随后在之后的 200 年里，整个西方社会其余阶层的睡眠习惯也开始改变。

sentences.en: By the 1920s, the idea of a first and second sleep had receded entirely from our social consciousness.
sentences.zh: 到了 20 世纪 20 年代，“第一觉、第二觉”的观念已彻底从我们的社会意识中淡出。

sentences.en: Ekirch attributes the initial shift to improvements in street and home lighting.
sentences.zh: 埃基奇把这一最初的转变归因于街道和家庭照明的改善。

sentences.en: As the night became a time for all kinds of activity, the length of time people slept declined.
sentences.zh: 随着夜晚变成各种活动的时间，人们的睡眠时长开始减少。

sentences.en: In 1667, Paris became the first city in the world to light its streets, using wax candles in glass lamps.
sentences.zh: 1667 年，巴黎成为世界上第一个为街道照明的城市，使用的是装在玻璃灯罩中的蜡烛。

sentences.en: It was followed by another French city, Lille, in the same year and by Amsterdam in Holland two years later, where a much more efficient oil-powered lamp was developed.
sentences.zh: 同年，法国另一座城市里尔（Lille）也紧随其后，两年后荷兰的阿姆斯特丹也跟上，在那里还研发出了效率高得多的油灯。

sentences.en: London didn’t light its streets until 1684, but by the end of the 17th century, more than 50 of Europe’s major towns and cities were lit at night.
sentences.zh: 伦敦直到 1684 年才开始为街道照明，但到 17 世纪末，欧洲已有 50 多座大型城镇在夜间有照明。

sentences.en: Coffee houses emerged as a fashionable phenomenon and many were open virtually around the clock.
sentences.zh: 咖啡馆作为一种时髦现象兴起，许多咖啡馆几乎全天候营业。

sentences.en: Going out at night became commonplace, and spending hours lying in bed was considered a waste of time.
sentences.zh: 夜间出门成了寻常之事，而花几个小时躺在床上则被视为浪费时间。

sentences.en: ‘People were becoming increasingly time-conscious and sensitive to efficiency, certainly before the 19th century,’ says Ekirch.
sentences.zh: “毫无疑问，早在 19 世纪以前，人们就已经越来越在意时间，对效率也越来越敏感，”埃基奇说。

sentences.en: ‘But the Industrial Revolution intensified that attitude considerably.’
sentences.zh: “不过，工业革命大大强化了这种态度。”

sentences.en: Strong evidence of this shifting attitude is contained in a medical journal from 1829 which urged parents to force their children out of the pattern of first and second sleep.
sentences.zh: 1829 年的一本医学期刊提供了这种态度转变的有力证据：它敦促家长强制孩子改掉第一觉和第二觉的睡眠模式。

sentences.en: (D) Today, most people seem to have adapted quite well to the eight-hour sleep, but Ekirch believes many sleeping problems may have roots in the human body’s natural preference for divided sleep, as well as in difficulties caused by extended exposure to artificial light in the modern world.
sentences.zh: 如今，大多数人似乎已相当好地适应了八小时睡眠，但埃基奇认为，许多睡眠问题可能根源于人体对分段睡眠的天然偏好，以及现代世界中长时间暴露于人造光线所造成的种种困扰。

sentences.en: This could be the cause of a condition called sleep maintenance insomnia, where people wake during the night and have trouble getting back to sleep.
sentences.zh: 这可能正是一种叫做“睡眠维持性失眠”的病症的成因，患者在夜间醒来后很难重新入睡。

sentences.en: The condition first appears in literature at the end of the 19th century, at the same time as accounts of interrupted sleep disappear.
sentences.zh: 这种病症首次出现在文献中是在 19 世纪末，恰好与中断睡眠的相关记述消失的时间重合。

sentences.en: (E) Sleep psychologist Gregg Jacobs says that the idea that we must sleep for an extended period of time could be damaging if it makes people who wake up in the night anxious, as this anxiety can itself discourage sleep and is likely to affect waking life too.
sentences.zh: 睡眠心理学家格雷格·雅各布斯（Gregg Jacobs）表示，“我们必须长时间连续睡觉”这个观念本身可能是有害的——如果它让夜里醒来的人感到焦虑的话，因为这种焦虑本身就会妨碍入睡，也可能影响清醒时的生活。

sentences.en: Jacobs suggests that the waking period between sleeps, when people simply rested and relaxed, could have played an important part in the human capacity to regulate stress naturally.
sentences.zh: 雅各布斯认为，两段睡眠之间那段人们仅仅静卧、放松的清醒期，可能在人类自然调节压力的能力中起到过重要作用。

sentences.en: Russell Foster, a professor of circadian (body clock) neuroscience at Oxford University in the UK, shares this point of view.
sentences.zh: 英国牛津大学的昼夜节律（即生物钟）神经科学教授拉塞尔·福斯特（Russell Foster）也持有同样的观点。

sentences.en: ‘Over 30% of the medical problems that doctors are faced with stem directly or indirectly from sleep.
sentences.zh: “医生面对的医学问题中，有 30% 以上都直接或间接地源于睡眠。

sentences.en: But sleep has been ignored in medical training, and there are very few centres where sleep is studied,’ Foster says.
sentences.zh: 可睡眠在医学培训中一直被忽视，专门研究睡眠的中心也寥寥无几，”福斯特说。

sentences.en: He feels this needs to change.
sentences.zh: 他认为这种状况必须改变。

sentences.en: (A) Today we take it for granted that we travel around the world to admire the monuments of the past.
sentences.zh: 今天我们已把环游世界、瞻仰昔日遗迹视为理所当然。

sentences.en: We prepare for such trips by reading about what we are going to see, set out on the journey with a good idea of how we will get there and where we will stay, and have a sense of what we will encounter on location.
sentences.zh: 我们为此类行程做准备时会先阅读将要看到的内容，启程时已经对怎么去、住哪里有清楚的计划，并大致知道在当地会遇到什么。

sentences.en: Cyriacus of Ancona (1391-1452), the first cultural tourist since antiquity, lacked these advantages when, in the first half of the 15th century, he sailed around the Mediterranean in search of the remains of Greek and Roman civilisations.
sentences.zh: 安科纳的西里亚库斯（Cyriacus of Ancona，1391—1452 年）作为古代之后的第一位文化游客，在 15 世纪上半叶绕地中海航行、寻找希腊与罗马文明遗迹时，并不享有这些便利。

sentences.en: (B) Cyriacus first became fascinated by ancient monuments while walking in his home city Ancona and looking at the marble arch, erected in AD 115, to the Roman Emperor Trajan.
sentences.zh: 西里亚库斯最早对古代遗迹产生兴趣，是在他家乡安科纳散步时看到那座建于公元 115 年、为纪念罗马皇帝图拉真而竖立的大理石拱门。

sentences.en: He suddenly saw the culture in a new light.
sentences.zh: 他突然以全新的眼光来看待这种文化。

sentences.en: He no longer saw it as just a familiar and generally overlooked landmark, but as a doorway to the wonders of ancient imperial Rome.
sentences.zh: 他不再把它视作一个熟悉却常被忽视的地标，而是看作通往古代罗马帝国奇观的一扇门。

sentences.en: Not many people of Cyriacus’s time were interested in historical travel; they generally ignored old buildings and structures, or worse, dismantled them for their building materials.
sentences.zh: 在西里亚库斯所处的时代，对历史性旅行感兴趣的人并不多；他们通常忽视那些古老的建筑物，更糟的是，将它们拆毁以获取建筑材料。

sentences.en: (C) Cyriacus decided to see the world for himself and to record details of whatever other antiquities remained to be discovered.
sentences.zh: 西里亚库斯决定亲自去看看这个世界，并记录下任何尚未被发现的古代遗物的细节。

sentences.en: His training as a merchant did not prepare him for this vocation; he did not know ancient languages, history or art.
sentences.zh: 他作为商人的训练并未为他这一志业做准备；他不懂古代语言、历史或艺术。

sentences.en: However, he set out to solve these failings, first by learning Latin at the age of 30 and then adding ancient Greek.
sentences.zh: 然而，他着手弥补这些不足，先是在 30 岁时学习拉丁文，随后又加上了古希腊文。

sentences.en: Having done this, he then set off on voyages around the Mediterranean to find, investigate and understand ancient cultures from their buildings, sculptures and inscriptions.
sentences.zh: 做到这点之后，他便开始环地中海航行，去寻找、考察并理解古代文化——从他们的建筑、雕塑和铭文入手。

sentences.en: Thus he became the first archaeologist and cultural tourist, predating other antiquarians by some 200 years.
sentences.zh: 由此，他成为第一位考古学家和文化游客，比其他古物研究者早了约 200 年。

sentences.en: (D) Travel in the 15th century, however, was anything but simple or enjoyable.
sentences.zh: 然而，在 15 世纪，旅行根本谈不上简单或愉快。

sentences.en: Overland journeys by foot or mule along bad roads, under constant threat from bandits, were bad; voyages by sea were even worse.
sentences.zh: 沿着糟糕的道路步行或骑骡的陆上行程很糟糕，且时时面临强盗的威胁；海上的航程则更为糟糕。

sentences.en: When the weather cooperated, sailing went relatively smoothly: ships proceeded along coasts from one recognisable landmark to another.
sentences.zh: 天气配合时，航行相对顺利：船只沿着海岸从一个可辨识的地标驶向另一个。

sentences.en: However, when there was no wind, the ship did not move.
sentences.zh: 然而，没有风时，船就动弹不得。

sentences.en: Strong winds were no friends either; they drenched the ship with lashing waves and blew it off course.
sentences.zh: 强风也不是朋友；它们让船被翻涌的浪头浇得湿透，并把船吹离航线。

sentences.en: Water swamped the deck, splashed into the cabins and soaked mattresses, clothes and food.
sentences.zh: 海水淹没甲板、溅入船舱，把床垫、衣物和食物都泡湿。

sentences.en: Remarkably, Cyriacus never complained about the miseries of travel.
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，西里亚库斯从未抱怨过旅途的种种艰辛。

sentences.en: Optimistic by nature, he endured such hardships unafraid and saw opportunities where other people saw setbacks.
sentences.zh: 他天性乐观，毫无畏惧地忍受这些艰辛，并在别人只看到挫折的地方看到机会。

sentences.en: (E) Among many of the important records made by Cyriacus was his crucial documenting, in 1431, of the remains of Cyzicus, an ancient Roman city that had relied on commerce for its financial success.
sentences.zh: 西里亚库斯所做的重要记录之中，包括他在 1431 年对古罗马城市基齐库斯（Cyzicus）遗址所做的关键性记录——这座城市在财政上曾依赖商业而兴盛。

sentences.en: He hired a local person to take him to the site and then had to work out for himself the significance of the ruins he was looking at because there was no guidebook on ancient architecture to help him.
sentences.zh: 他雇了一位当地人带他去这处遗址，然后只能自己来弄清楚眼前这些废墟的意义，因为没有任何古代建筑的指南可供参考。

sentences.en: (F) Indeed, he had no contemporary knowledge about the ruins.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他对这些废墟当时没有任何与时代相称的资料可借鉴。

sentences.en: Cyzicus had been a splendid city in its prime.
sentences.zh: 在鼎盛时期，基齐库斯曾是一座辉煌的城市。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, the area was highly seismic and in AD 123 the city was so devastated by a major earthquake that, when the Roman Emperor Hadrian visited it the following year, he was so saddened that he decided to subsidise a campaign to reconstruct Cyzicus.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，该地区地震活动频繁，公元 123 年一场大地震将这座城市几乎完全摧毁，以至于罗马皇帝哈德良次年到访时极为悲痛，决定资助一场重建基齐库斯的运动。

sentences.en: He made a substantial donation for a new temple to the Roman god Jupiter.
sentences.zh: 他为一座新的罗马神朱庇特的神庙作出了大笔捐赠。

sentences.en: Cyriacus thought the ruined city was awe-inspiring.
sentences.zh: 西里亚库斯认为这座废墟之城令人肃然起敬。

sentences.en: He found the remains of the temple and examined it in great detail, looking for clues in ancient texts to help him understand what he was seeing.
sentences.zh: 他找到了那座神庙的遗迹，并对其进行了非常仔细的考察，从古代文献中寻找线索来帮助理解眼前所见。

sentences.en: He sketched the great doorway adorned with carved foliage and mythological characters.
sentences.zh: 他还描绘了那座装饰着雕刻枝叶和神话人物的宏伟大门。

sentences.en: Cyriacus’s account of this temple is the only record of this building, as in the following centuries it was entirely stripped of all its stonework and all that remains is its base.
sentences.zh: 西里亚库斯对这座神庙的记述，是关于这座建筑的唯一记录，因为在随后的几个世纪里，它的所有石材都被掠走，如今所剩的只有基座。

sentences.en: (G) Cyriacus also visited mainland Greece, in 1436, when no one went to Greece in order to see the country’s ancient ruins.
sentences.zh: 西里亚库斯还在 1436 年访问了希腊本土——那时几乎无人为参观古代废墟而前往希腊。

sentences.en: One of his destinations was the sanctuary of Delphi.
sentences.zh: 他的目的地之一是德尔斐圣所。

sentences.en: The ancient Greeks considered Delphi as being situated in the most beautiful spot in Greece.
sentences.zh: 古希腊人认为德尔斐位于希腊最美的地方。

sentences.en: When Cyriacus arrived at the site of Delphi, however, he found war, earthquakes and avalanches had all but obliterated its ruins.
sentences.zh: 然而，当西里亚库斯到达德尔斐遗址时，他发现战争、地震和雪崩几乎已抹去了那里的废墟。

sentences.en: Determined to find any ancient traces, Cyriacus spent six days walking all over the area, peering at odd stone blocks sticking out of the ground, running his hands over inscriptions to trace fragments of words, and trying to puzzle out the few surviving structural remains.
sentences.zh: 他决意要找到任何古代遗迹，便在该地区跋涉了六天——细看露出地表的奇形石块，用手抚过铭文，描摹残存的字迹片段，并努力辨认仅存的几处建筑残遗。

sentences.en: Climbing uphill towards the rocks that tower over the site, he came upon a theatre built into the slope.
sentences.zh: 他向遗址上方耸立的岩石攀登而上，发现山坡上嵌着一座剧场。

sentences.en: Soon after his visit, the site was buried by a rockslide and was not seen again until archaeologists began to excavate the area systematically in the late 19th century.
sentences.zh: 在他造访不久之后，该遗址即被一场山崩掩埋，直到 19 世纪末考古学家开始系统发掘该地区时才重见天日。

sentences.en: (H) Cyriacus had hoped to visit Egypt and Ethiopia, but he never got there.
sentences.zh: 西里亚库斯本来希望访问埃及和埃塞俄比亚，但他从未到过那里。

sentences.en: However, in his life he did record for posterity countless ancient monuments around the Mediterranean, paving the way for future archaeologists and cultural tourists.
sentences.zh: 然而，他一生中确实为后世留下了对地中海周边无数古代遗迹的记录，为后来的考古学家和文化游客铺平了道路。

sentences.en: A The traditional kampung houses of Malaysia do not need air-conditioning.
sentences.zh: 马来西亚传统的甘榜房屋不需要空调。

sentences.en: Built on stilts and with steep roofs, they have year-round ventilation.
sentences.zh: 它们建在桩柱上、有陡峭的屋顶，全年通风。

sentences.en: The raised structure ensures a cooling breeze comes up through the floorboards, while the high roof acts as a chimney to release hot air.
sentences.zh: 抬高的结构确保凉爽的微风从地板缝里上来，而高高的屋顶则像烟囱一样把热空气排出。

sentences.en: The airtight, concrete boxes of modern city construction, in contrast, are heat traps, says Muhammad Peter Davis of University Putra Malaysia.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，现代城市建筑那种密不透风的混凝土盒子是热陷阱，马来西亚博特拉大学的Muhammad Peter Davis说。

sentences.en: He has calculated that typical modern Malaysian houses are 5°C hotter than the air outside.
sentences.zh: 他计算出，典型的现代马来西亚房屋比室外空气热5摄氏度。

sentences.en: The builders of kampung houses “had no knowledge of modern science or engineering but they came up with the perfect design,” says Davis.
sentences.zh: 甘榜房屋的建造者“没有现代科学或工程的知识，但他们想出了完美的设计，”Davis说。

sentences.en: B This story of ancient architectural sophistication and modern insanity is repeated around the world.
sentences.zh: 这个关于古代建筑智慧与现代疯狂的故事在世界各地重演。

sentences.en: In the name of modernism, people have thrown away architecture designed to cope with the environment in which they live, and adopted house designs originating from cold, northern environments, where the idea is to keep heat in.
sentences.zh: 以现代主义之名，人们抛弃了为应对他们所居住环境而设计的建筑，采用了源自寒冷北方环境、其理念是保住热量的房屋设计。

sentences.en: C Once, the aim of architectural modernists was to build structures that kept nature out and to replace it with air-conditioning.
sentences.zh: 曾经，建筑现代主义者的目标是建造把自然挡在外面、并用空调取而代之的结构。

sentences.en: Now they are learning that they cannot do that effectively.
sentences.zh: 如今他们正认识到自己无法有效地那样做。

sentences.en: Slowly, they are seeing the benefit of working with nature, rather than against it.
sentences.zh: 慢慢地，他们看到了顺应自然而非对抗自然的好处。

sentences.en: In California, they probably use more power for air-conditioning than anywhere else on Earth.
sentences.zh: 在加利福尼亚，他们用于空调的电力大概比地球上任何其他地方都多。

sentences.en: According to Arthur Rosenfeld from the University of California, what California needs is white paint.
sentences.zh: 据加州大学的Arthur Rosenfeld说，加利福尼亚需要的是白漆。

sentences.en: If Los Angeles painted its roofs white, planted trees to shade buildings, and chose lighter-colored paving, it could reduce city temperatures by 3°C and cut the annual air-conditioning bill by US$170 million a year.
sentences.zh: 如果洛杉矶把屋顶刷成白色、种树给建筑遮阴、选用浅色路面，它就能把城市温度降低3摄氏度，并把每年的空调账单削减1.7亿美元。

sentences.en: D Modern buildings are greedy in their use of energy.
sentences.zh: 现代建筑在能源使用上很贪婪。

sentences.en: Much is made of the contribution of transportation to global warming, through its emissions of greenhouse gases.
sentences.zh: 交通通过排放温室气体对全球变暖的贡献被大书特书。

sentences.en: But, globally, transportation is responsible for just 22 per cent of carbon dioxide emissions.
sentences.zh: 但在全球范围内，交通只占二氧化碳排放的22%。

sentences.en: The building sector is responsible for 31 per cent, mostly the result of heating and air conditioning systems.
sentences.zh: 建筑部门占31%，大多是供暖和空调系统造成的。

sentences.en: In developing countries, where demand for electricity for buildings is rising by 5 per cent a year, the biggest demand is for air-conditioning in modern buildings which are often designed to cope with every different climatic condition.
sentences.zh: 在发展中国家，建筑用电需求每年以5%的速度上升，最大的需求是现代建筑里的空调，这些建筑往往被设计为应对每一种不同的气候条件。

sentences.en: E Before air-conditioning, much of the Arab world kept cool through thoughtful building design.
sentences.zh: 在空调出现之前，阿拉伯世界的很大一部分通过深思熟虑的建筑设计来保持凉爽。

sentences.en: Many buildings were built according to the principles of the wind tower, a tall structure with vertical vents at the top that open in all directions to catch any passing breeze.
sentences.zh: 许多建筑按照风塔的原理建造，风塔是一种高耸的结构，顶部有朝各个方向开口的竖向通风口，以捕捉任何经过的微风。

sentences.en: Typically, these wind-tower buildings were made of local materials such as stone, mud brick, wood and palm-tree fronds.
sentences.zh: 这些风塔建筑通常用石头、泥砖、木头和棕榈叶等本地材料建造。

sentences.en: The buildings were inward-looking, which served the dual function of focusing attention on the courtyard, where family members spend time together, and protecting living areas from the rays of the sun.
sentences.zh: 这些建筑朝向内部，起到了双重作用，既把注意力集中到家人共度时光的庭院上，又保护居住区免受阳光照射。

sentences.en: F Throughout the Middle East today, wind towers are often little more than museum pieces.
sentences.zh: 如今在整个中东，风塔往往只不过是博物馆里的展品。

sentences.en: But there are exceptions.
sentences.zh: 但也有例外。

sentences.en: Jordan has won awards for the architecture of a village on the shores of the Red Sea, which is designed to conserve energy.
sentences.zh: 约旦因红海岸边一座旨在节能的村庄的建筑而获奖。

sentences.en: Made of rough, local stone in a traditional style, it combines the ventilation system of the wind towers for summer coolness with up-to-date heating and floor insulation to protect against the desert cold in winter.
sentences.zh: 它以传统风格用粗糙的本地石头建成，把风塔的通风系统用于夏季的凉爽，又结合最新的供暖和地板保温来抵御冬天沙漠的寒冷。

sentences.en: G Traditional building materials, like traditional building designs, are being rediscovered by those looking for low-energy solutions to the current construction needs.
sentences.zh: 和传统建筑设计一样，传统建筑材料正被那些为当前建筑需求寻找低能耗解决方案的人重新发现。

sentences.en: Clay is one such material: As the Dutch housing contractor R van der Ley has argued in promoting a series of clay housing projects in developing countries, clay has many benefits over its industrialized version, brick.
sentences.zh: 黏土就是一种这样的材料，正如荷兰住房承包商R van der Ley在推广一系列发展中国家黏土住房项目时所论证的，黏土比它工业化的版本砖块有许多好处。

sentences.en: Clay blocks cost only half as much as ordinary bricks.
sentences.zh: 黏土砖块的成本只有普通砖的一半。

sentences.en: Clay also generates work because people can find it, mould it, bake it and work it themselves.
sentences.zh: 黏土还创造工作，因为人们能自己找到它、塑造它、烧制它、加工它。

sentences.en: Two hundred clay bricks can be made with the fuel oil that makes just one ordinary brick.
sentences.zh: 用烧制一块普通砖的燃料油可以做出两百块黏土砖。

sentences.en: Moreover, clay is an excellent insulator against both cold and heat outside, and can easily be recycled.
sentences.zh: 而且，黏土是抵御室外寒冷和炎热的极好绝缘体，还能轻松回收。

sentences.en: H But although traditional methods and materials can be revived in appropriate settings, new green, low-energy technologies are needed, especially in urban environments.
sentences.zh: 但是，尽管传统的方法和材料能在合适的环境里复兴，新的绿色低能耗技术仍是必需的，尤其是在城市环境里。

sentences.en: The thermal insulation of homes in cold countries is an example.
sentences.zh: 寒冷国家住宅的隔热就是一个例子。

sentences.en: In 1983, Sweden adopted a national standard, requiring the country’s homes to lose no more than 60 kilowatt hours per square metre over the year.
sentences.zh: 1983年，瑞典采用了一项国家标准，要求该国的住宅一年内每平方米损失的热量不超过60千瓦时。

sentences.en: To meet that standard, windows were double glazed, and walls and roofs insulated.
sentences.zh: 为达到那个标准，窗户用了双层玻璃，墙壁和屋顶做了保温。

sentences.en: Every home became a fortress against the cold air outside.
sentences.zh: 每个家都成了抵御室外冷空气的堡垒。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, the rest of Europe has not followed the lead.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，欧洲其余地方没有效仿。

sentences.en: I In the United States, Amory Lovins has promoted a range of low-energy technologies: “super-windows”, for example, which let in invisible light but can be “tuned” to either allow in, or reflect away, infrared solar radiation — the stuff that heats.
sentences.zh: 在美国，Amory Lovins推广了一系列低能耗技术，比如“超级窗户”，它让不可见光进入，但可以被“调校”为允许或反射红外太阳辐射——也就是产生热量的那种。

sentences.en: Buildings with large expanses of window (and big energy bills) can be designed to achieve optimum temperatures.
sentences.zh: 有大面积窗户（和高额能源账单）的建筑可以被设计为达到最佳温度。

sentences.en: J As well as more efficient use of energy, the world also needs new sources of renewable power.
sentences.zh: 除了更高效地使用能源，世界还需要新的可再生能源来源。

sentences.en: Solar energy is being tried out in the developing world, in villages often far from electricity grids.
sentences.zh: 太阳能正在发展中世界、在往往远离电网的村庄里试用。

sentences.en: The world’s biggest solar power installation got underway in the Philippines, in 2001, where a project commenced to install solar panels for 400,000 people in 150 villages.
sentences.zh: 世界上最大的太阳能装置于2001年在菲律宾启动，那里开始了一个项目，为150个村庄的40万人安装太阳能板。

sentences.en: Such projects are demonstrating that countries, whether developing or developed, no longer need huge national grids to supply electricity.
sentences.zh: 这类项目正在表明，无论是发展中国家还是发达国家，都不再需要庞大的国家电网来供电。

sentences.en: Every home can do its own thing with the help of a solar panel and a storage battery.
sentences.zh: 借助一块太阳能板和一个蓄电池，每个家都能自给自足。

sentences.en: K Houses, of course, are more than machines for living in.
sentences.zh: 房屋当然不只是供居住的机器。

sentences.en: They are social and psychological spaces, too.
sentences.zh: 它们也是社会和心理空间。

sentences.en: Future houses may not look exactly like kampungs or wind towers or any other traditional models.
sentences.zh: 未来的房屋也许看起来不会和甘榜、风塔或任何其他传统范本一模一样。

sentences.en: But to work for us and for our environment, they will have to suit us as well as these traditional forms did.
sentences.zh: 但要为我们和我们的环境服务好，它们就得像这些传统形式一样适合我们。

sentences.en: (A) Travel anywhere and you see something so common it may not even catch your attention.
sentences.zh: 无论你走到哪里，都会看到某些事物如此普遍，以至于可能根本不会引起你的注意。

sentences.en: Wherever there are people, animals are being walked, herded and fed.
sentences.zh: 只要有人的地方，就有动物被遛、被放牧、被喂养。

sentences.en: Many, such as dogs, cats and sheep, are domesticated, but you will also find people living alongside wild creatures like monkeys and wolves.
sentences.zh: 许多动物——例如狗、猫和羊——被驯化了，但你也会发现人和猴、狼等野生动物毗邻而居。

sentences.en: Close contact with animals is not confined to one particular culture, region or ethnic group but is a universal human trait.
sentences.zh: 与动物的密切接触并不局限于某种特定的文化、地区或族群，而是一种普世的人类特征。

sentences.en: (B) On the face of it this makes little sense.
sentences.zh: 表面上看，这没什么道理。

sentences.en: No other mammal adopts individuals from another species, with good reason.
sentences.zh: 没有别的哺乳动物会从另一物种中“收养”个体——这是有充分理由的。

sentences.en: Since the ultimate prize in evolution is perpetuating your genes, providing food for another species is counterproductive to success.
sentences.zh: 既然进化中的终极奖赏是把自己的基因延续下去，那为另一个物种提供食物对成功而言反而是不利的。

sentences.en: Even if pets offer friendship, that cannot explain why our bond with other species arose in the first place.
sentences.zh: 即便宠物提供了陪伴，那也无法解释我们与其他物种的纽带最初是如何出现的。

sentences.en: Who would bring a ferocious wolf into their home in the hope that thousands of years later it would become a loving pet?
sentences.zh: 谁会把一只凶猛的狼带回家，希望几千年后它能变成一只可爱的宠物呢？

sentences.en: (C) As an anthropologist I have tried to understand this puzzle by looking to the past for the origins of our link with animals.
sentences.zh: 作为人类学家，我尝试通过回望过去、寻找我们与动物联系的起源来理解这个谜。

sentences.en: What I found was a long and unbroken evolutionary trail of evidence I call the ‘animal connection’.
sentences.zh: 我所发现的是一条漫长而连续的进化证据线索，我称之为“动物联结”。

sentences.en: This trail links to three important developments in human evolution: tool making, language and domestication.
sentences.zh: 这条线索连接到人类进化中的三项重要发展：制造工具、语言和驯化。

sentences.en: If I am correct, and I believe that further research will conclusively show that I am, the animal connection is a hugely significant force instrumental in our global success.
sentences.zh: 如果我是对的——我相信进一步的研究会决定性地证明我是对的——那么动物联结就是一股极其重要的力量，是我们取得全球性成功的关键。

sentences.en: (D) The trail begins at least 2.6 million years ago.
sentences.zh: 这条线索至少可追溯至 260 万年前。

sentences.en: That is when the first tools appear in the archaeological record.
sentences.zh: 那是工具首次出现在考古记录中的时间。

sentences.en: This development required the intellectual breakthrough of realizing that the properties of an object can be altered.
sentences.zh: 这一发展需要一次智力上的突破：意识到一个物体的属性可以被改变。

sentences.en: Man learnt how to turn stone into small, sharp items that could cut up animal carcasses, providing them with an evolutionary shortcut to becoming predators.
sentences.zh: 人学会了如何把石头变成可以切割动物尸体的小而锋利的物件，从而提供了一条进化捷径，让人成为捕食者。

sentences.en: (E) There were many consequences of the new hunting lifestyle.
sentences.zh: 新的狩猎生活方式带来了诸多后果。

sentences.en: On the plus side, eating more meat and fat was a requirement for the increase in relative brain size.
sentences.zh: 在好的方面，食用更多肉和脂肪是相对脑量增大所必需的。

sentences.en: And since meat tends to come in bigger packages than leaves and roots, meat eaters could spend less time finding food and more on activities like learning and social interaction.
sentences.zh: 而由于肉一般比叶子和根块以更大的“包装”出现，吃肉者花在寻找食物上的时间更少，可以把更多时间用于学习和社交等活动。

sentences.en: On the minus side, preying on animals put our ancestors into direct competition with the other predators that shared their ecosystem, animals such as lions and hyenas.
sentences.zh: 在坏的方面，捕食动物让我们的祖先与共享其生态系统的其他捕食者——如狮子和鬣狗——直接竞争。

sentences.en: To get the upper hand, they needed more than just tools, and that is where the animal connection comes in.
sentences.zh: 要占上风，他们需要的不仅是工具——这就是动物联结发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: What made it possible for our ancestors to compete successfully with true carnivores was the ability to pay very close attention to the habits of both potential prey and competitors.
sentences.zh: 让我们的祖先能与真正的食肉动物成功竞争的，是密切关注潜在猎物和竞争者两者习性的能力。

sentences.en: Knowledge was power, so we acquired a deep understanding of the minds of other animals.
sentences.zh: 知识就是力量，因此我们获得了对其他动物心智的深刻理解。

sentences.en: Another significant consequence of becoming more predatory was the need to live at lower densities, as successful predators soon exhaust food supplies.
sentences.zh: 成为更具捕食性的另一项重要后果是：必须以更低的密度生活，因为成功的捕食者会很快耗尽食物供应。

sentences.en: The record of the geographic distribution of our ancestors provides further support for my idea that the animal connection has shaped our evolution.
sentences.zh: 我们祖先地理分布的记录也进一步支持了“动物联结塑造了我们进化”这一观点。

sentences.en: Early man lived in Africa and nowhere else, but then underwent a dramatic expansion in territory, forced by the search for new hunting grounds.
sentences.zh: 早期的人类只生活在非洲，别无他处；但随后他们的领地经历了戏剧性的扩张，被对新狩猎地的寻求所驱动。

sentences.en: (F) Throughout the period of these enormous changes in the lifestyle of our ancestors, gathering, sharing and recording knowledge became increasingly advantageous, and examples of prehistoric art that appear in Europe, Asia, Africa and Australia allow us to eavesdrop on their conversations.
sentences.zh: 在我们祖先生活方式发生这些巨大变化的整个时期，搜集、分享和记录知识变得越来越有利。出现在欧洲、亚洲、非洲和澳大利亚的史前艺术作品，让我们得以“偷听”他们的对话。

sentences.en: Through the art, we realize the main topic was animals: their colours, shapes, postures and habits.
sentences.zh: 透过这些艺术，我们意识到主题主要是动物：它们的颜色、形状、姿态和习性。

sentences.en: This focus is even more striking considering that scenes of human life are rarely depicted.
sentences.zh: 考虑到人类生活的场景很少被描绘，这种聚焦就更加鲜明。

sentences.en: Pictures of people, social interaction and ceremonies are rare.
sentences.zh: 人物画像、社会互动和仪式则很罕见。

sentences.en: (G) This leads me on to the development of language.
sentences.zh: 这把我引向语言的发展。

sentences.en: Nobody doubts this proved a major adaptive advantage to our ancestors in developing complex behaviours.
sentences.zh: 没有人怀疑这对我们祖先发展复杂行为是一种重大适应性优势。

sentences.en: How it arose, however, remains a mystery.
sentences.zh: 然而语言是如何产生的，仍是个谜。

sentences.en: I believe I am the first to propose a continuity between the strong human-animal link that appeared 2.6 million years ago and the origin of language.
sentences.zh: 我相信我是第一个提出 260 万年前出现的“人—动物”强联结与语言起源之间存在连续性的人。

sentences.en: The complexity and importance of animal-related information, indicated in the predominance of animal images, spurred early humans to move beyond what other species could achieve.
sentences.zh: 动物相关信息的复杂性和重要性——其表现就是动物形象占据主导——促使早期人类超越了其他物种所能达到的水平。

sentences.en: Vervet monkeys, for example, have different cries for eagles and snakes, but they cannot discuss what threats might appear tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 例如，长尾黑颚猴对老鹰和蛇有不同叫声，但它们无法讨论明天可能出现什么威胁。

sentences.en: The property of full language is that it is comprised of vocabulary and grammatical rules that can be combined in an infinite number of ways to convey fine shades of meaning.
sentences.zh: 完整语言的属性是：由词汇和语法规则构成，二者可以以无限多种方式组合，传达细腻的意义层次。

sentences.en: (H) As our ancestors became more involved with animals, the third product of the animal connection appeared: domestication, which has long been linked with the keeping of animals like sheep.
sentences.zh: 随着我们的祖先与动物的关联越来越紧密，动物联结的第三个产物出现了：驯化——它长期以来与饲养羊等动物联系在一起。

sentences.en: Domestic animals are usually considered as ‘walking larders’, or easy food sources, reflecting the idea that the basis of this change was a drive for greater food security.
sentences.zh: 家养动物通常被视为“行走的食物库”，或便捷的食物来源——这反映出这样一种观念：这一变化的基础是对更高食物保障的追求。

sentences.en: Looking at the origins of domestication for clues to its underlying reasons, I found fundamental flaws in this idea.
sentences.zh: 在审视驯化的起源以寻找其根本原因的线索时，我发现这种观念存在根本性缺陷。

sentences.en: Instead, my analysis suggests domestication emerged as a natural progression of our close association with, and understanding of, other species.
sentences.zh: 相反，我的分析表明，驯化是作为我们与其他物种密切关联与理解的自然延伸而出现的。

sentences.en: If domestication was about knowing where your next meal was coming from, the first domesticate ought to have been a food source, yet analysis of fossils shows that the domestication of dogs pre-dated that of any other species, even plants, from wolves.
sentences.zh: 如果驯化是要知道下一顿在哪里，那第一个被驯化的对象应当是食物来源；可化石分析表明，狗的驯化早于任何其他物种——甚至早于植物——而且是来自狼的驯化。

sentences.en: Furthermore, if the objective was to have meat to eat, you wouldn’t select an animal that eats two kilograms of meat a day.
sentences.zh: 此外，如果目的是有肉可吃，你不会选择一只每天吃 2 公斤肉的动物。

sentences.en: It was familiarity with this species that led to eventual domestication.
sentences.zh: 是对这一物种的熟悉感，最终导致了驯化。

sentences.en: (A) Theories on the origin and evolution of language have been a major area of my research for many years.
sentences.zh: 关于语言起源与演化的理论，多年来一直是我研究的一个主要领域。

sentences.en: By 1859, when British scientist Charles Darwin published The Origin of Species, there was already a great deal of interest in this subject.
sentences.zh: 到1859年英国科学家查尔斯·达尔文发表《物种起源》时，人们对这一主题已经抱有浓厚的兴趣。

sentences.en: However, the debate became plagued by strange theories, so much so that in 1866 the influential Société de Linguistique de Paris banned all discussions about the origin of language.
sentences.zh: 然而，这场争论却被各种离奇的理论所困扰，以至于在1866年，颇具影响力的巴黎语言学会（Société de Linguistique de Paris）禁止了一切有关语言起源的讨论。

sentences.en: The ban lasted for more than a century, before a surge of research began during the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 这项禁令持续了一个多世纪，直到20世纪90年代相关研究才大量涌现。

sentences.en: Linguists, psychologists, anthropologists and archaeologists now frequently debate the origin of language and have published many articles and books on this topic.
sentences.zh: 如今，语言学家、心理学家、人类学家和考古学家经常就语言的起源展开争论，并就这一主题发表了大量文章和著作。

sentences.en: And yet, despite almost frenzied activity, limited progress has been made.
sentences.zh: 然而，尽管研究活动近乎狂热，取得的进展却很有限。

sentences.en: (B) I believe there are four reasons for this.
sentences.zh: 我认为，造成这种情况有四个原因。

sentences.en: The first is an insufficient concern with the archaeological and fossil proof of the brains and behaviour of our human ancestors.
sentences.zh: 第一，对我们人类祖先的大脑与行为的考古及化石证据关注不足。

sentences.en: Many theories to date rely on an assumed association between brain size and language abilities, without acknowledging the problem this creates: fossil evidence indicates that the Neanderthals had larger brains than modern humans, Homo sapiens, but archaeological evidence indicates that the Neanderthals lacked a capacity for language.
sentences.zh: 迄今为止，许多理论都依赖于一种假定，即大脑大小与语言能力之间存在关联，却没有正视这种假定所带来的问题：化石证据表明，尼安德特人的大脑比现代人（智人，Homo sapiens）更大，但考古证据却表明尼安德特人并不具备语言能力。

sentences.en: So something is seriously amiss with those theories.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些理论存在严重的问题。

sentences.en: (C) That 'something' might relate to the second reason for limited progress: insufficient concern with the other major aural and vocal communication system of modern humans: music.
sentences.zh: 这个“问题”或许与进展有限的第二个原因有关：对现代人另一种重要的听觉与发声交流系统——音乐——关注不足。

sentences.en: Even though the Société de Linguistique de Paris had nothing to say about studying the origin of music, academics appear to have had a self-imposed ban, with limited discussion of this issue during the 19th and 20th centuries.
sentences.zh: 尽管巴黎语言学会对研究音乐的起源未置一词，学者们似乎给自己设下了一道禁令，在19世纪和20世纪对这一问题的讨论十分有限。

sentences.en: However, there are notable exceptions that should be acknowledged.
sentences.zh: 不过，也有一些值得一提的显著例外。

sentences.en: One is the aforementioned Charles Darwin who, in his 1871 book on human evolution, The Descent of Man, devoted several pages to the development of music.
sentences.zh: 其一便是前面提到的查尔斯·达尔文，他在1871年论述人类演化的著作《人类的由来》中，用了好几页篇幅来讨论音乐的发展。

sentences.en: Another is the renowned ethnomusicologist John Blacking, whose 1973 book, How Musical is Man?, broached the idea that music is an inherent and universal human quality.
sentences.zh: 另一位是著名的民族音乐学家约翰·布莱金（John Blacking），他在1973年的著作《How Musical is Man？》中提出，音乐是人类与生俱来且普遍存在的一种特质。

sentences.en: (D) The origin of music deserves as much attention as that of language, as we cannot treat one without the other.
sentences.zh: 音乐的起源理应得到与语言起源同等的关注，因为二者无法割裂开来研究。

sentences.en: Those writers who had evidently annoyed the Société de Linguistique de Paris were quite aware of this.
sentences.zh: 那些显然惹恼了巴黎语言学会的作者们对此十分清楚。

sentences.en: For them, music and language were intimately linked; the French writer and philosopher Jean-Jacques Rousseau's On the Origin of Language (1781) was a reflection on both music and language.
sentences.zh: 在他们看来，音乐与语言密不可分；法国作家兼哲学家让-雅克·卢梭的《论语言的起源》（1781年）便是对音乐与语言二者的思考。

sentences.en: In contrast, Morten Christiansen and Simon Kirby's book, Language Evolution (2000), which they conceived as 'a definitive book on the subject', failed to mention music in any of its 17 chapters.
sentences.zh: 与之相反，莫滕·克里斯蒂安森（Morten Christiansen）和西蒙·柯比（Simon Kirby）合著的《Language Evolution》（2000年）——他们将其设想为“该主题的权威之作”——在全书17章中竟无一处提及音乐。

sentences.en: Those authors have an important lesson to learn from Rousseau and other writers of his time who addressed the origin of language.
sentences.zh: 这些作者应当从卢梭以及与他同时代论述语言起源的其他作家那里汲取一个重要的教训。

sentences.en: (E) Music is a universal feature of human society and plays a significant role in the lives of all individuals.
sentences.zh: 音乐是人类社会的一个普遍特征，在每个人的生活中都发挥着重要作用。

sentences.en: Indeed, music is perhaps in even greater need of study than language: the latter has a self-evident function—the transmission of information—and can be readily accepted as a product of evolution, even if its specific evolutionary history remains unclear.
sentences.zh: 实际上，音乐或许比语言更需要研究：语言有着不言而喻的功能——传递信息——因而很容易被视为演化的产物，即便其具体的演化历程仍不清楚。

sentences.en: But what is the point of music?
sentences.zh: 但音乐的意义又何在呢？

sentences.en: (F) That question leads directly to a third reason for our lack of progress in understanding how language evolved, and indeed the human mind in general: an insufficient concern with emotion.
sentences.zh: 这个问题直接引出了我们在理解语言如何演化——乃至理解整个人类心智——方面进展不足的第三个原因：对情感关注不足。

sentences.en: If music is about anything, it is about expressing emotion.
sentences.zh: 如果说音乐关乎什么，那就是关乎情感的表达。

sentences.en: But while archaeologists have put significant effort into examining the intellectual capacities of our ancestors, their emotional lives have been sorely neglected.
sentences.zh: 然而，尽管考古学家在考察我们祖先的智力能力上投入了大量精力，他们的情感生活却被严重忽视了。

sentences.en: This has contributed to the neglect of music, which, in turn, has constrained our understanding of language.
sentences.zh: 这导致了对音乐的忽视，而对音乐的忽视反过来又制约了我们对语言的理解。

sentences.en: (G) There is one further reason why progress has been limited: those who have been most influential regarding the evolution of language have simply got it wrong, and misled everyone else.
sentences.zh: 进展有限还有最后一个原因：那些在语言演化研究领域最具影响力的人根本就搞错了，并误导了其他所有人。

sentences.en: Linguist Derek Bickerton has made an important contribution towards our understanding of the origin of language by bringing his profound knowledge of linguistics to the discussions that have occurred.
sentences.zh: 语言学家德里克·比克顿（Derek Bickerton）将其深厚的语言学造诣带入相关讨论，为我们理解语言的起源作出了重要贡献。

sentences.en: But Bickerton's idea that the precursor of modern language consisted of words strung together with limited, if any, grammar is, I believe, fundamentally mistaken.
sentences.zh: 但比克顿认为现代语言的前身是由词语串连而成、几乎没有语法的观点，在我看来是根本错误的。

sentences.en: Bickerton refers to this precursor as 'proto-language' and suggests that it was similar to the type of language spoken by young children today, and mastered by apes through the use of computer keyboards.
sentences.zh: 比克顿把这种前身称为“原始语言”（proto-language），并认为它类似于当今幼儿所说的语言，以及猿类通过使用电脑键盘所掌握的语言。

sentences.en: This idea has dominated the field of language origins for the last two decades, and is one that I once found persuasive.
sentences.zh: 在过去二十年里，这一观点一直主导着语言起源研究领域，我自己也曾觉得它颇有说服力。

sentences.en: But I now understand that it is not only flawed but has severely limited the progress that should have been made.
sentences.zh: 但我如今明白，它不仅存在缺陷，还严重限制了本应取得的进展。

sentences.en: (H) My book therefore provides an alternative view, one that draws on the ideas of a linguist who has, I believe, identified the true nature of proto-language.
sentences.zh: 因此，我的书提供了另一种观点，它借鉴了一位语言学家的思想——我相信，这位学者已经揭示了原始语言的真正本质。

sentences.en: Her name is Alison Wray.
sentences.zh: 她的名字叫艾莉森·雷（Alison Wray）。

sentences.en: She argues that proto-language was 'holistic' rather than compositional in character.
sentences.zh: 她认为，原始语言在本质上是“整体性的”，而非组合性的。

sentences.en: By this she means that the precursor to language was a communication system composed of 'messages' rather than words; each message was uniquely associated with an arbitrary meaning, as are the utterances of language today.
sentences.zh: 她的意思是，语言的前身是一套由“信息”而非词语构成的交流系统；每条信息都唯一地对应着一个任意约定的意义，就像如今语言中的话语一样。

sentences.en: (A) One October afternoon, a young New Zealander, Sam Tobin, called his dogs and went for a walk down to the nearby Ruamahanga River.
sentences.zh: 10 月的一个下午，一位年轻的新西兰人萨姆·托宾（Sam Tobin）唤来他的狗，散步走到附近的鲁阿马汉加河（Ruamahanga River）。

sentences.en: Having been very high for days, the river had at last fallen, and Tobin was eager to see what changes the floods had brought.
sentences.zh: 在连日水位高涨之后，河水终于退去，托宾急于看看洪水带来了哪些变化。

sentences.en: The family farm borders the river, and a four-metre-high flood bank testifies to its natural tendency to flood.
sentences.zh: 自家的农场紧邻河边，4 米高的防洪堤说明了河水有泛滥的天然倾向。

sentences.en: (B) Tobin stepped out onto a broad shoulder of river sand, where he noticed what he initially took to be a whitish rock, lit by the sun.
sentences.zh: 托宾走到一片宽阔的河滩沙地上，注意到他起初以为是被阳光照亮的一块白色石头的东西。

sentences.en: Then, getting closer, he realised it was a bone.
sentences.zh: 靠近后，他才意识到那是一块骨头。

sentences.en: Such a thing was not uncommon in these parts - he had often come home with fragments, or even whole skeletons, of cows and sheep.
sentences.zh: 在这一带这种事并不少见——他常带回牛和羊的骨头碎片，甚至整副骨架。

sentences.en: But as he scraped aside a stone he realised that it was a human bone, something quite new in his experience.
sentences.zh: 但当他刮开一块石头时，他意识到这是一块人骨——这在他的经验中颇为新鲜。

sentences.en: As he picked it up, he saw it was a skull, discoloured with age.
sentences.zh: 他把它捡起来时，看出那是一具因年代久远而变色的头骨。

sentences.en: (C) Tobin replaced the skull and hurried home to tell his mother what the river had delivered to their doorstep.
sentences.zh: 托宾把头骨放回原处，匆匆赶回家把河水送到家门口的东西告诉母亲。

sentences.en: It would prove to be a spectacular find, setting in motion an investigation by some of the country’s most respected specialists, and ultimately challenging our most firmly held assertions about the human settlement of New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 这后来被证明是一项了不起的发现，引发了由本国一些最受尊敬的专家进行的调查，最终撼动了我们对新西兰人类定居最坚定持有的看法。

sentences.en: (D) The police were immediately called, but despite a thorough search they could find nothing that might shed light on the identity of the Ruamahanga skull, or the circumstances of its sudden appearance.
sentences.zh: 警方立即被叫来，但尽管进行了彻底搜查，他们没能找到任何可以说明鲁阿马汉加头骨身份或其突然出现情形的线索。

sentences.en: The skull was then taken north to be examined by forensic pathologist Dr Fetvis at Auckland Hospital.
sentences.zh: 随后，头骨被运到北边，由奥克兰医院的法医病理学家费维斯医生（Dr Fetvis）进行检查。

sentences.en: Despite being hampered by its damaged and incomplete condition - the jawbone and lower left portion of the cranium were missing - Dr Fetvis determined that the skull was that of a female.
sentences.zh: 尽管骨损残缺——下颌骨和颅骨左下部缺失——费维斯医生还是判定这块头骨属于一名女性。

sentences.en: He’d then consulted with a colleague, Dr Koelmeyer, who believed that the deterioration of the bone placed the time of dead ‘before living memory’ and, most significantly as it would turn out, the skull appeared to be European in origin.
sentences.zh: 然后他咨询了同事克尔迈尔医生（Dr Koelmeyer），后者认为骨头的劣化程度把死亡时间放在“活人记忆之前”；更关键的是，这块头骨看起来是欧洲人后裔。

sentences.en: (E) Wellington-based forensic anthropologist Dr Watt also examined the skull, and suggested it belonged to a 40–45-year-old.
sentences.zh: 位于惠灵顿的法医人类学家瓦特博士（Dr Watt）也检查了头骨，并提出它属于一名 40 至 45 岁的人。

sentences.en: He believed that it could be the remains of an old farm burial, but was not certain, and proposed the use of radiocarbon dating to make sure it wasn’t a recent death.
sentences.zh: 他认为这可能是某次古老农场埋葬的遗骸，但并不确定，并提议使用放射性碳定年法以确认这不是近期死亡的人。

sentences.en: As a result, the Institute of Geological and Nuclear Sciences (GNS) in Lower Hutt was contacted, and provided with a sample of bone that had originated in the top of the skull.
sentences.zh: 因此，位于下哈特的地质与核科学研究所（GNS）受到联系，并获得了一份从头骨顶部取下的骨头样本。

sentences.en: In a little over three weeks, the seemingly astonishing results from the GNS laboratory came back.
sentences.zh: 略多于三周后，GNS 实验室返回了看似惊人的结果。

sentences.en: Cutting through the bewildering complexity of the scientific analysis was a single line reading: conventional radiocarbon age approximately 296 years.
sentences.zh: 穿过令人眼花缭乱的科学分析复杂性的，是一行字：“常规放射性碳年龄约 296 年”。

sentences.en: This was staggering, for the skull was about 200 years older than Dr Koelmeyer had believed.
sentences.zh: 这令人震惊——这具头骨比克尔迈尔医生所认为的还要早约 200 年。

sentences.en: (F) Of course, a skull of this age wasn’t particularly unusual in New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 当然，这种年代的头骨在新西兰并不算特别罕见。

sentences.en: The Maori people have been living in the country for at least 800 years and scientists frequently come across human remains of considerable age.
sentences.zh: 毛利人在这片土地上已经生活了至少 800 年，科学家常会遇到相当古老的人类遗骸。

sentences.en: The fascinating question, however, was how a skull of this race, let alone this gender, had reached these remote islands in the South Pacific at such a time, long before the arrival of the explorer Captain Cook in 1769, and perhaps even before the very first European landfall-the fleeting visit of the Dutch explorer Tasman in 1642-neither of whom had women among their crews.
sentences.zh: 然而令人着迷的问题是：这样一个种族——更不用说性别——的头骨，是如何在那么早的时间到达南太平洋这些偏远岛屿上的？远在 1769 年探险家库克船长到来之前，甚至可能在第一次欧洲人登陆——即 1642 年荷兰探险家塔斯曼短暂到访——之前——而二人船员中都没有女性。

sentences.en: (G) The first known European women in the Pacific came with a doomed colonising venture which sailed from Peru in 1595 under the command of Spanish captain Mendana.
sentences.zh: 已知最早来到太平洋的欧洲女性，是 1595 年从秘鲁出发、由西班牙船长门达尼亚（Mendana）率领的一次失败的殖民远征。

sentences.en: However, it is unlikely the Ruamahanga skull originated from this expedition because no evidence of Mendana’s ships has ever been found in New Zealand, while a team of archaeologists working in the Solomon Islands in 1979 did discover the remains of European vessels dating from the 16th century.
sentences.zh: 然而，鲁阿马汉加头骨不太可能源自这次远征，因为在新西兰从未发现过任何门达尼亚船只的证据；而 1979 年一支在所罗门群岛工作的考古队确实发现了 16 世纪欧洲船只的遗骸。

sentences.en: (H) Two centuries were to pass before the first recorded European females arrived in New Zealand, both having escaped from prison in Australia.
sentences.zh: 两个世纪之后，首批有记录的欧洲女性才到达新西兰，两人都是从澳大利亚监狱逃出来的。

sentences.en: Kathleen Hagerty and Charlotte Edgar are known to have reached the country in 1806.
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳·哈格蒂（Kathleen Hagerty）和夏洛特·埃德加（Charlotte Edgar）已知在 1806 年抵达新西兰。

sentences.en: How then do we account for the Ruamahanga skull, which appears to be about 100 years older than that?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们如何解释比她们似乎还要早约 100 年的鲁阿马汉加头骨呢？

sentences.en: (I) It is impossible to say with certainty, but the most likely explanation is that a Spanish or Portuguese trading ship was washed onto these wild shores as a result of a shipwreck and a woman got ashore.
sentences.zh: 无法绝对确定，但最可能的解释是：一艘西班牙或葡萄牙的贸易船因船难被冲到这些荒野海岸，一名女性上了岸。

sentences.en: Implausible, perhaps, but the Ruamahanga skull, today resting in the Wellington Museum, could be the kind of concrete evidence that demands such a drastic re-evaluation of history.
sentences.zh: 也许令人难以置信，但鲁阿马汉加头骨——如今安放在惠灵顿博物馆——可能就是那种迫使我们对历史进行如此剧烈再评估的、扎实的证据。
