sentences.en: (A) All living languages undergo changes of various kinds, for which there are various reasons.
sentences.zh: 所有活的语言都经历着各种各样的变化，对此有各种各样的原因。

sentences.en: The changes that have caused most dispute are those in pronunciation.
sentences.zh: 引起最多争议的变化是发音上的变化。

sentences.en: We have various sources of evidence for the pronunciations of earlier times, like the evidence of spellings, the treatment of words borrowed from other languages or borrowed by them, the descriptions of contemporary grammarians, and the modern pronunciations in all the languages and dialects concerned.
sentences.zh: 我们有各种各样的证据来源来了解更早时代的发音，比如拼写的证据、从其他语言借入或被它们借走词语的处理方式、当时语法学家的描述、以及所有相关语言和方言的现代发音。

sentences.en: These, combined with a knowledge of the mechanism of speech production, can often give us a very good idea of the pronunciation of an earlier age, though absolute certainty is never possible.
sentences.zh: 这些，结合对言语产生机制的了解，往往能给我们一个关于更早时代发音的很好的概念，尽管绝对的确定性是永远不可能的。

sentences.en: When we study the pronunciation of a language over any period of a few generations or more, we find that it is subject to change.
sentences.zh: 当我们研究一门语言在几代人或更长任何时段里的发音时，我们发现它会发生变化。

sentences.en: Moreover, there are always large-scale regularities in the changes: for example, over a period of time, all the long a sounds in a language may change into long o sounds, or all the b sounds in a certain position (for example, at the end of a word) may change into p sounds.
sentences.zh: 此外，这些变化中总有大规模的规律性：比如，在一段时间里，一门语言中所有的长a音可能变成长o音，或者某个特定位置（比如词尾）的所有b音可能变成p音。

sentences.en: Such regular changes are often called sound laws.
sentences.zh: 这样的规律变化常被称为语音定律。

sentences.en: There are no universal sound laws, but simply particular sound laws for one given language at one given period.
sentences.zh: 没有普遍的语音定律，而只有针对某一给定语言在某一给定时期的特定语音定律。

sentences.en: (B) One cause of change is the influence of one language on another.
sentences.zh: 变化的一个原因是一门语言对另一门的影响。

sentences.en: We learn our mother tongue very thoroughly, and acquire a whole set of speech habits which become second nature to us.
sentences.zh: 我们非常透彻地学习我们的母语，习得一整套成为我们第二天性的言语习惯。

sentences.en: When later we learn a foreign language, we inevitably carry over some of these speech habits into it, and so do not speak it exactly like a native.
sentences.zh: 当后来我们学一门外语时，我们不可避免地把其中一些言语习惯带进去，因此说得不完全像母语者。

sentences.en: Consequently, in bilingual situations the second language tends to be modified.
sentences.zh: 因此，在双语情境中，第二语言往往会被改变。

sentences.en: Such modifications may not persist, of course: an isolated Polish or German immigrant to Britain will usually have grandchildren who speak English like natives because the influence of the general speech environment (playmates, school, work) is stronger than that of the home.
sentences.zh: 当然，这样的改变可能不会持续：一个孤立的波兰或德国移民到英国，通常会有像母语者一样说英语的孙辈，因为一般言语环境（玩伴、学校、工作）的影响比家庭的更强。

sentences.en: But if a large and closely knit group of people adopt a new language, then the modifications they make in it may persist among their descendants, even if the latter no longer speak the original language that caused the changes.
sentences.zh: 但如果一大群关系紧密的人采用一门新语言，那么他们在其中所做的改变可能在其后代中持续，即便后者不再说那门引起变化的原语言。

sentences.en: This can be seen in Wales, where the influence of Welsh has affected the pronunciation of English, and the very characteristic melody of Welsh English has been carried over from Welsh.
sentences.zh: 这一点可以在威尔士看到，那里威尔士语的影响已经影响了英语的发音，而威尔士英语非常有特色的语调就是从威尔士语带过来的。

sentences.en: (C) It is also possible that fashion plays a part in the process of change.
sentences.zh: 时尚在变化过程中起一定作用，这也是可能的。

sentences.en: It certainly plays a part in the spread of change: one person imitates another, and people with the most prestige are most likely to be imitated, so that a change that takes place in one social group may be imitated (more or less accurately) by speakers in another group.
sentences.zh: 它在变化的传播中肯定起作用：一个人模仿另一个人，而最有声望的人最可能被模仿，于是发生在一个社会群体中的变化可能被另一群体的说话者（或多或少准确地）模仿。

sentences.en: When a social group goes up or down in the world, its pronunciation will gain or lose prestige.
sentences.zh: 当一个社会群体在世界上升或降时，它的发音会获得或失去声望。

sentences.en: Some of the changes in accepted English pronunciation in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries have been shown to consist of the replacement of one style of pronunciation by another style already existing, and it is likely that such substitutions were a result of the great social changes of the period: the increased power and wealth of the middle classes, and their steady infiltration upwards into the ranks of the landed gentry probably carried elements of middle class dialect into upper class speech.
sentences.zh: 十七和十八世纪公认英语发音中的一些变化，已被表明是用一种已经存在的发音风格替换另一种，而这样的替换很可能是那一时期巨大社会变化的结果：中产阶级权力和财富的增加，以及他们稳步向上渗透进有地乡绅的行列，很可能把中产阶级方言的成分带入了上层阶级的言语。

sentences.en: However, besides spreading changes that have already taken place, fashion may actually cause changes in pronunciation.
sentences.zh: 然而，除了传播已经发生的变化之外，时尚实际上还可能引起发音的变化。

sentences.en: In a stratified society, the important thing about a fashion is that it is exclusive: as soon as the fashion has penetrated to a lower social group, it’s time to move on.
sentences.zh: 在一个分层的社会里，关于一种时尚的重要之处在于它是排他的：一旦这种时尚渗透到了一个更低的社会群体，就该换新的了。

sentences.en: (D) This can be seen in clothes: fashionable people may find it flattering to be imitated, but as soon as the new fashion has really caught on they must change to something else, to mark themselves off as different.
sentences.zh: 这一点可以在衣着上看到：时髦的人可能觉得被模仿是受恭维，但一旦新的时尚真正流行起来，他们就必须换成别的东西，以把自己标示为与众不同。

sentences.en: It may be the same with language, for social groups use characteristic styles of language to mark themselves off from other groups.
sentences.zh: 语言可能也是一样，因为社会群体用有特色的语言风格来把自己与其他群体区分开来。

sentences.en: A group that has high prestige may find that its style of speech is being imitated by other groups, and then its members may (perhaps subconsciously) begin to change it, perhaps by exaggerating its distinguishing characteristics.
sentences.zh: 一个声望高的群体可能发现自己的言语风格正被其他群体模仿，于是它的成员可能（也许是下意识地）开始改变它，也许是通过夸大其区别性的特征。

sentences.en: (E) However, while interaction between different languages, and between the dialects of a single language, can explain some changes in pronunciation, it cannot explain them all.
sentences.zh: 然而，虽然不同语言之间、以及一门语言各方言之间的相互作用能解释一些发音上的变化，但它无法解释所有的变化。

sentences.en: (F) Another cause that has been suggested is the fact that the imitation of children is imperfect: they copy their parents’ speech, but never reproduce it exactly.
sentences.zh: 被提出的另一个原因是，孩子的模仿是不完美的：他们模仿父母的言语，但从不完全准确地复制它。

sentences.en: This seems to be true enough and it moreover seems to be true that even adults show a certain amount of random variation in their pronunciation.
sentences.zh: 这似乎相当真实，而且似乎连成年人在他们的发音上也表现出一定程度的随机变异。

sentences.en: However, these facts cannot explain changes in pronunciation, unless it can be shown that there is some systematic trend in the failures in imitation.
sentences.zh: 然而，这些事实无法解释发音的变化，除非能表明在模仿失败中存在某种系统性的趋势。

sentences.en: If they are merely random deviations they will cancel one another out and there will be no net change in the language.
sentences.zh: 如果它们仅仅是随机的偏离，它们会相互抵消，语言中就不会有净变化。

sentences.en: For some of these random variations to be selected at the expense of others, there must be further forces at work.
sentences.zh: 要让这些随机变异中的一些以牺牲另一些为代价被选择出来，就必定有进一步的力量在起作用。

sentences.en: (G) One such force, which is often suggested, is known as the principle of ease.
sentences.zh: 一种这样的力量，常被提出，叫作省力原则。

sentences.en: We are all naturally lazy, it is argued, and so we tend to take short cuts in the movements of our speech organs, to replace movements calling for great accuracy or energy by less demanding ones, to omit sounds if they are not essential for understanding, and so on.
sentences.zh: 有人主张，我们天生都懒，所以我们倾向于在发音器官的动作上抄近道，用要求不那么高的动作来代替要求极高准确性或能量的动作，如果某些音对理解不是必需的就省略它们，等等。

sentences.en: For example, the word scant was once skamt, but the m has been changed to n under the influence of the following t.
sentences.zh: 比如，scant这个词曾经是skamt，但在后面t的影响下m已变成了n。

sentences.en: An economy of effort has thereby been achieved, because n and t are articulated in the same place (with the tip of the tongue against the teeth-ridge), whereas m is articulated elsewhere (with the two lips).
sentences.zh: 由此实现了一种省力，因为n和t是在同一个位置（用舌尖抵着齿龈）发音的，而m是在别处（用双唇）发音的。

sentences.en: The change from skamt to scant would be an example of assimilation, which is a very common kind of change.
sentences.zh: 从skamt到scant的变化会是同化的一个例子，同化是一种很常见的变化。

sentences.en: Assimilation is the changing of a sound under the influence of a neighbouring sound.
sentences.zh: 同化是一个音在相邻音的影响下发生的改变。

sentences.en: (H) Assimilation is not the only way in which we change our pronunciation in order to reduce effort.
sentences.zh: 同化并不是我们为减少力气而改变发音的唯一方式。

sentences.en: A sound may come to be pronounced less energetically, wherever it occurs: the English r and h sounds are undoubtedly pronounced much less vigorously now than they were a thousand years ago.
sentences.zh: 一个音可能逐渐被发得不那么用力，无论它出现在哪里：英语的r和h音如今无疑发得比一千年前要省力得多。

sentences.en: In some positions a sound may disappear altogether.
sentences.zh: 在某些位置，一个音可能完全消失。

sentences.en: At one time the t was pronounced in words like castle and Christmas, and the g in words like gnat and gnaw.
sentences.zh: 曾经，castle和Christmas这样的词里t是发音的，gnat和gnaw这样的词里g是发音的。

sentences.en: Sometimes a whole syllable is dropped out if it occurs twice running.
sentences.zh: 有时如果一个音节连续出现两次，整个音节就会被省去。

sentences.en: A modern example is temporary, which in Britain is pronounced as if it were tempory.
sentences.zh: 一个现代的例子是temporary，它在英国被读得好像是tempory。

records.title: The History of the Pencil V1

sentences.en: (A) The history of the pencil starts with a violent thunderstorm.
sentences.zh: 铅笔的历史起源于一场剧烈的雷暴。

sentences.en: When some particularly ferocious weather struck the Lake District in North West England in the sixteenth century, locals in the village of Borrowdale discovered a large uprooted tree.
sentences.zh: 16 世纪英格兰西北部湖区遭遇异常凶猛的天气时，博罗代尔（Borrowdale）村的当地人发现了一棵被连根拔起的大树。

sentences.en: Underneath the tree lay an unknown black substance which we now know as graphite, was slightly shiny and smooth to the touch.
sentences.zh: 树底下躺着一种当时未知的黑色物质，也就是我们如今所说的石墨——略微闪光、摸上去光滑。

sentences.en: And it left a black smear on the hands of all who touched it.
sentences.zh: 它会在每个触碰过它的人手上留下一道黑色痕迹。

sentences.en: (B) Initially, the local farmers used the newly discovered material as a handy way to identify their sheep.
sentences.zh: 起初，当地农夫把这种新发现的材料用作给绵羊做记号的便捷办法。

sentences.en: However, others quickly realised the potential for using this intriguing substance to write on paper.
sentences.zh: 然而，很快也有人意识到，这种引人好奇的物质有可以用来在纸上写字的潜力。

sentences.en: When it was untreated the material was very soft, which meant that it was messy to handle.
sentences.zh: 未经加工时，这种材料非常柔软，意味着处理起来很乱。

sentences.en: To make it fit for use with paper, people enclosed a thin core of the substance in stiff sheep hides or rope.
sentences.zh: 为了让它适合搭配纸张使用，人们把一根细小的物料芯包裹在坚硬的羊皮或绳索中。

sentences.en: At this time chemistry was still in its infancy.
sentences.zh: 那时的化学还处于起步阶段。

sentences.en: People searched for a word to describe this increasingly useful substance and came up with plumbago which, in Latin, means acts or writes like lead.
sentences.zh: 人们为这种愈发好用的物质寻找名字，最终得出 plumbago——这个拉丁文词意思是“像铅那样行为或书写”。

sentences.en: Later the name was changed to graphite.
sentences.zh: 后来这个名字被改为石墨（graphite）。

sentences.en: But because words have remarkable staying power, we still call graphite the lead of a pencil even though it is now known that there is no trace of real lead in graphite.
sentences.zh: 但由于词语有着惊人的延续力，我们至今仍把铅笔的笔芯称为“铅”，尽管现在已经清楚石墨中并没有真正铅的痕迹。

sentences.en: (C) Graphite has a very high melting point at around 3,500 degrees Celsius.
sentences.zh: 石墨的熔点非常高，约为 3500 摄氏度。

sentences.en: This made it invaluable to the British army and navy as a secret ingredient in the manufacture of cannon balls.
sentences.zh: 这使其作为铸造炮弹的一种秘密成分对英国陆军和海军极为珍贵。

sentences.en: The Royal Ordnance, or weaponry section of the British armed forces, used graphite as a lining inside the moulds for cannon balls, which, as a result, the British could turn out faster and more cheaply than their European rivals.
sentences.zh: 英国军械局（Royal Ordnance，即英国军队的兵器部门）将石墨用作炮弹模具内衬，结果英国可以比欧洲对手更快、更便宜地生产炮弹。

sentences.en: In addition to its value to the armed forces, the government quickly realised the commercial potential of the graphite at Borrowdale, and assumed control of all the mines there during the sixteenth century.
sentences.zh: 除了对军队的价值之外，政府很快也意识到博罗代尔石墨的商业潜力，并在 16 世纪间接管了那里的所有矿场。

sentences.en: Armed guards accompanied the precious graphite all the way down to the metal foundries by the naval shipyards in the south of England.
sentences.zh: 武装卫兵全程护送珍贵的石墨，一直送到位于英格兰南部海军船坞附近的金属铸造厂。

sentences.en: The graphite was so valuable that the locals, who called it wad, started to steal it.
sentences.zh: 石墨如此值钱，以至于当地人——他们把它称为 wad——开始偷盗它。

sentences.en: As a deterrent, an act of Parliament in 1752 made this offence punishable by time in prison.
sentences.zh: 为了起到震慑作用，1752 年议会通过一项法案，使这一罪行可以被判入狱。

sentences.en: (D) The Italians originally invented the wooden casing to hold a thin rod of plumbago firmly in place for ease of writing.
sentences.zh: 意大利人最早发明了用以稳固夹住一根细 plumbago 棒以便书写的木制外壳。

sentences.en: Italian craftsmen hollowed out two small sections of cedar wood, into one of which they laid the lead.
sentences.zh: 意大利工匠从一块雪松木材上挖出两个小槽，其中一个槽里放上“铅”。

sentences.en: They then glued the other section over the top and left the two halves to set.
sentences.zh: 然后他们把另一半木材粘在顶部，让两半放置凝固。

sentences.en: When dry, the whole apparatus formed what today we know as a pencil.
sentences.zh: 干透后，整个组件便构成了今天我们所知道的铅笔。

sentences.en: The Germans took this technique and developed it further by applying mass-production techniques to pencils.
sentences.zh: 德国人把这种工艺接过来，并以大规模生产工艺加以进一步发展，应用于铅笔。

sentences.en: At the same time Nicolas-Jacques Conté, a French officer in Napoleon Bonaparte’s army during the late 1700s, developed a method of mixing powdered graphite and clay together for firing in a kiln.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，1700 年代后期拿破仑·波拿巴军队中的法国军官尼古拉-雅克·孔泰（Nicolas-Jacques Conté）发明了一种把石墨粉和黏土混合后在窑中烧制的方法。

sentences.en: Adding more clay to the mixture helped make the pencil harder, sharper, and more precise in its mark.
sentences.zh: 在混合物中多加黏土可以让铅笔更硬、更锋利、笔迹更精确。

sentences.en: More graphite helped make a pencil mark that was softer, thicker and darker.
sentences.zh: 多加石墨则可以让铅笔笔迹更软、更粗、更深。

sentences.en: (E) The varying quality of pencil leads eventually gave rise to a system for categorizing the fineness of the pencil mark.
sentences.zh: 铅笔笔芯质量各异，最终催生了一套对笔迹细腻度进行分级的体系。

sentences.en: Pencil manufacturers all over the world still use this so-called HB grading system today.
sentences.zh: 全世界的铅笔制造商至今仍使用这种所谓的 HB 分级体系。

sentences.en: The H stands for the Hardness of the pencil while the B stands for its Blackness.
sentences.zh: H 代表铅笔的硬度（Hardness），B 代表其黑度（Blackness）。

sentences.en: An HB pencil is a standard pencil and a variety of letters and numbers are used to designate different types of lead.
sentences.zh: HB 铅笔是一种标准铅笔，人们用各种字母和数字组合来标示不同类型的笔芯。

sentences.en: (F) Significant seams of graphite exist in parts of China, which now produces most of the world’s pencils.
sentences.zh: 中国部分地区也存在重要的石墨矿层，目前全球大多数铅笔由中国生产。

sentences.en: Interestingly, the Borrowdale mine in the Lake District remains the only significant source of graphite in its near-pure form in the world.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，湖区的博罗代尔矿仍是世界上唯一一处接近纯净的石墨富集地。

sentences.en: Nowadays the highest grade of graphite at Borrowdale is totally exhausted, although other grades can still be found, and England’s pencil industry continues to thrive in the nearby town of Keswick.
sentences.zh: 如今博罗代尔最高品级的石墨已经完全枯竭，尽管仍可找到其他品级，而英格兰的铅笔业仍在附近的凯西克（Keswick）小镇蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: (G) The pencil has turned out to be a remarkably resilient and valuable tool whose use has survived well into our high-tech times, as a well-known story shows.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，铅笔是一种极具韧性、极有价值的工具，其使用在我们这个高科技时代仍然延续；一个广为流传的故事便可说明这一点。

sentences.en: It is sometimes said that the American space programme spent millions of dollars to invent a pen capable of writing in the zero gravity of space.
sentences.zh: 有时人们说，美国太空计划耗资数百万美元发明了一种能在太空零重力下书写的笔。

sentences.en: The Russians, by contrast, simply equipped their astronauts with good old-fashioned pencils that never let them down.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，俄罗斯人则简单地给宇航员配上了那种老式、靠谱的铅笔——从未让他们失望。

sentences.en: It should be pointed out though, that the popular myth about Americans overlooking the practical advantages of pencils in zero gravity is merely fiction.
sentences.zh: 不过，应当指出的是，关于美国人忽视铅笔在零重力下实用优势的流行说法纯属虚构。

sentences.en: In actual fact, both American and Russian astronauts were equipped with pencils in their respective countries’ first space flights.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在两国各自的首次太空飞行中，美国和俄罗斯的宇航员都配备了铅笔。

sentences.en: A private company later developed pens for writing in zero gravity.
sentences.zh: 一家私营公司后来才研发出可在零重力下书写的笔。

sentences.en: In fact, astronauts of every nation now use pens.
sentences.zh: 事实上，如今各国宇航员都使用笔了。

sentences.en: But no matter — pencils remain in use in every classroom, every planning, building and drawing office, and in every art studio in the world.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何——在世界每一间教室、每一处规划、建筑和绘图办公室以及每一间艺术工作室里，铅笔仍在被使用。

sentences.en: And there is nothing to suggest that we are likely to invent anything better than graphite to use in our pencils.
sentences.zh: 也没有任何迹象表明，我们会发明出比石墨更好的东西用作铅笔的笔芯。

sentences.en: (A) Tuatara are lizard-like reptiles found only in New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 楔齿蜥（tuatara）是一种形似蜥蜴的爬行动物，仅见于新西兰。

sentences.en: They are representative of ancient life forms.
sentences.zh: 它们是古老生命形态的代表。

sentences.en: Tuatara are the sole surviving members of an ancient lineage of reptiles called Sphenodontia, which is over 250 million years old.
sentences.zh: 楔齿蜥是一个名为楔齿蜥类（Sphenodontia）的古老爬行动物谱系中唯一存活至今的成员，该谱系已有超过2.5亿年的历史。

sentences.en: Because tuatara still resemble fossils of reptiles that lived during the age of dinosaurs, they are often called “living fossils”.
sentences.zh: 由于楔齿蜥至今仍与生活在恐龙时代的爬行动物化石相似，它们常被称为“活化石”。

sentences.en: Now only two species survive in New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 如今在新西兰仅存两个物种。

sentences.en: One is the Brothers Island tuatara which, until recent re-introductions to sanctuaries (safe places for wildlife), survived only on North Brother Island.
sentences.zh: 其一是兄弟岛楔齿蜥，在最近被重新引入各保护区（供野生动物栖息的安全之地）之前，它仅在北兄弟岛存活。

sentences.en: The other species is the common tuatara, which inhabits many other offshore islands.
sentences.zh: 另一个物种是普通楔齿蜥，栖息于许多其他近海岛屿。

sentences.en: Although the two species appear similar, they have genetic differences.
sentences.zh: 这两个物种虽然外表相似，却存在遗传上的差异。

sentences.en: Tuatara bones have been found in many parts of New Zealand; where dated, they are usually a few hundred to 5,000 years old.
sentences.zh: 在新西兰许多地区都发现过楔齿蜥的骨骼；凡经测定年代的，通常都有几百年至5000年的历史。

sentences.en: It is not known whether these bones belong to the two living species or to others that are now extinct.
sentences.zh: 这些骨骼究竟属于现存的两个物种，还是属于其他如今已灭绝的物种，尚不得而知。

sentences.en: (B) Many anatomical features distinguish tuatara from other living reptiles—for example, they have a distinctive pattern of openings in the skull, a unique type of haemoglobin in the blood, and males have no external reproductive organ.
sentences.zh: 许多解剖学特征把楔齿蜥与其他现存爬行动物区别开来——例如，它们的头骨上有一种独特的孔洞排布，血液中含有一种独特的血红蛋白，而雄性没有体外生殖器官。

sentences.en: Adults range from 30 to 75 centimetres in length and weigh between 250 and 1,200 grams.
sentences.zh: 成年个体体长在30至75厘米之间，体重介于250至1200克。

sentences.en: Males are larger than females and have more developed spines in the crest along the neck, back and tail.
sentences.zh: 雄性比雌性体型更大，沿颈、背和尾的脊冠上棘刺也更为发达。

sentences.en: (C) The male tuatara courts the female by approaching her with a proud walk.
sentences.zh: 雄性楔齿蜥求偶时，会以一种骄傲的步态向雌性靠近。

sentences.en: Tuatara mate in late summer, and the female usually lays 6–10 eggs the following spring in a shallow ground-level nest.
sentences.zh: 楔齿蜥在夏末交配，雌性通常在翌年春天于地面浅巢中产下6至10枚卵。

sentences.en: She may guard the nest for a few nights, then return to her underground burrow.
sentences.zh: 它可能会守护巢穴数晚，随后返回自己的地下洞穴。

sentences.en: The eggs incubate for about a year, so hatchlings emerge just as new eggs are being laid the next season.
sentences.zh: 卵的孵化期约为一年，因此幼体破壳而出之时，恰逢下一季新卵正被产下。

sentences.en: Evidence indicates that the sex of hatchlings is determined by both genetic and environmental factors: warmer eggs are more likely to produce males, while cooler eggs tend to produce females.
sentences.zh: 有证据表明，幼体的性别由遗传和环境两方面因素共同决定：较温暖的卵更可能孵出雄性，而较凉的卵则往往孵出雌性。

sentences.en: The hatchlings receive no parental care and must find their own food.
sentences.zh: 幼体得不到亲代的照料，必须自行觅食。

sentences.en: (D) Tuatara live a long time, reaching reproductive maturity at about 15 years and breeding for many decades.
sentences.zh: 楔齿蜥寿命很长，约在15岁达到性成熟，并能繁殖数十年之久。

sentences.en: Their maximum lifespan is uncertain, but many individuals have lived to 80 years while still looking vigorous and healthy.
sentences.zh: 它们的最长寿命尚不确定，但许多个体已活到80岁，看上去依然精力充沛、健康无恙。

sentences.en: Tuatara live in underground burrows and are more active at night, though they bask in the sun by day.
sentences.zh: 楔齿蜥栖居于地下洞穴，夜间更为活跃，不过白天也会晒太阳。

sentences.en: Both sexes are territorial; males aggressively defend their range by posturing and, if necessary, fighting.
sentences.zh: 雌雄两性都有领地意识；雄性会通过摆出姿态、必要时大打出手，来强势捍卫自己的领地。

sentences.en: Their teeth are their chief weapons, and a bite can cause serious injury.
sentences.zh: 牙齿是它们的主要武器，一口咬下去可造成严重伤害。

sentences.en: Tuatara are carnivorous, feeding on invertebrates, lizards and the baby seabirds with which they often share burrows.
sentences.zh: 楔齿蜥为肉食性动物，以无脊椎动物、蜥蜴，以及常与之共用洞穴的雏海鸟为食。

sentences.en: (E) Tuatara were once widespread and abundant on the New Zealand mainland, but when Polynesian settlers arrived (about 1250–1300 AD) they brought Pacific rats, which killed tuatara.
sentences.zh: 楔齿蜥曾在新西兰本岛广泛分布、数量众多，但当波利尼西亚移民到来（约公元1250至1300年）时，他们带来了太平洋鼠，而鼠会捕杀楔齿蜥。

sentences.en: By the time of European settlement in the 1840s, tuatara were almost extinct on the mainland.
sentences.zh: 到19世纪40年代欧洲人定居之时，楔齿蜥在本岛已近乎灭绝。

sentences.en: Some islands provided temporary refuges, but these too were eventually invaded by rats and other mammalian predators.
sentences.zh: 一些岛屿曾提供过暂时的庇护，但最终也遭到鼠类及其他哺乳类捕食者的入侵。

sentences.en: (F) Gradually tuatara became confined to 32 near-shore islands.
sentences.zh: 楔齿蜥逐渐被局限于32座近岸岛屿之上。

sentences.en: Many of these islands were tiny, some only one hectare in size.
sentences.zh: 这些岛屿大多很小，有的仅有1公顷大。

sentences.en: A few, such as the Poor Knights Islands off the northeastern coast of New Zealand and some islands in Cook Strait, still support the common tuatara.
sentences.zh: 其中少数岛屿，如位于新西兰东北海岸外的穷骑士群岛以及库克海峡中的一些岛屿，至今仍栖息着普通楔齿蜥。

sentences.en: The Brothers Island tuatara survived only on North Brother Island, but new populations have been created on Titi Island in the Marlborough Sounds and on Somes Island in Wellington Harbour.
sentences.zh: 兄弟岛楔齿蜥原本仅在北兄弟岛存活，但如今已在马尔堡峡湾的提提岛和惠灵顿港的索姆斯岛建立起新的种群。

sentences.en: (G) Tuatara can live in remarkably dense populations.
sentences.zh: 楔齿蜥能以相当高的密度聚居。

sentences.en: Most tuatara islands support 50–100 individuals per hectare, so an island of just 10 hectares may hold hundreds.
sentences.zh: 大多数有楔齿蜥栖息的岛屿每公顷可容纳50至100只，因此一座仅10公顷的岛屿就可能栖息着数百只。

sentences.en: Larger islands rich in seabirds and invertebrates—key tuatara prey—may support even greater densities.
sentences.zh: 较大的岛屿若海鸟和无脊椎动物——楔齿蜥的主要猎物——十分丰富，可承载的密度甚至更高。

sentences.en: The largest population is on Stephens Island, where numbers reach up to 2,500 per hectare in some areas, with a total of at least 30,000 individuals.
sentences.zh: 数量最多的种群在斯蒂芬斯岛，那里某些区域每公顷多达2500只，总数至少有3万只。

sentences.en: Overall, the tuatara population across all islands is estimated at 50,000–100,000.
sentences.zh: 总体而言，所有岛屿上的楔齿蜥种群估计在5万至10万只之间。

sentences.en: (H) Legal protection was granted to tuatara and their islands in 1895, yet the reptiles continued to decline.
sentences.zh: 1895年，楔齿蜥及其所在岛屿获得了法律保护，然而这种爬行动物的数量仍持续下降。

sentences.en: Since then, active conservation management has reversed the trend, and new populations have been established on predator-free islands.
sentences.zh: 此后，积极的保护管理扭转了这一趋势，并在没有捕食者的岛屿上建立了新的种群。

sentences.en: In the mid-1980s the New Zealand Wildlife Service (now the Department of Conservation) developed methods to eradicate rats from islands.
sentences.zh: 20世纪80年代中期，新西兰野生动物局（即如今的自然保护部）研究出了从岛上根除鼠害的方法。

sentences.en: Rats have since been removed from almost all tuatara islands, making these habitats safe for many threatened native species.
sentences.zh: 此后，几乎所有楔齿蜥岛屿上的鼠类都已被清除，使这些栖息地对许多受威胁的本土物种而言变得安全。

sentences.en: Conservationists have also collected eggs for incubation, bred tuatara in captivity, and relocated them to rat-free islands off the Northland coast and to Stephens Island in Cook Strait—areas never invaded by rats and largely free of other mammalian predators.
sentences.zh: 保护工作者还采集卵进行孵化，在人工饲养下繁育楔齿蜥，并将它们迁移到北地海岸外无鼠的岛屿以及库克海峡的斯蒂芬斯岛——这些地区从未遭鼠类入侵，也基本没有其他哺乳类捕食者。

sentences.en: Two additional predator-free islands now host tuatara, raising the total to 37.
sentences.zh: 如今又有两座无捕食者的岛屿栖息着楔齿蜥，使其岛屿总数增至37座。

sentences.en: Many more introductions are planned for islands and mainland reserves cleared of predators.
sentences.zh: 还有更多的引入计划，将在已清除捕食者的岛屿和本岛保护区中实施。

sentences.en: (A) You arrive at the office, review your to-do list and start to feel a headache coming on.
sentences.zh: 你到了办公室，看了看你的待办清单，开始觉得头疼起来。

sentences.en: You resolve to tackle the items as quickly as possible.
sentences.zh: 你下决心要尽快处理这些事项。

sentences.en: While you return calls, you sort e-mail and other letters.
sentences.zh: 在你回电话的同时，你整理电子邮件和其他信件。

sentences.en: You begin keying in slides for tomorrow’s presentation.
sentences.zh: 你开始为明天的演示录入幻灯片。

sentences.en: Then your manager comes in wanting an immediate update on sales figures.
sentences.zh: 然后你的经理进来，想要一份即时的销售数字更新。

sentences.en: You have just opened the spreadsheet when a very important customer calls.
sentences.zh: 你刚打开电子表格，一个非常重要的客户就打来了电话。

sentences.en: With the receiver held between your shoulder and your ear, you continue adding up the sales totals until, 15 minutes later, you finally manage, politely, to get rid of the client.
sentences.zh: 话筒夹在你的肩膀和耳朵之间，你继续把销售总额加起来，直到15分钟后，你终于设法礼貌地把这个客户打发走。

sentences.en: You’ve been multitasking again.
sentences.zh: 你又一次在多任务处理了。

sentences.en: (B) You may believe that anyone who wants to get ahead today should master the art of multitasking.
sentences.zh: 你可能相信，如今任何想出人头地的人都应该掌握多任务处理的艺术。

sentences.en: However, a recent study by the Families and Work Institute in New York City has found that 45 per cent of US workers believe that they are asked or expected to work on too many tasks at once.
sentences.zh: 然而，纽约市家庭与工作研究所最近的一项研究发现，45%的美国员工相信，他们被要求或被期望同时处理太多的任务。

sentences.en: Managers may be surprised to learn that they are actually wasting their workers’ time.
sentences.zh: 管理者可能会惊讶地得知，他们实际上是在浪费员工的时间。

sentences.en: As it turns out, the human brain cannot really master the computer’s art of crunching data in the background while moving between process windows.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，人类的大脑并不真正能掌握计算机那种在后台处理数据、同时在进程窗口之间切换的本领。

sentences.en: Instead, a growing number of studies show that trying to juggle jobs rather than completing them sequentially can take longer and leave workers with a reduced ability to perform each task.
sentences.zh: 相反，越来越多的研究表明，试图同时兼顾多项工作、而不是依次完成它们，可能花更长时间，并让员工执行每项任务的能力下降。

sentences.en: In addition, the stress associated with multitasking may contribute to short-term memory difficulties.
sentences.zh: 此外，与多任务处理相关的压力可能造成短期记忆困难。

sentences.en: The combination results in inefficiency, careless thinking and mistakes – not to mention the possible dangers of divided attention for drivers, air-traffic controllers and others who handle machinery.
sentences.zh: 这种组合导致低效、粗心的思考和错误——更不用说注意力分散对司机、空中交通管制员、以及其他操作机械者可能造成的危险了。

sentences.en: (C) How can a time-management strategy that has become part of the common wisdom actually be so wrong?
sentences.zh: 一种已成为常识一部分的时间管理策略，怎么会实际上如此错误呢？

sentences.en: Exploring that question requires a closer look at an area of consciousness research that examines how the brain focuses attention.
sentences.zh: 探究那个问题需要更仔细地审视意识研究的一个领域，它考察大脑如何集中注意力。

sentences.en: One of the modern foundations of current knowledge of multitasking was laid in 1935, when the American psychologist John Ridley Stroop reported that processing information from one task could cause interference with another.
sentences.zh: 当前关于多任务处理的知识，其现代根基之一奠定于1935年，当时美国心理学家约翰·里德利·斯特鲁普报告说，处理来自一项任务的信息会对另一项任务造成干扰。

sentences.en: Stroop noticed that when study participants were asked to name the colour of a word – such as ‘green’ – printed in a different colour – red, for example – they experienced difficulty saying the name of the colour.
sentences.zh: 斯特鲁普注意到，当研究参与者被要求说出一个用不同颜色——比如红色——印出的词——比如“绿色”——的颜色时，他们说出该颜色名称时感到困难。

sentences.en: This phenomenon is thought to occur when two tasks get tangled: the brain must suppress one that has been learned so well that it has become automatic (reading) to attend to a second task that requires concentration (naming the colour).
sentences.zh: 人们认为，这种现象在两项任务纠缠在一起时发生：大脑必须抑制一项已学得如此之好、以至于已变得自动化的任务（阅读），以照管一项需要专注的第二项任务（说出颜色）。

sentences.en: (D) During the past couple of decades, psychologists have probed more deeply into the nature and limitations of multitasking.
sentences.zh: 在过去几十年里，心理学家更深入地探究了多任务处理的本质和局限。

sentences.en: Psychologist and brain-researcher Ernst Pöppel, of the Ludwig-Maximilian University in Munich, believes that it is impossible to carry out two or three different tasks simultaneously with the same degree of concentration.
sentences.zh: 慕尼黑路德维希-马克西米利安大学的心理学家、大脑研究者恩斯特·珀佩尔相信，以同等的专注程度同时执行两三项不同的任务是不可能的。

sentences.en: He says that seemingly simultaneous awareness and processing of information actually take place in ‘three-second windows’.
sentences.zh: 他说，看似同时进行的对信息的觉察和处理，实际上发生在“三秒钟的窗口”里。

sentences.en: (E) In these three-second segments, the brain takes in, as a block, all the data about the environment streaming in from the sensory systems; subsequent events are processed in the next window.
sentences.zh: 在这些三秒钟的片段里，大脑把从感官系统涌入的关于环境的所有数据作为一个整块接收进来；随后的事件在下一个窗口里被处理。

sentences.en: So a person can concentrate on a conversation for three seconds, then for three seconds on a crying child, and three seconds on a computer screen.
sentences.zh: 所以一个人可以专注于一段对话三秒钟，然后专注于一个哭泣的孩子三秒钟，再专注于一个电脑屏幕三秒钟。

sentences.en: While one subject at a time occupies the foreground of consciousness, the others stay in the background until they, in turn, are given access to the central processor.
sentences.zh: 当一次一个主题占据意识的前台时，其他主题留在后台，直到它们轮流被给予进入中央处理器的机会。

sentences.en: (F) Another experiment by psychologist David E.
sentences.zh: 另一项实验，由心理学家戴维·E.

sentences.en: Meyer, of the University of Michigan, quantified just how much time we can lose when we shuttle between tasks.
sentences.zh: 迈耶（密歇根大学）量化了当我们在任务之间穿梭时究竟会损失多少时间。

sentences.en: The researchers asked test participants to write a report and check their e-mail at the same time.
sentences.zh: 研究人员要求测试参与者同时写一份报告并查看他们的电子邮件。

sentences.en: Those individuals who constantly jumped back and forth between the two tasks took about one and a half times as long to finish as those who completed one job before turning to the other.
sentences.zh: 那些在两项任务之间不断来回跳的人，完成所花的时间大约是那些先完成一项工作再转向另一项的人的一倍半。

sentences.en: Each switchover from one task to another meant re-thinking and thus involved additional neural resources.
sentences.zh: 每一次从一项任务切换到另一项，都意味着重新思考，因此涉及额外的神经资源。

sentences.en: In effect, the brain needs time to shut off the rules for one task and to turn on the rules for another.
sentences.zh: 实际上，大脑需要时间来关闭一项任务的规则、并开启另一项任务的规则。

sentences.en: ‘Multitasking saves time only when it is a matter of relaxed, routine tasks,’ Meyer says.
sentences.zh: 迈耶说：“只有在放松的、例行的任务上，多任务处理才会节省时间。”

sentences.en: It also takes the brain longer to adapt when switching rapidly back to an interrupted task rather than waiting longer before switching back.
sentences.zh: 当迅速切换回一项被打断的任务时，大脑也要花更长时间来适应，而不是在切换回去之前多等一会儿。

sentences.en: (G) By its nature multitasking is stressful, and the area in the brain most involved with multitasking is also most affected by the resulting stress.
sentences.zh: 多任务处理本质上就是有压力的，而大脑中最涉及多任务处理的区域，也最受由此产生压力的影响。

sentences.en: Located behind the forehead, the prefrontal cortex – which neuroscientists call the ‘executive’ part of the brain – helps us to assess tasks, prioritise them and assign mental resources.
sentences.zh: 位于前额后方的前额叶皮层——神经科学家称之为大脑的“执行”部分——帮助我们评估任务、对它们排定优先次序、并分配心理资源。

sentences.en: It also ‘marks’ the spot at which a task has been interrupted, so that we can return to it later.
sentences.zh: 它还“标记”出一项任务被打断的位置，以便我们日后能回到它那里。

sentences.en: This stress can also affect brain cells in another region, the hippocampus, which is important for forming new memories; damage in that area also makes it difficult for a person to acquire new skills.
sentences.zh: 这种压力还可能影响另一个区域、即海马体的脑细胞，海马体对形成新记忆很重要；那个区域的损伤也使一个人难以习得新技能。

sentences.en: (H) Psychiatrists Edward Hallowell and John Ratey, of Harvard University, say that multitasking can bring about a brain condition that causes sufferers to constantly seek new information while having difficulties concentrating on its content.
sentences.zh: 哈佛大学的精神科医生爱德华·哈洛韦尔和约翰·拉提说，多任务处理可能引发一种大脑状况，使患者不断寻求新信息、却难以专注于其内容。

sentences.en: All in all, it may be wise to let the e-mail wait while you work on your presentation.
sentences.zh: 总而言之，在你处理演示时，让电子邮件等一等也许是明智的。

sentences.en: You will save time and perform each task better.
sentences.zh: 你会节省时间、并把每项任务做得更好。

sentences.en: (A) The human settlement of the southern extremity of the Americas has always fascinated prehistorians.
sentences.zh: 美洲南端的人类定居一直让史前学家着迷。

sentences.en: Viewed from a global perspective, this was the last major continental land mass to be reached by human beings.
sentences.zh: 从全球视角看，这是人类抵达的最后一块主要大陆。

sentences.en: The earliest occupation of Patagonia carries obvious implications for understanding when the North and South American continents were peopled, because it gives a baseline that all calculations regarding the rate of dispersion of humans throughout both continents must take into account.
sentences.zh: 对巴塔哥尼亚最早占居的研究对理解南北美洲何时有人居住具有显然的意义，因为它提供了一条基线——一切关于人类在两大洲扩散速率的计算都必须考虑它。

sentences.en: (B) For many years the human settlement of North and South America has been conceived of as beginning in the far north and travelling progressively southwards to Patagonia.
sentences.zh: 许多年来，南北美洲的人类定居一直被设想为从遥远北方开始，向南逐步推进到巴塔哥尼亚。

sentences.en: However, fundamental disagreements developed concerning the length of time involved.
sentences.zh: 然而，在所涉时间长短上出现了根本分歧。

sentences.en: Some scholars accepted a human presence in the Americas as early as 20,000 years ago, while others proposed that it could date no earlier than 8,000 years ago, and the debate is still with us today.
sentences.zh: 一些学者接受人类早在 20000 年前就已在美洲存在，而另一些学者则提出可能不早于 8000 年前——这一争论至今仍在。

sentences.en: (C) The idea of a relatively ‘late’ settlement of the Americas (around 8,000 years ago) implies that a rapid process of migration took place.
sentences.zh: 美洲被相对“晚”地定居（约 8000 年前）这一想法意味着发生了一次快速迁徙过程。

sentences.en: Herein lies a second debate, which revolves around the question of how migration is to be understood.
sentences.zh: 这里就引出第二场争论，围绕的是“迁徙”该如何被理解。

sentences.en: The ‘late’ model demands a hypothetical migration conceived of as a single, continually advancing wave of settlement.
sentences.zh: “晚期”模型要求一种假想的迁徙——被设想为一波单一的、不断推进的定居浪潮。

sentences.en: This has always been difficult to take seriously, and many scholars now support the idea of an ‘early’ model that sees the migration as a less ordered migration, and this is surely the most realistic scenario as migrants slowly adapted to the diverse natural habitats they would have met while travelling through the continent.
sentences.zh: 这种说法一直难以让人当真，许多学者现在支持一种“早期”模型——把这次迁徙视为一种较无秩序的迁徙；考虑到迁徙者在穿越大陆时要慢慢适应各种自然栖息地，这显然是最符合现实的图景。

sentences.en: (D) Those who argue for an earlier settlement, however, must contend with the lack of unequivocal evidence for archaeological sites older than around 14,000 years.
sentences.zh: 然而，主张更早定居的人必须面对的事实是：没有 14000 年前的考古遗址的确凿证据。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, evidence for human occupation of the centre of South America is now securely dated to around 12,500 years ago at the Monte Verde site, which casts doubt on the ‘late’ model.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，关于人类占据南美中部的证据现在已可靠地被测定为距今约 12500 年（蒙特韦尔德遗址，Monte Verde），这让“晚期”模型受到质疑。

sentences.en: The lack of archaeological evidence further south for this time period may be explained by the obstacle to humans on foot posed by the huge glacial streams that were present at that time.
sentences.zh: 对于这一时期更南方缺乏考古证据的现象，可解释为当时存在的巨大冰川河流对步行的人类构成了障碍。

sentences.en: (E) We can speculate then that the retreat of the Patagonian glaciers around 14,000 years ago allowed the initial human intrusion into a pristine environment, which was similar to that of early post-glacial Europe.
sentences.zh: 那么我们可以推测：约 14000 年前巴塔哥尼亚冰川的后撤让最初的人类得以进入一种与冰期后欧洲相似的原始环境。

sentences.en: Human settlement of the vast horizontal expanse of treeless high country must have been tenuous at best, and the evidence for this occupation remains relatively scant, most of it coming from rock shelters in Argentina and Chile.
sentences.zh: 在辽阔横向、无树的高地上，人类定居最多也只能是单薄的，关于这种占居的证据相对稀少，大多来自阿根廷和智利的岩棚。

sentences.en: There is, however, reliable evidence from these sites to confirm the presence of humans by around 11,000 years ago in different habitats, and some hints of an even older occupation.
sentences.zh: 然而，来自这些遗址的可靠证据可以确认：约 11000 年前在不同栖息地都已有人类存在，并且有更早占居的某些线索。

sentences.en: However, some other sites where evidence for even earlier human occupation was initially posited have recently come under fresh scrutiny.
sentences.zh: 不过，最初被假定有更早人类占居证据的某些其他遗址近来受到了重新审视。

sentences.en: This is because anthropologists have come to recognise that bones or other evidence may be deposited in caves by natural agency—in other words, by other forces such as floods or predators—and not necessarily by humans.
sentences.zh: 原因在于人类学家已经认识到，骨骼或其他证据可能由自然作用——换言之，由洪水或捕食者等其他力量——堆积于洞穴中，而不必然由人类带入。

sentences.en: (F) We shall turn now to a more detailed discussion of the archaeological evidence found in various parts of Patagonia.
sentences.zh: 现在我们将更详细地讨论在巴塔哥尼亚各地发现的考古证据。

sentences.en: At the site located beside Chinchihuapi Creek, excavations have produced convincing evidence of human occupation, including hut foundations and wooden artefacts.
sentences.zh: 在 Chinchihuapi 溪畔的遗址处，发掘提供了人类占居的有力证据——包括小屋的地基和木质工艺品。

sentences.en: They were buried in layers of peat, which has the property of preserving wood remarkably well, and as a result, radiocarbon dating tests have shown these artefacts to date from around 12,500 years ago.
sentences.zh: 它们被埋在泥炭层中，而泥炭具有非常出色的保存木材的特性；结果，放射性碳测年表明这些工艺品距今约 12500 年。

sentences.en: One of the most famous Patagonian sites is a cave known as Los Toldos.
sentences.zh: 巴塔哥尼亚最著名的遗址之一是一个被称为 Los Toldos 的洞穴。

sentences.en: However, the evidence from this site has recently been called into question, because dispersed flecks of carbon used in the test process were taken unsystematically from many different places at the site.
sentences.zh: 然而该遗址的证据近来受到了质疑，因为测年过程所用的零散碳屑是从遗址许多不同位置无系统地采集的。

sentences.en: As a result, the association of this material with the artefacts is not at all clear.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些材料与工艺品之间的关联根本不清晰。

sentences.en: About 150 kilometres to the south is the site called El Ceibo, where a similar collection of artefacts to that found at Los Toldos has been discovered from the lowest levels of the dig, but as yet no radiocarbon dates are available, and this sort of analysis of the existing evidence is required before the site’s value can be confirmed.
sentences.zh: 以南约 150 公里处的遗址叫 El Ceibo——在那里从挖掘最低层中发现了一批与 Los Toldos 类似的工艺品，但目前还没有放射性碳测年；在该遗址价值得到确认之前，需要对现有证据进行此类分析。

sentences.en: (G) The Arroyo Eeo site is located very close to the high plateau.
sentences.zh: Arroyo Eeo 遗址位于非常靠近高原的地方。

sentences.en: The artefacts from the earliest occupations were found at the same depth and have the same origins as those from Los Toldos, and have been securely dated to around 9,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 来自最早期占居层的工艺品发现于同一深度，与 Los Toldos 的工艺品同源，并已被可靠地定年至约 9000 年前。

sentences.en: Another site that is mentioned in the debate is at Las Buitreras, where a number of stone flakes associated with bone remains of various animals have been discovered.
sentences.zh: 另一个在争论中被提及的遗址是 Las Buitreras——那里发现了一批与多种动物骨骼遗骸相关的石片。

sentences.en: However, anthropologists now believe that presumed cut marks on the bones are somewhat dubious, and despite detailed testing there is no way of securely relating any of these remains to human occupation.
sentences.zh: 然而人类学家现在认为，骨头上推测的切痕颇为可疑；尽管经过细致测试，仍无法将这些遗骸中的任何一件可靠地与人类占居联系起来。

sentences.en: Finally, some 50 kilometres to the south is the site at Cueva Fell, which was the first Patagonian site to be systematically studied by modern archaeological methods.
sentences.zh: 最后，向南约 50 公里的 Cueva Fell 遗址，是巴塔哥尼亚第一个被现代考古方法系统研究的遗址。

sentences.en: However, it is now recognised that the utility of this site must be restricted to its direct vicinity, given changes to the nearby area caused by flooding, and findings cannot be freely extrapolated further afield.
sentences.zh: 然而现在人们认识到，由于附近地区由洪水所致的变化，该遗址的有用性必须被限制在其直接附近，研究结果不能随意外推到更远的地方。

sentences.en: (H) In conclusion, based on the evidence from a number of reliable sites, it seems probable that human populations reached Patagonia around 11,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 总之，基于来自若干可靠遗址的证据，人类大约在 11000 年前抵达巴塔哥尼亚似乎是可能的。

sentences.en: A Music and the brain are both endlessly fascinating subjects, and as a neuroscientist specialising in auditory learning and memory, I find them especially intriguing.
sentences.zh: 音乐和大脑都是引人入胜得没有尽头的题目，而作为一名专攻听觉学习和记忆的神经科学家，我觉得它们尤其耐人寻味。

sentences.en: So I had high expectations of Musicophilia, the latest offering from neurologist and prolific author Oliver Sacks.
sentences.zh: 所以我对《音乐爱好》抱有很高的期望，这是神经病学家、多产作家奥利弗·萨克斯的最新作品。

sentences.en: And I confess to feeling a little guilty reporting that my reactions to the book are mixed.
sentences.zh: 而我承认，在报告我对这本书的反应是喜忧参半时，我感到有点内疚。

sentences.en: B Sacks himself is the best part of Musicophilia.
sentences.zh: 萨克斯本人是《音乐爱好》最精彩的部分。

sentences.en: He richly documents his own life in the book and reveals highly personal experiences.
sentences.zh: 他在书中详尽地记录了自己的人生，并披露了高度私人的经历。

sentences.en: The photograph of him on the cover of the book-which shows him wearing headphones, eyes closed, clearly enchanted as he listens to Alfred Brendel perform Beethoven’s Pathetique Sonata-makes a positive impression that is borne out by the contents of the book.
sentences.zh: 书封面上他的那张照片——照片中他戴着耳机、闭着眼睛，显然在聆听阿尔弗雷德·布伦德尔演奏贝多芬的《悲怆奏鸣曲》时陶醉其中——留下了一个正面的印象，而这一印象被书的内容所印证。

sentences.en: Sacks’ voice throughout is steady and erudite but never pontifical.
sentences.zh: 萨克斯的笔调通篇沉稳而博学，却从不说教。

sentences.en: He is neither self-conscious nor self-promoting.
sentences.zh: 他既不拘谨也不自我推销。

sentences.en: C The preface gives a good idea of what the book will deliver.
sentences.zh: 前言很好地说明了这本书将带来什么。

sentences.en: In it, Sacks explains that he wants to convey the insights gleaned from the “enormous and rapidly growing body of work on the neural underpinnings of musical perception and imagery, and the complex and often bizarre disorders to which these are prone.”
sentences.zh: 在其中，萨克斯解释说，他想传达从“关于音乐感知与意象之神经基础、以及它们容易出现的复杂而往往离奇之失调的庞大且快速增长的研究成果”中所采撷的见解。

sentences.en: He also stresses the importance of “the simple art of observation” and “the richness of the human context.”
sentences.zh: 他还强调“朴素的观察艺术”和“人类情境的丰富性”的重要性。

sentences.en: He wants to combine “observation and description with the latest in technology,” he says, and to imaginatively enter into the experience of his patients and subjects.
sentences.zh: 他说，他想把“观察和描述与最新的技术”结合起来，并富有想象力地进入他的病人和研究对象的体验之中。

sentences.en: The reader can see that Sacks, who has been practicing neurology for 40 years, is torn between the “old-fashioned” path of observation and the new-fangled, high-tech approach: He knows that he needs to take heed of the latter, but his heart lies with the former.
sentences.zh: 读者可以看出，从医已40年的萨克斯，在“老派的”观察之路和新潮的高科技方法之间左右为难：他知道自己需要重视后者，但他的心在前者。

sentences.en: D The book consists mainly of detailed descriptions of cases, most of them involving patients whom Sacks has seen in his practice.
sentences.zh: 这本书主要由对病例的详细描述构成，其中大多数涉及萨克斯在行医中见过的病人。

sentences.en: Brief discussions of contemporary neuroscientific reports are sprinkled liberally throughout the text.
sentences.zh: 对当代神经科学报告的简短讨论被大量地撒布在全书之中。

sentences.en: Part, “Haunted by Music,” begins with the strange case of Tony Cicoria, a nonmusical, middle-aged surgeon who was consumed by a love of music after being hit by lightning.
sentences.zh: 第一部分“被音乐萦绕”以托尼·奇科里亚这个奇特的病例开篇，他是一位不懂音乐、中年的外科医生，在被闪电击中后被对音乐的热爱所吞没。

sentences.en: He suddenly began to crave listening to piano music, which he had never cared for in the past.
sentences.zh: 他突然开始渴望聆听钢琴音乐，而他过去从不在意这种音乐。

sentences.en: He started to play the piano and then to compose music, which arose spontaneously in his mind in a “torrent” of notes.
sentences.zh: 他开始弹钢琴、然后作曲，音乐以一股音符的“激流”自发地在他脑海中涌现。

sentences.en: How could this happen?
sentences.zh: 这怎么会发生呢？

sentences.en: Was the cause psychological?
sentences.zh: 原因是心理上的吗？

sentences.en: (He had had a near-death experience when the lightning struck him.)
sentences.zh: （闪电击中他时他曾有过一次濒死体验。）

sentences.en: Or was it the direct result of a change in the auditory regions of his cerebral cortex?
sentences.zh: 还是它是他大脑皮层听觉区域发生变化的直接结果？

sentences.en: Electroencephalography (EEG) showed his brain waves to be normal in the mid-1990s, just after his trauma and subsequent “conversion” to music.
sentences.zh: 脑电图在20世纪90年代中期、就在他遭受创伤及随后“皈依”音乐之后，显示他的脑电波是正常的。

sentences.en: There are now more sensitive tests, but Cicoria, has declined to undergo them; he does not want to delve into the causes of his musicality.
sentences.zh: 现在有更灵敏的检测了，但奇科里亚谢绝接受它们；他不想深究他音乐才能的成因。

sentences.en: What a shame!
sentences.zh: 真是可惜！

sentences.en: E Part II, “A Range of Musicality,” covers a wider variety of topics, but unfortunately, some of the chapters offer little or nothing that is new.
sentences.zh: 第二部分“音乐才能的范围”涵盖了更广泛多样的话题，但不幸的是，有些章节提供的新东西很少或根本没有。

sentences.en: For example, chapter 13, which is five pages long, merely notes that the blind often has better hearing than the sighted.
sentences.zh: 比如，第13章有五页长，却仅仅指出盲人往往比视力正常者听觉更好。

sentences.en: The most interesting chapters are those that present the strangest cases.
sentences.zh: 最有意思的章节是那些呈现最奇特病例的。

sentences.en: Chapter 8 is about “amusia,” an inability to hear sounds like music, and “dysharmonia,” a highly specific impairment of the ability to hear harmony, with the ability to understand melody left intact.
sentences.zh: 第8章是关于“失乐症”，一种听不出音乐之类声音的无能，以及“失谐症”，一种听辨和声能力高度特定的损伤，而理解旋律的能力则完好无损。

sentences.en: Such specific “dissociations” are found throughout the cases Sacks recounts.
sentences.zh: 这样特定的“分离”现象贯穿于萨克斯所讲述的病例之中。

sentences.en: F To Sacks’s credit, part III, “Memory, Movement and Music,” brings us into the underappreciated realm of music therapy.
sentences.zh: 值得称道的是，萨克斯的第三部分“记忆、运动与音乐”把我们带入了音乐治疗这一未被充分重视的领域。

sentences.en: Chapter 16 explains how “melodic intonation therapy” is being used to help expressive aphasic patients (those unable to express their thoughts verbally following a stroke or other cerebral incident) once again become capable of fluent speech.
sentences.zh: 第16章解释了“旋律语调疗法”如何被用来帮助表达性失语症患者（那些在中风或其他脑部事件后无法用言语表达自己想法的人）重新变得能够流利说话。

sentences.en: In chapter 20, Sacks demonstrates the near-miraculous power of music to animate Parkinson’s patients and other people with severe movement disorders, even those who are frozen into odd postures.
sentences.zh: 在第20章，萨克斯展示了音乐近乎奇迹般的、让帕金森病患者及其他有严重运动障碍的人活跃起来的力量，甚至包括那些僵在古怪姿势中的人。

sentences.en: Scientists cannot yet explain how music achieves this effect
sentences.zh: 科学家还无法解释音乐是如何取得这种效果的。

sentences.en: G To readers who are unfamiliar with neuroscience and music behavior, Musicophilia may be something of a revelation.
sentences.zh: 对于不熟悉神经科学和音乐行为的读者来说，《音乐爱好》也许算得上一种启示。

sentences.en: But the book will not satisfy those seeking the causes and implications of the phenomena Sacks describes.
sentences.zh: 但这本书无法满足那些寻求萨克斯所描述现象之成因和含义的人。

sentences.en: For one thing, Sacks appears to be more at ease discussing patients than discussing experiments.
sentences.zh: 一方面，萨克斯讨论病人时似乎比讨论实验时更自在。

sentences.en: And he tends to be rather uncritical in accepting scientific findings and theories.
sentences.zh: 而且他在接受科学发现和理论时往往相当不加批判。

sentences.en: H It’s true that the causes of music-brain oddities remain poorly understood.
sentences.zh: 音乐与大脑之奇异现象的成因仍然知之甚少，这是真的。

sentences.en: However, Sacks could have done more to draw out some of the implications of the careful observations that he and other neurologists have made and of the treatments that have been successful.
sentences.zh: 然而，萨克斯本可以做更多，去引出他和其他神经病学家所做的那些仔细观察、以及那些已经成功的治疗的一些含义。

sentences.en: For example, he might have noted that the many specific dissociations among components of music comprehension, such as loss of the ability to perceive harmony but not melody, indicate that there is no music center in the brain.
sentences.zh: 比如，他本可以指出，音乐理解各组成部分之间的许多特定分离现象，比如丧失感知和声却不丧失感知旋律的能力，表明大脑中并不存在一个音乐中枢。

sentences.en: Because many people who read the book are likely to believe in the brain localisation of all mental functions, this was a missed educational opportunity.
sentences.zh: 由于许多读这本书的人很可能相信所有心理功能都在大脑中有定位，这是一个被错过的教育机会。

sentences.en: I Another conclusion one could draw is that there seem to be no “cures” for neurological problems involving music.
sentences.zh: 人们可以得出的另一个结论是，对于涉及音乐的神经学问题，似乎没有“治愈之法”。

sentences.en: A drug can alleviate a symptom in one patient and aggravate it in another or can have both positive and negative effects in the same patient.
sentences.zh: 一种药物可以缓解一个病人的某个症状、却使另一个病人的症状加重，或者在同一个病人身上既有正面又有负面的效果。

sentences.en: Treatments mentioned seem to be almost exclusively antiepileptic medications, which “damp down” the excitability of the brain in general; their effectiveness varies widely.
sentences.zh: 提到的治疗似乎几乎全都是抗癫痫药物，它们总体上“抑制”大脑的兴奋性；它们的有效性差异很大。

sentences.en: J Finally, in many of the cases described here the patient with music-brain symptoms is reported to have “normal” EEG results.
sentences.zh: 最后，在这里描述的许多病例中，有音乐与大脑症状的病人被报告有“正常”的脑电图结果。

sentences.en: Although Sacks recognises the existence of new technologies, among them far more sensitive ways to analyze brain waves than the standard neurological EEG test, he does not call for their use.
sentences.zh: 尽管萨克斯承认新技术的存在，其中包括比标准神经学脑电图检测灵敏得多的分析脑电波的方法，但他没有呼吁使用它们。

sentences.en: In fact, although he exhibits the greatest compassion for patients, he conveys no sense of urgency about the pursuit of new avenues in the diagnosis and treatment of music-brain disorders.
sentences.zh: 事实上，尽管他对病人表现出最大的同情，但他没有传达出任何对追求音乐与大脑失调诊断和治疗新途径的紧迫感。

sentences.en: This absence echoes the book’s preface, in which Sacks expresses fear that “the simple art of observation may be lost” if we rely too much on new technologies.
sentences.zh: 这种缺失呼应了这本书的前言，萨克斯在其中表达了一种担忧，即如果我们过于依赖新技术，“朴素的观察艺术可能会失传”。

sentences.en: He does call for both approaches, though, and we can only hope that the neurological community will respond.
sentences.zh: 不过他确实呼吁两种方法并用，而我们只能希望神经学界会作出回应。

records.title: Music Language We All Speak
records.titleZh: 我们都在使用的音乐语言

sentences.en: (A) Music is one of the human species’ relatively few universal abilities.
sentences.zh: 音乐是人类物种为数不多的普世能力之一。

sentences.en: Without formal training, any individual, from Stone Age tribesman to suburban teenager, has the ability to recognise music and, in some fashion, to make it.
sentences.zh: 任何个人——从石器时代部落人到郊区少年——不用经过正式训练，都能识别音乐，并以某种方式创造它。

sentences.en: Why this should be so is a mystery.
sentences.zh: 为什么如此，是个谜。

sentences.en: After all, music isn’t necessary for getting through the day, and if it aids in reproduction, it does so only in highly indirect ways.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，音乐对度过一天并非必需；如果它有助于繁殖，那也只是以非常间接的方式。

sentences.en: Language, by contrast, is also everywhere — but for reasons that are more obvious.
sentences.zh: 语言同样无处不在——但原因更明显。

sentences.en: With language, you and the members of your tribe can organise a migration across Africa, build reed boats and cross the seas, and communicate at night even when you can’t see each other.
sentences.zh: 通过语言，你和你部落的成员可以组织一场穿越非洲的迁徙、建造芦苇船渡海，并在夜里看不见对方时仍能交流。

sentences.en: Modern culture, in all its technological extravagance, springs directly from the human talent for manipulating symbols and syntax.
sentences.zh: 现代文化——以其全部技术上的炫目——直接源自人类操纵符号和句法的才能。

sentences.en: Scientists have always been intrigued by the connection between music and language.
sentences.zh: 科学家一直对音乐与语言之间的联系感兴趣。

sentences.en: Yet over the years, words and melody have acquired a vastly different status in the lab and the seminar room.
sentences.zh: 然而多年来，词语和旋律在实验室和研讨室中获得了截然不同的地位。

sentences.en: While language has long been considered essential to unlocking the mechanisms of human intelligence, music is generally treated as an evolutionary frippery — mere “auditory cheesecake”, as the Harvard cognitive scientist Steven Pinker puts it.
sentences.zh: 语言长期被视为解开人类智能机制的关键，而音乐通常被视为一种进化上的小装饰——正如哈佛认知科学家史蒂芬·平克（Steven Pinker）所言的“听觉芝士蛋糕”。

sentences.en: (B) But thanks to a decade-long wave of neuroscience research, that tune is changing.
sentences.zh: 但得益于过去十年神经科学研究的浪潮，这种基调正在改变。

sentences.en: A flurry of recent publications suggests that language and music may equally be able to tell us who we are and where we’re from — not just emotionally, but biologically.
sentences.zh: 近期一系列出版物表明：语言和音乐同样能够告诉我们“我们是谁、我们来自哪里”——不仅在情感层面，也在生物学层面。

sentences.en: In July, the journal Nature Neuroscience devoted a special issue to the topic.
sentences.zh: 今年 7 月，《自然·神经科学》（Nature Neuroscience）刊发了一期专题。

sentences.en: And in an article in the 6 August issue of the Journal of Neuroscience, David Schwartz, Catherine Howe and Dale Purves of Duke University argued that the sounds of music and the sounds of language are intricately connected.
sentences.zh: 而在 8 月 6 日的《神经科学杂志》（Journal of Neuroscience）上，杜克大学的戴维·施瓦茨（David Schwartz）、凯瑟琳·豪（Catherine Howe）和戴尔·珀维斯（Dale Purves）则提出：音乐之声与语言之声有着错综复杂的联系。

sentences.en: To grasp the originality of this idea, it’s necessary to realise two things about how music has traditionally been understood.
sentences.zh: 要把握这个观点的原创性，必须先认识到音乐传统上是如何被理解的两点。

sentences.en: First, musicologists have long emphasised that while each culture stamps a special identity onto its music, music itself has some universal qualities.
sentences.zh: 第一，音乐学家长期强调：尽管每种文化都会在其音乐上打上独特的印记，但音乐本身具有一些普世品质。

sentences.en: For example, in virtually all cultures, sound is divided into some or all of the 12 intervals that make up the chromatic scale — that is, the scale represented by the keys on a piano.
sentences.zh: 例如，几乎所有文化中，声音都被划分到构成半音阶——也就是钢琴键所代表的音阶——的 12 个音程中的部分或全部之中。

sentences.en: For centuries, observers have attributed this preference for certain combinations of tones to the mathematical properties of sound itself.
sentences.zh: 几百年来，观察者们把这种对某些音调组合的偏好归因于声音本身的数学性质。

sentences.en: Some 2,500 years ago, Pythagoras was the first to note a direct relationship between the harmoniousness of a tone combination and the physical dimensions of the object that produced it.
sentences.zh: 约 2500 年前，毕达哥拉斯首先注意到一组音调组合的和谐与产生这种声音的物体物理尺寸之间存在直接关系。

sentences.en: For example, a plucked string will always play an octave lower than a similar string half its size, and a fifth lower than a similar string two-thirds its length.
sentences.zh: 例如，一根被拨动的弦总比同类、尺寸为其一半的弦低一个八度，比同类、长度为其三分之二的弦低一个五度。

sentences.en: This link between simple ratios and harmony has influenced music theory ever since.
sentences.zh: 这种简单比率与和谐之间的联系，此后一直影响着音乐理论。

sentences.en: (C) This music-is-math idea is often accompanied by the notion that music, formally speaking at least, exists apart from the world in which it was created.
sentences.zh: “音乐即数学”的观念，常常伴随着这样的想法——音乐至少在形式上独立于它被创造出来的世界。

sentences.en: Writing recently in The New York Review of Books, pianist and critic Charles Rosen discussed the long-standing notion that while painting and sculpture reproduce at least some aspects of the natural world, and writing describes thoughts and feelings we are all familiar with, music is entirely abstracted from the world in which we live.
sentences.zh: 钢琴家兼评论家查尔斯·罗森（Charles Rosen）近期在《纽约书评》上撰文，谈到长期以来的观念：绘画和雕塑至少再现了自然世界的某些方面，写作描述我们都熟悉的思想和感受，而音乐则完全脱离我们所生活的世界。

sentences.en: Neither idea is right, according to David Schwartz and his colleagues.
sentences.zh: 戴维·施瓦茨及其同事认为，这两种说法都不对。

sentences.en: Human musical preferences are fundamentally shaped not by elegant algorithms or ratios but by the messy sounds of real life, and of speech in particular – which in turn is shaped by our evolutionary heritage.
sentences.zh: 人类对音乐的偏好从根本上不是由优雅的算法或比率塑造的，而是由真实生活的杂乱声音——尤其是言语的声音——塑造，而后者反过来又受我们进化遗产的塑造。

sentences.en: “The explanation of music, like the explanation of any product of the mind, must be rooted in biology, not in numbers per se,” says Schwartz.
sentences.zh: “对音乐的解释，正如对一切心智产物的解释，必须扎根于生物学，而非数字本身，”施瓦茨说。

sentences.en: Schwartz, Howe and Purves analysed a vast selection of speech sounds from a variety of languages to reveal the underlying patterns common to all utterances.
sentences.zh: 施瓦茨、豪和珀维斯分析了来自多种语言的大量言语声音，揭示了所有发声之下共通的潜在模式。

sentences.en: In order to focus only on the raw sounds, they discarded all theories about speech and meaning, and sliced sentences into random bites.
sentences.zh: 为了只聚焦于原始声音，他们抛弃了所有关于言语和意义的理论，把句子切成随机片段。

sentences.en: Using a database of over 100,000 brief segments of speech, they noted which frequency had the greatest emphasis in each sound.
sentences.zh: 利用一个包含超过 100000 段简短言语片段的数据库，他们记下每个声音中最强调的频率。

sentences.en: The resulting set of frequencies, they discovered, corresponded closely to the chromatic scale.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，由此得到的频率集与半音阶有密切对应。

sentences.en: In short, the building blocks of music are to be found in speech.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，音乐的构件可以在言语中找到。

sentences.en: Far from being abstract, music presents a strange analogue to the patterns created by the sounds of speech.
sentences.zh: 音乐远非抽象，它呈现出与言语之声所形成的模式奇异的类比。

sentences.en: “Music, like visual arts, is rooted in our experience of the natural world,” says Schwartz.
sentences.zh: “音乐，与视觉艺术一样，根植于我们对自然世界的体验，”施瓦茨说。

sentences.en: “It emulates our sound environment in the way that visual arts emulate the visual environment.”
sentences.zh: “它模仿我们的声音环境，正如视觉艺术模仿视觉环境。”

sentences.en: In music we hear the echo of our basic sound-making instrument — the vocal tract.
sentences.zh: 在音乐中，我们听到我们最基本发声乐器——声道——的回响。

sentences.en: The explanation for human music is simpler still than Pythagoras’s mathematical equations: we like the sounds that are familiar to us — specifically, we like the sounds that remind us of us.
sentences.zh: 对人类音乐的解释甚至比毕达哥拉斯的数学方程更简单：我们喜欢那些我们熟悉的声音——具体而言，我们喜欢那些让我们想起我们自己的声音。

sentences.en: This brings up some chicken-or-egg evolutionary questions.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了一些先有鸡还是先有蛋的进化问题。

sentences.en: It may be that music imitates speech directly, the researchers say, in which case it would seem that language evolved first.
sentences.zh: 研究者说，可能音乐直接模仿言语，那样看来语言先于音乐进化。

sentences.en: It’s also conceivable that music came first and language is in effect an imitation of song — that in everyday speech we hit the musical notes we especially like.
sentences.zh: 也可以想象音乐在先、语言实际上是对歌唱的模仿——即在日常言语中，我们击中那些自己特别喜欢的音调。

sentences.en: Alternatively, it may be that music imitates the general products of the human sound-making system, which just happens to be mostly speech.
sentences.zh: 或者也可能是：音乐模仿的是人类发声系统所产生的一般产物，而这些产物恰好大多是言语。

sentences.en: “We can’t know this,” says Schwartz.
sentences.zh: “我们无法知道这个，”施瓦茨说。

sentences.en: “What we do know is that they both come from the same system, and it is this that shapes our preferences.”
sentences.zh: “我们所知道的是：两者来自同一系统，正是这一系统塑造了我们的偏好。”

sentences.en: (D) Schwartz’s study also casts light on the long-running question of whether animals understand or appreciate music.
sentences.zh: 施瓦茨的研究也为长期争论的问题——动物是否理解或欣赏音乐——提供了启示。

sentences.en: Despite the apparent abundance of “music” in the natural world — birdsong, whale song, wolf howls, synchronised chimpanzee hooting — previous studies have found that many laboratory animals don’t show a great affinity for the human variety of music making.
sentences.zh: 尽管自然界中“音乐”似乎无处不在——鸟鸣、鲸歌、狼嗥、黑猩猩的同步呼叫——但以往研究发现，许多实验室动物并不太对人类那种音乐表现出特别的亲近感。

sentences.en: Marc Hauser and Josh McDermott of Harvard argued in the July issue of Nature Neuroscience that animals don’t create or perceive music the way we do.
sentences.zh: 哈佛的马克·豪泽（Marc Hauser）和乔什·麦克德莫特（Josh McDermott）在 7 月的《自然·神经科学》上撰文指出，动物并不像我们这样创造或感知音乐。

sentences.en: The fact that laboratory monkeys can show recognition of human tunes is evidence, they say, of shared general features of the auditory system, not any specific chimpanzee musical ability.
sentences.zh: 实验室猴子能够识别人类曲调，他们说，这是听觉系统共有一般特征的证据，而不是黑猩猩有任何特定音乐能力。

sentences.en: As for birds, those most musical beasts, they generally recognise their own tunes — a narrow repertoire — but don’t generate novel melodies like we do.
sentences.zh: 至于鸟——这些最具音乐性的动物——它们通常能识别自己的曲调（曲目狭窄），但不像我们那样生成新颖的旋律。

sentences.en: There are no avian Mozarts.
sentences.zh: 没有鸟界的莫扎特。

sentences.en: But what’s been played to animals, Schwartz notes, is human music.
sentences.zh: 但施瓦茨指出，给动物播放的都是人类音乐。

sentences.en: If animals evolve preferences for sound as we do — based upon the soundscape in which they live — then their “music” would be fundamentally different from ours.
sentences.zh: 如果动物像我们一样根据自己所处的声音景观演化出对声音的偏好，那么它们的“音乐”将与我们的从根本上不同。

sentences.en: In the same way our scales derive from human utterances, a cat’s idea of a good tune would derive from yowls and meows.
sentences.zh: 正如我们的音阶来自人类发声，猫所认为的好听旋律应来自嚎叫和喵声。

sentences.en: To demonstrate that animals don’t appreciate sound the way we do, we’d need evidence that they don’t respond to “music” constructed from their own sound environment.
sentences.zh: 要证明动物不像我们一样欣赏声音，我们需要证据：它们对从自身声音环境中构造出来的“音乐”也没有反应。

sentences.en: (E) No matter how the connection between language and music is parsed, what is apparent is that our sense of music, even our love for it, is as deeply rooted in our biology and in our brains as language is.
sentences.zh: 无论语言与音乐之间的联系如何拆解，明显的是：我们对音乐的感受——乃至我们对音乐的热爱——和语言一样深深扎根于我们的生物学和大脑之中。

sentences.en: This is most obvious with babies, says Sandra Trehub at the University of Toronto, who also published a paper in the Nature Neuroscience special issue.
sentences.zh: 在婴儿身上最为明显，多伦多大学的桑德拉·特雷胡布（Sandra Trehub）说。她也在《自然·神经科学》专题上发表了一篇论文。

sentences.en: For babies, music and speech are on a continuum.
sentences.zh: 对婴儿而言，音乐和言语处于一条连续谱上。

sentences.en: Mothers use musical speech to “regulate infants’ emotional states”, Trehub says.
sentences.zh: 特雷胡布说，母亲用音乐化的言语来“调节婴儿的情绪状态”。

sentences.en: Regardless of what language they speak, the voice all mothers use with babies is the same: “something between speech and song”.
sentences.zh: 无论她们讲什么语言，全世界母亲对婴儿用的声音都是一样的：“介乎言语和歌之间的东西”。

sentences.en: This kind of communication “puts the baby in a trance-like state, which may proceed to sleep or extended periods of rapture”.
sentences.zh: 这种交流“使婴儿进入一种近似入定的状态，可能进而入睡或长时间陶醉”。

sentences.en: So if the babies of the world could understand the latest research on language and music, they probably wouldn’t be very surprised.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果世界上的婴儿能够理解关于语言和音乐的最新研究，他们大概也不会太惊讶。

sentences.en: The upshot, says Trehub, is that music may be even more of a necessity than we realise.
sentences.zh: 特雷胡布说，结论是：音乐可能比我们意识到的更接近一种必需品。

1.stemZh: 这段文字的主要主题是什么？

sentences.en: (A) Group self-centredness seems to occur the minute people are divided into groups.
sentences.zh: 群体自我中心似乎一旦人们被分成群组就会出现。

sentences.en: It doesn’t matter what the group is, or on what basis it was formed, we perceive the group we belong to as being superior to other groups and we develop an ‘in-group’ bias.
sentences.zh: 无论群组是什么、或基于什么形成，我们都把自己所属的群组视为优于其他群组，并发展出一种“内群体”偏向。

sentences.en: (B) Probably one of the most famous pieces of research looking at group behaviour was a field study conducted by Sherif in 1956.
sentences.zh: 也许最著名的研究群体行为的工作之一，是谢里夫在1956年进行的一项实地研究。

sentences.en: This study involved 22 boys aged between 11 and 12, who were divided into two groups.
sentences.zh: 这项研究涉及22个11到12岁的男孩，他们被分成两组。

sentences.en: The groups were roughly matched in terms of sporting ability, camping experience and general popularity among their peers.
sentences.zh: 这两组在运动能力、露营经验和在同龄人中的总体受欢迎程度方面大致匹配。

sentences.en: Their parents were told that they were going to a three-week summer camp to see how well they would work alongside other boys when put into different teams.
sentences.zh: 他们的父母被告知，孩子们将去参加一个为期三周的夏令营，以观察当被分到不同队伍时他们与其他男孩协作得如何。

sentences.en: The parents were also told that the boys would not be allowed to be visited during that time, but would be able to go home if they wanted to.
sentences.zh: 父母还被告知，在那段时间里孩子们不被允许探视，但如果他们想回家就可以回家。

sentences.en: It was intended that the data for the study would be collected by participant observers.
sentences.zh: 研究的数据原计划由参与式观察者来收集。

sentences.en: (C) At first, neither set of boys knew of the existence of the other set.
sentences.zh: 起初，两组男孩谁都不知道另一组的存在。

sentences.en: They were taken to their respective campsites, which were located on a 200-acre, densely wooded area in Robbers Cave State Park, Oklahoma.
sentences.zh: 他们被带到各自的营地，营地位于俄克拉荷马州罗伯斯洞穴州立公园一片200英亩、林木茂密的区域。

sentences.en: The first week was spent doing a variety of activities, such as pitching tents and cooking.
sentences.zh: 第一周用来做各种各样的活动，比如搭帐篷和做饭。

sentences.en: During this week, the two groups seemed to develop different group norms, one group being more ‘tough’ than the other, from which two boys went home early, as they were homesick.
sentences.zh: 在这一周里，两组似乎发展出不同的群体规范，一组比另一组更“强悍”，从较温和的那组有两个男孩因为想家而提前回了家。

sentences.en: The groups were given a set of caps and T-shirts, and gave themselves names: the ‘Eagles’ and the ‘Rattlers’ (the latter being the tougher group).
sentences.zh: 两组各得到一套帽子和T恤，并给自己起了名字：“鹰队”和“响尾蛇队”（后者是更强悍的那组）。

sentences.en: (D) At the end of the first week, they became aware of each other’s existence by finding litter left by the other group or overhearing voices.
sentences.zh: 第一周结束时，他们通过发现另一组留下的垃圾、或无意中听到说话声，意识到了彼此的存在。

sentences.en: Sherif noticed that already the groups had started to refer to the other group as ‘them’ and their group as ‘us’.
sentences.zh: 谢里夫注意到，两组已经开始把另一组称为“他们”、把自己组称为“我们”。

sentences.en: This marked the beginning of phase two of the experiment.
sentences.zh: 这标志着实验第二阶段的开始。

sentences.en: (E) The groups were told that they were going to take part in a ‘Grand Tournament’, which involved ten different sporting events, and they were shown the prizes for winning.
sentences.zh: 两组被告知，他们将参加一场“大锦标赛”，包括十项不同的体育项目，而他们被展示了获胜的奖品。

sentences.en: The tournament was also to include in the final scores points which would be awarded for other activities, such as how tidy the cabins were kept.
sentences.zh: 锦标赛的最终得分还将包括为其他活动、比如小屋保持得有多整洁所颁发的分数。

sentences.en: These scores were displayed on big scoreboards in what now became a joint hall where the two groups ate their meals together.
sentences.zh: 这些分数被显示在大记分牌上，记分牌如今设在一个共用大厅里，两组在那里一起吃饭。

sentences.en: This was necessary so the two groups would think they were on almost equal scores in the time leading up to the final event, which would increase the sense of competition.
sentences.zh: 这样做是必要的，好让两组在通往最终项目的时段里以为他们分数几乎相当，这会增强竞争感。

sentences.en: Needless to say, these scores were manipulated by the experimenters.
sentences.zh: 不用说，这些分数是被实验者操纵的。

sentences.en: (F) In order to check how high the levels of group self-centredness were in the groups at this time, a number of tasks were set up which involved the groups rating their own members and members of the other group.
sentences.zh: 为了检查此时两组群体自我中心的程度有多高，设置了若干任务，让两组给自己组的成员和另一组的成员评分。

sentences.en: Each time, group members rated the boys in their own group much better at the tasks than the other boys, even though there was no real difference between them.
sentences.zh: 每一次，组员都把自己组里的男孩在任务上评得比另一组的男孩好得多，尽管他们之间并没有真正的差别。

sentences.en: They were also asked to rate all others in terms of how desirable they were as friends, and 93 per cent of friendship preferences were in-group preferences.
sentences.zh: 他们还被要求就所有其他人作为朋友的可取程度来评分，而百分之九十三的交友偏好都是内群体偏好。

sentences.en: (G) When the tournament started, the first game was basketball.
sentences.zh: 锦标赛开始时，第一场比赛是篮球。

sentences.en: The group that was thought to be less tough lost the game and claimed that they had lost only because the other group were bigger and older than they were.
sentences.zh: 被认为不那么强悍的那组输了比赛，并声称他们之所以输只是因为另一组比他们更高大、年纪更大。

sentences.en: The Eagles won the next ball game and then were said to be cheating in the tug-of-war.
sentences.zh: 鹰队赢了下一场球赛，然后被说在拔河中作弊。

sentences.en: This resulted in visits by both groups to each other’s cabins over the course of the next 24 hours, where they ripped the mosquito nets, turned over the beds and generally made a mess.
sentences.zh: 这导致两组在接下来24小时内互相到对方的小屋去，在那里他们撕破蚊帐、掀翻床铺、总体上弄得一团糟。

sentences.en: The Eagles devised a new weapon in the conflict which consisted of ‘rocks in socks’ – and so it went on.
sentences.zh: 鹰队在冲突中想出了一种新武器，由“装在袜子里的石头”组成——事情就这样继续下去。

sentences.en: Eventually, the Eagles won the tournament (with some help from the experimenters) and it was time for phase three to begin.
sentences.zh: 最终，鹰队赢得了锦标赛（在实验者的一些帮助下），而第三阶段开始的时候到了。

sentences.en: (H) Research has suggested that the best way to reduce group conflict is by non-competitive contact.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，减少群体冲突的最佳办法是非竞争性的接触。

sentences.en: This required two conditions: that the groups had equal status and that they had a common goal to work towards.
sentences.zh: 这需要两个条件：两组地位平等、且有一个共同的目标去努力实现。

sentences.en: This was exactly what Sherif engineered.
sentences.zh: 这正是谢里夫所设计的。

sentences.en: There were actually seven situations organised which gave the groups equal-status contact; these were things like having meals together or watching films together.
sentences.zh: 实际上组织了七种情境，给两组提供地位平等的接触；这些是诸如一起吃饭或一起看电影之类的事。

sentences.en: The meals resulted in food fights; the films were enjoyed by both groups sitting totally apart from each other.
sentences.zh: 吃饭导致了食物大战；看电影时两组完全分开坐着看得很尽兴。

sentences.en: (I) The other situations, where the groups had to work for common goals, had a much better outcome.
sentences.zh: 而那些两组必须为共同目标努力的情境，结果要好得多。

sentences.en: These included raising money to go and see a film and solving problems, such as one with the water supply.
sentences.zh: 这些包括筹钱去看一场电影、以及解决问题，比如一个有关供水的问题。

sentences.en: The final common goal was a visit by truck to Cedar Lake to camp there before the end of the holiday.
sentences.zh: 最后的共同目标是乘卡车去雪松湖，在假期结束前到那里露营。

sentences.en: In this situation, although both groups travelled in separate trucks, another problem-solving situation arose when one of the trucks became stuck.
sentences.zh: 在这种情境中，尽管两组乘坐分开的卡车，但当其中一辆卡车陷住时，又出现了另一个需要解决问题的情境。

sentences.en: All the boys joined in, using one of the tug-of-war ropes to help move it.
sentences.zh: 所有男孩都加入进来，用一根拔河绳来帮忙把它移动。

sentences.en: At this point the group boundaries were beginning to disappear.
sentences.zh: 在这一刻，群体的界限开始消失了。

sentences.en: On the final day, when they were due to return home, the boys themselves suggested that they travel in one bus and sat in friendship groups rather than as Eagles and Rattlers.
sentences.zh: 在最后一天，当他们该回家时，男孩们自己提议乘坐一辆巴士，并按照交友群组、而不是按鹰队和响尾蛇队来坐。

sentences.en: A Biophilic design, a movement related to green architecture, has gained much momentum within the building community in recent years.
sentences.zh: 亲生命设计，一场与绿色建筑相关的运动，近年来在建筑界获得了很大的势头。

sentences.en: The premise of biophilic design is to avoid or minimise harmful impacts on the natural environment and, equally importantly, to provide and restore beneficial contacts between people and nature in the built environment.
sentences.zh: 亲生命设计的前提是避免或尽量减少对自然环境的有害影响，同样重要的是，在建成环境中提供并恢复人与自然之间有益的接触。

sentences.en: B People have a psychologically developed need to commune with nature, but this has frequently been neglected.
sentences.zh: 人在心理上有一种与自然交流的、发展出来的需求，但这常常被忽视。

sentences.en: All too often, architects put creative originality before the needs of the people who must live and work in their futuristic constructions, with scant regard for emotional as well as practical considerations.
sentences.zh: 建筑师往往把创意上的独创性置于那些必须在他们未来主义建筑里生活和工作的人的需求之上，几乎不顾及情感上的以及实际上的考量。

sentences.en: Biophilic design does not advocate tree houses or cave-dwelling, but it does provide nature-based features that maximise human functioning and health.
sentences.zh: 亲生命设计并不提倡树屋或穴居，但它确实提供以自然为基础的特征，以最大化人的机能和健康。

sentences.en: Though not technically a biophilic design, Fallingwater—the stunning house in rural Pennsylvania designed in the 1930s by Frank Lloyd Wright—arguably speaks to the human soul far more than the box-like blocks of flats designed by his contemporary Le Corbusier.
sentences.zh: 虽然严格来说不算亲生命设计，但流水别墅——20世纪30年代由Frank Lloyd Wright设计、位于宾夕法尼亚乡间的那座惊艳房子——可以说远比他同时代的Le Corbusier设计的盒子状公寓楼更能触动人的灵魂。

sentences.en: C In the modern world, much of our built environment obstructs the age-old connection between humans and nature.
sentences.zh: 在现代世界，我们建成环境的很大一部分阻碍了人与自然之间古老的联系。

sentences.en: The rate of technological progress far exceeds the rate of psychological evolution, leaving us ill-equipped to cope with our lifestyles, which in turn leads to increased stress.
sentences.zh: 技术进步的速度远远超过心理演化的速度，使我们没有足够的能力应对自己的生活方式，这反过来又导致压力增加。

sentences.en: Because biophilia attempts to integrate basic and current needs, it can alleviate the difficulties caused by the brain’s constant efforts to function in a modern environment it has not yet evolved to handle.
sentences.zh: 由于亲生命试图整合基本的和当下的需求，它能缓解由大脑不断努力在一个它尚未进化到能处理的现代环境中运转所造成的困难。

sentences.en: For example, one crucial element of the natural landscape for human health is sunlight.
sentences.zh: 比如，对人类健康而言，自然景观的一个关键要素是阳光。

sentences.en: We are evolutionarily programmed to respond positively to sunny areas over dark or overcast ones and sense that they will foster restoration, improve emotional well-being and promote health.
sentences.zh: 我们在演化上被设定为对阳光充足的区域比对昏暗或阴沉的区域作出更积极的反应，并感觉到它们会促进恢复、改善情绪健康、增进健康。

sentences.en: D Because of its tremendous impact on human psychology, biophilic design plays a vital role in healthcare and its delivery.
sentences.zh: 由于对人类心理有巨大的影响，亲生命设计在医疗保健及其提供方面发挥着至关重要的作用。

sentences.en: The current healthcare system contains many flaws, especially in its physical spaces.
sentences.zh: 当前的医疗体系存在许多缺陷，尤其是在其物理空间方面。

sentences.en: Hospitals, clinics and offices are high-stress environments for patients, visitors and healthcare professionals alike.
sentences.zh: 医院、诊所和办公室对病人、访客和医护专业人员来说都是高压力的环境。

sentences.en: One well-known study looked at the impact of nature on patients after surgery.
sentences.zh: 一项著名的研究考察了自然对术后病人的影响。

sentences.en: One group had a view of a tree; the others had a window looking onto a brick wall.
sentences.zh: 一组病人能看到一棵树；另一些病人的窗户朝向一堵砖墙。

sentences.en: The first group had shorter hospital stays, received fewer negative comments from nurses, required fewer analgesics and had slightly fewer post-operative complications.
sentences.zh: 第一组住院时间更短、收到护士的负面评价更少、需要的止痛药更少，术后并发症也略少。

sentences.en: E As a consequence of this and other studies, nature and nature-based design have been integrated into the physical design of many hospitals.
sentences.zh: 作为这项及其他研究的结果，自然以及以自然为基础的设计已被纳入许多医院的物理设计中。

sentences.en: For example, Dartmouth Hitchcock Medical Center (DHMC) in New Hampshire boasts an atrium design illuminating the entire facility.
sentences.zh: 比如，新罕布什尔州的Dartmouth Hitchcock医疗中心（DHMC）有一个照亮整个设施的中庭设计。

sentences.en: Natural elements also permeate the building, including wood, stone and numerous live plants.
sentences.zh: 自然元素也渗透到这栋建筑里，包括木材、石头和众多活的植物。

sentences.en: While DHMC was built to incorporate these qualities, other hospitals have had biophilic features added to existing structures.
sentences.zh: 虽然DHMC在建造时就融入了这些特质，但其他医院则是在现有结构上加入了亲生命特征。

sentences.en: The application of biophilic concepts to hospital interiors has increased substantially as administrators have witnessed patients’ positive responses to nature.
sentences.zh: 随着管理者目睹病人对自然的积极反应，把亲生命理念应用于医院室内的做法已大幅增加。

sentences.en: F Many existing buildings contain biophilic elements, but only a few have been built with the specific idea of biophilic design in mind.
sentences.zh: 许多现有建筑都含有亲生命元素，但只有少数是带着亲生命设计这个具体理念建造的。

sentences.en: One such building is the Adam Joseph Lewis Center for Environmental Studies at Oberlin College in Ohio.
sentences.zh: 其中一栋建筑是俄亥俄州欧柏林学院的Adam Joseph Lewis环境研究中心。

sentences.en: The director of Oberlin’s Environmental Studies Program, David Orr, explained that the building’s goals were “to create not just a place for classes but rather a building that would help to redefine the relationship between humankind and the environment—one that would expand our sense of ecological possibilities”.
sentences.zh: 欧柏林环境研究项目的主任David Orr解释说，这栋建筑的目标是“不只是创造一个上课的地方，而是一栋有助于重新定义人类与环境关系的建筑——一栋能拓展我们对生态可能性之感知的建筑”。

sentences.en: The Lewis Center is sustainable in a broader sense than in the typical application of the word.
sentences.zh: Lewis中心在比这个词的典型用法更广的意义上是可持续的。

sentences.en: It harnesses solar power, utilises both active and passive air systems, and monitors the weather to adapt to conditions.
sentences.zh: 它利用太阳能，采用主动和被动两种空气系统，并监测天气以适应各种条件。

sentences.en: The Centre’s “Living Machine” treats wastewater by combining traditional wastewater technology with wetland ecosystems’ purification processes, producing water that can be used in the toilets and for irrigation.
sentences.zh: 该中心的“生命机器”把传统污水技术与湿地生态系统的净化过程结合起来处理废水，产出可用于冲厕和灌溉的水。

sentences.en: In their design, Orr and his team of architects engineered a healthy and comfortable space for students while ensuring the surrounding environment was undamaged.
sentences.zh: 在他们的设计中，Orr和他的建筑师团队为学生打造了一个健康舒适的空间，同时确保周围环境不受损害。

sentences.en: G Another example is the University of Guelph-Humber building in Ontario, Canada.
sentences.zh: 另一个例子是加拿大安大略省的Guelph-Humber大学大楼。

sentences.en: It contains a centrally located bio-wall, vertically spanning the building.
sentences.zh: 它有一面位于中央的生物墙，竖直贯穿整栋建筑。

sentences.en: The wall is covered in dense foliage which not only connects people to nature on the inside of the building, but also functions as a new filtration-system prototype.
sentences.zh: 这面墙覆盖着茂密的枝叶，不仅在建筑内部把人与自然连接起来，还充当一种新的过滤系统原型。

sentences.en: The wall purifies the air and has the potential to fulfil the building’s fresh-air-intake requirements.
sentences.zh: 这面墙净化空气，有可能满足这栋建筑的新风摄入需求。

sentences.en: These examples prove that the built environment need not interfere with biological human needs to commune with nature, nor with existing ecological systems.
sentences.zh: 这些例子证明，建成环境无需妨碍人类与自然交流的生物需求，也无需妨碍现有的生态系统。

sentences.en: H Ancient architects built for their cultures, which were almost always more in touch with the earth than Western society is today.
sentences.zh: 古代的建筑师为他们的文化而建造，那些文化几乎总是比今天的西方社会更贴近大地。

sentences.en: They mimicked nature’s forms, producing magnificent structures that still awe us—though biophilic design is a novel concept, they certainly employed some of its recommendations.
sentences.zh: 他们模仿自然的形式，造出至今仍令我们敬畏的宏伟结构——虽然亲生命设计是个新颖的概念，但他们确实运用了它的一些主张。

sentences.en: Today we can add another layer to this tradition and ensure maximal benefit for our planet and ourselves.
sentences.zh: 今天我们可以为这一传统再添一层，确保为我们的星球和我们自己带来最大的益处。
