24.stemZh: 作者对奥伯林学院亚当·约瑟夫·刘易斯中心的以下哪两项陈述是正确的？

sentences.en: (A) At the beginning of the 20th century, grocery stores in the United States were full-service.
sentences.zh: 在 20 世纪初，美国的杂货店都是全方位服务式的。

sentences.en: A customer would ask a clerk behind the counter for specific items and the clerk would package the items, which were limited to dry goods.
sentences.zh: 顾客会向柜台后的店员说出所需的具体商品，然后店员将商品包装好，且商品种类仅限于干货。

sentences.en: If they want to save some time, they have to ask a delivery boy or themselves to send the note of what they want to buy to the grocery store first and then go to pay for the goods later.
sentences.zh: 如果想省点时间，他们必须先让送货小弟或自己把要买东西的清单送到杂货店，事后再去付款。

sentences.en: These grocery stores usually carried only one brand of each good.
sentences.zh: 这些杂货店通常每种商品只售一个品牌。

sentences.en: There were early chain stores, such as the A&P Stores, but these were all entirely full-service and very time-consuming.
sentences.zh: 当时也有早期的连锁店，例如 A&P 连锁店，但都是全方位服务式且非常耗时。

sentences.en: (B) In 1885, a Virginia boy named Clarence Saunders began working part-time as a clerk in a grocery store when he was 14 years old, and quit school when the shopkeeper offered him full-time work with room and board.
sentences.zh: 1885 年，一位名叫克拉伦斯·桑德斯（Clarence Saunders）的弗吉尼亚男孩在 14 岁时开始在一家杂货店做兼职店员，后来店主提出提供食宿的全职工作时，他便从学校辍学。

sentences.en: Later he worked in an Alabama coke plant and in a Tennessee sawmill before he returned to the grocery business.
sentences.zh: 之后他在阿拉巴马州一家炼焦厂和田纳西州一家锯木厂做过工，然后才回到杂货行业。

sentences.en: By 1900, when he was nineteen years old, he was earning $30 a month as a salesman for a wholesale grocer.
sentences.zh: 到 1900 年他 19 岁时，他作为一家批发杂货商的销售员，每月可挣 30 美元。

sentences.en: During his years working in grocery stores, he found that it was very inconvenient and inefficient for people to buy things because more than a century ago, long before there were computers, shopping was done quite differently than it is today.
sentences.zh: 在杂货店工作的这些年里，他发现人们买东西非常不方便、效率也低；因为在一个多世纪以前——远在有计算机之前——购物的方式与今天大不相同。

sentences.en: Entering a store, the customer would approach the counter (or wait for a clerk to become available) and place an order, either verbally or, as was often the case for boys running errands, in the form of a note or list.
sentences.zh: 顾客进店后会走到柜台前（或等待一名店员有空），然后口头下单——或者像跑腿小孩常做的那样——以便条或清单形式下单。

sentences.en: While the customer waited, the clerk would move behind the counter and throughout the store, select the items on the list – some form shelves so high that a long-handled grasping device had to be used – and bring them back to the counter to be tallied and bagged or boxed.
sentences.zh: 在顾客等候时，店员会绕到柜台后并在店里到处走动，挑出清单上的商品——其中一些放在高得需要长柄抓取工具才能拿到的货架上——再把它们拿回柜台清点装袋或装盒。

sentences.en: The process might be expedited by the customer calling or sending in the order beforehand, or by the order being handled by a delivery boy on a bike, but otherwise, it did not vary greatly.
sentences.zh: 这个过程可以通过顾客提前打电话或派人送来订单、或由送货小弟骑自行车送单来加快，但其他方面变化不大。

sentences.en: Saunders, a flamboyant and innovative man, noticed that this method resulted in wasted time and expense, so he came up with an unheard-of solution that would revolutionize the entire grocery industry: he developed a way for shoppers to serve themselves.
sentences.zh: 桑德斯是个张扬而善于创新的人，他注意到这种方式既浪费时间又增加开支，于是想出一个闻所未闻、足以彻底改变整个杂货业的解决办法：他设计出一种让购物者自己取货的方式。

sentences.en: (C) So in 1902, he moved to Memphis where he developed his concept to form a grocery wholesale cooperative and a full-service grocery store.
sentences.zh: 于是在 1902 年，他迁居孟菲斯，在那里发展自己的构想，组建了一家杂货批发合作社和一家全方位服务式杂货店。

sentences.en: For his new “cafeteria grocery”, Saunders divided his grocery into three distinct areas: 1) A front “lobby” forming an entrance and exit and checkouts at the front.
sentences.zh: 为了他的新式“自助餐厅式杂货店”，桑德斯把店面划分为三块截然不同的区域：1）位于店前的“门厅”，包含入口、出口和收银台。

sentences.en: 2) A sales department, which was specially designed to allow customers to roam the aisles and select their own groceries.
sentences.zh: 2）销售区，专门设计成允许顾客在过道间漫步并自己挑选商品。

sentences.en: Removing unnecessary clerks, creating elaborate aisle displays, and rearranging the store to force customers to view all of the merchandise and over the shelving and cabinets units of sales department were “galleries” where supervisors were allowed to keep an eye on the customers while not disturbing them.
sentences.zh: 店里去掉不必要的店员，做出精心布置的过道陈列，并重新安排布局以迫使顾客浏览所有商品；在销售区的货架和柜架之上还设有“楼座”——那是允许监督人员在不打扰顾客的同时观察顾客的位置。

sentences.en: 3) And another section of his store is the room only allowed for the clerks which were called the “stockroom” or “storage room” where large refrigerators were situated to keep fresh products from being perishable.
sentences.zh: 3）店里另一区域是只允许店员进入的房间，被称为“库房”或“储藏室”，里面摆放着大型冷藏柜以避免新鲜食品变质。

sentences.en: The new format allowed multiple customers to shop at the same time and led to the previously unknown phenomenon of impulse shopping.
sentences.zh: 这种新格局允许多名顾客同时购物，并催生了此前不为人知的现象——冲动消费。

sentences.en: Though this format of grocery market was drastically different from its competitors, the style became the standard for the modern grocery store and later supermarket.
sentences.zh: 尽管这种杂货市场格局与当时的竞争对手截然不同，但这种风格后来成为现代杂货店乃至超市的标准。

sentences.en: (D) On September 6, 1916, Saunders launched the self-service revolution in the USA by opening the first self-service Piggly Wiggly store, at 79 Jefferson Street in Memphis, Tennessee, with its characteristic turnstile at the entrance.
sentences.zh: 1916 年 9 月 6 日，桑德斯在田纳西州孟菲斯杰斐逊街 79 号开设了第一家自助式 Piggly Wiggly 门店，门口装有标志性的旋转闸门，由此在美国掀起了自助服务革命。

sentences.en: Customers paid cash and selected their own goods from the shelves.
sentences.zh: 顾客付现金，并自己从货架上挑选商品。

sentences.en: It was unlike any other grocery store of that time.
sentences.zh: 它与当时任何其他杂货店都不一样。

sentences.en: Inside a Piggly Wiggly, shoppers were not at the mercy of shop clerks.
sentences.zh: 在 Piggly Wiggly 店里，购物者不再受店员的摆布。

sentences.en: They were free to roam the store, check out the merchandise and get what they needed with their own two hands and feet.
sentences.zh: 他们可以在店里自由地逛、查看商品、用自己的双手和双脚拿到所需要的东西。

sentences.en: Prices on items at Piggly Wiggly were clearly marked.
sentences.zh: Piggly Wiggly 店里每件商品的价格都明确标示。

sentences.en: No one pressured customers to buy milk or pickles.
sentences.zh: 没人会强迫顾客购买牛奶或腌菜。

sentences.en: And the biggest benefit at the Piggly Wiggly was that shoppers saved money.
sentences.zh: 而在 Piggly Wiggly 购物最大的好处，就是消费者能省钱。

sentences.en: Self-service was positive all around.
sentences.zh: 自助服务对各方都有好处。

sentences.en: “It’s good for both the consumer and retailer because it cuts costs,” noted George T.
sentences.zh: 乔治·T.

sentences.en: Haley, a professor at the University of New Haven and director of the Center for International Industry Competitiveness.
sentences.zh: 哈雷（George T. Haley）是纽黑文大学的教授，也是国际产业竞争力研究中心主任，他指出：“这对消费者和零售商都有好处，因为它降低了成本。”

sentences.en: “If you looked at the way grocery stores were run previous to Piggly Wiggly and Alpha Beta, what you find is that there was a tremendous amount of labor involved, and labor is a major expense.”
sentences.zh: “如果回头看 Piggly Wiggly 和 Alpha Beta 之前杂货店的经营方式，你会发现其中涉及大量人工，而人工是一大开支。”

sentences.en: Piggly Wiggly cut the fat.
sentences.zh: Piggly Wiggly 把这块“赘肉”切掉了。

sentences.en: (E) Piggly Wiggly and the self-service concept took off.
sentences.zh: Piggly Wiggly 和自助服务的理念迅速腾飞。

sentences.en: Saunders opened nine stores in the Memphis area within the first year of business.
sentences.zh: 开业第一年内，桑德斯就在孟菲斯地区开了九家门店。

sentences.en: Consumers embraced the efficiency, the simplicity and most of all the lower food prices.
sentences.zh: 消费者拥抱了这种效率、简单——更重要的是，更低的食品价格。

sentences.en: Saunders soon patented his self-service concept and began franchising Piggly Wiggly stores.
sentences.zh: 桑德斯很快为他的自助服务理念申请了专利，并开始把 Piggly Wiggly 门店做成连锁特许经营。

sentences.en: Thanks to the benefits of self-service and franchising, Piggly Wiggly ballooned to nearly 1,300 stores by 1923.
sentences.zh: 得益于自助服务和特许加盟的优势，到 1923 年 Piggly Wiggly 已扩张到近 1300 家门店。

sentences.en: Piggly Wiggly sold $100 million – worth $1.3 billion today – in groceries, making it the third-biggest grocery retailer in the nation.
sentences.zh: Piggly Wiggly 当时卖出了价值 1 亿美元的杂货——相当于今天的 13 亿美元——成为全美第三大杂货零售商。

sentences.en: The company’s stock was even listed on the New York Stock Exchange, doubling from late 1922 to march 1923.
sentences.zh: 公司的股票甚至在纽约证券交易所挂牌，从 1922 年末到 1923 年 3 月翻了一番。

sentences.en: Saunders had his hands all over Piggly Wiggly.
sentences.zh: 桑德斯把 Piggly Wiggly 的方方面面都牢牢抓在手里。

sentences.en: He was instrumental in the design and layout of his stores.
sentences.zh: 他在门店的设计和布局中起了关键作用。

sentences.en: He even invented the turnstile.
sentences.zh: 他甚至发明了门口的旋转闸门。

sentences.en: (F) However, Saunders was forced into bankruptcy in 1923 after a dramatic spat which the New York Stock Exchange and he went on to create the “Clarence Saunders sole-owner-of-my-name” chain, which went into bankruptcy.
sentences.zh: 然而，1923 年桑德斯在与纽约证券交易所发生戏剧性争执后被迫破产，他随后又创办了名为“Clarence Saunders sole-owner-of-my-name”的连锁店，但也以破产收场。

sentences.en: (G) Until the time of his death in October 1953, Saunders was developing plans for another automatic store system called the Foodelectric.
sentences.zh: 直到 1953 年 10 月他去世前，桑德斯一直在为一个名为 Foodelectric 的全自动门店系统拟定方案。

sentences.en: But the store, which was to be located two blocks from the first Piggly Wiggly store, never opened.
sentences.zh: 但这家本应位于第一家 Piggly Wiggly 店两个街区开外的门店，最终从未开业。

sentences.en: But his name was well-remembered along with the name Piggly Wiggly.
sentences.zh: 但他的名字与 Piggly Wiggly 一道，一直被人们清晰地记住。

sentences.en: A These days the feet of a typical city dweller rarely encounter terrain any more uneven than a crack in the pavement.
sentences.zh: 如今，典型城市居民的双脚很少接触到比人行道上的裂缝更不平整的地面。

sentences.en: While that may not seem like a problem, it turns out that by flattening our urban environment we have put ourselves at risk of a surprising number of chronic illnesses and disabilities.
sentences.zh: 这看起来或许并不像问题，但事实证明，通过把我们的城市环境压平，我们让自己面临数量惊人的多种慢性疾病和功能障碍的风险。

sentences.en: Fortunately, the commercial market has come to the rescue with a choice of products.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，商业市场已经带着一系列产品前来救场。

sentences.en: Research into the idea that flat floors could be detrimental to our health was pioneered back in the late 1960s in Long Beach, California.
sentences.zh: 早在 1960 年代末，加州长滩就开创了“平整地面可能有害健康”这一观念的研究。

sentences.en: Podiatrist Charles Brantingham and physiologist Bruce Beekman were concerned with the growing epidemic of high blood pressure, varicose veins and deep-vein thromboses and reckoned they might be linked to the uniformity of the surfaces that we tend to stand and walk on.
sentences.zh: 足科医生查尔斯·布兰廷厄姆（Charles Brantingham）和生理学家布鲁斯·比克曼（Bruce Beekman）担忧高血压、静脉曲张和深静脉血栓的流行越来越广，他们认为这可能与我们倾向于站立和行走其上的地面均一性有关。

sentences.en: B The trouble, they believed, was that walking continuously on flat floors, sidewalks and streets concentrates forces on just a few areas of the foot.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，问题在于持续在平整地面、人行道和街道上行走，会把作用力集中在脚的少数几个区域。

sentences.en: As a result, these surfaces are likely to be far more conducive to chronic stress syndromes than natural surfaces, where the foot meets the ground in a wide variety of orientations.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些地面比起自然地面，更容易引发慢性应力综合征——在自然地面上，脚以多种角度接触地面。

sentences.en: They understood that the anatomy of the foot parallels that of the human hand - each having 26 bones, 33 joints and more than 100 muscles, tendons and ligaments - and that modern lifestyles waste all this potential flexibility.
sentences.zh: 他们了解到，人足的解剖结构与人手相似——每只都有 26 块骨、33 个关节，以及超过 100 条肌肉、肌腱和韧带——而现代生活方式浪费了这些潜在的灵活性。

sentences.en: C Brantingham and Beekman became convinced that the damage could be rectified by making people wobble.
sentences.zh: 布兰廷厄姆和比克曼确信，可以通过让人们晃动来纠正这些损伤。

sentences.en: To test their ideas, they got 65 factory workers to try standing on a variable terrain floor - spongy mats with varying degrees of resistance across the surface.
sentences.zh: 为检验他们的想法，他们让 65 名工厂工人尝试站在一种“地形多变”的地板上——即在表面各处具有不同阻力的海绵垫上。

sentences.en: This modest irregularity allowed the soles of the volunteers’ feet to deviate slightly from the horizontal each time they shifted position.
sentences.zh: 这种适度的不平整，让志愿者的脚底每次变换姿势时都能稍微偏离水平面。

sentences.en: As the researchers hoped, this simple intervention made a huge difference, within a few weeks.
sentences.zh: 正如研究者所希望的那样，这个简单的干预在几周之内就带来了巨大的差别。

sentences.en: Even if people were wobbling slightly, it activated a host of muscles in their legs, which in turn helped pump blood back to their hearts.
sentences.zh: 即便人们只是轻微地晃动，腿部的一大批肌肉也被激活，进而帮助把血液泵回心脏。

sentences.en: The muscle action prevented the pooling of blood in their feet and legs, reducing the stress on the heart and circulation.
sentences.zh: 肌肉的运动阻止了血液在脚和腿中淤积，减轻了心脏和循环系统的压力。

sentences.en: Yet decades later, the flooring of the world's largest workplaces remains relentlessly smooth.
sentences.zh: 然而几十年过去了，世界上最大型工作场所的地板仍然顽固地平滑。

sentences.en: Earlier this year, however, the idea was revived when other researchers in the US announced findings from a similar experiment with people over 60.
sentences.zh: 不过今年早些时候，当美国其他研究者宣布对 60 岁以上人群进行的一项类似实验的结果时，这一想法被重新唤起。

sentences.en: John Fisher and colleagues at the Oregon Research Institute in Eugene designed a mat intended to replicate the effect of walking on cobblestones*.
sentences.zh: 位于尤金市俄勒冈研究所的约翰·费希尔（John Fisher）及其同事设计了一种垫子，旨在复现走在鹅卵石上的效果。

sentences.en: D In tests funded by the National Institute of Aging, they got some 50 adults to walk on the mats in their bare feet for less than an hour, three times a week.
sentences.zh: 在由美国国家衰老研究所资助的试验中，他们让约 50 名成年人每周三次、每次不到 1 小时赤脚在垫子上走。

sentences.en: After 16 weeks, these people showed marked improvements in mobility, and even a significant reduction in blood pressure.
sentences.zh: 16 周后，这些人的活动能力显著改善，甚至血压也明显下降。

sentences.en: People in a control group who walked on ordinary floors also improved but not as dramatically.
sentences.zh: 在普通地面上行走的对照组的人也有所改善，但程度不及他们。

sentences.en: The mats are now available for purchase and production is being scaled up.
sentences.zh: 这些垫子现已上市，产量正在扩大。

sentences.en: Even so, demand could exceed supply if this foot-stimulating activity really is a ‘useful nonpharmacological approach for preventing or controlling hypertension of older adults, as the researchers believe.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，如果这种刺激脚部的活动真的是“预防或控制老年人高血压的有效非药物方法”（如研究者所相信的），需求可能会超过供给。

sentences.en: They are not alone in recognising the benefits of cobblestones.
sentences.zh: 认识到鹅卵石益处的并不只有他们。

sentences.en: Reflexologists have long advocated walking on textured surfaces to stimulate so-called ‘acupoints’ on the soles of the feet.
sentences.zh: 反射疗法师长期以来一直主张走在有质地的表面上，以刺激所谓的脚底“穴位”。

sentences.en: They believe that pressure applied to particular spots on the foot connects directly to particular organs of the body and somehow enhances their function.
sentences.zh: 他们相信，施加在脚上特定穴位的压力会直接连通身体特定的器官，并以某种方式增强其功能。

sentences.en: In China, spas, apartment blocks and even factories promote their cobblestone paths as healthful amenities.
sentences.zh: 在中国，温泉、住宅楼甚至工厂都把它们的鹅卵石小径作为有益健康的设施推广。

sentences.en: Fisher admits he got the concept from regular visits to the country.
sentences.zh: 费希尔承认，他是从经常造访中国得到这个想法的。

sentences.en: Here, city dwellers take daily walks along cobbled paths for five or ten minutes, perhaps several times a day, to improve their health.
sentences.zh: 在这里，城市居民每天沿着鹅卵石路走五到十分钟，可能一天数次，以改善健康。

sentences.en: The idea is now taking off in Europe too.
sentences.zh: 现在这一想法在欧洲也正在兴起。

sentences.en: E People in Germany, Austria and Switzerland can now visit ‘barefoot parks’ and walk along ‘paths of the senses - with mud, logs, stone and moss underfoot.
sentences.zh: 德国、奥地利和瑞士的人现在可以去“赤足公园”，沿着“感觉小径”行走——脚下有泥土、原木、石头和苔藓。

sentences.en: And it is not difficult to construct your own path with simple everyday objects such as stones or bamboo poles.
sentences.zh: 用石头或竹竿等简单的日常物件，就可以自己搭建出这样一条小径。

sentences.en: But if none of these solutions appeal, there is another option.
sentences.zh: 但如果这些方案都不合你意，还有另一个选择。

sentences.en: A new shoe on the market claims to transform flat, hard, artificial surfaces into something like uneven ground.
sentences.zh: 市场上一种新出的鞋宣称能把平整、坚硬、人造的地面变成类似不平整地面的东西。

sentences.en: ‘These shoes have an unbelievable effect,’ says Benno Nigg, an exercise scientist at Calgary University in Canada.
sentences.zh: “这种鞋具有令人难以置信的效果，”加拿大卡尔加里大学运动科学家本诺·尼格（Benno Nigg）说。

sentences.en: F Known as the Masai Barefoot Technology, the shoes have rounded soles that cause you to rock slightly when you stand still, exercising the small muscles around the ankle that are responsible for stability.
sentences.zh: 这种被称为“马赛赤足科技”（Masai Barefoot Technology）的鞋，鞋底为圆弧形，让你站立不动时也会轻微晃动，从而锻炼负责稳定的踝关节周围的小肌肉。

sentences.en: Forces in the joint are reduced, putting less strain on the system, Nigg claims.
sentences.zh: 尼格声称，关节中的力被降低了，从而减轻了对系统的压力。

sentences.en: G Some of these options may not appeal to all consumers and there is a far simpler alternative.
sentences.zh: 这些选项中的某些可能并不吸引所有消费者，但还有一个更简单得多的替代方案。

sentences.en: If the urban environment is detrimental to our health, then it is obvious where we should turn.
sentences.zh: 如果城市环境对我们的健康有害，那么我们该向哪里求助也就很明显。

sentences.en: A weekend or even a few hours spent in the countryside could help alleviate a sufferer’s aches and pains, and would require only the spending of time.
sentences.zh: 在乡村度过一个周末，甚至只是几小时，就可能帮助缓解患者的疼痛——而这只需要花时间。

sentences.en: However, for many modern citizens, the countryside is not as accessible as it once was and is in fact a dwindling resource.
sentences.zh: 然而，对许多现代市民来说，乡村已不像过去那样容易抵达，事实上它正是一种日益萎缩的资源。

sentences.en: Our concrete cities are growing at a terrifying rate - perhaps at the same rate as our health problems.
sentences.zh: 我们的混凝土城市正在以可怕的速度增长——也许就和我们的健康问题增长的速度相同。

records.title: Mark Strizic: A Career of an Australian Photographer
records.titleZh: 马克·斯特里齐奇：一位澳大利亚摄影师的职业生涯

sentences.en: (A) Mark Strizic, who passed away in December last year, was the last representative of a remarkable generation of European émigré photographers who settled in Australia after the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 马克·斯特里齐克（Mark Strizic）去年 12 月辞世，是二战后定居澳大利亚的一代杰出欧洲流亡摄影师中最后一位代表人物。

sentences.en: Alongside Wolfgang Sievers and Henry Talbot, Strizic contributed significantly to the visual culture of his adopted country.
sentences.zh: 与沃尔夫冈·西弗斯（Wolfgang Sievers）和亨利·塔尔博特（Henry Talbot）一道，斯特里齐克为他所归化的国家的视觉文化做出了重要贡献。

sentences.en: Yet, unlike many of his contemporaries, whose reputations were largely based on industrial or commercial photography, Strizic developed a career that was unusually complex.
sentences.zh: 然而，与他许多以工业或商业摄影为名的同代人不同，斯特里齐克发展出了一份异常复杂的事业。

sentences.en: Over a span of five decades, he explored multiple photographic styles, experimented with new printing processes, engaged in book design, produced large-scale murals, and participated actively in teaching the next generation of photographers.
sentences.zh: 在长达五十年的时间里，他探索过多种摄影风格、尝试新的印刷工艺、参与图书设计、制作大型壁画，并积极参与培养下一代摄影师的教学工作。

sentences.en: (B) After his arrival in Melbourne from Zagreb in 1950, Strizic initially studied science, but soon turned to photography.
sentences.zh: 1950 年从萨格勒布到达墨尔本后，斯特里齐克最初学习的是理科，但很快转向摄影。

sentences.en: From the mid-1950s he began to establish himself, not only through individual works but also through collaborations.
sentences.zh: 从 1950 年代中期起，他开始确立自己的地位，不仅通过个人作品，还通过合作。

sentences.en: One of his most enduring achievements was his partnership with the critic and historian David Saunders, with whom he produced Melbourne: A Portrait in 1960.
sentences.zh: 他最持久的成就之一是与评论家兼历史学家戴维·桑德斯（David Saunders）的合作，二人于 1960 年共同推出《墨尔本：一幅肖像》（Melbourne：A Portrait）。

sentences.en: The book was distinctive for its use of offset printing, a relatively new process at the time, which allowed photographs and text to be integrated seamlessly on the page.
sentences.zh: 该书因采用当时相对新颖的胶印工艺而别具一格，使照片与文字能够在版面上无缝结合。

sentences.en: Strizic, as both photographer and designer, arranged his images so that one composition flowed into the next, often leaving areas of blank space or floating lines of text to balance the spreads.
sentences.zh: 作为摄影师兼设计师，斯特里齐克让一张图像的构图自然过渡到下一张，常常留下大块空白或漂浮的文字行来平衡跨页。

sentences.en: The result was a visually coherent book, which also carried an ambitious cultural agenda: Saunders’ text was printed in Italian and German as well as English, suggesting an international readership.
sentences.zh: 结果是一本视觉连贯的图书，并承载着雄心勃勃的文化议程：桑德斯的文字除英文外还印有意大利文和德文，意指面向国际读者。

sentences.en: The book’s bright and cheerful cover, designed by Leonard French, contributed to its appeal.
sentences.zh: 该书由伦纳德·弗伦奇（Leonard French）设计的明快而欢愉的封面也增添了其吸引力。

sentences.en: In 1961 it was awarded Book of the Year, recognition not only of the photographs themselves but of the integrated design of the whole publication.
sentences.zh: 1961 年它获评年度图书，这一认可不仅是对照片本身，也是对整本出版物的综合设计的肯定。

sentences.en: (C) Strizic later admitted that the idea for Melbourne: A Portrait had been shaped by his father’s earlier work.
sentences.zh: 斯特里齐克后来承认，《墨尔本：一幅肖像》的构想受到他父亲早年作品的塑造。

sentences.en: His father, an architect in Zagreb, had published Light and Shade in 1955, a reflective “city book” in the European style, which contrasted sharply with the more commercial boosterism of contemporary Australian publications.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲是萨格勒布的一名建筑师，1955 年出版了《光与影》（Light and Shade）——一本欧洲风格的、富于反思的“城市之书”，与当时澳大利亚出版物中更为商业化的鼓吹风格形成鲜明对比。

sentences.en: Strizic deliberately sought to emulate this contemplative approach, presenting Melbourne as a modern yet cultured metropolis.
sentences.zh: 斯特里齐克有意效仿这种沉思式的取径，将墨尔本呈现为一座既现代又有文化的都市。

sentences.en: (D) During the 1960s and 70s, Strizic continued to photograph the rapid transformation of Melbourne.
sentences.zh: 在 1960 年代和 70 年代，斯特里齐克继续记录墨尔本的快速变化。

sentences.en: His distinctive technique often involved pointing the camera directly into the sunlight, creating stark contrasts in which buildings and figures were reduced to silhouettes.
sentences.zh: 他独特的技法常常是把镜头直接对准阳光，制造强烈反差，把建筑和人物简化为剪影。

sentences.en: Many of his images juxtapose old Victorian facades with newly constructed skyscrapers, capturing a city in the midst of radical expansion.
sentences.zh: 他的许多影像让维多利亚时代的旧立面与新建摩天大楼并置，捕捉一个正处于剧烈扩张之中的城市。

sentences.en: Cars, highways and office towers dominate the frame, while human figures are frequently marginalised, squeezed into the bottom corners or overshadowed by the built environment.
sentences.zh: 汽车、高速公路和写字楼主导画面，而人物则常被边缘化，被挤到底角，或被建成环境所遮蔽。

sentences.en: By the late 1970s, Strizic’s vision of Melbourne had grown darker.
sentences.zh: 到 1970 年代末，斯特里齐克镜头下的墨尔本变得更加阴郁。

sentences.en: Using experimental methods, such as printing black-and-white negatives on colour paper or duplicating them onto high-contrast lithographic film, he produced cityscapes that glowed with intense, sometimes psychedelic colours, giving Melbourne an almost hallucinatory quality.
sentences.zh: 采用实验性方法——比如把黑白底片印在彩色相纸上、或把它们复制到高反差平版印刷胶片上——他制作出闪着强烈、有时近乎迷幻色彩的城市景观，让墨尔本带上几乎幻觉般的质感。

sentences.en: (E) Collaboration remained central to Strizic’s career.
sentences.zh: 合作一直是斯特里齐克职业生涯的核心。

sentences.en: In 1967 he worked with Sun Books, a small but ambitious publishing house, on several innovative projects.
sentences.zh: 1967 年，他与一家小而雄心勃勃的出版社 Sun Books 合作了几个创新项目。

sentences.en: For Tim Burstall’s film 2000 Weeks he created a photo-roman, a paperback-sized publication in which his stills from the film were combined with dialogue.
sentences.zh: 为蒂姆·伯斯托尔（Tim Burstall）的电影《2000 Weeks》，他创作了一部“图像小说”——一本平装书大小的出版物，把电影剧照与对白结合在一起。

sentences.en: Although the film was produced in a European art-house style and tackled existential themes, it failed at the box office, and Strizic’s book met a similar fate.
sentences.zh: 尽管该片以欧洲艺术电影的风格制作并触及存在主义主题，但票房失败，斯特里齐克的这本书也遭遇了同样命运。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the project demonstrated his willingness to experiment with new formats.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，这个项目展示了他乐于尝试新形式的意愿。

sentences.en: (F) A more prestigious venture was Involvement (1968), a limited-edition art book edited by Andrew Grimwade.
sentences.zh: 另一个更具声望的项目是由安德鲁·格里姆韦德（Andrew Grimwade）编辑的限量版艺术图书《Involvement》（1968）。

sentences.en: The concept was to pair Strizic’s photographic portraits with paintings by the artist Clifton Pugh.
sentences.zh: 其构想是把斯特里齐克的摄影肖像与艺术家克利夫顿·普赫（Clifton Pugh）的画作并置。

sentences.en: The accompanying text, written by Geoffrey Dutton, sought to place the collaboration in a grand cultural framework.
sentences.zh: 由杰弗里·达顿（Geoffrey Dutton）撰写的随附文字，试图把这次合作置于一种宏大的文化框架之中。

sentences.en: Yet the book was widely regarded as unsatisfactory, largely because of its design.
sentences.zh: 然而，这本书被普遍认为不令人满意，主要是因为其设计。

sentences.en: Unlike Melbourne: A Portrait, Strizic did not design the volume himself, and the layout by Les Gray failed to balance the colour plates of Pugh’s paintings with the black-and-white photographs.
sentences.zh: 与《墨尔本：一幅肖像》不同，斯特里齐克并未自己设计该卷，由莱斯·格雷（Les Gray）担纲的版面未能让普赫画作的彩色印张与那些黑白照片相得益彰。

sentences.en: Despite this, Strizic’s portraits attracted attention for their originality.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，斯特里齐克的肖像因其原创性而引人注目。

sentences.en: He employed experimental methods such as “pushing” his 35mm film to increase contrast and grain, and often shot his sitters against dominant backgrounds or with objects intruding into the foreground.
sentences.zh: 他采用了一些实验性方法，例如“推冲”35 毫米胶片以增加反差和颗粒感，并常常让被摄者面对压迫性的背景，或让物体侵入前景。

sentences.en: The effect was to highlight their individuality and resistance to their surroundings.
sentences.zh: 其效果是凸显他们的个性，以及他们对周围环境的抵抗。

sentences.en: His portrait of Sir Charles Moses, head of the ABC, shows him through a haze of cigar smoke, while Barry Humphries appears surrounded by eccentric antiques in his London flat.
sentences.zh: 他为澳大利亚广播公司（ABC）负责人查尔斯·摩西爵士（Sir Charles Moses）所拍的肖像中，他透过雪茄烟雾出现；而巴里·汉弗里斯（Barry Humphries）则出现在他位于伦敦公寓中、被奇特古董包围的画面里。

sentences.en: These images were exhibited in 1968 at the National Gallery of Victoria under the title Some Australian Personalities, marking the institution’s first solo exhibition devoted to photography.
sentences.zh: 1968 年，这些影像在维多利亚国家美术馆以《Some Australian Personalities》为题展出，是该机构首次为摄影举办的个展。

sentences.en: (G) Strizic’s collaborative spirit extended into many other areas.
sentences.zh: 斯特里齐克的合作精神延伸到许多其他领域。

sentences.en: He documented the sculptor John Davis and the furniture designer Schulim Krimper for monographs commissioned in the 1980s, but his connection with Krimper went back to 1959.
sentences.zh: 他为雕塑家约翰·戴维斯（John Davis）和家具设计师舒利姆·克里姆珀（Schulim Krimper）拍摄了 1980 年代受托的专著，但他与克里姆珀的渊源可以追溯到 1959 年。

sentences.en: He also worked with avant-garde artists such as Asher Bilu, producing the only surviving photographic record of Bilu’s interactive electronic work Sculptron (1967).
sentences.zh: 他还与前卫艺术家阿舍尔·比卢（Asher Bilu）合作，制作了比卢的互动电子作品《Sculptron》（1967）唯一存世的摄影记录。

sentences.en: This task required considerable technical skill, since Strizic had to balance the exposure for glowing cathode-ray tubes with the surrounding sculptural elements.
sentences.zh: 这项任务需要相当高的技术功力，因为斯特里齐克必须在发光的阴极射线管与周围雕塑元素之间平衡曝光。

sentences.en: In the field of murals, he developed large-scale photographic works for government buildings and corporate headquarters, sometimes combining his “photochromes” with paintings.
sentences.zh: 在壁画领域，他为政府建筑和企业总部制作大型摄影作品，有时把他的“photochrome”与绘画结合。

sentences.en: A notable example was his collaboration with Stanislav Ostoja-Kotkowski in 1970 on a twelve-metre mural for the Ciba-Geigy building in Preston, which merged infrared photography with Strizic’s experimental prints.
sentences.zh: 一个显著例子是 1970 年他与斯坦尼斯拉夫·奥斯托亚-科特科夫斯基（Stanislav Ostoja-Kotkowski）合作，为 Preston 的 Ciba-Geigy 大楼制作了一面 12 米长的壁画，将红外摄影与斯特里齐克的实验性印片融合在一起。

sentences.en: (H) That same year, Strizic worked with the influential architect Robin Boyd on Living in Australia, a book which sought to articulate Boyd’s design philosophy.
sentences.zh: 同年，斯特里齐克与颇具影响力的建筑师罗宾·博伊德（Robin Boyd）合作完成《Living in Australia》，该书试图阐明博伊德的设计哲学。

sentences.en: Strizic’s photography reinforced Boyd’s arguments, presenting domestic architecture through dramatic diagonal compositions and sharp contrasts.
sentences.zh: 斯特里齐克的摄影强化了博伊德的论点——通过戏剧性的对角线构图和强烈反差呈现住宅建筑。

sentences.en: The book was recently republished, confirming its continuing relevance.
sentences.zh: 该书近期再版，印证了其持续的现实意义。

sentences.en: (I) In later years, Strizic combined his artistic practice with teaching in Melbourne’s new photography departments during the boom of the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 晚年，在 1970 年代摄影学科蓬勃发展的时代，斯特里齐克把他的艺术实践与在墨尔本新设立的摄影系的教学结合起来。

sentences.en: In 1988 he returned to his earliest negatives of Melbourne, staging an exhibition that highlighted his long-standing interest in the city’s changing urban landscape.
sentences.zh: 1988 年，他重新审视自己最早拍摄的墨尔本底片，举办了一场展览，凸显他对这座城市不断变化的都市景观长期以来的兴趣。

sentences.en: Since then, he has often been remembered as a nostalgic chronicler of “old Melbourne” or “disappearing Melbourne.”
sentences.zh: 从那以后，他常被记作“老墨尔本”或“消失中的墨尔本”的怀旧记录者。

sentences.en: Yet such a label oversimplifies his contribution.
sentences.zh: 然而，这样的标签把他的贡献简单化了。

sentences.en: His career was marked by continuous experimentation, by fruitful collaborations with artists, writers and designers, and by a willingness to engage with both traditional and avant-garde practices.
sentences.zh: 他的职业生涯以持续的实验、与艺术家、作家和设计师富有成效的合作，以及对传统与前卫实践兼收并蓄的意愿为特征。

sentences.en: In this sense, he occupies a significant though sometimes under-recognised position in the development of Australian visual culture.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，他在澳大利亚视觉文化的发展中占据着一个重要却有时未被充分认识的位置。

records.title: Clarence Birdseye and the Development of Frozen Food
records.titleZh: 克拉伦斯·伯德西与冷冻食品的发展

sentences.en: (A) Born in 1886 in New York, the American naturalist Clarence Birdseye had an instinctive curiosity, a love of food, and a strong entrepreneurial streak.
sentences.zh: 美国博物学家克拉伦斯·伯德赛（Clarence Birdseye）于 1886 年生于纽约，天生好奇心强、热爱美食，并有强烈的创业精神。

sentences.en: At the age of ten, he was hunting, selling live animals and teaching himself taxidermy, the art of preserving and mounting the skins of animals.
sentences.zh: 在十岁时，他就在打猎、卖活体动物，并自学动物标本制作——即将动物皮毛保存并装架的技艺。

sentences.en: He studied science in college, but had to drop out because tuition was too expensive.
sentences.zh: 他在大学里学的是理科，但因学费过于昂贵而被迫辍学。

sentences.en: Forced to support himself, he moved west, where he worked in Montana as an assistant naturalist, capturing small mammals to study the parasites that they often carried in their fur.
sentences.zh: 为了养活自己，他迁往西部，在蒙大拿州担任助理博物学家，捕捉小型哺乳动物以研究其毛皮中常携带的寄生虫。

sentences.en: Eventually, partly as a result of this research, the source of a prevalent disease was isolated.
sentences.zh: 最终，部分得益于这项研究，一种流行病的源头被分离出来。

sentences.en: (B) Within a few years, Birdseye moved to the arctic tundra of Labrador, in what is now northern Canada, where he worked for several years as a fur trader.
sentences.zh: 几年之内，伯德赛搬到了今天属于加拿大北部的拉布拉多地区的极地苔原，在那里以皮毛贸易商的身份工作了几年。

sentences.en: He spent much of his time among the local trappers who worked year-round in the icy wilderness, and he rode long journeys with a nine-dog sled to purchase goods that were exported to a company in New York.
sentences.zh: 他大部分时间都和那些常年在冰封荒原上劳作的当地猎人在一起，并驾着九只狗的雪橇进行长途旅行，去采购运回纽约一家公司的货物。

sentences.en: It appeared that Birdseye relished the challenge that came with the cold climate and rugged landscape of Labrador.
sentences.zh: 看起来，伯德赛很享受拉布拉多严寒气候和崎岖地貌所带来的挑战。

sentences.en: (C) However, the food in Labrador left a great deal to be desired.
sentences.zh: 然而，拉布拉多的食物实在乏善可陈。

sentences.en: The bleak climate meant that everything he ate during the winter was either from cans or frozen.
sentences.zh: 严酷的气候意味着他冬天吃的每样东西要么是罐头，要么是冷冻的。

sentences.en: When the frozen food was thawed, Birdseye found it to be tasteless.
sentences.zh: 当冷冻食物解冻后，伯德赛发现它们寡淡无味。

sentences.en: What’s more, the texture of the food became mushy and unappealing.
sentences.zh: 更糟的是，食物的口感变得软烂而毫无吸引力。

sentences.en: Other than fish, there were no fresh sources of food, so the naturalist took up ice fishing with some of the local Inuit people, carving holes in frozen lakes and casting a line for trout.
sentences.zh: 除了鱼之外没有新鲜食材来源，于是这位博物学家便和当地的因纽特人一起冰钓——在冰冻的湖面上凿洞，再放线钓鳟鱼。

sentences.en: With air temperatures so far below zero, a fish pulled out of the lake would freeze solid in a matter of seconds.
sentences.zh: 由于气温远低于零度，一条从湖中拉出来的鱼会在几秒内被冻得硬邦邦。

sentences.en: But when he thawed out the frozen trout, Birdseye found it tasted far fresher than the usual food he was used to eating.
sentences.zh: 但当他把冻硬的鳟鱼解冻之后，伯德赛发现它比他平时吃到的食物要新鲜得多。

sentences.en: Unwittingly, the young adventurer had made a powerful discovery.
sentences.zh: 这位年轻的探险者无意间做出了一项重大发现。

sentences.en: He would come to realize that the dramatic difference in taste was all due to the speed of the freezing process, or what we call flash freezing, and that by recreating the science, he could make high quality frozen food.
sentences.zh: 他后来意识到，这种口感上的巨大差异，全是因冷冻速度——也就是我们所说的速冻——所致；而通过重现这一科学过程，他便能制作高品质的冷冻食品。

sentences.en: (D) In the first decades of the 20th century, the frozen-food business was considered to be the very bottom of the barrel.
sentences.zh: 在 20 世纪头几十年，冷冻食品产业被视为食品行业里最末等的一类。

sentences.en: Frozen food was terrible.
sentences.zh: 冷冻食品糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: In fact, it was even banned in New York State prisons for being beneath the culinary standard of convicts.
sentences.zh: 事实上，纽约州的监狱甚至禁止使用冷冻食品，因为它达不到囚犯餐食的标准。

sentences.en: A key problem was that the food was being frozen at relatively high temperatures, often just a few degrees below freezing.
sentences.zh: 关键问题在于食品是在相对较高的温度下被冷冻——通常只比冰点低几度。

sentences.en: A slow freeze allowed ice to form larger crystals that broke the membranes surrounding and protecting each of the cells within the food.
sentences.zh: 缓慢冷冻使得冰能够形成较大的晶体，从而刺破包裹和保护食物中每个细胞的细胞膜。

sentences.en: When the food was defrosted, the ice crystals melted and the juice would leak out.
sentences.zh: 食物解冻时，冰晶融化，汁液就会流失。

sentences.en: But flash freezing avoided this problem, plus scientific advances had made it possible to artificially produce temperatures that were much like Birdseye had experienced in Labrador.
sentences.zh: 但速冻可以避免这一问题，加上科学进步使人们能够人工制造出类似伯德赛在拉布拉多所体验到的低温。

sentences.en: By the early 1920s, Birdseye had created a flash-freezing process using cartons of fish, stacked and frozen at minus 40 degrees Celsius.
sentences.zh: 到 1920 年代初，伯德赛已经创造出一种速冻工艺，把鱼装进纸箱并在零下 40 摄氏度下叠放冷冻。

sentences.en: (E) Birdseye was also concerned about eliminating the little air pockets that in whole fish could harbor bacteria and lead to decomposition.
sentences.zh: 伯德赛还关注消除整鱼内可能藏匿细菌、导致腐败的小气孔。

sentences.en: So a key part of his original 1924 process called for removing the bones, which allowed the fish parts to be tightly packed into rectangular fiberboard boxes.
sentences.zh: 因此，他 1924 年原始工艺的一个关键环节就是去除鱼骨，这样鱼肉可以紧密地装入长方形的纤维板盒中。

sentences.en: Birdseye had to pioneer almost everything else in his process as well.
sentences.zh: 伯德赛还几乎不得不为整个流程的其余每个环节作开创性的工作。

sentences.en: This included inventing a glue for the packaging boxes, to withstand the changes in temperature, as well as a waterproof ink for the labels.
sentences.zh: 这包括发明一种能承受温度变化的包装盒胶水，以及一种用于标签的防水油墨。

sentences.en: He found that just about anything he froze with his method - fruit, meat, vegetables - would be remarkably fresh after thawing.
sentences.zh: 他发现，几乎任何用他这种方法冷冻的东西——水果、肉类、蔬菜——在解冻后都依然非常新鲜。

sentences.en: (F) Frozen food was still more than a decade away from becoming common in the average diet across the United States.
sentences.zh: 冷冻食品距离在美国普通家庭餐桌上变得普及，还有十几年的时间。

sentences.en: This required a critical mass of freezers - in supermarkets and home kitchens - that wouldn’t be available until the late 1940s.
sentences.zh: 这需要在超市和家庭厨房里达到一定规模的冰柜保有量——而这要等到 1940 年代末才得以实现。

sentences.en: But Birdseye’s experiments were so promising that in 1929, his company, General Seafood, was acquired by the Postum Cereal Company.
sentences.zh: 但伯德赛的实验前景非常看好，以至于在 1929 年，他的公司“通用海产”（General Seafood）被博斯顿谷物公司（Postum Cereal Company）收购。

sentences.en: His adventures in ice fishing had made him a multimillionaire.
sentences.zh: 他在冰钓中的探险，让他成了百万富翁。

sentences.en: (G) In our current age of locally sourced food production, frozen food has fallen out of favor with the public.
sentences.zh: 在如今提倡本地化食物生产的时代，冷冻食品已经不再受公众青睐。

sentences.en: But the advent of flash-frozen food had a positive impact on the American economy and the health of everyday people.
sentences.zh: 但速冻食品的出现对美国经济和普通人的健康都产生了积极影响。

sentences.en: It extended distribution across the entire country so that fish caught in the North Atlantic could be eaten in distant cities like Denver or Dallas.
sentences.zh: 它把分销范围扩展到全国——这样，从北大西洋捕来的鱼可以送到丹佛或达拉斯这样的遥远城市供人食用。

sentences.en: And produce harvested in summer could be consumed months later.
sentences.zh: 夏季收获的农产品也可以在数月后被消费。

sentences.en: By the mid-20th century, frozen food was a worldwide phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 到 20 世纪中叶，冷冻食品已成为一种全球现象。

sentences.en: (H) In fact, while nutritionists today would prefer we eat fresh food grown locally, they acknowledge the value of frozen food.
sentences.zh: 事实上，尽管今天的营养学家会更希望我们食用本地种植的新鲜食材，但他们也承认冷冻食品的价值。

sentences.en: And scientists at the University of Chester in England came to the same conclusion after performing tests on the nutritional value of frozen produce.
sentences.zh: 英国切斯特大学（University of Chester）的科学家在对冷冻农产品的营养价值进行测试后，得出了相同的结论。

sentences.en: They found in many cases that frozen fruits and vegetables are more nutritious and healthier than the regular unfrozen variety sold in stores.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，许多情况下，冷冻水果和蔬菜比商店里出售的常规未冷冻品种更具营养、更健康。

sentences.en: This is because the minute a fruit or vegetable is harvested, it begins to decay.
sentences.zh: 这是因为水果或蔬菜被采收的一刻，就开始衰败。

sentences.en: But, as most frozen fruits and vegetables are flash-frozen within hours of their harvest, at their peak of ripeness, this locks in many of the important nutrients.
sentences.zh: 但由于大多数冷冻水果和蔬菜在采收后数小时内、处于成熟巅峰时即被速冻，这就锁住了许多重要营养素。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the unfrozen produce can undergo change while being transported thousands of kilometers over several days.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，未冷冻的农产品在经数千公里运输、历时数天的过程中可能发生变化。

sentences.en: In one report, the vitamin C content in raspberries frozen for a year was compared to that of unfrozen raspberries stored in a refrigerator for three days.
sentences.zh: 在一项报告中，将冷冻保存一年的覆盆子的维生素 C 含量，与在冰箱中冷藏三天的未冷冻覆盆子进行了比较。

sentences.en: Their levels of vitamin C were nearly the same.
sentences.zh: 二者的维生素 C 水平几乎相同。

sentences.en: (A) The story of tea begins in China.
sentences.zh: 茶的故事始于中国。

sentences.en: According to legend, in 2737 BC the Chinese emperor Shen Nung was sitting beneath a tree while his servant boiled drinking water, when some leaves from the tree blew into the water.
sentences.zh: 相传在公元前2737年，中国的神农帝坐在一棵树下，仆人正在烧饮用水，这时树上的几片叶子飘落到了水中。

sentences.en: Shen Nung, a renowned herbalist, decided to try the infusion that his servant had accidentally created.
sentences.zh: 神农是一位著名的草药学家，他决定尝一尝仆人无意间泡出的这种饮品。

sentences.en: The tree was a Camellia sinensis, and the resulting drink was what we now call tea.
sentences.zh: 那棵树是茶树（学名Camellia sinensis），由此泡成的饮品就是我们今天所称的茶。

sentences.en: It is impossible to know whether there is any truth in this story, but tea-drinking certainly became established in China many centuries before it had even been heard of in the West.
sentences.zh: 这个故事是否属实已无从知晓，但可以肯定的是，早在西方听说茶之前的许多个世纪，饮茶就已在中国确立。

sentences.en: Containers for tea have been found in tombs dating from the Han Dynasty (206 BC–220 AD), but it was under the Tang Dynasty (618–906 AD) that tea became firmly established as the national drink of China.
sentences.zh: 在汉代（公元前206年至公元220年）的墓葬中已发现盛茶的器皿，但茶真正稳固确立为中国的国饮，是在唐代（公元618年至906年）。

sentences.en: (B) It became such a favourite that during the late eighth century a writer called Lu Yu wrote the first book entirely about tea, the Ch’a Ching, or Tea Classic.
sentences.zh: 茶大受欢迎，以致八世纪后期一位名叫陆羽的作者写下了第一部专门论茶的著作《茶经》。

sentences.en: It was shortly after this that tea was first introduced to Japan, by Japanese Buddhist monks who had travelled to China to study.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，茶由前往中国求学的日本僧人首次传入日本。

sentences.en: Tea received almost instant imperial sponsorship and spread rapidly from the royal court and monasteries to the other sections of Japanese society.
sentences.zh: 茶几乎立刻获得了皇室的扶持，并迅速从宫廷和寺院传播到日本社会的其他阶层。

sentences.en: (C) So at this stage in the history of tea, Europe was rather lagging behind.
sentences.zh: 因此，在茶发展史的这一阶段，欧洲相当落后。

sentences.en: In the latter half of the sixteenth century there are the first brief mentions of tea as a drink among Europeans, mostly from Portuguese who were living in the East as traders and missionaries.
sentences.zh: 十六世纪后半叶，欧洲人中开始零星出现关于茶这种饮品的最早记述，大多出自以商人和传教士身份居住在东方的葡萄牙人之手。

sentences.en: But although some of these individuals may have brought back samples of tea to their native country, it was not the Portuguese who were the first to ship back tea as a commercial import.
sentences.zh: 但尽管其中一些人或许把茶样带回了本国，最早把茶作为商业进口品运回的却并非葡萄牙人。

sentences.en: (D) This was done by the Dutch, who in the last years of the sixteenth century began to encroach on Portuguese trading routes in the East.
sentences.zh: 做到这一点的是荷兰人，他们在十六世纪最后几年开始侵入葡萄牙人在东方的贸易航线。

sentences.en: By the turn of the century they had established a trading post on the island of Java, and it was via Java that in 1606 the first consignment of tea was shipped from China to Holland.
sentences.zh: 到世纪之交，他们已在爪哇岛建立了贸易站，正是经由爪哇，1606年第一批茶从中国运往荷兰。

sentences.en: Tea soon became a fashionable drink among the Dutch, and from there spread to other countries in continental western Europe, but because of its high price it remained a drink for the wealthy.
sentences.zh: 茶很快在荷兰人中成为时尚饮品，并由此传播到西欧大陆的其他国家，但由于价格高昂，它始终是富人的饮品。

sentences.en: (E) Britain, always a little suspicious of continental trends, had yet to become the nation of tea- drinkers that it is today.
sentences.zh: 英国对欧洲大陆的风尚向来略带疑虑，当时还远未成为如今这样一个饮茶之国。

sentences.en: Starting in 1600, the British East India Company had a monopoly on importing goods from outside Europe, and it is likely that sailors on these ships brought tea home as gifts.
sentences.zh: 从1600年起，英国东印度公司垄断了从欧洲以外进口货物的贸易，这些船上的水手很可能把茶作为礼物带回了家。

sentences.en: The first coffee-house had been established in London in 1652, and tea was still somewhat unfamiliar to most readers, so it is fair to assume that the drink was still something of a curiosity.
sentences.zh: 伦敦第一家咖啡馆于1652年开张，当时茶对多数人而言仍较为陌生，因此可以合理地推断，这种饮品当时还只是一种新奇之物。

sentences.en: (F) Gradually, it became a popular drink in coffee-houses, which were as much locations for the transaction of business as they were for relaxation or pleasure.
sentences.zh: 渐渐地，茶在咖啡馆里成为一种受欢迎的饮品，而咖啡馆既是放松消遣的场所，也同样是洽谈生意的地方。

sentences.en: They were, though, the preserve of middle- and upper-class men; women drank tea in their own homes, and as yet tea was still too expensive to be widespread among the working classes.
sentences.zh: 不过，咖啡馆是中上层阶级男性的专属之地；女性则在自己家中饮茶，而当时茶仍然过于昂贵，未能在劳动阶层中普及。

sentences.en: In part, its high price was due to a punitive system of taxation.
sentences.zh: 茶价高昂的部分原因在于一套惩罚性的税收制度。

sentences.en: (G) One unforeseen consequence of the taxation of tea was the growth of methods to avoid taxation—smuggling and adulteration.
sentences.zh: 对茶征税的一个意想不到的后果，是各种逃税手段的滋长——走私与掺假。

sentences.en: By the eighteenth century many Britons wanted to drink tea but could not afford the high prices, and their enthusiasm for the drink was matched by the enthusiasm of criminal gangs to smuggle it in.
sentences.zh: 到十八世纪，许多英国人想喝茶却负担不起高昂的价格，而他们对茶的热情，正与犯罪团伙走私茶叶的热情不相上下。

sentences.en: What began as a small-time illegal trade, selling a few pounds of tea to personal contacts, developed by the late eighteenth century into an astonishing organised-crime network, perhaps importing as much as seven million lb annually, compared to a legal import of five million lb!
sentences.zh: 起初只是向私人熟客出售几磅茶叶的小本非法买卖，到十八世纪后期已发展成一张惊人的有组织犯罪网络，每年走私进口的茶叶或许多达700万磅，而合法进口量不过500万磅！

sentences.en: (H) Worse for the drinkers was that taxation also encouraged the adulteration of tea, particularly of smuggled tea which was not quality-controlled through customs and excise.
sentences.zh: 对饮茶者更糟的是，征税还助长了茶叶掺假，尤其是那些未经海关消费税质量管控的走私茶。

sentences.en: Leaves from other plants, or leaves which had already been brewed and then dried, were added to tea leaves.
sentences.zh: 人们把其他植物的叶子，或是已经冲泡过再晒干的叶子，掺进茶叶里。

sentences.en: By 1784, the government realised that enough was enough, and that heavy taxation was creating more problems than it was worth.
sentences.zh: 到1784年，政府意识到不能再这样下去了，沉重的税负带来的麻烦已得不偿失。

sentences.en: The new Prime Minister, William Pitt the Younger, slashed the tax from 119 per cent to 12.5 per cent.
sentences.zh: 新任首相小威廉·皮特把税率从119%大幅削减到12.5%。

sentences.en: Suddenly legal tea was affordable, and smuggling stopped virtually overnight.
sentences.zh: 合法茶叶一下子变得人人买得起，走私几乎一夜之间销声匿迹。

sentences.en: (I) Another great impetus to tea-drinking resulted from the end of the East India Company’s monopoly on trade with China, in 1834.
sentences.zh: 推动饮茶的另一大动力，来自1834年东印度公司对华贸易垄断权的终结。

sentences.en: Before that date, China was the country of origin of the vast majority of the tea imported to Britain, but the end of its monopoly stimulated the East India Company to consider growing tea outside China.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，英国进口的茶叶绝大多数原产于中国，但垄断权的终结促使东印度公司开始考虑在中国之外种植茶叶。

sentences.en: India had always been the centre of the Company’s operations, which led to the increased cultivation of tea in India, beginning in Assam.
sentences.zh: 印度一直是该公司经营的中心，于是印度的茶叶种植日渐增多，最早始于阿萨姆。

sentences.en: There were a few false starts, including the destruction by cattle of one of the earliest tea nurseries, but by 1888 British tea imports from India were for the first time greater than those from China.
sentences.zh: 其间经历了几次失败的尝试，包括最早的一处茶苗圃被牛群毁坏，但到1888年，英国从印度进口的茶叶首次超过了从中国进口的数量。

sentences.en: (J) The end of the East India Company’s monopoly on trade with China also had another result, which was more dramatic though less important in the long term: it ushered in the era of the tea clippers.
sentences.zh: 东印度公司对华贸易垄断的终结还带来了另一个结果，它更为戏剧性，但从长远看并不那么重要：它开启了飞剪式运茶帆船的时代。

sentences.en: While the Company had had the monopoly on trade, there was no rush to bring the tea from China to Britain, but after 1834 the tea trade became a virtual free-for-all.
sentences.zh: 在该公司垄断贸易期间，人们并不急于把茶从中国运回英国，但1834年之后，茶叶贸易几乎成了一场人人参与的混战。

sentences.en: (K) Individual merchants and sea-captains with their own ships raced to bring home the tea and make the most money, using fast new clippers which had sleek lines, tall masts and huge sails.
sentences.zh: 拥有自己船只的个体商人和船长竞相把茶运回国以赚取最多的钱，他们使用线条流畅、桅杆高耸、风帆巨大的新式快速飞剪船。

sentences.en: In particular, there was competition between British and American merchants, leading to the famous clipper races of the 1860s.
sentences.zh: 尤其在英国和美国商人之间存在竞争，由此引发了1860年代著名的飞剪船竞赛。

sentences.en: But these races soon came to an end with the opening of the Suez Canal, which made the trade routes to China viable for steamships for the first time.
sentences.zh: 但随着苏伊士运河的开通，这些竞赛很快走到了尽头，因为运河首次使蒸汽船得以航行于通往中国的贸易航线。

sentences.en: (A) In the sixth century Gregory of Tours, a chronicler* of the Germanic people known as the Franks, told of an extraordinary event in what is now Switzerland, where the Rhone River spills into Lake Geneva.
sentences.zh: 六世纪时，记述被称为法兰克人的日耳曼民族的编年史家格雷戈里·德·图尔，讲述了一件发生在今天瑞士境内、罗讷河汇入日内瓦湖之处的非凡事件。

sentences.en: He wrote of a big rockfall in the year 563 AD in the vicinity of a place called Tauredunum.
sentences.zh: 他写到公元563年在一个名叫陶雷杜努姆的地方附近发生的一场大规模岩崩。

sentences.en: The debris plunged into the river, and a great mass of water 'overwhelmed with a sudden and violent flood all that was on the banks as far as the city of Geneva,' more than 64 kilometres across the lake.
sentences.zh: 碎石坠入河中，一大股水“以突如其来的猛烈洪流，淹没了两岸的一切，一直冲到日内瓦城”，那里距此横跨湖面64多公里。

sentences.en: The Geneva bridge was demolished, and several people inside the city walls of Geneva were killed.
sentences.zh: 日内瓦的桥被冲毁，日内瓦城墙内也有数人丧生。

sentences.en: Historians and scientists have long believed that Gregory and another chronicler, Marius of Avenches, who told a similar tale, were describing a tsunami that raced across the lake.
sentences.zh: 历史学家和科学家长期以来一直相信，格雷戈里以及另一位讲述过类似故事的编年史家阿旺什的马里乌斯，所描述的是一场横扫湖面的海啸。

sentences.en: But there has not been any direct evidence of it until now.
sentences.zh: 但直到如今，一直没有任何关于它的直接证据。

sentences.en: (B) Researchers at the University of Geneva now say they have found that evidence, in the form of a large deposit of sediment in the middle of the lake.
sentences.zh: 日内瓦大学的研究者现在表示，他们已经找到了那个证据，其形式是湖中央一大片沉积物。

sentences.en: In a study published in the journal Nature Geoscience, they also propose the sequence of events that caused the deadly surge.
sentences.zh: 在一篇发表于《自然·地球科学》杂志的研究中，他们还提出了引发这场致命浪涌的一连串事件。

sentences.en: The researchers think that large boulders crashed down onto soft sediments which had accumulated at the river mouth because of the slowing of the river's flow when it enters the lake.
sentences.zh: 研究者认为，大块巨砾崩落到松软的沉积物上，这些沉积物因河流注入湖中、流速放缓而在河口堆积。

sentences.en: These sediments formed an underwater delta that had several canyon-like channels.
sentences.zh: 这些沉积物形成了一片水下三角洲，其中有几条峡谷状的水道。

sentences.en: When the falling rocks hit the delta they destabilised the sediments and caused the canyons to collapse.
sentences.zh: 当崩落的岩石砸到三角洲上时，它们使沉积物失去稳定，导致那些峡谷塌陷。

sentences.en: It was this collapse that created the tsunami.
sentences.zh: 正是这次塌陷造就了海啸。

sentences.en: The sediments from this collapse would have been propelled towards the lake's centre.
sentences.zh: 这次塌陷产生的沉积物，会被推向湖的中央。

sentences.en: (C) Guy Simpson, a lecturer in the University of Geneva's Department of Geology and Paleontology, says the thick layer of sediment, which has the same curved shape as a lens, lies more than 305 metres down in the deepest part of the lake, and was found largely by chance.
sentences.zh: 日内瓦大学地质与古生物学系的讲师居伊·辛普森说，这层厚厚的沉积物形状像透镜一样弯曲，位于湖最深处的水下305米以下，而它的发现在很大程度上是出于偶然。

sentences.en: Katrina Kremer, a University of Geneva doctoral student and the study's lead author, had been conducting seismic soundings, searching for thin sediment layers that might be evidence of major floods that had taken place in pre-historic times, long before the event described by Gregory of Tours.
sentences.zh: 日内瓦大学的博士生、该研究的第一作者卡特里娜·克雷默，当时一直在进行地震测深，寻找可能是史前时期大洪水证据的薄层沉积，那些洪水远早于格雷戈里·德·图尔所描述的事件。

sentences.en: 'But we came across this enormous deposit,' Simpson says.
sentences.zh: “但我们却偶然发现了这处巨大的沉积，”辛普森说。

sentences.en: 'We didn't know straight away that it was the deposit that caused the [sixth- century] tsunami.
sentences.zh: “我们并没有立刻就明白，正是这处沉积造成了那场（六世纪的）海啸。

sentences.en: But it was a jumbled mess of sediment.
sentences.zh: 但它是一团杂乱无章的沉积物。

sentences.en: It was quite obvious that it was deposited rapidly.'
sentences.zh: 很明显，它是迅速堆积而成的。”

sentences.en: (D) The researchers then took samples of the sediments and used carbon-dating techniques on remains of leaves and other organic matter they found to determine when the deposit formed.
sentences.zh: 研究者随后采集了沉积物的样本，并对其中发现的树叶残余及其他有机物使用碳定年技术，以确定这处沉积是何时形成的。

sentences.en: This narrowed the range to a period between the late fourth century and the early seventh century.
sentences.zh: 这把年代范围缩小到了四世纪末到七世纪初之间。

sentences.en: Other than the rockfall, there is no record of any special event during that period, Simpson says.
sentences.zh: 辛普森说，除了那场岩崩之外，那一时期没有任何特殊事件的记载。

sentences.en: (E) The researchers estimated that the deposit, which is at least 9.6 kilometres long by 4.8 kilometres wide, and averages about five metres thick, contains more than 248 million cubic metres of material.
sentences.zh: 研究者估计，这处沉积至少长9.6公里、宽4.8公里，平均厚约五米，所含物质超过2.48亿立方米。

sentences.en: They ran multiple computer simulations showing that the collapse of that much sediment at the mouth of the Rhone would have caused a tsunami with an estimated height of 7.9 metres at Geneva - where it would have arrived in about 70 minutes.
sentences.zh: 他们进行了多次计算机模拟，结果显示，罗讷河口这么多沉积物的塌陷，会在日内瓦引发一场估计高达7.9米的海啸——海啸大约70分钟后就会抵达那里。

sentences.en: The rockfall itself may have been set off by a major earthquake, as some scientists have speculated.
sentences.zh: 正如一些科学家所推测的，岩崩本身可能是由一场大地震引发的。

sentences.en: (F) Lake tsunamis, although unusual, are not unknown, says Richard Schweickert, an Emeritus Professor of Geology at the University of Nevada in Reno, in the United States.
sentences.zh: 美国内华达大学里诺分校的地质学荣休教授理查德·施韦克特说，湖泊海啸虽不寻常，却并非闻所未闻。

sentences.en: He cites evidence that the collapse of part of the shoreline of Lake Tahoe in northern California within the past 20,000 years caused a tsunami with wave heights of about 30 metres.
sentences.zh: 他举证说，在过去两万年间，加利福尼亚北部塔霍湖部分湖岸的塌陷，曾引发一场浪高约30米的海啸。

sentences.en: There are two faults under the lake that could have caused an earthquake, he says and that the collapse of the Rhone delta sediments, as calculated by the Swiss researchers, 'would certainly be capable of moving a large amount of material into the lake.'
sentences.zh: 他说，湖底有两条断层本可能引发地震，而正如这几位瑞士研究者所计算的，罗讷河三角洲沉积物的塌陷，“确实有能力把大量物质推入湖中”。

sentences.en: He suggests that the findings could be corroborated by careful mapping of the shoreline to look for unusual deposits or erosion left behind by the giant waves.
sentences.zh: 他建议，可以通过对湖岸进行细致测绘、寻找巨浪留下的异常沉积或侵蚀痕迹，来佐证这些发现。

sentences.en: (G) Simpson says the Rhone delta sediments might collapse again, perhaps from an earthquake or even their own weight.
sentences.zh: 辛普森说，罗讷河三角洲的沉积物可能会再次塌陷，或许是因地震，甚至可能是因其自身的重量。

sentences.en: In the sixth century, Geneva was a small community, mostly behind walls on a hill, whereas today it is home to international organisations and about 200,000 people, many living in low-lying areas near the water.
sentences.zh: 六世纪时，日内瓦还是一个小小的聚居地，大多躲在山丘上的城墙之内，而今天它却是众多国际组织的所在地，约有20万人口，其中许多人就住在临水的低洼地带。

sentences.en: Testing the stability of nearby slopes, and creating more detailed models of how a tsunami could affect Geneva today, would provide a more accurate assessment of whether or not this is something the lakeside city should be concerned about.
sentences.zh: 检验附近坡地的稳定性，并建立更详尽的模型来推演海啸在今天会如何影响日内瓦，将能更准确地评估这座湖畔城市究竟是否需要为此担忧。

sentences.en: (H) Most tsunamis occur in oceans and are generated by earthquakes.
sentences.zh: 大多数海啸发生在海洋中，由地震引发。

sentences.en: However, the study is a reminder that even a landlocked nation like Switzerland is not immune to catastrophic waves.
sentences.zh: 然而，这项研究提醒人们，即便是瑞士这样一个内陆国家，也并非不会遭受灾难性巨浪的侵袭。

sentences.en: (A) In 1818 a whale became the subject of a controversial court case in New York City.
sentences.zh: 1818年，一头鲸鱼成了纽约市一桩争议性诉讼案的主角。

sentences.en: The case involved an old law requiring those who sold fish oil to pay a fee in order to have their barrels inspected by city officials, and certified.
sentences.zh: 此案涉及一条旧法律，该法律要求出售鱼油的人缴纳一笔费用，以便由市政官员检验其油桶并予以认证。

sentences.en: However, an oil merchant named Samuel Judd refused to pay the inspection fee on three barrels of oil, claiming that no inspection was necessary because it was whale oil, and whales were not fish.
sentences.zh: 然而，一位名叫塞缪尔·贾德的油商拒绝为三桶油缴纳检验费，声称无需检验，因为那是鲸油，而鲸鱼并不是鱼。

sentences.en: The state disagreed, and so a date was set for a court to decide not a point of law, but the answer to a more fundamental question: is a whale a fish?
sentences.zh: 州方不同意，于是法院定下日期，要裁决的不是一个法律问题，而是一个更根本问题的答案：鲸鱼是鱼吗？

sentences.en: (B) As simple as that question may appear today, the answer was far from obvious in the early nineteenth century.
sentences.zh: 这个问题在今天看来或许十分简单，但在19世纪初，答案却远非显而易见。

sentences.en: Indeed, the public debate in New York sparked off by the trial was sensational.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这场审判在纽约引发的公众辩论轰动一时。

sentences.en: At stake was nothing less than what most regarded as the order of nature.
sentences.zh: 事关重大，所牵涉的不外乎是大多数人所认定的自然秩序。

sentences.en: According to the commonly accepted scheme of things, if an animal was not a beast or a bird, it was a fish, regardless of whether it breathed air or suckled its young.
sentences.zh: 按照当时普遍接受的观念体系，一种动物只要不是走兽或飞禽，就是鱼，无论它是否呼吸空气、是否哺乳幼崽。

sentences.en: For as long as anyone could remember, all non-human creatures had been organised according to the categories of birds, beasts and fish.
sentences.zh: 在人们的记忆所及，所有非人类的生物一直都是按照飞禽、走兽和鱼这几类来划分的。

sentences.en: For the average person the answer seemed perfectly obvious: whales swam in the sea and therefore they were fish.
sentences.zh: 对普通人来说，答案似乎再明显不过：鲸鱼在海里游，所以它们就是鱼。

sentences.en: (C) Against this traditional framework stood the new Linnaean system of classification, which sought to introduce more scientific values into the classification of living things.
sentences.zh: 与这一传统框架相对立的，是新的林奈分类系统，它力图把更多科学的标准引入对生物的分类之中。

sentences.en: Barely half a century old in 1818, the Linnaean system controversially classified whales as mammals because they shared two mammalian characteristics: they were warm-blooded and breathed air.
sentences.zh: 到1818年，林奈系统问世还不到半个世纪，它颇有争议地把鲸鱼归为哺乳动物，因为鲸鱼具备两项哺乳动物的特征：温血和呼吸空气。

sentences.en: (D) So the trial began in December 1818.
sentences.zh: 于是，审判于1818年12月开始。

sentences.en: Judd’s defence lawyers chose as their star witness one of New York’s most prominent figures, the congressman Samuel Mitchill.
sentences.zh: 贾德的辩护律师挑选了纽约最显赫的人物之一——国会议员塞缪尔·米切尔——作为他们的明星证人。

sentences.en: Referred to as a ‘living encyclopaedia’ and a ‘walking library’, Mitchill was a renowned natural history lecturer at the college of Physicians and Surgeons who liked to dare his students to test his knowledge of the natural world.
sentences.zh: 米切尔被称为“活百科全书”和“行走的图书馆”，是内外科医学院一位著名的博物学讲师，他喜欢激将学生来考验自己对自然界的知识。

sentences.en: ‘Show me the fin, and I will name the fish,’ he boasted.
sentences.zh: “把鱼鳍指给我看，我就能说出那是什么鱼，”他夸口道。

sentences.en: Scientifically, it was an open-and-shut case, and Judd’s defence lawyers believed they only had to do one simple thing to win the trial: insist that it be decided by biology alone.
sentences.zh: 从科学上讲，这是一桩一目了然、毫无悬念的案子，贾德的辩护律师相信，他们只需做一件简单的事就能赢得审判：坚持此案仅凭生物学来裁决。

sentences.en: Mitchill seemed fully qualified for this role.
sentences.zh: 米切尔似乎完全胜任这一角色。

sentences.en: (E) But this is where the case becomes interesting, and is the reason why the trial of the whale is not some dusty nineteenth-century obscurity.
sentences.zh: 但正是在这里，此案变得耐人寻味，这也是这场鲸鱼审判并非某桩落满尘埃、湮没无闻的19世纪旧案的原因。

sentences.en: For rather than debate Mitchill on his area of expertise, lawyers for the New York City fish-oil inspectors chose a different tack.
sentences.zh: 因为纽约市鱼油检验官一方的律师，没有就米切尔的专业领域与他争辩，而是另辟蹊径。

sentences.en: Lead counsel William Sampson turned the trial into a contest between scientific learning and common sense, by asking plain-spoken whalers to make their case before the jury.
sentences.zh: 首席律师威廉·桑普森请来言谈质朴的捕鲸人在陪审团面前陈词，把这场审判变成了一场科学学识与常识之间的较量。

sentences.en: (F) The crux of Sampson’s case was the trial’s implication with regard to humans, should Judd be found not guilty.
sentences.zh: 桑普森一方论点的关键，在于一旦贾德被判无罪，这场审判对于人类意味着什么。

sentences.en: Sampson told jury members that if they accepted Mitchill’s testimony on whales, they were obliged to accept a lower place for their own kind in the natural order.
sentences.zh: 桑普森告诉陪审团成员，如果他们接受米切尔关于鲸鱼的证词，就不得不接受人类自身在自然秩序中处于一个更低的位置。

sentences.en: As a result, Mitchill’s day in court did not go smoothly, not least because he was forced to acknowledge serious disputes among his peers regarding exactly how to classify biological organisms.
sentences.zh: 结果，米切尔的出庭并不顺利，尤其是因为他被迫承认，在究竟该如何对生物体进行分类的问题上，他的同行之间存在严重的分歧。

sentences.en: Sampson then took aim at Mitchill himself and what he represented: privileged aristocrats from the scientific community who had lost touch with reality.
sentences.zh: 桑普森随后把矛头对准了米切尔本人以及他所代表的群体：那些脱离现实、享有特权的科学界精英。

sentences.en: The smooth-talking Sampson then claimed Mitchill’s beliefs had their origin in Europe – something he rightly judged would infuriate the citizens of always-independent New York.
sentences.zh: 能言善辩的桑普森接着声称，米切尔的观念源自欧洲——他正确地判断到，这一点会激怒一向独立自主的纽约市民。

sentences.en: This revolutionary new thinking Sampson claimed, was something that honest working New Yorkers could do without.
sentences.zh: 桑普森声称，这种革命性的新思想，是诚实劳作的纽约人完全可以不要的东西。

sentences.en: No longer was this a case about barrels of oil but the proper place of scientific knowledge in the U.S.A.
sentences.zh: 此案不再是关于几桶油，而是关于科学知识在美国应有的位置。

sentences.en: (G) Ultimately, what won the case for Samuel Judd were not Mitchill’s scientific arguments, but testimony from a different sphere altogether.
sentences.zh: 最终，为塞缪尔·贾德赢得此案的，并不是米切尔的科学论证，而是来自一个截然不同领域的证词。

sentences.en: In New York’s markets, the merchants implicitly understood that whale oil and fish oil were not the same: whale oil could be used as a fuel for lamps because it could be burned without giving off smoke; fish oil, on the other hand, was nasty, impure stuff used primarily in tanning leather.
sentences.zh: 在纽约的市场上，商人们心照不宣地懂得，鲸油和鱼油并不是一回事：鲸油可以用作灯的燃料，因为它燃烧时不冒烟；鱼油则是一种气味难闻、不纯净的东西，主要用于鞣制皮革。

sentences.en: In the end it was this testimony that led to Judd’s victory.
sentences.zh: 最终，正是这一证词使贾德获得了胜诉。

sentences.en: (H) The trial of the whale still has relevance today, when the court of public opinion remains easily swayed by sceptics.
sentences.zh: 这场鲸鱼审判在今天仍有现实意义，因为舆论的法庭依然容易被怀疑论者所左右。

sentences.en: The 1818 trial was really about this question: who gets to decide on the place of the natural world in the human world – scientific experts or public opinion?
sentences.zh: 1818年的这场审判，真正要问的是这样一个问题：究竟由谁来裁定自然界在人类世界中的位置——是科学专家，还是公众舆论？

sentences.en: Whether the issue today is the effects of human activity on the climate of this planet, or one of many other contemporary topics, the legacy of Judd’s case continues to be of relevance.
sentences.zh: 无论今天的议题是人类活动对地球气候的影响，还是当代众多其他话题之一，贾德这桩案子留下的影响都依然具有现实意义。

sentences.en: A The term ‘graffiti’ derives from the Italian word graffio meaning ‘scratching’, and can be defined as uninvited markings or writing scratched or applied to objects, built structures, and natural features.
sentences.zh: “涂鸦”一词源自意大利语单词graffio，意为“刮擦”，可定义为在物件、建筑结构和自然景物上刮划或施加的、未经允许的痕迹或文字。

sentences.en: It is not a new phenomenon; examples can be found on ancient structures around the world, in some cases predating the Greeks and Romans.
sentences.zh: 这并不是一种新现象；世界各地的古代建筑上都能找到例子，有些甚至早于希腊人和罗马人。

sentences.en: In such circumstances, it has acquired invaluable historical and archaeological significance as it provides a social history of life and events at that time.
sentences.zh: 在那样的情形下，它具有了无可估量的历史与考古价值，因为它提供了当时生活与事件的一部社会史。

sentences.en: This is not true of more recent graffiti, which has become a pervasive problem particularly over the last 50 years, as a result of the availability of cheap and quick means of mark-making.
sentences.zh: 对于较晚近的涂鸦却并非如此，由于出现了廉价而快捷的留痕手段，它在过去50年里尤其成了一个无处不在的难题。

sentences.en: These include the ubiquitous spray paints.
sentences.zh: 这些手段包括随处可见的喷漆。

sentences.en: B Graffitists, the people who are responsible for creating graffiti, are indiscriminate about the surfaces they choose.
sentences.zh: 涂鸦者，即制造涂鸦的人，对自己所选的表面毫不挑剔。

sentences.en: Wherever graffiti appears, it is usually considered a priority to remove it as quickly as possible.
sentences.zh: 无论涂鸦出现在哪里，通常都被认为应当尽快清除，这是头等大事。

sentences.en: One reason for this is to prevent ‘copy-cat’ emulation, which can occur rapidly once a clean surface is defaced, and so many companies and councils have a policy of removing graffiti within an hour or two of it being reported.
sentences.zh: 原因之一是要防止“模仿者”的效仿，一旦一个干净的表面被弄脏，这种效仿就可能迅速发生，因此许多公司和议会都有一项政策，即在涂鸦被举报后的一两个小时内将其清除。

sentences.en: Another reason is that as paints, glues, and inks dry out, they can become increasingly difficult to remove.
sentences.zh: 另一个原因是，随着颜料、胶水和墨水的干涸，它们可能变得越来越难以清除。

sentences.en: A more important factor, however, is that graffiti can lead to more serious forms of vandalism and, ultimately, to the deterioration of a neighborhood area, and in this way contributes to a general social decline.
sentences.zh: 然而，一个更重要的因素在于，涂鸦可能导致更严重的破坏行为，并最终导致一个街区的衰败，从而助长一种普遍的社会衰退。

sentences.en: For this reason, the police like to be notified of new graffiti incidents.
sentences.zh: 出于这个原因，警方希望新出现的涂鸦事件能被通报给他们。

sentences.en: To aid in achieving a successful prosecution, they encourage owners of properties to take photographs of any new graffiti, as there could be other related incidents occurring locally.
sentences.zh: 为了有助于成功提起诉讼，他们鼓励业主为任何新出现的涂鸦拍照，因为当地可能还有其他相关的事件发生。

sentences.en: An incidence pattern can help to identify possible culprits, as can their ‘tag’—the distinctive mark graffitists leave to show the graffiti is their work.
sentences.zh: 一种发生规律有助于查明可能的肇事者，他们的“签名标记”也是如此——那是涂鸦者留下的、用以表明涂鸦出自他们之手的独特标记。

sentences.en: C Any proposal to remove graffiti has to be carefully considered because techniques designed for robust or utilitarian surfaces may result in considerable damage to older, more historic buildings.
sentences.zh: 任何清除涂鸦的方案都必须慎重考虑，因为为坚固或实用表面设计的技术，可能会对更古老、更具历史价值的建筑造成相当大的损害。

sentences.en: Consequently, as no two sites are the same, there is no one treatment which will be suitable for all situations; each site must be looked at individually.
sentences.zh: 因此，由于没有两处场地是完全相同的，也就没有哪一种处理方法适用于一切情形；每一处场地都必须单独加以审视。

sentences.en: The owners of some graffiti-affected sites may wish to attempt their own treatment, whereas others may prefer to contact a specialist contractor.
sentences.zh: 某些受涂鸦影响场地的业主，也许想自行尝试处理，而另一些人则可能更愿意联系专业的承包商。

sentences.en: However, whichever course is decided on, it is important to follow a systematic approach.
sentences.zh: 然而，无论决定采取哪种做法，重要的是要遵循一套有条理的方法。

sentences.en: The first step is to carry out cleaning trials to see which method is suitable for the removal of the graffiti media used, and also which method has the least impact on the site surface.
sentences.zh: 第一步是进行清洗试验，看看哪种方法适合清除所用的涂鸦媒材，以及哪种方法对场地表面的影响最小。

sentences.en: These trials should be carried out on a small unobtrusive area if possible and should always start with the least aggressive cleaning method, usually water, and stop once a successful method has been found.
sentences.zh: 这些试验应尽可能在一小块不显眼的区域上进行，并且总应从最温和的清洗方法——通常是水——开始，一旦找到一种行之有效的方法就停下来。

sentences.en: D Apart from water, a variety of methods can be used to remove graffiti; broadly, these are divided into chemical and mechanical systems.
sentences.zh: 除了水之外，还可以用多种方法来清除涂鸦；大体上，这些方法分为化学法和机械法两类。

sentences.en: When using either of these systems, care must be taken with regard to protecting both passers-by and the person carrying out the graffiti removal.
sentences.zh: 在使用这两类方法中的任何一种时，都必须注意保护过往行人和清除涂鸦的操作者。

sentences.en: Chemical preparations are based on dissolving the graffiti media; these solvents can range from mild to potentially dangerous chemical ‘cocktails’.
sentences.zh: 化学制剂的原理是溶解涂鸦媒材；这些溶剂的性质从温和到具有潜在危险的化学“鸡尾酒”不等。

sentences.en: When using chemicals, it is important to wear protective clothing, take measures to minimize any run-off of potentially harmful chemicals, and avoid the drifting of aerial mists.
sentences.zh: 在使用化学品时，重要的是要穿戴防护服，采取措施尽量减少潜在有害化学品的流淌，并避免空气中的雾气飘散。

sentences.en: Mechanical systems are often in the form of wire-brushing and grit blasting, which attempt to chip off the graffiti media.
sentences.zh: 机械法往往采取钢丝刷擦和喷砂的形式，试图把涂鸦媒材剥落下来。

sentences.en: Operators of mechanical systems must also wear protective clothing to avoid being hurt by hard airborne particles.
sentences.zh: 机械法的操作者也必须穿戴防护服，以免被空气中坚硬的颗粒所伤。

sentences.en: This method often leaves marks on a surface.
sentences.zh: 这种方法往往会在表面留下痕迹。

sentences.en: E Different measures can be adopted to combat a recurring problem of graffiti.
sentences.zh: 可以采取不同的措施来对付涂鸦反复出现的问题。

sentences.en: It is clear that protection measures will ultimately be more successful and less damaging than multiple removal treatments.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，防护措施最终会比多次的清除处理更见成效，造成的损害也更小。

sentences.en: Popular places for graffiti are often readily accessible flat surfaces where the graffiti will have an instant impact, but this is not always the case, and graffitists may scale bridges to give their work greater prominence.
sentences.zh: 涂鸦常见的地方往往是容易接近的平整表面，涂鸦在那里能立刻产生影响，但情况并不总是如此，涂鸦者也可能攀上桥梁，让自己的作品更加醒目。

sentences.en: Possible protection measures may include a combination of floodlighting to illuminate dark areas and surveillance systems such as closed-circuit television.
sentences.zh: 可行的防护措施可能包括把照亮黑暗区域的泛光照明与闭路电视等监控系统结合起来。

sentences.en: Research has shown that prominently placed cameras can reduce the incidence of graffiti in areas with a recurring problem.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，在显眼位置安装的摄像头，能够降低问题反复出现地区涂鸦的发生率。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, the cost of any of these measures may be too high, and so physical obstacles such as fences, railings, doors, or gates can be introduced to discourage unauthorized access, though in some cases, these obstacles simply provide a new surface for graffiti.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，上述任何一种措施的成本都可能过高，因此可以设置围栏、栏杆、门或大门之类的实体障碍，以阻止未经许可的进入，不过在某些情况下，这些障碍只是为涂鸦提供了一个新的表面。

sentences.en: F Another strategy is to apply a removable anti-graffiti barrier-coating as a form of preventive measure.
sentences.zh: 另一种策略是涂上一层可去除的防涂鸦隔离涂层，作为一种预防手段。

sentences.en: Although this will not stop graffiti being applied, it will make its removal much easier and usually only involves using water, which reduces the possibility of damage to the site surface.
sentences.zh: 尽管这并不能阻止涂鸦被画上去，但它会让清除涂鸦容易得多，通常只需用水，从而降低了损坏场地表面的可能性。

sentences.en: Barrier coatings are usually applied by brush or spray, leaving a thin veneer that essentially serves to isolate the graffiti from the surface.
sentences.zh: 隔离涂层通常用刷涂或喷涂的方式施加，留下一层薄薄的面层，其作用基本上是把涂鸦与表面隔开。

sentences.en: So, although there is no prescription for dealing with every graffiti incident, there are some steps that can be taken to minimize the impact of graffiti and to protect vulnerable surfaces.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管没有一套现成的办法能应对每一起涂鸦事件，但确实有一些步骤可以采取，以尽量减小涂鸦的影响并保护脆弱的表面。

sentences.en: (A) There really is no such thing as art, only artists.
sentences.zh: 其实根本不存在艺术这种东西，只有艺术家。

sentences.en: Once these were people who took coloured earth and roughed out the forms of a bison on the wall of a cave; today some buy their paints, and others design posters for hoardings; they did and do many other things.
sentences.zh: 从前，这些人取来彩色的泥土、在洞穴的墙上粗略勾出一头野牛的形状；如今，有些人买来颜料，另一些人为广告牌设计海报；他们过去和现在都做着许多其他的事。

sentences.en: There is no harm in calling all these activities art as long as we keep in mind that such a word may mean very different things in different times and places, and as long as we realize that Art with a capital A has no existence: it has become something of an obsession.
sentences.zh: 把所有这些活动都称为艺术并无害处，只要我们记住这样一个词在不同的时间和地点可能意味着非常不同的东西，并且只要我们认识到大写A的“艺术”并不存在：它已经变成了某种执念。

sentences.en: You may crush an artist by telling him that what he has just done may be quite good in its own way, only it is not true art.
sentences.zh: 你可以这样来打击一位艺术家：告诉他，他刚刚所做的就其自身而言也许相当不错，只是它不是真正的艺术。

sentences.en: (B) Actually, I do not think that there are any wrong reasons for liking a statue or a picture.
sentences.zh: 其实，我不认为喜欢一座雕像或一幅画有什么错误的理由。

sentences.en: We may like a painting of a village scene because it reminds us of home.
sentences.zh: 我们可能喜欢一幅乡村景色的画，因为它让我们想起家。

sentences.en: There is nothing wrong with that.
sentences.zh: 那并没有什么错。

sentences.en: All of us, when we see a painting, are bound to be reminded of a hundred-and-one things which influence our likes and dislikes.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人在看到一幅画时，都必然会被勾起千百样影响我们好恶的东西。

sentences.en: As long as these memories help us to enjoy what we see, we need not worry.
sentences.zh: 只要这些记忆帮助我们享受所看到的东西，我们就不必担心。

sentences.en: (C) It is only when some irrelevant memory makes us prejudiced, when we instinctively turn away from a magnificent picture of an alpine scene because we dislike climbing, that we should search our mind for the reason for the aversion which spoils a pleasure we might otherwise have had.
sentences.zh: 只有当某种无关的记忆使我们产生偏见时，当我们因为不喜欢爬山而本能地从一幅壮丽的高山风景画前转身离开时，我们才应该在心里寻找这种厌恶的原因，正是它破坏了我们本可以拥有的一种愉悦。

sentences.en: There are wrong reasons for disliking a work of art.
sentences.zh: 确实有一些不喜欢一件艺术作品的错误理由。

sentences.en: (D) Most people like to see in pictures what they would also like to see in reality.
sentences.zh: 大多数人喜欢在画中看到他们在现实中也愿意看到的东西。

sentences.en: This is quite a natural preference.
sentences.zh: 这是一种相当自然的偏好。

sentences.en: We all like beauty in nature, and are grateful to the artists who have preserved it in their works.
sentences.zh: 我们都喜爱自然中的美，并感激那些在作品中把它保存下来的艺术家。

sentences.en: Nor would these artists themselves have rebuffed us for our taste.
sentences.zh: 这些艺术家自己也不会因为我们的品味而斥责我们。

sentences.en: When the great Flemish painter Rubens made a drawing of his young son, he was surely proud of his good looks, and wanted us, too, to delight in the child's appearance.
sentences.zh: 当伟大的佛兰德斯画家鲁本斯为他年幼的儿子画一幅素描时，他一定为孩子的俊美而自豪，并希望我们也为这孩子的容貌而欣喜。

sentences.en: But this bias for the pretty and engaging subject is apt to become a stumbling block if it leads us to reject works which represent a less appealing subject.
sentences.zh: 但这种对漂亮、讨喜题材的偏好，如果它使我们拒绝那些表现不那么吸引人题材的作品，就容易成为一块绊脚石。

sentences.en: (E) The great German painter Dürer certainly drew his mother with as much devotion and love as Rubens felt for his child.
sentences.zh: 伟大的德国画家丢勒画他母亲时，所怀的虔敬和爱当然不亚于鲁本斯对他孩子的感情。

sentences.en: His truthful study of old age may give us a shock which makes us turn away from it - and yet, if we fight against that first reaction we may be richly rewarded.
sentences.zh: 他对老年真实的描摹可能给我们一种冲击，使我们从它面前转身离开——然而，如果我们对抗那第一反应，我们可能会得到丰厚的回报。

sentences.en: For Dürer's drawing in its tremendous sincerity is a great work.
sentences.zh: 因为丢勒这幅素描以其巨大的真诚而成为一件伟大的作品。

sentences.en: The beauty of a picture does not really lie in the beauty of its subject matter.
sentences.zh: 一幅画的美其实并不在于其题材的美。

sentences.en: The trouble about beauty is that tastes and standards of what is beautiful vary so much.
sentences.zh: 关于美的麻烦在于，对什么是美的品味和标准差异如此之大。

sentences.en: (F) What is true of beauty is also true of facial expression.
sentences.zh: 对美而言为真的东西，对面部表情而言也为真。

sentences.en: In fact, it is often the expression of a figure in the painting which makes us like or loathe the work.
sentences.zh: 事实上，往往正是画中一个人物的表情使我们喜欢或厌恶这件作品。

sentences.en: Some people like an expression - perhaps of suffering or of compassion - which they can readily understand, and which therefore moves them profoundly.
sentences.zh: 有些人喜欢一种表情——也许是痛苦或同情的表情——他们能轻易理解、因而深受感动。

sentences.en: But we should not, for that reason, turn away from works whose expression is perhaps less easy to understand.
sentences.zh: 但我们不应因此而从那些表情也许不那么容易理解的作品前转身离开。

sentences.en: Often we must first learn to know the artist's methods of drawing to understand the feelings he or she wishes to portray, and may even come to prefer works of art in which expression is not obvious.
sentences.zh: 我们往往必须先学会了解艺术家的绘画方法，才能理解他或她希望描绘的情感，甚至可能逐渐偏爱那些表情并不一目了然的艺术作品。

sentences.en: Just as some of us would rather people use few words and gestures and leave something to be guessed, so some of us would rather look at paintings or sculptures which are open to interpretation.
sentences.zh: 正如我们当中有些人宁愿别人少用言语和手势、留点东西让人去猜，我们当中有些人也宁愿去看那些有待解读的绘画或雕塑。

sentences.en: (G) But here newcomers to art are often brought up against another difficulty.
sentences.zh: 但在这里，艺术的新手常常撞上另一个难题。

sentences.en: They want to admire the artist's skill in representing the things they see.
sentences.zh: 他们想钦佩艺术家在表现他们所见事物时的技艺。

sentences.en: What they like best are paintings which 'look real'.
sentences.zh: 他们最喜欢的是那些“看起来真实”的画。

sentences.en: This is an important consideration, and the patience and skill which go into the faithful rendering of the visible world are indeed to be admired.
sentences.zh: 这是一个重要的考量，而那种投入到对可见世界忠实再现中的耐心和技艺确实值得钦佩。

sentences.en: Great artists of the past have devoted much labour to works in which every tiny detail is carefully recorded.
sentences.zh: 过去伟大的艺术家为那些每一个微小细节都被仔细记录的作品付出了大量的劳作。

sentences.en: Dürer's watercolour study of a hare is one of the most famous examples of this loving patience.
sentences.zh: 丢勒画野兔的水彩习作就是这种充满爱意之耐心最著名的例子之一。

sentences.en: But who would say that Rembrandt's drawing of an elephant is necessarily less good because it shows fewer details?
sentences.zh: 但谁会说伦勃朗画大象的素描就一定因为它显示的细节更少而不那么好呢？

sentences.en: Indeed Rembrandt gave us the feel of the elephant's wrinkly skin with just a few lines of his chalk.
sentences.zh: 的确，伦勃朗仅用几笔粉笔就让我们感受到了大象那布满皱纹的皮肤。

sentences.en: (H) If we find fault with the accuracy of a picture, we must remember that artists may have their reasons for changing the appearance of what they see.
sentences.zh: 如果我们挑剔一幅画准确性上的毛病，我们必须记住，艺术家可能有他们的理由去改变他们所见之物的外观。

sentences.en: We should also never condemn a work for being incorrectly drawn unless we are quite sure that we are right and the painter is wrong.
sentences.zh: 我们也绝不应该谴责一件作品画得不正确，除非我们十分确定是我们对、而画家错。

sentences.en: We have a curious habit of thinking that nature must always look like the pictures we are accustomed to.
sentences.zh: 我们有一种奇怪的习惯，认为自然必定总是看起来像我们所习惯的那些画。

sentences.en: For generations, paintings showed horses galloping with outstretched legs in full flight through the air, and we came to believe that this was indeed how they moved.
sentences.zh: 世世代代，绘画都把马画成伸展着腿、全速凌空飞奔的样子，而我们逐渐相信马奔跑时确实就是这样。

sentences.en: It was only the development of photography which proved that horses simply do not gallop in that way.
sentences.zh: 正是摄影的发展才证明了马根本不是那样奔驰的。

sentences.en: And yet, when painters began to apply this new discovery, and painted horses moving as they actually do, everyone complained that their pictures looked wrong.
sentences.zh: 然而，当画家们开始应用这一新发现、把马画成它们实际奔跑的样子时，每个人都抱怨说他们的画看起来不对。

sentences.en: A We run risks.
sentences.zh: 我们承担风险。

sentences.en: Most of the time we ignore them; sometimes we stop and decide how to deal with them.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候我们忽视它们；有时我们停下来、决定如何应对它们。

sentences.en: That’s life.
sentences.zh: 这就是人生。

sentences.en: Risks arise in sports, in business, in personal relationships; they are present in the laboratory, in political calculations, everywhere.
sentences.zh: 风险出现在体育、商业、个人关系中；它们存在于实验室、政治盘算、以及任何地方。

sentences.en: Acting individually, we often prefer to gain some benefit by accepting some danger.
sentences.zh: 作为个体行动时，我们往往倾向于通过接受某些危险来获得某些好处。

sentences.en: Acting collectively, we make similar trade-offs.
sentences.zh: 作为集体行动时，我们做出类似的权衡。

sentences.en: B When society must assess risks, and those risks can be clarified, at least in part, by science, technology or mathematics, the responsibility of the research community is to be clear and complete.
sentences.zh: 当社会必须评估风险、而这些风险至少能部分地由科学、技术或数学来澄清时，研究界的责任就是做到清晰而完整。

sentences.en: But that is not always so easy.
sentences.zh: 但那并不总是那么容易。

sentences.en: Furthermore, too few people pay full attention to the best evidence, much less modify their behaviors as a result.
sentences.zh: 此外，太少有人充分关注最好的证据，更不用说因此改变他们的行为了。

sentences.en: Even when the evidence of high risk is clear – about smoking, for instance – many will deny the risk, or dispute it, or accept that it exists and still go ahead.
sentences.zh: 即便高风险的证据很清楚——比如关于吸烟——许多人也会否认这种风险、或对它提出异议、或承认它存在却仍然一意孤行。

sentences.en: As a former cigarette smoker, I understand denial.
sentences.zh: 作为一个曾经吸烟的人，我理解这种否认。

sentences.en: C Perhaps more important than the basic facts of risk are the varied perception of it.
sentences.zh: 也许比风险的基本事实更重要的，是对它各种各样的感知。

sentences.en: Hearing the prediction of 60% chance of rain, or recognizing the minuscule likelihood of becoming ill from a flu shot, most people understand the right responses: take your umbrella and get your flu shot.
sentences.zh: 听到60%的降雨概率的预测、或认识到打了流感疫苗后生病的微乎其微的可能性，大多数人都明白正确的应对：带上你的伞、去打你的流感疫苗。

sentences.en: But some, fearfully but irrationally, go to the extreme and stay at home and avoid all contact with other people.
sentences.zh: 但有些人，出于恐惧却不理性地，走向极端，待在家里、避免与其他任何人接触。

sentences.en: Irrational decisions occasionally affect us all.
sentences.zh: 不理性的决定偶尔会影响我们所有人。

sentences.en: When it comes to risks the best odds do not always influence people to make the correct decision.
sentences.zh: 说到风险，最好的几率并不总能促使人们做出正确的决定。

sentences.en: People will risk a lot to prevent a loss, she notes; some people will rush into a burning building to save a pet.

sentences.en: E Organizations face the same hurdles whenever they must cope with major shifts in policy.
