sentences.en: Such a period of change in the outside world is filled with danger, Grove notes, precisely because it is so easy for executives to try to disregard it or misinterpret the mounting evidence showing the profound risks of not making change at the very core.
sentences.zh: 格罗夫指出，外部世界这样一段变化时期充满危险，恰恰因为高管很容易试图无视它、或误读那不断积累、显示出不在最核心处做出改变之深刻风险的证据。

sentences.en: The distinction Cole cites is instructive here: one reason management and staff may not act is that they tend to focus on the potential gains of risking change (which they characterize as small), rather than on the catastrophic losses that risking change could prevent.
sentences.zh: 科尔所引用的区别在这里很有启发：管理层和员工之所以可能不行动，一个原因是他们往往聚焦于冒险求变的潜在收获（他们把它形容为很小），而不是聚焦于冒险求变本可以防止的灾难性损失。

sentences.en: The period becomes critical for a company, according to Grove, and deadly when unattended to.
sentences.zh: 据格罗夫说，这段时期对一家公司变得至关重要，而在被忽视时则是致命的。

sentences.en: F Likewise, at the national level, and even the global one, institutions tend to be more willing to take a risk if it means avoiding a loss, than they are if it might confer a gain.
sentences.zh: 同样，在国家层面、乃至全球层面，机构往往更愿意承担一种意味着避免损失的风险，而不是一种可能带来收益的风险。

sentences.en: Almost everyone, for instance, sees the signs of ecological decay.

sentences.en: Lifset’s article, ‘Full Accounting’, describes newly developed techniques for clarifying which critical decision would have the highest pay-offs for the environment.
sentences.zh: 利夫塞特的文章《全面核算》描述了一些新开发的技术，用于澄清哪个关键决定会为环境带来最高的回报。

sentences.en: Once these ‘leverage points’ as he calls them, are located, many environmental organizations will be willing to risk the resources needed to prevent further deterioration.
sentences.zh: 他把这些称为“杠杆点”，一旦它们被找到，许多环保组织就会愿意投入防止进一步恶化所需的资源去冒险。

sentences.en: G More complicated are decisions by nations to invest broadly in educational research.
sentences.zh: 更复杂的是各国广泛投资教育研究的决定。

sentences.en: Some governmental leaders are oblivious to the risks posed by social underinvestment, because the urgent needs of the present take precedence over actions that would give rise to even more substantial gains in the future.
sentences.zh: 一些政府领导人对社会投资不足所带来的风险视而不见，因为当前迫切的需求优先于那些会在未来带来更可观收益的行动。

sentences.en: Their attitude is that today’s risks must be manageable, and that tomorrow’s gains are at the very least difficult to measure.
sentences.zh: 他们的态度是，今天的风险必须是可管理的，而明天的收益至少是难以衡量的。

sentences.en: Better consideration and decision making for what lies ahead is essential.
sentences.zh: 对前方之事更好的考量和决策是必不可少的。

sentences.en: H Nevertheless, I confess to being an optimist.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，我承认自己是个乐观主义者。

sentences.en: My glass is generally half full – though that may not help me handle risk.

sentences.en: Whether one’s temperament is optimistic or pessimistic, everyone in our scientific and engineering community has a social responsibility: measure with care and portray with honesty the level of risk involved in any action or decision.
sentences.zh: 无论一个人的性情是乐观还是悲观，我们科学和工程界的每一个人都有一项社会责任：谨慎地衡量、诚实地描绘任何行动或决定所涉及的风险水平。

records.title: Let's teach them how to teach
records.titleZh: 让我们教他们如何教学

sentences.en: (A) Forget smart uniforms and small classes.
sentences.zh: 别再纠结于漂亮的校服和小班教学。

sentences.en: The secret to stellar grades and thriving students is teachers.
sentences.zh: 优异成绩与学生茁壮成长的秘诀在于教师。

sentences.en: One US study found that in a single year’s teaching the top 10% of teachers impart three times as much learning to their pupils as the worst 10% do.
sentences.zh: 美国一项研究发现，在一学年的教学中，排名前10%的教师传授给学生的知识，是排名后10%的教师的三倍。

sentences.en: Another US study suggests that if black pupils were taught by the best quarter of teachers, the gap between their achievement and that of white pupils would disappear.
sentences.zh: 美国另一项研究表明，如果黑人学生由水平最高的那四分之一教师来教，他们与白人学生在成绩上的差距就会消失。

sentences.en: But efforts to ensure that every teacher can teach are hindered by the persistent myth that good teachers are born, not made.
sentences.zh: 但要确保每位教师都会教学，这类努力却受到一种根深蒂固的迷思的阻碍：好教师是天生的，而非后天造就的。

sentences.en: Government policies, which often start from the same assumption, seek to raise teaching standards by attracting high flying graduates to join the profession and prodding bad teachers to leave.
sentences.zh: 政府的各项政策往往也从同一假设出发，试图通过吸引出类拔萃的毕业生加入这一行业、并促使不称职的教师离开，来提高教学水平。

sentences.en: Teachers’ unions, meanwhile, insist that if only their members were free from centralised policies, excellence would follow.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，教师工会则坚称，只要其成员摆脱集中统一的政策束缚，卓越自会随之而来。

sentences.en: (B) The premise that teaching ability is something you either have or don’t is mistaken.
sentences.zh: “教学能力要么有、要么没有”这一前提是错误的。

sentences.en: A new breed of teacher trainers is founding a rigorous science of pedagogy.
sentences.zh: 新一代的教师培训者正在创立一门严谨的教学法科学。

sentences.en: The aim is to make ordinary teachers great, just as sports coaches help athletes of all abilities to improve their personal best.
sentences.zh: 其目标是让普通教师变得出色，正如体育教练帮助各种水平的运动员刷新个人最佳成绩一样。

sentences.en: Done right, this will revolutionise schools and change lives.
sentences.zh: 若运用得当，这将彻底变革学校，并改变人们的人生。

sentences.en: (C) Education has a history of lurching from one ‘miracle’ solution to the next.
sentences.zh: 教育历来有一种从一个“奇迹”方案踉跄奔向下一个的传统。

sentences.en: The best of them even achieve some good.
sentences.zh: 其中最好的那些方案，甚至确实带来了一些益处。

sentences.en: The US initiative Teach for America has brought energetic new graduates into the profession, and dismissing teachers for bad performance has boosted results in Washington, DC.
sentences.zh: 美国的“为美国而教”项目把精力充沛的应届毕业生带入了教师行业，而因表现不佳而解聘教师的做法，则提升了华盛顿特区的教学成绩。

sentences.en: But each approach has its limits.
sentences.zh: 但每一种做法都有其局限。

sentences.en: Teaching is a mass profession: it cannot grab all the top graduates, year after year.
sentences.zh: 教学是一个从业人数众多的行业：它不可能年复一年地把所有顶尖毕业生都揽入麾下。

sentences.en: When poor teachers are fired, new ones are needed – and they will have come through the same educational system that failed to make fine teachers of their predecessors.
sentences.zh: 不称职的教师被解雇之后，就需要补充新教师——而这些新人也是经由同一套教育体系培养出来的，正是这套体系当初未能把他们的前任造就成优秀教师。

sentences.en: (D) By contrast, the idea of improving the average teacher could revolutionise the entire profession.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，提升普通教师水平这一思路，有可能彻底变革整个行业。

sentences.en: Around the world, few newly qualified teachers are well enough prepared for the classroom.
sentences.zh: 放眼全球，很少有新近取得资格的教师为课堂教学做好了充分准备。

sentences.en: A recent report found 31 countries in which more than a quarter of primary-school teachers had not reached minimal national standards.
sentences.zh: 最近一份报告发现，有31个国家，其四分之一以上的小学教师未达到本国的最低标准。

sentences.en: In rich countries, the problem is subtler.
sentences.zh: 在富裕国家，问题则更为微妙。

sentences.en: Teachers qualify after completing a long, specialised course, which almost always involves superficial and seemingly useless discussions of theory.
sentences.zh: 教师要在修完一门漫长而专业的课程之后才能取得资格，而这门课程几乎总是充斥着肤浅且看似无用的理论探讨。

sentences.en: Some of these courses, including master’s degrees in education, have no effect on how well their graduates’ pupils end up being taught.
sentences.zh: 这类课程中的一些——包括教育学硕士学位——对其毕业生最终把学生教得好不好，毫无影响。

sentences.en: (E) What teachers fail to learn in universities and teacher-training colleges they rarely pick up on the job.
sentences.zh: 教师在大学和师范院校未能学到的东西，他们在工作中也很少能补上。

sentences.en: They become better teachers in their first few years as they get to grips with real pupils in real classrooms, but after that improvements tail off.
sentences.zh: 在最初几年里，随着他们在真实课堂上与真实学生打交道，他们会成长为更好的教师，但此后进步便逐渐减缓。

sentences.en: This is largely because schools neglect their most important learners: teachers themselves.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上是因为，学校忽视了它们最重要的学习者：教师本身。

sentences.en: Across the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) club of mostly rich countries, two-fifths of teachers say they have never had a chance to learn by sitting in on another teacher’s lessons; nor have they been asked to give feedback on their peers.
sentences.zh: 在以富裕国家为主的经济合作与发展组织（OECD）各成员国中，五分之二的教师表示，他们从未有机会通过旁听其他教师的课来学习；也从未被要求对同行给出反馈。

sentences.en: (F) If this is to change, teachers need to learn how to impart knowledge and prepare young minds to receive and retain it.
sentences.zh: 若要改变这一状况，教师就需要学会如何传授知识，并使年轻的头脑做好接受并记住知识的准备。

sentences.en: Good teachers set clear goals, enforce high standards of behaviour and manage their lesson time wisely.
sentences.zh: 优秀的教师会设定明确的目标，严格执行高标准的行为规范，并明智地安排自己的课堂时间。

sentences.en: They use tried-and-tested instructional techniques to ensure that all brains are working all the time – for example, asking questions in the classroom with “cold calling*” rather than relying on the same eager pupils putting up their hands.
sentences.zh: 他们运用久经检验的教学技巧，确保所有人的大脑始终都在运转——例如在课堂上采用“随机点名”（cold calling*）的方式提问，而不是依赖那几个总是踊跃举手的学生。

sentences.en: (G) Like other complex skills, teaching requires a route to mastery that is not based on abstruse theory but on intense, guided practice grounded in subject-matter knowledge and pedagogical methods.
sentences.zh: 与其他复杂技能一样，教学要走向精通，所依凭的并非晦涩的理论，而是以学科知识与教学法为根基、高强度且有指导的练习。

sentences.en: Trainees should spend more time in the classroom.
sentences.zh: 受训教师应当在课堂上花更多时间。

sentences.en: The places where pupils do best – for example, Finland, Singapore and Shanghai – put novice teachers through a demanding apprenticeship.
sentences.zh: 学生表现最好的那些地方——例如芬兰、新加坡和上海——会让新手教师经历严格的学徒式训练。

sentences.en: In the US, high-performing schools teach trainees in the classroom and bring them on with coaching and feedback.
sentences.zh: 在美国，成绩优异的学校会在课堂上培养受训教师，并通过指导和反馈来帮助他们成长。

sentences.en: (H) Teacher-training institutions need to be more rigorous.
sentences.zh: 师资培训机构需要更加严格。

sentences.en: A century ago, medical schools raised the calibre of doctors by introducing systematic curriculums and providing clinical experience.
sentences.zh: 一个世纪前，医学院通过引入系统化的课程并提供临床经验，提升了医生的素质。

sentences.en: It is essential that teacher-training colleges start to collect and publish data on how their graduates perform in the classroom.
sentences.zh: 师范院校必须开始收集并公布有关其毕业生课堂表现的数据，这一点至关重要。

sentences.en: Courses that produce teachers who go on to do little to improve their pupils’ learning should not receive subsidies or see their graduates become teachers.
sentences.zh: 如果某些课程培养出的教师日后对改善学生的学习几乎毫无作用，这些课程就不应获得补贴，其毕业生也不应成为教师。

sentences.en: They would then have to improve to survive.
sentences.zh: 如此一来，它们就不得不通过改进来求得生存。

sentences.en: (I) Big changes are needed in schools, too, to ensure that teachers improve throughout their careers.
sentences.zh: 学校也需要作出重大变革，以确保教师在整个职业生涯中不断进步。

sentences.en: Teachers in the best ones hone their craft through observation and coaching.
sentences.zh: 在最好的学校里，教师通过观摩和指导来磨炼自己的技艺。

sentences.en: They accept critical feedback, which their unions should not resist but welcome, as it is only proper for people doing such an important job.
sentences.zh: 他们接受批评性的反馈；对此，他们的工会不应抵制，而应欢迎，因为对于从事如此重要工作的人来说，这本是理所应当的。

sentences.en: The best head teachers hold novices’ hands by helping them prepare high quality lessons and arranging for more-experienced teachers to cover for them when they need time for further study and practice.
sentences.zh: 最优秀的校长会悉心扶持新手教师，帮助他们备出高质量的课，并在他们需要时间深造和练习时，安排更有经验的教师代他们上课。

sentences.en: (J) Money is less important than one might think.
sentences.zh: 金钱并不像人们想象的那么重要。

sentences.en: Teachers in top-of-the-class Finland, for example, earn about the OECD average.
sentences.zh: 以名列前茅的芬兰为例，那里的教师收入大致相当于经济合作与发展组织的平均水平。

sentences.en: But ensuring the best teachers stay in the classroom will, in most places, mean paying more.
sentences.zh: 但要确保最优秀的教师留在课堂上，在大多数地方都意味着要支付更高的薪酬。

sentences.en: People who thrive in front of pupils should not have to become managers to earn a pay rise.
sentences.zh: 那些在学生面前如鱼得水的人，不应为了加薪而不得不去当管理者。

sentences.en: And more flexibility on salaries would make it much easier to attract the best teachers to the worst schools.
sentences.zh: 而在薪酬上给予更大的灵活性，会让最薄弱的学校更容易吸引到最优秀的教师。

sentences.en: (K) Improving the quality of the average teacher would raise the profession’s prestige, setting up a virtuous cycle in which more talented graduates clamoured to join.
sentences.zh: 提升普通教师的素质，会提高这一行业的声望，从而形成一种良性循环：更多有才华的毕业生争相加入。

sentences.en: But the biggest gains will come from preparing new teachers better, and upgrading the ones already in classrooms.
sentences.zh: 但最大的收益将来自更好地培养新教师，以及提升那些已经身处课堂的教师。

sentences.en: (A) Parrots are found across the tropics and in all southern hemisphere continents except Antarctica, but nowhere do they display such a richness of diversity and form as in Australia.
One-sixth of the world's 345 parrot species are found there, and Australia has long been renowned for the number and variety of its parrots.

(B) In the 16th century, the German cartographer Mercator made a world map that included a place, somewhere near present-day Australia, that he named Terra Psittacorum – the Land of Parrots – and the first European settlers in Australia often referred to the country as Parrot Land.

In 1865, the celebrated British naturalist and wildlife artist John Gould said: "No group of birds gives Australia so tropical and benign an air as the numerous species of this great family by which it is tenanted."
(C) Parrots are descendants of an ancient line.

Due to their great diversity, and since most species inhabit Africa, Australia and South America, it seems almost certain that parrots originated millions of years ago on the ancient southern continent of Gondwana, before it broke up into the separate southern hemisphere continents we know today.
Much of Gondwana comprised vast rainforests intersected by huge slow-flowing rivers and expansive lakes, but by eight million years ago, great changes were underway.

The center of the continent of Australia had begun to dry out, and the rainforests that once covered it gradually contracted to the continental margins, where, to a limited extent, they still exist today.
(D) The creatures that remained in those shrinking rainforests had to adapt to the drier conditions or face extinction.
Reacting to these desperate circumstances, the parrot family, typically found in jungles in other parts of the world, has populated some of Australia's harshest environments.

The parrots spread from ancestral forests through eucalypt woodlands to colonise the central deserts of Australia, and as a consequence they diversified into a wide range of species with adaptations that reflect the many changes animals and plants had to make to survive in these areas.
(E) These evolutionary pressures helped mould keratin, the substance from which beaks are made, into a range of tools capable of gathering the new food types favored by various species of parrot.
The size of a parrot's short, blunt beak and the length of that beak's curved upper section are related to the type of food each species eats.
Some have comparatively long beaks that are perfect for extracting seeds from fruit; Others have broader and stronger beaks that are designed for cracking hard seeds.
(F) Differently shaped beaks are not the only adaptations that have been made during the developing relationship between parrots and their food plants.

Like all of Australia's many honey-eating birds, the rainbow-coloured lorikeets and the flowers on which they feed have long co-evolved with features such as the shape and colour of the flowers adapted to the bird's particular needs.

For example, red is the most attractive colour to birds, and thus flowers which depend on birds for pollination are more often red, and lorikeets' tongues have bristles which help them to collect as much pollen as possible.
(G) Today, most of Australia's parrots inhabit woodland and open forest, and their numbers decline towards both deserts and wetter areas.
The majority are nomadic to some degree, moving around to take advantage of feeding and breeding places.
Two of the dry country parrots, the pink and grey galah and the pink, white and yellow corella, have expanded their ranges in recent years.
They are among the species that have adapted well to the changes brought about by European settlement; Forest felling created grasslands where galahs and corellas thrive.
(H) But other parrot species did not fare so well when their environments were altered.

The clearing of large areas of rainforest is probably responsible for the disappearance of the double-eyed fig parrot, and numbers of ground parrots declined when a great part of their habitat was destroyed by the draining of coastal swamps.
Even some parrot species that benefited from forest clearing at first are now confronted by a shortage of nesting sites due to further man-made changes.
(I) New conditions also sometimes favour an incoming species over one that originally inhabited the area.
For example, after farmers cleared large areas of forest on Kangaroo Island off the coast of South Australia, the island was colonised by galahs.
They were soon going down holes and destroying black cockatoo eggs in order to take the hole for their own use.
Their success precipitated a partial collapse in the black cockatoo population when the latter lost the struggle for scarce nesting hollows.
(J) There may be no final answer to ensuring an equitable balance between parrot species.

Nest box programmes help ease the shortage of nesting sites in some places, but there are not enough, they are expensive, and they are not an adequate substitute for large, old trees, such as the habitat they represent and the nectar, pollen and seeds they provide.
Competition between parrots for nest sites is a result of the changes we humans have made to the Earth.
We are the most widespread and dangerous competitors that parrots have ever had to face, but we also have the knowledge and skill to maintain the wonderfully rich diversity of Australia's parrots.
All we need is the will to do so.

records.title: The History of the Pencil V2

sentences.en: (A) Pencils have existed for millennia.
sentences.zh: 铅笔已经存在了数千年。

sentences.en: It is known that the ancient Egyptians, Greeks and Romans all used small pieces of metal as writing instruments, and that 14th-century European artists made pale grey drawings with thin rods of lead, silver or zinc.
sentences.zh: 已知古代埃及人、希腊人和罗马人都曾用小块金属作为书写工具，而 14 世纪的欧洲艺术家则用细细的铅、银或锌棒来画淡灰色的素描。

sentences.en: It is, however, generally accepted that the history of the modern pencil began in the 16th century, in the hilly, rural county of Cumberland in north-west England.
sentences.zh: 但人们普遍认为，现代铅笔的历史始于 16 世纪英格兰西北部多丘陵的乡村郡——坎伯兰郡。

sentences.en: (B) Some time before 1565, an enormous deposit of the soft, dark grey mineral now known as graphite was discovered in the Borrowdale district of the county.
sentences.zh: 在 1565 年之前的某个时间，在该郡的博罗代尔（Borrowdale）地区发现了一处大量蕴藏的软质深灰色矿物，即如今所称的石墨。

sentences.en: Then, as now, Cumberland was a farming area, and the locals found the mineral useful for marking their sheep so they could identify the ones that belonged to them.
sentences.zh: 当时和现在一样，坎伯兰郡是个农业地区，当地人发现这种矿物可用来给绵羊做标记，以便辨认哪些是自家的羊。

sentences.en: It was thought to be a form of lead, and so was referred to as plumbago, a term deriving from the Latin name for that element.
sentences.zh: 它被认为是一种铅，因此被称为 plumbago——这是源自拉丁文中表示“铅”的词。

sentences.en: However, the mineral was later identified as a form of carbon, and in 1789 the German geologist Abraham Gottlob Werner renamed it graphite, a word based on the ancient Greek grapho, meaning ‘draw’ or ‘write’.
sentences.zh: 然而，这种矿物后来被鉴定为碳的一种形式，1789 年德国地质学家亚伯拉罕·戈特洛布·维尔纳（Abraham Gottlob Werner）将其改名为石墨（graphite），这个词来自古希腊语 grapho，意为“画”或“写”。

sentences.en: (C) The graphite found at Borrowdale was extremely dense and it could easily be sawn into sticks to be used for marking, writing or drawing.
sentences.zh: 在博罗代尔发现的石墨非常致密，可以方便地锯成小条，用来做标记、写字或绘画。

sentences.en: But because graphite is also soft, it requires some form of encasement around it, and so the sticks were initially wrapped in string for stability and ease of use.
sentences.zh: 但由于石墨同时也很柔软，需要一些外层加以包裹，因此这些条最初被绳子缠裹起来，以增加稳定性和便于使用。

sentences.en: The news of the usefulness of these early pencils spread far and wide, attracting the attention of artists throughout Europe.
sentences.zh: 关于这种早期铅笔好用的消息广为流传，吸引了整个欧洲艺术家的注意。

sentences.en: (D) In England, the government soon realised the value of the Borrowdale find, particularly for national defence purposes, because graphite proved ideal for lining the moulds used in the making of cannon balls.
sentences.zh: 在英国，政府很快意识到博罗代尔这一发现的价值，尤其是从国防目的的角度，因为石墨被证明非常适合用作铸造炮弹的模具内衬。

sentences.en: The mines were therefore taken over by the government, which guarded and periodically flooded them to prevent theft.
sentences.zh: 于是矿场被政府接管，由其守卫并定期注水，以防偷盗。

sentences.en: Because of this, there were occasions when supplies for use in pencils had to be smuggled out in secret.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，有时候用于制作铅笔的石墨需要被秘密偷运出来。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, England still became the centre of a thriving pencil-making industry.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，英国仍发展成了蓬勃的制铅笔工业的中心。

sentences.en: (E) Although deposits of graphite existed in other parts of the world, they were not of the same exceptional purity and quality as Borrowdale graphite, and had to be crushed to a powder to get rid of the impurities.
sentences.zh: 尽管世界其他地区也存在石墨矿藏，但其纯度和品质都不及博罗代尔石墨那样卓越，必须被研磨成粉以去除杂质。

sentences.en: England therefore continued to enjoy a monopoly on the production of pencils until a method of reconstituting the graphite powder could be found.
sentences.zh: 因此，英国得以在铅笔生产上保持垄断，直到一种可以把石墨粉重新成型的方法被找到。

sentences.en: English pencils continued to be made with sticks cut from pure Borrowdale graphite into the 1860s, after which the design was modified.
sentences.zh: 英国铅笔一直用切自纯博罗代尔石墨的条棒制造，直至 1860 年代，此后设计才有所改变。

sentences.en: The town of Keswick, close to the Cumberland graphite find, still manufactures pencils today, the factory also being the location of the Cumberland pencil museum
sentences.zh: 靠近坎伯兰石墨矿藏的凯西克镇（Keswick）今天仍在制造铅笔，工厂里同时也是坎伯兰铅笔博物馆所在地。

sentences.en: (F) Experimentation in pencil production was widespread across Europe during the 16th and 17th centuries.
sentences.zh: 在 16 至 17 世纪间，整个欧洲都在大量尝试改进铅笔生产。

sentences.en: Around 1560, an Italian couple named Simonio and Lyndiana Bernacotti made what are probably the first blueprints for the modern, wood-encased pencil.
sentences.zh: 大约在 1560 年，一对意大利夫妇西莫尼奥与琳迪亚娜·贝尔纳科蒂（Simonio and Lyndiana Bernacotti）制作了被认为是第一份现代木壳铅笔的设计蓝图。

sentences.en: Their concept involved the hollowing out of a stick of juniper wood, and placing a stick of graphite inside.
sentences.zh: 他们的构想是把一根杜松木棒掏空，再把一段石墨条放入其中。

sentences.en: Shortly thereafter, a superior technique to that of the Bernacottis was adopted: two wooden halves were carved, a graphite stick inserted, and the halves then glued together — essentially the same method in use to this day.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，一种比贝尔纳科蒂夫妇更优的工艺被采用：把两块木材分别雕成两半，插入一根石墨条，再把两半粘合到一起——这本质上就是沿用至今的方法。

sentences.en: (G) The first attempt to manufacture graphite sticks from powdered graphite was in Nuremberg, Germany, in 1662, using a mixture of graphite together with the elements sulphur and antimony.
sentences.zh: 首次尝试用石墨粉制造石墨条，是 1662 年在德国纽伦堡进行的，使用了石墨与硫元素及锑元素的混合物。

sentences.en: (H) Today, pencils are manufactured around the world, using graphite from a number of sources.
sentences.zh: 今天的铅笔在世界各地生产，所用的石墨来自多个产地。

sentences.en: Most manufacturers use a mix of graphite and clay as the core of their pencils.
sentences.zh: 大多数制造商以石墨与黏土的混合物作为铅笔的笔芯。

sentences.en: Each of these substances is ground into a fine powder, which goes on to be cleaned in order to remove any impurities.
sentences.zh: 每种成分都被磨成细粉，再经过清洗以去除杂质。

sentences.en: After the two types of powders have been dried, they are mixed together using water.
sentences.zh: 在两种粉末干燥之后，再用水把它们混合在一起。

sentences.en: The amount of clay added to the mixture depends on how hard the pencil is intended to be — higher proportions of clay will make the pencil harder — and the amount of time spent grinding the mixture determines the quality of the core.
sentences.zh: 加入混合物中的黏土量取决于希望铅笔的硬度——黏土比例越高，铅笔越硬——而研磨混合物的时间长短则决定了笔芯的品质。

sentences.en: The graphite-clay mixture is then shaped into long sticks, and after drying these are heated in a kiln to 1,200°C.
sentences.zh: 随后，这种石墨—黏土混合物被塑成长条，干燥后在窑中加热到 1200 °C。

sentences.en: In the next step in the process, the graphite-clay sticks are immersed in melted wax, which is absorbed into the mixture and helps to make it write more smoothly.
sentences.zh: 在下一道工序中，这些石墨—黏土棒被浸入熔化的蜡中，蜡被吸入混合物内，有助于让铅笔写起来更顺滑。

sentences.en: In the next stage, the manufacturers use thin planks of cedar wood or juniper wood.
sentences.zh: 在下一阶段，制造商使用雪松木或杜松木的薄板。

sentences.en: Several long parallel grooves are cut into the planks, and the graphite-clay sticks are inserted into these.
sentences.zh: 在木板上切出若干长长的、相互平行的凹槽，再将石墨—黏土棒嵌入这些凹槽。

sentences.en: A second plank which has been prepared in the same way is then glued on top.
sentences.zh: 之后把另一块以相同方式准备好的木板粘合在顶部。

sentences.en: The whole assembly is then cut into separate pencils.
sentences.zh: 整个组合体随后被切成一支支独立的铅笔。

sentences.en: The outside may then be varnished, retaining the natural colour of the wood, or painted in different colours.
sentences.zh: 外表面可以再涂清漆，保留木材的自然色泽，或者上不同颜色的漆。

records.title: New Understanding of Giraffes in the Wild
records.titleZh: 对野生长颈鹿的新认识

sentences.en: (A) Even as the tallest animals on Earth, giraffes can be easy to overlook.
sentences.zh: 作为地球上最高的动物，长颈鹿可能也很容易被忽视。

sentences.en: Despite being a favorite in zoos, until recently almost nobody studied giraffes in the wild.
sentences.zh: 尽管它是动物园的宠儿，但直到近年来几乎没人在野外研究长颈鹿。

sentences.en: ‘When I first became interested in giraffes in 2008 and started looking through the scientific literature, I was really surprised to see how little had been done,’ said Megan Strauss, an animal researcher at the University of Minnesota, USA.
sentences.zh: “我 2008 年第一次对长颈鹿感兴趣并开始翻阅科学文献时，真的很惊讶地发现做的工作如此之少，”美国明尼苏达大学动物研究员梅根·施特劳斯（Megan Strauss）说。

sentences.en: All that is changing fast, as a growing number of researchers seek to understand the biology and complex behavior of this graceful giant in its native habitat.
sentences.zh: 这一切正在迅速改变，越来越多的研究人员正在试图理解这种优雅的庞然大物在其本土栖息地的生物学特征和复杂行为。

sentences.en: (B) Giraffes, found throughout sub-Saharan Africa, are currently classified as a single species with up to nine varieties that differ by features like head shape and whether the fur on their legs is plain or patterned.
sentences.zh: 长颈鹿分布于撒哈拉以南的非洲，目前被归为一个物种，下分多达九个变种，区别在于头形以及腿部毛色是否带花纹等特征。

sentences.en: The giraffe is listed as endangered, but researchers point to evidence that in the past 15 years, the population has fallen some 40 percent.
sentences.zh: 长颈鹿被列为濒危物种，研究人员指出有证据显示在过去 15 年里其数量下降了约 40%。

sentences.en: (C) Recent studies have allowed researchers new insights into giraffes’ social structure.
sentences.zh: 近期的研究让研究者对长颈鹿的社会结构有了新的洞察。

sentences.en: Groups of female giraffes, for example, have been found to form close friendships that can last for years.
sentences.zh: 例如，已经发现一些雌性长颈鹿群体会形成可持续多年的亲密友谊。

sentences.en: ‘We’re just at the beginnings of trying to understand this kind of behavior,’ Dr Strauss said.
sentences.zh: “我们才刚开始尝试理解这种行为，”施特劳斯博士说。

sentences.en: Female giraffes can live 20 years or more, and it makes sense they might rely on each other for clues to the best feeding grounds, help with taking care of their young, or the reduction of stress, by staying in groups.
sentences.zh: 雌性长颈鹿可以活 20 年或更久，它们可能彼此依赖以获得最佳采食地点的线索、帮助照看幼崽，或通过群居来减轻压力，这是合理的。

sentences.en: (D) Mother giraffes have displayed signs of grief after losing their young, known as calves, to lions.
sentences.zh: 长颈鹿妈妈在失去被称为 calf 的幼崽——尤其是被狮子吃掉时——表现出悲痛迹象。

sentences.en: Dr Strauss described one case in which a mother spent four days at the place where a lion had eaten her calf, refusing food, and often in the company of two other adult females.
sentences.zh: 施特劳斯博士描述了一个案例：一只母长颈鹿在狮子吃掉她幼崽的地方停留了四天，拒绝进食，常常有另外两只成年雌鹿相伴。

sentences.en: Giraffe calves are extremely vulnerable to predators, and though mothers will fight valiantly to keep their young alive — kicking forward and backward — half of all calves are killed in their first year of life.
sentences.zh: 长颈鹿幼崽极易受到捕食者侵害；尽管母鹿会奋力前后踢踏来保住幼崽性命，但所有幼崽中仍有一半会在出生后第一年死亡。

sentences.en: (E) Male giraffes, known as bulls, generally become more important with age, and older bulls display that dominance physically and behaviorally: as their neck muscles grow, the male’s posture becomes prouder and more vertical.
sentences.zh: 被称为 bull 的雄性长颈鹿一般会随着年龄增长而越发重要，而年长的公鹿在身体和行为上都展示这种支配地位：随着颈部肌肉发达，雄鹿的姿态会变得更骄傲、更竖直。

sentences.en: Recent observations show young bulls, when left on their own, mimicking their elders: head held high and neck puffed out.
sentences.zh: 近期观察表明，年幼的公鹿在独处时会模仿年长者：头高高仰起、颈部鼓起。

sentences.en: But should a dominant older bull come into view, the younger males instantly try to make themselves look small and innocent.
sentences.zh: 但一旦一头占主导地位的年长公鹿出现在视野中，年幼的雄鹿立刻试图让自己显得小而无害。

sentences.en: (F) The younger bulls have reason to fear their elders.
sentences.zh: 年幼的公鹿有理由害怕年长者。

sentences.en: Clashes have been witnessed between adults when each bull repeatedly ‘necks’ the other, using his massive neck to slam his head against his rival.
sentences.zh: 已观察到成年公鹿之间的冲突——每只公鹿都反复“以颈相搏”，用自己粗壮的脖颈把头猛撞对手。

sentences.en: One bull somehow survived with a broken neck.
sentences.zh: 曾有一只公鹿带着断颈竟然活了下来。

sentences.en: (G) The skin of a giraffe is mostly gray.
sentences.zh: 长颈鹿的皮肤大部分是灰色的。

sentences.en: The coat has dark patches separated by light hair, which serves as camouflage, allowing them to blend in with the light and shade patterns of the acacia trees from which they feed.
sentences.zh: 皮毛上有深色斑块，被浅色毛分开，起到伪装作用，让它们能融入它们采食的金合欢树的光影图案中。

sentences.en: Grazing giraffes are hard to see even a few meters away.
sentences.zh: 正在吃草的长颈鹿即便在几米外也很难被看见。

sentences.en: (H) Research indicates that giraffes also have excellent sight, can see in color and over great distances, which helps them to spot lions and keep track of each other.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，长颈鹿还有极佳的视力，能看到颜色、看到远处的物体，这有助于它们发现狮子并彼此保持联系。

sentences.en: In addition, a giraffe’s extraordinary mouth has lips and tongue that can together grasp a branch and then pluck away the leaves while avoiding thorns, almost as humans would grab with their hands.
sentences.zh: 此外，长颈鹿那张非凡的嘴——嘴唇和舌头一起——能抓住一根枝条然后扯下叶子并避开刺，几乎像人类用手抓东西一样。

sentences.en: Each day, a giraffe consumes about 30 kilograms of leaves, shoots and vines, all digested in its four-chambered stomach.
sentences.zh: 每天，一头长颈鹿会消耗约 30 公斤叶子、嫩芽和藤蔓，全部在它四室的胃里消化。

sentences.en: (I) A giraffe can stand more than six meters tall, with its neck accounting for roughly a third of its height and its legs the same.
sentences.zh: 一头长颈鹿可以站到 6 米多高，其颈部约占身高的三分之一，腿部也是。

sentences.en: The giraffe’s long neck is due to the length of the vertebrae, not the number of vertebrae.
sentences.zh: 长颈鹿的长颈来自椎骨的长度，而不是椎骨的数量。

sentences.en: The growth of the neck largely takes place during early childhood, as giraffe mothers would have a difficult time giving birth to young with longer necks.
sentences.zh: 颈部的生长主要发生在幼年早期，因为长颈鹿妈妈分娩颈更长的幼崽会很困难。

sentences.en: The giraffe’s head and neck are held up by large muscles attached to the lower spine.
sentences.zh: 长颈鹿的头颈由附着在下脊柱上的大块肌肉支撑。

sentences.en: (J) Recent studies show that the greatest challenge to a giraffe’s cardiovascular system is how to both pump blood very high and retrieve it from far below.
sentences.zh: 近期研究表明，长颈鹿心血管系统所面临的最大挑战是：如何把血液既泵得很高，又能从远处的下方收回。

sentences.en: The outside of a giraffe’s veins are extremely thick, to prevent blood leaking into surrounding tissue.
sentences.zh: 长颈鹿静脉外壁极厚，以防血液漏入周围组织。

sentences.en: Other adaptations in the cardiovascular system allow the giraffe to bend over for a drink of water, and then raise its head again quickly without fainting.
sentences.zh: 心血管系统中其他适应性使长颈鹿能弯下身喝水，然后又能迅速抬起头而不晕倒。

sentences.en: (K) Researchers were also surprised to find that a giraffe does not have an unusually large heart.
sentences.zh: 研究人员还惊讶地发现，长颈鹿并没有特别大的心脏。

sentences.en: It is half a percent of body mass, the same as in a mouse.
sentences.zh: 它占身体质量的 0.5%，与小鼠相同。

sentences.en: Moreover, the amount of blood pumped into circulation is modest, proportionally lower than it is in humans.
sentences.zh: 此外，泵入循环的血液量也并不大，按比例算比人类还少。

sentences.en: That could help explain why giraffes rarely run for very long: enough oxygen cannot be delivered to their muscles fast enough for them to keep running.
sentences.zh: 这或许可以帮助解释为什么长颈鹿很少长时间奔跑：氧气无法以足够快的速度送达肌肉以维持奔跑。

sentences.en: Or maybe the giraffes are worried about tripping over their own feet.
sentences.zh: 或者长颈鹿可能担心绊到自己的脚。

sentences.en: This is because signals from the nerves travel at about the same speed in giraffes as in rats or other mammals.
sentences.zh: 这是因为长颈鹿体内神经信号的传播速度与大鼠或其他哺乳动物大致相同。

sentences.en: Given the greater distance they have to travel in the giraffe to reach the brain, it is possible the giraffe faces real challenges in reacting quickly to a rock beneath its hoof or a bite to its ankle.
sentences.zh: 考虑到信号要传到大脑必须在长颈鹿体内走得更远，长颈鹿在对蹄下石块或脚踝被咬作出快速反应方面，可能确实面临挑战。

sentences.en: (L) New understanding of this wonderful animal sheds light on both its physiology and its behavior.
sentences.zh: 对这种神奇动物的新认识，既照亮了它的生理，也照亮了它的行为。

sentences.en: Researchers hope to use this knowledge to increase their ability to work with preservation, as its habitat is reduced and the giraffe becomes scarcer.
sentences.zh: 研究人员希望利用这些知识，在长颈鹿栖息地萎缩、长颈鹿越来越稀少的当下，增强他们开展保护工作的能力。

sentences.en: (A) The founding and development of many universities has been dependent on philanthropy*.
sentences.zh: 许多大学的创建与发展都依赖于慈善捐赠。

sentences.en: This has been true from some of the oldest universities such as Bologna, Oxford and Cambridge in the twelfth century, to relative newcomers like the universities of Harvard and Yale in the seventeenth century.
sentences.zh: 从某些最古老的大学——如 12 世纪的博洛尼亚大学、牛津大学和剑桥大学——到 17 世纪相对较新的哈佛大学和耶鲁大学，无不如此。

sentences.en: Wealthy merchants gave young institutions money, land, libraries and rare items.
sentences.zh: 富有的商人会向年轻的学府捐赠资金、土地、图书馆和珍贵物品。

sentences.en: Their belief in the value of higher learning is echoed by the growing number of philanthropists whose gifts have helped transform the University of Auckland, the largest university in New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 他们对高等教育价值的笃信，在如今越来越多的慈善家身上得到了回响——正是他们的馈赠帮助新西兰最大的大学——奥克兰大学焕然一新。

sentences.en: (B) In 1884 Mr Justice Gillies made history when he gave $3,000 to the then very young University of Auckland, and so became its original philanthropist.
sentences.zh: 1884 年，吉利斯大法官（Mr Justice Gillies）创下了历史：他向当时还非常年轻的奥克兰大学捐赠了 3000 美元，由此成为该校最早的捐赠人。

sentences.en: Gillies’ gift was more generous even than those regularly given to New Zealand’s older University of Otago, and was exceptional because Auckland had a smaller population and was less wealthy than the other university cities at that time.
sentences.zh: 吉利斯的馈赠甚至比当时人们经常给新西兰更古老的奥塔哥大学的捐款还要慷慨；而且因为奥克兰当时人口较少、富裕程度也不及其他大学城，这份捐赠尤其难得。

sentences.en: However, from the 1930s privately funded prizes and scholarships began to be seen more frequently in Auckland.
sentences.zh: 然而，自 1930 年代起，私人资助的奖项和奖学金开始在奥克兰更多地出现。

sentences.en: In that decade a local engineer and former lecturer in engineering, Samuel Crookes, launched a fund to save the engineering school in Auckland, which the state was determined to see discontinued, and raised over $6,500 in three years.
sentences.zh: 那十年间，一位本地工程师、曾任工程学讲师的塞缪尔·克鲁克斯（Samuel Crookes）发起了一项基金，挽救了奥克兰那所政府执意要停办的工程学院，三年内筹集了 6500 多美元。

sentences.en: Another significant philanthropist, Sir William Goodfellow, made his initial gift to the University in 1947—$50,000 to build the Maclaurin Chapel.
sentences.zh: 另一位重要的慈善家威廉·古德费洛爵士（Sir William Goodfellow）于 1947 年首次向该校捐赠——5 万美元用于建造麦克劳林教堂（Maclaurin Chapel）。

sentences.en: Since then, he and succeeding generations of the family have given numerous scholarships and fellowships and established a school within the University bearing the family’s name.
sentences.zh: 此后，他及其家族数代人陆续提供了大量奖学金和研究奖学金，并在校内创立了一所冠以家族姓氏的学院。

sentences.en: (C) The University had a difficult decade in the 1950s as it was short of equipment, buildings and money.
sentences.zh: 1950 年代对奥克兰大学来说是艰难的十年，设备、楼宇和资金都告匮乏。

sentences.en: It also had its first taste of international rivalry, when universities in many parts of the world competed to attract first-class lecturers.
sentences.zh: 它还首次尝到了国际竞争的滋味——当时世界许多地方的大学纷纷争夺一流讲师。

sentences.en: In Auckland the problem largely resulted from the fact that academic salaries had slipped well behind those available in Britain and Australia, so the strongest candidates tended to be recruited to those countries.
sentences.zh: 在奥克兰，问题主要源于学术薪资远远落后于英国和澳大利亚的水平，因此最强的应聘者往往被那两个国家招走。

sentences.en: But when the new Medical School opened in 1968, it attracted significant gifts for academic positions and equipment from an unusually wide range of donors, including individuals, trusts, charitable foundations, societies and community groups.
sentences.zh: 但 1968 年新医学院开办时，它吸引了来自异常广泛的捐赠者——包括个人、信托、慈善基金会、学会和社区团体——为学术职位和设备所做的大量捐赠。

sentences.en: It also became the permanent home of the Philson Library, which by then consisted of some 8,000 books.
sentences.zh: 它还成为菲尔森图书馆（Philson Library）的永久所在地，当时该馆藏书约 8000 册。

sentences.en: (D) The first of the modern public appeals for funds took place in the 1960s, when Alan Highet built the Student Union complex.
sentences.zh: 现代意义上的首次公开募款活动发生在 1960 年代，当时艾伦·海特（Alan Highet）建造了学生会综合楼。

sentences.en: This was followed by another appeal in 1983 under the then Chancellor Henry Cooper, who raised $800,000 to celebrate the University’s centenary.
sentences.zh: 1983 年又有一次募款活动，由时任校长亨利·库珀（Henry Cooper）主持，为庆祝该校百年校庆筹集了 80 万美元。

sentences.en: These modern campaigns built on the successful campaigns of the past but included a number of new features.
sentences.zh: 这些现代募款活动是在以往成功活动的基础上展开的，但加入了若干新特点。

sentences.en: There was, of course, the familiar emphasis on donations from individuals, but the modern approach also stressed the importance of bringing the University and business closer together and specifically seeking donations from that sector.
sentences.zh: 它们当然继承了对个人捐赠的传统重视，但现代做法还强调拉近大学与商界的距离，并专门面向商界寻求捐赠。

sentences.en: (E) Building on this success, the current “Leading the Way” campaign was launched.
sentences.zh: 在这种成功基础上，当前的“引领前行”（Leading the Way）募款活动应运而生。

sentences.en: It is intended as a drive to secure support for the whole University, with a focus on generating funds to recruit, support and retain the very best staff for the University.
sentences.zh: 它的目标是为整所大学争取支持，重点是筹集资金以招募、支持并留住大学最优秀的教职人员。

sentences.en: The current campaign has raised the whole process of philanthropy to a new level, and changed expectations.
sentences.zh: 当前这场募款活动把整个慈善流程提升到了一个新高度，也改变了人们的预期。

sentences.en: The University is investing considerable time and energy in devising new methods of fund-raising both within its local communities and—remembering that New Zealanders love to travel—by looking at campaigns in other parts of the world, and targeting alumni, or former students now living overseas.
sentences.zh: 该校投入大量时间和精力，在本地社区内外构思新型筹款方式——并考虑到新西兰人喜欢出国旅行，他们还把目光投向世界其他地方的募款活动，并瞄准校友——即如今居住在海外的旧校友。

sentences.en: (F) “What it taught us,” says John Taylor, Director of External Relations, “was that the campaign had to fit into the Strategic Plan of the University …
sentences.zh: “它教会我们的是，”对外关系主任约翰·泰勒（John Taylor）说，“募款活动必须契合大学的战略规划……

sentences.en: As we kept talking we realised that we could have a transformative effect on the future of New Zealand by highlighting the potential benefits of high-quality research.”
sentences.zh: 我们在不断讨论中意识到，通过凸显高质量研究的潜在效益，我们可以对新西兰的未来产生变革性的影响。“

sentences.en: The example Taylor gives is the $4.5 million gift to establish an information centre at the University’s Marine Science laboratory on the coast at Leigh.
sentences.zh: 泰勒举了一个例子：450 万美元的捐赠，用于在该校位于利伊（Leigh）海边的海洋科学实验室建立一个信息中心。

sentences.en: He stresses that the fund-raising drive was so successful in part because the publicity used at the time highlighted the public benefit from the project.
sentences.zh: 他强调，这次募款之所以如此成功，部分原因在于当时使用的宣传强调了该项目带来的公共利益。

sentences.en: (G) On the financial side, the University’s Vice-Chancellor, Stuart McCutcheon, explains that a fault they found in their campaigns actually turned out to be a stroke of good fortune.
sentences.zh: 在财务方面，该校副校长斯图尔特·麦卡岑（Stuart McCutcheon）解释说，他们在募款活动中发现的一个漏洞，结果却成了一种意外之喜。

sentences.en: “In the course of developing these new fund-raising systems,” he says, “we have come to realise that there has been considerable giving to the University that has not been previously recorded through our Advancement Office …
sentences.zh: “在开发这些新筹款系统的过程中，”他说，“我们意识到，过去一直有相当数量的捐款进入大学，但并未经过我们的发展办公室登记……

sentences.en: This has been in the order of $10 million per year over the campaign period.”
sentences.zh: 按当时这场募款活动期间的规模算，每年约 1000 万美元。“

sentences.en: The good news from this error is that at the recent Chancellor’s dinner it was announced that the campaign target was now being increased from $100 million to $150 million, and would recognise all sources of philanthropic support.
sentences.zh: 这场失误带来的好消息是：在最近一次校长晚宴上宣布，募款目标从 1 亿美元提高到 1.5 亿美元，并将涵盖所有来源的慈善支持。

sentences.en: It’s a long way from Gillies’ first $3,000 gift.
sentences.zh: 这距离吉利斯当年第一笔 3000 美元的捐赠，已经走了很长的路。

records.title: How to find your way out of a food desert

sentences.en: (A) Over the last few months, a survey has been carried out of over 200 greengrocers and convenience stores in Crown Heights, a neighborhood in Brooklyn, New York.
sentences.zh: 在过去几个月里，针对纽约布鲁克林皇冠高地（Crown Heights）社区 200 多家果蔬店和便利店的一项调查已经开展。

sentences.en: As researchers from the Brooklyn Food Association enter the details, colorful dots appear on their online map, which display the specific location of each of the food stores in a handful of central Brooklyn neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 当布鲁克林食品协会（Brooklyn Food Association）的研究人员录入详情时，他们的在线地图上便会出现一颗颗彩色圆点，显示出布鲁克林中部几个社区每家食品店的具体位置。

sentences.en: Clicking on a dot will show you the store’s name and whether it carries fresh fruit and vegetables, wholegrain bread, low-fat dairy and other healthy options.
sentences.zh: 点击一颗圆点，就能看到这家店的名字以及它是否售卖新鲜水果蔬菜、全谷物面包、低脂乳制品等健康食品。

sentences.en: (B) The researchers plan eventually to survey the entire borough of Brooklyn.
sentences.zh: 研究人员计划最终对布鲁克林整个区进行调查。

sentences.en: ‘We want to get to a more specific and detailed description of what that looks like,’ says Jeffrey Heehs, who leads the project.
sentences.zh: “我们想得到一种更具体、更详细的描述，”项目负责人杰弗里·希斯（Jeffrey Heehs）说。

sentences.en: He hopes it will help residents find fresh food in urban areas where the stores sell mostly packaged snacks or fast food, areas otherwise known as food deserts.
sentences.zh: 他希望这能帮助城市中那些商店主要售卖包装零食或快餐的地区——也就是所谓“食物荒漠”地区——的居民找到新鲜食物。

sentences.en: The aim of the project is also to assist government officials in assessing food availability, and in forming future policies about what kind of food should be sold and where.
sentences.zh: 该项目的另一目的是协助政府官员评估食品的可获得性，并在未来制定关于什么食品应在何处售卖的政策。

sentences.en: (C) In fact, the Brooklyn project represents the intersection of two growing trends: mapping fresh food markets in US cities, and private citizens creating online maps of local neighborhood features.
sentences.zh: 事实上，布鲁克林这项工作处在两股正在增长的潮流的交汇处：一是绘制美国城市中新鲜食品市场的地图，二是普通公民为本地社区特征绘制在线地图。

sentences.en: According to Michael Goodchild, a geographer at the University of California at Santa Barbara, citizen map makers may make maps because there is no good government map, or to record problems such as burned-out traffic lights.
sentences.zh: 加州大学圣芭芭拉分校的地理学家迈克尔·古德柴尔德（Michael Goodchild）说，公民制图者绘制地图，可能是因为没有好用的政府地图，或者是为了记录诸如交通信号灯坏掉之类的问题。

sentences.en: (D) According to recent studies, people at higher risk of chronic disease and who receive minimal incomes for the work they do frequently live in neighborhoods located in food deserts.
sentences.zh: 根据近年来的研究，慢性病高风险人群和那些做工却收入微薄的人，常常居住在位于食物荒漠的社区里。

sentences.en: But how did these food deserts arise?
sentences.zh: 但这些食物荒漠是如何形成的呢？

sentences.en: Linda Alwitt and Thomas Donley, marketing researchers at DePaul University in Chicago, found that supermarkets often can’t afford the amount of land required for their stores in cities.
sentences.zh: 芝加哥德保罗大学的营销研究人员琳达·阿尔维特（Linda Alwitt）和托马斯·唐利（Thomas Donley）发现，超市在城市里往往负担不起开店所需的那么多土地。

sentences.en: City planning researcher Cliff Guy and colleagues at the University of Leeds in the UK found in 2004 that smaller urban groceries tend to close due to competition from suburban supermarkets.
sentences.zh: 英国利兹大学的城市规划研究人员克利夫·盖伊（Cliff Guy）及其同事在 2004 年发现，较小型的城市杂货店常因郊区超市的竞争而倒闭。

sentences.en: (E) As fresh food stores leave a neighborhood, residents find it harder to eat well and stay healthy.
sentences.zh: 当新鲜食品店离开一个社区，居民就更难吃得好、保持健康。

sentences.en: Food deserts are linked with lower local health outcomes, and they may be a driving force in the health disparities between lower-income and affluent people in the US.
sentences.zh: 食物荒漠与本地较差的健康状况相关联，可能是美国低收入人群与富裕人群之间健康差距的一个重要推动因素。

sentences.en: Until recently, the issue attracted little national attention, and received no ongoing funding for research.
sentences.zh: 直到最近，这一问题在全国层面所引起的关注都很少，研究方面也没有获得持续的资金支持。

sentences.en: (F) Now, more US cities are becoming aware of their food landscapes.
sentences.zh: 如今，越来越多的美国城市开始意识到自身的食品景观。

sentences.en: Last year, the United States Department of Agriculture launched a map of where food stores are located in all the US counties.
sentences.zh: 去年，美国农业部推出了一张全美各县食品店分布地图。

sentences.en: Mari Gallagher, who runs a private consulting firm, says her researchers have mapped food stores and related them to health statistics for the cities of Detroit, Chicago, Cincinnati and Washington, DC.
sentences.zh: 运营一家私人咨询公司的玛丽·加拉格尔（Mari Gallagher）说，她的研究人员为底特律、芝加哥、辛辛那提和华盛顿特区绘制了食品店地图，并把它们与健康统计数据关联起来。

sentences.en: These maps help cities identify where food deserts are and, occasionally, have documented that people living in food deserts have higher rates of diet-related diseases.
sentences.zh: 这些地图帮助城市识别食物荒漠所在地，并偶尔记录了住在食物荒漠中的人患饮食相关疾病的比例较高。

sentences.en: (G) The Brooklyn project differs in that it’s run by a local core of five volunteers who have worked on the project for the past year, rather than trained, academic researchers.
sentences.zh: 布鲁克林这个项目的不同之处在于，它由 5 名本地核心志愿者运作——过去一年来一直在做这个项目——而不是受过训练的学术研究人员。

sentences.en: To gather data, they simply go to individual stores with pre-printed surveys in hand, and once the storekeeper’s permission has been obtained, check off boxes on their list against the products for sale in the store.
sentences.zh: 为收集数据，他们只需手持预印好的调查表去单个商店，征得店主许可后，对照店里出售的商品在清单上勾选项目。

sentences.en: Their approach to data collection and research has been made possible by technologies such as mapping software and GPS-related smart phones, Google Maps and OpenStreetMap, an open-source online map with a history of involvement in social issues.
sentences.zh: 他们这种数据采集和研究方式之所以可行，得益于地图软件、与 GPS 相关的智能手机、Google 地图以及 OpenStreetMap——一张在社会议题中有参与历史的开源在线地图——这些技术。

sentences.en: Like Brooklyn Food Association volunteers, many citizen online map makers use maps to bring local problems to official attention, Goodchild says.
sentences.zh: 古德柴尔德说，像布鲁克林食品协会志愿者一样，许多公民在线制图者用地图把本地问题摆到官方面前。

sentences.en: (H) Heehs, the mapping project leader, says that after his group gathers more data, it will compare neighborhoods, come up with solutions to address local needs, and then present them to New York City officials.
sentences.zh: 该制图项目负责人希斯说，团队在收集到更多数据后，将对比社区情况，提出针对本地需求的解决方案，并向纽约市官员汇报。

sentences.en: Their website hasn’t caught them much local or official attention yet, however.
sentences.zh: 不过，他们的网站目前还没有引起多少本地或官方的关注。

sentences.en: It was launched only recently, but its creators haven’t yet set up systems to see who’s looking at it.
sentences.zh: 它刚刚上线不久，创建者也尚未设立系统去查看谁在浏览。

sentences.en: (I) Experts who visited the Brooklyn group’s site were optimistic but cautious.
sentences.zh: 考察过布鲁克林这个项目网站的专家们表示乐观，但谨慎。

sentences.en: ‘This kind of detailed information could be very useful,’ says Michele Ver Ploeg, an economist for the Department of Agriculture.
sentences.zh: “这种详细信息可能非常有用，”美国农业部经济学家米歇尔·韦尔·普洛厄格（Michele Ver Ploeg）说。

sentences.en: To make the map more helpful to both residents and policy makers, she would like to see price data for healthy products, too.
sentences.zh: 为了让地图对居民和决策者都更有帮助，她希望还能看到健康食品的价格数据。

sentences.en: Karen Ansel, a registered dietician and a spokesperson for the American Dietetic Association, found the site confusing to navigate.
sentences.zh: 美国饮食协会发言人、注册营养师凯伦·安塞尔（Karen Ansel）则发现该网站浏览起来有些令人困惑。

sentences.en: ‘That said, with this information in place the group has the tools to build a more user-friendly site that could be …
sentences.zh: “话虽如此，有了这些信息在手，该团队具备了搭建一个更易用网站的工具，那将……

sentences.en: very helpful to consumers,’ she says.
sentences.zh: 对消费者非常有帮助，“她说。

sentences.en: ‘The group also should ensure their map is available to those who don’t have internet access at home,’ she adds.
sentences.zh: “该团队还应确保他们的地图能向家中没有互联网接入的人开放，”她补充道。

sentences.en: In fact, a significant proportion of Brooklyn residents don’t have internet access at home and 8 percent rely on dial-up service, instead of high-speed internet access, according to Gretchen Maneval, director of Brooklyn College’s Center for the Study of Brooklyn.
sentences.zh: 事实上，布鲁克林相当一部分居民家中并没有互联网接入；根据布鲁克林学院布鲁克林研究中心主任格雷琴·马涅瓦尔（Gretchen Maneval）的说法，有 8% 的人依赖拨号上网，而不是高速互联网。

sentences.en: ‘It’s still very much a work in progress,’ Heehs says of the online map.
sentences.zh: “它仍然在不断完善之中，”希斯谈到这张在线地图时说。

sentences.en: They’ll start advertising it online and by email to other community groups, such as urban food garden associations, next month.
sentences.zh: 下个月他们将开始通过网络以及电子邮件向其他社区团体——如城市食物菜园协会——做推广。

sentences.en: He also hopes warmer days in the spring will draw out fresh volunteers to spread awareness and to finish surveying, as they have about two-thirds of Brooklyn left to cover.
sentences.zh: 他还希望春天里更暖和的日子能吸引新的志愿者出来加入推广和完成调查的工作，因为他们还有大约三分之二的布鲁克林尚未走完。

sentences.en: A Fifty-six million prescriptions for sleeping medication were handed out by doctors in America last year.
sentences.zh: 去年，美国的医生开出了五千六百万张安眠药处方。

sentences.en: Yet remarkably little is being done to understand insomnia’s root causes.
sentences.zh: 然而，为了解失眠的根本原因而做的工作却少得惊人。

sentences.en: Socially and economically, the undertreatment of sleeplessness is hugely expensive.
sentences.zh: 无论从社会还是经济角度看，对失眠的治疗不足都代价极为高昂。

sentences.en: The Institute of Medicine, an independent scientific advisory group, estimates nearly 20 percent of all major accidents on the road are associated with driver sleepiness.
sentences.zh: 独立的科学咨询机构美国医学研究所估计，公路上近20%的重大事故都与驾驶员困倦有关。

sentences.en: The loss in terms of productivity within the workplace is even higher, costing billions.
sentences.zh: 就职场内的生产力损失而言，代价甚至更高，达数十亿之巨。

sentences.en: Then there are the softer costs which remain unmeasured but still exist; for example, the damaged relationships with others.
sentences.zh: 此外还有一些更隐性的代价，它们无从计量却依然存在，例如与他人受损的关系。

sentences.en: If other medical problems were causing such widespread harm, governments would act, but US authorities contribute only about $230 million a year for the funding of sleep research, comparable to the amount that the manufacturers of popular sleeping pills spent in three months on advertising.
sentences.zh: 如果是其他医学问题造成了如此广泛的危害，政府早就会采取行动了，但美国当局每年仅为睡眠研究提供约2.3亿美元的资助，这与畅销安眠药的生产商在三个月里花在广告上的金额相当。

sentences.en: Currently most medical school students get no more than four hours of training on sleep disorders; some get none.
sentences.zh: 目前，大多数医学院学生在睡眠障碍方面所受的培训不超过四小时，有些人则一点也没有。

sentences.en: B If we don’t know why we can’t sleep, it’s in part because we don’t really know why we need to sleep in the first place.
sentences.zh: 如果说我们不知道自己为何无法入睡，那在一定程度上是因为我们其实并不真正清楚自己一开始为什么需要睡眠。

sentences.en: We know that we divide it between periods of deep-wave sleep and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, when the brain is as active as when we’re awake, but our voluntary muscles are paralyzed.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，睡眠分为深波睡眠和快速眼动（REM）睡眠两个阶段，在快速眼动睡眠期间，大脑像我们清醒时一样活跃，但我们的随意肌却处于麻痹状态。

sentences.en: We know that all mammals sleep, and that there are some insects and reptiles that only half sleep, in order to remain aware of their environment and predators.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，所有哺乳动物都会睡眠，还有一些昆虫和爬行动物只是半睡，以便对周围环境和捕食者保持警觉。

sentences.en: C The predominant theory of sleep is that the brain demands it.
sentences.zh: 关于睡眠占主导地位的理论是，大脑需要它。

sentences.en: Recently, researchers at Harvard, led by Robert Stickgold, tested undergraduates on various aptitude tests, allowed them to nap, then tested them again.
sentences.zh: 最近，哈佛大学由罗伯特·斯蒂克戈尔德带领的研究者，让本科生做了各种能力测验，让他们小睡一会儿，然后再次测验他们。

sentences.en: They found that those who had engaged in REM sleep subsequently performed better in pattern recognition tasks, such as grammar, while those who slept deeply were better at memorization.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，那些进入过快速眼动睡眠的人，随后在语法等模式识别任务中表现更好，而那些睡得很深的人则更擅长记忆。

sentences.en: D Such studies suggest that memory consolidation may be one function of sleep.
sentences.zh: 这类研究表明，巩固记忆可能是睡眠的一项功能。

sentences.en: Giulio Tononi, a sleep researcher at the University of Wisconsin, published an interesting twist on this theory a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 威斯康星大学的睡眠研究者朱利奥·托诺尼，几年前为这一理论发表了一个有趣的新解。

sentences.en: His study showed that the sleeping brain seems to delete redundant or unnecessary synapses or connections.
sentences.zh: 他的研究显示，睡眠中的大脑似乎会删除多余或不必要的突触或连接。

sentences.en: So the purpose of sleep may be to help us remember what’s important, by letting us forget what’s not.
sentences.zh: 因此，睡眠的目的也许是通过让我们忘掉不重要的东西，来帮助我们记住重要的东西。

sentences.en: E Sleep is likely to have physiological purposes too.
sentences.zh: 睡眠很可能也有生理上的目的。

sentences.en: Some researchers have found that sleep deprivation impedes wound healing in rats, and others have suggested that sleep helps boost the immune system and control infection.
sentences.zh: 一些研究者发现，睡眠剥夺会妨碍大鼠的伤口愈合，另一些研究者则提出，睡眠有助于增强免疫系统、控制感染。

sentences.en: But these studies are not conclusive.
sentences.zh: 但这些研究都不是定论。

sentences.en: At Stanford University, William Dement, co-founder of the Stanford Sleep Medicine Center, explains what he knows after 50 years of research, about the reason we sleep.
sentences.zh: 在斯坦福大学，斯坦福睡眠医学中心的联合创始人威廉·德门特，讲述了他经过50年研究之后，对我们为何睡眠这一问题的认识。

sentences.en: ‘As far as I know,’ he said, ‘the only reason we need to sleep that is really, really solid is because we get sleepy.’
sentences.zh: “据我所知，”他说，“我们需要睡眠的唯一真正、真正站得住脚的理由，就是我们会犯困。”

sentences.en: F The Stanford clinic does more than 3,000 overnight sleep studies a year.
sentences.zh: 斯坦福这家诊所每年进行3000多例过夜睡眠研究。

sentences.en: Their main diagnostic tool is the polysomnogram, the main element of which is the electroencephalograph (EEG), which captures the electrical output from a patient’s brain.
sentences.zh: 他们主要的诊断工具是多导睡眠图，其主要部分是脑电图（EEG），它记录下患者大脑发出的电信号。

sentences.en: As the EEG records a person’s sleep patterns, the polysomnogram technicians also measure body temperature, muscle activity, eye movement, and breathing.
sentences.zh: 在脑电图记录一个人睡眠模式的同时，多导睡眠图技术员还会测量体温、肌肉活动、眼球运动和呼吸。

sentences.en: Then they look over the data for signs of abnormal sleep.
sentences.zh: 然后，他们仔细查看这些数据，寻找睡眠异常的迹象。

sentences.en: When a person has narcolepsy, for instance, they plunge from wakefulness into REM sleep without any intermediate steps.
sentences.zh: 举例来说，当一个人患有发作性睡病时，他会从清醒状态直接坠入快速眼动睡眠，中间没有任何过渡阶段。

sentences.en: However, Clete Kushida, the clinic director, told me he can spot most people’s sleep problems right at the intake interview.
sentences.zh: 不过，诊所主任克莱特·库希达告诉我，他在接诊面谈时就能看出大多数人的睡眠问题。

sentences.en: ‘There are those who cannot keep their eyes open, and those who just speak of their exhaustion but don’t actually fall asleep.
sentences.zh: “有些人睁不开眼，还有些人只是诉说自己有多疲惫，却并不会真的睡着。

sentences.en: The former often have sleep apnea where they stop breathing.
sentences.zh: 前者往往患有睡眠呼吸暂停，会出现呼吸中止。

sentences.en: The latter have true insomnia.’
sentences.zh: 后者才是真正的失眠。”

sentences.en: G In sleep apnea, muscle relaxation allows the soft tissue of the throat to close, shutting off the sleeper’s air passage.
sentences.zh: 在睡眠呼吸暂停中，肌肉松弛使喉部的软组织闭合，堵住了睡眠者的气道。

sentences.en: When the brain realizes it is not getting oxygen, it sends a signal to the body to wake up.
sentences.zh: 当大脑意识到自己得不到氧气时，便向身体发出醒来的信号。

sentences.en: The sleeper awakes, inhales, and sleep returns.
sentences.zh: 睡眠者醒来，吸气，然后又重新入睡。

sentences.en: Apnea is a serious problem but only indirectly a sleep disease.
sentences.zh: 呼吸暂停是个严重的问题，但只是间接地算作一种睡眠疾病。

sentences.en: True insomniacs are people who either can’t get to, or can’t stay asleep for any evident reason.
sentences.zh: 真正的失眠者，是那些没有任何明显原因却无法入睡、或无法保持睡眠状态的人。

sentences.en: H While apnea can be treated with a device that forces air down the sleeper’s throat to keep the airways open, the treatment of classic insomnia is not so clear cut.
sentences.zh: 呼吸暂停可以用一种把空气压入睡眠者喉咙、使气道保持畅通的装置来治疗，而典型失眠的治疗却没有这么明确。

sentences.en: Acupuncture may help.
sentences.zh: 针灸可能有帮助。

sentences.en: It has long had this role in Asian medicine and is being studied at the University of Pittsburgh sleep center now.
sentences.zh: 它在亚洲医学中长期扮演着这一角色，如今正在匹兹堡大学睡眠中心接受研究。

sentences.en: Typically in the US, insomnia is treated in two ways.
sentences.zh: 在美国，失眠通常以两种方式治疗。

sentences.en: First come the sleeping pills.
sentences.zh: 首先是安眠药。

sentences.en: Though safer than they once were, they can still lead to psychological addiction.
sentences.zh: 尽管它们比从前更安全了，却仍可能导致心理上的依赖。

sentences.en: ‘Many users complain that their sleeping-pill sleep seems different, and they feel unfocused on waking.
sentences.zh: “许多服用者抱怨说，靠安眠药得来的睡眠似乎不一样，他们醒来时感到注意力涣散。

sentences.en: Sleeping pills are not a natural way to sleep,’ points out Charles Czeisler, director of the Harvard Health and Safety Group.
sentences.zh: 安眠药并不是一种自然的入睡方式，”哈佛健康与安全研究组主任查尔斯·切斯勒指出。

sentences.en: I The second step in treating insomniacs is usually cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT).
sentences.zh: 治疗失眠者的第二步通常是认知行为疗法（CBT）。

sentences.en: In CBT, a psychologist teaches insomniacs to think about sleep problems as manageable, and to practice good ‘sleep hygiene’: sleep in a dark room, go to bed only when you are sleepy, don’t exercise beforehand.
sentences.zh: 在认知行为疗法中，心理学家教失眠者把睡眠问题看作是可以掌控的，并教他们践行良好的“睡眠卫生”：在黑暗的房间里睡觉，只在困了的时候才上床，睡前不要运动。

sentences.en: Studies have shown that CBT is more effective than sleeping pills at treating long-term insomnia, but many sufferers aren’t convinced.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，在治疗长期失眠方面，认知行为疗法比安眠药更有效，但许多受失眠困扰的人并不信服。

sentences.en: ‘Some people continue in my experience to struggle,’ says John Winkelman, another sleep center director.
sentences.zh: “以我的经验，有些人仍在苦苦挣扎，”另一位睡眠中心主任约翰·温克尔曼说。

sentences.en: ‘They’re not super-satisfied with their sleep.’
sentences.zh: “他们对自己的睡眠并不十分满意。”

records.title: The origin and development of applause

sentences.en: A Scholars aren’t quite sure about the origins of applause, but the form that is still most common, clapping the hands together, was formalized in Western culture during and after performances.
sentences.zh: 学者们对鼓掌的起源并不十分确定，但仍最常见的那种形式——双手拍在一起——是在西方文化中于演出期间和之后逐渐定型的。

sentences.en: During the time of the Roman Republic (509 BC – 27 BC) the common way to end a play was for the chief actor to yell ‘Valete et plaudite!’
sentences.zh: 在罗马共和国时期（公元前509年至公元前27年），结束一场戏的常见方式是主角高喊“Valete et plaudite！”

sentences.en: (‘Goodbye and applause!’)
sentences.zh: （“再见，鼓掌！”）

sentences.en: thus signaling to the audience that it was time for them to give praise by striking hands and making explosive noise.
sentences.zh: 从而向观众示意，是时候让他们击掌、发出爆裂般的声响来表示赞赏了。

sentences.en: It’s no surprise, then, that this became a means of crowd manipulation.
sentences.zh: 那么，这成为一种操纵人群的手段也就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: Rome saw the rise of a professional class of applauders, or ‘people who clapped for their dinner’, hired to infiltrate crowds and manipulate their reaction to performances.
sentences.zh: 罗马出现了一个专业鼓掌者阶层，或者说“为晚餐而鼓掌的人”，他们被雇来混入人群、操纵人群对演出的反应。

sentences.en: Actors would hire a dozen or so people to spread out among their audiences and prolong the applause, or, if they were feeling especially bold, to start ‘spontaneous’ chants and shouts of praise.
sentences.zh: 演员会雇十来个人散布在观众中、延长掌声，或者，如果他们特别大胆，去发起“自发的”齐声欢呼和赞美。

sentences.en: B The Roman Republic came to an end and was replaced by the Roman Empire (27 BC – 476 AD) where applause became a way for leaders to interact directly with their citizens.
sentences.zh: 罗马共和国走到尽头，被罗马帝国（公元前27年至公元476年）取代，在那里鼓掌成为领导者与公民直接互动的一种方式。

sentences.en: One of the chief methods they used to estimate their standing with the people was gauging the greetings they got when they entered the arena.
sentences.zh: 他们用来估量自己在民众中地位的主要方法之一，是衡量他们进入竞技场时得到的欢迎。

sentences.en: Leaders became astute at reading the volume, the rhythm, and the length of the crowd’s claps for clues about how well they were doing as officials and lawmakers.
sentences.zh: 领导者变得善于从人群掌声的音量、节奏和长度中读取线索，判断自己作为官员和立法者做得有多好。

sentences.en: ‘We should think of it as an ancient type of opinion poll,’ says Greg Aldrete, a professor of history.
sentences.zh: “我们应该把它看作一种古老的民意调查，”历史学教授Greg Aldrete说。

sentences.en: ‘This is how you gauge the people.’
sentences.zh: “这就是你衡量民众的方式。”

sentences.en: Roman leaders were gathering data about people by listening to applause.
sentences.zh: 罗马领导者通过聆听掌声来收集关于民众的数据。

sentences.en: C Clever leaders of the ancient world researched their rivals, too.
sentences.zh: 古代世界聪明的领导者也研究他们的对手。

sentences.en: Cicero, the Roman lawyer, would send friends to stand around outside the arena, taking notes to see what kind of greeting each official got when he entered, the better to see who was beloved by the people, and who was not.
sentences.zh: 罗马律师西塞罗会派朋友站在竞技场外面，做笔记，看每位官员进场时得到什么样的欢迎，以便更好地看出谁受民众爱戴、谁不受。

sentences.en: They had a lot of information to assess.
sentences.zh: 他们有大量信息要评估。

sentences.en: ‘Ancient crowds were more interactive than they are today,’ Aldrete points out.
sentences.zh: “古代的人群比今天更具互动性，”Aldrete指出。

sentences.en: ‘There was a lot of back and forth between speakers and crowds.
sentences.zh: “演讲者和人群之间有大量的来回。

sentences.en: And particularly in the Greco-Roman world, crowds, especially in cities, were really good at communicating messages through rhythmic clapping, sometimes coupled with shouts.’
sentences.zh: 尤其在希腊罗马世界，人群，特别是在城市里，非常善于通过有节奏的鼓掌、有时配以呼喊来传达信息。”

sentences.en: The coding was, he says, invaluable when assessing an orator’s fortunes.
sentences.zh: 他说，在评估一位演说家的命运时，这套编码是极其宝贵的。

sentences.en: D Around the first century AD, those systems of applause became more and more elaborate.
sentences.zh: 大约在公元一世纪，那些鼓掌的体系变得越来越精细。

sentences.en: Applause no longer meant, simply, ‘claps’.
sentences.zh: 鼓掌不再仅仅意味着“拍手”。

sentences.en: While Greco-Roman audiences certainly smacked their palms together the same way we do today, their overall strategies of applause were much more varied than clapping alone.
sentences.zh: 虽然希腊罗马的观众确实和我们今天一样把手掌拍在一起，但他们整体的鼓掌策略远比单纯拍手丰富。

sentences.en: Crowds expressed degrees of approval of the person or persons before them, ranging from claps, to snaps (of the finger and thumb), to waves (of the edge of the toga).
sentences.zh: 人群对面前的人或人们表达不同程度的认可，从拍手，到打响指（用食指和拇指），到挥动（托加长袍的边缘）。

sentences.en: The emperor Aurelian decided to replace this gesture by waving a special handkerchief instead, a prop which he then distributed to all Roman citizens, so they would never be without a way to praise him.
sentences.zh: 皇帝奥勒良决定用挥动一块特制的手帕来取代这个手势，他随后把这种道具分发给所有罗马公民，好让他们永远不会没有办法赞美他。

sentences.en: E Although style of applause may have changed over the centuries, the need to manipulate remained.
sentences.zh: 尽管鼓掌的方式或许几个世纪以来有所改变，操纵的需要却依然存在。

sentences.en: 16th-century French poet Jean Daurat is credited with bringing back the Roman practice of hiring professional applauders.
sentences.zh: 16世纪法国诗人Jean Daurat被认为重新带回了雇佣职业鼓掌者的罗马做法。

sentences.en: In France, this group became known as a ‘claque’.
sentences.zh: 在法国，这群人被称为“claque”（捧场队）。

sentences.en: Daurat handed out tickets to his own performances to people who promised to applaud at the end.
sentences.zh: Daurat把自己演出的票分发给那些承诺在结束时鼓掌的人。

sentences.en: By the early 1820s, claques had become institutionalized, with an agency in Paris specializing in the distribution of the claqueurs’ services.
sentences.zh: 到19世纪20年代初，捧场队已经制度化，巴黎有一家中介专门分配捧场者的服务。

sentences.en: The historian William B.
sentences.zh: 历史学家William B.

sentences.en: Cohen describes the intricate price lists agencies of this kind would hand out to potential patrons: polite clapping would cost this many francs, enthusiastic applause would cost this many.
sentences.zh: Cohen描述了这类中介会发给潜在主顾的精细价目表，礼貌的鼓掌要花这么多法郎，热烈的掌声要花这么多。

sentences.en: The claque also underwent a kind of classification: the rieurs (laughers) would laugh loudly at the jokes; the pleureurs (criers) would feign tears in reaction to performances; the commissaires (officers) would learn a play or a piece of music by heart and then call attention to its best parts.
sentences.zh: 捧场队还经历了一种分工，rieurs（笑者）会对笑话大声发笑；pleureurs（哭者）会对演出佯装落泪；commissaires（officers，即引导者）会把一出戏或一段乐曲背下来，然后让人注意它最精彩的部分。

sentences.en: This practice spread to Milan, to Vienna, and to London before falling out of fashion.
sentences.zh: 这种做法传到米兰、维也纳和伦敦，之后才不再流行。

sentences.en: The claque lost its power once people became aware of its tricks.
sentences.zh: 一旦人们意识到捧场队的把戏，它就失去了它的力量。

sentences.en: F And clapping itself evolved.
sentences.zh: 而鼓掌本身也在演变。

sentences.en: In the 18th century, symphonies and concerts became more serious, aligning themselves with the reverence and spirituality associated with religious ceremonies.
sentences.zh: 18世纪，交响乐和音乐会变得更严肃，使自己与宗教仪式所关联的敬畏和灵性相一致。

sentences.en: Knowing when to maintain silence, as well as when to clap, became a mark of sophistication, a kind of code for audiences to learn.
sentences.zh: 知道何时保持安静、以及何时鼓掌，成了一种修养的标志，一种供观众学习的密码。

sentences.en: Applause became a matter of ‘do’ or ‘don’t’, so losing many old shades of meaning.
sentences.zh: 鼓掌成了“该做”或“不该做”的事，因而失去了许多旧有的细微含义。

sentences.en: Those changes changed performers, too.
sentences.zh: 那些变化也改变了表演者。

sentences.en: Applause became much less of a true dialogue with an audience, especially so with opera, where the singers saw it as part of a basic transaction with the crowd.
sentences.zh: 鼓掌变得远不再是与观众真正的对话，尤其在歌剧中，歌唱者把它视为与人群一种基本交易的一部分。

sentences.en: So by the time the 19th century arrived, applause had become standardized and institutionalized, and had become an expectation rather than the reward it used to be.
sentences.zh: 所以到了19世纪，鼓掌已变得标准化、制度化，并成了一种期待，而非它过去那种奖赏。

sentences.en: G In the 21st century we’re reinventing applause, to make it what it used to be: a coded form of communication.
sentences.zh: 在21世纪，我们正在重新发明鼓掌，让它变回它过去的样子，一种编码化的交流形式。

sentences.en: More and more the digital world allows us to link and like and share through our devices.
sentences.zh: 数字世界越来越允许我们通过设备来链接、点赞和分享。

sentences.en: By connecting with others in this way, we become part of the performance by participating in it, demonstrating our appreciation by amplifying and extending the show through commenting and praising.
sentences.zh: 通过以这种方式与他人连接，我们参与其中而成为表演的一部分，通过评论和称赞来放大、延伸演出，从而表达我们的赞赏。

sentences.en: Our kind of applause matters more now, in many ways, because it is no longer momentary and short-lived, but is far more permanent instead.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，我们这种鼓掌如今更重要，因为它不再是转瞬即逝、短暂的，反而远为持久。

sentences.en: A The general perception of plants is that they are defenceless when faced with threat from animals (including man), insects and other plants.
sentences.zh: 人们对植物的普遍看法是，它们在面对来自动物（包括人）、昆虫和其他植物的威胁时是毫无防御能力的。

sentences.en: This, however, is not the case.
sentences.zh: 然而，事实并非如此。

sentences.en: Plants are able to defend themselves against attack from their environment in many ways.
sentences.zh: 植物能够以许多方式抵御来自其环境的攻击。

sentences.en: There are two major features of plants that ensure their continuation as species.
sentences.zh: 植物有两大特征，确保了它们作为物种的延续。

sentences.en: One of these relates to their physical attributes.
sentences.zh: 其中之一与它们的物理属性有关。

sentences.en: Spinifex grass, a plant native to Australia, provides a notable example.
sentences.zh: 原产于澳大利亚的鬣刺草，就是一个突出的例子。

sentences.en: Adapted to life in the hot, desert inland, spinifex has developed tightly rolled leaves which reduce the effects of drought stress.
sentences.zh: 鬣刺草适应了炎热的内陆沙漠生活，进化出了紧紧卷曲的叶子，以减轻干旱胁迫的影响。

sentences.en: The hairs, or trichomes, which are found on the inner surface of the rolled-up spinifex leaf are believed to assist in minimising water loss.
sentences.zh: 卷曲的鬣刺草叶片内表面所生的毛，即毛状体，被认为有助于把水分流失降到最低。

sentences.en: Trichomes also have defensive roles against predators.
sentences.zh: 毛状体还具有抵御捕食者的防御作用。

sentences.en: Many plants, such as the sunflower, have hairy leaves which are rough to the touch.
sentences.zh: 许多植物，例如向日葵，长着多毛的叶子，摸上去很粗糙。

sentences.en: When the plant is bitten by a grazing animal, the sensation is unpleasant on the tongue and the animal normally moves on to find more palatable food.
sentences.zh: 当植株被吃草的动物咬到时，那种感觉令舌头不适，动物通常就会转而去寻找更可口的食物。

sentences.en: B Some families of plants such as the Solanaceae, which includes the tomato, the potato and other food plants, feature glandular trichomes.
sentences.zh: 有些植物科，例如包括番茄、马铃薯及其他食用植物在内的茄科，长有腺毛。

sentences.en: In these structures a tiny sac is carried on the hair, which rises from the epidermis, or skin, of the plant.
sentences.zh: 在这些结构中，一个微小的囊袋长在毛上，毛则从植物的表皮、即外皮上长出。

sentences.en: The sac contains chemicals which may perform a range of functions.
sentences.zh: 这个囊袋里含有可能发挥一系列功能的化学物质。

sentences.en: For example, an insect landing on a tomato leaf and rupturing the sac is exposed to a toxic chemical which will deter it from feeding on that plant in future.
sentences.zh: 例如，一只落在番茄叶上、弄破了囊袋的昆虫，会接触到一种有毒的化学物质，使它今后不敢再以那株植物为食。

sentences.en: In other plants of the same family, the sacs contain a natural adhesive and the unsuspecting insect landing on such a leaf and rupturing a trichome sac is held onto the plant, unable to depart.
sentences.zh: 在同科的其他植物中，这些囊袋里含有一种天然的黏合剂，那只毫无戒心、落在这样一片叶子上、弄破了一个毛状体囊袋的昆虫，便被粘在植物上，无法离开。

sentences.en: In the leaves of the nettle plant these trichomes resemble miniature hypodermic syringes.
sentences.zh: 在荨麻的叶子上，这些毛状体形似微型的皮下注射器。

sentences.en: An irritant chemical is stored at the base of the ‘syringe’.
sentences.zh: 一种刺激性的化学物质储存在“注射器”的底部。

sentences.en: If an animal touches it, a shot of the chemical is discharged through the ‘needle’ and into the skin of the animal.
sentences.zh: 如果有动物碰到它，一剂化学物质就会从“针头”射出，注入动物的皮肤。

sentences.en: The irritation the chemical causes is a deterrent against future threat.
sentences.zh: 这种化学物质所引起的刺激，是对未来威胁的一种威慑。

sentences.en: C The poisons and glues of the Solanaceae and the irritant of the nettle indicate the other major method of plant survival: that some plants use chemicals to protect themselves, sometimes from each other.
sentences.zh: 茄科的毒素和胶质，以及荨麻的刺激物，指向了植物求生的另一种主要方法：有些植物利用化学物质来保护自己，有时是为了防范彼此。

sentences.en: Chemical interactions that occur between plants are known as ‘allelopathy’, and in natural plant communities it is one of many factors which determine how plants grow in relation to one another.
sentences.zh: 植物之间发生的化学相互作用被称为“化感作用”，在天然的植物群落中，它是决定植物彼此相对如何生长的众多因素之一。

sentences.en: An example in Australia is the suppression of vegetation growth beneath eucalypt trees, an effect which decreases with increasing distance from the trunk of the tree.
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚的一个例子是桉树底下植被生长受到抑制，这种效应随着与树干距离的增加而减弱。

sentences.en: D The most detailed studies of allelopathy have generally been carried out on agricultural plant communities.
sentences.zh: 对化感作用最详尽的研究，一般都是在农业植物群落中进行的。

sentences.en: In agriculture, allelopathy has been identified particularly with weeds, which compete with desired crop or pasture species, such as wheat, oats and grass, for environmental resources.
sentences.zh: 在农业中，化感作用尤其与杂草联系在一起，杂草会为环境资源而与小麦、燕麦和牧草等人们想要的作物或牧草物种竞争。

sentences.en: Competition can be physical, where the growth of one plant maximises the use of water, nutrients and light to the disadvantage of another.
sentences.zh: 竞争可以是物理性的，即一株植物的生长最大限度地占用水分、养分和光照，使另一株处于不利地位。

sentences.en: Allelopathy, on the other hand, involves plant-produced chemicals which may poison a neighbouring plant.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，化感作用涉及植物所产生的、可能毒害邻近植物的化学物质。

sentences.en: On the whole, weeds are far more physically and chemically aggressive than crop and pasture species.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，杂草在物理上和化学上都远比作物和牧草物种更具侵略性。

sentences.en: As an example, recent research on the common thorn apple, Datura stramonium, a weed found throughout Australia, has found that two powerful chemicals are released from the seed during the early stages of germination.
sentences.zh: 举例来说，最近对遍布澳大利亚的杂草曼陀罗（学名Datura stramonium）的研究发现，在萌发的早期阶段，种子会释放出两种强效的化学物质。

sentences.en: In fact, it is necessary for the chemicals to be released from the seed coat so that the seed can germinate.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这些化学物质必须从种皮中释放出来，种子才能萌发。

sentences.en: Once released, the chemicals then provide a barrier that inhibits the growth of any potential plant competitor near the thorn apple seedling.
sentences.zh: 一旦释放出来，这些化学物质便会形成一道屏障，抑制曼陀罗幼苗附近任何潜在植物竞争者的生长。

sentences.en: E Allelopathic chemicals function in quite subtle ways.
sentences.zh: 化感化学物质以相当微妙的方式发挥作用。

sentences.en: Generally they are active in small quantities, they are effective only with certain other plants, they act by disrupting the plant’s natural processes and they have no known residual effects.
sentences.zh: 一般来说，它们在微量时就有活性，只对某些特定的其他植物有效，它们通过扰乱植物的自然过程来起作用，而且没有已知的残留效应。

sentences.en: It has also been found that the activity of these chemicals may be synergistic, that is, two or more such substances may combine to produce an effect that is greater than the effects of the substances acting in isolation.
sentences.zh: 人们还发现，这些化学物质的活性可能具有协同性，也就是说，两种或更多这样的物质可能结合起来，产生比这些物质单独作用时更大的效果。

sentences.en: These are the very attributes which are being targeted in the current development of synthetic herbicides*.
sentences.zh: 这些正是当前合成除草剂*研发中所要瞄准的属性。

sentences.en: Allelopathy is not restricted to weeds in agriculture, but allelopathic activity in crop and pasture plants appears to have diminished, possibly because plant breeders may have concentrated on improving aspects of crop quality and quantity rather than aspects of defence against natural enemies.
sentences.zh: 化感作用并不局限于农业中的杂草，但作物和牧草植物中的化感活性似乎已经减弱，这可能是因为植物育种者把精力集中在改良作物质量和产量的方面，而不是抵御天敌的方面。

sentences.en: F Allelopathic chemicals may be harvested for development as ‘natural herbicides’, similar to the harvest of pyrethrins from the pyrethrum daisy for use as natural insecticides.
sentences.zh: 化感化学物质可以被采集出来，开发成“天然除草剂”，就像从除虫菊中采集除虫菊酯用作天然杀虫剂一样。

sentences.en: Harnessing allelopathy is highly attractive to the farming industry, as at least half of the more than A$200-million annual cost of crop protection in Australia is spent on herbicides.
sentences.zh: 驾驭化感作用对农业极具吸引力，因为在澳大利亚，每年两亿多澳元的作物保护成本中，至少有一半花在了除草剂上。

sentences.en: Enhancing allelopathic activity in crop and pasture plants could reduce this enormous bill.
sentences.zh: 增强作物和牧草植物中的化感活性，可以减少这笔庞大的开支。

sentences.en: Developing and harvesting natural herbicides might also offer real advantages in addressing environmental concerns about the over-use of synthetic chemicals currently used in crop protection.
sentences.zh: 开发和采集天然除草剂，或许还能在缓解人们对当前作物保护中过度使用合成化学品的环境担忧方面带来切实的好处。

sentences.en: In many parts of the world, communities are showing an increased willingness to pay a premium for products grown with few or no synthetic chemicals, and natural products are becoming increasingly attractive.
sentences.zh: 在世界许多地方，各社区正表现出越来越大的意愿，愿意为用极少或不用合成化学品种出的产品支付溢价，天然产品也正变得越来越有吸引力。
