records.title: How Well Do We Concentrate?
records.titleZh: 我们的注意力集中能力有多好？

sentences.en: A Do you read while listening to music?
sentences.zh: 你会一边听音乐一边看书吗？

sentences.en: Do you like to watch TV while finishing your homework?
sentences.zh: 你喜欢一边看电视一边完成作业吗？

sentences.en: People who have these kinds of habits are called multitaskers.
sentences.zh: 有这类习惯的人被称为多任务处理者。

sentences.en: Multitaskers are able to complete two tasks at the same time by dividing their focus.
sentences.zh: 多任务处理者能够通过分散自己的注意力，同时完成两项任务。

sentences.en: However, Thomas Lehman, a researcher in psychology, believes people never really do multiple things simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 然而，心理学研究者托马斯·莱曼认为，人其实从来不会真正同时做多件事。

sentences.en: Maybe a person is reading while listening to music, but in reality the brain can only focus on one task.
sentences.zh: 也许一个人在听音乐的同时看书，但实际上大脑只能专注于一项任务。

sentences.en: Reading the words in a book will cause you to ignore some of the words of the music.
sentences.zh: 读书中的文字会使你忽略掉音乐中的一些词句。

sentences.en: When people think they are accomplishing two different tasks efficiently, what they are really doing is dividing their focus.
sentences.zh: 当人们以为自己在高效地完成两项不同任务时，他们真正在做的其实是在分散注意力。

sentences.en: While listening to music, people become less able to focus on their surroundings.
sentences.zh: 在听音乐时，人们对周围环境的专注力会下降。

sentences.en: For example, we all have experienced times when we talk with friends and they are not responding properly.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们都有过这样的经历：和朋友说话，他们却没有恰当地回应。

sentences.en: Maybe they are listening to someone else talk, or maybe they are reading a text on their smartphone and don’t hear what you are saying.
sentences.zh: 也许他们在听别人讲话，又或许他们在看手机上的一条短信，根本没听见你在说什么。

sentences.en: Lehman called this phenomenon “email voice.”
sentences.zh: 莱曼把这种现象称为“电邮嗓音”。

sentences.en: B The world has been changed by computers and their spin-offs such as smartphones or cellphones.
sentences.zh: 计算机及其衍生品，比如智能手机或手机，已经改变了世界。

sentences.en: Now that most individuals have a personal device, like a smartphone or a laptop, they are frequently reading, watching or listening to virtual information.
sentences.zh: 如今大多数人都拥有一台个人设备，比如智能手机或笔记本电脑，他们经常在阅读、观看或聆听虚拟信息。

sentences.en: This increases the occurrence of multitasking in our day-to-day life.
sentences.zh: 这使得多任务处理在我们的日常生活中愈发频繁。

sentences.en: Nowadays, when you work, you may use your typewriter, your cellphone, and speak with colleagues who may drop by at any time.
sentences.zh: 如今，当你工作时，你可能用着打字机、手机，还要和随时可能顺道来访的同事交谈。

sentences.en: In professional meetings, when one would normally focus on and listen to one another, people are more likely to have a cellphone in their lap, reading or communicating silently with more people than ever.
sentences.zh: 在专业会议上，人们本应专注地彼此倾听，如今却更可能腿上放着一部手机，默默地阅读，或与比以往更多的人交流。

sentences.en: Even inventions such as the cordless phone have increased multitasking.
sentences.zh: 甚至像无绳电话这样的发明，也增加了多任务处理。

sentences.en: In the old days, a traditional wall phone would ring, and the housewife would have to stop her activities to answer it.
sentences.zh: 在过去，传统的挂壁电话会响起，家庭主妇不得不停下手中的活儿去接听。

sentences.en: When it rang, the housewife would sit down with her legs up and chat, with no laundry, sweeping or answering the door.
sentences.zh: 电话铃响时，家庭主妇会坐下来，跷起腿闲聊，不再洗衣、扫地或应门。

sentences.en: In the modern era, our technology is convenient enough not to interrupt our daily tasks.
sentences.zh: 在现代，我们的技术已便利到无需打断我们日常的事务。

sentences.en: C Earl Miller, an expert at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, studied the prefrontal cortex, which guides the brain while a person is multitasking.
sentences.zh: 麻省理工学院的专家厄尔·米勒研究了前额叶皮层，它在人进行多任务处理时引导着大脑。

sentences.en: According to his studies, the size of this cortex varies between species.
sentences.zh: 根据他的研究，这一皮层的大小因物种而异。

sentences.en: He found that for humans, it constitutes one-third of the brain, whereas it is only 4 – 5 percent in dogs and about 15 percent in monkeys.
sentences.zh: 他发现，对人类而言，它占大脑的三分之一，而在狗身上只占4%到5%，在猴子身上约占15%。

sentences.en: Because this cortex is larger in humans, it allows a person to be more flexible and accurate in multitasking.
sentences.zh: 由于这一皮层在人类身上更大，它使人在多任务处理时能够更灵活、更准确。

sentences.en: However, Miller wanted to know whether the cortex was truly processing information about two different tasks simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 然而，米勒想知道，这一皮层是否真的在同时处理关于两项不同任务的信息。

sentences.en: He designed an experiment in which he presented visual stimuli to his subjects in a way that mimicked multitasking.
sentences.zh: 他设计了一项实验，以一种模拟多任务处理的方式向受试者呈现视觉刺激。

sentences.en: Miller then attached sensors to the patients’ heads to pick up the electrical patterns of the brain.
sentences.zh: 随后，米勒在受试者头上贴上传感器，以采集大脑的电活动模式。

sentences.en: These sensors would show whether the neurons were truly processing two different tasks.
sentences.zh: 这些传感器会显示出神经元是否真的在处理两项不同的任务。

sentences.en: What he found was that the brain neurons lit up in singular areas one at a time—never simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 他发现的是，大脑神经元是在单个区域里一次一个地亮起来——从不会同时亮起。

sentences.en: D David Meyer, a professor at the University of Michigan, studied young adults in a similar experiment.
sentences.zh: 密歇根大学的教授戴维·迈耶在一项类似的实验中研究了年轻的成年人。

sentences.en: He instructed them to solve math problems while simultaneously classifying simple words into different categories.
sentences.zh: 他指示他们在解数学题的同时，把一些简单的词语归入不同的类别。

sentences.en: Meyer found that when you think you are doing several jobs at the same time, you are actually switching between jobs.
sentences.zh: 迈耶发现，当你以为自己在同时做几件事时，你实际上是在不同的任务之间来回切换。

sentences.en: Even though the participants tried to do the tasks at the same time and both tasks were eventually accomplished, overall the task took more time than if the person had focused on a single task.
sentences.zh: 尽管参与者努力同时完成这些任务，两项任务最终也都完成了，但总体而言，所花的时间比一个人只专注于单项任务时要多。

sentences.en: E People sacrifice efficiency when multitasking.
sentences.zh: 人们在进行多任务处理时牺牲了效率。

sentences.en: Gloria Mark used office workers as her subjects.
sentences.zh: 格洛丽亚·马克以办公室职员作为她的研究对象。

sentences.en: She found that they were constantly multitasking.
sentences.zh: 她发现他们一直在进行多任务处理。

sentences.en: She observed that nearly every 11 minutes people at work were disrupted.
sentences.zh: 她观察到，工作中的人几乎每隔11分钟就会被打断一次。

sentences.en: She found that doing different jobs at the same time may actually save time.
sentences.zh: 她发现，同时做不同的工作实际上可能会节省时间。

sentences.en: However, despite the fact that they are faster, it does not mean they are more efficient.
sentences.zh: 然而，尽管他们更快，但这并不意味着他们更有效率。

sentences.en: We are equally likely to self-interrupt as to be interrupted by outside sources.
sentences.zh: 我们自我打断的可能性，和被外界来源打断的可能性是一样的。

sentences.en: She found that in the office nearly every 12 minutes an employee would stop and, with no reason at all, check a website on their computer, call someone or write an email.
sentences.zh: 她发现，在办公室里，几乎每隔12分钟，一名员工就会停下来，毫无缘由地查看电脑上的某个网页、给某人打电话或写封电子邮件。

sentences.en: If they concentrated for more than 20 minutes, they would feel distressed.
sentences.zh: 如果他们连续专注超过20分钟，就会感到苦恼。

sentences.en: She suggested that the average person may suffer from a short concentration span.
sentences.zh: 她由此提出，普通人也许患有注意力持续时间过短的毛病。

sentences.en: This short attention span might be natural, but others suggest that new technology may be the problem.
sentences.zh: 这种短暂的注意力跨度也许是天生的，但也有人认为，新技术可能才是问题所在。

sentences.en: With cellphones and computers at our sides at all times, people will never run out of distractions.
sentences.zh: 手机和电脑时刻伴随在我们身边，人们将永远不缺让自己分心的东西。

sentences.en: The format of media—such as advertisements, music, news articles and TV shows—is also shortening, so people are used to paying attention to information for a very short time.
sentences.zh: 媒体的形式——比如广告、音乐、新闻报道和电视节目——也在变短，因此人们习惯于只在很短的时间里关注一条信息。

sentences.en: F Even though focusing on a single task is the most efficient way for our brains to work, it is not always practical in real life.
sentences.zh: 尽管专注于单项任务是我们大脑最高效的工作方式，但它在现实生活中并不总是切合实际。

sentences.en: According to human nature, people feel more comfortable and efficient in environments with a variety of tasks.
sentences.zh: 依照人的天性，人们在任务多样的环境中会感到更舒适、更有效率。

sentences.en: Edward Hallowell said that people are losing a lot of efficiency in the workplace due to multitasking, outside distractions and self-distractions.
sentences.zh: 爱德华·哈洛韦尔说，由于多任务处理、外界干扰和自我干扰，人们在职场上正损失大量的效率。

sentences.en: In fact, the changes made to the workplace do not have to be dramatic.
sentences.zh: 事实上，对职场所做的改变不必是翻天覆地的。

sentences.en: No one is suggesting we ban e-mail or make employees focus on only one task.
sentences.zh: 没有人主张我们禁用电子邮件，或让员工只专注于一项任务。

sentences.en: However, certain common workplace situations—such as group meetings—would be more efficient if we banned cellphones, a common distraction.
sentences.zh: 然而，某些常见的职场情形——比如小组会议——如果我们禁用手机这一常见的干扰源，会更有效率。

sentences.en: A person can also apply these tips to prevent self-distraction.
sentences.zh: 一个人也可以运用这些诀窍来防止自我分心。

sentences.en: Instead of arriving at the office and checking all of your e-mails for new tasks—a common ritual—you could dedicate an hour to a single task first thing in the morning.
sentences.zh: 与其一到办公室就查看所有的电子邮件、寻找新任务——这是一种常见的习惯——你不如在早晨一开始就拿出一个小时专注于一项任务。

sentences.en: Self-timing is a great way to reduce distraction and finish tasks one by one, instead of slowing ourselves down with multitasking.
sentences.zh: 自我计时是一种很好的办法，可以减少分心，把任务一件接一件地完成，而不是用多任务处理拖慢自己。

sentences.en: (A) We can choose our friends, the saying goes, but we cannot choose our family of origin.
sentences.zh: 俗话说，我们可以选择朋友，但无法选择我们的原生家庭。

sentences.en: Our parents provide the genetic material and make powerful early role models, but even more influential in determining what kind of adult we will become are our brothers and sisters — our siblings.
sentences.zh: 父母提供遗传材料，并是早期强有力的榜样，但比这更影响我们成为什么样的成年人的，是我们的兄弟姐妹——即我们的同胞。

sentences.en: They occupy a position of unique intimacy in our lives and cast a longer shadow than many recognise or are prepared to acknowledge.
sentences.zh: 他们在我们的生命中占据着独特的亲密位置，所投下的影子比许多人意识到或愿意承认的更长。

sentences.en: By turns, enraging and lovable, familiar and mysterious, our brothers and sisters are the human beings who people our first social relationships.
sentences.zh: 我们的兄弟姐妹时而令人生气、时而可爱，时而熟悉、时而神秘，是我们最初社会关系中的人。

sentences.en: And a sibling relationship is the most enduring relationship many of us will ever have — no less emotionally intense than the bonds we form with our spouses and our own children — if only because they started when we were so young.
sentences.zh: 对许多人而言，兄弟姐妹关系是一生中最持久的关系——其情感强度不亚于我们与配偶和孩子建立的纽带——只因它在我们很小的时候就开始了。

sentences.en: (B) Surprising new research by Dr Gene Brody found that having older children who do well in school and are well liked by other children leads to parental ‘basking’ — increasing mothers’ self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 基因·布罗迪博士（Dr Gene Brody）一项令人惊讶的新研究发现，年长的孩子在学校表现好、且受其他孩子喜爱，会带来父母的“沐浴”感——母亲的自尊提升。

sentences.en: It is clear that in turn this is associated with more positive parenting of younger children, who display fewer behavioural problems as a result.
sentences.zh: 显然，这又与对年幼孩子的更正面养育相关联，从而使他们表现出更少行为问题。

sentences.en: Conversely, parents who get a difficult first child may in turn experience a negative spiral of household tension.
sentences.zh: 反过来，如果父母有一个难带的头胎，则可能陷入家庭紧张的恶性循环之中。

sentences.en: (C) International sports star Piri Weepu is a rugby hard man, but at least some of his tough temperament was forged long ago in the family home.
sentences.zh: 国际体育明星皮里·维普（Piri Weepu）是橄榄球场上的硬汉，但他强硬性情的至少一部分早在家庭中就已铸就。

sentences.en: His older brother Billy started rugby — tackling little Piri when he was just four — to ‘harden him up’.
sentences.zh: 他的哥哥比利在皮里只有四岁时就开始打橄榄球——把小皮里铲倒——为的是“把他练硬”。

sentences.en: It seemed to work.
sentences.zh: 看来这奏效了。

sentences.en: Piri followed his brother in playing for the under-sevens league before he even started school.
sentences.zh: 皮里还没上学就跟着哥哥参加了七岁以下的联赛。

sentences.en: There are as many such stories as there are families: in the formative hothouse of the family, siblings interact in complex ways with the powerful forcefields of parents, genetics and personality already at work.
sentences.zh: 这样的故事和家庭一样多：在家庭这个塑造性的温室里，兄弟姐妹与父母、遗传和性格这些已经运作的强大力场进行着复杂互动。

sentences.en: It starts with birth order, which determines play roles: the firstborn leader, the middle-child mediator and the rebellious youngest.
sentences.zh: 它从出生顺序开始——这决定了游戏中的角色：领头的老大、调停的中间子和反叛的老幺。

sentences.en: These are roles that can stick for life.
sentences.zh: 这些角色可能伴随终身。

sentences.en: (D) Clinical psychologist Claire Cartwright says she has clients who believe, and it might not have been true, that they were treated differently from their siblings, that one child in the family was preferred over others.
sentences.zh: 临床心理学家克莱尔·卡特赖特（Claire Cartwright）说，她有客户相信——虽然这未必是真的——自己与兄弟姐妹被区别对待，家中有一个孩子比其他人更受偏爱。

sentences.en: They are quite convinced that the parental judgements on them all those years ago were harsher, and that they were the ones who always got into trouble.
sentences.zh: 他们深信，那么多年前父母对他们的评判更为严苛，而自己总是惹麻烦的那一个。

sentences.en: Later, in the workplace, such a person might be particularly defensive, and so behave in a way more prone to attracting harsh judgements.
sentences.zh: 后来在工作场所，这样的人可能特别防御性强，行为反而更容易招来严厉的评判。

sentences.en: (E)However, the research shows that being Mummy or Daddy’s favourite has its own traps.
sentences.zh: 然而，研究表明，做爸爸妈妈的最爱也有自己的陷阱。

sentences.en: If you were the easy-going, co-operative child at home, you probably excelled at pleasing parents and, later, bosses.
sentences.zh: 如果你是家里随和、合作的孩子，那你可能擅长讨好父母，后来也擅长讨好上司。

sentences.en: But you might, as an adult, find it hard to be assertive with authority figures and lack direction.
sentences.zh: 但作为成年人，你可能很难对权威人物坚持己见，并缺乏方向感。

sentences.en: On the other hand, the sibling who is disruptive and annoying as a child may be able to reinterpret that role later, turning those attention-seeking characteristics into strengths like determination and leadership.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，作为孩子时调皮、惹人厌的兄弟姐妹，可能后来能够重新解读这种角色——把那些寻求关注的特质转化为决心和领导力等优势。

sentences.en: (F) How is it that full siblings, despite sharing DNA, can turn out so differently?
sentences.zh: 亲生兄弟姐妹尽管共享 DNA，为何会变得如此不同？

sentences.en: One answer is that, in fact, each sibling grows up in a different family, a unique micro-culture.
sentences.zh: 一个答案是：实际上，每个兄弟姐妹长大于不同的家庭——一种独特的小文化。

sentences.en: For example, the firstborn is, for a while, an only child, and therefore has a completely different experience of the parents than those born later.
sentences.zh: 例如，老大有一段时间是独生子女，因此对父母的体验与之后出生的孩子截然不同。

sentences.en: The parents themselves are growing up too, weathering hardship or good fortune, so one sibling might experience stability and closeness while another might be raised in the midst of crisis.
sentences.zh: 父母自己也在成长，经历艰辛或好运，所以一个孩子可能体验到稳定与亲密，而另一个则可能是在危机中被抚养长大。

sentences.en: (G) Of course, there are many positive aspects of sibling relationships.
sentences.zh: 当然，兄弟姐妹关系也有许多积极方面。

sentences.en: Annette Henderson, a lecturer in psychology, says firstborn children learn vocabulary more quickly than their siblings because they are not competing to spend one-on-one time with parents.
sentences.zh: 心理学讲师安妮特·亨德森（Annette Henderson）说，头胎的孩子比弟妹学习词汇更快，因为他们不必去争夺与父母一对一相处的时间。

sentences.en: But younger children in turn benefit from unintentional instruction from their bigger brothers and sisters, acquiring entire phrases and an understanding of social concepts such as politeness.
sentences.zh: 但弟妹反过来又受益于哥哥姐姐无意中的“教导”，习得整个短语并理解礼貌等社交概念。

sentences.en: Similarly, a Cambridge University study of 140 children found that even when there is a great deal of conflict, siblings will still create a rich world of play and make-believe that extends them developmentally.
sentences.zh: 同样，剑桥大学一项对 140 名儿童的研究发现，即使存在大量冲突，兄弟姐妹仍会创造一个丰富的玩耍和假想世界，在发展上拓展他们。

sentences.en: Love-hate relationships were common among the children, but even those who fought the most had as many positive interactions as the other sibling pairs.
sentences.zh: 爱恨交织的关系在这些孩子中很常见，但即便最爱打架的那些孩子，与其他兄弟姐妹相比，所拥有的积极互动一样多。

sentences.en: It is also true that children compete for parental attention by making themselves different from their brothers and sisters, particularly if they are close in age.
sentences.zh: 同样真实的是，孩子会通过让自己与兄弟姐妹不同来争取父母关注，尤其在年龄相近时。

sentences.en: A 2003 research paper studied adolescents from 185 families over two years, finding that those who changed to differentiate themselves from their siblings increased the amount of warmth they gained from parents, and also developed stronger personalities and a better sense of their own identity.
sentences.zh: 2003 年一篇研究论文跟踪了 185 个家庭的青少年两年，发现那些通过改变自己来与兄弟姐妹区分开来的青少年，从父母那里获得的温情有所增加，性格也更强、对自我身份的把握更好。

sentences.en: (H) Another consideration is that many families today are smaller and more intimate than their historical counterparts.
sentences.zh: 另一个考虑因素是，今天许多家庭比历史上的家庭更小、更亲密。

sentences.en: This may be advantageous because siblings tend to know each other better and remain lifelong friends compared to children from bigger or more widely spaced families, who perhaps lose touch with one another after leaving home.
sentences.zh: 这或许是有利的，因为与来自更大家庭或年龄间隔更大家庭的孩子（他们可能在离家后失去联系）相比，兄弟姐妹之间往往更彼此了解、并保持终身的友谊。

sentences.en: Then there was a 2010 American study which found that having a sister, whether younger or older, meant that 10- to 14-year-olds were less likely to feel lonely, unloved, self-conscious or fearful.
sentences.zh: 还有一项 2010 年的美国研究发现，无论是妹妹还是姐姐，有姐妹意味着 10—14 岁的孩子更不容易感到孤独、不被爱、自我意识过强或恐惧。

sentences.en: The same study found that having a loving sibling of either gender promoted good deeds, such as helping a neighbour around the house or helping other children at school.
sentences.zh: 同一项研究还发现，无论性别，有一个有爱的兄弟姐妹会促进做好事，例如在家中帮邻居、或在学校里帮其他孩子。

sentences.en: (A) Why is musical behavior universal?
sentences.zh: 为什么音乐行为是普世的？

sentences.en: What could be its adaptive, or survival, value?
sentences.zh: 它的适应性、或生存价值可能是什么？

sentences.en: And just what is music anyway?
sentences.zh: 而音乐究竟是什么？

sentences.en: Like speech, it is not one identifiable cognitive capacity but is composed of multiple separate components.
sentences.zh: 和语言一样，音乐不是一种可识别的认知能力，而是由多个独立成分构成的。

sentences.en: Pitch recognition varies from ‘tone deaf’ to ‘perfect’ and influences abilities for musical memory, discrimination of melodies, awareness of changing harmony, and even the ability to keep time.
sentences.zh: 对音高的识别能力从“五音不全”到“完美”不等，并影响音乐记忆、旋律辨别、对和声变化的察觉、甚至对节拍的把握。

sentences.en: Other components of music include perception of melody, meter, and rhythm.
sentences.zh: 音乐的其他成分包括对旋律、拍子和节奏的感知。

sentences.en: Often disregarded are additional important abilities to synchronize and take turns.
sentences.zh: 常被忽视的还有“同步”和“轮替”等重要能力。

sentences.en: Individuals vary in their endowment of these different features, and individual cultures vary in the importance they give to a particular musical feature.
sentences.zh: 个体在这些不同特征上的禀赋各有差异，不同文化对某一特定音乐特征的重视程度也各不相同。

sentences.en: (B) Steven Mithen, a cognitive archeologist and professor of early prehistory at Reading University in England, has boldly tackled the difficult subject of the origin and adaptive value of human music.
sentences.zh: 史蒂文·米森（Steven Mithen）——英格兰雷丁大学的认知考古学家、早期史前史教授——大胆触及了一个困难的话题：人类音乐的起源与适应价值。

sentences.en: Whether or not one is convinced by his concluding hypothesis, his book The Singing Neanderthals* is a treasure trove of information and analysis relevant to understanding the evolution of music.
sentences.zh: 无论人们是否被他最后的假说所说服，他的著作《会唱歌的尼安德特人》（The Singing Neanderthals）是与理解音乐演化相关的信息和分析的宝库。

sentences.en: Anyone who subsequently proposes another hypothesis will not be able to neglect the knowledge and questions set forth by Mithen, nor can his conclusions be ignored, based as they are on careful consideration and synthesis of this vast range of specialist material.
sentences.zh: 此后任何提出另一种假说的人都无法忽视米森所提出的知识和问题，也不能忽视他基于对这片庞大专业材料的细致考量与综合所得的结论。

sentences.en: (C) Mithen rightly pays tribute to his predecessors in the study of the evolution of music, including John Blacking (1973) and Nils Wallin (1991).
sentences.zh: 米森恰当地向他在音乐演化研究领域的前辈致敬，包括约翰·布莱金（John Blacking，1973 年）和尼尔斯·瓦林（Nils Wallin，1991 年）。

sentences.en: Although both contributed important insights and were themselves musically trained, they did not (and at the time could not) command the resources Mithen brings to bear.
sentences.zh: 虽然二位都贡献了重要洞见，并且本身受过音乐训练，但他们并未（且当时也不可能）调动米森所运用的那些资源。

sentences.en: (D) Anthropologist and performing classical musician Blacking’s ideas lacked evidence from archeology and neurology, while neuroscientist and musicologist Wallin neglected paleontology and ethnomusicology.
sentences.zh: 作为人类学家和古典音乐演奏者的布莱金，其想法缺乏来自考古学和神经学的证据；而作为神经科学家和音乐学家的瓦林，则忽视了古生物学和民族音乐学。

sentences.en: Mithen considers ideas proposed in more recent comprehensive evolutionary hypotheses of music and incorporates them into the strands that he gradually weaves into two major themes.
sentences.zh: 米森考虑了近期在更全面的音乐演化假说中提出的想法，并把它们融入他逐步编织成两条主要主题的线索中。

sentences.en: The first, proposed in a preliminary form by Steven Brown (2000), is the co-evolution of what we today call music and language.
sentences.zh: 第一条由史蒂文·布朗（Steven Brown，2000 年）以初步形式提出——我们今天称之为音乐与语言的共同演化。

sentences.en: The second is a completely original hypothesis of the existence among Neanderthals of a proto music language that was holistic (not composed of segmented elements), manipulative (influencing emotional states and hence responses of oneself and others), multimodal (using both sound and movement), musical (temporally controlled, rhythmic, and melodic), and mimetic (utilizing sound symbolism and gesture) — what Mithen terms ‘the “Hmmmmm” communication system …
sentences.zh: 第二条是一个完全原创的假说：尼安德特人中存在一种原始的“音乐—语言”——它是整体的（不由分段元素构成）、操控性的（影响情绪状态、从而影响自我和他人的反应）、多模态的（同时使用声音和动作）、音乐性的（在时间上受控、有节奏且有旋律）、模仿性的（运用声音象征和姿态）——米森称之为“”Hmmmmm“沟通系统……

sentences.en: a prelinguistic musical mode of thought and action.’
sentences.zh: 一种前语言的、音乐性的思维与行动模式。“

sentences.en: (E) Mithen’s hypotheses account for important aspects that are usually excluded in the majority of discussions of music: he appreciates that it typically includes bodily movement (toe tapping, head-nodding, hand-clapping, and dance) and that ‘music-making is first and foremost a shared activity, not just in the modern Western world, but throughout human cultures and history.’
sentences.zh: 米森的假说说明了在大多数音乐讨论中通常被排除的重要方面：他理解到音乐通常包括身体的动作（脚跟轻点、点头、拍手和舞蹈），并且“音乐创作首先是一种共享的活动，不仅在当代西方世界，在整个人类文化与历史中都是如此”。

sentences.en: Although he does not describe the musical behavior of Mbuti or Ba Benjellé pygmies in Central Africa, or Kaluli villagers in the Southern Highlands of Papua New Guinea, as others have done, such small-scale societies well illustrate the ubiquity (and complexity) of communal singing during most daily activity — ‘woven tapestries’ (Meurant 1995) of sound that may even incorporate the natural sounds of the forest (Feld 2001).
sentences.zh: 虽然他没有像别人那样描述中部非洲姆布蒂人（Mbuti）或巴本杰勒人（Ba Benjellé）矮人，或巴布亚新几内亚南部高地卡卢利村民的音乐行为，但这些小规模社会很好地说明了在日常活动中合唱（以及其复杂性）的无处不在——“声音织成的挂毯”（Meurant，1995 年）——甚至可能融入森林中的自然之声（Feld，2001 年）。

sentences.en: (F) Especially welcome to communication and cognitive studies in general is Mithen’s emphasis on the importance of acquiring emotional intelligence — the ability to communicate one’s feelings with face, voice, and body, and to decode the emotional signals of others in increasingly complex social interactions.
sentences.zh: 对沟通与认知研究整体而言，米森对获取情感智能之重要性的强调尤其受欢迎——即用面部、声音和身体传达自己感受的能力，以及在日益复杂的社会互动中解码他人情感信号的能力。

sentences.en: Mithen proposes that ‘vocal grooming’ (Aiello and Dunbar 1993) would have been initially musical more than verbal.
sentences.zh: 米森提出，“声音梳理”（Aiello 与 Dunbar，1993 年）最初更多是音乐性的，而非言语性的。

sentences.en: Rather than emphasizing the competitive advantages of comprehending the intentions and desires of others, Mithen points out that the emotional content of musical vocalizations would have been more ‘honest’ than words — contributing to social commitment and expressing, inducing, and sharing emotion, especially happiness, thereby promoting selectively advantageous cooperative behavior.
sentences.zh: 与其强调理解他人意图和欲望所带来的竞争优势，米森指出音乐性的发声所传达的情感内容比词语更“诚实”——这有助于社会承诺，并表达、诱发和分享情感，尤其是快乐，从而推动具有选择优势的合作行为。

sentences.en: (G) Mithen appreciates that behavior may have had more than one adaptive function — and admits that, at least in homo ergaster (a common ancestor of both Neanderthals and homo sapiens), ‘singing and dancing may have provided both indicator and esthetic traits for females when choosing mates.’
sentences.zh: 米森理解到一种行为可能不止有一种适应性功能——并承认，至少在直立人（homo ergaster，尼安德特人和智人共同的祖先）身上，“唱歌和跳舞可能为女性在择偶时提供了既作为指标又作为审美特征的特质”。

sentences.en: However, he disagrees completely with the now notorious pronouncement by Steven Pinker (1997) that music, although derived from other adaptive capacities, is itself peripheral and even nonadaptive — like a taste for sugar or fat.
sentences.zh: 然而，他完全不同意如今臭名昭著的史蒂文·平克（Steven Pinker，1997 年）的论断——即音乐尽管派生自其他适应性能力，但其本身是边缘性的、甚至非适应性的——就像对糖或脂肪的偏好。

sentences.en: Music, says Mithen, is too different from language (or anything else) to be a spin-off.
sentences.zh: 米森说，音乐与语言（或任何别的东西）的不同太大，它不可能是某种“副产品”。

sentences.en: He makes the further point that the emotional power of music indicates a long evolutionary history, not a recent invention aimed at pleasure: ‘We don’t have emotions for fun.’
sentences.zh: 他进一步指出，音乐的情感力量表明其有漫长的演化史，而非一项为取悦而生的近期发明：“我们并不是为了好玩才有情感”。

sentences.en: (H) The book is both thought-provoking and informative, but some of Mithen’s claims are questionable.
sentences.zh: 这本书既发人深省又富有信息含量，但米森的某些主张是值得质疑的。

sentences.en: He thinks that modern humans are relatively limited in their musical abilities compared to Neanderthals.
sentences.zh: 他认为，与尼安德特人相比，现代人在音乐能力上是相对受限的。

sentences.en: He suggests that the evolution of language has inhibited the musical abilities that modern humans have inherited from the common ancestor that we share with Neanderthals.
sentences.zh: 他暗示，语言的演化抑制了现代人从我们与尼安德特人共享的祖先那里继承来的音乐能力。

sentences.en: Yet here I think he slips into the Westernized assumptions about music that he decries elsewhere and reveals his own weak spot — insufficient acquaintance with the ethnomusicological literature.
sentences.zh: 然而我认为他在此处滑入了他在别处所批评的对音乐的西方化假设，并暴露了他自己的弱点——对民族音乐学文献了解不足。

sentences.en: It is not spoken language itself that stunts musical ability, but the factors in modernized societies that have made music a specialty — individuality, competitiveness, compartmentalization, and institutionalization — reinforced by the high degree of literate training required to read (and compose) musical scores as well as literary texts.
sentences.zh: 使音乐能力萎缩的并不是口语本身，而是现代化社会中那些把音乐变成一种“专业”的因素——个性化、竞争性、条块化和制度化——再加上阅读（和创作）乐谱以及文学文本所需的高度识字训练。

sentences.en: In small-scale pre-modern societies, everyone participates in music — regularly, spontaneously, and wholeheartedly — and benefits thereby from the many adaptive advantages Mithen recognizes and so expertly describes.
sentences.zh: 在小规模前现代社会中，每个人都参与音乐——经常地、自发地、全心全意地——并因此从米森所认识到并出色描述的诸多适应性优势中受益。

records.title: How do plants talk to each other

sentences.en: A In 1983, plant scientists Jack Schultz and Ian Baldwin reported that the leaves of young maple trees increased their defense systems when exposed to maples that had been damaged by plant-eating (herbivorous) insects.
sentences.zh: 1983年，植物科学家杰克·舒尔茨和伊恩·鲍德温报告说，当幼年枫树暴露在被食植（食草）昆虫损害过的枫树旁时，它们的叶子会增强自身的防御系统。

sentences.en: The injured trees, they suggested, were alerting neighbors to the presence of a predator by releasing chemical signals into the air.
sentences.zh: 他们提出，受伤的树木是通过向空气中释放化学信号，来提醒邻树有捕食者出现。

sentences.en: But the plant research community did not accept this.
sentences.zh: 但植物研究界并不接受这一点。

sentences.en: The results were difficult to replicate, critics pointed out.
sentences.zh: 批评者指出，这些结果很难重现。

sentences.en: Many also questioned how it could be evolutionarily stable if it benefited neighboring plants but not the plant releasing the signal.
sentences.zh: 许多人还质疑，如果它有利于邻近的植物、却无益于释放信号的那株植物，那它在进化上怎么可能是稳定的。

sentences.en: By the late 1980s, most ecologists felt that Schultz and Baldwin’s ideas had been discredited.
sentences.zh: 到20世纪80年代后期，大多数生态学家都认为舒尔茨和鲍德温的想法已经站不住脚。

sentences.en: B A decade later, however, a number of more carefully designed experiments began to yield convincing indications to the contrary.
sentences.zh: 然而，十年之后，一些设计更为缜密的实验开始得出令人信服的相反迹象。

sentences.en: In 2000, evolutionary ecologist Richard Karban showed that wild tobacco plants became resistant to herbivores when grown in close proximity to sagebrush plants whose leaves had been damaged by cutting.
sentences.zh: 2000年，进化生态学家理查德·卡尔班表明，当野生烟草植株紧挨着叶子被切割损伤过的山艾树生长时，它们会变得能够抵御食草动物。

sentences.en: This change appeared to be in response to chemicals – known as volatile organic compounds or VOCs – released by the sagebrush plants.
sentences.zh: 这种变化似乎是对山艾树所释放的化学物质——即所谓挥发性有机化合物（VOC）——的一种反应。

sentences.en: Other researchers soon reported similar VOC-induced defense responses in several other plants, including lima bean, broad bean, barley, and corn.
sentences.zh: 其他研究者很快就报告说，在另外几种植物中也出现了类似的由挥发性有机化合物诱发的防御反应，包括利马豆、蚕豆、大麦和玉米。

sentences.en: And in 2006, Karban showed that VOCs released by damaged sagebrush induce herbivore resistance in plants growing at distances of up to 60 cm, well within the range of sagebrush neighbors in nature.
sentences.zh: 而在2006年，卡尔班表明，受损山艾树释放的挥发性有机化合物，能在距其多达60厘米处生长的植物中诱发抗食草动物的反应，这完全在自然界中山艾树邻株的范围之内。

sentences.en: C But the question still remains: ‘Why should a plant waste valuable resources on a function which has no obvious advantage for it?’
sentences.zh: 但问题依然存在：“一株植物为什么要把宝贵的资源浪费在一项对它没有明显好处的功能上呢？”

sentences.en: One hypothesis is that external communication channels are merely an extension of within-plant signaling.
sentences.zh: 一种假说认为，对外的交流渠道不过是植物体内信号传导的一种延伸。

sentences.en: In sagebrush, lima bean, and poplar, VOCs released from damaged parts of a plant induce resistance in intact sections of the same plant, suggesting that each individual plant uses the signals to coordinate its own physiological responses to protect itself.
sentences.zh: 在山艾树、利马豆和杨树中，植物受损部位释放的挥发性有机化合物，会在同一株植物完好的部分诱发抗性，这表明每一株植物都利用这些信号来协调自身的生理反应以保护自己。

sentences.en: Karban agrees, saying: ‘The interplant signaling we see may be a result of plants co-opting that process.’
sentences.zh: 卡尔班对此表示赞同，他说：“我们所看到的植株间信号传导，可能是植物借用了那一过程的结果。”

sentences.en: Alternatively, VOC-based signaling between plants may have been favored because it enhances the ‘extended fitness’ of the sender by aiding related plants of the same species: a strategy known as kin selection.
sentences.zh: 另一种可能是，植物间基于挥发性有机化合物的信号传导之所以受到青睐，是因为它通过帮助同种的近缘植物，增强了发送者的“广义适合度”：这是一种被称为亲缘选择的策略。

sentences.en: D Over the past few years, a team led by Ariel Novoplansky of Ben-Gurion University of the Negev in Israel seems to have found proof that distress signals can be passed through the plants’ roots.
sentences.zh: 在过去几年里，由以色列内盖夫本-古里安大学的阿里尔·诺沃普兰斯基带领的一个团队，似乎已经找到证据，证明求救信号可以通过植物的根部传递。

sentences.en: They planted garden pea plants in rows and subjected the first in each row to conditions similar to those experienced in a drought.
sentences.zh: 他们把豌豆植株成排种植，并让每一排中的第一株遭受类似于干旱时所经历的条件。

sentences.en: They then evaluated the response by measuring the microscopic holes on leaves, known as pores, which react when there is a shortage of water.
sentences.zh: 随后，他们通过测量叶片上被称为气孔的微小孔洞来评估反应，这些气孔会在缺水时做出反应。

sentences.en: After fifteen minutes, the stressed plant was seen to be closing its pores, followed by all of its neighbors, one by one.
sentences.zh: 十五分钟后，人们看到那株受到胁迫的植物开始关闭气孔，紧接着它所有的邻株也一株接一株地关闭气孔。

sentences.en: Importantly, in a control setup where root contact between neighboring plants was blocked, pores stayed open.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，在一个邻近植株之间的根部接触被阻断的对照装置中，气孔始终保持张开。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, David Johnson’s team at the University of Aberdeen in Scotland have been studying the labyrinths of hair-like fungi that occur around the roots of most plants.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，苏格兰阿伯丁大学戴维·约翰逊的团队，一直在研究存在于大多数植物根部周围、迷宫般的毛发状真菌。

sentences.en: These fungi are involved in an important two-way relationship: in exchange for sugars, they provide plants with much-needed phosphorus and nitrogen.
sentences.zh: 这些真菌参与一种重要的双向关系：作为对糖分的回报，它们为植物提供急需的磷和氮。

sentences.en: Research in which broad bean plants were infested with aphids – small herbivorous insects – revealed that these networks also served as a channel for warning neighboring plants of the infestation.
sentences.zh: 一项让蚕豆植株感染蚜虫——一种食草小昆虫——的研究揭示，这些网络还充当了向邻近植物预警虫害的渠道。

sentences.en: E Monica Gagliano of the University of Western Australia believes that plants may even use sounds to alert their neighbors.
sentences.zh: 西澳大利亚大学的莫妮卡·加利亚诺相信，植物甚至可能用声音来提醒它们的邻株。

sentences.en: In one study, she demonstrated that chili plants growing next to fennel plants developed more quickly than seedlings grown with other chili plants.
sentences.zh: 在一项研究中，她证明，紧挨着茴香生长的辣椒植株，比与其他辣椒植株一起生长的幼苗发育得更快。

sentences.en: Gagliano and her colleagues suspect the chili plants were compensating for the presence of the fennel, which is known to release chemicals that inhibit the growth of other plants.
sentences.zh: 加利亚诺和她的同事猜测，辣椒植株是在补偿茴香的存在，而茴香已知会释放抑制其他植物生长的化学物质。

sentences.en: Remarkably, however, when plant communication pathways – airborne volatiles, root contact, and common fungal networks – were blocked, the results begged for an alternative explanation.
sentences.zh: 然而，值得注意的是，当植物的交流途径——空气中的挥发物、根部接触和共有的真菌网络——都被阻断时，结果却亟须一种别样的解释。

sentences.en: ‘We think this other channel of communication might be acoustic,’ says Gagliano.
sentences.zh: “我们认为，这另一条交流渠道也许是声学的，”加利亚诺说。

sentences.en: But behavioral ecologist Carel ten Cate of the University of Leiden in the Netherlands points out that taking advantage of such benefits would require sensory mechanisms yet to be described in plants.
sentences.zh: 但荷兰莱顿大学的行为生态学家卡雷尔·滕·卡特指出，要利用这类益处，需要植物身上尚未被描述过的感觉机制。

sentences.en: Despite widespread skepticism, Gagliano has received some encouragement.
sentences.zh: 尽管普遍存在质疑，加利亚诺还是得到了一些鼓励。

sentences.en: Richard Karban, for example, is cautiously enthusiastic.
sentences.zh: 例如，理查德·卡尔班就持谨慎的热情态度。

sentences.en: ‘Whether or not the explanation she favors is the right one,’ he says, ‘I think that she’s gotten results that, as a field, we need to come to grips with.’
sentences.zh: “无论她所青睐的那种解释对不对，”他说，“我认为她所得到的结果，是我们作为一个领域需要认真对待的。”

sentences.en: F Researchers believe that knowledge of this phenomenon could eventually be applied to agriculture, and lead to the cultivation of hardier crops.
sentences.zh: 研究者相信，对这一现象的认识最终可以应用于农业，并培育出更耐受的作物。

sentences.en: But all agree that there is still much work to be done.
sentences.zh: 但所有人都一致认为，仍有大量工作有待完成。

sentences.en: ‘Applying our limited knowledge [of plant-communication mechanisms] to agriculture is a big jump,’ says Johnson, ‘but it is definitely on the horizon.’
sentences.zh: “把我们有限的知识（关于植物交流机制的知识）应用到农业上，是一个很大的跨越，”约翰逊说，“但它无疑已近在眼前。”

sentences.en: Nevertheless, one message has emerged loud and clear from those studying this new realm of botanical interaction: despite not possessing eyes, ears, or a nervous system, plants are anything but uncommunicative.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，从那些研究这一植物互动新领域的人那里，已经清晰而响亮地传出一条讯息：尽管植物没有眼睛、耳朵或神经系统，它们却绝非不善交流。

sentences.en: ‘When I started my PhD (in the late 1980s), all this stuff was considered very weird,’ recalls Ariel Novoplansky.
sentences.zh: “我开始读博士时（在20世纪80年代后期），所有这些东西都被认为非常怪异，”阿里尔·诺沃普兰斯基回忆道。

sentences.en: ‘Today, there is no doubt.
sentences.zh: “而今天，已不容置疑。

sentences.en: We now recognise that plants are capable of some very sophisticated exchanges of information with other plants.
sentences.zh: 我们如今认识到，植物能够与其他植物进行某些非常复杂的信息交流。

sentences.en: This idea is not strange anymore.’
sentences.zh: 这个想法不再奇怪了。”

records.title: Nanotechnology the science of the very small
records.titleZh: 纳米技术，微观世界的科学

sentences.en: A Nanoscience and nanotechnology have become very fashionable in recent times.
sentences.zh: 纳米科学和纳米技术近来变得非常时髦。

sentences.en: Their prominence has inspired science fiction and raised a lot of hope and hype about the possibilities.
sentences.zh: 它们的显赫地位激发了科幻作品，也引发了关于其种种可能性的大量希望与炒作。

sentences.en: But what exactly is nanotechnology?
sentences.zh: 但纳米技术究竟是什么呢？

sentences.en: Most definitions agree that it is the manufacture of structures that measure up to 100 nanometres (nm).
sentences.zh: 大多数定义都认同，它是对尺寸最大达100纳米（nm）的结构的制造。

sentences.en: The diameter of an atom is typically only two or three tenths of a nanometre while that of the human hair is around 1,000,000 nm.
sentences.zh: 一个原子的直径通常只有十分之二到十分之三纳米，而人类头发的直径约为1000000纳米。

sentences.en: Essentially, we are now able to build new structures from atoms and molecules as if we were using the bricks of a children’s construction toy.
sentences.zh: 从根本上说，我们如今能够用原子和分子来搭建新的结构，就好像我们在用一套儿童积木玩具的砖块一样。

sentences.en: B Most of the electronic consumer goods that we use today contain components that measure less than 100 nm.
sentences.zh: 我们今天所使用的大多数电子消费品，都含有尺寸小于100纳米的元件。

sentences.en: The lasers in our CD and DVD players make use of the properties of semiconductor layers that are just a few atoms in thickness, so we clearly are in the nanotechnology age.
sentences.zh: 我们CD和DVD播放机里的激光器，利用了仅有几个原子厚度的半导体层的特性，因此我们显然身处纳米技术时代。

sentences.en: There are many other everyday items that we take for granted that have nanoparticles in them.
sentences.zh: 还有许多我们习以为常的日常物品，里面也含有纳米颗粒。

sentences.en: One of these is sunscreen.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是防晒霜。

sentences.en: In the 1990s there were safety issues with many of the sunscreen products available, so scientists at Oxford University set about finding a solution.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪90年代，市面上许多防晒产品都存在安全问题，于是牛津大学的科学家着手寻找一个解决办法。

sentences.en: The product they developed uses nanoparticles of titanium dioxide that are doped with the element manganese.
sentences.zh: 他们研制的产品使用了掺入锰元素的二氧化钛纳米颗粒。

sentences.en: This product is almost transparent to the eye when spread on the skin, and it is effective for much longer than many of the traditional preparations.
sentences.zh: 这种产品涂在皮肤上时，肉眼看去几乎是透明的，而且它的有效时间比许多传统制剂要长得多。

sentences.en: In this case, we see an example of nanotechnology providing a solution to an existing problem rather than opening up new product areas.
sentences.zh: 在这个例子中，我们看到的是纳米技术为一个既有问题提供解决方案的范例，而不是开辟新的产品领域。

sentences.en: C The technique of using nanotechnology to adapt existing products can also be applied to garments, upholstery, paint, and plastics to improve their longevity.
sentences.zh: 用纳米技术改良既有产品的这种手法，也可以应用于服装、软垫家具、油漆和塑料，以提高它们的耐久性。

sentences.en: Bearing this in mind, it is interesting to ask whether nanotechnology can help with some of the world’s major current issues.
sentences.zh: 考虑到这一点，有意思的是要问一问，纳米技术能否帮助解决当今世界的一些重大问题。

sentences.en: The recent growth in climate change awareness calls a range of things into question.
sentences.zh: 近来对气候变化日益增强的意识，使一系列问题受到追问。

sentences.en: Can we use energy more effectively?
sentences.zh: 我们能更有效地利用能源吗？

sentences.en: Can we reduce the carbon dioxide in the atmosphere?
sentences.zh: 我们能减少大气中的二氧化碳吗？

sentences.en: Can we use and purify water more effectively?
sentences.zh: 我们能更有效地利用和净化水吗？

sentences.en: Can health care be improved?
sentences.zh: 医疗保健能得到改善吗？

sentences.en: Nanotechnology may very well provide the solutions.
sentences.zh: 纳米技术很可能会提供解决方案。

sentences.en: There are few times in history when the application of science to improving the human condition has been so apparent.
sentences.zh: 在历史上，科学的应用如此明显地用于改善人类境况的时刻屈指可数。

sentences.en: D We are already making new types of solar cells and batteries by using our newfound ability to manipulate matter at the atomic and molecular scale.
sentences.zh: 我们已经在利用自己新获得的在原子和分子尺度上操控物质的能力，制造新型的太阳能电池和电池。

sentences.en: If we can capture some of the huge quantities of energy that arrive at the Earth’s surface from the Sun, and store it effectively, we can reduce the need for fossil fuel-based power stations.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能捕获从太阳抵达地球表面的巨量能量中的一部分，并把它有效地储存起来，我们就能减少对以化石燃料为基础的发电站的需求。

sentences.en: We are already using nanoparticles and nanoporous materials to capture harmful greenhouse gases, and we may possibly convert some of them back into fuel.
sentences.zh: 我们已经在使用纳米颗粒和纳米多孔材料来捕集有害的温室气体，并且我们或许有可能把其中一些重新转化为燃料。

sentences.en: There are, however, many technical problems involved, and it will be another decade or so before some of these ideas are deployed.
sentences.zh: 然而，其中涉及许多技术难题，还要再过十年左右，这些设想中的一部分才会得到应用。

sentences.en: E Water purification is increasingly challenging and many believe that water, which we take for granted, is going to become more valuable than oil.
sentences.zh: 水的净化越来越具有挑战性，许多人相信，被我们视为理所当然的水，将变得比石油更宝贵。

sentences.en: Currently we do not use water efficiently, and many industrial and food processes leave contamination in water that is potentially toxic and difficult to remove.
sentences.zh: 目前我们对水的利用并不高效，而许多工业和食品加工过程会在水中留下可能有毒、难以去除的污染。

sentences.en: Nanofiltration may provide the solution to these problems, and may also offer new routes to the desalination of brackish water and groundwater in some parts of the world.
sentences.zh: 纳米过滤也许能为这些问题提供解决方案，也可能为世界某些地区微咸水和地下水的淡化提供新的途径。

sentences.en: F Food production and processing are becoming more important as the world’s population increases.
sentences.zh: 随着世界人口的增长，粮食的生产和加工正变得越来越重要。

sentences.en: There are concerns that potentially harmful nano-products might enter the body via the gut.
sentences.zh: 有人担心，具有潜在危害的纳米产品可能会经由肠道进入人体。

sentences.en: Such concerns are being addressed, but it is even more important to ask questions about how nanotechnology might increase the nutritious yield of food and be adapted to help preserve and package food.
sentences.zh: 这类担忧正在得到应对，但更重要的是要追问：纳米技术可以如何提高食物的营养产出，又可以如何被加以改造来帮助保存和包装食物。

sentences.en: There is already evidence to show that it might also be helpful in the primary production of raw food materials, by way of better delivery of pesticides in the field and better extraction of protein and carbohydrates.
sentences.zh: 已经有证据表明，它在原料食材的初级生产中或许也有帮助，途径是在田间更好地施用农药，以及更好地提取蛋白质和碳水化合物。

sentences.en: G Healthcare is an area where the application of nanotechnology is already exceeding the expectations of ten years ago.
sentences.zh: 在医疗保健领域，纳米技术的应用已经超出了十年前的预期。

sentences.en: It is happening across several fronts: better appreciation of what the ‘natural’ nanoparticles circulating in body fluid do; better methods of delivering drugs to the body via nanoparticles that target the diseased body part; improvements to the diagnostic imaging techniques of ultrasound, magnetic resonance imaging and X-ray computerised tomography.
sentences.zh: 它正在多条战线上推进：更好地认识在体液中循环的“天然”纳米颗粒的作用；通过靶向患病身体部位的纳米颗粒，以更好的方法向体内输送药物；以及改进超声、磁共振成像和X射线计算机断层扫描等诊断成像技术。

sentences.en: We are now at the threshold of a new subject, ‘theranostics’, whereby nanoparticles will first deliver the diagnostic information to the clinician and then, using the same particle, deliver a form of therapy.
sentences.zh: 我们如今正站在一门新学科“诊疗一体学”的门槛上，借助它，纳米颗粒将先把诊断信息送达临床医生，然后用同一颗粒输送一种形式的治疗。

sentences.en: H Nanotechnology is a life-changing technology, making the quality of life better, enabling us to make use of our resources more effectively, thereby protecting our environment, and creating new business opportunities.
sentences.zh: 纳米技术是一项改变生活的技术，它让生活质量变得更好，使我们能更有效地利用资源，从而保护我们的环境，并创造新的商机。

sentences.en: There are many other examples in the world of ‘new materials’ that also make use of nanotechnology.
sentences.zh: 在“新材料”的世界里，还有许多其他同样运用了纳米技术的例子。

sentences.en: The possibilities may well be limitless.
sentences.zh: 其种种可能性很可能是无穷无尽的。

records.title: The return of the black-footed ferret

sentences.en: A The black-footed ferret (Mustela nigripes) is a small carnivorous mammal, similar in length to a domestic cat, and is the only ferret species native to North America.
sentences.zh: 黑足鼬（Mustela nigripes）是一种小型食肉哺乳动物，长度与家猫相似，是北美唯一的本土鼬属物种。

sentences.en: For at least 100,000 years they lived in an area that extended almost uninterrupted from southern Canada to northern Mexico.
sentences.zh: 至少10万年来，它们生活在一片从加拿大南部几乎不间断延伸到墨西哥北部的区域。

sentences.en: But numbers fell dramatically throughout the 19th and 20th centuries, to such an extent that the black-footed ferret was declared ‘possibly extinct’.
sentences.zh: 但在整个19和20世纪，数量急剧下降，以至于黑足鼬被宣布为“可能灭绝”。

sentences.en: Then, almost miraculously, it returned from the dead.
sentences.zh: 然后，几乎奇迹般地，它从灭绝中归来。

sentences.en: B Within the genus Mustela, the ferret belongs to the subgenus Putorius, of which there are only three extant species: the European polecat; the Siberian polecat; and the black-footed ferret.
sentences.zh: 在鼬属之内，黑足鼬属于臭鼬亚属，该亚属只有三个现存物种，欧洲艾鼬、西伯利亚艾鼬和黑足鼬。

sentences.en: The European polecat lives in open forests and meadows, and is thought to be the ancestor of the domestic ferret.
sentences.zh: 欧洲艾鼬生活在开阔的森林和草甸里，被认为是家养雪貂的祖先。

sentences.en: The Siberian polecat looks more similar to the black-footed ferret, and leads a similar life on open grasslands and semi-desert regions across Russia, China and Siberia.
sentences.zh: 西伯利亚艾鼬看起来与黑足鼬更相似，在俄罗斯、中国和西伯利亚各地开阔的草原和半沙漠地区过着相似的生活。

sentences.en: C Ferrets probably evolved in Europe between three and four million years ago, and dispersed into North America across an ice-age land bridge at least two million years ago.
sentences.zh: 鼬大概在三四百万年前于欧洲进化，并在至少两百万年前经由一座冰河时期的陆桥扩散到北美。

sentences.en: They then advanced south-eastward to the Great Plains through ice-free passageways.
sentences.zh: 它们随后通过无冰的通道向东南推进到大平原。

sentences.en: The black-footed ferret’s history in North America is inextricably linked to the creature which became almost its sole prey — the prairie dog.
sentences.zh: 黑足鼬在北美的历史与那种几乎成为它唯一猎物的生物——草原犬鼠——密不可分。

sentences.en: These small rodents are a type of ground squirrel which live in networks of underground tunnels, known as burrows.
sentences.zh: 这些小型啮齿动物是一种地松鼠，生活在被称为洞穴的地下隧道网络里。

sentences.en: The black-footed ferret’s short legs and long, slim body make it superbly adapted for life in the burrow systems of its prey.
sentences.zh: 黑足鼬短短的腿和又长又细的身体使它极好地适应了在其猎物洞穴系统中的生活。

sentences.en: D Spending virtually all their time underground, black-footed ferrets have always been elusive.
sentences.zh: 黑足鼬几乎所有时间都在地下度过，一向行踪难觅。

sentences.en: Ferrets are never mentioned in accounts of the early explorers or pioneers who crossed the Great Plains by wagon train during the early to mid-1800s.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪初到中叶乘坐大篷车队穿越大平原的早期探险家或拓荒者的记述中，从未提到过鼬。

sentences.en: They were, however, occasionally listed in records kept by fur companies in the upper Missouri River basin during that period.
sentences.zh: 然而，那一时期上密苏里河流域毛皮公司所保存的记录里偶尔列有它们。

sentences.en: Black-footed ferrets were not officially recognized by scientists until 1851, when a description and drawing of one featured in a book by the renowned naturalist John James Audubon and Reverend John Bachman.
sentences.zh: 黑足鼬直到1851年才被科学家正式承认，当时著名博物学家John James Audubon和John Bachman牧师的一本书中刊载了一只黑足鼬的描述和图画。

sentences.en: For over two decades, no other specimens were seen, and scientists even began to question their existence.
sentences.zh: 二十多年里，没有再见到其他标本，科学家甚至开始质疑它们的存在。

sentences.en: Then, in 1874, a Dr Elliott Coues issued a request for specimens through the popular magazine The American Sportsman, and was soon rewarded.
sentences.zh: 然后，在1874年，一位Elliott Coues博士通过当时流行的杂志《The American Sportsman》发出征集标本的请求，很快就有了回报。

sentences.en: With these he was able to add to Audubon’s description, and confirm the existence of the black-footed ferret.
sentences.zh: 凭借这些，他得以补充Audubon的描述，并确认了黑足鼬的存在。

sentences.en: E In the decades that followed, European settlement across North America changed the landscape dramatically, with vast areas being transformed into crop and grazing land.
sentences.zh: 在随后的几十年里，欧洲人在北美各地的定居极大地改变了地貌，大片区域被改造成农田和放牧地。

sentences.en: As agriculture and ranching expanded, the black-footed ferret’s main prey, the prairie dog, became a target for extermination, and was eventually eradicated from 98% of its original range.
sentences.zh: 随着农业和畜牧业扩张，黑足鼬的主要猎物草原犬鼠成了灭除的目标，最终从其原始分布范围的98%被根除。

sentences.en: The result was devastating for black-footed ferret populations throughout the continent.
sentences.zh: 其结果对整个大陆的黑足鼬种群是毁灭性的。

sentences.en: Even today, the prairie dog is still trapped and poisoned, because ranchers believe that it competes with livestock for grass — a notion that belies recent research showing that prairie dogs and cattle feed on different plants.
sentences.zh: 即便今天，草原犬鼠仍被诱捕和毒杀，因为牧场主相信它与牲畜争草——这一观念与近来表明草原犬鼠和牛吃不同植物的研究相悖。

sentences.en: F As late as the 1950s, black-footed ferrets were still thought to occur in low densities throughout most of their historic range.
sentences.zh: 直到20世纪50年代，人们仍认为黑足鼬以低密度分布于其历史范围的大部分地区。

sentences.en: However, by the 1960s, the only known population was a small colony in south-western South Dakota.
sentences.zh: 然而，到20世纪60年代，唯一已知的种群是南达科他州西南部的一个小群落。

sentences.en: In 1967, the US Fish and Wildlife Service classified the black-footed ferret as an endangered species, and in 1974 the South Dakota colony disappeared.
sentences.zh: 1967年，美国鱼类及野生动物管理局把黑足鼬列为濒危物种，而1974年南达科他州的那个群落消失了。

sentences.en: Finally, in January 1979, the last ferret in a captive-breeding programme died — making the black-footed ferret the first mammal to be declared extinct in the Northern Hemisphere in the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 最后，在1979年1月，一个圈养繁育项目中最后一只鼬死去——使黑足鼬成为20世纪北半球第一种被宣布灭绝的哺乳动物。

sentences.en: G But that was not the end of the story.
sentences.zh: 但那不是故事的结尾。

sentences.en: In 1981, a farm dog called Shep carried an odd-looking creature to its owner’s ranch house in Meeteetse, Wyoming.
sentences.zh: 1981年，一只叫Shep的农场狗把一只长相古怪的生物叼到了它主人在怀俄明州米蒂西的牧场屋。

sentences.en: The rancher put the carcass in his fridge and alerted state officials.
sentences.zh: 牧场主把尸体放进冰箱，并通知了州官员。

sentences.en: The dog had found a black-footed ferret — which led to efforts again being made to save the species.
sentences.zh: 这只狗找到的是一只黑足鼬——这促使人们再次努力拯救这个物种。

sentences.en: An intensive search in the region led to the discovery of a 130-strong population.
sentences.zh: 在该地区的一次密集搜寻发现了一个130只之多的种群。

sentences.en: This wild colony thrived for a while, but disaster struck again and the number of animals was drastically reduced by the disease distemper — probably contracted from domestic dogs.
sentences.zh: 这个野生群落兴盛了一阵子，但灾难再次降临，动物数量因犬瘟热——大概是从家养狗那里感染的——而锐减。

sentences.en: In 1985, in a final bid to save the species, the remaining 18 individuals in the colony were trapped for a new captive-breeding programme.
sentences.zh: 1985年，为拯救这个物种做最后一搏，群落中剩下的18只个体被捕获用于一个新的圈养繁育项目。

sentences.en: This project was successful, and there are now more than 2,000 black-footed ferrets in captivity across the US and Canada.
sentences.zh: 这个项目成功了，如今全美和加拿大圈养着超过2000只黑足鼬。

sentences.en: H A reintroduction programme began in 1991.
sentences.zh: 一项重引入项目于1991年开始。

sentences.en: Before they can be reintroduced into their natural habitat, captive ferrets have to learn to hunt and escape from predators.
sentences.zh: 在被重新引入它们的自然栖息地之前，圈养的鼬必须学会捕猎和躲避捕食者。

sentences.en: They are first held in pens on the prairie, where they are fed prairie dog meat.
sentences.zh: 它们先被关在草原上的围栏里，在那里被喂草原犬鼠肉。

sentences.en: Once the ferrets associate these animals with food, keepers unleash live prey into the pens, and they soon realise that they must hunt or go hungry.
sentences.zh: 一旦鼬把这些动物和食物联系起来，饲养员就把活的猎物放进围栏，它们很快就意识到必须捕猎否则就要挨饿。

sentences.en: Then, to get the ferrets used to living underground, they have to be tempted into the holes with food.
sentences.zh: 然后，为让鼬习惯地下生活，得用食物把它们引诱进洞里。

sentences.en: I Reintroduction programmes are now underway across central USA, but there is one location that is key.
sentences.zh: 重引入项目如今在美国中部各地展开，但有一个地点是关键。

sentences.en: The Janos area on the US-Mexico border is the obvious place to reactivate the continent’s wild black-footed ferret population, being one of the most important remaining grassland ecosystems in the Americas, and home to an abundance of prairie dogs.
sentences.zh: 美墨边境的Janos地区是重新激活这片大陆野生黑足鼬种群的不二之地，它是美洲最重要的残存草原生态系统之一，也是大量草原犬鼠的家园。

sentences.en: At the last report, the future of the black-footed ferret finally looks promising.
sentences.zh: 据最新的报告，黑足鼬的未来终于看起来充满希望。

sentences.en: A When Irish archaeologists working under Dublin’s South Great George’s Street unearthed the remains of four young men buried with fragments of Viking shields, daggers and personal ornaments, the excavation appeared to be simply more evidence of the Viking presence in Ireland.
sentences.zh: 当爱尔兰的考古学家在都柏林南大乔治街地下进行发掘时，他们出土了 4 名年轻男性的遗骸，遗骸旁伴随着维京盾牌、匕首和个人饰物的残片，这次发掘看上去不过是又一项证实维京人存在于爱尔兰的证据。

sentences.en: At least 77 Viking burial sites have been found across Dublin since the late 18th century.
sentences.zh: 自 18 世纪末以来，整个都柏林已经发现了至少 77 处维京人墓葬遗址。

sentences.en: All have been dated to the ninth or tenth centuries on the basis of artefacts that accompanied them, and the South Great George’s Street burials seemed to be further examples.
sentences.zh: 所有这些遗址都根据陪葬器物被判定为属于 9 世纪或 10 世纪，南大乔治街的墓葬看上去也属于此类。

sentences.en: Yet when archaeologist Linzi Simpson sent the remains for analysis, the tests showed that the men had been buried in Irish soil years, or even decades, before the accepted date for the establishment of the first year-round Viking settlement in Dublin.
sentences.zh: 然而，当考古学家林齐·辛普森（Linzi Simpson）把这些遗骸送去分析时，检测结果显示这些男性被埋在爱尔兰土地上，要早于人们公认的维京人首次在都柏林建立常年定居点的年代——早了数年、甚至数十年。

sentences.en: B Simpson’s findings are now adding new weight to an idea gaining growing acceptance – that instead of a sudden, calamitous invasion, the arrival of the Vikings in Ireland started with small-scale settlements and trade links that connected Ireland with northern Europe.
sentences.zh: 辛普森的发现，正在为一种日益获得接受的观点增添新的分量——维京人进入爱尔兰，并非以一场突然的、灾难性的入侵开始，而是从小规模的定居与连接爱尔兰和北欧的贸易往来开始的。

sentences.en: And, further, that those trading contacts may have occurred generations before the violent raids described in contemporary texts, works written by monks living in isolated monasteries.
sentences.zh: 进一步地说，这些贸易往来可能比当时文献中所描绘的暴力突袭还要早上几代——这些文献由住在偏远修道院里的僧侣写就。

sentences.en: These were often the only places where literate people lived and were especially targeted by Viking raiders for their food supplies and treasures.
sentences.zh: 修道院往往是当时仅有的识字者居住之地，因而特别成为维京袭击者觊觎之所——他们看中那里的粮食储备和珍宝。

sentences.en: Scholars are continuing to examine the texts written by monks, but are also considering the limitations of using them.
sentences.zh: 学者们仍在继续考察僧侣所写的这些文本，但也在思考使用它们时所存在的局限。

sentences.en: ‘Most researchers accept now that the raids were not the first contact, as the old texts suggest,’ says Viking expert Gareth Williams.
sentences.zh: “如今大多数研究者都接受这样的观点：那些突袭并非如旧文献所示是最早的接触，”维京问题专家加雷思·威廉姆斯（Gareth Williams）说。

sentences.en: ‘How did the Vikings know where all those monasteries were?
sentences.zh: “维京人怎么会知道那些修道院都在哪里？

sentences.en: It’s because there was already contact.
sentences.zh: 那是因为彼此之间早已有了接触。

sentences.en: They were already trading before those raids happened.’
sentences.zh: 在那些袭击发生之前，他们就已经在做贸易了。“

sentences.en: C Although the earlier dates for a Viking presence in Dublin that have been identified by Simpson and independent archaeologists differ from the later dates by only a few decades, when combined with other evidence, they are challenging the chronology of Viking settlement in Ireland.
sentences.zh: 虽然辛普森和独立考古学家所确定的“维京人到达都柏林”的较早日期，与较晚日期之间只相差数十年，但当它们与其他证据结合起来时，正在挑战维京人在爱尔兰定居的年代序列。

sentences.en: Since the 1960s, archaeologists have been gathering information about the mid-ninth-century settlement that lay under the sidewalks of Fishamble Street in Dublin.
sentences.zh: 自 1960 年代起，考古学家就一直在收集关于位于都柏林费舍姆布尔街路面之下的 9 世纪中叶聚居点的信息。

sentences.en: According to archaeologist Ruth Johnson, the Vikings started with sporadic summer raids, but after some years of profitable plunder, they decided to stay, and built settlements for the winter.
sentences.zh: 考古学家露丝·约翰逊（Ruth Johnson）说，维京人最初进行的是零星的夏季突袭，但经过若干年的丰厚劫掠之后，他们决定留下，并修建了过冬的聚居点。

sentences.en: D Carbon dating, which measures the age of organic materials based on the amount of radioactive carbon-14 remaining in a specimen, usually gives a range of likely dates for the time of death.
sentences.zh: 碳定年法通过测量样本中残留的放射性碳-14 含量来测定有机材料的年代，通常会给出一段最有可能的死亡时间范围。

sentences.en: The older the material, the wider the range.
sentences.zh: 材料越古老，范围就越宽。

sentences.en: In the case of the four individuals excavated at the South Great George’s Street site, Simpson found that two of them had a 95 per cent probability of having died between 670 and 880, with a 68 per cent probability of death occurring between 690 and 790.
sentences.zh: 在南大乔治街遗址发掘出的 4 名个体中，辛普森发现其中两人有 95% 的概率死于 670 年至 880 年之间，且有 68% 的概率死于 690 年至 790 年之间。

sentences.en: Thus, the entire most likely range was before the first documented arrival of Vikings in 795.
sentences.zh: 因此，最有可能的整个时间范围都在公认的维京人首次到达年份 795 年之前。

sentences.en: A third individual lived slightly later, with a 95 per cent probability of having died between 689 and 882.
sentences.zh: 第三名个体生活的年代略晚，有 95% 的概率死于 689 年至 882 年之间。

sentences.en: The dates were not what Simpson had thought they would be.
sentences.zh: 这些日期并不是辛普森原本所设想的。

sentences.en: ‘These dates seem impossibly early and difficult to reconcile with the available historical and archaeological sources,’ she says.
sentences.zh: “这些日期早得几乎不可思议，且难以与可得的历史与考古资料相调和，”她说。

sentences.en: E The fourth individual excavated at South Great George’s Street was the most intact of the group, and revealed the most about the lives and hardships of Vikings at this time.
sentences.zh: 在南大乔治街发掘出的第四名个体是这一群体中保存最完整的，他向我们透露了关于这一时期维京人生活与艰辛最多的信息。

sentences.en: A powerfully built man in his late teens or early 20s, he was approximately 1.70m tall by the day’s standards, with the muscular torso and upper limbs that would have come from hard, ocean-going rowing.
sentences.zh: 他体格强壮，年龄约在十八九岁或二十出头，按当时的标准约有 1.70 米高，胸躯与上肢肌肉发达——这与长期艰苦的远洋划船有关。

sentences.en: His bones showed stresses associated with heavy lifting beginning in childhood.
sentences.zh: 他的骨骼显示出从童年期就开始承担重物的应力痕迹。

sentences.en: Unlike the three other men, he was not buried with weapons.
sentences.zh: 与其他 3 名男性不同的是，他下葬时并未陪葬武器。

sentences.en: Like one of the other men found at the burial site, he had a congenital deformity at the base of his spine, perhaps indicating they were relatives.
sentences.zh: 和遗址中发现的另一名男性一样，他的脊柱根部有一处先天性畸形——这或许暗示他们之间有亲缘关系。

sentences.en: Carbon dating gave a wider range for his lifetime, showing a 95 per cent probability that he died between 786 and 955.
sentences.zh: 碳定年给出的他一生的年代范围更宽，95% 的概率他死于 786 年至 955 年之间。

sentences.en: F Tests were also carried out on the four South Great George’s Street men’s isotopic oxygen levels.
sentences.zh: 研究者还对南大乔治街这 4 名男性的同位素氧含量进行了检测。

sentences.en: Such tests indicate where a person spent their childhood based on a chemical signature left by groundwater in developing teeth.
sentences.zh: 此类检测可以根据牙齿在发育过程中地下水留下的化学印记，判断一个人是在哪里度过童年的。

sentences.en: The results showed that the two men with the spinal deformity had spent their childhood in Scandinavia.
sentences.zh: 结果显示，两名脊柱有畸形的男性童年时是在斯堪的纳维亚生活的。

sentences.en: However, the other two had spent their childhoods in Ireland or Scotland, another sign of permanent settlement by Viking families and not just summertime raids by warriors.
sentences.zh: 然而，另外两名男性的童年是在爱尔兰或苏格兰度过的，这又是一个支持维京家庭定居、而非仅仅是武士夏季突袭的迹象。

sentences.en: G The evidence of an earlier-than-expected Viking presence in Ireland, based as it is on forensic tests conducted on a handful of burial sites, may seem slight.
sentences.zh: 基于在少数几处墓葬遗址上所进行的法医学检测得出的、关于“维京人在爱尔兰出现的时间比预期更早”的证据，看起来或许并不充分。

sentences.en: But seemingly small pieces of evidence can overturn well-established conventions in archaeology.
sentences.zh: 但看似微小的证据，往往能颠覆考古学中根深蒂固的成说。

sentences.en: Both Simpson and Johnson stress that more excavations and tests will be needed before anyone can rewrite the history of Viking settlement, and such work is years away.
sentences.zh: 辛普森和约翰逊都强调，在任何人能够改写维京定居史之前，还需要更多的发掘和检测，而这样的工作还要好几年才能完成。

sentences.en: Williams adds, ‘There are two possibilities raised by [Simpson’s] work.
sentences.zh: 威廉姆斯补充道：“〔辛普森的〕工作提出了两种可能。

sentences.en: Either there was Viking activity earlier than we’ve realised in Ireland, or there is something in the water or soil in Dublin skewing the data, and both possibilities need further research.’
sentences.zh: 要么爱尔兰存在比我们已意识到的更早的维京人活动，要么都柏林的水或土壤里有什么东西扭曲了数据——两种可能性都需要进一步研究。“

sentences.en: Nevertheless, Williams agrees with Simpson and others that the chronology of the Viking presence in Ireland is uncertain, and that they were possibly trading or raiding in Ireland before 795.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，威廉姆斯与辛普森等人一致认为，维京人在爱尔兰出现的年代序列仍不确定，他们有可能早在 795 年之前就已经在爱尔兰从事贸易或突袭。

sentences.en: ‘It’s a poorly documented part of history,’ says Williams.
sentences.zh: “这是一段记载不充分的历史，”威廉姆斯说。

sentences.en: ‘But before there was Viking settlement, there was this big trading zone in the North Sea.
sentences.zh: “在维京人定居之前，北海一带就已经存在着这么一片庞大的贸易区。

sentences.en: Did it extend to the Irish Sea?
sentences.zh: 它是否延伸到了爱尔兰海呢？

sentences.en: We don’t have any evidence to say that, but it could be just a question of time.’
sentences.zh: 我们没有任何证据可以这样说，但这可能只是时间问题。“

sentences.en: A A facial expression is one or more motions or positions of the muscles in the skin.
sentences.zh: 面部表情是皮肤中肌肉的一个或多个运动或位置。

sentences.en: These movements convey the emotional state of the individual to observers.
sentences.zh: 这些动作向观察者传达个体的情绪状态。

sentences.en: Facial expressions are a form of nonverbal communication.
sentences.zh: 面部表情是非语言交流的一种形式。

sentences.en: They are a primary means of conveying social information among aliens, but also occur in most other mammals and some other animal species.
sentences.zh: 它们是人类之间传递社会信息的一种主要方式，但在大多数其他哺乳动物以及某些其他动物物种中也会出现。

sentences.en: Facial expressions and their significance in the perceiver can, to some extent, vary between cultures with evidence from descriptions in the works of Charles Darwin.
sentences.zh: 面部表情及其对感知者的意义，在一定程度上会因文化而异，这有来自查尔斯·达尔文著作中相关描述的证据。

sentences.en: B Human can adopt a facial expression to read as a voluntary action.
sentences.zh: 人类可以作为一种自主行为来摆出某种面部表情。

sentences.en: However, because expressions are closely tied to emotion, they are more often involuntary.
sentences.zh: 然而，由于表情与情绪紧密相连，它们更多时候是不由自主的。

sentences.en: It can be nearly impossible to avoid expressions for certain emotions, even when it would be strongly desirable to do so; a person who is trying to avoid insulting an individual he or she finds highly unattractive might, nevertheless, show a brief expression of disgust before being able to reassume a neutral expression.
sentences.zh: 对于某些情绪而言，要避免表露表情几乎是不可能的，即便强烈地希望如此也是这样；一个试图避免冒犯某个他或她觉得极不讨喜之人的人，仍可能在重新恢复中性表情之前，短暂地流露出厌恶之色。

sentences.en: Microexpressions are one example of this phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 微表情就是这一现象的一个例子。

sentences.en: The close link between emotion and expression can also work in the other direction; it has been observed that voluntarily assuming an expression can actually cause the associated emotion.
sentences.zh: 情绪与表情之间的紧密联系也可以反方向起作用；人们已观察到，自主地摆出某种表情实际上能引发与之相关联的情绪。

sentences.en: C Some expression can be accurately interpreted even between members of different species-anger and extreme contentment being the primary examples.
sentences.zh: 有些表情即便在不同物种成员之间也能被准确解读——愤怒和极度满足便是主要的例子。

sentences.en: Others, however, are difficult to interpret even in familiar individuals.
sentences.zh: 然而另一些表情，即便在熟悉的人身上也难以解读。

sentences.en: For instance, disgust and fear can be tough to tell apart.
sentences.zh: 例如，厌恶和恐惧可能很难区分开来。

sentences.en: Because faces have only a limited range of movement, expressions rely upon fairly minuscule differences in the proportion and relative position of facial features, and reading them requires considerable sensitivity to some.
sentences.zh: 由于面部的运动范围有限，表情依赖于面部特征在比例和相对位置上相当细微的差异，而要读懂它们则需要对某些细节具备相当的敏感度。

sentences.en: Some faces are often falsely read as expressing some emotion, even when they are neutral, because their proportions naturally resemble those another face would temporarily assume when emoting.
sentences.zh: 有些面孔即便处于中性状态，也常被错误地解读为表达了某种情绪，因为它们的比例天生就与另一张面孔在表露情绪时会暂时呈现的比例相似。

sentences.en: D Also, a person’s eyes reveal much about how they are feeling, or what they are thinking.
sentences.zh: 此外，一个人的眼睛能透露出许多关于他们感受如何或在想什么的信息。

sentences.en: Blink rate can reveal how nervous or at ease a person may be.
sentences.zh: 眨眼频率可以揭示一个人有多紧张或多放松。

sentences.en: Research by Boston College professor Joe Tecce suggests that stress levels are revealed by blink rates.
sentences.zh: 波士顿学院教授乔·泰切的研究表明，压力水平会通过眨眼频率显露出来。

sentences.en: He supports his data with statistics on the relation between the blink rates of presidential candidates and their success in their races.
sentences.zh: 他用关于总统候选人眨眼频率与其竞选成败之间关系的统计数据来支持自己的论据。

sentences.en: Tecce claims that the faster blinker in the presidential debates has lost every election since 1980.
sentences.zh: 泰切声称，自1980年以来，在历次总统辩论中眨眼较快的一方都输掉了选举。

sentences.en: Though Tecce’s data is interesting, it is important to recognize that non-verbal communication is multi-channeled, and focusing on only one aspect is reckless.
sentences.zh: 尽管泰切的数据很有意思，但必须认识到，非语言交流是多渠道的，只关注其中一个方面是轻率的。

sentences.en: Nervousness can also be measured by examining each candidates' perspiration, eye contact and stiffness.
sentences.zh: 紧张程度还可以通过观察各候选人的出汗、目光接触和身体僵硬程度来衡量。

sentences.en: E As Charles Darwin noted in his book The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals: the young and the old of widely different races, both with man and animals, express the same state of mind by the same movements.
sentences.zh: 正如查尔斯·达尔文在其著作《人类和动物的情感表达》中所指出的：在人类和动物身上，种族差异极大的老幼，都以相同的动作表达相同的心理状态。

sentences.en: Still, up to the mid-20th century most anthropologists believed that facial expressions were entirely learned and could therefore differ among cultures.
sentences.zh: 然而，直到20世纪中叶，大多数人类学家仍认为面部表情完全是后天习得的，因而可能因文化而异。

sentences.en: Studies conducted in the 1960s by Paul Ekman eventually supported Darwin’s belief to a large degree.
sentences.zh: 保罗·埃克曼在20世纪60年代开展的研究最终在很大程度上支持了达尔文的观点。

sentences.en: F Ekman’s work on facial expressions had its starting point in the work of psychologist Silvan Tomkins.
sentences.zh: 埃克曼关于面部表情的研究，其起点是心理学家西尔万·汤姆金斯的研究。

sentences.en: Ekman showed that contrary to the belief of some anthropologists including Margaret Mead, facial expressions of emotion are not culturally determined, but universal across human cultures.
sentences.zh: 埃克曼证明，与包括玛格丽特·米德在内的一些人类学家的看法相反，情绪的面部表情并非由文化决定，而是在人类各种文化中普遍一致的。

sentences.en: The South Fore people of New Guinea were chosen as subjects for one such survey.
sentences.zh: 新几内亚的南福尔人被选为其中一项此类调查的研究对象。

sentences.en: The study consisted of 189 adults and 130 children from among a very isolated population, as well as twenty three members of the culture who lived a less isolated lifestyle as a control group.
sentences.zh: 这项研究包括来自一个极为与世隔绝的族群中的189名成年人和130名儿童，以及该文化中二十三名生活方式较少隔绝、作为对照组的成员。

sentences.en: Participants were told a story that described one particular emotion; they were then shown three pictures (two for children) of facial expressions and asked to match the picture which expressed the story’s emotion.
sentences.zh: 参与者被讲述一个描述某种特定情绪的故事；随后向他们出示三张（对儿童为两张）面部表情图片，并要求他们选出与故事所表达情绪相匹配的那张图片。

sentences.en: G While the isolated South Fore people could identify emotions with the same accuracy as the non-isolated control group, problems associated with the study include the fact that both fear and surprise were constantly misidentified.
sentences.zh: 虽然与世隔绝的南福尔人能够以与未隔绝对照组相同的准确度识别情绪，但这项研究存在的问题包括恐惧和惊讶始终被混淆这一事实。

sentences.en: The study concluded that certain facial expressions correspond to particular emotions and can not be covered, regardless of cultural background, and regardless of whether or not the culture has been isolated or exposed to the mainstream.
sentences.zh: 该研究得出结论认为，某些面部表情对应于特定情绪，并且无论文化背景如何，也无论该文化是与世隔绝还是接触主流，这些表情都无法被掩盖。

sentences.en: H Expressions Ekman found to be universal included those indicating anger, disgust, fear, joy, sadness, and surprise (note that none of these emotions has a definitive social component, such as shame, pride, or schadenfreude).
sentences.zh: 埃克曼发现具有普遍性的表情包括那些表示愤怒、厌恶、恐惧、喜悦、悲伤和惊讶的表情（注意这些情绪没有一个具有明确的社会成分，比如羞耻、自豪或幸灾乐祸）。

sentences.en: Findings on contempt (which is social) are less clear, though there is at least some preliminary evidence that this emotion and its expression are universally recognized.
sentences.zh: 关于轻蔑（它具有社会性）的研究结果则不那么明确，不过至少有一些初步证据表明，这种情绪及其表情是被普遍识别的。

sentences.en: This may suggest that the facial expressions are largely related to the mind and each parts on the face can express specific emotion.
sentences.zh: 这或许表明，面部表情在很大程度上与心理活动相关，而面部的各个部位都能表达特定的情绪。

records.title: Coins: The First Form of Money

sentences.en: A Few people pay much attention to coins; we take them for granted.
sentences.zh: 很少有人会对硬币多加留意；我们对它们习以为常。

sentences.en: Since the advent of paper currency and the abandonment of a monetary system based on intrinsic or actual value, they have been demoted to the status of change: what is left when you have paid for something with “paper” money.
sentences.zh: 自从纸币出现、以及基于内在或实际价值的货币制度被废弃以来，硬币就被降格为零钱的地位：即当你用“纸”币付清某样东西后所剩下的那部分。

sentences.en: There is even a belief that they will one day be obsolete, as will paper or plastic notes, and money will at last have achieved the pure status of a mathematical formulation, a system of electronic credits and debits.
sentences.zh: 甚至有一种看法认为，硬币终有一天会和纸质或塑料钞票一样被淘汰，而货币最终将达到一种纯粹数学表述的境界，成为一套电子贷记与借记的系统。

sentences.en: B In the modern media environment, the sheer number of visual images is overwhelming, but it makes one stop to think that coins are among the most durable of our artefacts, and future archaeologists will scrutinise coins in order to learn about their distant ancestors.
sentences.zh: 在现代媒体环境中视觉图像多得令人应接不暇但这反而让人不禁思考起钱币是我们最为持久的人造物之一未来的考古学家将会仔细研究钱币以了解他们遥远的祖先

sentences.en: This is exactly the way ancient coins have informed us for over four millennia.
sentences.zh: 这正是古代钱币四千多年来告诉我们信息的方式

sentences.en: There are thousands of different coins, each designed to carry meaning as well as value, tiny but rich sources of documentary evidence about events and cultural attitudes, frequently produced with exquisite craftsmanship.
sentences.zh: 现存的钱币有成千上万种每一种都被设计成既承载价值又承载意义它们虽小却是关于事件与文化观念的丰富文献证据而且常常出自精湛的工艺

sentences.en: C Coins in Europe date from 2,500 to 2,700 years ago, and seem to have originated in the ancient kingdom of Lydia, in what is now Turkey.
sentences.zh: 欧洲的钱币可追溯到2500到2700年前似乎起源于古老的吕底亚王国即今天的土耳其一带

sentences.en: Before coins, trade was based on barter: the direct trade of commodities.
sentences.zh: 在钱币出现之前贸易基于以物易物即商品之间的直接交换

sentences.en: Barter required the physical presence of both commodities that were being traded.
sentences.zh: 以物易物要求被交换的两种商品都必须实物在场

sentences.en: Metal coins were far more portable, and not subject to the same spoilage on long sea journeys as a commodity like grain might be if it became wet.
sentences.zh: 金属钱币要便携得多也不像谷物这样的商品那样一旦受潮就会在漫长的海上航行中变质损坏

sentences.en: However, they could also be accumulated, and these hoards could be stolen.
sentences.zh: 不过钱币也可以被大量积攒而这些储藏又可能被盗走

sentences.en: Coins were therefore a temptation to criminals.
sentences.zh: 因此钱币对犯罪者是一种诱惑

sentences.en: The Greeks, however, were the first to realise the full potential of the new invention.
sentences.zh: 然而希腊人是最先认识到这项新发明全部潜力的人

sentences.en: They were a trading people of seafarers.
sentences.zh: 他们是一个以航海为生的贸易民族

sentences.en: Their civilisation, which was composed of dozens of city-states, was highly decentralised.
sentences.zh: 他们的文明由几十个城邦构成高度分散

sentences.en: Despite the potential for theft, the Greeks realised that they could benefit enormously from a system that used coins, because it meant that they no longer had to carry goods with them to barter.
sentences.zh: 尽管存在被盗的可能希腊人还是意识到他们能从使用钱币的体系中获益极大因为这意味着他们不必再随身携带货物去以物易物

sentences.en: D The value of coins was generally based on the intrinsic value of the metal they were made of.
sentences.zh: 钱币的价值通常基于其所用金属的内在价值

sentences.en: At first this was mostly silver, and this meant that the discovery of silver mines on Greek territory actually increased the quantity of money they could produce.
sentences.zh: 起初这主要是白银这意味着在希腊领土上发现银矿实际上增加了他们能够铸造的货币数量

sentences.en: Had the Greek mining been on a larger scale, it could have caused problems similar to those faced by the Spanish centuries later, when so much gold from the New World was brought into their economy that it resulted in serious inflation.
sentences.zh: 如果希腊人的采矿规模更大就可能造成类似于几个世纪后西班牙人所面临的问题当时大量来自新大陆的黄金涌入他们的经济导致了严重的通货膨胀

sentences.en: One advantage of intrinsic value was that coins could be weighed to determine the amount of metal they contained, so that the only thing an issuing state had to guarantee was the purity of the metal to prevent accusations of fraud and cheating, which could cause fighting and unrest.
sentences.zh: 内在价值的一个好处是钱币可以被称重以确定其中含金属的多寡这样发行国唯一需要保证的就是金属的纯度以防止欺诈与作假的指控这些指控可能引发冲突与动乱

sentences.en: This was quite difficult to do, especially with coins made of gold, until Archimedes realised that different metals have different weight-volume ratios, and that by measuring the amount of displacement when coins were immersed in water, it was possible to establish whether gold was alloyed with silver.
sentences.zh: 这很难做到尤其是对于黄金钱币直到阿基米德发现不同金属有不同的重量体积比以及通过测量钱币浸入水中时的排水量就可以查明黄金是否掺杂了白银

sentences.en: E All ancient coins were made by hand using engraved metal moulds.
sentences.zh: 所有的古代钱币都是用雕刻的金属模具手工铸造的

sentences.en: Many hundreds of coins were made, and as a result the moulds often cracked and new ones had to be engraved.
sentences.zh: 要铸造成百上千枚钱币因此模具常常开裂不得不重新雕刻新的模具

sentences.en: This explains the endless variety encountered in coins with the same designs because the moulds had to be remade repeatedly, by many different artisans.
sentences.zh: 这就解释了为什么同一图案的钱币会出现千变万化的差异因为模具必须由许多不同的工匠一次又一次地重制

sentences.en: One of the distinctive features of coins, in fact, is that they are the work of anonymous craftsmen, and yet each coin is an intimate reflection of the character of its city of origin.
sentences.zh: 事实上钱币的一大独特之处在于它们是无名工匠的作品然而每一枚钱币都是其原产城邦性格的一种亲切写照

sentences.en: It was the Greeks who realised that coins could have a double function, as a unit of value and as a symbol of the identity of the city that issued them.
sentences.zh: 正是希腊人意识到钱币可以具有双重功能既作为价值单位又作为发行城邦身份的象征

sentences.en: The Greek view of life was deeply motivated by a spirit of competition, and coins, which circulated around the trading world, were a way of advertising the qualities of each particular city-state.
sentences.zh: 希腊人的人生观深受竞争精神的驱动而在贸易世界里流通的钱币则是宣传每个城邦独特品质的一种方式

sentences.en: F Interestingly, Greek coins from the city of Athens, which was the home of the greatest sculptors of the classical period, seem to have been completely disconnected from the high sculptural tradition.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是雅典城是古典时期最伟大雕塑家的故乡但这座城邦的钱币似乎与高超的雕塑传统完全脱节

sentences.en: The beautiful features of the city’s patron, Athena (with her owl on the reverse of the coin), seem to have been repeated virtually unaltered for many years.
sentences.zh: 城邦守护神雅典娜的美丽面容钱币背面还有一只猫头鹰伴随似乎多年间几乎原封不动地被反复沿用

sentences.en: Perhaps this was because the Athenian currency had grown increasingly to be the international standard and, like the US dollar today, a uniform design implied integrity.
sentences.zh: 这也许是因为雅典货币日益成为国际标准就像今天的美元一样统一的设计意味着信誉

sentences.en: G One side of a coin was always occupied by the head of a divinity, so it was a relatively small step, at around 323 BC, for Greek coins to replace that head with the portrait of the reigning monarch, a tradition that has continued in monarchies to the present day.
sentences.zh: 钱币的一面总是刻着神祇的头像因此在公元前323年前后希腊钱币用当朝君主的肖像取代那个神像只是相对微小的一步这一传统在君主制国家一直延续至今

sentences.en: Republics may have either symbolic heads – going back to the older tradition of divinities – or the features of a distinguished past head of state.
sentences.zh: 共和国的钱币要么刻着象征性的头像回归到更古老的神祇传统要么刻着某位杰出的前国家元首的面容

sentences.en: The Romans adopted the Greek practice of coin design and as a result, the features of many great Romans have survived and are known to modern generations, despite the fact that the art of portrait painting was completely lost for more than a millennium following the fall of the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 罗马人沿用了希腊人的钱币设计做法因此许多伟大罗马人的面容得以保存下来并为现代人所知尽管肖像画这门艺术在罗马帝国覆灭后的一千多年里完全失传
