sentences.en: (A) The discovery of ancient fishing hooks in New Zealand has revealed that the Māori people were remarkably skilled at crafting highly effective tools for catching fish.
sentences.zh: 在新西兰发现的古代鱼钩表明，毛利人在打造捕鱼用的高效工具方面有着非凡的技艺。

sentences.en: These hooks, often made from organic materials such as bone or shell, functioned with surprising precision, even when compared to modern alternatives.
sentences.zh: 这些鱼钩通常由骨头或贝壳等天然材料制成，其运作精度之高令人惊讶，即便与现代替代品相比也是如此。

sentences.en: However, for many centuries, their true purpose was misunderstood by researchers and collectors alike.
sentences.zh: 然而，在长达数个世纪的时间里，无论是研究者还是收藏者，都误解了它们真正的用途。

sentences.en: Many assumed these intricately shaped hooks served only decorative, ceremonial, or ritualistic purposes due to their unusual appearance and craftsmanship.
sentences.zh: 由于其不同寻常的外观和工艺，许多人认为这些造型精巧的鱼钩仅用于装饰、典礼或宗教仪式。

sentences.en: Ironically, in recent years, engineers and product designers have turned to modern technologies – such as 3D scanning and computer-aided manufacturing – to recreate these hooks.
sentences.zh: 颇具讽刺意味的是，近年来工程师和产品设计师转而借助三维扫描与计算机辅助制造等现代技术来复刻这些鱼钩。

sentences.en: These reproductions, now made using high-tech materials, replicate the original Māori designs that were created over a millennium ago.
sentences.zh: 这些采用高科技材料制成的复制品，再现了一千多年前毛利人创造的原始设计。

sentences.en: (B) When the Māori first arrived in New Zealand from the Pacific Islands, they encountered an environment rich in natural resources.
sentences.zh: 当毛利人最初从太平洋诸岛抵达新西兰时，他们遇到了一个自然资源丰富的环境。

sentences.en: They quickly adapted by using familiar materials such as bones and stones to make their fishing hooks and began practicing intensive agriculture.
sentences.zh: 他们很快就利用骨头和石头等熟悉的材料来制作鱼钩，并开始从事集约化的农业。

sentences.en: Their fishing lines and nets, made from native plants like flax and cabbage trees, proved just as strong – if not stronger – than those used by Europeans, which were typically made from hemp.
sentences.zh: 他们用亚麻和卷心菜树等本地植物制成的钓线和渔网，其坚固程度丝毫不逊于欧洲人通常用大麻制成的渔具，甚至更胜一筹。

sentences.en: Although the structure of the Māori hooks was highly efficient for catching fish, their form was somewhat limited.
sentences.zh: 尽管毛利人的鱼钩在捕鱼方面结构十分高效，但其形态却受到一定限制。

sentences.en: This was because the materials they had access to could not be forged or bent like metal, thus restricting the range of shapes the hooks could take.
sentences.zh: 这是因为他们所能获得的材料无法像金属那样锻造或弯曲，从而限制了鱼钩可以呈现的形状种类。

sentences.en: (C) More than 230 years after the Māori settled, Europeans landed in New Zealand and began exploring the land.
sentences.zh: 在毛利人定居二百三十多年后，欧洲人登陆新西兰并开始探索这片土地。

sentences.en: As they moved through the region, they came across various local fishing tools, including the Māori hooks.
sentences.zh: 在穿越这一地区的过程中，他们接触到了各种当地的捕鱼工具，其中就包括毛利人的鱼钩。

sentences.en: Despite their effectiveness, many Europeans viewed the tools with skepticism.
sentences.zh: 尽管这些工具行之有效，许多欧洲人却对它们持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: They considered them awkward and ineffective, failing to recognize the ingenuity of the designs.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这些工具笨拙且无效，未能认识到这些设计的精巧之处。

sentences.en: Even modern archaeologists sometimes share this view, finding the hooks odd and questioning their efficiency.
sentences.zh: 即便是现代考古学家有时也持有同样的看法，觉得这些鱼钩很奇怪，并质疑它们的效率。

sentences.en: In 1777, however, William Anderson made an observation that challenged this view.
sentences.zh: 然而在1777年，威廉·安德森提出的一个观察结果挑战了这一看法。

sentences.en: He noted that although the hooks looked unconventional, the Māori had already developed advanced methods of intensive farming – evidence of their broader ingenuity.
sentences.zh: 他指出，尽管这些鱼钩看上去不合常规，毛利人却早已发展出先进的集约化耕作方法，这正是他们更广泛智慧的证明。

sentences.en: Still, the unusual appearance of the hooks overshadowed how successful they truly were.
sentences.zh: 然而，鱼钩不同寻常的外观掩盖了它们实际上有多么成功。

sentences.en: (D) Recent research conducted by Victoria University has revealed that Māori fishing hooks functioned quite differently from those used by Europeans.
sentences.zh: 维多利亚大学近期开展的研究揭示，毛利人的鱼钩与欧洲人使用的鱼钩在功能上有着很大不同。

sentences.en: Rather than piercing directly like a standard hook, Māori hooks worked by rotating the fish away from the point and catching it securely under the jaw.
sentences.zh: 毛利人的鱼钩并不像普通鱼钩那样直接刺穿，而是通过让鱼转离钩尖，将其牢牢地钩在下颌处。

sentences.en: This rotational mechanism proved remarkably effective in practice.
sentences.zh: 这种旋转机制在实践中被证明极为有效。

sentences.en: Unlike the lever-based mechanisms common in European designs, the Māori hooks employed a unique principle that required neither barbs nor baiting in the same manner, showcasing a distinctly original approach to fishing.
sentences.zh: 与欧洲设计中常见的杠杆式机制不同，毛利人的鱼钩运用了一种独特的原理，既不需要倒刺，也不必以同样的方式挂饵，展现出一种别具一格的捕鱼思路。

sentences.en: (E) After the 1700s, Māori craftsmen began using new materials introduced by Europeans, such as metals.
sentences.zh: 1700年代之后，毛利工匠开始使用欧洲人引入的金属等新材料。

sentences.en: However, they did not abandon their traditional designs.
sentences.zh: 然而，他们并没有放弃自己的传统设计。

sentences.en: Instead, they incorporated the new materials into the same forms they had long used.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们将新材料融入到长期沿用的同一形制之中。

sentences.en: As bones and stones fell out of use, hooks made from traded metals became more common.
sentences.zh: 随着骨头和石头逐渐弃用，用交易得来的金属制成的鱼钩变得更加普遍。

sentences.en: Some artisans even used rare and valuable materials like ivory or greenstone, crafting hooks that were later taken into luxury markets and sold as jewelry, blurring the line between utility and art.
sentences.zh: 一些工匠甚至使用象牙或绿石等珍稀贵重的材料，所制成的鱼钩后来进入奢侈品市场，作为首饰出售，模糊了实用与艺术之间的界限。

sentences.en: (F) Following the 1800s, Europe began exporting mass-produced hooks to New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 1800年代以后，欧洲开始向新西兰出口大批量生产的鱼钩。

sentences.en: These items were cheaper and quickly gained popularity among local users.
sentences.zh: 这些产品更为便宜，很快便在当地用户中流行起来。

sentences.en: Despite their affordability, the production of traditional Māori hooks declined due to the nails and other metallic materials required, which were difficult to manipulate without specialized tools.
sentences.zh: 尽管价格低廉，传统毛利鱼钩的生产却因所需的钉子及其他金属材料而日渐衰落，因为这些材料若没有专门工具便难以加工。

sentences.en: In the early 1900s, however, interest in Pacific culture grew, and collectors began to seek out original Māori fishing hooks once again.
sentences.zh: 然而，到了1900年代初，人们对太平洋文化的兴趣日益浓厚，收藏者再次开始寻觅原始的毛利鱼钩。

sentences.en: This renewed attention turned the hooks into coveted antique items.
sentences.zh: 这种重新燃起的关注使这些鱼钩成为令人垂涎的古董。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, the demand also led to a wave of imitations—many of the hooks appearing on the market today are fake, though they can usually be identified by their inconsistent design and materials.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，这种需求也引发了一波仿制浪潮——如今市面上出现的许多鱼钩都是赝品，不过通常可以通过其前后不一致的设计和材料将其辨认出来。

sentences.en: (G) The Māori did not only adapt their fishing hooks through European influence but also modified other traditional items using both metals and more recently, synthetic plastic.
sentences.zh: 毛利人不仅在欧洲影响下改进了自己的鱼钩，还利用金属乃至近来的合成塑料对其他传统物件加以改造。

sentences.en: Importantly, these changes were often adaptations rather than complete replacements, preserving core aspects of Māori design.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，这些变化往往是改良而非彻底替换，从而保留了毛利设计的核心要素。

sentences.en: What is perhaps most remarkable is that many hooks found on boats in New Zealand today still bear a striking resemblance to the ancient forms crafted hundreds of years ago, a testament to the enduring utility and brilliance of traditional Māori design.
sentences.zh: 或许最引人注目的是，如今在新西兰船只上发现的许多鱼钩，仍与数百年前打造的古代形制惊人地相似，这正是传统毛利设计经久不衰的实用价值与卓越智慧的明证。

sentences.en: (A) Libraries are collections of materials containing information, ideas, and works of imagination that are organized for public use and staffed by people trained to provide a service.
sentences.zh: 图书馆是各种资料的集合，这些资料蕴含信息、思想和富有想象力的作品，经过整理以供公众使用，并由受过专门培训、能够提供服务的人员负责管理。

sentences.en: They take many physical forms ranging from large purpose-built buildings to rooms in parent institutions and small temporary structures.
sentences.zh: 它们以多种实体形式存在，从专门建造的大型建筑，到母体机构内的房间，再到小型的临时构筑物，不一而足。

sentences.en: They are a vital resource in an age in which people and communities desperately need to consider alternative points of view and information in order to challenge the mass media and make up their own minds.
sentences.zh: 在这样一个时代——人们和社区迫切需要考虑不同的观点和信息，以便质疑大众媒体并形成自己的判断——图书馆是一种至关重要的资源。

sentences.en: (B) Despite a popular misconception, libraries have never confined themselves to the collection of books.
sentences.zh: 尽管存在一种普遍的误解，图书馆其实从未将自己局限于收藏书籍。

sentences.en: Traditionally, they have acquired a range of print-based materials, including newspapers, maps, pamphlets, illustrations, and many other items.
sentences.zh: 传统上，它们收集各类印刷资料，包括报纸、地图、小册子、插图以及许多其他物品。

sentences.en: Indeed, libraries pre-dated the invention of the book.
sentences.zh: 事实上，图书馆的出现早于书籍的发明。

sentences.en: For example, the original library in Alexandria, the capital of ancient Egypt, collected papyrus scrolls, and mediaeval monasteries collected manuscripts.
sentences.zh: 例如，位于古埃及首都亚历山大的那座最初的图书馆收集莎草纸卷轴，而中世纪的修道院则收集手稿。

sentences.en: It was therefore widely regarded as a logical step for libraries to collect every new medium that contained information as it emerged.
sentences.zh: 因此，图书馆每当有蕴含信息的新媒介出现便加以收集，这被广泛视为顺理成章之举。

sentences.en: All forms of sound and visual recording (for example, gramophone records, cassettes, videos, CDs, and DVDs) joined the collections in many libraries as they became available.
sentences.zh: 随着各种声音和影像记录形式（例如留声机唱片、磁带、录像带、CD和DVD）问世，它们陆续进入许多图书馆的馆藏。

sentences.en: Digital formats were also quickly added to collections and there are now countless libraries around the world which have fully integrated electronic resources such as e-books, audiobooks, online databases, and digitised archives.
sentences.zh: 数字格式也很快被纳入馆藏，如今全世界已有数不清的图书馆将电子书、有声读物、在线数据库和数字化档案等电子资源完全整合在一起。

sentences.en: (C) However, the role of libraries has expanded beyond mere collection.
sentences.zh: 然而，图书馆的角色已经超越了单纯的收藏。

sentences.en: Modern libraries also function as community hubs, offering public internet access, literacy programmes, and spaces for civic engagement.
sentences.zh: 现代图书馆还充当社区中心的角色，提供公共互联网接入、识字教育项目以及供公民参与的空间。

sentences.en: In many regions, libraries provide essential services such as assistance with job applications, legal guidance, and support for small businesses.
sentences.zh: 在许多地区，图书馆提供诸如协助求职申请、法律指导以及对小型企业的支持等基本服务。

sentences.en: Furthermore, librarians have adapted to the digital age by developing skills in data management, digital literacy training, and fact-checking – all of which help users navigate an increasingly complex information landscape.
sentences.zh: 此外，图书馆员通过培养数据管理、数字素养培训和事实核查方面的技能来适应数字时代——所有这些都有助于用户驾驭日益复杂的信息环境。

sentences.en: (D) Nevertheless, libraries face significant challenges.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，图书馆仍面临着重大挑战。

sentences.en: Budget cuts in many countries have reduced opening hours and staff numbers.
sentences.zh: 许多国家的预算削减已经减少了开放时间和员工人数。

sentences.en: Some critics argue that physical libraries are obsolete, given that so much information is now available online.
sentences.zh: 一些批评者认为，鉴于如今如此多的信息都可在网上获取，实体图书馆已经过时。

sentences.en: Yet proponents maintain that libraries offer something the internet cannot: curated, trustworthy information and equitable access regardless of income or social status.
sentences.zh: 然而支持者坚持认为，图书馆提供了互联网所不能提供的东西：经过甄选的、可信赖的信息，以及不论收入或社会地位都人人平等的获取机会。

sentences.en: In conclusion, while the format of materials has evolved, the core mission of libraries – to provide free and open access to knowledge – remains as relevant today as it was in ancient Alexandria.
sentences.zh: 总而言之，尽管资料的形式已经演变，图书馆的核心使命——提供对知识自由而开放的获取途径——在今天仍像在古代亚历山大时一样切合时宜。

sentences.en: A Photography gained the interest of many scientists and artists from its inception.
sentences.zh: 摄影自诞生之初就吸引了许多科学家和艺术家的兴趣。

sentences.en: Scientists have used photography to record and study movements, such as Eadweard Muybridge’s study of human and animal locomotion in 1887.
sentences.zh: 科学家们利用摄影来记录和研究运动，例如Eadweard Muybridge于1887年对人类和动物运动的研究。

sentences.en: Artists are equally interested by these aspects but also try to explore avenues other than the photo-mechanical representation of reality, such as the pictorialist movement.
sentences.zh: 艺术家们对这些方面同样感兴趣，但他们也尝试探索以摄影机械方式再现现实之外的途径，例如画意摄影运动。

sentences.en: Military, police, and security forces use photography for surveillance, recognition and data storage.
sentences.zh: 军队、警察和安全部队利用摄影进行监视、识别和数据存储。

sentences.en: Photography is used by amateurs to preserve memories, to capture special moments, to tell stories, to send messages, and as a source of entertainment.
sentences.zh: 业余爱好者利用摄影来保存记忆、捕捉特别的时刻、讲故事、传递信息，并把它当作一种娱乐来源。

sentences.en: Various technological improvements and techniques have even allowed for visualising events that are too fast or too slow for the human eye.
sentences.zh: 各种技术改进和技术手段甚至使呈现那些对人眼来说过快或过慢的事件成为可能。

sentences.en: B One of such techniques is called fast motion or professionally known as time-lapse.
sentences.zh: 其中一种技术被称为快动作，在专业上称为延时摄影。

sentences.en: Time-lapse photography is the perfect technique for capturing events and movements in the natural world that occur over a timescale too slow for human perception to follow.
sentences.zh: 延时摄影是捕捉自然界中那些发生过程的时间尺度太慢、人类感知无法跟上的事件和运动的完美技术。

sentences.en: The life cycle of a mushroom, for example, is incredibly subtle to the human eye.
sentences.zh: 例如，蘑菇的生命周期在人眼看来极其细微难察。

sentences.en: To present its growth in front of audiences, the principle applied is a simple one: a series of photographs are taken and used in sequence to make a moving-image film, but since each frame is taken with a lapse at a time interval between each shot, when played back at normal speed, a continuous action is produced and it appears to speed up.
sentences.zh: 为了在观众面前呈现它的生长，所采用的原理很简单：拍摄一系列照片并按顺序使用来制作成动态影像影片，但由于每一帧都是在两次拍摄之间间隔一段时间才拍摄的，因此以正常速度播放时便产生了连续的动作，而且看起来像是加快了。

sentences.en: Put simply: we are shrinking time.
sentences.zh: 简而言之：我们在压缩时间。

sentences.en: Objects and events that would normally take several minutes, days or even months can be viewed to completion in seconds having been sped up by factors of tens to millions.
sentences.zh: 通常需要几分钟、几天甚至几个月的物体和事件，在经过数十倍到数百万倍的加速之后，可以在几秒钟内看完全过程。

sentences.en: C Another commonly used technique is high-speed photography, the science of taking pictures of very fast phenomena.
sentences.zh: 另一种常用技术是高速摄影，即拍摄极快现象的科学。

sentences.en: High-speed photography can be considered to be the opposite of time-lapse photography.
sentences.zh: 高速摄影可以被视为延时摄影的对立面。

sentences.en: One of the many applications is found in biology studies to study birds, bats and even spider silk.
sentences.zh: 在其众多应用中，有一种是在生物学研究中用于研究鸟类、蝙蝠甚至蜘蛛丝。

sentences.en: Imagine a hummingbird hovering almost completely still in the air, feeding on nectar.
sentences.zh: 想象一只蜂鸟悬停在空中，几乎完全静止，正在取食花蜜。

sentences.en: With every flap, its wings bend, flex and change shape.
sentences.zh: 它的翅膀每扇动一次都会弯曲、屈伸并改变形状。

sentences.en: These subtle movements precisely control the lift its wings generate, making it an excellent hoverer.
sentences.zh: 这些细微的动作精确控制着翅膀产生的升力，使它成为出色的悬停高手。

sentences.en: But a hummingbird flaps its wings up to 80 times every second.
sentences.zh: 但蜂鸟每秒钟扇动翅膀多达80次。

sentences.en: The only way to truly capture this motion is with cameras that will, in effect, slow down time.
sentences.zh: 真正捕捉这种运动的唯一办法是使用实际上能让时间放慢的摄像机。

sentences.en: To do this, a greater length of film is taken at a high sampling frequency or frame rate, which is much faster than it will be projected on screen.
sentences.zh: 为此，要以高采样频率或帧率拍摄更长的胶片，其速度比之后在银幕上放映的速度快得多。

sentences.en: When replayed at normal speed, time appears to be slowed down proportionately.
sentences.zh: 以正常速度回放时，时间看起来按比例放慢了。

sentences.en: That is why high-speed cameras have become such a mainstay of biology.
sentences.zh: 这就是高速摄像机已成为生物学领域一大支柱的原因。

sentences.en: D In common usage, high-speed photography can also refer to the use of high-speed cameras that the photograph itself may be taken in a way as to appear to freeze the motion, especially to reduce motion blur.
sentences.zh: 在通常用法中，高速摄影也可以指高速摄像机的使用，即照片本身以某种方式拍摄，使画面看似将动作定格，尤其是为了减少运动模糊。

sentences.en: It requires a sensor with good sensitivity and either a very good shuttering system or a very fast strobe light.
sentences.zh: 它需要一枚灵敏度良好的传感器，以及一套非常好的快门系统或一盏非常快的频闪灯。

sentences.en: The recent National Geographic footage—captured last summer during an intensive three-day shoot at the Cincinnati Zoo—is unprecedented in its clarity and detail.
sentences.zh: National Geographic最近的这段影像——于去年夏天在Cincinnati Zoo为期三天的密集拍摄中捕捉——其清晰度和细节前所未有。

sentences.en: “I’ve watched cheetahs run for 30 years,” said Cathryn Hilker, founder of the zoo’s Cat Ambassador Program.
sentences.zh: “我观察猎豹奔跑已经30年了，”该动物园Cat Ambassador Program的创始人Cathryn Hilker说。

sentences.en: “But I saw things in that super slow-motion video that I’ve never seen before.”
sentences.zh: “但我在那段超慢动作视频中看到了我以前从未见过的东西。”

sentences.en: The slow-motion video is entrancing.
sentences.zh: 这段慢动作视频令人着迷。

sentences.en: Every part of the sprinting cat’s anatomy—supple limbs, rippling muscles, hyperflexible spine—works together in a symphony of speed, revealing the fluid grace of the world’s fastest land animal.
sentences.zh: 这只疾驰的猫科动物身体的每一部分——柔韧的四肢、涌动的肌肉、极度柔韧的脊椎——都在一场速度的交响乐中协同运作，展现出世界上跑得最快的陆地动物的流畅优雅。

sentences.en: E But things can’t get any more complicated in the case of filming a frog catching its prey.
sentences.zh: 但在拍摄青蛙捕捉猎物时，情况再复杂不过了。

sentences.en: Frogs can snatch up prey in a few thousandths of a second—striking out with elastic tongues.
sentences.zh: 青蛙能在千分之几秒内捕获猎物——用富有弹性的舌头弹射出击。

sentences.en: Biologists would love to see how a frog’s tongue roll out, adhere to prey, and roll back into the frog’s mouth.
sentences.zh: 生物学家很想看到青蛙的舌头如何弹出、粘住猎物、再卷回青蛙口中。

sentences.en: But this all happened too fast, 50 times faster than an eye blink.
sentences.zh: 但这一切发生得太快，比一次眨眼还要快50倍。

sentences.en: So naturally people thought of using high-speed camera to capture this fantastic movement in slow motion.
sentences.zh: 于是人们自然而然地想到用高速摄像机以慢动作捕捉这一奇妙的动作。

sentences.en: Yet one problem still remains—viewers would be bored if they watch the frog swim in slow motion for too long.
sentences.zh: 然而仍有一个问题存在——如果长时间观看慢动作里青蛙游泳的画面，观众会感到无聊。

sentences.en: So how to skip this?
sentences.zh: 那么，如何跳过这一点呢？

sentences.en: The solution is a simple one—adjust the playback speed, which is also called by some the film speed adjustment.
sentences.zh: 解决办法很简单——调整播放速度，有些人也称之为影片速度调整。

sentences.en: The film will originally be shot at a high frame (often 300 frames per second, because it can be converted to much lower frame rates without major issues), but at later editing stage this high frame rate will only be preserved for the prey catching part, while the swimming part will be converted to the normal speed at 24 frames per second.
sentences.zh: 影片最初会以高帧率拍摄（通常为每秒300帧，因为它可以毫无大碍地转换为低得多的帧率），但在后期剪辑阶段，这一高帧率只会保留给捕捉猎物的部分，而游泳部分则会被转换为每秒24帧的正常速度。

sentences.en: Voila, the scientists can now sit back and enjoy watching without having to go through the pain of waiting.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，科学家们如今就可以安然坐享观影之乐，而不必经历等待之苦。

sentences.en: F Sometimes taking a good picture or shooting a good film is not all about technology, but patience, like in the case of bat.
sentences.zh: 有时候，拍出一张好照片或一部好影片并不全在于技术，而在于耐心，拍摄蝙蝠的情况便是如此。

sentences.en: Bats are small, dark-colored; they fly fast and are active only at night.
sentences.zh: 蝙蝠体型小、颜色深；它们飞行迅速，而且只在夜间活动。

sentences.en: To capture bats on film, one must use some type of camera-tripping device.
sentences.zh: 要将蝙蝠拍摄下来，必须使用某种类型的相机触发装置。

sentences.en: Photographers or film-makers often place camera near the bat cave, on the path of the flying bats.
sentences.zh: 摄影师或影片制作者常把相机安放在蝙蝠洞附近、飞行蝙蝠经过的路径上。

sentences.en: The camera must be hard-wired with a tripping device so that every time a bat breaks the tripping beam the camera fires and it will keep doing so through the night until the camera’s battery runs out.
sentences.zh: 相机必须与触发装置硬连线相连，这样每当蝙蝠截断触发光束，相机就会拍摄，并且会整夜持续如此，直到相机的电池耗尽。

sentences.en: Though highly-advanced tripping device can now allow for unmanned shooting, it still may take several nights lo get a truly high quality film.
sentences.zh: 尽管如今高度先进的触发装置已经可以实现无人拍摄，但要得到一部真正高质量的影片，可能仍需要好几个晚上。

sentences.en: G Is it science?
sentences.zh: 这是科学吗？

sentences.en: Is it art?
sentences.zh: 这是艺术吗？

sentences.en: Since the technique was first pioneered around two hundred years ago, photography has developed to a state where it is almost unrecognisable.
sentences.zh: 自从这项技术在大约两百年前首次开创以来，摄影已经发展到几乎让人认不出来的地步。

sentences.en: Some people would even say the future of photography will be nothing like how we imagine it.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至会说，摄影的未来将完全不是我们想象的样子。

sentences.en: No matter what future it may hold, photography will continue to develop as it has been repeatedly demonstrated in many aspects of our life that “a picture is worth a thousand words.”
sentences.zh: 无论未来会怎样，摄影都将持续发展，正如我们生活的许多方面已经一再证明的那样：“一图胜千言”。

sentences.en: A Imagine a page with a square box in the middle.
sentences.zh: 想象一张纸，中间有一个方框。

sentences.en: The box is lined with rows of the number 5, repeated over and over.
sentences.zh: 方框里排列着一行行数字5，反复重复出现。

sentences.en: All of the 5s are identical in size, font and colour, and equally distributed across the box.
sentences.zh: 所有的5在大小、字体和颜色上都完全相同，并且均匀地分布在方框中。

sentences.en: There is, however, a trick: among those 5s, hiding in plain sight is a single, capital letter S.
sentences.zh: 然而，这里有个小把戏：在那些5之中，明明就在眼前却藏着一个大写字母S。

sentences.en: Almost the same in shape, it is impossible to spot without straining your eyes for a good few minutes.
sentences.zh: 它的形状几乎一模一样，不眯着眼睛盯上好几分钟根本不可能发现它。

sentences.en: Unless that is, you are a grapheme–colour synaesthete – a person who sees each letter and number in different colours.
sentences.zh: 除非你是一名字位-颜色联觉者——一个能看到每个字母和数字呈现不同颜色的人。

sentences.en: With all the 5s painted in one colour and the rogue S painted in another, a grapheme–colour synaesthete will usually only need a split second to identify the latter.
sentences.zh: 由于所有的5都被染成一种颜色，而那个混入的S被染成另一种颜色，字位-颜色联觉者通常只需一瞬间就能辨认出后者。

sentences.en: B Synaesthesia, loosely translated as “senses coming together” from the Greek words syn (“with”) and aesthesis (“sensation”), is an interesting neurological phenomenon that causes different senses to be combined.
sentences.zh: 联觉一词大致译为“感官交融”，源自希腊语syn（意为“与……一起”）和aesthesis（意为“感觉”），它是一种有趣的神经现象，会使不同的感官结合在一起。

sentences.en: This might mean that words have a particular taste (for example, the word “door” might taste like bacon), or that certain smells produce a particular colour.
sentences.zh: 这可能意味着词语带有某种特定的味道（例如，“door”这个词尝起来可能像培根），或者某些气味会产生某种特定的颜色。

sentences.en: It might also mean that each letter and number has its own personality—the letter A might be perky, the letter B might be shy and self-conscious, etc.
sentences.zh: 它也可能意味着每个字母和数字都有自己的个性——字母A可能活泼俏皮，字母B可能羞涩而拘谨，等等。

sentences.en: Some synaesthetes might even experience other people’s sensations, for example feeling pain in their chest when they witness a film character gets shot.
sentences.zh: 有些联觉者甚至可能体验到他人的感受，例如当他们看到电影角色中枪时，自己的胸口会感到疼痛。

sentences.en: The possibilities are endless: even though synaesthesia is believed to affect less than 5% of the general population, at least 60 different combinations of senses have been reported so far.
sentences.zh: 可能性无穷无尽：尽管人们认为联觉影响的人不到普通人群的5%，但迄今为止已报告了至少60种不同的感官组合。

sentences.en: What all these sensory associations have in common is that they are all involuntary and impossible to repress and that they usually remain quite stable over time.
sentences.zh: 所有这些感官关联的共同点在于，它们都是不由自主、无法抑制的，而且通常会随时间保持相当稳定。

sentences.en: C Synaesthesia was first documented in the early 19th century by German physician Georg Sachs, who dedicated two pages of his dissertation on his own experience with the condition.
sentences.zh: 联觉最早在19世纪初由德国医生格奥尔格·萨克斯记录下来，他在自己的论文中用两页篇幅描述了自身患有这种状况的经历。

sentences.en: It was not, however, until the mid-1990s that empirical research proved its existence when Professor Simon Baron-Cohen and his colleagues used fMRIs on six synaesthetes and discovered that the parts of the brain associated with vision were active during auditory stimulation, even though the subjects were blindfolded.
sentences.zh: 然而，直到20世纪90年代中期，实证研究才证明了它的存在。当时西蒙·巴伦-科恩教授及其同事对六名联觉者进行了功能性磁共振成像，发现即便受试者被蒙住双眼，与视觉相关的大脑区域在听觉刺激下仍然处于活跃状态。

sentences.en: D What makes synaesthesia a particularly interesting condition is that it is not an illness at all.
sentences.zh: 联觉之所以是一种特别有趣的状况，原因在于它根本不是一种疾病。

sentences.en: If anything, synaesthetes often report feeling sorry for the rest of the population, as they do not have the opportunity to experience the world in a multisensory fashion like they do.
sentences.zh: 如果说有什么的话，联觉者往往表示为其余人感到惋惜，因为这些人没有机会像他们那样以多感官的方式去体验世界。

sentences.en: Very few drawbacks have been described, usually minimal: for instance, some words might have an unpleasant taste (imagine the word “hello” tasting like spoilt milk), while some synaesthetes find it distressing when they encounter people with names which do not reflect their personality (imagine meeting a very interesting person named “Lee”, when the letter E has a dull or hideous colour for you—or vice versa).
sentences.zh: 已被描述的弊端极少，且通常很轻微：例如，有些词语可能带有令人不快的味道（想象一下“hello”这个词尝起来像变质的牛奶），而有些联觉者在遇到名字与其个性不符的人时会感到困扰（想象一下遇见一位非常有趣的人名叫“Lee”，可对你来说字母E却是一种暗淡或丑陋的颜色——或者反过来也一样）。

sentences.en: Overall, however, synaesthesia is widely considered more of a blessing than a curse and it is often linked to intelligence and creativity, with celebrities such as Lady Gaga and Pharrell Williams claiming to have it.
sentences.zh: 然而总体而言，联觉被广泛认为更像是一种福分而非诅咒，它常常与智力和创造力联系在一起，像Lady Gaga和Pharrell Williams这样的名人都声称自己拥有这种能力。

sentences.en: E Another fascinating side of synaesthesia is the way it could potentially benefit future generations.
sentences.zh: 联觉另一个引人入胜的方面在于它可能为后代带来益处。

sentences.en: In a 2013 study, Dr Witthof and Dr Winawer discovered that grapheme-colour synaesthetes who had never met each other before experienced strikingly similar pairings between graphemes and colours—pairings which were later traced back to a popular set of Fischer-Price magnets that ten out of eleven participants distinctly remembered possessing as children.
sentences.zh: 在一项2013年的研究中，威特霍夫博士和威纳沃博士发现，此前从未见过面的字位-颜色联觉者对字位与颜色之间的配对惊人地相似——这些配对后来被追溯到一套流行的Fischer-Price磁贴，十一名参与者中有十人都清楚地记得自己儿时拥有过这套磁贴。

sentences.en: This was particularly peculiar as synaesthesia is predominantly considered to be a hereditary condition, and the findings suggested that a synaesthete’s environment might play a determining role in establishing synaesthetic associations.
sentences.zh: 这一点尤其奇特，因为联觉主要被认为是一种遗传性状况，而这些发现表明联觉者所处的环境可能在建立联觉关联中起着决定性作用。

sentences.en: If that was true, researchers asked, then might it not be possible that synaesthesia can actually be taught?
sentences.zh: 研究人员发问道，如果这是真的，那么联觉是否实际上有可能被教会呢？

sentences.en: F As it turns out, the benefits of teaching synaesthesia would be tremendous.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，教授联觉所带来的益处将是巨大的。

sentences.en: According to research conducted by Dr Clare Jonas at the University of East London, teaching people to create grapheme-colour associations the same way as a synaesthete may have the possibility to improve cognitive function and memory.
sentences.zh: 根据东伦敦大学克莱尔·乔纳斯博士开展的研究，教人像联觉者那样建立字位-颜色关联，有可能改善认知功能和记忆力。

sentences.en: As she put it, ‘one possibility is guarding against cognitive decline in older people—using synaesthesia in the creation of mnemonics to remember things such as shopping lists.’
sentences.zh: 正如她所说：“一种可能性是防范老年人的认知衰退——利用联觉来创建记忆口诀，以记住诸如购物清单之类的事情。”

sentences.en: To that end, researchers in the Netherlands have already begun developing a web browser plug-in that will change the colours of certain letters.
sentences.zh: 为此，荷兰的研究人员已经开始开发一款网页浏览器插件，它会改变某些字母的颜色。

sentences.en: Rothen and his colleagues corroborate the theory: in a paper published in 2011, they suggest that synaesthesia might be more than a hereditary condition, as the non-synaesthetic subjects of their study were able to mimic synaesthetic associations long after leaving the lab.
sentences.zh: 罗滕及其同事印证了这一理论：在2011年发表的一篇论文中，他们提出联觉可能不止是一种遗传性状况，因为他们研究中那些非联觉受试者在离开实验室很久之后仍能模仿出联觉关联。

sentences.en: G There is obviously still a long way to go before we can fully understand synaesthesia and what causes it.
sentences.zh: 显然，在我们能够完全理解联觉及其成因之前，还有很长的路要走。

sentences.en: Once we do, however, it might not be too long before we find out how to teach non-synaesthetes how to imitate its symptoms in a way that induces the same benefits 4.4% of the world’s population currently enjoy.
sentences.zh: 然而，一旦我们做到了这一点，或许用不了多久，我们就能弄清楚如何教非联觉者模仿其表现，从而诱发出当今全球4.4%人口所享有的那些益处。

sentences.en: A Six miles outside the town of Decorah, Iowa in the USA, an 890-acre stretch of rolling fields and woods called Heritage Farm is letting its crops go to seed.
sentences.zh: 在美国艾奥瓦州迪科拉镇外六英里处，一片占地890英亩、由起伏的田野和林地构成的区域名为传承农场，它正任由自己的作物结籽。

sentences.en: Everything about Heritage Farm is in stark contrast to the surrounding acres of intensively farmed fields of corn and soybean that are typical of modern agriculture.
sentences.zh: 传承农场的一切都与周围那些典型代表现代农业的集约化玉米和大豆田形成鲜明对比。

sentences.en: Heritage Farm is devoted to collecting rather than growing seeds.
sentences.zh: 传承农场致力于收集种子而非种植种子。

sentences.en: It is home to the Seed Savers Exchange, one of the largest non government-owned seed banks in the United States.
sentences.zh: 这里是种子保存交流会的所在地，它是美国最大的非政府所有种子库之一。

sentences.en: B In 1975 Diane Ott Whealy was given the seedlings of two plant varieties that her great grandfather had brought to America from Bavaria in 1870: Grandpa Ott’s morning glory and his German Pink tomato.
sentences.zh: 1975年，黛安·奥特·惠利得到了两个植物品种的幼苗，那是她的曾祖父在1870年从巴伐利亚带到美国的——奥特爷爷的牵牛花和他的德国粉番茄。

sentences.en: Wanting to preserve similar traditional varieties, known as heirloom plants, Diane and her husband, Kent, decided to establish a place where the seeds of the past could be kept and traded.
sentences.zh: 由于想要保存类似的传统品种——即所谓的传家宝植物——黛安和她的丈夫肯特决定建立一个可以保存和交换昔日种子的地方。

sentences.en: The exchange now has more than 13,000 members, and the many thousands of heirloom varieties they have donated are kept in its walk-in coolers, freezers, and root cellars.
sentences.zh: 如今该交流会拥有超过13000名会员，他们捐赠的数千个传家宝品种被保存在其步入式冷藏室、冷冻库和地窖中。

sentences.en: As you walk around an old red barn that is covered in Grandpa Ott’s beautiful morning glory blossoms, you come across the different vegetables, herbs, and flowers they have planted there.
sentences.zh: 当你绕着一座爬满奥特爷爷美丽牵牛花的红色旧谷仓走动时，会遇到他们在那里种植的各种蔬菜、香草和花卉。

sentences.en: C “Each year our members list their seeds in this,” Diane Ott Whealy says, handing over a copy of the Seed Savers Exchange 2010 Yearbook.
sentences.zh: 黛安·奥特·惠利说道，“每年我们的会员都会把他们的种子登记在这里面”，同时递过来一本《种子保存交流会2010年鉴》。

sentences.en: It is as thick as a big-city telephone directory, with page after page of exotic beans, garlic, potatoes, peppers, apples, pears, and plums—each with its own name and personal history.
sentences.zh: 它像大城市的电话簿一样厚，一页又一页地列着各种奇特的豆类、大蒜、土豆、辣椒、苹果、梨和李子——每一种都有自己的名字和身世。

sentences.en: For example, there’s an Estonian Yellow Cherry tomato, which was brought to the seed bank by “an elderly Russian lady” who lived in Tallinn, and a Persian Star garlic from “a bazaar in Samarkand.”
sentences.zh: 例如，有一种爱沙尼亚黄樱桃番茄，是由一位住在塔林的“俄罗斯老妇人”带到种子库的，还有一种波斯星大蒜来自“撒马尔罕的一个集市”。

sentences.en: There’s also a bean donated by archaeologists searching for pygmy elephant fossils in New Mexico.
sentences.zh: 还有一种豆子，是由在新墨西哥州寻找侏儒象化石的考古学家捐赠的。

sentences.en: D Heirloom vegetables have become fashionable in the United States and Europe over the past decade, prized by a food movement that emphasizes eating locally and preserving the flavor and uniqueness of heirloom varieties.
sentences.zh: 在过去十年间，传家宝蔬菜在美国和欧洲变得时髦起来，受到一场强调本地饮食并保留传家宝品种风味与独特性的食物运动的推崇。

sentences.en: Found mostly in farmers' markets and boutique groceries, heirloom varieties have been squeezed out of supermarkets in favor of modern single-variety fruits and vegetables bred to ship well and have a uniform appearance, not to enhance flavor.
sentences.zh: 传家宝品种大多只能在农贸市场和精品杂货店里见到，它们已被挤出超市，取而代之的是为便于运输和外观统一而培育、而非为提升风味而培育的现代单一品种水果和蔬菜。

sentences.en: But the movement to preserve heirloom varieties goes way beyond the current interest in North America and Europe in tasty, locally grown food.
sentences.zh: 但保护传家宝品种的运动远远超出了当前北美和欧洲对美味、本地种植食物的兴趣。

sentences.en: It’s also a campaign to protect the world’s future food supply.
sentences.zh: 它也是一场保护世界未来粮食供应的运动。

sentences.en: Most people in the well-fed world give little thought to where their food comes from or how it’s grown.
sentences.zh: 在那些衣食无忧的地区，大多数人很少去想自己的食物从何而来或是如何种植的。

sentences.en: They wander through well-stocked supermarkets without realizing that there may be problem ahead.
sentences.zh: 他们在货品充足的超市里闲逛，却没有意识到前方可能存在问题。

sentences.en: We’ve been hearing for some time about the loss of flora and fauna in our rainforests.
sentences.zh: 一段时间以来，我们一直听说雨林中动植物的消失。

sentences.en: Very little, by contrast, is being said or done about the parallel decline in the diversity of the foods we eat.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，对于我们所吃食物多样性同步衰减一事，人们说得很少，做得也很少。

sentences.en: E Food variety extinction is happening all over the world - and it's happening fast.
sentences.zh: 食物品种的灭绝正在世界各地发生——而且发生得很快。

sentences.en: In the United States an estimated 90 percent of historic fruit and vegetable varieties are no longer grown.
sentences.zh: 在美国，据估计有90%的历史悠久的水果和蔬菜品种已不再种植。

sentences.en: Of the 7,000 different apple varieties that were grown in the 1800s, fewer than a hundred remain.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪种植的7000个不同的苹果品种中，如今留存下来的不足一百个。

sentences.en: In the Philippines thousands of varieties of rice once thrived; now only about a hundred are grown there.
sentences.zh: 在菲律宾，曾经有数千个水稻品种繁盛生长，如今那里只种植大约一百个品种。

sentences.en: In China 90 percent of the wheat varieties cultivated just a hundred years ago have disappeared.
sentences.zh: 在中国，仅仅一百年前栽培的小麦品种中，有90%已经消失。

sentences.en: Experts estimate that in total we have lost more than 50 percent of the world's food varieties over the past century.
sentences.zh: 专家估计，在过去的一个世纪里，我们总共失去了世界上超过50%的食物品种。

sentences.en: F Why is this a problem?
sentences.zh: 这为什么是个问题呢？

sentences.en: Because if disease or future climate change affects one of the handful of plants we've come to depend on to feed our growing planet, we might desperately need one of those varieties we've let become extinct.
sentences.zh: 因为如果疾病或未来的气候变化影响到我们赖以养活这个不断增长的星球的少数几种植物中的某一种，我们可能会迫切需要那些已被我们任其灭绝的品种中的某一个。

sentences.en: The loss of the world's cereal diversity is a particular cause for concern.
sentences.zh: 世界谷物多样性的丧失尤其令人担忧。

sentences.en: A fungus called Ug99, which was first identified in Uganda in 1999, is spreading across the world's wheat crops.
sentences.zh: 一种名为Ug99的真菌于1999年首次在乌干达被发现，如今正在世界各地的小麦作物中蔓延。

sentences.en: From Uganda it moved to Kenya, Ethiopia, Sudan, and Yemen.
sentences.zh: 它从乌干达蔓延到了肯尼亚、埃塞俄比亚、苏丹和也门。

sentences.en: By 2007 it had jumped the Persian Gulf into Iran.
sentences.zh: 到2007年，它已越过波斯湾进入伊朗。

sentences.en: Scientists predict that the fungus will soon make its way into India and Pakistan, then spread to Russia and China, and eventually the USA.
sentences.zh: 科学家预测，这种真菌很快会进入印度和巴基斯坦，然后蔓延到俄罗斯和中国，最终到达美国。

sentences.en: G Roughly 90 percent of the world's wheat has no defense against this particular fungus.
sentences.zh: 全世界大约90%的小麦对这种特定的真菌毫无抵抗力。

sentences.en: If it reached the USA, an estimated one billion dollars' worth of crops would be at risk.
sentences.zh: 如果它到达美国，据估计将有价值十亿美元的作物面临风险。

sentences.en: Scientists believe that in Asia and Africa alone, the portion currently in danger could leave one billion people without their primary food source.
sentences.zh: 科学家认为，仅在亚洲和非洲，目前处于危险中的那部分小麦就可能使十亿人失去他们的主要食物来源。

sentences.en: A famine with significant humanitarian consequences could follow, according to Rick Ward of Cornell University.
sentences.zh: 据康奈尔大学的里克·沃德所说，随之而来的可能是一场具有重大人道主义后果的饥荒。

sentences.en: H The population of the world is expected to reach nine billion by 2045.
sentences.zh: 预计到2045年世界人口将达到九十亿。

sentences.en: Some experts say we'll need to double our food production to keep up with this growth.
sentences.zh: 一些专家说，我们将需要把食物产量翻一番才能跟上这一增长。

sentences.en: Given the added challenge of climate change and disease, it is becoming ever more urgent to find ways to increase food yield.
sentences.zh: 考虑到气候变化和疾病带来的额外挑战，寻找提高粮食产量的方法变得越来越紧迫。

sentences.en: The world has become increasingly dependent upon a technology-driven, one-size-fits-all approach to food supply.
sentences.zh: 世界已日益依赖一种技术驱动的、一刀切的粮食供应方式。

sentences.en: Yet the best hope for securing our food's future may depend on our ability to preserve the locally cultivated foods of the past.
sentences.zh: 然而，确保我们粮食未来的最大希望，或许取决于我们保存昔日本地栽培食物的能力。

records.title: John Ray And The Study Of Plants

sentences.en: A The 17th-century English scholar and botanist John Ray was well aware that he lived through, and participated in, a profound revolution in the way people interacted with nature.
sentences.zh: 17世纪的英国学者兼植物学家约翰·雷十分清楚，他亲历并参与了人与自然互动方式的一场深刻变革。

sentences.en: In the preface to his Synopsis of British Plants, published in 1690, he gave thanks that he had been born at a time when traditional dependence on the teaching of the Greek philosopher Aristotle (384-322 BCE) had given way to a new philosophy, based on experiment and observation of the real world, that we now call science.
sentences.zh: 在1690年出版的《英国植物概要》的序言中，他庆幸自己出生在这样一个时代——对希腊哲学家亚里士多德（公元前384-前322年）学说的传统依赖，已让位于一种以实验和对真实世界的观察为基础的新哲学，也就是我们如今所说的科学。

sentences.en: B Ray was born in 1627.
sentences.zh: 雷出生于1627年。

sentences.en: His father was a village blacksmith, and his mother was also a respected member of the community, a healer who was an expert in folk medicine and the use of herbs to treat ailments.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲是一名乡村铁匠，母亲也是社区中备受尊敬的一员，是一位精通民间医术、擅长用草药治病的疗愈者。

sentences.en: Ray must have stood out as an unusually bright boy among his schoolmates, and his talents were recognised by a church official, Samuel Covell, who had graduated from Cambridge University in 1600, and maintained his links with his university.
sentences.zh: 在同学之中，雷一定是个异常聪颖的男孩，他的才能受到了一位教会官员塞缪尔·科维尔的赏识——此人于1600年毕业于剑桥大学，并一直与母校保持着联系。

sentences.en: Through his influence, Ray was admitted to Cambridge University in 1644 at the age of seventeen - a huge step for a village blacksmith's son.
sentences.zh: 在他的影响下，雷于1644年十七岁时被剑桥大学录取——对一个乡村铁匠的儿子来说，这是迈出的巨大一步。

sentences.en: There he made a solid start, and quickly gained a reputation as a brilliant student.
sentences.zh: 在那里他开局扎实，很快就赢得了优秀学生的名声。

sentences.en: He studied the classics (Greek, Latin and Hebrew) and mathematics, but there was nothing yet we would now call science in the curriculum.
sentences.zh: 他研习古典学科（希腊语、拉丁语和希伯来语）以及数学，但课程中还没有任何我们如今会称之为科学的内容。

sentences.en: After graduating in 1648, he became a minor member of staff at Trinity College, Cambridge.
sentences.zh: 1648年毕业后，他成为剑桥三一学院的一名低级教职人员。

sentences.en: He was appointed Lecturer in Greek in 1651, Lecturer in Mathematics in 1653, and Lecturer in Humanities in 1655.
sentences.zh: 他于1651年被任命为希腊语讲师，1653年被任命为数学讲师，1655年被任命为人文学讲师。

sentences.en: C Almost immediately after graduating, Ray also seems to have developed the interest to which he would devote the rest of his life: the study of the natural world.
sentences.zh: 几乎在毕业后立刻，雷似乎也培养起了他将为之奉献余生的兴趣——对自然世界的研究。

sentences.en: He explains this conversion into a naturalist - in particular into a botanist - in the preface to his first book, the Cambridge Catalogue of English Plants.
sentences.zh: 他在自己第一本书《剑桥英国植物名录》的序言中，解释了他向博物学家——尤其是向植物学家——的这一转变。

sentences.en: Here Ray tells us that he suffered an illness in his early twenties, and was advised to take long walks and ride in the fresh air while recovering.
sentences.zh: 在书中雷告诉我们，他二十出头时生了一场病，康复期间有人建议他多在新鲜空气中长途散步和骑马。

sentences.en: While doing this, he became interested in the local flora, and finding nobody able to teach him, Ray investigated it for himself.
sentences.zh: 在做这些事时，他对当地的植物群产生了兴趣，而由于找不到能教他的人，雷便自己去钻研。

sentences.en: He then went on to pass on the knowledge he acquired to others.
sentences.zh: 随后他又把自己获得的知识传授给他人。

sentences.en: D By the mid-1650s, even the first-year students at Trinity College were able to identify the plants and flowers around Cambridge, as they were being taught (unofficially - none of this was part of their formal education) by Ray.
sentences.zh: 到了1650年代中期，连三一学院的一年级学生都能辨认出剑桥周边的植物和花卉，因为他们正受教于雷（这是非正式的——这一切都不属于他们的正规教育）。

sentences.en: Many of them were the sons of landowners, and so had a natural, if amateurish, interest in country matters.
sentences.zh: 他们当中许多人是地主之子，因而对乡间事务怀有一种天然的——尽管业余的——兴趣。

sentences.en: But a few of them took his efforts to understand the natural world much more seriously.
sentences.zh: 但其中少数人则远为认真地对待他理解自然世界的努力。

sentences.en: One of these, Francis Willughby, later played an important part in Ray's life.
sentences.zh: 其中一人弗朗西斯·威路比，后来在雷的人生中扮演了重要角色。

sentences.en: E Having himself had no authority on the subject of plants on which to draw, Ray also started work on what would become his Cambridge Catalogue of English Plants.
sentences.zh: 由于在植物这一主题上自己没有任何权威可资借鉴，雷也开始着手编写后来成为他《剑桥英国植物名录》的著作。

sentences.en: The work was not published until 1660 because, as Ray explained in the preface, he had to start from scratch: "I had first to become familiar with the literature, to compare the plants that I found with the pictures, and when there seemed to be a resemblance, to go fully into any unknown descriptions.
sentences.zh: 正如雷在序言中所解释的，这部著作直到1660年才出版，因为他不得不从头做起——“我首先得熟悉相关文献，把我找到的植物与图片加以比对，当似乎存在相似之处时，再深入研究任何未知的描述。

sentences.en: Gaining skill by experience, I acquired at last the ability to recognise to what tribe and family similars or could be assigned; this taught me to search for similarities and saved a vast deal of labour, which others would have spent in their difficulties.
sentences.zh: 凭经验逐渐获得技能，我最终具备了识别相似类群可归入何种族属与科目的能力；这教会了我去寻找相似之处，省去了大量劳作，而他人本会在其困难中耗费这些精力。

sentences.en: I was eager to make the most of this and was fortunate to share my enthusiasm with my friends..."
sentences.zh: 我渴望充分利用这一点，并有幸与我的朋友们分享我的热情……”

sentences.en: F Ray's Cambridge Catalogue of English Plants was much more than a simple list of species.
sentences.zh: 雷的《剑桥英国植物名录》远不只是一份简单的物种清单。

sentences.en: It gave the names of plants found in the area around Cambridge and included information about where they grew and how common they were.
sentences.zh: 它给出了剑桥周边地区所发现植物的名称，并收录了关于它们生长地点及其常见程度的信息。

sentences.en: In doing this, Ray was producing something that would be of practical use to students and other readers interested in the local natural world.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，雷便创作出了一部对学生及其他对当地自然世界感兴趣的读者具有实际用途的著作。

sentences.en: At the same time, the book showed his determination to describe plants accurately, on the basis of direct examination rather than reliance on old authorities.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，这本书显示出他立志准确描述植物的决心——以直接考察为依据，而非依赖前人权威。

sentences.en: In this respect, it reflected the spirit of the new learning that Ray admired.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，它体现了雷所推崇的新学问的精神。

sentences.en: G Ray's studies of plants were only the beginning of a much larger ambition.
sentences.zh: 雷对植物的研究只是一个远为宏大的抱负的开端。

sentences.en: With the support of Francis Willughby, he began to imagine a more comprehensive investigation of nature, one that would attempt to classify living things according to careful observation of their shared characteristics.
sentences.zh: 在弗朗西斯·威路比的支持下，他开始构想一项对自然更为全面的考察——一项试图依据对生物共有特征的细致观察来对其进行分类的工作。

sentences.en: This was an ambitious undertaking, especially at a time when many aspects of the natural world remained poorly described.
sentences.zh: 这是一项雄心勃勃的事业，尤其是在自然世界的许多方面仍未得到充分描述的当时。

sentences.en: Yet Ray believed that by collecting evidence systematically and comparing related forms, it would be possible to build a more reliable understanding of nature than scholars had possessed before.
sentences.zh: 然而雷相信，通过系统地收集证据并对相关形态加以比较，就有可能建立起一种比以往学者所拥有的更为可靠的对自然的理解。

sentences.en: (A) Guédelon is no ordinary building site.
sentences.zh: 盖德隆并非一处普通的建筑工地。

sentences.en: There is no rumble of diggers or shriek of circular saws.
sentences.zh: 这里没有挖掘机的轰鸣，也没有圆锯的尖啸。

sentences.en: All is peaceful and quiet, save for the continual tapping of the small army of stonemasons, the quacking of the ducks or the occasional crow of the cockerel.
sentences.zh: 一切都安宁而寂静，只有那一小队石匠持续不断的敲凿声、鸭子的嘎嘎叫声以及偶尔传来的公鸡啼鸣。

sentences.en: Slowly but surely, a brand new medieval castle is rising from the woods of Guédelon, Yonne, home to the Burgundy vineyards in the heart of France.
sentences.zh: 在法国心脏地带、勃艮第葡萄园所在的约讷省盖德隆的树林里，一座崭新的中世纪城堡正缓慢却坚定地拔地而起。

sentences.en: The year is 1229—that is, for the purposes of this project: to build a prince’s château fort using only the techniques and tools of the 13th century.
sentences.zh: 如今是1229年——就这个项目的设定而言是这样：仅用13世纪的技术与工具，建造一座王公的城堡式要塞。

sentences.en: (B) ‘The project has four main aims,’ explains Maryline Martin, managing director for Guédelon.
sentences.zh: 盖德隆的总经理玛丽琳·马丁解释说：“这个项目有四个主要目标。”

sentences.en: ‘The first is experimental archaeology – to try and verify all the theories, based on documents of the time.
sentences.zh: “第一个是实验考古学——根据当时的文献，尝试去验证所有的理论。

sentences.en: There’s also a social aim, because this region is very poor, with high unemployment: so it provides jobs.
sentences.zh: 还有一个社会层面的目标，因为这个地区非常贫穷、失业率很高：所以它能提供工作岗位。

sentences.en: Then there’s tourism: the project couldn’t work without visitors because a lot of money is needed to pay people working here and to run the site.
sentences.zh: 接下来是旅游：没有游客，这个项目就无法运转，因为需要大量资金来支付在这里工作的人员并维持工地运营。

sentences.en: And finally, we want to open experimental archaeology to everybody – because in France, history and architecture are still very much oriented to academics.’
sentences.zh: 最后，我们希望把实验考古学向所有人开放——因为在法国，历史与建筑在很大程度上仍然是面向学术界的。”

sentences.en: (C) The idea for the project emerged about five years ago.
sentences.zh: 这个项目的构想大约在五年前萌生。

sentences.en: It was the brainchild of Michel Guyot, who bought and renovated the nearby castle of Saint-Fargeau, which was built and rebuilt between the 10th and 18th centuries.
sentences.zh: 它是米歇尔·居约的创意结晶，他买下并修复了附近的圣法尔若城堡，那座城堡在10世纪到18世纪之间历经建造与重建。

sentences.en: Beneath his castle were the original foundations of the 13th-century building.
sentences.zh: 在他的城堡之下，是那座13世纪建筑最初的地基。

sentences.en: Guyot thought it would be fun to construct a château to the same plans, but this proved too big to attempt.
sentences.zh: 居约觉得按照同样的图纸建造一座城堡会很有趣，但事实证明这个规模太大、难以尝试。

sentences.en: So Jacques Moulin, managing director for the local historical monuments, drew up plans for a smaller castle that would still be ambitious, but realistic.
sentences.zh: 于是当地历史古迹的总负责人雅克·穆兰绘制了一座较小城堡的图纸，它既有雄心又切合实际。

sentences.en: Five months later, having managed to get together 600,000 Euros in funding, they began looking for a site that would provide all the materials they needed: stone, water, sand, wood, iron and clay.
sentences.zh: 五个月后，他们设法筹集到了600000欧元的资金，开始寻找一处能提供他们所需全部材料的场地：石头、水、沙子、木材、铁和黏土。

sentences.en: They found it at Guédelon.
sentences.zh: 他们在盖德隆找到了这样的地方。

sentences.en: (D) The only major cheat so far was early on when a mechanical earthmover was brought in to raise the castle floor.
sentences.zh: 迄今为止唯一一次重大的取巧发生在早期，当时引入了一台机械挖土机来抬高城堡的地面。

sentences.en: Archaeologists know how it was done in the 13th century: by backbreaking, tedious work.
sentences.zh: 考古学家知道在13世纪这是怎么做的：靠累断脊背、枯燥乏味的劳作。

sentences.en: ‘To do it by hand would have added ten years to the project,’ says Franck, one of the site’s guides.
sentences.zh: “若全靠手工完成，这个项目要多花十年。”工地向导之一弗兰克说。

sentences.en: It’s still a long, painstaking task.
sentences.zh: 这依然是一项漫长而费力的工作。

sentences.en: Next to the beginnings of the east wall is the quarry, where masons extract the ferruginous limestone to build the thick castle walls.
sentences.zh: 在东墙的起始处旁边是采石场，石匠们在那里开采含铁的石灰岩，用来砌筑厚实的城堡墙。

sentences.en: They bore lines of holes into the rocks and then they hammer metal wedges into them until the rock splits along the line.
sentences.zh: 他们在岩石上钻出一排排孔洞，然后把金属楔子敲进去，直到岩石沿着这条线裂开。

sentences.en: It is then hewn into bricks, and cemented together with a mortar of chalk, sand and quicklime.
sentences.zh: 随后岩石被凿成砖块，并用白垩、沙子和生石灰制成的砂浆黏合在一起。

sentences.en: Quicklime is made by heating limestone to 800°C – done off-site because of the poisonous gases that come from the process.
sentences.zh: 生石灰是把石灰岩加热到800°C制成的——由于这一过程会产生有毒气体，所以在场外进行。

sentences.en: Little wonder that 13th-century lime-burners had a life expectancy of only 25–30 years.
sentences.zh: 难怪13世纪的烧石灰工人预期寿命只有25–30岁。

sentences.en: ‘The bricks are then laid horizontally for the first metre of the wall, and vertically thereafter,’ says Franck, ‘because if there was a shock from, say, a catapult, and the stones were all laid in the same way, the shockwave would shatter the wall.’
sentences.zh: “墙的第一米，砖块是水平铺砌的，此后则是竖直铺砌，”弗兰克说，“因为如果遭到——比方说投石机——的冲击，而石头又都以同样方式铺砌，冲击波就会震碎整面墙。”

sentences.en: (E) The scientists and craftspeople alike are learning on the job, as they don’t know exactly why or how things were done as the historical evidence suggests.
sentences.zh: 科学家和工匠都在边干边学，因为他们并不确切知道历史证据所提示的那些做法究竟为何、又是如何完成的。

sentences.en: One such discovery concerns the significance of the marks that masons carved into each finished stone.
sentences.zh: 其中一项发现，关乎石匠在每块完工石料上所刻标记的意义。

sentences.en: It was thought that these probably had superstitious meaning, but experience and archaeological research reveals three very practical uses: to establish how much each mason should be paid; to keep track of who made what, in case of any problems; and to specify where the stone should be placed in the castle reconstruction.
sentences.zh: 人们曾认为这些标记大概带有迷信含义，但经验和考古研究揭示了三种非常实用的用途：用来确定每位石匠应得的报酬；在出现任何问题时追踪谁做了哪块；以及指明这块石料在城堡重建中应放置的位置。

sentences.en: (F) Guédelon has a scientific committee of archaeologists that discusses ideas and problems as they emerge, and will approve works and practices only when its members are sure that they are true to the 13th century.
sentences.zh: 盖德隆有一个由考古学家组成的科学委员会，随着各种想法和问题的出现进行讨论，只有当成员们确信某项工艺与做法忠实于13世纪时，才会予以批准。

sentences.en: Reaching unanimity is not always easy.
sentences.zh: 要达成一致意见并不总是容易的。

sentences.en: ‘All the big plans for the castle itself are all done but the details aren’t settled,’ says Martin.
sentences.zh: “城堡本身的所有大型规划都已完成，但细节尚未敲定，”马丁说。

sentences.en: ‘So, during the winter, the site manager and I visit other castles in the region.
sentences.zh: “所以在冬天，工地经理和我会去参观这个地区的其他城堡。

sentences.en: When we see something we want to do here, we draw a sketch, make plans and show this to the committee.’
sentences.zh: 当我们看到想在这里采用的东西时，就画一张草图、做出规划，再把它展示给委员会。”

sentences.en: (G) The castle will take at least a decade longer to build than it would have in the 13th century.
sentences.zh: 这座城堡的建造时间，至少要比它在13世纪建造时多出十年。

sentences.en: ‘With the same number of workers it would have taken 15 years then,’ says Franck.
sentences.zh: “用同样数量的工人，当年只需15年就能建成，”弗兰克说。

sentences.en: ‘But we could do this too if we had only professional workers, if the site wasn’t open to the public and if we worked harder – today it’s illegal to work more than 8 hours a day, as they did at the time.’
sentences.zh: “但如果我们只用专业工人、工地不向公众开放、而且工作更卖力，我们也能做到——如今每天工作超过8小时是违法的，而当时他们却是这样干的。”

sentences.en: (H) Workers come and go but at any one time about 40 people are working on the site.
sentences.zh: 工人来来去去，但任何时候大约都有40人在工地上劳作。

sentences.en: Some are students, others have ‘downshifted’ from other careers, others are local unemployed people learning skills they might use elsewhere – say, in château restorations around France.
sentences.zh: 有些是学生，有些是从别的职业“降速转行”而来，还有些是当地的失业者，他们在学习一些或许能用在别处的技能——比如用于法国各地的城堡修复。

sentences.en: They are trained on the site as the need arises, and in the winter they may be trained in modern techniques as part of Guédelon’s social remit.
sentences.zh: 他们随需要在工地上接受培训，到了冬天，作为盖德隆社会职责的一部分，他们还可能接受现代技术的培训。

sentences.en: (I) So, indeed, what will happen when Guédelon’s magical-looking castle is complete?
sentences.zh: 那么，当盖德隆这座看起来如梦似幻的城堡建成之后，究竟会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: They might build houses around it; perhaps villages may develop, testing out 13th-century agricultural techniques.
sentences.zh: 他们或许会在它周围建造房屋；也许会发展出村庄，来检验13世纪的农业技术。

sentences.en: If they can build this castle, anything seems possible.
sentences.zh: 如果他们能建成这座城堡，那么一切似乎都皆有可能。

records.title: Lawrence Johnston and Hidcote Garden V2
records.titleZh: 劳伦斯·约翰斯顿与希德科特花园V2

sentences.en: (A) Today, the National Trust in the UK administers hundreds of public gardens, but sixty-odd years ago there was only one: Hidcote Manor near the English village of Chipping Campden.
sentences.zh: 如今，英国国民信托管理着数百座公共花园，但六十多年前只有一座——位于英格兰村庄奇平卡姆登附近的希德科特庄园。

sentences.en: In 1949, Hidcote attracted a mere 600 visitors and took only £30 during its first public season.
sentences.zh: 1949年，希德科特仅吸引了600名游客，在它首个对公众开放的季节里只收入了30英镑。

sentences.en: Nowadays, Hidcote is famous worldwide as a masterpiece of design and planting, attracting 150,000 visitors and raising nearly £1 million annually from entrance tickets.
sentences.zh: 如今，希德科特作为设计与种植的杰作而闻名于世，每年吸引15万名游客，并通过门票收入近100万英镑。

sentences.en: (B) Hidcote Garden was the creation of an American in Britain, the shy Major Lawrence Johnston, who came to live on the site in 1907 with his widowed mother, Gertrude Winthrop.
sentences.zh: 希德科特花园是一位旅居英国的美国人——腼腆的劳伦斯·约翰斯顿少校的杰作，他于1907年与守寡的母亲格特鲁德·温思罗普一同搬到这片土地上居住。

sentences.en: In some respects, Winthrop feared her son's talents for expensive landscape gardening and never allowed him full access to the family's funds.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，温思罗普对儿子在昂贵的景观造园上的才能心怀忧虑，从未允许他完全动用家族的资金。

sentences.en: Nonetheless, with her inspiration and guidance, Johnston started his design in 1908 and brought it to a peak in the early 1930s when he was in his 60s.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，在她的启发与指引下，约翰斯顿于1908年开始了他的设计，并在20世纪30年代初他六十多岁时将其推向了巅峰。

sentences.en: At that time, Johnston may rightly be ranked beside Harold Nicolson and Vita Sackville-West, creators of Sissinghurst, his garden's only surviving equal.
sentences.zh: 在那个时候，约翰斯顿理应与西辛赫斯特的缔造者哈罗德·尼科尔森和维塔·萨克维尔-韦斯特相提并论，西辛赫斯特是与他的花园唯一存世的同等之作。

sentences.en: (C) In the last years of his life, Johnston placed faith in his head gardener Nancy Lindsay.
sentences.zh: 在生命的最后几年里，约翰斯顿把信任寄托在他的园艺主管南希·林赛身上。

sentences.en: Lindsay was undoubtedly a skilled plantswoman, but she had many other talents as well, including one for taking offence.
sentences.zh: 林赛无疑是一位技艺娴熟的植物专家，但她还有许多其他的本领，包括动辄生气这一点。

sentences.en: Johnston was ill-suited to dealing with her impassioned views.
sentences.zh: 约翰斯顿不善于应对她那些充满激情的看法。

sentences.en: When the National Trust subsequently acquired the garden from Johnston, none of his crucial garden diaries could be found, and some speculated that Lindsay had burned them to hurt her employer.
sentences.zh: 后来当国民信托从约翰斯顿手中接管这座花园时，他那些至关重要的园艺日记一本也找不到了，有人猜测是林赛烧毁了它们以伤害她的雇主。

sentences.en: Whatever their actual fate, Trust gardener Graham Thomas was tasked with reviving Hidcote.
sentences.zh: 无论它们的真实下落如何，信托的园艺师格雷厄姆·托马斯被委以复兴希德科特的任务。

sentences.en: Without these crucial documents, Thomas had to rely on his instincts.
sentences.zh: 在缺少这些关键文件的情况下，托马斯不得不依靠自己的直觉。

sentences.en: He knew that for the gardens to be a commercial success, he needed to extend areas of most interest to the general public, so he introduced new plants and a Mediterranean Bank where Johnston had planted nothing of the sort, while retaining the superb structure of avenues and evergreen rooms.
sentences.zh: 他知道，要让花园在商业上取得成功，就需要扩展最能引起公众兴趣的区域，于是他引入了新的植物，并开辟了一处地中海花圃——而约翰斯顿原本在那里并没有种植此类植物——同时保留了林荫道与常绿绿廊那卓越的结构。

sentences.en: As a result, since 1949, the visiting public has innocently been admiring Thomas's flower plantings, not Johnston's own.
sentences.zh: 结果是，自1949年以来，前来参观的公众一直在不知情地欣赏托马斯的花卉种植，而非约翰斯顿本人的种植。

sentences.en: When the important designer Russell Page visited Hidcote in 1934, he hailed the half-hardy plants in the summer house as one of the highlights.
sentences.zh: 当重要的设计师拉塞尔·佩奇于1934年到访希德科特时，他盛赞夏屋里那些半耐寒植物是亮点之一。

sentences.en: However, Thomas later removed these plants and pulled the house down, fearing that such relatively colourless exhibits would not capture the public's imagination.
sentences.zh: 然而，托马斯后来移除了这些植物并拆掉了那座房子，他担心这类相对缺乏色彩的展品无法激发公众的想象。

sentences.en: (D) Then, in 2002, Johnston's old diaries and notebooks resurfaced.
sentences.zh: 随后，在2002年，约翰斯顿昔日的日记和笔记本重见天日。

sentences.en: The present head gardener had started giving lectures about Hidcote's lost early designs, during which he appealed for memories from his audience.
sentences.zh: 当时的园艺主管开始就希德科特那些失传的早期设计举办讲座，期间他向听众征集相关的回忆。

sentences.en: A few months later, an envelope arrived.
sentences.zh: 几个月后，一个信封寄到了。

sentences.en: There was no letter inside, only Johnston's personal diaries from the 1920s and 30s.
sentences.zh: 里面没有信，只有约翰斯顿20世纪20年代和30年代的个人日记。

sentences.en: The sender remains unknown, but the importance of these documents to Hidcote is certain.
sentences.zh: 寄件人至今不明，但这些文件对希德科特的重要性是确定无疑的。

sentences.en: They contain invaluable notes regarding the selection of plants and, even better still, detailed sketches by Johnston himself showing how the different parts of the garden are related and how those relationships evolve over the seasons.
sentences.zh: 它们包含了关于植物选择的宝贵笔记，更妙的是，还有约翰斯顿亲手绘制的详细草图，展示了花园不同部分之间如何相互关联，以及这些关联如何随季节演变。

sentences.en: These documents are a rarity in other ways too, for they never dwell on the issues typically addressed in diaries—relationships, loves, and longings.
sentences.zh: 这些文件在其他方面也属罕见，因为它们从不纠缠于日记中通常会涉及的那些话题——人际关系、爱恋与渴望。

sentences.en: These are far more interesting, as they represent a classic social history of an English country house during the inter-war years.
sentences.zh: 这些内容要有趣得多，因为它们呈现了两次世界大战之间英国乡间宅邸的一段经典社会史。

sentences.en: (E) On page after page, Johnston describes the layout of the plants and gardens, interspersed with notes about that day's guests.
sentences.zh: 一页又一页，约翰斯顿描述着植物与花园的布局，其间穿插着关于那天宾客的记述。

sentences.en: The famous novelist Edith Wharton is recorded as coming for lunch, beside a recipe for poison to kill garden weeds.
sentences.zh: 著名小说家伊迪丝·华顿被记录前来共进午餐，旁边还有一份用来杀灭花园杂草的毒药配方。

sentences.en: It is this mix of glamour and the everyday that makes the diaries so fascinating.
sentences.zh: 正是这种魅力与日常的交融，使这些日记如此引人入胜。

sentences.en: At their heart, though, these are useful documents containing, for example, lengthy lists of those who might one day be of service around the estate, including local stonemasons and glaziers, or repairers of broken china from as far away as France.
sentences.zh: 不过，这些日记本质上是实用的文件，比如其中包含了长长的名单，列出日后可能为庄园效力的人——包括当地的石匠和玻璃工，乃至远至法国的破损瓷器修复匠。

sentences.en: (F) The discovery of the diaries has offered Hidcote a new direction for the years ahead.
sentences.zh: 这些日记的发现为希德科特未来的岁月指明了一个新方向。

sentences.en: Inspired by them, an anonymous American has donated £1.6 million to the gardens.
sentences.zh: 受这些日记的启发，一位匿名的美国人向花园捐赠了160万英镑。

sentences.en: This remarkable chance has been seized by the Trust to fund crucial repair work on paths and the famous pool, as well as the reconstruction of the old summer house.
sentences.zh: 信托抓住了这个难得的机会，用以资助对小径和那座著名水池的关键修缮工程，以及那座旧夏屋的重建。

sentences.en: However, the real implications of the discoveries made from the diaries are more challenging, as the Trust now possesses information about the very plants that most appealed to Johnston during the garden's golden years.
sentences.zh: 然而，从这些日记中获得的发现所带来的真正影响更具挑战性，因为信托如今掌握了关于约翰斯顿在花园黄金时期最钟爱的那些植物的信息。

sentences.en: Today, these may not be easy to source or appealing to contemporary tastes.
sentences.zh: 如今，这些植物可能不易获得，也不一定符合当代的审美趣味。

sentences.en: (G) ‘But isn’t it all so long ago?’
sentences.zh: “可这一切不都是很久以前的事了吗？”

sentences.en: a non-gardening academic recently asked me.
sentences.zh: 一位不懂园艺的学者最近这样问我。

sentences.en: On the contrary, Hidcote is still with us, a living legacy.
sentences.zh: 恰恰相反，希德科特依然与我们同在，是一份鲜活的遗产。

sentences.en: It includes the greatest central vista in British gardening, a design I regard as the greatest in British art in the past century.
sentences.zh: 它拥有英国园艺中最宏伟的中央景观轴线，我认为这一设计是过去一个世纪英国艺术中最伟大的作品。

sentences.en: It was the work of an American genius building an un-American garden of his own.
sentences.zh: 它是一位美国天才所创造的、一座非美国式的、属于他自己的花园。

sentences.en: I do not believe the fashionable guess that Johnston was informed by books on contemporary design by Britain’s Thomas Mawson, an altogether less innovative mind.
sentences.zh: 我不相信那个流行的猜测——即约翰斯顿受到了英国人托马斯·莫森关于当代设计著作的影响，莫森的头脑总体上远没有那么富有创新。

sentences.en: This is because so much in the garden reminds us how Johnston had travelled widely in Europe, which Mawson had not.
sentences.zh: 这是因为花园中的种种细节无不提醒我们，约翰斯顿曾广泛游历欧洲，而莫森并未如此。

sentences.en: Johnston’s own origins, the events of his life, and his individual design flair all contribute to making Hidcote so unique.
sentences.zh: 约翰斯顿自身的出身、他生平的种种经历，以及他个人独特的设计天赋，共同造就了希德科特的如此独一无二。

sentences.en: (A) The pioneering forecast on August 1, 1861, was introduced with a deceptively simple heading: ‘General weather probable during next two days.’
sentences.zh: 1861年8月1日这份开创性的天气预报以一个看似简单的标题登场：“未来两天大致的天气状况”。

sentences.en: But those few words started an ongoing controversy that still continues today - after all, everyone remembers the forecasts that go wrong, but rarely the ones that are right.
sentences.zh: 但正是这寥寥数语引发了一场延续至今的持续争论——毕竟人们总记得那些出错的预报，却很少记得那些准确的预报。

sentences.en: (B) The first forecast was the idea of Admiral Robert FitzRoy, head of the newly founded Meteorological Department, and one of Britain’s greatest but least-known heroes.
sentences.zh: 首份预报出自海军上将罗伯特·菲茨罗伊的构想。他是新成立的气象部门负责人，也是英国最伟大却最鲜为人知的英雄之一。

sentences.en: It was a brave undertaking, because in those days predicting the weather had gained a reputation similar to astrology or fortune-telling.
sentences.zh: 这是一项勇敢的尝试，因为在那个年代，预测天气已落得与占星术或算命相似的名声。

sentences.en: The few people who attempted it had become a national joke when their forecasts inevitably went wrong.
sentences.zh: 少数尝试此事的人在预报不可避免地出错时，都沦为了全国的笑柄。

sentences.en: (C) FitzRoy was different, though.
sentences.zh: 不过菲茨罗伊与众不同。

sentences.en: His background was faultless, most famously his captaining of the ship HMS Beagle on Charles Darwin’s voyage around the world, which eventually led to the publication of Darwin’s well-known book On the Origin of Species.
sentences.zh: 他的经历无可挑剔，其中最著名的是他曾指挥小猎犬号军舰载着查尔斯·达尔文进行环球航行，这次航行最终促成了达尔文名著《物种起源》的出版。

sentences.en: When FitzRoy retired from active service as an admiral in Britain’s navy, he was looking for a new direction.
sentences.zh: 当菲茨罗伊以海军上将身份从英国海军现役退役后，他正在寻找新的方向。

sentences.en: He subsequently secured a job as chief statistician at the Meteorological Department, part of the Board of Trade.
sentences.zh: 随后他谋得了气象部门首席统计师的职位，该部门隶属于贸易委员会。

sentences.en: Parliament had voted to set up and fund the Meteorological Department on June 30, 1854, to chart the safest sailing routes across the Atlantic Ocean.
sentences.zh: 议会曾于1854年6月30日投票决定设立并资助该气象部门，以规划横渡大西洋最安全的航线。

sentences.en: However, the British Government was not impressed with the idea of collecting weather reports and establishing a weather forecast, and the suggestion by one Member of Parliament for this was met with laughter from the other MPs.
sentences.zh: 然而英国政府对收集天气报告并建立天气预报的想法并不看好，一位议员为此提出的建议还招来了其他议员的哄笑。

sentences.en: (D) FitzRoy was given a staff of three clerks in a small office in London, but he soon grew bored with the tedium of transcribing thousands of ships’ reports.
sentences.zh: 菲茨罗伊在伦敦一间小办公室里配有三名文员，但他很快就厌倦了誊抄成千上万份船只报告的枯燥工作。

sentences.en: Instead, he focused on a much more pressing issue - the huge loss of life at sea from storms.
sentences.zh: 相反，他把精力投向一个更为紧迫的问题——风暴造成的海上重大人员伤亡。

sentences.en: This problem came to a head in 1859, when gale-force winds sank the ship named Royal Charter, with the loss of 430 lives, within sight of the shore.
sentences.zh: 这个问题在1859年到达顶点，当时狂风把名为皇家宪章号的船只掀沉，430人在岸边可见之处丧生。

sentences.en: Even in those days when ships regularly sank in storms, the loss of the Royal Charter was considered a national tragedy.
sentences.zh: 即便在那个船只常在风暴中沉没的年代，皇家宪章号的失事也被视为一场全国性的悲剧。

sentences.en: FitzRoy stirred up feelings even further when he wrote a letter to The Times newspaper explaining that the storm had been entirely predictable.
sentences.zh: 菲茨罗伊给《泰晤士报》写了一封信，说明那场风暴本来完全可以预测，这更进一步激起了公众的情绪。

sentences.en: (E) That same year, a total of 1,645 lives were lost off the British coast, and FitzRoy wrote repeatedly to The Times pushing for a storm-warning service for shipping.
sentences.zh: 同年在英国沿海共有1645人遇难，菲茨罗伊多次致信《泰晤士报》，力促为航运设立风暴预警服务。

sentences.en: This was just the right moment for a national forecasting service.
sentences.zh: 这正是设立全国性预报服务的绝佳时机。

sentences.en: Knowledge of the weather was improving, barometer readings gave warning of approaching storms, and the invention of the electric telegraph and Morse code in 1844 gave instant communication for the first time.
sentences.zh: 人们对天气的认识在不断加深，气压计的读数能对逼近的风暴发出预警，而1844年电报和摩尔斯电码的发明首次实现了即时通信。

sentences.en: (F) So in February 1861, FitzRoy pressed ahead with a storm-warning service.
sentences.zh: 于是在1861年2月，菲茨罗伊着手推进风暴预警服务。

sentences.en: Previously, weather reports had been unreliable, but FitzRoy’s innovation was to issue ships with standardised instruments which allowed for accurate weather reports.
sentences.zh: 此前天气报告一直不可靠，而菲茨罗伊的创新在于为船只配发标准化仪器，从而能够得到准确的天气报告。

sentences.en: At exactly the same time each day the information was sent to him by telegraph, and he was able to draw up more detailed weather maps.
sentences.zh: 每天在完全相同的时刻，这些信息通过电报发送给他，他便能绘制出更为详尽的天气图。

sentences.en: The approach of an incoming storm could be recognised, and from London, FitzRoy could telegraph warnings to ports on the coast, where an ingenious system of flags was hoisted up high for passing ships to read.
sentences.zh: 逼近的风暴能够被识别出来，菲茨罗伊在伦敦就能把警报电传到沿海各港口，那里会用一套巧妙的旗语系统把旗帜高高升起，供过往船只辨读。

sentences.en: This represented the biggest advance in shipping safety after the introduction of the lifeboat, and in subsequent years the number of lives lost around Britain fell by about a third.
sentences.zh: 这是继救生艇问世之后航运安全领域最大的进步，在随后几年里，英国周边海域的遇难人数下降了约三分之一。

sentences.en: FitzRoy became a hero to the fishing and maritime fleets.
sentences.zh: 菲茨罗伊成了渔业和海运船队心目中的英雄。

sentences.en: (G) Encouraged by his storm-warning success, FitzRoy then started a public weather forecasting service.
sentences.zh: 受风暴预警成功的鼓舞，菲茨罗伊随后开办了面向公众的天气预报服务。

sentences.en: As he had a close connection with The Times, this newspaper introduced his daily forecast in August 1861.
sentences.zh: 由于他与《泰晤士报》关系密切，这家报纸于1861年8月刊出了他的每日预报。

sentences.en: It attracted huge attention, including from Queen Victoria, who regularly sent messengers to FitzRoy’s office to get a forecast for the sea crossing over the Solent to an island which she liked to visit off the south coast of England.
sentences.zh: 它吸引了极大的关注，其中包括维多利亚女王。她常派信使到菲茨罗伊的办公室，为横渡索伦特海峡前往她喜欢造访的英格兰南岸一座岛屿获取天气预报。

sentences.en: He was also popular with ordinary fishermen, who were happy not to be out at sea in bad weather.
sentences.zh: 他在普通渔民中也很受欢迎，他们乐得在恶劣天气里不必出海。

sentences.en: The owners of fishing vessels, however, were not supportive of FitzRoy’s forecasts, which often caused delays for them when bad weather was forecast.
sentences.zh: 然而渔船船主并不支持菲茨罗伊的预报，因为一旦预报出恶劣天气，往往会给他们造成延误。

sentences.en: (H) Nevertheless, weather forecasting at that time was very difficult, and one mistake could result in much bad publicity.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，当时的天气预报非常困难，一次失误就可能招致大量负面舆论。

sentences.en: It wasn’t long before some forecasts turned out wrong, and the letters pages of The Times were full of heated correspondence.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，一些预报就被证明是错误的，《泰晤士报》的读者来信版面上满是言辞激烈的争论。

sentences.en: It is indisputable that FitzRoy was way ahead of his time, but it is only in recent years that he has been recognised as a towering figure in meteorology, with the honour of an area of sea being given his name in the shipping forecast (a radio broadcast of weather reports for the seas around Britain).
sentences.zh: 菲茨罗伊远远超越了他所处的时代，这一点毋庸置疑，但直到近些年他才被公认为气象学界的巨擘，并获此殊荣——航运预报中的一片海域以他的名字命名（航运预报是针对英国周边海域天气报告的广播）。

sentences.en: His extraordinary determination to get forecasting established cost him dearly though, and he died prematurely.
sentences.zh: 不过他为确立天气预报所付出的非凡决心让他付出了沉重代价，他英年早逝。

sentences.en: But his legacy lives on, because late in his life he published a book about weather forecasting which was recognised by other scientists to be well ahead of its time.
sentences.zh: 但他的遗产得以延续，因为在晚年他出版了一本关于天气预报的著作，被其他科学家公认远远领先于时代。

sentences.en: A It was difficult to get about in eighteenth-century London.
sentences.zh: 在十八世纪的伦敦出行十分困难。

sentences.en: During the first half of that century, the physical mobility of the upper classes in the city had been considerably restricted: the poor condition of the streets did not allow ‘walking for pleasure’ outside private parks or pleasure gardens.
sentences.zh: 在那个世纪的前半叶，城中上层阶级的出行活动受到相当大的限制：糟糕的街道状况使人们无法在私家园林或游乐花园之外“悠闲散步”。

sentences.en: Streets were dirty, rubbish was everywhere and the British climate did not help.
sentences.zh: 街道肮脏，垃圾遍地，英国的气候也帮不上忙。

sentences.en: Walking could be a risky business.
sentences.zh: 步行可能是一件冒险的事。

sentences.en: The terrible state of roads, always flooded and muddy, created a metropolitan world of shoe cleaners and street sweepers.
sentences.zh: 道路状况糟糕，总是积水泥泞，由此在这座大都市里催生出一大批擦鞋匠和清道夫。

sentences.en: B References to walking are not abundant in early eighteenth-century texts.
sentences.zh: 在十八世纪早期的文献中，关于步行的记述并不多见。

sentences.en: This is truer for urban spaces than for places in the countryside, where country life had always been dominated by a lifestyle of outdoor activities.
sentences.zh: 相比乡村，这一点在城市空间里更为明显，因为乡村生活历来以户外活动的方式为主导。

sentences.en: For instance, in eighteenth-century London, a sightseer’s experience was restricted to touristic places and involved journeys by a series of boats and coaches.
sentences.zh: 例如在十八世纪的伦敦，观光者的游览仅限于旅游景点，而且要靠一连串的船只和马车代步。

sentences.en: Walking was considered to be an activity for the poorer members of society — or simply those who could not afford a coach.
sentences.zh: 步行被视为社会中较贫穷者的活动——或者干脆说是那些坐不起马车的人的活动。

sentences.en: C This situation underwent a sudden improvement in the mid-eighteenth century, with measures implementing the provision of public spaces in which to walk.
sentences.zh: 到了十八世纪中叶，随着一系列提供公共步行空间的举措出台，这种状况骤然改善。

sentences.en: The first legislation concerning paving in London was passed in 1762, and during the following decades similar laws were enacted in many cities.
sentences.zh: 伦敦第一部关于铺设路面的立法于1762年通过，在随后的数十年里许多城市也颁布了类似法律。

sentences.en: By the end of the century, areas for walking were commonplace, and far more people were enjoying the pastime than before.
sentences.zh: 到那个世纪末，供人步行的场所已随处可见，享受这一消遣的人比以往多了许多。

sentences.en: Sophie von La Roche writes about metropolitan street life in the diary of her visit to London of 1786.
sentences.zh: 索菲·冯·拉罗什在她1786年访问伦敦的日记中描写了这座大都市的街头生活。

sentences.en: She comments on how many more pedestrians there were on the broad, clean pavements, alongside the houses where, she says ‘many thousands of neatly clad people, eminent men and dressy women, pursue their way safe from the carriages, horses and dirt’.
sentences.zh: 她评述道，在房屋旁那些宽阔洁净的人行道上，行人比过去多了许多，用她的话说“成千上万衣着整洁的人、显赫的男士和盛装的女士，安然前行，远离马车、马匹和污泥”。

sentences.en: Although the pastime of walking was pursued only in specific spaces designed for the purpose, the number of these spaces increased as the nineteenth century approached.
sentences.zh: 尽管步行这一消遣只能在为此专门设计的特定场所进行，但随着十九世纪临近，这类场所的数量不断增加。

sentences.en: Travelling on foot became smoother and less dangerous.
sentences.zh: 徒步出行变得更顺畅，也更安全。

sentences.en: D Attitudes toward walking through public spaces and their changes over time were visible in the practical designs of fashionable footwear.
sentences.zh: 人们对穿行于公共空间步行的态度及其随时间的变化，在时髦鞋履的实用设计上清晰可见。

sentences.en: Protective overshoes and other devices designed to keep feet above the dirty and wet ground soon disappeared, and ease of mobility increased.
sentences.zh: 那些用来让双脚不沾污湿地面的护套鞋及其他装置很快消失，出行也变得更加便利。

sentences.en: In the early eighteenth century, the look of men’s and women’s shoes started to diverge in appearance as a distinction between male and female footwear filtered into production.
sentences.zh: 在十八世纪早期，随着男女鞋履之间的区分逐渐渗入制作环节，男鞋和女鞋的外观开始出现差异。

sentences.en: Contemporary descriptions of the boot and shoe trade underlined the differences between ladies’ shoemakers and men’s shoemakers too.
sentences.zh: 当时对靴鞋行业的描述也着重指出了女鞋匠与男鞋匠之间的区别。

sentences.en: E The production of men’s and women’s footwear required different skills, as the products were essentially different.
sentences.zh: 制作男鞋和女鞋需要不同的技艺，因为二者的产品本质上就不相同。

sentences.en: Men wore more sober footwear, not unlike modern shoes.
sentences.zh: 男士穿的鞋更为素净，与现代的鞋子颇为相似。

sentences.en: Their shoes were entirely made of leather, which provided resistance to rain, mud and bad weather.
sentences.zh: 他们的鞋全部用皮革制成，能够抵御雨水、泥泞和恶劣天气。

sentences.en: Women’s shoes had uppers made of textiles — silk, satin or cloth — and their resistance to bad weather and dirty streets was limited.
sentences.zh: 女鞋的鞋面用纺织品制成——丝绸、缎子或布料——因而抵御恶劣天气和肮脏街道的能力有限。

sentences.en: Only the lower ranks of women wore leather shoes of a form similar to men’s.
sentences.zh: 只有社会地位较低的女性才穿样式与男鞋相似的皮鞋。

sentences.en: The high-quality shoes for women were often embroidered and were normally worn with protective overshoes, as they were prone to being damaged or disfigured by the conditions of the time.
sentences.zh: 供女性穿着的高档鞋常绣有花纹，通常要配上护套鞋一起穿，因为它们很容易被当时的环境损坏或弄花外观。

sentences.en: F The shoes of men and women related to their more general clothing in different ways.
sentences.zh: 男鞋和女鞋与各自的整体着装以不同的方式相互呼应。

sentences.en: Wealthy women’s footwear harmonised with their other garments, a harmony that could be effected through matching textiles, general colour, embroidered detail or buckles.
sentences.zh: 富裕女性的鞋履与其他衣物相协调，这种协调可以通过相配的面料、整体色调、刺绣细节或鞋扣来实现。

sentences.en: In the eighteenth century, men’s shoes matched their clothing in different ways, for example with glossy black, red or pink heels.
sentences.zh: 在十八世纪，男鞋以不同的方式与服装相配，例如配上光亮的黑色、红色或粉色鞋跟。

sentences.en: The shoe of an upper-class man also acted as a type of sign which emphasised the difference between the wearer and young boys and women.
sentences.zh: 上层男士的鞋还充当一种标志，凸显穿着者与男孩及女性之间的区别。

sentences.en: The shoe also distinguished him from working men who wore leather or cloth protective leggings, ragged shoes and clogs.
sentences.zh: 这种鞋也将他与劳动者区分开来，后者穿的是皮制或布制的护腿、破旧的鞋子和木屐。

sentences.en: The symbolic marking of the entry of a wealthy young man into manhood through his shoes, as well as his other dress, may have been of more importance than has previously been acknowledged in costume history.
sentences.zh: 富家青年通过鞋子以及其他服饰象征性地标示自己步入成年，这一点的重要性也许比服饰史以往所承认的更为突出。
