records.title: A River Reveals Its Roman Past
records.titleZh: 一条河流揭示了其罗马历史

sentences.en: (A) 2,000 years ago, the town of Arles, in what is now south-western France, was a busy gateway to the area of the Roman Empire known as Gaul.
sentences.zh: 2000年前，位于今天法国西南部的阿尔勒镇，是通往罗马帝国境内那片被称为高卢地区的一处繁忙门户。

sentences.en: Goods from all over the Mediterranean were transferred there to barges – long, shallow riverboats – then pulled up the Rhône river to supply the northern half of the great empire.
sentences.zh: 来自地中海各地的货物在那里被转载到驳船上——那是一种狭长而吃水浅的内河船——然后被拖曳着沿罗讷河北上，供应这个庞大帝国的北半部。

sentences.en: Today, Arles is a small, quiet place, and the Rhône is polluted and mostly ignored.
sentences.zh: 如今的阿尔勒是一处安静的小地方，罗讷河则受到污染，大多被人忽视。

sentences.en: (B) Archaeologist Luc Long is a native of Arles.
sentences.zh: 考古学家吕克·隆是土生土长的阿尔勒人。

sentences.en: He had already worked on sunken ships all over the Mediterranean when, in 1986, a friend persuaded him to dive for the first time in his home river.
sentences.zh: 他此前已在地中海各处研究过沉船，直到1986年，一位朋友说服他第一次潜入自己家乡的这条河。

sentences.en: Long reluctantly agreed.
sentences.zh: 隆勉强答应了。

sentences.en: The two men entered the river on a chilly November morning, when the water was around 8°C, thick, cloudy and foul-smelling.
sentences.zh: 两人在11月一个寒冷的早晨下了河，当时水温约8摄氏度，水体浑浊黏稠、气味难闻。

sentences.en: They could see no more than a metre ahead through the murky water.
sentences.zh: 在浑浊的水中，他们向前最多只能看到一米远。

sentences.en: At a depth of about six metres, Long saw a sunken truck.
sentences.zh: 在大约六米深处，隆看到了一辆沉没的卡车。

sentences.en: To his surprise, he discovered an ancient Roman jar – known as an amphora – on the driver’s seat.
sentences.zh: 令他惊讶的是，他在驾驶座上发现了一只古罗马陶罐——也就是所谓的双耳瓶。

sentences.en: These containers were used throughout the Roman Empire to transport olive oil, fish sauce, and other products.
sentences.zh: 这类容器在整个罗马帝国被用来运输橄榄油、鱼露以及其他物品。

sentences.en: When empty, they would simply be discarded.
sentences.zh: 一旦空了，它们就会被随手丢弃。

sentences.en: Within a short time the divers found themselves swimming over a vast field of amphorae.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，两位潜水者就发现自己正游过一大片双耳瓶堆积的区域。

sentences.en: Long had never seen so many intact ones, and he has been mapping this Roman rubbish dump ever since.
sentences.zh: 隆从未见过如此之多完好无损的双耳瓶，此后他便一直在为这处罗马垃圾场绘制分布图。

sentences.en: (C) For the first 20 years or so, no one paid much attention to what Long was doing.
sentences.zh: 在最初的20年左右，几乎没有人关注隆正在做的事。

sentences.en: When, in 2004, one of his colleagues came across a 34-metre-long Roman barge, Long doubted that there would ever be enough money available to raise it.
sentences.zh: 2004年，当他的一位同事偶然发现一艘34米长的罗马驳船时，隆怀疑是否会有足够的资金把它打捞上来。

sentences.en: In 2007, Long handed over the study of this wreck – which he named Arles-Rhône 3 – to three younger archaeologists, and continued his survey of the rest of the dump, around 50 metres upstream.
sentences.zh: 2007年，隆把这艘沉船的研究工作交给了三位更年轻的考古学家——他为这艘船取名为阿尔勒-罗讷3号——自己则继续勘察上游约50米处那片垃圾场的其余部分。

sentences.en: This was where he started finding pieces of the Roman town of Arles, including statues.
sentences.zh: 正是在那里，他开始发现罗马时期阿尔勒城的遗物，其中包括一些雕像。

sentences.en: Word began to leak out.
sentences.zh: 消息开始走漏。

sentences.en: The French customs police warned Long that antiquities thieves might be watching his operation.
sentences.zh: 法国海关警察警告隆，文物窃贼可能正盯着他的作业。

sentences.en: So when his divers found a two-metre statue of the god Neptune, they brought it to the surface at night.
sentences.zh: 因此，当他的潜水员发现一尊两米高的海神尼普顿雕像时，他们选择在夜间将其打捞出水。

sentences.en: (D) Before the diving season was over, divers had discovered a rare marble bust of the Roman emperor Julius Caesar.
sentences.zh: 还没等潜水季结束，潜水员们又发现了一尊罕见的罗马皇帝尤利乌斯·凯撒大理石半身像。

sentences.en: An exhibition was built around the statue, and news of it spread around the world.
sentences.zh: 围绕这尊雕像举办了一场展览，相关消息传遍了世界各地。

sentences.en: ‘The exhibition’s success was astonishing,’ said Claude Sintes, director of Arles’ local antiquities museum, where the exhibition was held.
sentences.zh: “这场展览的成功令人惊叹。”阿尔勒当地文物博物馆馆长克洛德·桑特斯说，展览正是在该馆举办的。

sentences.en: ‘When a modest town like ours gets 400,000 visitors, the politicians understood that the economic return was strong.’
sentences.zh: “当我们这样一个不起眼的小镇迎来40万名游客时，政界人士就明白其经济回报是相当可观的。”

sentences.en: By the autumn of 2010, the Caesar exhibition was nearing its end, and some politicians were looking for more culture to invest in, because the European Union had designated the region around Arles a 2013 European Capital of Culture.
sentences.zh: 到2010年秋天，凯撒展览已接近尾声，一些政界人士正在寻找更多可供投资的文化项目，因为欧盟已将阿尔勒周边地区定为2013年欧洲文化之都。

sentences.en: Suddenly nine million euros became available to build a new wing on the museum and put a Roman barge into it.
sentences.zh: 忽然之间，900万欧元的资金到位，用于为博物馆增建一处新侧翼，并把一艘罗马驳船安置其中。

sentences.en: There was just one small problem.
sentences.zh: 只是有一个小问题。

sentences.en: The project would need to be completed by 2013.
sentences.zh: 这个项目必须在2013年之前完成。

sentences.en: That meant the barge needed to be extracted by the end of the diving season in 2011.
sentences.zh: 这意味着必须在2011年潜水季结束前把这艘驳船打捞出来。

sentences.en: This was because although the wood of the boat had suffered no microbial decay, water had filled its cells, leaving the whole structure soft and spongy.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，尽管船体木材没有遭受微生物腐蚀，水却已充满其细胞，使整个结构变得松软而多孔。

sentences.en: If that were to evaporate, the boat would collapse.
sentences.zh: 一旦这些水分蒸发，船体就会垮塌。

sentences.en: The solution was to bathe the wood for months in a polymer called polyethylene glycol, then freeze-dry it in small sections – gradually infusing it with the polymer before extracting the water.
sentences.zh: 解决办法是把木材在一种名为聚乙二醇的聚合物中浸泡数月，然后分成小段进行冷冻干燥——先让聚合物逐渐渗入木材，再把其中的水分抽走。

sentences.en: The process would take nearly two years.
sentences.zh: 这一过程将耗时近两年。

sentences.en: (E) So there was only one diving season to extract the boat from the Rhône.
sentences.zh: 因此，把这艘船从罗讷河中打捞上来只剩下一个潜水季的时间。

sentences.en: ‘We thought the project was doomed to fail,’ said Benoît Poinard, a professional diver and the site foreman.
sentences.zh: “我们原以为这个项目注定要失败。”职业潜水员、现场工头伯努瓦·普瓦纳尔说。

sentences.en: Normally, Poinard explained, the Rhône is safe for diving only from late June to October; otherwise the current is too strong.
sentences.zh: 普瓦纳尔解释说，通常情况下，罗讷河只有从6月下旬到10月才适合安全潜水，其余时候水流太急。

sentences.en: Only three or four months would not be enough to excavate Arles-Rhône 3.
sentences.zh: 仅有三四个月的时间，不足以完成对阿尔勒-罗讷3号的发掘。

sentences.en: Then 2011 arrived.
sentences.zh: 然后2011年到来了。

sentences.en: It hardly snowed in the Alps that winter and that spring it barely rained.
sentences.zh: 那年冬天阿尔卑斯山几乎没有下雪，那个春天也几乎没有下雨。

sentences.en: The Rhône’s current was so gentle that the team got in the water by early May.
sentences.zh: 罗讷河的水流如此平缓，以至于团队在5月初就下了水。

sentences.en: The team worked straight into November, losing only a single week to bad weather – and completed the job.
sentences.zh: 团队一直工作到11月，仅因恶劣天气损失了一周时间——并且完成了这项工作。

sentences.en: ‘Two hours after we finished,’ Poinard said, ‘the Rhône became undiveable for the whole winter.’
sentences.zh: “我们完工两小时之后，”普瓦纳尔说，“罗讷河整个冬天就再也无法下潜了。”

sentences.en: (F) When Arles-Rhône 3 sank, it was carrying 33 tons of stone for building work.
sentences.zh: 阿尔勒-罗讷3号沉没时，船上载着33吨用于建筑工程的石料。

sentences.en: It had come from a quarry just north of Arles, and was probably heading towards a construction site further down the river.
sentences.zh: 这些石料来自阿尔勒以北不远处的一座采石场，很可能正被运往河流下游更远处的一个建筑工地。

sentences.en: The boat was pointed upstream, though, rather than downstream, indicating it had been moored at the quay when it sank.
sentences.zh: 不过这艘船的船头朝向上游而非下游，这表明它沉没时正停泊在码头边。

sentences.en: A flash flood had probably swamped it.
sentences.zh: 很可能是一场突发的洪水将它淹没。

sentences.en: As soon as the flood subsided, the barge would have been covered in a coating of fine clay no more than 20 cm thick.
sentences.zh: 洪水一退去，这艘驳船就会被一层厚度不超过20厘米的细黏土所覆盖。

sentences.en: This was where the archaeologists discovered the personal effects that the crew had left on the boat, including cooking utensils and plates.
sentences.zh: 正是在这里，考古学家发现了船员留在船上的私人物品，其中包括炊具和盘子。

sentences.en: When the restorers were taking the boat apart, they also found a silver coin sealed between two planks of wood; it had been put there to bring good luck.
sentences.zh: 修复人员在拆解这艘船时，还在两块木板之间发现了一枚被封存其中的银币，那是为求好运而放置的。

sentences.en: And it did – 2,000 years later.
sentences.zh: 而它确实带来了好运——在2000年之后。

sentences.en: Arles-Rhône 3 was able to take its place in the new wing of the museum, on schedule, just over two years after re-emerging from the cloudy depths of the Rhône.
sentences.zh: 阿尔勒-罗讷3号得以按期在博物馆的新侧翼中占据一席之地，此时距它从罗讷河浑浊的深处重见天日仅过去两年多。

sentences.en: (A) The Examinations School at Oxford University is where, last August, 34 contestants gathered at the World Memory Championships.
sentences.zh: 去年八月，34名参赛者聚集在牛津大学考试院参加世界记忆锦标赛。

sentences.en: It is an impressive historical venue, known for its austere yet grandiose setting of oak-paneled rooms, large Gothic windows, and looming portraits of eminent dukes and earls.
sentences.zh: 这是一处令人印象深刻的历史场所，以其朴素而宏伟的布置著称：橡木镶板的房间、巨大的哥特式窗户，以及一幅幅居高临下的公爵与伯爵画像。

sentences.en: It is here that generations of Oxford students have been tested in their final exams on their memory and knowledge, and it is here that these contestants were challenged to demonstrate their exceptional mnemonic abilities.
sentences.zh: 正是在这里，一代代牛津学生在期末考试中接受记忆与学识的检验，也正是在这里，这些参赛者被要求展示自己非凡的记忆本领。

sentences.en: Reciting poems, memorizing digit sequences, and recalling faces from photographs are just a few of the tasks that test the limits of human memory in this competitive setting.
sentences.zh: 背诵诗歌、记忆数字序列、从照片中辨认面孔，这些只是在这一竞技场合中考验人类记忆极限的部分项目。

sentences.en: (B) They are using a technique known as the loci method, reportedly originating in 477 BC with the Greek poet Simonides of Ceos.
sentences.zh: 他们使用的是一种被称为位置记忆法的技巧，据说源自公元前477年的希腊诗人凯奥斯的西蒙尼德斯。

sentences.en: He was able to memorize the guest list at a dinner by closing his eyes and recalling each individual around the table.
sentences.zh: 他能够闭上眼睛、回想餐桌旁的每一个人，从而记住一场晚宴的宾客名单。

sentences.en: The loci method, which was rediscovered and popularized by Simonides, has become an integral part of historical and modern memory training.
sentences.zh: 位置记忆法经由西蒙尼德斯重新发现并推广，已成为古今记忆训练不可或缺的一部分。

sentences.en: This method involves associating items to be remembered with specific physical locations, creating a mental map that facilitates recall.
sentences.zh: 这种方法是把需要记住的事物与特定的实际地点联系起来，构建一幅有助于回忆的心理地图。

sentences.en: After Simonides's discovery, the loci method became widely embraced across ancient Greece, serving as a fundamental technique for orators and scholars.
sentences.zh: 在西蒙尼德斯的发现之后，位置记忆法在古希腊被广泛采用，成为演说家和学者的一项基本技巧。

sentences.en: It was so effective that it was incorporated into educational curricula and became a cornerstone of rhetorical training.
sentences.zh: 它效果极佳，以至于被纳入教育课程，并成为修辞训练的基石。

sentences.en: Aristotle wrote favorably about it, recognizing its value and effectiveness.
sentences.zh: 亚里士多德对此给予了肯定，认可其价值与成效。

sentences.en: Later, a number of treatises on the art of memory were published in Rome, further cementing its importance and utility in memory training.
sentences.zh: 后来，罗马出版了多部关于记忆术的论著，进一步巩固了它在记忆训练中的重要性与实用性。

sentences.en: This method not only aids in memorization but also enhances the ability to retrieve information by navigating through these mental loci, effectively walking through a structured memory palace.
sentences.zh: 这种方法不仅有助于记忆，还能通过在这些心理位置之间穿行来增强信息提取能力，实际上就是走过一座结构化的记忆宫殿。

sentences.en: (C) One memory champion, Ed Cooke, can memorize the order of ten decks of playing cards in less than one hour or one deck of cards in less than one minute.
sentences.zh: 记忆冠军埃德·库克能在不到一小时内记住10副扑克牌的顺序，或在不到一分钟内记住一副牌。

sentences.en: Psychologists Elizabeth Valentine and John Wilding have teamed up with Eleanor Maguire to study how memory champions like Cooke operate differently from average individuals.
sentences.zh: 心理学家伊丽莎白·瓦伦丁和约翰·怀尔丁与埃莉诺·马奎尔展开合作，研究像库克这样的记忆冠军与普通人在运作方式上有何不同。

sentences.en: Their collaboration aims to explore the neural underpinnings that might explain the exceptional memory skills exhibited by competitors in high-pressure environments such as memory championships.
sentences.zh: 他们的合作旨在探究其神经基础，以解释参赛者在记忆锦标赛这类高压环境中所展现的超凡记忆能力。

sentences.en: When the researchers analyzed the brain scans from the number memorization, they found that the memory champions were activating some brain regions that were different from those the control subjects were using.
sentences.zh: 研究人员分析数字记忆环节的脑部扫描时发现，记忆冠军激活的某些脑区与对照受试者所用的脑区并不相同。

sentences.en: These regions are known to be involved in visual memory and spatial navigation.
sentences.zh: 已知这些区域参与视觉记忆和空间导航。

sentences.en: (D) To enable himself to memorize quickly, Ed Cooke has memorized a specific human being, verb, and object that he associates with every card in the deck.
sentences.zh: 为了让自己能够快速记忆，埃德·库克为牌堆中的每一张牌都记下了与之关联的特定人物、动作和物品。

sentences.en: This detailed and highly personalized system allows him to rapidly encode and decode information during competitions.
sentences.zh: 这套细致而高度个人化的系统使他能在比赛中迅速编码和解码信息。

sentences.en: When Cooke commits a deck to memory, he does it three cards in one go, with every three-card group forming a composite picture of a person doing something to an object.
sentences.zh: 库克记忆一副牌时是三张一组进行的，每三张牌构成一幅某人对某物做某事的合成画面。

sentences.en: This method not only enhances the memorization process but also makes the recall process faster and more efficient.
sentences.zh: 这种方法不仅提升了记忆过程，也让回忆过程更快、更高效。

sentences.en: He then places those images along a specific familiar path in his mind, creating a vivid mental journey that he can easily traverse.
sentences.zh: 随后他把这些画面安放在心中一条特定的熟悉路径上，构建出一段可以轻松走完的生动心理旅程。

sentences.en: When it comes to recall, Cooke takes a mental walk along his route and translates the images into cards, effectively and efficiently converting his vivid mental images back into the specific order of the deck.
sentences.zh: 到了回忆的时候，库克会沿着自己的路线在心中走一遍，把画面转换回牌，从而高效而准确地还原出这副牌的具体顺序。

sentences.en: This innovative approach to memory exercises showcases the extraordinary capabilities of mental athletes and the sophisticated strategies they employ to achieve their remarkable feats.
sentences.zh: 这种创新的记忆训练方式，展现出心智运动员的非凡能力，以及他们为取得惊人成绩所采用的精巧策略。

sentences.en: (E) The term ‘photographic memory’ is frequently used to describe people with exceptional recall.
sentences.zh: “照相式记忆”这一说法常被用来形容那些记忆力超群的人。

sentences.en: Yet, most researchers agree there is no proof that such a memory truly exists.
sentences.zh: 然而，大多数研究者一致认为，没有证据表明这种记忆真的存在。

sentences.en: If it is indeed a myth, it highlights how learned strategies are often more effective than natural talent.
sentences.zh: 如果它确实只是一个神话，那就凸显出习得的策略往往比天赋更为有效。

sentences.en: The belief in ‘photographic memory’ remains a point of contention among the public and scientists alike.
sentences.zh: 对“照相式记忆”的信念在公众和科学家之间始终存在争议。

sentences.en: Despite the absence of solid scientific evidence, this myth endures, reflecting how society’s fascination with remarkable memory tends to ignore the practical techniques and training that genuinely drive mnemonic success.
sentences.zh: 尽管缺乏确凿的科学证据，这一说法仍然经久不衰，反映出社会对惊人记忆力的痴迷往往忽视了真正带来记忆成就的实用技巧与训练。

sentences.en: (F) The most renowned of the naturals was the Russian journalist S.V.
sentences.zh: 天赋型记忆者中最负盛名的是俄罗斯记者S.V.

sentences.en: Shereshevski, who could remember long sequences of numbers learned decades before, as well as poems, strings of meaningless syllables, and nearly anything else he was asked to recall.
sentences.zh: 舍列舍夫斯基，他能够记住几十年前学过的长串数字，还能记住诗歌、无意义音节串，以及几乎任何被要求回忆的内容。

sentences.en: Shereshevski also experienced synaesthesia, a rare sensory condition where the senses are interconnected, which significantly improved his memorization ability.
sentences.zh: 舍列舍夫斯基还患有联觉，这是一种各种感官相互连通的罕见感觉状况，大大提升了他的记忆能力。

sentences.en: His skills were not limited to these accomplishments; his remarkable memory covered an almost endless range of information, making him a figure of great interest and study.
sentences.zh: 他的本领不止于此，他惊人的记忆几乎涵盖了无穷无尽的信息门类，使他成为备受关注和研究的人物。

sentences.en: This synthetic trait not only made his memorization tasks easier but also more vivid and long-lasting.
sentences.zh: 这种综合性特质不仅让他的记忆任务更轻松，也让记忆更加生动、更为持久。

sentences.en: His case has been extensively examined, as it offers deep insights into the potential of human memory when enhanced by neurological variations.
sentences.zh: 他的案例已被广泛研究，因为它为人类记忆在神经差异加持下的潜能提供了深刻洞见。

sentences.en: (G) K.
sentences.zh: K.

sentences.en: Anders Ericsson, a well-known psychologist, claims that anyone can develop memory abilities comparable to those of memory champions through consistent practice and proper techniques.
sentences.zh: 安德斯·埃里克森，一位知名心理学家，声称任何人都能通过持续练习和恰当技巧，发展出可与记忆冠军相媲美的记忆能力。

sentences.en: During two years of experimentation, S.V. increased his ability to recall numbers from seven to over eighty.
sentences.zh: 在为期两年的实验中，S.V.把回忆数字的能力从7个提高到了80多个。

sentences.en: This study led Ericsson to conclude that there is no such thing as an innately superior memory.
sentences.zh: 这项研究使埃里克森得出结论：不存在天生更优越的记忆。

sentences.en: When he revisited original case reports of natural memorizers, he discovered that their remarkable abilities were actually based on the use of specific techniques — sometimes unconsciously — combined with extensive practice.
sentences.zh: 当他重新审视天赋型记忆者的原始个案报告时，发现他们惊人的能力实际上是基于对特定技巧的运用——有时是无意识的——再加上大量练习。

sentences.en: Strategists are usually outstanding at remembering only certain kinds of material, whereas naturals exhibit strong memory across many types of tasks and can retain those memories more easily.
sentences.zh: 策略型记忆者通常只在记忆某些类型的材料上表现出色，而天赋型记忆者则在多种任务上都展现出很强的记忆力，并且更容易保持这些记忆。

records.title: The Role Of Mothers In The Origins Of Music
records.titleZh: 母亲在音乐起源中的作用

sentences.en: A In a recent lecture Richard Parncutt, a professor of systematic musicology at the University of Graz, Austria, discussed the idea that music originated from ‘motherese’ - the playful voices mothers adopt when speaking to infants and toddlers.
sentences.zh: 在最近的一次讲座中，奥地利格拉茨大学系统音乐学教授理查德·帕恩卡特探讨了这样一个想法：音乐起源于“妈妈语”——母亲对婴幼儿说话时所采用的那种嬉戏语调。

sentences.en: According to the theory, evolutionary growth in human brain size between one and two million years ago led to earlier births, more fragile infants, and a vital need for stronger bonds between mothers and their newborns.
sentences.zh: 按照该理论，100万到200万年前人类脑容量的演化性增长导致分娩提前、婴儿更为脆弱，也迫切需要母亲与新生儿之间建立更牢固的纽带。

sentences.en: According to Parncutt, ‘motherese’ arose as a way to strengthen this maternal bond and to help infants survive.
sentences.zh: 帕恩卡特认为，“妈妈语”正是作为强化这种母子纽带、帮助婴儿存活的方式而产生的。

sentences.en: ‘If babies were born earlier, it is clear they would need better care in order to survive...
sentences.zh: “如果婴儿出生得更早，显然他们需要更好的照料才能存活……

sentences.en: this would involve the baby communicating its state and needs more clearly to the mother,’ he says.
sentences.zh: 这就要求婴儿更清楚地向母亲传达自己的状态和需求。”他说。

sentences.en: Parncutt adds that this makes it very likely that motherese developed as an evolutionary adaptation, and that there is a large body of contemporary empirical evidence supporting the musical characteristics of motherese.
sentences.zh: 帕恩卡特补充说，这使得妈妈语很可能是作为一种演化适应而发展起来的，而且有大量当代实证证据支持妈妈语所具有的音乐特征。

sentences.en: B Although it might appear amusing - or even nonsensical - at first glance, ‘motherese’ is actually a complex and refined form of communication.
sentences.zh: 尽管乍看之下可能显得有趣、甚至荒唐，“妈妈语”其实是一种复杂而精细的交流形式。

sentences.en: It contains structural musical elements such as rhythm and melody, and codes that babies and mothers understand.
sentences.zh: 它包含节奏和旋律等结构性音乐要素，也包含婴儿与母亲彼此理解的编码。

sentences.en: It also contains cross-cultural similarities with regard to the physical gestures and movements it incorporates - an important consideration when examining the origin of music.
sentences.zh: 它还在所包含的肢体姿势和动作方面存在跨文化的相似性——这在考察音乐起源时是一项重要的考量。

sentences.en: ‘The sonic-gestural vocabulary conveys to both mother and infant information about the present physical and emotional condition of each, along with the current nature of interaction between them,’ states Parncutt.
sentences.zh: 帕恩卡特指出：“这套声音与姿势构成的词汇，向母亲和婴儿双方传达了彼此当下的身体与情绪状况，以及两人之间互动的当前性质。”

sentences.en: ‘Here, emotions such as surprise and disappointment are learned for the first time in a social and musical context.
sentences.zh: “在这里，惊讶和失望等情绪第一次在社会性与音乐性的情境中被习得。

sentences.en: It is about survival in that it motivates the mother to care for the infant and gives her information about the infant’s needs.’
sentences.zh: 它关乎生存，因为它促使母亲照顾婴儿，并向她提供关于婴儿需求的信息。”

sentences.en: For example, mothers can understand when their babies are tired or hungry.
sentences.zh: 例如，母亲能够听出自己的宝宝什么时候累了或饿了。

sentences.en: Motherese also helps infants to acquire language.
sentences.zh: 妈妈语还有助于婴儿习得语言。

sentences.en: C Parncutt explains that a fetus begins hearing nearly four months before birth, as it regularly hears its mother’s voice, heartbeat, and digestive sounds - all of which provide information about its mother’s emotional state.
sentences.zh: 帕恩卡特解释说，胎儿在出生前近四个月就开始有听觉，因为它会经常听到母亲的说话声、心跳声和消化声——所有这些都提供了关于母亲情绪状态的信息。

sentences.en: After birth, the baby recognises these sound patterns and its mother’s correlating mood.
sentences.zh: 出生之后，婴儿会认出这些声音模式以及与之对应的母亲情绪。

sentences.en: Gary McPherson, head of the University of Melbourne’s School of Music, reiterates the importance of this prenatal association, saying that music is the very first form of intelligence to reveal itself - even before birth.
sentences.zh: 墨尔本大学音乐学院院长加里·麦克弗森重申了这种产前关联的重要性，他说音乐是最早显现出来的智能形式——甚至早于出生。

sentences.en: D However, there are several competing theories about the origins of music.
sentences.zh: 不过，关于音乐的起源存在若干相互竞争的理论。

sentences.en: Parncutt developed a grading system to assess these theories, the objective being to measure their validity against a set of criteria which he called ‘universal aspects of music’.
sentences.zh: 帕恩卡特设计了一套评分体系来评估这些理论，目的是依据他称之为“音乐的普遍面向”的一组标准来衡量其成立程度。

sentences.en: Some theories suggest music originated as a form of sexual selection, similar to a peacock’s tail, used to attract mates.
sentences.zh: 有些理论认为音乐起源于一种性选择形式，类似孔雀的尾巴，用来吸引配偶。

sentences.en: Others propose it evolved to enhance social cohesion and cooperation within larger groups, or that it was a byproduct of other evolutionary adaptations with no specific survival purpose of its own.
sentences.zh: 另一些理论则提出，它是为增强较大群体内部的社会凝聚力与协作而演化出来的，或者它只是其他演化适应的副产品，本身并无特定的生存用途。

sentences.en: Parncutt’s system graded each theory based on its ability to explain music’s emotional power, its presence in all known cultures, and its apparent lack of a direct survival function compared to language.
sentences.zh: 帕恩卡特的体系依据每种理论解释音乐情感力量的能力、音乐在所有已知文化中的存在，以及与语言相比音乐明显缺乏直接生存功能这几点来评分。

sentences.en: E When evaluated against these criteria, Parncutt argues that the motherese theory provides the most comprehensive explanation.
sentences.zh: 依据这些标准衡量，帕恩卡特认为妈妈语理论提供了最全面的解释。

sentences.en: It accounts for the deep emotional connection inherent in music by linking it to the primal bond between mother and child.
sentences.zh: 它把音乐与母子之间的原始纽带联系起来，从而解释了音乐内在具有的深刻情感联结。

sentences.en: Furthermore, because caregiving for infants is a human universal, the theory naturally explains why music is found in all cultures around the world.
sentences.zh: 此外，由于照料婴儿是人类的普遍现象，该理论自然解释了为何世界上所有文化中都能找到音乐。

sentences.en: The playful, non-utilitarian nature of motherese also mirrors the aesthetic and seemingly non-functional aspects of music itself, addressing the question of why music exists beyond strict survival needs.
sentences.zh: 妈妈语那种嬉戏而非实用的特性，也映照出音乐本身的审美性与看似无功能的一面，回应了音乐为何能超越严格的生存需要而存在这一问题。

sentences.en: F Nevertheless, the evidence supporting the motherese theory remains far from conclusive.
sentences.zh: 然而，支持妈妈语理论的证据仍远谈不上确凿。

sentences.en: Sandra Trehub, a psychologist at the University of Toronto Mississauga who has studied motherese extensively, warns that every account of music's beginnings is speculative: vocal music, like speech, leaves no physical trace, so none of these theories can ever be proven.
sentences.zh: 多伦多大学密西沙加分校的心理学家桑德拉·特雷胡布对妈妈语做过大量研究，她提醒说，关于音乐起源的每一种说法都是推测性的：声乐和言语一样不会留下实物痕迹，因此这些理论没有一种能够被证明。

sentences.en: A further objection is that the theory says little about music which is not vocal.
sentences.zh: 另一项异议是，该理论对非声乐的音乐几乎没有什么可说的。

sentences.en: Neil McLachlan, a music psychologist at the University of Melbourne, argues that motherese may well be the earliest source, but that musical behaviours are likely to have arisen from a plurality of demands spread across history, pointing to rhythmic traditions that developed independently of infant care.
sentences.zh: 墨尔本大学音乐心理学家尼尔·麦克拉克伦认为，妈妈语很可能确实是最早的源头，但音乐行为很可能源自历史长河中分布各处的多重需求，他举出了独立于育儿之外发展起来的节奏传统作为例证。

sentences.en: Parncutt himself concedes that the evidence is inconclusive and that a combination of factors may be responsible.
sentences.zh: 帕恩卡特本人也承认证据尚无定论，可能是多种因素共同作用的结果。

sentences.en: Set against the alternatives, however, he maintains that his own account is the least speculative, observing that no rival theory has anything definite to say about the link between music and religion that appears in every culture.
sentences.zh: 不过，与其他各种说法相比，他坚持认为自己的解释是推测成分最少的，并指出没有任何一种对立理论能就每种文化中都出现的音乐与宗教之间的联系说出什么确切的东西。

records.title: The Longest Conservation Fence In The World
records.titleZh: 世界上最长的保护围栏

sentences.en: (A) When a wooden post was hammered into a path of Kenyan soil on 28 August 2009, it marked the completion of the longest conservation fence in the world.
sentences.zh: 2009年8月28日，当一根木桩被钉入肯尼亚的一段土路时，它标志着世界上最长的保护围栏竣工。

sentences.en: The 400-kilometre-long, two-metre-high electrified barrier, which protects more than 2,000 square kilometres of lush, green rainforest, took more than 20 years to construct.
sentences.zh: 这道长400公里、高两米的电围栏保护着2000多平方公里郁郁葱葱的雨林，其建造历时20多年。

sentences.en: It was originally built by an animal conservation charity to conserve the black rhino – an endangered species of rhino whose numbers in the region had fallen from hundreds to dozens.
sentences.zh: 它最初由一家动物保护慈善机构修建，用以保护黑犀牛——这是一种濒危犀牛，在该地区的数量已从数百头降至几十头。

sentences.en: However, its effects and beneficiaries have proved to be considerably more wide-ranging.
sentences.zh: 然而事实证明，它的作用和受益者要广泛得多。

sentences.en: (B) The fence encircles part of the Aberdare mountains, a 160-kilometre-long range that forms the eastern rim of the Great Rift Valley just north of the capital Nairobi.
sentences.zh: 这道围栏环绕着阿伯德尔山脉的一部分，这条长160公里的山脉构成了首都内罗毕以北东非大裂谷的东缘。

sentences.en: Well loved by safari-goers, it's a water-rich region that contains a mixture of habitats, including rainforest, bamboo forest and moorland.
sentences.zh: 这里深受野生动物观光者喜爱，是一个水源丰沛的地区，拥有包括雨林、竹林和高山荒原在内的多种栖息地。

sentences.en: But its wildlife had been suffering as Nairobi's growing population crept up into the highlands to farm its volcanic soils.
sentences.zh: 但随着内罗毕不断增长的人口逐渐向高地推进、开垦那里的火山土壤，当地野生生物一直深受其害。

sentences.en: Kenya's population has grown from about three million at the start of the 20th century to around 40 million today, and although many have migrated into the country's cities, about three quarters of Kenyans still live off the land.
sentences.zh: 肯尼亚人口已从20世纪初的约300万增长到今天的约4000万，尽管许多人迁入了国内城市，仍有约四分之三的肯尼亚人以土地为生。

sentences.en: But unfortunately, Kenya doesn't have much fertile land.
sentences.zh: 但遗憾的是，肯尼亚的肥沃土地并不多。

sentences.en: Vast areas of the country are little more than desert, and only around 17 per cent is suitable for farming.
sentences.zh: 该国大片区域几乎就是沙漠，只有约17%的土地适合耕作。

sentences.en: As people moved up into the Aberdares' forests the region became degraded, as trees were felled for firewood or to make way for farming and cattle grazing, and local wildlife was hunted.
sentences.zh: 随着人们迁入阿伯德尔的森林，该地区日益退化，树木被砍作柴薪或为耕作与放牧让路，当地野生生物也遭到捕猎。

sentences.en: (C) Various government and conservation organisations had tried to halt the destruction, but it was difficult to stop illegal uses of the forest, including poaching – the unlawful hunting of animals – when there was no barrier to prevent entry.
sentences.zh: 多个政府部门和保护组织曾试图阻止这种破坏，但在没有屏障阻挡进入的情况下，很难制止对森林的非法利用，其中包括偷猎，也就是非法猎杀动物。

sentences.en: 'One of the problems was that people couldn't really tell where the state-owned, out-of-bounds area began,' explains Colin Church, the chairman of the animal conservation charity.
sentences.zh: “问题之一在于，人们其实分不清国有禁入区域从哪里开始。”这家动物保护慈善机构的主席科林·丘奇解释说。

sentences.en: 'We needed to communicate to local people which land was theirs and which was for the benefit of all Kenyans.'
sentences.zh: “我们需要向当地人说清楚，哪些土地属于他们，哪些土地是为全体肯尼亚人的利益而存在的。”

sentences.en: (D) Initially, there were concerns that the fence would be rejected by the people living in the nearby area, who had become accustomed to supplementing their income with the forest's resources.
sentences.zh: 起初有人担心，这道围栏会遭到附近居民的抵制，他们已经习惯用森林资源补贴收入。

sentences.en: However, that doesn't seem to have been the case.
sentences.zh: 然而事实似乎并非如此。

sentences.en: 'When we were carrying out the assessments, we held five meetings with fence-adjacent communities and most of them were very happy with the fence,' says Professor David Mungai of the University of Nairobi, who led the team that prepared a report on the fence's impact.
sentences.zh: “我们在开展评估时，与围栏周边社区召开了五次会议，其中大多数人对这道围栏都很满意。”内罗毕大学的戴维·蒙盖教授说，他带领团队编写了关于围栏影响的报告。

sentences.en: (E) It soon became clear that the fence has been welcomed because it doesn't just protect animals from people, it also protects people from animals.
sentences.zh: 很快人们就清楚地看到，这道围栏之所以受欢迎，是因为它不仅保护动物免受人的侵扰，也保护人免受动物的伤害。

sentences.en: Before it was built, farmers near the forests would regularly lose a substantial proportion of their harvest to marauding wild animals, and children were often attacked on their way to school by predators.
sentences.zh: 在它建成之前，森林附近的农民经常有相当一部分收成被四处劫掠的野生动物毁掉，孩子们上学路上也常遭猛兽袭击。

sentences.en: 'In this situation, it was difficult for those living near the fence to care too much about conserving the area and its wildlife,' says Church.
sentences.zh: “在这种情况下，住在围栏附近的人很难太在意保护这片区域及其野生生物。”丘奇说。

sentences.en: But the fence has changed that relationship.
sentences.zh: 但这道围栏改变了这种关系。

sentences.en: Since its construction, the 40,000 farmers whose lands border the fence have gained considerably.
sentences.zh: 自建成以来，土地与围栏接壤的40000名农民获益颇丰。

sentences.en: 'Most are now able to harvest 100 per cent of their crops,' says Church.
sentences.zh: “如今大多数人能够收获100%的作物。”丘奇说。

sentences.en: The improved security has seen land values increase by up to 300 per cent, and poaching is down by 99 per cent, according to Dr Julius Kipng'etich, Director of the Kenya Wildlife Service.
sentences.zh: 据肯尼亚野生动物管理局局长朱利叶斯·基普恩盖蒂奇博士介绍，安全状况的改善使地价最高上涨了300%，偷猎下降了99%。

sentences.en: (F) Further local support has been secured by hiring local people to build the fence and act as its guardians – living in specially created cabins beside the fence and patrolling sections up to 20 kilometres in length on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 通过雇用当地人修建围栏并担任守护者，项目进一步赢得了本地支持——这些人住在围栏旁专门搭建的小屋里，每天巡查长达20公里的路段。

sentences.en: 'The fence isn't possible without the support of the local community,' says Mungai.
sentences.zh: “没有当地社区的支持，这道围栏根本不可能建成。”蒙盖说。

sentences.en: He believes that the increased support of local people – many of whom are under-educated and unemployed – will be secured through government investment in schools and job creation, including the setting up of more ecotourism businesses.
sentences.zh: 他认为，当地人——其中许多人受教育程度不高且没有工作——的支持将通过政府在学校和就业方面的投入得到进一步巩固，其中包括开办更多生态旅游企业。

sentences.en: The area currently receives around 50,000 visitors a year, but there is a widespread view that its tourism potential remains relatively untapped.
sentences.zh: 该地区目前每年接待约50000名游客，但普遍认为其旅游潜力仍相对有待开发。

sentences.en: (G) As the region's forests start to recover – reports show that indigenous forest cover within the enclosure has increased by 20 per cent – its rivers have also started to stabilize.
sentences.zh: 随着该地区森林开始恢复——有报告显示围栏内本土森林覆盖率已提高20%——河流也开始趋于稳定。

sentences.en: 'If you remove an area's vegetation, the troughs and peaks of water flow are increased – so the base flow becomes lower, and flooding and erosion become an issue,' says Mungai.
sentences.zh: “如果把一个地区的植被清除掉，水流的低谷和高峰都会加剧——基流因此变低，洪水和侵蚀就成了问题。”蒙盖说。

sentences.en: 'What's important is that a river is stable, so the local people can trust in what that river will be able to deliver.'
sentences.zh: “重要的是河流要稳定，这样当地人才能对这条河能带来什么心里有底。”

sentences.en: Colin Church also sees the Aberdare fence as a true success story.
sentences.zh: 科林·丘奇同样把阿伯德尔围栏视为一个真正的成功案例。

sentences.en: 'The conservation struggle is so often presented as man versus nature.
sentences.zh: “保护之争常常被描述成人与自然的对立。

sentences.en: But with the right management, that doesn't need to be the case,' he says.
sentences.zh: 但只要管理得当，情况不必如此。”他说。

sentences.en: 'The two can benefit each other and live sustainably side by side.
sentences.zh: “两者可以彼此受益，可持续地共存。

sentences.en: We've proved it.'
sentences.zh: 我们已经证明了这一点。”

sentences.en: (H) The success of the Aberdare fence has attracted international attention.
sentences.zh: 阿伯德尔围栏的成功已引起国际关注。

sentences.en: Conservationists from other African countries, as well as from Asia and South America, have visited the site to learn from the experience.
sentences.zh: 来自其他非洲国家以及亚洲和南美洲的保护人士纷纷到访该地，学习其中的经验。

sentences.en: The key lesson, according to Church, is that conservation must work with local communities, not against them.
sentences.zh: 丘奇认为，最关键的启示是保护工作必须与当地社区合作，而不是与之对抗。

sentences.en: 'Too many conservation projects fail because they try to exclude people,' he says.
sentences.zh: “太多保护项目之所以失败，是因为它们试图把人排除在外。”他说。

sentences.en: 'But people are part of the ecosystem.
sentences.zh: “但人本身就是生态系统的一部分。

sentences.en: If they don't benefit from protecting nature, they will have no reason to protect it.'
sentences.zh: 如果他们不能从保护自然中获益，就没有理由去保护它。”

sentences.en: The fence model is now being considered for other sensitive habitats, including national parks in Tanzania and wildlife corridors in India.
sentences.zh: 这种围栏模式目前正在被考虑用于其他敏感栖息地，包括坦桑尼亚的国家公园和印度的野生动物走廊。

sentences.en: (I) Looking ahead, the challenge will be to maintain the fence and the goodwill it has generated.
sentences.zh: 展望未来，挑战在于维护这道围栏以及它所赢得的善意。

sentences.en: The electrified barrier requires regular maintenance, and the guardians need ongoing support and training.
sentences.zh: 电围栏需要定期维护，守护者也需要持续的支持与培训。

sentences.en: Climate change poses a new threat, with more erratic rainfall potentially affecting both the forest and the farms that depend on it.
sentences.zh: 气候变化构成了新的威胁，更加反复无常的降雨可能同时影响森林以及依赖森林的农田。

sentences.en: Yet the project's founders remain optimistic.
sentences.zh: 但项目的发起者依然乐观。

sentences.en: 'We've shown that it's possible to balance human needs with conservation,' says Mungai.
sentences.zh: “我们已经表明，在人的需求与保护之间取得平衡是可能的。”蒙盖说。

sentences.en: 'The fence is just a tool.
sentences.zh: “围栏只是一件工具。

sentences.en: The real achievement is the change in people's attitudes.'
sentences.zh: 真正的成就是人们态度的转变。”

sentences.en: To most of us such questions are either meaningless or suitable only for poetry.
sentences.zh: 对我们大多数人来说，这类问题要么毫无意义，要么只适合出现在诗歌里。

sentences.en: But for some people these are questions to which very precise answers can be given.
sentences.zh: 但对某些人而言，这些问题都能给出非常确切的答案。

sentences.en: Five, for example, for some people is green, while others say the sound of a guitar is like someone blowing on their ankles.
sentences.zh: 例如，对一些人来说，五是绿色的，而另一些人则说吉他的声音像是有人朝自己的脚踝吹气。

sentences.en: People who "see" colour in numbers or letters of the alphabet and "feel" sensation in sound have synesthesia - meaning literally "joined sensation" - an extraordinary condition that causes certain senses to "leak" into one another.
sentences.zh: 那些能“看到”数字或字母的颜色、并能“感觉到”声音的人患有联觉——字面意思是“联合的感觉”——这是一种会让某些感官相互“渗透”的奇特状况。

sentences.en: B People whose senses behave in this way are called "synesthetes".
sentences.zh: 感官以这种方式运作的人被称为“联觉者”。

sentences.en: Some synesthetes take pleasure in it.
sentences.zh: 有些联觉者以此为乐。

sentences.en: "To me it's like other people see the world in black and white," says one, who sees every letter, number, sound and pain in colour.
sentences.zh: “对我来说，这就像别人眼里的世界是黑白的一样。”其中一位如是说，他能看到每个字母、数字、声音和疼痛的颜色。

sentences.en: Others learn to keep it a secret for fear of people laughing at them.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则学会了对此保密，生怕被人取笑。

sentences.en: But to neurologists investigating the brain it is of great interest.
sentences.zh: 但对研究大脑的神经学家来说，这具有极大的意义。

sentences.en: "When scientists study normal perception," says Daniel Smilek of the University of Waterloo in Ontario, Canada, "there are lots of things we don't question because most of us perceive in the same way.
sentences.zh: “当科学家研究正常知觉时，”加拿大安大略省滑铁卢大学的丹尼尔·斯米莱克说，“有很多东西我们不会去质疑，因为我们大多数人的感知方式是一样的。

sentences.en: Synesthesia, because it's abnormal, can give us new insights into normal perception."
sentences.zh: 而联觉由于是反常的，能让我们对正常知觉获得新的认识。”

sentences.en: C Seventeenth-century English philosopher John Locke was the first westerner to describe synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 十七世纪英国哲学家约翰·洛克是最早描述联觉的西方人。

sentences.en: He wrote about a man who experienced bright red as the sound of the trumpet.
sentences.zh: 他写到一个人把鲜红色体验为小号的声音。

sentences.en: Later, the condition excited the imagination of nineteenth-century European painters, such as the non-synesthete Wassily Kandinsky, who believed synesthetes were like good, much-played violins, which vibrate in all their parts and fibres.
sentences.zh: 后来，这种状况激发了十九世纪欧洲画家的想象，比如并非联觉者的瓦西里·康定斯基，他认为联觉者就像被反复演奏的好小提琴，全身各个部件和纤维都在共振。

sentences.en: But it proved impossible to research and people lost interest.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明这无法研究，人们也就失去了兴趣。

sentences.en: Recently, however, advances in brain imaging have sparked renewed interest.
sentences.zh: 不过最近，脑成像技术的进步重新点燃了人们的兴趣。

sentences.en: D Early claims that the multi-sensory experiences of synesthesia were linked with the hallucinations of mental illness have long been disproved.
sentences.zh: 早先有人宣称联觉的多感官体验与精神疾病的幻觉有关，这一说法早已被推翻。

sentences.en: Until 1993, many researchers dismissed it as another name for a vivid imagination, but then an experiment by Simon Baron-Cohen of Cambridge University in the UK showed that synesthetes who, when tested, had linked particular colours or shapes to letters, gave the same answers in 92 per cent of instances when tested again a week later.
sentences.zh: 直到1993年，许多研究者仍把它斥为丰富想象力的另一种说法，但随后英国剑桥大学西蒙·巴伦-科恩的一项实验表明，那些在测试中把特定颜色或形状与字母关联起来的联觉者，一周后再次接受测试时，有92%的情形给出了相同答案。

sentences.en: Non-synesthetes, given similar examples to imagine, returned the same answers in only 37 per cent of instances.
sentences.zh: 而非联觉者在被要求想象类似例子时，只有37%的情形给出了相同答案。

sentences.en: E Although there is some overlap between synesthetes as to what colour is linked to what - 56 per cent see the letter "o" as white - most of the responses are individual.
sentences.zh: 尽管联觉者之间在何种颜色对应何物上存在一些重合——56%的人把字母“o”看作白色——但大多数反应因人而异。

sentences.en: There are 30 possible sensory combinations, but links between sounds and colours are the most common.
sentences.zh: 感官组合共有30种可能，但声音与颜色之间的关联最为常见。

sentences.en: Women are between two and eight times more likely than men to have the condition.
sentences.zh: 女性出现这种状况的可能性是男性的2到8倍。

sentences.en: F As yet there is no explanation for any of this, but small pieces of the jigsaw are emerging.
sentences.zh: 目前对上述现象还没有解释，但拼图的碎片正在逐渐浮现。

sentences.en: A brain scanning experiment by Baron-Cohen in 1995 found that when synesthetes were listening to words, areas of the brain lit up that are normally only active in response to vision and colour.
sentences.zh: 巴伦-科恩1995年的一项脑扫描实验发现，当联觉者在听词语时，大脑中一些通常只对视觉和颜色作出反应的区域被激活了。

sentences.en: From this comes the notion that we may all have synesthesia at birth, when many parts of the brain are linked, but, as we develop, connections are pruned, so our senses become separated and the synesthetic mechanism is no longer intact.
sentences.zh: 由此产生了一种观点：我们所有人出生时可能都有联觉，那时大脑许多部位相互连接，但随着发育，这些连接被修剪掉，于是我们的各种感官彼此分离，联觉机制不再完整。

sentences.en: Somehow, synesthetes have kept their synaptic connections intact.
sentences.zh: 而联觉者不知何故保留了完整的突触连接。

sentences.en: It's an idea that has been challenged, however, on the grounds that if you give people certain drugs they will have synesthetic experiences, which suggests the mechanism is intact in adults but repressed.
sentences.zh: 不过这一观点也受到了质疑，理由是：如果给人服用某些药物，他们会产生联觉体验，这表明该机制在成人体内是完整的，只是被抑制了。

sentences.en: G There are many more unanswered questions about synesthesia.
sentences.zh: 关于联觉，还有许多悬而未决的问题。

sentences.en: For example, is the synesthete's colour response to a number five triggered by actually seeing the number five written on a page, or does the synesthete "see" the colour just by thinking of the number five?
sentences.zh: 例如，联觉者对数字五的颜色反应，是由真正看到写在纸上的数字五触发的，还是仅仅想到数字五就能“看见”那种颜色？

sentences.en: The neurologist Vilyanur Ramachandran came up with a test for synesthesia which seemed to suggest it was the sight of the number that was important.
sentences.zh: 神经学家维拉亚努尔·拉马钱德兰设计了一项联觉测试，其结果似乎表明重要的是看到这个数字。

sentences.en: He asked people to look at a page made up of specially drawn twos and fives that were a mirror image of each other.
sentences.zh: 他让人们看一页纸，上面画着特意设计成彼此镜像的2和5。

sentences.en: The fives were placed at random on the page but the twos were placed to form shapes such as circles or triangles.
sentences.zh: 5在页面上随机排列，而2则被排成圆形或三角形之类的形状。

sentences.en: To most people the numbers just looked like a jumble without order, but to synesthetes the patterns made by the twos were very obvious as a different colour from the fives.
sentences.zh: 对大多数人来说，这些数字看上去只是杂乱无章，但在联觉者眼中，2所构成的图案因颜色与5不同而十分明显。

sentences.en: "This shows they were really sensing colour in the numbers they saw," says Ramachandran.
sentences.zh: “这表明他们确实在所看到的数字中感知到了颜色。”拉马钱德兰说。

sentences.en: "Ideas don't form these kinds of patterns."
sentences.zh: “念头是不会形成这类图案的。”

sentences.en: H However, Smilek subsequently came up with evidence that what really matters is the idea of a number rather than the sight of it on a page.
sentences.zh: 然而，斯米莱克随后拿出证据表明，真正起作用的是数字这个概念，而不是它印在纸上的样子。

sentences.en: He asked a synesthete to do some simple mental arithmetic while looking at different coloured papers.
sentences.zh: 他让一位联觉者在看着不同颜色的纸张时做一些简单的心算。

sentences.en: The subject did not write her answers, but only thought of them and said them aloud.
sentences.zh: 受试者不写下答案，只在心里想并大声说出来。

sentences.en: Smilek found that when the colour of the paper clashed with the colour of the answer, the subject's response was slower than when the colours were the same.
sentences.zh: 斯米莱克发现，当纸张的颜色与答案的颜色相冲突时，受试者的反应比颜色相同时更慢。

sentences.en: An actual colour (the colour of the paper) could interfere with the colour of a number that existed only in her head (the answer to the mental arithmetic question).
sentences.zh: 一种实际存在的颜色（纸张的颜色）会干扰一个只存在于她脑中的数字的颜色（心算题的答案）。

sentences.en: "My research suggests that colour experiences coincide with the processing of meaning," says Smilek.
sentences.zh: “我的研究表明，颜色体验与意义加工是同时发生的。”斯米莱克说。

sentences.en: "It's the concept of a number that's coloured."
sentences.zh: “被赋予颜色的是数字这一概念。”

sentences.en: I So which is it?
sentences.zh: 那么究竟是哪一种呢？

sentences.en: At present, we don't know, but in the future neurologists may be able to explain what's going on in the brains of people like the novelist Nabokov, who perceived the English "a" as dark brown and the French "e" as black.
sentences.zh: 目前我们还不知道，但将来神经学家或许能解释，像小说家纳博科夫那样的人脑中究竟发生了什么——他把英语的“a”感知为深棕色，把法语的“e”感知为黑色。

sentences.en: (A) Chicken as the universal food of our era, crossing cultural boundaries with ease.
sentences.zh: 鸡肉堪称我们这个时代的通用食物，能够轻松跨越文化边界。

sentences.en: With its mild taste and uniform texture, chicken presents a blank canvas for the national flavours of almost any cuisine.
sentences.zh: 鸡肉味道清淡、质地均一，为几乎任何菜系的民族风味都提供了一块空白画布。

sentences.en: However, until the introduction of large-scale industrial production in the 20th century, the economic and nutritional contribution of chickens was small.
sentences.zh: 然而，直到20世纪大规模工业化生产出现之前，鸡在经济和营养方面的贡献都很小。

sentences.en: Chickens were considered as domestic birds that were useful to humanity, but unlike other animals such as the horse or the ox, they did little to change the course of history.
sentences.zh: 鸡曾被视为对人类有用的家禽，但与马或牛之类的其他动物不同，它们对历史进程几乎没有产生什么改变。

sentences.en: Nonetheless, the chicken has inspired contributions to culture, art, cuisine, science and religion over the millennia.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，数千年来鸡还是在文化、艺术、烹饪、科学和宗教方面激发了种种贡献。

sentences.en: Chickens were, and still are, a sacred animal in some cultures.
sentences.zh: 在某些文化中，鸡过去是、如今仍是一种神圣的动物。

sentences.en: The hen is a worldwide symbol of nurturing and fertility.
sentences.zh: 母鸡是全世界通行的养育与生育力的象征。

sentences.en: The rooster is a universal sign of masculinity.
sentences.zh: 公鸡则是普遍意义上的雄性标志。

sentences.en: (B) The domesticated chicken has a complicated family tree, stretching back 10,000 years.
sentences.zh: 家鸡有着复杂的家族谱系，可追溯到一万年前。

sentences.en: Recent DNA testing has shown that the chicken's wild ancestor is the red junglefowl.
sentences.zh: 近期的DNA检测表明，鸡的野生祖先是红原鸡。

sentences.en: The bird's resemblance to modern chickens is seen in the red feathers on top of its head, the red flesh around its mouth, and its distinctive call in the morning.
sentences.zh: 这种鸟与现代鸡的相似之处，体现在其头顶的红色羽毛、嘴部周围的红色肉冠，以及它清晨独特的啼叫声上。

sentences.en: The females of this breed protect their eggs in the same way modern-day chickens do, and they make the same clucking sounds.
sentences.zh: 这一品种的雌鸟护卵的方式与今天的母鸡如出一辙，发出的咯咯声也一模一样。

sentences.en: In its habitat, which stretches from northeastern India to the Philippines, the red junglefowl looks on the forest floor for insects, seeds and fruit and flies up to nest in the trees at night.
sentences.zh: 红原鸡的栖息地从印度东北部一直延伸到菲律宾，它在林地地面上寻找昆虫、种子和果实，夜间则飞到树上筑巢栖息。

sentences.en: That's about as much flying as it can manage, a trait that made it relatively easy for humans to capture and domesticate it.
sentences.zh: 这大概就是它飞行能力的极限了，这一特点使人类相对容易捕捉并驯化它。

sentences.en: But the red junglefowl is not the sole ancestor of the modern chicken.
sentences.zh: 但红原鸡并非现代鸡的唯一祖先。

sentences.en: Scientists have identified three closely related species that might have bred with the red junglefowl.
sentences.zh: 科学家已经确认了三个可能与红原鸡杂交过的近缘物种。

sentences.en: Precisely how much genetic material these other birds contributed to the DNA of domesticated chickens is unknown.
sentences.zh: 这些其他鸟类究竟为家鸡的DNA贡献了多少遗传物质，目前尚不清楚。

sentences.en: However, recent research suggests that modern chickens inherited at least one trait, their yellow skin, from the grey junglefowl of southern India.
sentences.zh: 不过近期研究表明，现代鸡至少从印度南部的灰原鸡那里继承了一项性状，也就是它们的黄色皮肤。

sentences.en: (C) Once chickens were domesticated, cultural contacts, trade, migration and territorial conquest resulted in their introduction to different regions around the world over several thousand years.
sentences.zh: 鸡被驯化之后，文化交往、贸易、迁徙和领土征服使它们在数千年间被引入世界各地。

sentences.en: Chickens arrived in Egypt in around 1750 BC, as fighting birds and additions to zoos.
sentences.zh: 鸡大约在公元前1750年传入埃及，作为斗鸡和动物园的新增物种。

sentences.en: Drawings of the birds decorated royal tombs, which contained the treasures that the kings and queens would take to the afterlife.
sentences.zh: 鸡的图画装饰着王室陵墓，那里存放着国王与王后要带往来世的珍宝。

sentences.en: Yet it would be another 100 years before the bird became popular among ordinary Egyptians.
sentences.zh: 但又过了100年，这种鸟才在普通埃及人中流行起来。

sentences.en: (D) It was in that era that Egyptians mastered the technique of artificial incubation, which freed hens to lay more eggs.
sentences.zh: 正是在那个时代，埃及人掌握了人工孵化技术，使母鸡得以腾出精力多产蛋。

sentences.en: This was not easy.
sentences.zh: 这并不容易。

sentences.en: Most chicken eggs will hatch in three weeks, but only if the temperature remains at around 38 degrees Celsius.
sentences.zh: 大多数鸡蛋会在三周内孵化，但前提是温度必须保持在38摄氏度左右。

sentences.en: The eggs must also be turned three to five times a day, and the humidity must remain stable at about 55 percent, otherwise physical deformities can result, or the eggs won't hatch.
sentences.zh: 蛋每天还必须翻动三到五次，湿度必须稳定在55%左右，否则可能导致畸形，或者蛋根本孵不出来。

sentences.en: The Egyptians constructed vast complexes of large rooms, which were essentially ovens, and these were connected to a series of corridors and vents that allowed attendants to regulate the heat from fires.
sentences.zh: 埃及人建造了由大房间组成的庞大建筑群，这些房间实质上就是烤炉，它们与一系列走廊和通风口相连，使看管人员能够调节火的热度。

sentences.en: The egg attendants kept their methods a secret from outsiders for centuries.
sentences.zh: 数百年间，这些看蛋人一直对外人保守着他们的方法。

sentences.en: (E) Around the Mediterranean, archaeologists have uncovered chicken bones from about 800 BC.
sentences.zh: 在地中海周边，考古学家发掘出了约公元前800年的鸡骨。

sentences.en: Chickens were a delicacy among the Romans, whose culinary innovations included the omelette, and the practice of stuffing birds for cooking.
sentences.zh: 鸡在罗马人中是一道美味，他们在烹饪上的创新包括煎蛋卷，以及给禽类填馅烹制的做法。

sentences.en: European farmers began developing methods to fatten the birds, such as feeding them bread which had been soaked in wine.
sentences.zh: 欧洲农民开始研究给鸡增肥的方法，比如喂食浸过葡萄酒的面包。

sentences.en: But the chicken's status in Europe appears to have diminished with the collapse of Rome.
sentences.zh: 但随着罗马的崩溃，鸡在欧洲的地位似乎有所下降。

sentences.en: In the period after the fall of the Roman Empire, chicken farms vanished and the birds returned to the size they had been 1,000 years earlier.
sentences.zh: 罗马帝国覆亡之后的那段时期，养鸡场消失了，鸡又回到了1000年前的体型。

sentences.en: (F) Well into the 20th century chickens, although valued as a source of eggs, played a relatively minor role in diet and the economy.
sentences.zh: 直到20世纪，鸡虽然作为蛋的来源受到重视，但在饮食和经济中所起的作用仍相对次要。

sentences.en: Long after cattle had entered the industrial age of centralized and mechanized large-scale production, chicken production was still mostly a small-scale local enterprise.
sentences.zh: 在牛已进入集中化、机械化大规模生产的工业时代很久之后，养鸡在很大程度上仍是小规模的地方性经营。

sentences.en: The breakthrough that made today's huge bird farms possible was the inclusion of antibiotics, along with a mixture of different vitamins, in the food chickens ate.
sentences.zh: 使今天大型养鸡场成为可能的突破，是在鸡饲料中加入抗生素以及多种维生素的混合物。

sentences.en: This allowed chickens to be raised indoors and be protected from cold temperatures and heavy rain as well as predators.
sentences.zh: 这使得鸡可以在室内饲养，免受低温、暴雨以及天敌的侵害。

sentences.en: This factory farming represents the chicken's final step in its transformation into a big protein-producing business.
sentences.zh: 这种工厂化养殖标志着鸡最终转变为一门规模庞大的蛋白质生产产业。

sentences.en: (G) Factory farms turning out an increasing amount of chicken have resulted in an increasing demand.
sentences.zh: 工厂化养殖场产出越来越多的鸡肉，这带来了不断增长的需求。

sentences.en: Modern chickens are cogs in a system designed to convert grain into protein with staggering efficiency.
sentences.zh: 现代的鸡是一套系统中的齿轮，这套系统旨在以惊人的效率把谷物转化为蛋白质。

sentences.en: It takes less than 1 kilogram of feed to produce 400 grams of chicken.
sentences.zh: 生产400克鸡肉所需的饲料不到1公斤。

sentences.en: By comparison, around 3 kilograms of feed are required to produce 400 grams of beef.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，生产400克牛肉大约需要3公斤饲料。

sentences.en: A day-old chick can be turned into a 2 kilogram bird in six weeks - half the time it took two generations ago.
sentences.zh: 一只一日龄的雏鸡可以在六周内长成2公斤重的鸡——只有两代人之前所需时间的一半。

sentences.en: (H) Chickens also make wonderful pets, as breeders will tell you.
sentences.zh: 正如养殖者会告诉你的，鸡也是极好的宠物。

sentences.en: They are as colourful as tropical fish but more affectionate, as cute as guinea pigs and better at catching mice than cats.
sentences.zh: 它们像热带鱼一样色彩斑斓，却更亲人；像豚鼠一样可爱，抓老鼠还比猫更在行。

sentences.en: In the USA, exotic and heritage breeds of chicken are being sold for considerable sums of money as the fashion for keeping chickens in the backyard becomes more popular.
sentences.zh: 在美国，随着在自家后院养鸡的风尚日益流行，珍稀品种和传统品种的鸡正被卖出相当可观的价钱。

sentences.en: (I) All in all, the globe-spanning chicken is an epic story of evolutionary, agricultural and culinary success, outnumbering human beings on the planet by nearly three to one.

sentences.en: (A) Coffee originated around the Red Sea, most probably in Ethiopia in Africa, and there are records of coffee cultivation in Yemen as early as the 6th century.
sentences.zh: 咖啡起源于红海一带，最有可能是非洲的埃塞俄比亚，早在6世纪也门就有种植咖啡的记载。

sentences.en: By the 13th century, the growing, roasting and grinding of coffee to make a strong-flavoured infusion was widespread throughout the Arab world.
sentences.zh: 到13世纪，种植、烘焙并研磨咖啡以冲泡出风味浓郁的饮品，在整个阿拉伯世界已十分普遍。

sentences.en: News of the drink was brought to Europe by traders, but people there were at first wary of the new drink.
sentences.zh: 商人把这种饮品的消息带到了欧洲，但那里的人起初对这种新饮料心存戒备。

sentences.en: However, Pope Clement the Eighth gave the drink his seal of approval after trying a cup for himself, and the trend quickly caught on.
sentences.zh: 然而，教皇克莱门特八世亲自尝过一杯之后表示认可，这股风潮很快便流行开来。

sentences.en: The 17th century saw the spread of coffee drinking throughout Europe.
sentences.zh: 17世纪，喝咖啡的习惯传遍了欧洲。

sentences.en: Coffee houses opened in Vienna, Paris and London, and they soon became the favourite meeting places of politicians, and were also known to attract artists of all kinds.
sentences.zh: 维也纳、巴黎和伦敦相继开设咖啡馆，它们很快成为政界人士最喜爱的聚会场所，据说也吸引着各类艺术家。

sentences.en: By the 18th century, coffee production was well established in Java in Indonesia and also throughout the Caribbean.
sentences.zh: 到18世纪，咖啡种植已在印度尼西亚的爪哇以及整个加勒比地区牢固确立。

sentences.en: Coffee drinking continued to grow in popularity; one of the repercussions of the famous Boston Tea Party of 1773 was that the USA adopted coffee as its national beverage.
sentences.zh: 喝咖啡日益流行，1773年著名的波士顿倾茶事件所带来的后果之一，就是美国把咖啡定为其国民饮品。

sentences.en: Today, coffee is drunk around the world, though each nation has its own ways of preparing and serving it.
sentences.zh: 如今，全世界的人都喝咖啡，不过各国都有自己冲泡和享用咖啡的方式。

sentences.en: (B) Coffee is now grown in more than 50 countries, although production is not at all straightforward.
sentences.zh: 咖啡现在在50多个国家种植，尽管生产过程绝不简单。

sentences.en: Because it is vulnerable to frost, coffee can only be grown successfully between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn.
sentences.zh: 由于咖啡不耐霜冻，只有在北回归线与南回归线之间才能成功种植。

sentences.en: In addition, crop maintenance is labour intensive.
sentences.zh: 此外，作物的养护也非常耗费人力。

sentences.en: The plants require constant care and attention, and in most areas the picking is carried out by hand.
sentences.zh: 咖啡植株需要持续的照料与关注，而且在大多数地区采摘都由人工完成。

sentences.en: (C) The ripe berry-like fruits which are harvested are called ‘cherries’.
sentences.zh: 收获的那种成熟的浆果状果实被称为“咖啡樱桃”。

sentences.en: These ripen over a period of six to eight months and turn a deep red when ripe, which explains their name.
sentences.zh: 这些果实要经过六到八个月才成熟，成熟时会变成深红色，这也是它们名字的由来。

sentences.en: Inside there are two green beans that have to be separated from the pulp and the skin, and dried.
sentences.zh: 果实内部有两粒绿色的豆子，必须把它们与果肉和外皮分离并进行干燥。

sentences.en: This process is known as curing, and it can be done by one of two methods.
sentences.zh: 这道工序称为处理，可以采用两种方法之一来完成。

sentences.en: For the traditional ‘dry method’ of curing, the cherries are laid out in the sun until completely dry, and then the dried skins and pulp are removed from the beans.
sentences.zh: 传统的“日晒法”是把咖啡樱桃摊在阳光下晒至完全干燥，然后再把干燥的外皮和果肉从豆子上去除。

sentences.en: The ‘wet method’ is a more recent development and it is employed for high-quality hand-picked cherries.
sentences.zh: “水洗法”是较晚出现的做法，用于处理品质上乘的手工采摘果实。

sentences.en: The outer, fleshy layer is removed, then the cherries are soaked and fermented, followed by washing and drying.
sentences.zh: 先去掉外层的果肉，然后把果实浸泡发酵，接着清洗并干燥。

sentences.en: Finally, the skins are removed by a machine, revealing the green beans.
sentences.zh: 最后由机器去除外皮，露出绿色的咖啡豆。

sentences.en: (D) In both cases, the green beans are sorted, graded and packed for export.
sentences.zh: 两种方法处理后的绿色咖啡豆都会被分选、分级并包装出口。

sentences.en: Roasting tends to be done in the country of import.
sentences.zh: 烘焙通常在进口国进行。

sentences.en: The roasting process is necessary to reduce the acidity of the beans and to develop the aromatic oils, which give the coffee its aroma and flavour.
sentences.zh: 烘焙这道工序是必要的，它可以降低豆子的酸度并催生芳香油脂，正是这些油脂赋予咖啡香气与风味。

sentences.en: Finally, grinding exposes a larger surface area to the water, ensuring optimum contact between the ground beans and the water, resulting in a more satisfying cup of coffee.
sentences.zh: 最后，研磨使更大的表面积暴露于水中，确保咖啡粉与水充分接触，从而冲出一杯更令人满意的咖啡。

sentences.en: (E) The flavour, character and quality of coffee varies tremendously – not only between countries, but also between estates within the same country.
sentences.zh: 咖啡的风味、特性与品质差异极大——不仅国与国之间不同，同一个国家不同庄园之间也有差别。

sentences.en: The soil, altitude and climate are all factors that contribute to the character of the bean, thereby affecting the final taste.
sentences.zh: 土壤、海拔和气候都是影响豆子特性的因素，从而影响最终的口感。

sentences.en: There are four varieties of coffee plant, but only two are sold on any commercial scale.
sentences.zh: 咖啡植物有四个品种，但只有两个进行商业规模的销售。

sentences.en: The most important of these is coffea arabica, which grows on steep mountain slopes at high altitudes.
sentences.zh: 其中最重要的是阿拉比卡咖啡（coffea arabica），它生长在高海拔的陡峭山坡上。

sentences.en: The arabica bean produces coffee that is rich, aromatic and full of flavour, and it accounts for 70% of world coffee production.
sentences.zh: 阿拉比卡豆冲出的咖啡醇厚、芳香、风味饱满，占世界咖啡产量的70%。

sentences.en: Coffee experts agree that the arabica bean is far superior in flavour to other types.
sentences.zh: 咖啡专家一致认为，阿拉比卡豆的风味远胜其他类型。

sentences.en: The other main variety, coffea canephora, produces the coffee bean known as robusta.
sentences.zh: 另一个主要品种中果咖啡（coffea canephora）产出的咖啡豆被称为罗布斯塔。

sentences.en: (F) Grown on the lower slopes, where cultivation is easier, robusta beans have a higher caffeine content than arabica beans, and a rougher, almost earthy flavour that lacks delicacy and subtlety.
sentences.zh: 罗布斯塔生长在较低的山坡上，那里种植更为容易，其咖啡因含量高于阿拉比卡豆，风味更粗糙、近乎带有土味，缺乏细腻与微妙。

sentences.en: It costs about half the price of arabica and is used in the cheaper blends of both fresh and instant coffee.
sentences.zh: 它的价格约为阿拉比卡的一半，被用于较便宜的鲜咖啡和速溶咖啡拼配之中。

sentences.en: (G) There are three types of instant coffee.
sentences.zh: 速溶咖啡有三种类型。

sentences.en: The cheapest is made from robusta beans that have been brewed into a concentrate.
sentences.zh: 最便宜的一种由罗布斯塔豆冲煮成浓缩液制成。

sentences.en: This is sprayed into a stream of hot air that instantly evaporates all moisture, leaving a fine powder.
sentences.zh: 这种浓缩液被喷入热气流中，瞬间蒸发掉所有水分，留下细细的粉末。

sentences.en: Some of the spray-dried powders undergo further heating to produce granular coffees; the better ones include some arabica beans.
sentences.zh: 有些喷雾干燥的粉末会经过进一步加热制成颗粒状咖啡，其中较好的会掺入一些阿拉比卡豆。

sentences.en: The best instant coffees are freeze-dried.
sentences.zh: 最好的速溶咖啡采用冷冻干燥法制作。

sentences.en: For these, an arabica coffee concentrate is frozen and processed in a vacuum to produce crisp, dry particles of coffee.
sentences.zh: 制作时，把阿拉比卡咖啡浓缩液冷冻，并在真空中加工，制成松脆干燥的咖啡颗粒。

sentences.en: (H) Caffeine is a stimulant that is present in coffee.
sentences.zh: 咖啡因是咖啡中含有的一种兴奋剂。

sentences.en: It makes the nervous system more active, which is usually the desired effect.
sentences.zh: 它会使神经系统更加活跃，这通常正是人们想要的效果。

sentences.en: However, it can cause sleeplessness and therefore some consumers prefer to buy coffee without caffeine.
sentences.zh: 不过，它也可能引起失眠，因此有些消费者更愿意购买不含咖啡因的咖啡。

sentences.en: Decaffeinated coffee is available in all the regular coffee forms: whole beans, ground or instant.
sentences.zh: 脱因咖啡有各种常规形态可供选择：整豆、研磨咖啡粉或速溶咖啡。

sentences.en: Caffeine is removed by soaking the beans in water, or by the use of solvents or carbon dioxide.
sentences.zh: 去除咖啡因的方法包括把豆子浸泡在水中，或使用溶剂或二氧化碳。

sentences.en: The latter is thought to be the best method as it does not affect the flavour and there is no residue.
sentences.zh: 后一种方法被认为是最好的，因为它不影响风味，也不会留下残留物。

sentences.en: To qualify as decaffeinated, coffee must contain less than 0.9% caffeine.
sentences.zh: 要符合脱因咖啡的标准，咖啡中咖啡因含量必须低于0.9%。

sentences.en: A Invasive species are among the leading threats to the native wildlife of most countries, with approximately 42 percent of endangered species at risk from them.
sentences.zh: 入侵物种是大多数国家本土野生生物面临的主要威胁之一，约42%的濒危物种因它们而处于危险之中。

sentences.en: Invasive species can be any kind of organism – for example, a mammal, amphibian, fish, insect or plant – that is not native to an ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 入侵物种可以是任何一类生物——例如哺乳动物、两栖动物、鱼类、昆虫或植物——只要它并非某个生态系统的原生物种。

sentences.en: Often they reproduce and spread with great speed.
sentences.zh: 它们往往以极快的速度繁殖和扩散。

sentences.en: Contrary to popular belief, a plant or animal classified as an invasive species does not necessarily originate in another country.
sentences.zh: 与普遍看法相反，被归类为入侵物种的动植物未必来自另一个国家。

sentences.en: For example, lake trout are native to the Great Lakes of North America, but are considered to be an invasive species in Yellowstone Lake in Wyoming because they compete with native cutthroat trout for habitat.
sentences.zh: 例如，湖鳟原产于北美五大湖，但在怀俄明州的黄石湖却被视为入侵物种，因为它们与本土的割喉鳟争夺栖息地。

sentences.en: B When a new species is introduced into an ecosystem, native wildlife may struggle to compete with it for food and other resources.
sentences.zh: 当一个新物种被引入某个生态系统时，本土野生生物可能难以与之争夺食物和其他资源。

sentences.en: Invasive species can change the food web in an ecosystem by destroying or replacing native food sources, while providing little or no food for local wildlife.
sentences.zh: 入侵物种会破坏或取代本土食物来源，从而改变生态系统中的食物网，同时几乎不为当地野生生物提供食物。

sentences.en: In extreme cases, the invader may prey on the native species.
sentences.zh: 在极端情况下，入侵者可能会捕食本土物种。

sentences.en: Above all, invasive species threaten biodiversity in many habitats.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，入侵物种威胁着许多栖息地的生物多样性。

sentences.en: For instance, the climbing plant species kudzu (which is native to East Asia) can easily replace a habitat that had a wide range of plants with a monoculture consisting solely of kudzu, as has started to happen in the south-east of the USA.
sentences.zh: 例如，攀缘植物葛藤（原产于东亚）能够轻易地把原本植物种类丰富的栖息地变成只有葛藤一种植物的单一群落，美国东南部已经开始出现这种情况。

sentences.en: C The phenomenon is not an exclusively modern one.
sentences.zh: 这一现象并非现代所独有。

sentences.en: Humans have always transferred a variety of species from one region to another, but the development of rapid means of transportation has increased the frequency of such introductions.
sentences.zh: 人类一直在把各种物种从一个地区带到另一个地区，但快速交通方式的发展提高了这类引入的频率。

sentences.en: Aquatic organisms can be shipped across the oceans, while insects can easily get into the wooden crates that are transported around the world in this way.
sentences.zh: 水生生物可以随船跨越海洋，而昆虫也很容易钻进以这种方式运往世界各地的木箱之中。

sentences.en: In addition, climate change has enabled some invasive plant species to colonise new areas.
sentences.zh: 此外，气候变化使一些入侵植物得以在新的区域定殖。

sentences.en: Other invasive species include pets such as snakes or turtles which are intentionally set free into the wild.
sentences.zh: 其他入侵物种还包括蛇或龟之类被人有意放归野外的宠物。

sentences.en: D Invasive species do not all present the same level of threat to native ecosystems and can be classified into three types.
sentences.zh: 入侵物种对本土生态系统构成的威胁程度并不相同，可以分为三类。

sentences.en: The first of these may be introduced species which can maintain themselves in a limited range of habitats without upsetting the ecological equilibrium of the area.
sentences.zh: 第一类是那些能够在有限的栖息地范围内维持自身生存、又不会打破当地生态平衡的引入物种。

sentences.en: Some scientists have even argued that in these cases the introduction enhances the diversity of animal and plant life in that specific area.
sentences.zh: 一些科学家甚至认为，在这类情况下，引入反而提升了该特定区域内动植物的多样性。

sentences.en: A second group of invaders present a greater threat because their spread is at the expense of one native species.
sentences.zh: 第二类入侵者威胁更大，因为它们的扩散是以某一种本土物种为代价的。

sentences.en: The North American grey squirrel, for example, was introduced to the UK in 1876 largely because wealthy landowners thought it would be a fashionable and attractive addition to the local wildlife on their estates.
sentences.zh: 例如，北美灰松鼠于1876年被引入英国，主要是因为富有的地主认为它会为自家庄园的本地野生生物增添一份时髦而迷人的点缀。

sentences.en: It spread widely, leading directly to the dramatic decline in the population of the native red squirrel.
sentences.zh: 它广泛扩散，直接导致本土红松鼠数量急剧下降。

sentences.en: However, it would appear that this is the only definite negative impact of the grey squirrel.
sentences.zh: 不过，这似乎是灰松鼠唯一确定无疑的负面影响。

sentences.en: E There is a third level of threat in which the dominance of the introduced species has an extremely destructive effect on the entire ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 还有第三个层级的威胁，即引入物种的优势地位会对整个生态系统造成极具破坏性的影响。

sentences.en: One of the most damaging examples involved a species of comb jellyfish.
sentences.zh: 危害最大的例子之一涉及一种栉水母。

sentences.en: Native to estuaries along the western Atlantic coast from the northern United States to the Valdés Peninsula in Argentina, this species was released from a ship into the Black Sea in Eastern Europe in 1982, almost certainly by accident.
sentences.zh: 该物种原产于从美国北部到阿根廷巴尔德斯半岛的大西洋西岸各河口，1982年几乎可以肯定是被一艘船意外排入了东欧的黑海。

sentences.en: The Black Sea has levels of industrial waste which are by international standards exceptionally high.
sentences.zh: 按国际标准衡量，黑海的工业废弃物含量高得异乎寻常。

sentences.en: Despite this, fishing boats were still able to catch healthy numbers of fish.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，渔船当时仍能捕到数量可观的鱼。

sentences.en: But when the invading jellyfish underwent a population explosion in the space of just six years, the entire marine ecosystem was transformed, and fish numbers declined dramatically because they were in competition with the jellyfish, preying on exactly the same microscopic creatures.
sentences.zh: 但当这种入侵水母在短短六年内出现种群爆发之后，整个海洋生态系统随之改变，鱼类数量急剧下降，因为它们与水母相互竞争，捕食的正是同一类微小生物。

sentences.en: The jellyfish had a more serious impact on the ecosystem than the heavily polluted water.
sentences.zh: 这种水母对生态系统的影响比严重污染的水体更为严重。

sentences.en: F More than a century after its introduction outside its native range on the Amazon River in South America, a plant known as a water hyacinth can be found in tropical lakes, streams, and rivers around the world.
sentences.zh: 一种名为凤眼莲的植物，在被引出其南美亚马孙河原生分布区一个多世纪之后，如今可见于世界各地的热带湖泊、溪流与河流之中。

sentences.en: Its beauty attracted botanists seeking exotic plants for botanical gardens and they imported it to a horticultural exhibition in New Orleans in 1884.
sentences.zh: 它的美丽吸引了那些为植物园寻找奇异植物的植物学家，他们于1884年把它带到了新奥尔良的一场园艺展览上。

sentences.en: Visitors were so impressed they planted it in many locations during the 1880s and 1890s, resulting in the aquatic ecosystems of the south-eastern United States being progressively colonised by vast, floating, dense carpets of water hyacinth.
sentences.zh: 参观者印象极为深刻，在19世纪80年代和90年代把它种到了许多地方，结果美国东南部的水生生态系统被大片漂浮而密集的凤眼莲逐渐占据。

sentences.en: Today it is present around the globe, damaging boat engines and even blocking cooling pipes for power plants, occasionally leading to massive blackouts.
sentences.zh: 如今它遍布全球，损坏船只发动机，甚至堵塞发电厂的冷却管道，偶尔还会导致大面积停电。

sentences.en: The impact of the water hyacinth on native water plants is largely unstudied, as is unfortunately the case for most ecosystems invaded by new plant species.
sentences.zh: 凤眼莲对本土水生植物的影响在很大程度上尚无研究，遗憾的是，大多数被新植物入侵的生态系统都是如此。

sentences.en: G In the United States, more than 7,000 introduced species have established themselves, of which at least 15 percent cause ecological damage.
sentences.zh: 在美国，已有7000多种引入物种立足扎根，其中至少15%造成了生态破坏。

sentences.en: As the number of invasive species expands, legislation to deal with this problem is rare or non-existent in the majority of countries.
sentences.zh: 随着入侵物种数量不断增加，多数国家应对这一问题的立法却很少见，甚至根本不存在。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, ordinary people outside the scientific community have a very limited understanding of the threat posed by invasive species, which means that other environmental threats receive considerably more media attention.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，科学界之外的普通人对入侵物种所构成的威胁了解非常有限，这意味着其他环境威胁获得的媒体关注要多得多。

sentences.en: The introduction of new species can initially seem highly desirable, but the full extent of their impact is consistently underestimated.
sentences.zh: 引入新物种起初看起来可能十分可取，但其影响的全部程度却始终被低估。

sentences.en: H Although ultimately measures need to be taken at an international level, limited action is possible by individuals.
sentences.zh: 尽管最终需要在国际层面采取措施，但个人也能做一些有限的事情。

sentences.en: One way is for people to plant native plants in their gardens rather than species from abroad.
sentences.zh: 其中一种办法是在自家花园里种植本土植物，而不是来自国外的物种。

sentences.en: It is also useful to learn to identify invasive species, and report any sightings to wildlife organisations.
sentences.zh: 学会辨认入侵物种并把发现情况报告给野生生物机构，同样很有帮助。

sentences.en: Regularly cleaning clothing, boots, boats, tyres, and any other equipment regularly used outdoors can remove insects and plant parts that may introduce invasive species into new locations.
sentences.zh: 定期清洁衣物、靴子、船只、轮胎以及其他经常在户外使用的装备，可以去除那些可能把入侵物种带到新地点的昆虫和植物残体。

records.titleZh: 当今英国的孩子由谁来照顾？

sentences.en: A When Simon Baron-Cohen recently published a book, The Essential Difference, in which he claimed that the female brain is predominantly hard-wired for empathy, the male brain is predominantly hard-wired for understanding and building systems, he caught the mood of the moment.
sentences.zh: 西蒙·巴伦-科恩最近出版了一本名为《本质差异》的书，书中他宣称女性大脑主要天生擅长共情，男性大脑主要天生擅长理解和构建系统，这一说法正好迎合了当时的社会氛围。

sentences.en: His team's experiments on day-old babies, and the finding that the male babies looked for longer at a hanging toy and the female babies longer at a face, has been repeatedly cited in the press since his book's publication.
sentences.zh: 他的团队对出生仅一天的婴儿所做的实验发现，男婴注视悬挂玩具的时间更长，女婴注视人脸的时间更长，这一结果自他的书出版以来被媒体反复引用。

sentences.en: However, Elizabeth Spelke is one expert who is sceptical about whether this experiment deserves such attention.
sentences.zh: 然而，伊丽莎白·斯佩尔克是对这项实验是否值得如此关注持怀疑态度的专家之一。

sentences.en: This is one isolated experiment, she says.
sentences.zh: 她说，这只是一项孤立的实验。

sentences.en: 'Its findings fly in the face of dozens of studies on similar aspects of cognition carried out on young babies over decades.
sentences.zh: “它的结论与几十年来针对幼儿类似认知方面所做的数十项研究截然相反。

sentences.en: It is astonishing how much this one study has been cited, when the many studies that show no difference between the sexes, or a difference in the other direction, are ignored.'
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，这一项研究被引用得如此之多，而那些显示两性并无差异、或差异方向相反的众多研究却被忽视了。”

sentences.en: B One of Baron-Cohen's other main studies was conducted by collecting and examining responses to questionnaires completed by adults on their own behaviour: the sort of quiz well known to readers of magazines.
sentences.zh: 巴伦-科恩另一项主要研究，是通过收集并分析成年人就自身行为填写的问卷来进行的：这类测验为杂志读者所熟知。

sentences.en: The answers recorded in such cases will reflect differences formed by cultural assumptions and socialisation: it is hard to see what they tell us about innate differences.
sentences.zh: 这类情形下记录的答案，反映的是由文化预设和社会化所形成的差异：很难看出它们能告诉我们什么关于先天差异的东西。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, they have become a fashionable reference point, and recently Princess Anne, patron of Women into Science and Engineering, gave a speech in which she quoted Baron-Cohen's research as proof that six out of ten men have a systemising brain.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，这些答案已成为时髦的参照，最近，“女性投身科学与工程”组织的赞助人安妮公主发表演讲时，还引用巴伦-科恩的研究作为证据，称十个男性中有六个拥有系统化的大脑。

sentences.en: This kind of science has passed into everyday culture, often outrunning the intentions of those who did the original work.
sentences.zh: 这类科学已经进入日常文化，其影响常常超出最初研究者的本意。

sentences.en: C Social expectations play heavily with young men and women, and expectations are in some ways more conventional in Britain today than they were ten or 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 社会期待对年轻男女影响极大，而且今天英国的某些期待比十年或二十年前还要传统。

sentences.en: It is particularly when they have children that women find out how society reinforces traditional expectations of their behaviour.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在有了孩子之后，女性才会发现社会如何强化对其行为的传统期待。

sentences.en: They discover that many pressures - including the work schedule of their male partner and the expectations of his employer that it should be maintained - make it hard to combine work and home without giving their paid work a lower priority than their male colleagues do.
sentences.zh: 她们发现，许多压力——包括男伴的工作安排以及其雇主要求这种安排必须维持下去——使得她们很难在不把有薪工作的优先级降到低于男同事的情况下兼顾工作与家庭。

sentences.en: In such a context, the claims about males' greater power to systemise and compete only serve to put further pressure on women.
sentences.zh: 在这样的背景下，关于男性更善于系统化和竞争的种种说法，只会给女性带来更多压力。

sentences.en: D The pressures are equally powerful on men to continue in a traditional lifestyle.
sentences.zh: 男性在延续传统生活方式方面同样承受着强大的压力。

sentences.en: Some educationalists argue that among young men the concern that they might appear 'feminine' is higher than ever and may even hold back educational achievement, since studying is often seen as girlish.
sentences.zh: 一些教育学者认为，年轻男性对自己可能显得“女性化”的担忧比以往任何时候都强，甚至可能拖累学业成绩，因为用功读书常被看作是女孩子的事。

sentences.en: In later life, the drive to competitiveness in the workplace is mythologised as being tied to high levels of masculinity.
sentences.zh: 在此后的人生中，职场上的竞争驱动力被神化为与高度男子气概相关联。

sentences.en: Men are also told that high achievers attract more women, even though evidence shows that as women slowly become more equal at work, they begin to care less about the economic status of potential partners.
sentences.zh: 人们还告诉男性，成就高的人更能吸引女性，尽管有证据表明，随着女性在职场上逐渐趋于平等，她们开始不那么在意潜在伴侣的经济地位。

sentences.en: E Men are often held back from making the choice to move deeper into domestic life, and in particular childcare, feeling that it lacks status.
sentences.zh: 男性往往被阻碍着，难以选择更深入地投入家庭生活，尤其是育儿，因为他们觉得这缺乏地位。

sentences.en: While the gains in making a social revolution were clear for women - they could gain status and income by moving beyond the home - the gains in the parallel social revolution are harder for men to see, since it will involve them in losing status and income.
sentences.zh: 对女性而言，这场社会革命带来的收益是明确的——她们可以走出家庭获得地位和收入；而对男性来说，与之平行的社会革命所带来的收益却更难看到，因为这会让他们失去地位和收入。

sentences.en: The idea that men are naturally less empathetic also produces feelings of fatalism about their role.
sentences.zh: 认为男性天生较不善共情的观念，也让他们对自己的角色产生宿命感。

sentences.en: Yet there is much evidence to show that even being empathetic and good at parenting is a learned behaviour.
sentences.zh: 然而大量证据表明，即便是共情能力和育儿本领，也都是习得的行为。

sentences.en: F It is true that, as the linguist Steven Pinker noted, in our culture women respond more readily to their children's cries, but there is nothing to say that this is down to anything other than practice and socialisation.
sentences.zh: 的确，正如语言学家史蒂芬·平克所指出的，在我们的文化中女性对孩子的哭声反应更快，但没有任何依据说明这是出于练习和社会化之外的原因。

sentences.en: In a culture where most men return to work straight after the birth of their children, it would be extraordinary if they did manage to remain as alert to their needs as women who remain at home.
sentences.zh: 在一种大多数男性在孩子出生后立刻重返工作的文化里，如果他们真能像留在家中的女性那样始终敏锐地察觉孩子的需要，那才叫奇怪。

sentences.en: In one test carried out with teenagers, although girls said that they liked children more than boys said they did, when left alone with a crying infant, their responses were no different.
sentences.zh: 在一项针对青少年的测试中，尽管女孩说自己比男孩更喜欢孩子，但当被单独留下面对一个啼哭的婴儿时，他们的反应并无差别。

sentences.en: Women can testify to the fact that parenting is a tricky, complicated process, not always a natural, easy role.
sentences.zh: 女性可以证明，养育子女是一个棘手而复杂的过程，并不总是一种天生而轻松的角色。

sentences.en: G However, while the definite trend of a decade ago is no longer evident, the movement towards equality has not completely stalled.
sentences.zh: 不过，虽然十年前那种明确的趋势已不复存在，走向平等的进程并未完全停滞。

sentences.en: A more equal sharing of childcare and even domestic labour is still desired by many men as well as women.
sentences.zh: 更为平等地分担育儿乃至家务，仍是许多男性和女性共同的期望。

sentences.en: Nearly three-quarters of young British men say that if it were financially possible they would like to stay at home to look after their families.
sentences.zh: 近四分之三的英国年轻男性表示，如果经济上可行，他们愿意待在家里照顾家人。

sentences.en: And three-quarters of young men tell pollsters that the amount of time fathers are allowed to take off work after a birth - paternity leave - is too short in Britain.
sentences.zh: 还有四分之三的年轻男性告诉民调机构，英国允许父亲在孩子出生后休假的时间——也就是陪产假——太短了。

sentences.en: The government is therefore proposing more equal policies on maternity/paternity leave, knowing that the pressure is still forwards rather than backwards.
sentences.zh: 因此政府正在提出更为平等的产假与陪产假政策，因为它知道这股压力仍是向前而非向后的。

sentences.en: And remember that in Britain, young men in full-time work spend about an hour a day looking after their children.
sentences.zh: 另外别忘了，在英国，全职工作的年轻男性每天大约花一小时照顾孩子。

sentences.en: That may sound paltry, but not compared to the 15 minutes they spent 30 years ago: if the time went on increasing fourfold every 30 years, equal partnership would become a reality for their grandchildren.
sentences.zh: 这听起来或许微不足道，但与30年前的15分钟相比就不然了：如果这个时间每30年变为原来的四倍，到他们的孙辈那一代，平等的伙伴关系就会成为现实。
