sentences.en: (A) During the 1600s, very early in the development of steam engines, inventive spirits like the Frenchman Denis Papin dreamed of - and experimented with - boats driven by steam, rather than by the wind or human effort, but many decades passed before those visions became reality.
sentences.zh: 17世纪，在蒸汽机发展的极早期，法国人德尼·帕潘等富有创造力的人物就曾梦想并试验过以蒸汽而非风力或人力驱动的船，但那些设想过了几十年才成为现实。

sentences.en: (B) Englishman Jonathan Hulls took out patents on a steamboat in 1736, but it was to be driven by a Newcomen engine, which was heavy and therefore inefficient, and would never be a success.
sentences.zh: 英国人乔纳森·赫尔斯于1736年为一艘蒸汽船申请了专利，但它要用纽科门蒸汽机驱动，那种机器笨重因而效率低下，永远不可能成功。

sentences.en: In 1763, William Henry, an American, put a Watt steam engine in a boat, but it sank.
sentences.zh: 1763年，美国人威廉·亨利把一台瓦特蒸汽机装上了船，但船沉了。

sentences.en: Nearly 20 years later, in the 1780s, a steam-powered paddle-wheeler managed to last fifteen minutes against the current on the River Saone in France, but lacked the endurance for longer trips.
sentences.zh: 将近20年后的18世纪80年代，一艘蒸汽明轮船在法国索恩河上顶着水流坚持了十五分钟，却缺乏进行更长航程的耐力。

sentences.en: Developments elsewhere included a boat driven by a steam-powered water-jet and able to do six kilometres per hour.
sentences.zh: 其他地方的进展包括一艘由蒸汽驱动的水射流推进、时速可达六公里的船。

sentences.en: However, all these steamboats were either too slow or too expensive to run.
sentences.zh: 然而，所有这些蒸汽船要么太慢，要么运营成本太高。

sentences.en: For example, American John Fitch successfully trialled his first steamboat in 1787, but although he tried a number of designs and solved many technical challenges - one of his boats could even travel at 13 km/h - he could never convince sceptics that steamboats would pay.
sentences.zh: 例如，美国人约翰·菲奇于1787年成功试航了他的第一艘蒸汽船，尽管他尝试了多种设计并解决了许多技术难题——他的一艘船甚至能以每小时13公里的速度航行——他却始终无法让怀疑者相信蒸汽船能够盈利。

sentences.en: (C) The 19th century came before real success could be claimed.
sentences.zh: 直到19世纪，才谈得上真正的成功。

sentences.en: In Scotland in 1802, Lord Dundas launched the steamboat Charlotte Dundas, which was driven by a paddle wheel and had an improved engine designed by William Symington.
sentences.zh: 1802年在苏格兰，邓达斯勋爵推出了蒸汽船 Charlotte Dundas 号，它由明轮驱动，并装有威廉·西明顿设计的改良发动机。

sentences.en: Barges, some weighing as much as 70 tonnes, were towed by this steamboat 30 kilometres along the Forth and Clyde Canal to Glasgow, Scotland’s second city.
sentences.zh: 一些重达70吨的驳船被这艘蒸汽船沿福斯–克莱德运河拖行30公里，抵达苏格兰第二大城市格拉斯哥。

sentences.en: Soon after, success came to American Robert Fulton, whose countrymen called him "the father of the steamboat".
sentences.zh: 不久之后，美国人罗伯特·富尔顿也获得了成功，他的同胞称他为“蒸汽船之父”。

sentences.en: Inspired by news of the Charlotte Dundas, Fulton ran steamboat trials on the River Seine, in an attempt to attract French support for his submarine Nautilus.
sentences.zh: 受 Charlotte Dundas 号消息的启发，富尔顿在塞纳河上进行了蒸汽船试航，试图为他的潜艇 Nautilus 号争取法国方面的支持。

sentences.en: He later imported a Boulton-Watt steam engine and built a boat to use it in.
sentences.zh: 他后来进口了一台博尔顿–瓦特蒸汽机，并专门造了一艘船来安装它。

sentences.en: In 1807, the Clermont began a scheduled passenger steamboat service between New York and Albany, 250 kilometres up the Hudson River, taking 30 hours for the trip.
sentences.zh: 1807年，Clermont 号开通了纽约与奥尔巴尼之间的定期客运蒸汽船服务，沿哈得孙河上行250公里，全程耗时30小时。

sentences.en: Within a few years, steamers were running on the St Lawrence River in Canada and would soon appear on other rivers and lakes, including the Mississippi River, a most famous venue for the paddle-wheelers.
sentences.zh: 短短几年内，蒸汽船就已行驶在加拿大的圣劳伦斯河上，并很快出现在其他河流和湖泊，包括密西西比河这一明轮船最著名的舞台。

sentences.en: (D) Back in Scotland, Fulton’s ideas inspired Henry Bell, who launched his Comet in 1812 on the Clyde between Glasgow and Greenock.
sentences.zh: 回到苏格兰，富尔顿的构想启发了亨利·贝尔，他于1812年让自己的 Comet 号在格拉斯哥与格里诺克之间的克莱德河上首航。

sentences.en: Inside a decade, dozens of steamboats were to be seen on the rivers, lochs and canals of Scotland, carrying cargo and occasionally passengers.
sentences.zh: 不到十年，苏格兰的河流、湖泊和运河上就出现了数十艘蒸汽船，运送货物，偶尔也载客。

sentences.en: The age of steamboats had come.
sentences.zh: 蒸汽船的时代来临了。

sentences.en: (E) Once steamboats were carrying passengers and industrial goods along the inland waterways and sheltered coastlines of Europe, North America and elsewhere, the challenge became to send steamboats onto the open ocean, such as across the Atlantic Ocean, between Europe and the US.
sentences.zh: 一旦蒸汽船开始在欧洲、北美及其他地区的内陆水道和有遮蔽的海岸线上运送旅客与工业货物，新的挑战便是让蒸汽船驶入开阔的大洋，比如横渡欧美之间的大西洋。

sentences.en: Travelling under steam power alone would require engines to use less coal so the ship could stay at sea for several weeks.
sentences.zh: 仅靠蒸汽动力航行，要求发动机消耗更少的煤，这样船才能在海上停留数周。

sentences.en: In order to provide a reliable service, it was also necessary to replace paddle wheels as a source of power with something less affected by the rolling of the ship.
sentences.zh: 为了提供可靠的服务，还必须用受船体摇晃影响更小的装置来取代明轮作为动力来源。

sentences.en: (F) Without waiting for such breakthroughs, crossings under a combination of steam and sail got underway in 1819 with the American ship Savannah.
sentences.zh: 没等这些突破出现，蒸汽与风帆并用的横渡便已在1819年随美国船 Savannah 号展开。

sentences.en: A regular service took another two decades and introduced the famous name of Cunard.
sentences.zh: 定期航线又过了二十年才出现，并引出了丘纳德这个著名的名字。

sentences.en: Securing the British government contract for the mail service across the Atlantic, Samuel Cunard established a shipping line in 1840, soon carrying passengers as well, and offering guaranteed sailing dates.
sentences.zh: 塞缪尔·丘纳德拿下了英国政府横跨大西洋的邮政合同，于1840年创办了一家航运公司，很快也开始载客，并承诺确定的开航日期。

sentences.en: Cunard’s first ships used a sail-steam combination, but the era of the passenger liner, using steam alone, was getting close.
sentences.zh: 丘纳德最早的船采用帆与蒸汽的组合，但纯粹依靠蒸汽的客轮时代已经临近。

sentences.en: When it came to building the ships, the versatile British engineer Isambard Kingdom Brunel set the pace.
sentences.zh: 说到造船，多才多艺的英国工程师伊桑巴德·金德姆·布鲁内尔引领了潮流。

sentences.en: Brunel, brilliant and daring, had already built the Great Western Railway.
sentences.zh: 布鲁内尔才华横溢又敢于冒险，此前已建成了大西部铁路。

sentences.en: He created ever bigger ships - faster, more luxurious and comfortable for passengers.
sentences.zh: 他不断造出更大的船——更快，更豪华，也让乘客更舒适。

sentences.en: The Great Western, launched in 1838, was 70 metres long and crossed from Bristol to New York in just fifteen days.
sentences.zh: 1838年下水的 Great Western 号长70米，从布里斯托尔到纽约仅用十五天。

sentences.en: The largest paddle steamer ever built was Brunel’s Great Eastern.
sentences.zh: 有史以来最大的明轮蒸汽船是布鲁内尔的 Great Eastern 号。

sentences.en: Ultimately too expensive to run as a passenger ship, it was leased to lay the first submarine telegraph cable from Europe to America.
sentences.zh: 它作为客船运营终究过于昂贵，最后被租用去铺设从欧洲到美洲的第一条海底电报电缆。

sentences.en: His 1853 Great Britain, nearly 100 metres long and luxuriously appointed, was the first ocean-going steamship made of iron, and the first to use the underwater screw propeller for powering movement in place of paddle wheels.
sentences.zh: 他1853年建成的 Great Britain 号将近100米长，内部装潢豪华，是第一艘用铁建造的远洋蒸汽船，也是第一艘以水下螺旋桨取代明轮来推进的船。

sentences.en: The idea of the screw had been around since the experiments of the American John Stevens in 1803, but only in 1838 did a large steamer use one, the riverboat Archimedes built by Francis Pettit Smith.
sentences.zh: 螺旋桨的构想自1803年美国人约翰·史蒂文斯的试验以来就已存在，但直到1838年才有一艘大型蒸汽船用上它，那就是弗朗西斯·佩蒂特·史密斯建造的内河船 Archimedes 号。

sentences.en: Later ships had twin screws for reliability.

sentences.en: (G) In many modern ships, steam turbines have replaced engines with pistons, with fuel oil instead of coal to fire the boilers.
sentences.zh: 在许多现代船舶上，蒸汽轮机已取代了带活塞的发动机，锅炉也改用燃料油而非煤来点火。

sentences.en: Diesel engines keep others moving.
sentences.zh: 另一些船则靠柴油机航行。

sentences.en: The largest ships afloat now would dwarf Brunel’s Great Eastern, launched in 1860; the Atlantic can be crossed in only four days.
sentences.zh: 如今最大的船会让1860年下水的布鲁内尔 Great Eastern 号相形见绌；横渡大西洋只需四天。

sentences.en: But in whatever form, the ever-evolving descendants of the original visions of Denis Papin and Robert Fulton continue to travel the seas in vast numbers.

sentences.en: A Scientists have succeeded in copying the silk-producing genes of the Golden Orb Weaver spider and are using them to create a synthetic material which they believe is the model for a new generation of advanced bio-materials.
sentences.zh: 科学家已成功复制了金色圆网蛛的产丝基因，并正用它们制造一种合成材料，他们相信这是新一代先进生物材料的范本。

sentences.en: The new material, biosilk, which has been spun for the first time by researchers at DuPont, has an enormous range of potential uses in construction and manufacturing.
sentences.zh: 这种名为生物丝的新材料由杜邦公司的研究人员首次纺出，在建筑和制造领域有着极其广泛的潜在用途。

sentences.en: B The attraction of the silk spun by the spider is a combination of great strength and enormous elasticity, which man-made fibres have been unable to replicate.
sentences.zh: 蜘蛛所纺之丝的迷人之处，在于极高强度与极大弹性的结合，而这是人造纤维一直无法复制的。

sentences.en: On an equal-weight basis, spider silk is far stronger than steel and it is estimated that if a single strand could be made about 10m in diameter, it would be strong enough to stop a jumbo jet in flight.
sentences.zh: 在同等重量下，蜘蛛丝远比钢更坚韧，据估计，如果能制成一根直径约10米的单丝，它足以拦住一架飞行中的巨型喷气客机。

sentences.en: A third important factor is that it is extremely light.
sentences.zh: 第三个重要因素是它极其轻。

sentences.en: Army scientists are already looking at the possibilities of using it for lightweight, bulletproof vests and parachutes.
sentences.zh: 军方科学家已经在考虑用它制造轻质防弹背心和降落伞的可能性。

sentences.en: C For some time, biochemists have been trying to synthesise the drag-line silk of the Golden Orb Weaver.
sentences.zh: 一段时间以来，生物化学家一直在尝试合成金色圆网蛛的牵引丝。

sentences.en: The drag-line silk, which forms the radial arms of the web, is stronger than the other parts of the web and some biochemists believe a synthetic version could prove to be as important a material as nylon, which has been around for 50 years, since the discoveries of Wallace Carothers and his team ushered in the age of polymers.
sentences.zh: 构成蛛网辐射状支臂的牵引丝比网的其他部分更坚韧，一些生物化学家认为，其合成版本的重要性可能不亚于尼龙——尼龙问世已有50年，当年华莱士·卡罗瑟斯及其团队的发现开启了聚合物时代。

sentences.en: D To recreate the material, scientists, including Randolph Lewis at the University of Wyoming, first examined the silk-producing gland of the spider.
sentences.zh: 为了再造这种材料，包括怀俄明大学兰道夫·刘易斯在内的科学家首先检查了蜘蛛的产丝腺体。

sentences.en: 'We took out the glands that produce the silk and looked at the coding for the protein material they make, which is spun into a web.
sentences.zh: 他说：“我们取出了产丝的腺体，研究了它们所生成、随后被纺成蛛网的蛋白质材料的编码。

sentences.en: We then went looking for clones with the right DNA,' he says.
sentences.zh: 随后我们去寻找带有正确 DNA 的克隆体。”

sentences.en: E At DuPont, researchers have used both yeast and bacteria as hosts to grow the raw material, which they have spun into fibres.
sentences.zh: 在杜邦，研究人员已用酵母和细菌作为宿主来培养这种原材料，并把它纺成了纤维。

sentences.en: Robert Dorsch, DuPont's director of biochemical development, says the globules of protein, comparable with marbles in an egg, are harvested and processed.
sentences.zh: 杜邦生化开发部主管罗伯特·多施说，这些蛋白质小球就像蛋里的弹珠，会被收集起来加以处理。

sentences.en: 'We break open the bacteria, separate out the globules of protein and use them as the raw starting material.
sentences.zh: 他说：“我们把细菌破开，分离出蛋白质小球，把它们当作原始起始材料。

sentences.en: With yeast, the gene system can be designed so that the material excretes the protein outside the yeast for better access,' he says.
sentences.zh: 用酵母时，可以设计基因系统，让该物质把蛋白质分泌到酵母之外，以便更好地获取。”

sentences.en: F 'The bacteria and the yeast produce the same protein, equivalent to that which the spider uses in the draglines of the web.
sentences.zh: “细菌和酵母产生同一种蛋白质，与蜘蛛用于蛛网牵引丝的那种相当。

sentences.en: The spider mixes the protein into a water-based solution and then spins it into a solid fibre in one go.
sentences.zh: 蜘蛛把这种蛋白质混入水基溶液，然后一次成型地纺成固态纤维。

sentences.en: Since we are not as clever as the spider and we are not using such sophisticated organisms, we substituted man-made approaches and dissolved the protein in chemical solvents, which are then spun to push the material through small holes to form the solid fibre.'
sentences.zh: 由于我们不如蜘蛛聪明，用的也不是这么精巧的生物体，我们改用人工方法，把蛋白质溶解在化学溶剂中，再通过纺丝把材料从细孔中挤出，形成固态纤维。”

sentences.en: G Researchers at DuPont say they envisage many possible uses for a new biosilk material.
sentences.zh: 杜邦的研究人员表示，他们设想这种新型生物丝材料有许多可能的用途。

sentences.en: They say that earthquake-resistant suspension bridges hung from cables of synthetic spider silk fibres may become a reality.
sentences.zh: 他们说，用合成蜘蛛丝纤维制成的缆索悬吊的抗震悬索桥，或许会成为现实。

sentences.en: Stronger ropes, safer seat belts, shoe soles that do not wear out so quickly and tough new clothing are among the other applications.
sentences.zh: 更结实的绳索、更安全的安全带、不那么快磨穿的鞋底和坚韧的新式衣物，也在其他应用之列。

sentences.en: Biochemists such as Lewis see the potential range of uses of biosilk as almost limitless.
sentences.zh: 刘易斯这样的生物化学家认为，生物丝的潜在用途范围几乎是无限的。

sentences.en: 'It is very strong and retains elasticity: there are no man-made materials that can mimic both these properties.
sentences.zh: 他说：“它非常坚韧，同时保有弹性：没有任何人造材料能同时模仿这两种特性。

sentences.en: It is also a biological material with all the advantages that have over petrochemicals,' he says.
sentences.zh: 它还是一种生物材料，具备生物材料相对于石化产品的全部优势。”

sentences.en: H At DuPont's laboratories, Dorsch is excited by the prospect of new super-strong materials but he warns they are many years away.
sentences.zh: 在杜邦的实验室里，多施对新型超强材料的前景感到兴奋，但他提醒说这还需要很多年。

sentences.en: 'We are at an early stage but theoretical predictions are that we will wind up with a very strong, tough material, with an ability to absorb shock, which is stronger and tougher than the man-made materials that are conventionally available to us,' he says.
sentences.zh: 他说：“我们还处在早期阶段，但理论预测是，我们最终会得到一种非常坚韧、非常强韧、能够吸收冲击的材料，它比我们通常能拿到的人造材料更强、更韧。”

sentences.en: I The spider is not the only creature that has aroused the interest of material scientists.
sentences.zh: 蜘蛛并不是唯一引起材料科学家兴趣的生物。

sentences.en: They have also become envious of the natural adhesive secreted by the sea mussel.
sentences.zh: 他们也对贻贝分泌的天然黏合剂心生羡慕。

sentences.en: It produces a protein adhesive to attach itself to rocks.
sentences.zh: 它会产生一种蛋白质黏合剂，把自己附着在岩石上。

sentences.en: It is tedious and expensive to extract the protein from the mussel, so researchers have already produced a synthetic gene for use in surrogate bacteria.
sentences.zh: 从贻贝身上提取这种蛋白质既繁琐又昂贵，因此研究人员已经制造出一种合成基因，供替代性的细菌使用。

sentences.en: A Coral reefs are estimated to cover 284,300 km² just under 0.1% of the oceans’ surface area, about half the area of France.
sentences.zh: 据估计，珊瑚礁覆盖284300平方公里，略低于海洋表面积的0.1%，约相当于法国面积的一半。

sentences.en: The Indo-Pacific region accounts for 91.9% of this total area.
sentences.zh: 印度洋–太平洋地区占这一总面积的91.9%。

sentences.en: Southeast Asia accounts for 32.3% of that figure, while the Pacific including Australia accounts for 40.8%.
sentences.zh: 东南亚占其中的32.3%，而包括澳大利亚在内的太平洋地区占40.8%。

sentences.en: Atlantic and Caribbean coral reefs account for 7.6%.
sentences.zh: 大西洋和加勒比海的珊瑚礁占7.6%。

sentences.en: Yet often called "rainforests of the sea", coral reefs form some of the most diverse ecosystems on Earth.
sentences.zh: 珊瑚礁常被称为“海洋中的雨林”，它们构成了地球上最具多样性的生态系统之一。

sentences.en: They provide a home for 25% of all marine species, including fish, mollusks, worms, crustaceans, echinoderms, sponges, tunicates and other cnidarians.
sentences.zh: 它们为全部海洋物种中的25%提供了家园，包括鱼类、软体动物、蠕虫、甲壳动物、棘皮动物、海绵、被囊动物和其他刺胞动物。

sentences.en: Paradoxically, coral reefs flourish even though they are surrounded by ocean waters that provide few nutrients.
sentences.zh: 矛盾的是，珊瑚礁虽被几乎不提供养分的海水包围，却依然繁盛。

sentences.en: They are most commonly found at shallow depths in tropical waters, but deep water and cold water corals also exist on smaller scales in other areas.
sentences.zh: 它们最常见于热带水域的浅处，但深水珊瑚和冷水珊瑚也以较小的规模存在于其他区域。

sentences.en: Although corals exist both in temperate and tropical waters, shallow-water reefs form only in a zone extending from 30°N to 30°S of the equator.
sentences.zh: 尽管温带和热带水域都有珊瑚，浅水珊瑚礁却只形成于赤道以北30°到以南30°之间的区域。

sentences.en: Deepwater coral can exist at greater depths and colder temperatures at much higher latitudes, as far north as Norway.
sentences.zh: 深水珊瑚可以在纬度高得多的地方、于更深更冷的水中生存，最北可达挪威。

sentences.en: Coral reefs are rare along the American and African west coasts.
sentences.zh: 沿美洲和非洲西海岸，珊瑚礁十分罕见。

sentences.en: This is due primarily to upwelling and strong cold coastal currents that reduce water temperatures in these areas (respectively the Peru, Benguela and Canary streams).
sentences.zh: 这主要是由于上升流和强劲的沿岸寒流降低了这些区域的水温（分别是秘鲁寒流、本格拉寒流和加那利寒流）。

sentences.en: Corals are seldom found along the coastline of South Asia from the eastern tip of India (Madras) to the Bangladesh and Myanmar borders.
sentences.zh: 从印度东端的马德拉斯到孟加拉国和缅甸边境的南亚海岸线上，很少见到珊瑚。

sentences.en: They are also rare along the coast around northeastern South America and Bangladesh due to the freshwater released from the Amazon and Ganges Rivers, respectively.
sentences.zh: 在南美洲东北部一带和孟加拉国沿岸，珊瑚同样稀少，原因分别是亚马孙河和恒河注入的淡水。

sentences.en: B Coral reefs deliver ecosystem services to tourism, fisheries and coastline protection.
sentences.zh: 珊瑚礁为旅游业、渔业和海岸线防护提供生态系统服务。

sentences.en: The global economic value of coral reefs has been estimated at as much as $US375 billion per year.
sentences.zh: 珊瑚礁的全球经济价值据估计高达每年3750亿美元。

sentences.en: Coral reefs protect shorelines by absorbing wave energy, and many small islands would not exist without their reef to protect them.
sentences.zh: 珊瑚礁通过吸收波浪能量来保护海岸，许多小岛若没有礁体的守护便不复存在。

sentences.en: C The value of reefs in biodiverse regions can be even higher.
sentences.zh: 在生物多样性丰富的地区，珊瑚礁的价值可能还要更高。

sentences.en: In parts of Indonesia and the Caribbean where tourism is the main use, reefs are estimated to be worth US$1 million per square kilometer, based on the cost of maintaining sandy beaches and the value of attracting snorkelers and scuba divers.
sentences.zh: 在印度尼西亚和加勒比海以旅游为主要用途的部分地区，按维护沙滩的成本以及吸引浮潜者和水肺潜水者的价值计算，珊瑚礁估计每平方公里价值100万美元。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, a recent study of the Great Barrier Reef in Australia found that the reef is worth more to the country as an intact ecosystem than an extractive reserve for fishing.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，近期一项关于澳大利亚大堡礁的研究发现，作为完整生态系统的大堡礁对该国的价值，高于把它当作供捕捞的资源开采区。

sentences.en: Each year more than 1.8 million tourists visit the reef, spending an estimated AU$4.3 billion (Australian dollars) on reef-related industries from diving to boat rental to posh island resort stays.
sentences.zh: 每年有超过180万名游客到访大堡礁，在潜水、租船乃至入住高档岛屿度假村等与礁体相关的产业上花费估计达43亿澳元。

sentences.en: In the Caribbean, says UNEP, the net annual benefits from diver tourism were US$2 billion in 2000 with US$625 million spent directly on diving on reefs.
sentences.zh: 联合国环境规划署表示，在加勒比海地区，2000年潜水旅游带来的年度净收益为20亿美元，其中直接用于礁区潜水的支出为6.25亿美元。

sentences.en: Further, reef tourism is an important source of employment, especially for some of the world’s poorest people.
sentences.zh: 此外，礁区旅游是重要的就业来源，对世界上一些最贫困的人尤其如此。

sentences.en: UNEP says that of the estimated 30 million small-scale fishers in the developing world, most are dependent to a greater or lesser extent on coral reefs.
sentences.zh: 联合国环境规划署称，发展中世界估计有3000万小规模渔民，其中大多数或多或少依赖珊瑚礁。

sentences.en: In the Philippines, for example, more than one million small-scale fishers depend directly on coral reefs for their livelihoods.
sentences.zh: 例如在菲律宾，有超过一百万小规模渔民直接依靠珊瑚礁维持生计。

sentences.en: The report estimates that reef fisheries were worth between $15,000 and $150,000 per square kilometer a year, while fish caught for aquariums were worth $500 a kilogram against $6 for fish caught as food.
sentences.zh: 该报告估计，礁区渔业每平方公里每年价值15000至150000美元，而供水族箱饲养捕捞的鱼每公斤价值500美元，作为食物捕捞的鱼每公斤仅6美元。

sentences.en: The aquarium fish export industry supports around 50,000 people and generates some US$5.5 million a year in Sri Lanka alone.
sentences.zh: 仅在斯里兰卡，观赏鱼出口业就支撑着约50000人的生计，每年产生约550万美元收入。

sentences.en: D Unfortunately, coral reefs are dying around the world.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，全世界的珊瑚礁正在死去。

sentences.en: In particular, coral mining, agricultural and urban runoff, pollution (organic and inorganic), disease, and the digging of canals and access into islands and bays are localized threats to coral ecosystems.
sentences.zh: 尤其是珊瑚开采、农业与城市径流、有机和无机污染、病害，以及开挖运河、修建通往岛屿和海湾的通道，都是珊瑚生态系统面临的局部威胁。

sentences.en: Broader threats are sea temperature rise, sea-level rise and pH changes from ocean acidification, all associated with greenhouse gas emissions.
sentences.zh: 更广泛的威胁则是海水温度上升、海平面上升以及海洋酸化带来的酸碱度变化，这些都与温室气体排放有关。

sentences.en: Some current fishing practices are destructive and unsustainable.
sentences.zh: 当前的一些捕捞方式具有破坏性且不可持续。

sentences.en: These include cyanide fishing, overfishing and blast fishing.
sentences.zh: 这些方式包括氰化物捕鱼、过度捕捞和炸鱼。

sentences.en: Although cyanide fishing supplies live reef fish for the tropical aquarium market, most fish caught using this method are sold in restaurants, primarily in Asia, where live fish are prized for their freshness.
sentences.zh: 氰化物捕鱼虽为热带水族箱市场提供活体礁鱼，但用这种方法捕到的鱼大多被卖给餐馆，主要在亚洲，那里的活鱼因新鲜而受到推崇。

sentences.en: To catch fish with cyanide, fishers dive down to the reef and squirt cyanide in coral crevices and on the fast-moving fish, to stun the fish making them easy to catch.
sentences.zh: 为了用氰化物捕鱼，渔民潜到礁石处，把氰化物喷进珊瑚缝隙以及游动迅速的鱼身上，把鱼击晕，使其容易被捕捉。

sentences.en: Overfishing is another leading cause for coral reef degradation.
sentences.zh: 过度捕捞是珊瑚礁退化的另一个主要原因。

sentences.en: Often, too many fish are taken from one reef to sustain a population in that area.
sentences.zh: 同一片礁区常常被捕走过多的鱼，以致该地区的种群难以维持。

sentences.en: Poor fishing practices, such as banging on the reef with sticks (muro-ami), destroy coral formations that normally function as fish habitat.
sentences.zh: 用棍棒敲击礁体这类拙劣的捕捞方式（muro-ami），会毁掉本可充当鱼类栖息地的珊瑚构造。

sentences.en: In some instances, people fish with explosives (blast fishing), which blast apart the surrounding coral.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，人们用炸药捕鱼，也就是炸鱼，把周围的珊瑚炸得四分五裂。

sentences.en: E Tourist resorts that empty their sewage directly into the water surrounding coral reefs contribute to coral reef degradation.
sentences.zh: 把污水直接排入珊瑚礁周边水域的旅游度假区，也在助长珊瑚礁的退化。

sentences.en: Wastes kept in poorly maintained septic tanks can also leak into surrounding groundwater, eventually seeping out to the reefs.
sentences.zh: 存放在维护不善的化粪池中的废物，也可能渗入周边地下水，最终渗出到礁区。

sentences.en: Careless boating, diving, snorkeling and fishing can also damage coral reefs.
sentences.zh: 不当的驾船、潜水、浮潜和垂钓同样会损害珊瑚礁。

sentences.en: Whenever people grab, kick, and walk on, or stir up sediment in the reefs, they contribute to coral reef destruction.
sentences.zh: 只要人们抓握、踢踏、踩踏礁体，或搅起礁区的沉积物，就是在加剧珊瑚礁的破坏。

sentences.en: Corals are also harmed or killed when people drop anchors on them or when people collect coral.
sentences.zh: 当人们把船锚抛落在珊瑚上，或采集珊瑚时，珊瑚同样会受伤或死亡。

sentences.en: F To find answers for these problems, scientists and researchers study the various factors that impact reefs.
sentences.zh: 为寻找这些问题的答案，科学家和研究人员研究了影响珊瑚礁的各种因素。

sentences.en: The list includes the ocean’s role as a carbon dioxide sink, atmospheric changes, ultraviolet light, ocean acidification, viruses, impacts of dust storms carrying agents to far-flung reefs, pollutants, algal blooms and others.
sentences.zh: 这份清单包括海洋作为二氧化碳汇的作用、大气变化、紫外线、海洋酸化、病毒、把各种物质带到遥远礁区的沙尘暴的影响、污染物、藻华等等。

sentences.en: Reefs are threatened well beyond coastal areas.
sentences.zh: 珊瑚礁受到的威胁远远超出沿海地区。

sentences.en: General estimates show approximately 10% of the world’s coral reefs are dead.
sentences.zh: 总体估计显示，全球约10%的珊瑚礁已经死亡。

sentences.en: About 60% of the world’s reefs are at risk due to destructive, human-related activities.
sentences.zh: 全球约60%的珊瑚礁因具有破坏性的人类相关活动而处于危险之中。

sentences.en: The threat to the health of reefs is particularly strong in Southeast Asia, where 80% of reefs are endangered.
sentences.zh: 礁体健康所受的威胁在东南亚尤为严重，那里80%的珊瑚礁面临危险。

sentences.en: G In Australia, the Great Barrier Reef is protected by the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority and is the subject of much legislation, including a biodiversity action plan.
sentences.zh: 在澳大利亚，大堡礁受大堡礁海洋公园管理局保护，并是许多立法的对象，其中包括一项生物多样性行动计划。

sentences.en: Inhabitants of Ahus Island, Manus Province, Papua New Guinea, have followed a generations-old practice of restricting fishing in six areas of their reef lagoon.
sentences.zh: 巴布亚新几内亚马努斯省阿胡斯岛的居民，遵循着世代相传的做法，在其礁湖的六个区域限制捕捞。

sentences.en: Their cultural traditions allow line fishing, but not net or spearfishing.
sentences.zh: 他们的文化传统允许手钓，但不允许使用渔网或鱼叉捕鱼。

sentences.en: The result is both the biomass and individual fish sizes are significantly larger in these areas than in places where fishing is unrestricted.
sentences.zh: 结果是，这些区域的生物量和鱼的个体大小都明显超过不限制捕捞的地方。

sentences.en: A For most of its history, biotechnology was associated with medicine and agriculture.
sentences.zh: 在其历史的大部分时间里，生物技术都与医学和农业联系在一起。

sentences.en: Its first wave brought drugs, vaccines and diagnostic tests; its second wave produced genetically modified crops and improved varieties of plants.
sentences.zh: 它的第一波浪潮带来了药物、疫苗和诊断检测，第二波浪潮则催生了转基因作物和改良的植物品种。

sentences.en: A third wave, however, is now moving beyond hospitals and farms into factories, mines, paper mills and even clothing manufacturers.
sentences.zh: 然而，第三波浪潮如今正走出医院与农田，进入工厂、矿山、造纸厂，甚至服装制造企业。

sentences.en: Instead of using heat, pressure and harsh chemicals to make products, this new form of biotechnology uses living systems, especially enzymes and microorganisms, to perform industrial tasks.
sentences.zh: 这种新形态的生物技术不再依靠高温、高压和强效化学品来制造产品，而是利用生命系统，尤其是酶和微生物，来完成工业任务。

sentences.en: Supporters argue that this change could be as important for manufacturing as steam power or electricity once were.
sentences.zh: 支持者认为，这一变化对制造业的重要性，可能不亚于当年的蒸汽动力或电力。

sentences.en: B The central agents in this third wave are enzymes, natural proteins that speed up chemical reactions.
sentences.zh: 这第三波浪潮的核心角色是酶，也就是能加速化学反应的天然蛋白质。

sentences.en: In the human body, enzymes help digest food, repair cells and release energy.
sentences.zh: 在人体内，酶帮助消化食物、修复细胞和释放能量。

sentences.en: In industry, the same basic principle can be used to break down starch, clean fibres, remove stains or convert plant material into useful substances.
sentences.zh: 在工业中，同样的基本原理可以用来分解淀粉、清洁纤维、去除污渍，或把植物材料转化为有用的物质。

sentences.en: The advantage is that enzymes are highly specific: each one tends to perform only one type of reaction.
sentences.zh: 其优势在于酶具有高度专一性：每一种酶往往只完成一类反应。

sentences.en: This means that a factory can achieve a desired result with fewer unwanted by-products than traditional chemical processes usually produce.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，与传统化学工艺通常产生的情况相比，工厂能以更少的副产物达成想要的结果。

sentences.en: C Enzymes are not new to industry.
sentences.zh: 酶对工业来说并不新鲜。

sentences.en: For decades, they have been added to washing powders to remove grease and protein stains at lower temperatures.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，人们一直把酶加进洗衣粉，以便在较低温度下去除油脂和蛋白质污渍。

sentences.en: They are also used in cheese-making, brewing and baking.
sentences.zh: 它们也被用于制作奶酪、酿酒和烘焙。

sentences.en: What is new is the scale and precision with which they can now be designed.
sentences.zh: 新鲜之处在于如今设计酶的规模和精度。

sentences.en: By studying the structure of natural enzymes and altering the genes of microorganisms, scientists can produce enzymes that remain active in unusual conditions, such as extreme acidity, high salt levels or relatively low temperatures.
sentences.zh: 通过研究天然酶的结构并改变微生物的基因，科学家可以制造出在异常条件下仍保持活性的酶，比如极端酸性、高盐浓度或相对较低的温度。

sentences.en: This has made them attractive to companies looking for cleaner and cheaper methods of production.
sentences.zh: 这让那些寻求更清洁、更便宜生产方法的公司对酶产生了兴趣。

sentences.en: D One widely cited example is the textile industry.
sentences.zh: 一个被广泛引用的例子是纺织业。

sentences.en: Traditionally, cotton fabrics were treated with strong chemicals to remove tiny loose fibres from the surface, a process that used large amounts of water and created chemical waste.
sentences.zh: 传统上，棉织物要用强效化学品处理，以去除表面细小的浮毛，这一工序耗水量大，还会产生化学废弃物。

sentences.en: Some manufacturers now use enzymes to perform the same task more gently.
sentences.zh: 如今一些制造商改用酶，以更温和的方式完成同样的任务。

sentences.en: The fabric becomes smoother and brighter, while less water and energy are consumed.
sentences.zh: 织物变得更平滑、更明亮，同时耗水和耗能都更少。

sentences.en: Enzymes are also used to fade denim jeans, replacing some of the stones and chemical bleaching agents once needed to create the popular worn look.
sentences.zh: 酶也被用来给牛仔裤褪色，取代了从前为营造流行的做旧外观所需的部分石料和化学漂白剂。

sentences.en: For consumers, the final product may appear no different, but the method of production can be far less damaging.
sentences.zh: 对消费者而言，最终产品也许看不出差别，但生产方式的破坏性可以小得多。

sentences.en: E The paper and pulp industry has also experimented with enzyme-based processes.
sentences.zh: 纸浆与造纸行业同样试验过以酶为基础的工艺。

sentences.en: Wood pulp contains lignin, a tough material that must be removed or modified before paper can be whitened.
sentences.zh: 木浆中含有木质素，这是一种坚韧的物质，必须先去除或改性，纸张才能被漂白。

sentences.en: Conventional bleaching can involve chlorine compounds, which may produce harmful pollutants if not carefully controlled.
sentences.zh: 常规漂白可能涉及氯化合物，若控制不当会产生有害污染物。

sentences.en: Certain enzymes can help loosen lignin or prepare the pulp for bleaching, reducing the amount of chlorine-based chemicals required.
sentences.zh: 某些酶可以帮助松解木质素或为漂白做准备，从而减少所需含氯化学品的用量。

sentences.en: In other cases, enzymes help fibres drain more quickly, allowing paper machines to run faster and use less energy.
sentences.zh: 在另一些情形下，酶还能帮助纤维更快脱水，使造纸机跑得更快、耗能更少。

sentences.en: These changes may sound minor, but in large factories even a small percentage saving can have significant economic value.
sentences.zh: 这些变化听上去也许微小，但在大型工厂里，哪怕百分之几的节省也可能带来可观的经济价值。

sentences.en: F A further development combines enzymes with genetic engineering.
sentences.zh: 又一项进展是把酶与基因工程结合起来。

sentences.en: Instead of simply finding useful enzymes in nature, researchers can insert selected genes into bacteria, yeasts or fungi, turning them into miniature factories.
sentences.zh: 研究人员不再只是从自然界中寻找有用的酶，而是可以把选定的基因插入细菌、酵母或真菌，把它们变成微型工厂。

sentences.en: These organisms can then produce large quantities of enzymes for commercial use.
sentences.zh: 这些生物随后就能大量生产供商业使用的酶。

sentences.en: Some scientists are also designing microbes that can convert agricultural waste into biofuels, biodegradable plastics or industrial solvents.
sentences.zh: 一些科学家还在设计能把农业废弃物转化为生物燃料、可生物降解塑料或工业溶剂的微生物。

sentences.en: This combination of enzyme technology and genetic engineering is one reason the third wave is considered broader than earlier applications of biotechnology.
sentences.zh: 酶技术与基因工程的这种结合，正是第三波浪潮被认为比生物技术早期应用更为宽广的原因之一。

sentences.en: It is not merely improving existing products; it is changing the way raw materials are processed.
sentences.zh: 它不只是在改良既有产品，更是在改变原材料的加工方式。

sentences.en: G The commercial appeal is obvious, but it is not the only reason governments and companies are interested.
sentences.zh: 商业上的吸引力显而易见，但这并不是各国政府和企业感兴趣的唯一原因。

sentences.en: Many countries are under pressure to reduce pollution, cut carbon emissions and use resources more efficiently.
sentences.zh: 许多国家面临着减少污染、削减碳排放和更高效利用资源的压力。

sentences.en: Industrial biotechnology can contribute to these goals because biological reactions often take place at lower temperatures and in water rather than in toxic solvents.
sentences.zh: 工业生物技术有助于实现这些目标，因为生物反应往往在较低温度下、在水中而非有毒溶剂中进行。

sentences.en: As a result, factories may require less energy, produce less waste and rely less heavily on petroleum-based raw materials.
sentences.zh: 因此，工厂可能耗能更少、产生的废弃物更少，对石油基原材料的依赖也更轻。

sentences.en: However, critics warn that the environmental benefits are not automatic.
sentences.zh: 不过，批评者提醒说，环境效益并非自动产生。

sentences.en: Growing crops for bio-based products, for example, can compete with food production or lead to land-use problems if not managed carefully.
sentences.zh: 例如，为生物基产品种植作物，若管理不当，可能与粮食生产争地，或引发土地利用问题。

sentences.en: H Despite these concerns, many analysts believe the third wave could bring major environmental advantages.
sentences.zh: 尽管有这些担忧，许多分析人士仍认为第三波浪潮可能带来重大的环境优势。

sentences.en: In theory, it offers a way to make industrial production cleaner without asking consumers to give up the goods they use every day.
sentences.zh: 理论上，它提供了一条让工业生产变得更清洁的途径，而无需要求消费者放弃日常使用的商品。

sentences.en: Detergents can work in cold water, jeans can be faded with fewer chemicals, paper can be bleached with less pollution, and fuels can be made from plant waste rather than crude oil.
sentences.zh: 洗涤剂可以在冷水中起效，牛仔裤可以用更少的化学品做旧，纸张可以在更少污染的情况下漂白，燃料可以用植物废弃物而非原油来制造。

sentences.en: The promise is especially attractive because it links environmental protection with profit: companies save money while improving their public image.
sentences.zh: 这一前景格外诱人，因为它把环境保护与利润联系在一起：企业既省钱，又改善了公众形象。

sentences.en: For this reason, biotechnology is increasingly viewed not just as a scientific field, but as a tool of sustainable commerce.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，生物技术越来越不只是被视为一个科学领域，而是被看作可持续商业的一种工具。

sentences.en: I There remain obstacles.
sentences.zh: 障碍依然存在。

sentences.en: New biological processes must be reliable, safe and cost-effective before manufacturers will adopt them.
sentences.zh: 新的生物工艺必须可靠、安全且成本可控，制造商才会采用。

sentences.en: Customers may also be suspicious if they hear that genetic engineering is involved, even when the genetically modified organism is used only inside a factory and is not present in the final product.
sentences.zh: 顾客若听说其中涉及基因工程，也可能心存疑虑，哪怕转基因生物只在工厂内部使用、并不存在于最终产品之中。

sentences.en: Regulation varies from country to country, and companies must prove that their methods do not create new risks.
sentences.zh: 各国的监管不尽相同，企业必须证明自己的方法不会带来新的风险。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the direction of travel is clear.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，前进的方向是清楚的。

sentences.en: The third wave of biotechnology is moving from the laboratory into everyday industry, and its influence may become visible not in what consumers buy, but in how those products are made.
sentences.zh: 生物技术的第三波浪潮正从实验室走进日常工业，其影响也许不体现在消费者买什么，而体现在这些产品是怎么造出来的。

sentences.en: A The bittern, a British waterbird, does not have a good record as far as survival is concerned.
sentences.zh: 就生存而言，英国的一种水鸟大麻鳽的记录并不光彩。

sentences.en: By 1886, habitat destruction and other pressures had pushed it close to extinction.
sentences.zh: 到1886年，栖息地破坏和其他压力已把它逼到濒临灭绝的境地。

sentences.en: Fortunately, it recovered a decade later, and in 1950 the numbers of male bitterns rose to a peak of about 70.
sentences.zh: 所幸十年后它有所恢复，到1950年，雄性大麻鳽的数量升至约70只的高峰。

sentences.en: By the 1980s, however, it was clear that the bird was in trouble again.
sentences.zh: 然而到了20世纪80年代，这种鸟显然再度陷入困境。

sentences.en: The bittern needs extensive wet reedbeds to survive, and long periods of drainage, pollution and lack of management had destroyed most of its habitat.
sentences.zh: 大麻鳽需要大片湿润的芦苇地才能生存，而长期的排水、污染和缺乏管理已毁掉它大部分栖息地。

sentences.en: By 1997, it again faced imminent extinction.
sentences.zh: 到1997年，它再次面临迫在眉睫的灭绝危险。

sentences.en: To prevent this, the British government set up a plan for the bittern, aiming to establish a population of 50 males by 2010.
sentences.zh: 为阻止这一点，英国政府为大麻鳽制定了一项计划，目标是到2010年建立起50只雄鸟的种群。

sentences.en: However, this target was reached six years early, a rate of recovery faster than anyone had dared hope for.
sentences.zh: 然而这一目标提前六年就实现了，恢复速度之快超出了任何人敢于期望的程度。

sentences.en: The Royal Society for the Protection of Birds (RSPB) now claims the bittern as one of Britain’s greatest wildlife success stories, since figures reveal that the number of these rare birds has increased fivefold in just seven years.
sentences.zh: 英国皇家鸟类保护协会（RSPB）如今把大麻鳽称作英国最了不起的野生动物成功案例之一，因为数据显示，这种稀有鸟类的数量在短短七年间增长了四倍。

sentences.en: B Bitterns have feathers that help them to conceal themselves and a shy nature; they usually remain hidden within the cover of reedbed vegetation.
sentences.zh: 大麻鳽的羽毛有助于它们隐蔽，性情也很怯生，它们通常藏身于芦苇丛的掩蔽之中。

sentences.en: Our first challenge was to develop standard methods to monitor their numbers.
sentences.zh: 我们面临的第一个挑战，是制定出监测其数量的标准方法。

sentences.en: The booming call of the male bittern is its most distinctive feature during the breeding season, and we developed a method to count them using the sound patterns unique to each individual.
sentences.zh: 雄性大麻鳽响亮的叫声是它在繁殖季最显著的特征，我们据此开发出一种方法，利用每只个体独有的声音模式来计数。

sentences.en: This not only allowed us to estimate local survival of males from one year to the next.
sentences.zh: 这不仅让我们得以估算雄鸟从一年到下一年的本地存活情况。

sentences.en: C Our first direct understanding of what breeding bitterns require in their ideal habitat came from comparisons of reedbed sites that had lost their male birds with those that retained them.
sentences.zh: 我们对繁殖期大麻鳽在理想栖息地中的需求，最早的直接认识来自把失去雄鸟的芦苇地与仍保有雄鸟的芦苇地作比较。

sentences.en: This research showed that bitterns had been retained in reedbeds where the natural process of drying out had been slowed through management.
sentences.zh: 这项研究表明，在那些通过管理减缓了自然干涸过程的芦苇地里，大麻鳽得以留存。

sentences.en: Based on this work, broad recommendations on how to manage and rehabilitate reedbeds for bitterns were made, and funding was provided through a European Union (EU) wildlife fund to manage 13 sites within the core breeding range.
sentences.zh: 基于这项工作，人们就如何为大麻鳽管理和修复芦苇地提出了总体建议，并通过欧盟（EU）野生动物基金拨款，用于管理核心繁殖区内的13处场地。

sentences.en: D To refine these recommendations and provide fine-scale, quantitative habitat prescriptions on the bitterns’ preferred feeding habitat, we started radio-tracking male bitterns on the RSPB’s Minsmere and Leighton Moss reserves.
sentences.zh: 为细化这些建议，并就大麻鳽偏好的觅食栖息地给出精细的定量处方，我们开始在RSPB的明斯米尔和莱顿沼泽保护区对雄性大麻鳽进行无线电追踪。

sentences.en: This showed clear preferences for feeding in the wetter reedbed areas, particularly within reed next to larger open pools.
sentences.zh: 结果显示，它们明显偏好在较湿润的芦苇地觅食，尤其是紧邻较大开阔水塘的芦苇丛。

sentences.en: The average home range sizes of the male bitterns we followed (about 20 hectares) provided a good indication of the area of reedbed necessary when managing or creating habitat for this species.
sentences.zh: 我们所追踪的雄性大麻鳽平均活动范围（约20公顷），为在管理或营造该物种栖息地时所需的芦苇地面积提供了很好的参考。

sentences.en: Female bitterns undertake all the incubation and care of the young, so it was important to understand their requirements as well.
sentences.zh: 雌性大麻鳽承担全部孵卵和育雏工作，因此了解它们的需求同样重要。

sentences.en: Over the course of our research, we located 87 bittern nests and found that female bitterns preferred to nest in areas of continuous vegetation, well into the reedbed, but where water was still present during the driest part of the breeding season.
sentences.zh: 在研究过程中，我们定位了87个大麻鳽巢，发现雌鸟偏好在植被连续、深入芦苇地内部、且在繁殖季最干旱时期仍有积水的区域筑巢。

sentences.en: E The success of the habitat prescriptions developed from this research has been spectacular.
sentences.zh: 由这项研究得出的栖息地处方，其成效十分显著。

sentences.en: For instance, at Minsmere, male bittern numbers gradually increased from one to ten following reedbed lowering, a management technique designed to halt the drying out process.
sentences.zh: 例如在明斯米尔，实施芦苇地降低作业这一旨在遏止干涸过程的管理手段之后，雄性大麻鳽的数量从一只逐步增加到十只。

sentences.en: After a low point of 11 mature males in 1997, bittern numbers in Britain responded to all the habitat management work and started to increase for the first time since 1950.
sentences.zh: 在1997年跌至11只成年雄鸟的低点之后，英国的大麻鳽数量对全部栖息地管理工作作出了回应，自1950年以来首次开始上升。

sentences.en: F The final phase of research involved understanding the diet, survival and dispersal of bittern chicks.
sentences.zh: 研究的最后阶段是了解大麻鳽雏鸟的食物、存活和扩散情况。

sentences.en: To do this, we fitted small radio tags to young bittern chicks in the nest, to determine their fate through to fledging, when they begin to fly, and beyond.
sentences.zh: 为此，我们给巢中的幼雏装上小型无线电标签，以追踪它们直到出飞、也就是开始飞行乃至之后的命运。

sentences.en: Many chicks did not survive to this stage, and starvation was found to be the most likely reason for their demise.
sentences.zh: 许多雏鸟没能活到这一阶段，而饥饿被认为是它们死亡最可能的原因。

sentences.en: The first prey fed to chicks were mainly those species penetrating into the reed edge.
sentences.zh: 最先喂给雏鸟的猎物，主要是那些能进入芦苇边缘地带的物种。

sentences.en: So, an important element of recent studies has been development of recommendations on habitat and water conditions to promote native fish populations.
sentences.zh: 因此，近期研究的一个重要内容，是就促进本地鱼类种群的栖息地与水文条件提出建议。

sentences.en: Once independent, radio-tagged young bitterns were found to seek out new sites during their first winter; a proportion of these would remain on new sites if the conditions were suitable.
sentences.zh: 一旦独立，装有无线电标签的幼鸟被发现会在第一个冬天寻找新的栖息地，其中一部分若条件合适便会留在新址。

sentences.en: A second EU-funded project aims to provide these suitable sites in new areas.
sentences.zh: 欧盟资助的第二个项目，正是要在新的区域提供这类合适的场地。

sentences.en: A network of 19 sites developed through this partnership project will secure a more sustainable UK bittern population with successful breeding outside of the core area, less vulnerable to chance and sea level rise.
sentences.zh: 通过这一合作项目建成的19处场地网络，将使英国大麻鳽种群更可持续，在核心区之外也能成功繁殖，从而更不易受偶然因素和海平面上升的影响。

sentences.en: G By 2004, the number of booming male bitterns in the UK had increased to 55.
sentences.zh: 到2004年，英国鸣叫的雄性大麻鳽已增至55只。

sentences.en: Almost all the increase occurred on those sites undertaking management based on advice from our research.
sentences.zh: 几乎全部增量都出现在那些依据我们研究建议开展管理的场地上。

sentences.en: While rescuing the bittern, the work has helped a range of other wetland species such as otters.
sentences.zh: 在拯救大麻鳽的同时，这项工作也惠及了水獭等一系列其他湿地物种。

sentences.en: Although science has been at the core of the recovery story, success has only been achieved through the trust, hard work and dedication of all the managers, owners and wardens of sites that have implemented, in some cases very drastic, management to secure the future of this wetland species in the UK.
sentences.zh: 尽管科学一直是这个复苏故事的核心，成功却只有依靠所有场地的管理者、所有者和看护员的信任、辛劳与奉献才得以实现，他们为保住这一湿地物种在英国的未来，实施了有时相当激烈的管理措施。

sentences.en: A The start of the automobile's history went all the way back to 1769 when automobiles running on the steam engine were invented as carriers for human transport.
sentences.zh: 汽车的历史可一直追溯到1769年，当时人们发明了以蒸汽机驱动的汽车，用作载人的运输工具。

sentences.en: In 1806, the first batch of cars powered by an internal combustion engine came into being, which pioneered the introduction of the widespread modem petrol-fueled internal combustion engine in 1885.
sentences.zh: 1806年，第一批由内燃机驱动的汽车问世，它们为1885年现代汽油内燃机的广泛引入开了先河。

sentences.en: B It is generally acknowledged that the first practical automobiles equipped with petrol/gaso-line-powered internal combustion engines were invented almost at the same time by different German inventors who were Working on their own.
sentences.zh: 人们普遍认为，第一批装有汽油内燃机的实用汽车，几乎是由几位各自独立工作的德国发明家在同一时期发明的。

sentences.en: Karl Benz first built the automobile in 1885 in Mannheim.
sentences.zh: 卡尔·本茨于1885年在曼海姆首次造出了汽车。

sentences.en: Benz attained a patent for his invention on 29 January 1886, and in 1888, he started to produce automobiles in a company that later became the renowned Mercedes-Benz.
sentences.zh: 本茨在1886年1月29日为其发明取得专利，并于1888年开始在一家公司生产汽车，该公司后来成为著名的梅赛德斯–奔驰。

sentences.en: C As this century began, the automobile industry marched into the transportation market for the wealth.
sentences.zh: 进入本世纪时，汽车产业挺进了面向富人的交通市场。

sentences.en: Drivers at that time were an adventurous bunch; they would go out regardless of the weather condition even if they weren't even protected by an enclosed body or a convertible top.
sentences.zh: 当时的驾驶者是一群勇于冒险的人，他们不顾天气状况就出门，哪怕连封闭车身或折叠车篷的保护都没有。

sentences.en: Everybody in the community knew who owned what car, and cars immediately became a symbol of identity and status.
sentences.zh: 社区里人人都知道谁拥有哪辆车，汽车随即成为身份与地位的象征。

sentences.en: Later, cars became more popular among the public since it allowed people to travel whenever and wherever they wanted.
sentences.zh: 后来，汽车在公众中更受欢迎，因为它让人们可以随时随地出行。

sentences.en: Thus, the price of automobiles in Europe and North America kept dropping, and more people from the middle class could afford them.
sentences.zh: 于是，欧洲和北美的汽车价格不断下跌，越来越多的中产阶级买得起汽车。

sentences.en: This was especially attributed to Henry Ford who did two crucial things.
sentences.zh: 这尤其要归功于亨利·福特，他做了两件关键的事。

sentences.en: First, he set the price as reasonable as possible for his cars; second, he paid his employees enough salaries so that they could afford the cars made by their very own hands.
sentences.zh: 第一，他把自家汽车的价格定得尽可能合理；第二，他给员工足够的薪水，使他们买得起自己亲手造出的汽车。

sentences.en: D The trend of interchangeable parts and mass production in an assembly line style had been led by America, and from 1914, this concept was significantly reinforced by Henry Ford.
sentences.zh: 可互换零件与流水线式大规模生产的潮流由美国引领，而从1914年起，这一理念被亨利·福特大大强化。

sentences.en: This large-scale, production-line manufacture of affordable automobiles was debuted.
sentences.zh: 这种大规模、流水线式的平价汽车制造由此登场。

sentences.en: A Ford car would come off all assembled from the line every 15 minutes, an interval shorter than any of the former methods.
sentences.zh: 每隔15分钟就有一辆福特汽车整装下线，这个间隔比以往任何方法都短。

sentences.en: Not only did it raise productivity, but also cut down on the requirement for manpower.
sentences.zh: 它不仅提高了生产率，也减少了对人力的需求。

sentences.en: Ford significantly lowered the chance of injury by carrying out complicated safety procedures in production—particularly assigning workers to specific locations rather than giving them the freedom to wander around.
sentences.zh: 福特通过在生产中执行复杂的安全流程大幅降低了受伤几率，尤其是把工人安排在特定工位，而不是让他们随意走动。

sentences.en: This mixture of high wages and high efficiency was known as Fordism, which provided a valuable lesson for most major industries.
sentences.zh: 这种高工资与高效率的结合被称为福特主义，为大多数主要产业提供了宝贵的经验。

sentences.en: E The first Jeep automobile that came out as the prototype Bantam BRC was the primary light 4-wheel-drive automobile of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 最早以 Bantam BRC 原型车面世的吉普汽车，是美国

sentences.en: Army and Allies, and during World War II and the postwar period, its sale skyrocketed.
sentences.zh: 陆军及盟军的主力轻型四轮驱动汽车，在第二次世界大战期间及战后，它的销量猛增。

sentences.en: Since then, plenty of Jeep derivatives with similar military and civilian functions have been created and kept upgraded in terms of overall performance in other nations.
sentences.zh: 此后，许多具有类似军用和民用功能的吉普衍生车型在其他国家被造出来，并在整体性能上持续升级。

sentences.en: F Through all the 1950s, engine power and automobile rates grew higher, designs evolved into a more integrated and artful form, and cars were spreading globally.
sentences.zh: 整个20世纪50年代，发动机功率和汽车产量不断攀升，设计演变得更为整体化也更具艺术性，汽车正在全球扩散。

sentences.en: In the 1960s, the landscape changed as Detroit was confronted with foreign competition.
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪60年代，局面发生变化，底特律面临来自国外的竞争。

sentences.en: The European manufacturers, used the latest technology, and Japan came into the picture as a dedicated car-making country.
sentences.zh: 欧洲制造商采用了最新技术，日本也作为一个专注造车的国家进入了人们视野。

sentences.en: General Motors, Chrysler, and Ford dabbled with radical tiny cars such as the GM A-bodies with little success.
sentences.zh: 通用汽车、克莱斯勒和福特尝试过 GM A-bodies 这类激进的小型车，却收效甚微。

sentences.en: As joint ventures such as the British Motor Corporation unified the market, captive imports and badge imports swept all over the US and the UK.
sentences.zh: 随着英国汽车公司这样的合资企业整合市场，贴牌进口车和换标进口车席卷了美国和英国。

sentences.en: BMC first launched a revolutionary space-friendly Mini in 1959, which turned out to harvest large global sales.
sentences.zh: 英国汽车公司于1959年率先推出了革命性的、空间利用出色的 Mini，结果在全球斩获了巨大销量。

sentences.en: Previously remaining under the Austin and Morris names, Mini later became an individual marque in 1969.
sentences.zh: Mini 此前一直挂在 Austin 和 Morris 名下，后来于1969年成为独立品牌。

sentences.en: The trend of corporate consolidation landed in Italy when niche makers such as Maserati, Ferrari, and Lancia were bought by larger enterprises.
sentences.zh: 当玛莎拉蒂、法拉利和蓝旗亚这类小众厂商被更大的企业收购时，企业整合的潮流也来到了意大利。

sentences.en: By the end of the 20th century, there had been a sharp fall in the number of automobile marques.
sentences.zh: 到20世纪末，汽车品牌的数量已急剧减少。

sentences.en: G In the US, car performance dominated marketing, justified by the typical cases of pony cars and muscle cars.
sentences.zh: 在美国，汽车性能主导着营销，小马车和肌肉车就是典型例证。

sentences.en: However, in the 1970s, everything changed as the American automobile industry suffered from the 1973 oil crisis, competition with Japanese and European imports, automobile emission-control regulations* and moribund innovation.
sentences.zh: 然而到了20世纪70年代，一切都变了，美国汽车业遭受1973年石油危机、与日欧进口车竞争、汽车排放控制法规以及创新乏力的冲击。

sentences.en: The irony in all this was that full-size sedans such as Cadillac and Lincoln scored a huge comeback between the years of economic crisis.
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，凯迪拉克和林肯这类全尺寸轿车却在经济危机的那些年里大幅回潮。

sentences.en: H In terms of technology, the most mentionable developments that postwar era had seen were the widespread use of independent suspensions, broader application of fuel injection, and a growing emphasis on safety in automobile design.
sentences.zh: 在技术方面，战后时期最值得一提的进展是独立悬架的普遍采用、燃油喷射的更广泛应用，以及汽车设计中对安全性日益增强的重视。

sentences.en: Mazda achieved many triumphs with its engine firstly installed in the fore-wheel, though it gained itself a reputation as a gas-guzzler.
sentences.zh: 马自达凭借最早装在前轮位置的发动机取得了许多成功，尽管它也落下了油老虎的名声。

sentences.en: I The modem era also has witnessed a sharp elevation of fuel power in the modem engine management system with the.
sentences.zh: 现代时期还见证了现代发动机管理系统中燃油动力的急剧提升，这要借助

sentences.en: help of the computer.
sentences.zh: 计算机之力。

sentences.en: Nowadays, most automobiles in use are powered by an internal combustion engine, fueled by gasoline or diesel.
sentences.zh: 如今，在用的大多数汽车由内燃机驱动，燃料为汽油或柴油。

sentences.en: Toxic gas from both fuels is known to pollute the air and is responsible for climate change as well as global warming.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，这两种燃料产生的有毒气体会污染空气，并对气候变化和全球变暖负有责任。

sentences.en: A The amount of time people spend watching television is astonishing.
sentences.zh: 人们看电视花掉的时间之多令人吃惊。

sentences.en: On average, individuals in the industrialized world devote three hours a day to the pursuit – fully half of their leisure time, and more than on any single activity save work and sleep.
sentences.zh: 在工业化世界，个人平均每天把三小时投入其中——整整占去闲暇时间的一半，除工作和睡眠外，没有任何一项活动耗时更多。

sentences.en: At this rate, someone who lives to 75 would spend nine years in front of the tube.
sentences.zh: 按这个速度，活到75岁的人会有九年待在电视机前。

sentences.en: To some commentators, this devotion means simply that people enjoy TV and make a conscious decision to watch it.
sentences.zh: 在一些评论者看来，这种投入只不过说明人们喜欢电视，并有意识地决定去看。

sentences.en: But if that is the whole story, why do so many people experience misgivings about how much they view?
sentences.zh: 但如果事情仅止于此，为什么那么多人对自己的收视量心怀不安呢？

sentences.en: In Gallup polls in 1992 and 1999, two out of five adult respondents and seven out of 10 teenagers said they spent too much time watching TV.
sentences.zh: 在1992年和1999年的盖洛普民调中，每五名成年受访者中有两人、每十名青少年中有七人表示自己看电视的时间过多。

sentences.en: Other surveys have consistently shown that roughly 10 percent of adults calls themselves TV addicts.
sentences.zh: 其他调查也一贯显示，约有10%的成年人自称是电视上瘾者。

sentences.en: B To study people's reactions to TV, researchers have undertaken laboratory experiments in which they have monitored the brain waves (using an electroencephalograph, or EEG) to track behavior and emotion in the normal course of life, as opposed to the artificial conditions of the lab.
sentences.zh: 为研究人们对电视的反应，研究者开展了实验室实验，在其中监测脑电波（使用脑电图仪，即EEG），以追踪日常生活自然状态下而非实验室人为条件下的行为与情绪。

sentences.en: Participants carried a beeper, and we signaled them six to eight times a day, at random, over the period of a week; whenever they heard the beep, they wrote down what they were doing and how they were feeling using a standardized scorecard.
sentences.zh: 参与者随身携带一个传呼器，我们在一周时间里每天随机呼叫他们六到八次，每当他们听到呼叫声，就用一份标准化记分卡写下自己在做什么、感觉如何。

sentences.en: C As one might expect, people who were watching TV when we beeped them reported feeling relaxed and passive.
sentences.zh: 不出所料，被呼叫时正在看电视的人报告说自己感到放松而被动。

sentences.en: The EEG studies similarly show less mental stimulation, as measured by alpha brain-wave production, during viewing than during reading.
sentences.zh: 脑电图研究同样显示，以α脑波的产生来衡量，观看电视时的心智激活程度低于阅读时。

sentences.en: What is more surprising is that the sense of relaxation ends when the set is turned off, but the feelings of passivity and lowered alertness continue.
sentences.zh: 更令人意外的是，放松感在关掉电视时便告结束，被动感和警觉度下降却仍在持续。

sentences.en: Survey participants say they have more difficulty concentrating after viewing than before.
sentences.zh: 调查参与者说，看完电视后比看之前更难集中注意力。

sentences.en: In contrast, they rarely indicate such difficulty after reading.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，他们在阅读之后很少表示有这种困难。

sentences.en: After playing sports or engaging in hobbies, people report improvements in mood.
sentences.zh: 在做完运动或从事爱好之后，人们报告心情有所改善。

sentences.en: After watching TV, people's moods are about the same or worse than before.
sentences.zh: 而看完电视后，人们的心情与之前差不多，甚至更糟。

sentences.en: That may be because of viewers' vague learned sense that they will feel less relaxed if they stop viewing.
sentences.zh: 这也许是因为观众隐约学到一种感觉，觉得一旦停止观看就会不那么放松。

sentences.en: So they tend not to turn the set-off.
sentences.zh: 于是他们往往不去关掉电视。

sentences.en: Viewing begets more viewing which is the same as the experience of habit-forming drugs.
sentences.zh: 观看催生更多观看，这与那些会形成习惯的药物所带来的体验如出一辙。

sentences.en: Thus, the irony of TV: people watch a great deal longer than they plan to, even though prolonged viewing is less rewarding.
sentences.zh: 电视的讽刺之处正在于此：人们看的时间远远超出自己的计划，尽管看得越久回报越少。

sentences.en: In our ESM studies the longer people sat in front of the set, the less satisfaction they said they derived from it.
sentences.zh: 在我们的经验取样研究中，人们坐在电视机前的时间越长，他们所说从中获得的满足感就越低。

sentences.en: For some, a twinge of unease or guilt that they aren't doing something more productive may also accompany and depreciate the enjoyment of prolonged viewing.
sentences.zh: 对某些人来说，一丝不安或愧疚，觉得自己没在做更有产出的事，也会伴随并折损长时间观看的乐趣。

sentences.en: Researchers in Japan, the U.K. and the U.S. have found that this guilt occurs much more among middle-class viewers than among less affluent ones.
sentences.zh: 日本、英国和美国的研究者发现，这种愧疚感在中产阶级观众中比在较不富裕的观众中要常见得多。

sentences.en: D What is it about TV that has such a hold on us?
sentences.zh: 电视究竟有什么能这样牢牢抓住我们呢？

sentences.en: In part, the attraction seems to spring from our biological 'orienting response.'
sentences.zh: 这种吸引力似乎有一部分源自我们生物学上的“定向反应”。

sentences.en: First described by Ivan Pavlov in 1927, the orienting response is our instinctive visual or auditory reaction to any sudden or novel stimulus.
sentences.zh: 定向反应最早由伊万·巴甫洛夫在1927年描述，它是我们对任何突然或新奇刺激的本能视觉或听觉反应。

sentences.en: It is part of our evolutionary heritage, a built-in sensitivity to movement and potential predatory threats.
sentences.zh: 它是我们演化遗产的一部分，是对运动和潜在捕食威胁与生俱来的敏感。

sentences.en: In 1986 Byron Reeves of Stanford University, Esther Thorson of the University of Missouri and their colleagues began to study whether the simple formal features of television – cuts, edits, zooms, pans, sudden noises – activate the orienting response, thereby keeping attention on the screen.
sentences.zh: 1986年，斯坦福大学的拜伦·里夫斯、密苏里大学的埃丝特·索森及其同事开始研究电视那些简单的形式特征——切换、剪辑、变焦、摇镜、突如其来的声响——是否会激活定向反应，从而把注意力留在屏幕上。

sentences.en: By watching how brain waves were affected by formal features, the researchers concluded that these stylistic tricks can indeed trigger involuntary responses and 'derive their attentional value through the evolutionary significance of detecting movement…
sentences.zh: 通过观察脑电波如何受这些形式特征影响，研究者得出结论认为，这些风格化手法确实能触发不由自主的反应，并且“通过察觉运动这一演化意义获得其吸引注意的价值……

sentences.en: It is the form, not the content, of television that is unique.'
sentences.zh: 电视之独特，在于它的形式，而非内容。”

sentences.en: E The natural attraction to television's sound and the light starts very early in life.
sentences.zh: 对电视声光的天然吸引力在生命极早期就已开始。

sentences.en: Dafna Lemish of Tel Aviv University has described babies at six to eight weeks attending to television.
sentences.zh: 特拉维夫大学的达夫娜·莱米什曾描述过六到八周大的婴儿注视电视的情形。

sentences.en: We have observed slightly older infants who, when lying on their backs on the floor, crane their necks around 180 degrees to catch what light through yonder window breaks.
sentences.zh: 我们也观察到稍大一些的婴儿，他们仰卧在地板上时，会把脖子扭转近180度，去捕捉那窗外透进的光。

sentences.en: This inclination suggests how deeply rooted the orienting response is.
sentences.zh: 这种倾向说明定向反应扎根有多深。

sentences.en: F The Experience Sampling Method permitted us to look closely at most every domain of everyday life: working, eating, reading, talking to friends, playing a sport, and so on.
sentences.zh: 经验取样法让我们得以细致考察日常生活几乎每一个领域：工作、进食、阅读、与朋友交谈、做运动等等。

sentences.en: We found that heavy viewers report feeling significantly more anxious and less happy than light viewers do in unstructured situations, such as doing nothing, daydreaming or waiting in line.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，在无所事事、发呆或排队等待这类没有明确结构的情境中，重度观看者报告的焦虑感明显高于轻度观看者，幸福感则明显更低。

sentences.en: The difference widens when the viewer is alone.
sentences.zh: 当观看者独处时，这一差距还会拉大。

sentences.en: Subsequently, Robert D.
sentences.zh: 随后，马尼托巴大学的罗伯特·D·

sentences.en: McIlwraith of the University of Manitoba extensively studies those who called themselves TV addicts on surveys.
sentences.zh: 麦基尔雷斯对那些在调查中自称电视上瘾者的人做了广泛研究。

sentences.en: On a measure called the Short Imaginal Processes Inventory (SIPI), he found that the self-described addicts are more easily bored and distracted and have poorer attentional control than the non-addicts.
sentences.zh: 在一项名为简版想象过程量表（SIPI）的测量中，他发现这些自称上瘾者更容易感到无聊和分心，注意力控制也比非上瘾者更差。

sentences.en: The addicts said they used TV to distract themselves from unpleasant thoughts and to fill time.
sentences.zh: 这些上瘾者说，他们用电视把自己从不愉快的念头中引开，并用来打发时间。

sentences.en: Other studies over the years have shown that heavy viewers are less likely to participate in community activities and sports and are more likely to be obese than moderate viewers or non-viewers.
sentences.zh: 多年来的其他研究还表明，与适度观看者或不看电视者相比，重度观看者更少参加社区活动和体育运动，也更可能肥胖。

sentences.en: G More than 25 years ago psychologist Tannis M.
sentences.zh: 二十五年多以前，心理学家坦尼斯·M·

sentences.en: MacBeth Williams of the University of British Columbia studied a mountain community that had no television until cable finally arrived.
sentences.zh: 不列颠哥伦比亚大学的麦克白·威廉姆斯研究了一个在有线电视终于接入之前一直没有电视的山区社区。

sentences.en: Over time, both adults and children in the town became less creative in problem-solving, less able to persevere at tasks, and less tolerant of unstructured time.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，镇上的成人和儿童在解决问题时都变得不那么有创造力，在任务上更难坚持，对没有安排的时间也更难忍受。

sentences.en: H Nearly 40 years ago Gary A.
sentences.zh: 将近四十年前，加里·A·

sentences.en: Steiner of the University of Chicago collected fascinating individual accounts of families whose set had broken.
sentences.zh: 芝加哥大学的施泰纳收集了一些家庭电视机坏掉后引人入胜的个人记述。

sentences.en: In experiments, families have volunteered or been paid to stop viewing, typically for a week or a month.
sentences.zh: 在实验中，有些家庭自愿或受酬停止收看，通常为期一周或一个月。

sentences.en: Some fought, verbally and physically.
sentences.zh: 有些人吵了起来，既动口也动手。

sentences.en: In a review of these could-turkey studies, Charles Winick of the City University of New York concluded: 'The first three or four days for most persons were the worst, even in many homes where the viewing was minimal and where there were other ongoing activities.
sentences.zh: 纽约市立大学的查尔斯·威尼克在评述这些戒断式研究时得出结论：“对多数人而言，最初的三四天最难熬，即便在许多平时收看很少、且有其他日常活动的家庭里也是如此。

sentences.en: In over half of all the households, during these first few days of loss, the regular routines were disrupted, family members had difficulties in dealing with the newly available time, anxiety and aggressions were expressed….
sentences.zh: 在超过一半的家庭中，失去电视的最初这几天里，日常作息被打乱，家庭成员难以应对突然多出来的时间，焦虑和攻击性也表现了出来……

sentences.en: By the second week, a move toward adaptation to the situation was common.'
sentences.zh: 到第二周，普遍出现了向这种状况适应的趋势。”

sentences.en: Unfortunately, researchers have yet to flesh out these anecdotes; no one has systematically gathered statistics on the prevalence of these withdrawal symptoms.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，研究者尚未把这些轶事充实为系统证据，还没有人系统收集过这些戒断症状发生率的统计数据。

sentences.en: I Even though TV does seem to meet the criteria for substance dependence, not all researchers would go so far as to call TV addictive.
sentences.zh: 尽管电视看上去确实符合物质依赖的标准，并非所有研究者都愿意走到把电视称为成瘾物的地步。

sentences.en: McIlwraith said in 1988 that 'displacement of other activities by television may be socially significant but still fall short of the clinical requirement of significant impairment.'
sentences.zh: 麦基尔雷斯在1988年说过，“电视对其他活动的挤占也许具有社会意义，但仍达不到临床上关于显著功能损害的要求。”

sentences.en: He argued that a new category of 'TV addiction' may not be necessary if heavy viewing stems from conditions such as depression and social phobia.
sentences.zh: 他认为，如果重度观看源于抑郁和社交恐惧这类状况，也许并不需要新设一个“电视成瘾”的类别。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, whether or not we formally diagnose someone as TV-dependent, millions of people sense that they cannot readily control the amount of television they watch.
sentences.zh: 不过，无论我们是否正式把某人诊断为电视依赖，都有数以百万计的人感到自己无法轻易控制看电视的时长。

records.title: A New Voyage Round The World

sentences.en: (A) Part travelogue, part historical record of the Caribbean pirates, part scientific treatise, A New Voyage Round the World was William Dampier’s account of his twelve-year series of journeys around the globe from 1679 to 1691.
sentences.zh: 《A New Voyage Round the World》一半是游记，一半是加勒比海盗的历史记录，同时又是一部科学论著，它是威廉·丹皮尔对自己1679年至1691年间历时十二年的环球系列航行的记述。

sentences.en: (B) The wealth and novelty of Dampier’s descriptions, combined with the highly counts of his comrades’, escapades, proved so popular with a public hungry for tales of discovery and adventure that A New Voyage went into its third reprint within a year of publication.
sentences.zh: 丹皮尔描述之丰富新奇，加上他对同伴们种种冒险经历的生动记述，深受渴求探索与冒险故事的公众喜爱，以致《A New Voyage》在出版一年之内就出到了第三次重印。

sentences.en: So groundbreaking was Dampier’s account that the writers Swift and Defoe were inspired to create two of the most famous books in the English language, Gulliver’s Travels and Robinson Crusoe.
sentences.zh: 丹皮尔的记述如此开创性，以至于作家斯威夫特和笛福受其启发，写出了英语中最著名的两部作品《格列佛游记》和《鲁滨逊漂流记》。

sentences.en: (C) Dampier’s commentators have portrayed him as an unusual, not to say peculiar, man.
sentences.zh: 评论丹皮尔的人把他描绘成一个不同寻常、甚至可以说古怪的人。

sentences.en: Notwithstanding his undoubted qualities as an observer, he has been variously characterised as aloof, arrogant, hot-tempered and a weak leader of men.
sentences.zh: 尽管他作为观察者的素质毋庸置疑，他却被人们各种各样地形容为冷淡、傲慢、脾气暴躁，而且不善带人。

sentences.en: When he arrived on the western coast of Australia, he promptly elected to leave and head north out of dislike for the cold of more southerly latitudes.
sentences.zh: 当他抵达澳大利亚西海岸时，因不喜欢更南纬度的寒冷，随即决定离开并北上。

sentences.en: This physical sensitivity has often been seized on by his detractors, who point out that, as a result, Dampier missed out on becoming the name forever associated with the European discovery of Australia, that honour instead going to Captain James Cook some 80 years later.
sentences.zh: 这种对气候的敏感常被贬低他的人抓住不放，他们指出，正因如此，丹皮尔错失了成为与欧洲发现澳大利亚永远联系在一起的那个名字，这份荣誉转而在大约80年后归于詹姆斯·库克船长。

sentences.en: Yet it should be remembered that he was able to endure a never-ending plague of discomforts and ailments in the tropics.
sentences.zh: 不过应当记住，他能够在热带忍受没完没了的种种不适与疾病。

sentences.en: And once, wrecked off Ascension Island in the South Atlantic Ocean, he managed with his crew to survive for five weeks without help, living entirely on turtles and goats.
sentences.zh: 而且有一次，在南大西洋的阿森松岛附近遭遇海难后，他和船员们在无人相助的情况下靠海龟和山羊完全维生，撑过了五个星期。

sentences.en: (D) What of his early life, then?
sentences.zh: 那么，他的早年生活又如何呢？

sentences.en: Dampier was born in 1651 in Somerset, England, the son of a tenant farmer, George, and his wife Ann.
sentences.zh: 丹皮尔1651年生于英格兰萨默塞特郡，是佃农乔治与妻子安的儿子。

sentences.en: His birthplace, Hymerford House, stands to this day.
sentences.zh: 他的出生地海默福德宅至今仍在。

sentences.en: His parents died before he reached seniority and his guardians apprenticed the young William to a ship’s captain, the boy having shown very early inclinations to see the world’.
sentences.zh: 他尚未成年，父母便已去世，监护人把年少的威廉送去给一位船长当学徒，因为这男孩很早就显露出想去见识世界的意向。

sentences.en: There was nothing in his childhood to set Dampier apart from the numerous other young boys who were sent to sea at this time.
sentences.zh: 他的童年并没有什么能把丹皮尔与当时被送去航海的众多其他男孩区分开来。

sentences.en: (E) Having made brief passages to France and Newfoundland, he completed a more extended voyage to Java, where he began to learn the art of navigation.
sentences.zh: 在短暂前往法国和纽芬兰之后，他完成了一趟更远的爪哇之行，并在那里开始学习航海术。

sentences.en: Returning briefly to Somerset, a neighbour offered Dampier a position overseeing his plantation in Jamaica, which he took up for a time, but he soon returned to sea on a trading voyage among the Caribbean islands.
sentences.zh: 短暂回到萨默塞特郡时，一位邻居请丹皮尔去牙买加照管自己的种植园，他做了一段时间，但很快又重返海上，在加勒比群岛之间从事贸易航行。

sentences.en: From the viewpoint of posterity, the most significant aspect of this time was that, as plantation manager, Dampier first started to keep a journal.
sentences.zh: 从后世的角度看，这段时期最重要的一点是，丹皮尔正是在担任种植园管理者时开始记日志的。

sentences.en: (F) Although Dampier wrote several books, A New Voyage Round the World is the most important and it is worth considering just why this text met with such success.
sentences.zh: 丹皮尔虽写过好几本书，《A New Voyage Round the World》却是最重要的一本，值得思考这部作品何以如此成功。

sentences.en: Certainly, the book would not have done so well purely on the merits of Dampier’s findings regarding meteorology and natural history, even though they broke new ground at the time.
sentences.zh: 可以肯定的是，仅凭丹皮尔在气象学和博物学方面的发现，这本书不会卖得这么好，尽管那些发现在当时确实开辟了新天地。

sentences.en: What appealed more to book buyers of this era was his narrative of life among the pirates of the Caribbean islands, whom he joined for several years after leaving Jamaica.
sentences.zh: 更吸引那个时代购书者的，是他讲述的加勒比群岛海盗生活，他离开牙买加后曾与这些海盗共处数年。

sentences.en: These tales of adventure among rogues and villains who had no regard for the law sparked widespread interest among his countrymen back home.
sentences.zh: 这些关于无视法纪的无赖与恶徒之间的冒险故事，在他国内的同胞中激起了广泛兴趣。

sentences.en: More important even than this, however, it is the superb nature of Dampier’s prose, and his ability to communicate so vividly that raised the book above the common lot.
sentences.zh: 不过，比这更重要的，是丹皮尔文笔之出色，以及他生动传达的能力，正是这一点把这本书抬升到寻常之作以上。

sentences.en: (G) Dampier himself admits in the book’s preface that he received help with the writing of the book, and other evidence exists to suggest that he was assisted by an unknown source.
sentences.zh: 丹皮尔本人在书的序言中承认，写作此书时他得到过帮助，另有证据表明他受到过某个不知名者的协助。

sentences.en: But whatever outside assistance he may have had, the book still has certain problems.
sentences.zh: 但无论他得到过怎样的外部帮助，这本书仍存在某些问题。

sentences.en: In particular, his observations about nature are sometimes roughly dropped into the narrative at very odd junctures and these asides can sometimes interrupt the flow of the story Dampier himself kept his observations about nature entirely separate from the main body of his travels, and we should therefore hold James Knapton responsible, as he was in charge of checking and revising Dampier’s text, and his publishing company brought the finished book to a wider audience.
sentences.zh: 尤其是，他对自然的观察有时被生硬地塞进叙述中极不合适的地方，这些插叙有时会打断故事的节奏 丹皮尔本人把他对自然的观察与游历正文完全分开，因此责任应归于詹姆斯·纳普顿，因为是他负责核查和修订丹皮尔的文稿，而他的出版公司又把成书带给了更广泛的读者。

sentences.en: (H) Dampier’s life has been chronicled in full by numerous biographers, and I refer the reader in particular to Clennell Wilkinson’s excellent (and sadly out-of- print) 1929 biography, as well as the recent portrait by Anton Gill.
sentences.zh: 丹皮尔的一生已被众多传记作者完整记述，我特别推荐读者参看克伦内尔·威尔金森1929年那本出色的传记（遗憾的是已绝版），以及安东·吉尔近期所作的评传。

sentences.en: In short, despite wide acclaim for his writing, Dampier was not blessed in the art of wealth accumulation Travelling with the pirates, while providing subsistence and adventure, never netted him the treasure chest that a more astute financial operative might have acquired.
sentences.zh: 简言之，尽管他的写作广受赞誉，丹皮尔却不擅长积累财富 与海盗同行虽带来了生计与冒险，却从未为他挣得一个更精明的理财者本可获得的宝箱。

sentences.en: He died in 1715, aged sixty-three, in Colerman Street, London.
sentences.zh: 他于1715年去世，享年六十三岁，卒于伦敦科尔曼街。

sentences.en: (I) We have then a man of myriad and colourful parts, and perhaps not always the easiest of sailors to get along with because of his arrogance and hot temper.
sentences.zh: 于是我们看到的是一个多面而多彩的人，也许由于傲慢和暴躁的脾气，他并不总是最好相处的水手。

sentences.en: But to dwell on these aspects today is to miss the point: it is A New Voyage Round the World that should provide the most illuminating and entertaining of Dampier’s legacies.
sentences.zh: 但今天若只盯着这些方面，便是没抓住要点：真正应当带来最富启发也最有趣味的丹皮尔遗产的，是《A New Voyage Round the World》。

sentences.en: Above all, the text is studded with some wonderfully colourful expressions, and readers will enjoy some of the finest descriptions of storms in the English language, and the liberal wit throughout.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，这部作品中点缀着一些绝妙生动的表达，读者会读到英语中对风暴最精彩的一些描写，以及全书中挥洒自如的机智。

sentences.zh: 不过，巧克力曾被视为价值非凡的商品，这也许会让人吃惊。

sentences.en: The discovery of the cocoa tree, the source of chocolate, occurred approximately 2,000 years ago in the lush tropical rainforests of the Americas.
sentences.zh: 可可树也就是巧克力的来源，大约在2000年前被发现于美洲茂密的热带雨林中。

sentences.en: The evolution of chocolate -- from a regionally significant Mesoamerican drink to globally consumed confectionery -- has been shaped through cross-continental cultural exchanges and the successive influences of multiple civilisations.
sentences.zh: 巧克力的演变——从一种在中美洲具有地区意义的饮品，变为全球消费的糖果——是由跨大陆的文化交流以及多个文明的先后影响所塑造的。

sentences.en: B Historians suggest that the ancient Maya pioneered cocoa tree cultivation in Mesoamerica, with evidence dating back approximately 2,000 years.
sentences.zh: 历史学家认为，古代玛雅人最早在中美洲开创了可可树的栽培，证据可追溯到大约2000年前。

sentences.en: They transplanted cocoa trees from the dense rainforest into their domesticated gardens, where cocoa beans were initially roasted and ground into a smooth paste.
sentences.zh: 他们把可可树从茂密的雨林移植到自家园圃中，最初把可可豆烘焙后磨成细腻的糊状。

sentences.en: The paste was combined with spices and water to produce unsweetened chocolate beverages.
sentences.zh: 这种糊状物再与香料和水调和，制成不加糖的巧克力饮品。

sentences.en: The Maya also employed a distinctive technique of transferring the liquid back and forth between containers, generating a foamy layer on the drink’s surface.
sentences.zh: 玛雅人还采用一种独特手法，把液体在容器之间来回倾倒，从而在饮品表面生成一层泡沫。

sentences.en: C Cocoa and chocolate were integral to Maya culture, commonly depicted in their architectural structures and artistic works.
sentences.zh: 可可与巧克力是玛雅文化不可或缺的部分，常出现在他们的建筑构造和艺术作品中。

sentences.en: While the aristocracy, particularly the royal families, consumed chocolate during elaborate ceremonies, even less privileged groups occasionally savoured the drink.
sentences.zh: 贵族尤其是王室成员会在隆重的仪式上饮用巧克力，而地位较低的群体偶尔也能品尝这种饮品。

sentences.en: Furthermore, cocoa beans served as a powerful emblem of marital union and were ritually exchanged during wedding ceremonies.
sentences.zh: 此外，可可豆是婚姻结合的有力象征，会在婚礼仪式上作为礼节相互赠送。

sentences.en: D The Aztec civilisation in Mexico regarded chocolate as a prestigious commodity, despite being geographically unable to cultivate cocoa trees within their heartland.
sentences.zh: 墨西哥的阿兹特克文明把巧克力视为一种尊贵的商品，尽管其核心地带在地理上无法种植可可树。

sentences.en: Accordingly, they sourced cocoa beans through extensive trade networks, even utilising them as currency for tax payments.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们通过庞大的贸易网络获取可可豆，甚至把可可豆用作缴税的货币。

sentences.en: Chocolate held an exclusive function within Aztec imperial and religious ceremonies, where priests offered cocoa beans as divine offerings and prepared sacred chocolate drinks.
sentences.zh: 巧克力在阿兹特克的帝国典礼和宗教仪式中具有专属功能，祭司会把可可豆当作献给神灵的祭品，并调制神圣的巧克力饮品。

sentences.en: Due to the scarcity of cocoa beans, consumption remained restricted to the societal elite, with historical accounts suggesting Emperor Montezuma consumed up to 50 cups daily.
sentences.zh: 由于可可豆稀缺，饮用一直限于社会上层，史料记载蒙特祖马皇帝每天最多饮用50杯。

sentences.en: Linguists trace the term "chocolate" to the Aztec Nahuatl word xocolatl, meaning "bitter water" in the Nahuatl language, though some scholars argue that it has hybrid origins combining Maya and Nahuatl linguistic elements.
sentences.zh: 语言学家把“chocolate”一词追溯到阿兹特克纳瓦特尔语的 xocolatl，在纳瓦特尔语中意为“苦水”，不过也有学者认为该词源头混合，兼具玛雅语和纳瓦特尔语的成分。

sentences.en: E In 1502, explorer Christopher Columbus introduced cocoa beans to Spain after voyaging to Mesoamerica, and later Spanish explorer Hernán Cortés quickly recognised the potential economic value of chocolate.
sentences.zh: 1502年，探险家克里斯托弗·哥伦布在航行至中美洲后把可可豆带回西班牙，后来西班牙探险家埃尔南·科尔特斯很快意识到巧克力潜在的经济价值。

sentences.en: Upon arriving in present-day Mexico in 1519, Cortés observed that chocolate beverages would appeal to the Spanish.
sentences.zh: 1519年抵达今天的墨西哥后，科尔特斯察觉到巧克力饮品会受西班牙人喜爱。

sentences.en: After conquering the Aztec Empire, Spanish forces exported confiscated cocoa supplies to Spain.
sentences.zh: 征服阿兹特克帝国之后，西班牙军队把没收的可可存货运回西班牙。

sentences.en: In response to the growing demand, Spain began cultivating cocoa trees in its American colonies.
sentences.zh: 为回应不断增长的需求，西班牙开始在其美洲殖民地种植可可树。

sentences.en: Spanish elites first developed a taste for sweetened chocolate drinks, but the beverage rapidly spread across Europe.
sentences.zh: 西班牙上层最先喜欢上加糖的巧克力饮品，但这种饮品迅速传遍欧洲。

sentences.en: England, the Netherlands, and France followed suit by establishing cocoa plantations in their own colonies.
sentences.zh: 英格兰、荷兰和法国也纷纷效仿，在各自的殖民地建起可可种植园。

sentences.en: By the 18th century, chocolate remained primarily a luxury restricted to the affluent.
sentences.zh: 到18世纪，巧克力主要仍是限于富人的奢侈品。

sentences.en: However, the Industrial Revolution’s technologies enabled mechanised production, dramatically reducing costs and making chocolate available to a broader population.
sentences.zh: 然而，工业革命的技术使机械化生产成为可能，成本大幅下降，巧克力得以进入更广大人群。

sentences.en: F Cocoa trees are cultivated across multiple countries in Africa, Mesoamerica, and South America, thriving in cool, shaded environments within equatorial zones.
sentences.zh: 可可树种植遍及非洲、中美洲和南美洲的多个国家，它们在赤道地带凉爽而有遮荫的环境中长势良好。

sentences.en: Despite widespread cultivation, cocoa farming remains labour-intensive, due to the trees’ requirement for specific water thresholds, temperature ranges, soil compositions, and protection from environmental threats.
sentences.zh: 尽管种植广泛，可可农事仍是劳动密集型的，因为这种树对水量阈值、温度范围、土壤成分都有特定要求，还需防范环境威胁。

sentences.en: Approximately five years after planting, cocoa trees begin to yield large, pod-shaped fruits that grow on the trunk.
sentences.zh: 种下约五年后，可可树开始结出长在树干上的荚形大果实。

sentences.en: These pods contain the beans used in chocolate production.
sentences.zh: 这些果荚里装着用于生产巧克力的豆子。

sentences.en: While several types of cocoa trees exist, the bulk of the chocolate is produced from the seeds of the most commonly cultivated varieties.
sentences.zh: 可可树虽有若干类型，大部分巧克力却是用最常栽培的那些品种的种子制成的。

sentences.en: However, farmers opt to grow more specialised types, such as Criollo or Trinitario, valued for distinctive flavour profiles.
sentences.zh: 不过，也有农户选择种植更为专门的品种，比如因风味特征鲜明而受重视的 Criollo 或 Trinitario。

sentences.en: Unexpectedly, cocoa trees grown on farms are more vulnerable to disease and pests than their wild counterparts.
sentences.zh: 出人意料的是，农场里种植的可可树比野生同类更易受病害和虫害侵袭。

sentences.en: Cocoa cultivation presents a strenuous endeavour for farmers, who sell their harvests on futures markets, exposing their incomes to external market fluctuations.
sentences.zh: 对农户而言，可可种植是一项艰辛的营生，他们在期货市场上出售收成，收入因而暴露在外部市场波动之下。

sentences.en: G The process of chocolate production involves a series of steps, carried out in specialised factories where cocoa beans are meticulously processed.
sentences.zh: 巧克力的生产过程包含一系列工序，在专门的工厂里对可可豆进行精细加工。

sentences.en: Workers first sort, clean, and roast the beans before extracting the outer shells, leaving only the inner nibs.
sentences.zh: 工人先把豆子分选、清洗、烘焙，再剥去外壳，只留下内部的可可碎粒。

sentences.en: These nibs are then ground into a dense paste known as chocolate liquor, which is subsequently separated into two components: cocoa solids and cocoa butter.
sentences.zh: 这些碎粒随后被磨成一种浓稠的糊状物，称为可可液块，接着再分离为两种成分：可可固形物和可可脂。

sentences.en: Following standardised formulations, chocolate manufacturers blend the chocolate liquor with precise ratios of sugar, milk, and cocoa butter.
sentences.zh: 巧克力制造商按标准化配方，把可可液块与糖、奶和可可脂按精确比例调和。

sentences.en: The resulting mixture, often referred to as the "crumb", undergoes fine grinding to create a smooth consistency.
sentences.zh: 所得的混合料常被称作“crumb”，需经细磨才能达到顺滑的质地。

sentences.en: Finally, the mixture is then subjected to two additional processes -- conching and tempering -- before being placed into moulds to create various forms, such as bars or other chocolate products.
sentences.zh: 最后，这种混合料还要经过两道额外工序——精炼和调温——然后被注入模具，制成条状等各种形态的巧克力产品。

sentences.en: H Chocolate holds significant global economic value, with the manufacturing industry generating over $5 billion annually from cocoa crops, and its reputation remains most prominent in Europe and the United States.
sentences.zh: 巧克力具有可观的全球经济价值，制造业每年从可可作物上创造超过50亿美元的产值，而其声誉在欧洲和美国最为突出。

sentences.en: For instance, US cocoa product imports reached $1.4 billion in 2005.
sentences.zh: 例如，2005年美国的可可制品进口额达到14亿美元。

sentences.en: On average, Americans consume over five kilogrammes of chocolate per person each year.
sentences.zh: 美国人平均每人每年消费超过五公斤巧克力。

sentences.en: In addition, upscale chocolate boutiques, which offer premium chocolates, have gained significant popularity.
sentences.zh: 此外，供应高端巧克力的精品巧克力店也大受欢迎。

sentences.en: Many of these shops specialise in artisanal chocolates, crafted with unique flavour profiles.
sentences.zh: 其中许多店专营手工巧克力，风味特征独一无二。

sentences.en: Renowned chocolate brands such as Cadbury, Godiva, Lindt, and Ferrero Rocher dominate the market.
sentences.zh: 吉百利、歌帝梵、瑞士莲和费列罗等知名巧克力品牌主导着市场。

sentences.en: However, the cocoa and chocolate production sectors often face challenges related to fair trade, sustainable development, and environmental preservation.
sentences.zh: 不过，可可与巧克力生产部门常常面临与公平贸易、可持续发展和环境保护相关的挑战。

sentences.en: These issues are now being actively addressed by industry stakeholders, including officials, activists, and researchers, who are working closely with farmers to promote farming practices that foster sustainability and protect the environment.
sentences.zh: 这些问题如今正由包括官员、活动人士和研究者在内的行业相关方积极应对，他们与农户密切合作，推广既促进可持续性又保护环境的耕作方式。
