sentences.en: A Violins made by long-dead Italian craftsmen from the Cremona region are beautiful works of art, coveted by collectors as well as players.
sentences.zh: 克雷莫纳地区早已作古的意大利工匠所制的小提琴是精美的艺术品，收藏家和演奏者都极为渴求。

sentences.en: Particularly outstanding violins have reputedly changed hands for over a million pounds.
sentences.zh: 据说特别出色的小提琴曾以超过一百万英镑的价格易手。

sentences.en: In contrast, fine modern instruments can be bought for under £100.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，优良的现代乐器不到 100 英镑就能买到。

sentences.en: Do such figures really reflect such large differences in quality?
sentences.zh: 这样的价格差距真能反映如此巨大的品质差异吗？

sentences.en: After more than a hundred years of vigorous debate, this question remains highly contentious, provoking strongly held but divergent views among musicians, violin makers and scientists alike.
sentences.zh: 经过一百多年的激烈争论，这个问题依然极具争议，在音乐家、制琴师和科学家中都激起了立场坚定却彼此分歧的看法。

sentences.en: B Every violin, whether a Stradivarius or the cheapest factory- made copy, has a distinctive ‘voice’ of its 0.
sentences.zh: 每一把小提琴，无论是斯特拉迪瓦里琴还是最廉价的工厂仿制品，都有自己独特的“嗓音”。

sentences.en: Just as any musician can immediately recognise the difference between Domingo and Pavarotti singing the same operatic aria, so a skilled violinist can distinguish between different qualities in the sound produced by individual Stradivari or Guarneri violins.
sentences.zh: 正如任何音乐家都能立刻分辨多明戈与帕瓦罗蒂演唱同一段歌剧咏叹调的差别，熟练的小提琴手也能分辨不同斯特拉迪瓦里琴或瓜尔内里琴所发出声音在品质上的差异。

sentences.en: Individual notes on a single instrument sound different each time they are played, which suggests that the perceived tone of a violin must be related to the overall design of the instrument, rather than the frequencies of particular resonances on it.
sentences.zh: 同一把琴上的单个音符每次演奏听起来都不一样，这表明人们所感知的小提琴音色必定与乐器的整体设计有关，而非与琴上某些特定共振的频率有关。

sentences.en: But although various attempts have been made to analyse such global properties, it is extremely difficult to distinguish between a fine Stradivarius instrument and an indifferent modern copy on the basis of the measured response alone.
sentences.zh: 但尽管人们多次尝试分析这类整体属性，仅凭实测响应仍极难区分一把上乘的斯特拉迪瓦里琴与一把平庸的现代仿制品。

sentences.en: The ear is a supreme detection device, and a system has yet to be developed which can match the brain’s sophisticated ability to assess complex sounds.
sentences.zh: 耳朵是极其出色的检测装置，而能够比肩大脑评估复杂声音那种精妙能力的系统，至今尚未问世。

sentences.en: C So how do skilled violinmakers optimise the tone of an instrument during the construction process?
sentences.zh: 那么，熟练的制琴师是如何在制作过程中优化一把琴的音色的呢？

sentences.en: They begin by selecting a wood of the highest possible quality for the front and back plates (or parts of the violin), which they test by tapping with a hammer and judging how well it ‘rings’.
sentences.zh: 他们首先为面板和背板（即小提琴的部件）挑选品质尽可能高的木材，并用锤子敲击、判断其“共鸣”好坏来加以检验。

sentences.en: The next important step is to skillfully carve the plates out of the solid wood, taking great care to get the right degree of arching and variations in thickness.
sentences.zh: 下一个重要步骤是从整块木料中娴熟地雕出琴板，格外小心地做出恰当的拱度和厚度变化。

sentences.en: Traditional makers optimise the thickness by testing the ‘feel’ of the plates when they are flexed, and by the sounds produced when they are tapped at different positions with the knuckles.
sentences.zh: 传统制琴师通过弯折琴板时的“手感”，以及用指节在不同位置敲击时发出的声音，来优化厚度。

sentences.en: D However, in the last 50 years or so a group of violin makers has emerged who have tried to take a more overtly scientific approach to violin making.
sentences.zh: 不过，在过去 50 年左右，出现了一批试图以更明确的科学方法制琴的制琴师。

sentences.en: One common practice they have adopted is to replace the traditional flexing and tapping of plates by controlled measurements.
sentences.zh: 他们采用的一种常见做法，是用可控测量取代传统的弯折与敲击琴板。

sentences.en: During the carving process, the thinned plates are sprinkled with flakes of glitter and suspended horizontally above a loudspeaker.
sentences.zh: 在雕削过程中，把削薄的琴板撒上闪粉，水平悬挂在一只扬声器上方。

sentences.en: The glitter forms a pattern each time the loudspeaker excites a resonance.
sentences.zh: 每当扬声器激发出一个共振，闪粉就会形成一种图案。

sentences.en: The aim is to interactively ‘tune’ these first few free plate resonances to specified patterns.
sentences.zh: 目的是以交互方式把最初这几个自由琴板共振“调”成指定的图案。

sentences.en: E Unfortunately, there are very few examples of such measurements for really fine Italian instruments because their owners are naturally reluctant to allow their violins to be taken apart for the sake of science.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，针对真正上乘的意大利乐器，这类测量的实例极少，因为其主人自然不愿为了科学而让自己的琴被拆开。

sentences.en: The few tests that have been performed suggest that the first Italian makers may have tuned the resonant modes of the individual plates – which they could identify as they tapped them – to exact musical intervals.
sentences.zh: 少数已完成的测试表明，最早的意大利制琴师可能把各块琴板的共振模式——他们敲击时便能辨识——调到了精确的音程上。

sentences.en: This would be consistent with the prevailing Renaissance view of ’perfection1, which was measured in terms of numbers and exact ratios.
sentences.zh: 这与文艺复兴时期以数字和精确比例来衡量“完美”的主流观念是一致的。

sentences.en: However, there is no historical data to support this case.
sentences.zh: 然而，并没有历史数据支持这一说法。

sentences.en: F Another factor that affects sound quality is the presence of moisture.
sentences.zh: 影响音质的另一个因素是湿气的存在。

sentences.en: To achieve the quality of “vibrancy” in a violin requires high-quality wood with low internal damping.
sentences.zh: 要让一把小提琴具备“鲜活感”那样的品质，需要内部阻尼低的优质木材。

sentences.en: By measuring the pattern of growth-rings in the wood of a Stradivarius, we know that the Italian violin makers sometimes used planks of wood that had only been seasoned for five years.
sentences.zh: 通过测量一把斯特拉迪瓦里琴木材中的年轮图样，我们知道意大利制琴师有时使用只自然干燥了五年的木板。

sentences.en: However, such wood is now 300 years old, and the intrinsic internal damping will almost certainly have decreased with time.
sentences.zh: 然而，这些木材如今已有 300 年之久，其固有的内部阻尼几乎肯定已随时间下降。

sentences.en: The age of the wood may therefore automatically contribute to the improved quality of older instruments.
sentences.zh: 因此，木材的年岁本身可能就有助于提升较老乐器的品质。

sentences.en: This may also explain why the quality of a modern instrument appears to improve in its first few years.
sentences.zh: 这或许也解释了为什么一件现代乐器的品质在最初几年里似乎会有所改善。

sentences.en: G Another factor thought to account for sound quality is the nature of the varnish used to protect the instrument.
sentences.zh: 另一个被认为能解释音质的因素，是用于保护乐器的清漆的性质。

sentences.en: One of the most popular theories for well over a century to account for the Stradivarius secret has been that the varnish had some sort of ‘magic’ composition.
sentences.zh: 一个多世纪以来，用来解释斯特拉迪瓦里之谜最流行的理论之一，是那种清漆有某种“神奇”的配方。

sentences.en: However, historical research has shown that it was very similar to the varnish used today.
sentences.zh: 然而历史研究表明，它与今天所用的清漆非常相似。

sentences.en: So apart from the possibility that the Italian varnish was contaminated with the wings of passing insects and debris from the workshop floor, there is no convincing evidence to support the idea of a secret formula.
sentences.zh: 因此，除了意大利清漆可能混入过路昆虫的翅膀和作坊地面碎屑这种可能性之外，并没有令人信服的证据支持存在秘密配方的说法。

sentences.en: H Other researchers, meanwhile, have claimed that Stradivarius’s secret was to soak the timber in water, to leach out supposedly harmful chemicals, before it was seasoned.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，另一些研究者声称，斯特拉迪瓦里的秘诀是在木材自然干燥之前先把它浸在水里，以浸出据称有害的化学物质。

sentences.en: Although this would be consistent with the idea that the masts and cars of recently sunken Venetian war galleys might have been used to make violins, other scientific and historical evidence to support this view is unconvincing.
sentences.zh: 尽管这与近期沉没的威尼斯战船的桅杆和桨可能被用来制琴的说法相符，支持该观点的其他科学与历史证据却并不令人信服。

sentences.en: I In conclusion, science has not provided any convincing evidence to set Cremonese instruments apart from the finest violins made by skilled craftsmen today.
sentences.zh: 总之，科学并未提供任何令人信服的证据，能把克雷莫纳乐器与当今熟练工匠所制的最优秀小提琴区分开来。

sentences.en: Indeed, some leading soloists do occasionally play on modern instruments.
sentences.zh: 事实上，一些顶尖独奏家偶尔确实会使用现代乐器。

sentences.en: However, the foremost soloists – and, not surprisingly, violin dealers, who have a vested interest in maintaining the Cremonese legend of intrinsic superiority – remain utterly unconvinced.
sentences.zh: 然而，最杰出的独奏家——以及毫不意外地，那些在维护克雷莫纳琴天生优越这一传说上有既得利益的琴商——仍然完全不为所动。

sentences.en: (A) O’ Connell-Rodwell, a post-doctoral fellow at Stanford University, has traveled to Namibia’s first-ever wildlife reserve to explore the mystical and complicated realm of elephant communication.
sentences.zh: 斯坦福大学博士后研究员奥康奈尔-罗德韦尔前往纳米比亚有史以来第一座野生动物保护区，探索大象交流那个神秘而复杂的领域。

sentences.en: She, along with her colleagues, is part of a scientific revolution that started almost 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 她和同事们参与的这场科学革命，始于将近 20 年前。

sentences.en: This revolution has made a stunning revelation: elephants are capable of communicating with one another over long distances by means of low-frequency sounds, also known as infrasound, which are too deep for humans to hear.
sentences.zh: 这场革命带来一个惊人的发现：大象能够借助低频声波即次声，在远距离上彼此交流，而这种声音低沉到人类无法听见。

sentences.en: (B) As might be expected, African elephants’ ability to detect seismic sound may have something to do with their ears.
sentences.zh: 不出所料，非洲象探测地震波声音的能力可能与它们的耳朵有关。

sentences.en: The hammer bone in an elephant’s inner ear is proportionally huge for a mammal, but it is normal for animals that use vibrational signals.
sentences.zh: 大象内耳中的锤骨，按哺乳动物的比例来说异常巨大，但对使用振动信号的动物而言这很正常。

sentences.en: Thus, it may be a sign that elephants can use seismic sounds to communicate.
sentences.zh: 因此，这可能表明大象能够利用地震波声音进行交流。

sentences.en: (C) Other aspects of elephant anatomy also support this ability.
sentences.zh: 大象解剖结构的其他方面也支持这种能力。

sentences.en: First, their massive bodies, which enable them to give out low-frequency sounds almost as powerful as the sound a jet makes during take-off, serve as ideal frames for receiving ground vibrations and transmitting them to the inner ear.
sentences.zh: 首先，它们庞大的身躯使其能发出几乎与喷气机起飞时一样强劲的低频声，同时也是接收地面振动并将其传入内耳的理想骨架。

sentences.en: Second, the elephant’s toe bones are set in a fatty pad, which might help focus vibrations from the ground into the bone.
sentences.zh: 其次，大象的趾骨嵌在一块脂肪垫中，这或许有助于把来自地面的振动汇聚到骨骼里。

sentences.en: Finally, the elephant has an enormous brain that sits in the cranial cavity behind the eyes, in line with the auditory canal.
sentences.zh: 最后，大象拥有硕大的脑，位于双眼后方的颅腔内，与听道处在同一条线上。

sentences.en: The front of the skull is riddled with sinus cavities, which might function as resonating chambers for ground vibrations.
sentences.zh: 颅骨前部布满窦腔，它们可能充当地面振动的共鸣室。

sentences.en: (D) It remains unclear how elephants detect such vibrations, but O’ Connell-Rodwell suggests that the pachyderms are ‘listening’ with their trunks and feet instead of (or in addition to) their ears.
sentences.zh: 大象究竟如何探测这类振动仍不清楚，但奥康奈尔-罗德韦尔认为，这些厚皮动物是在用鼻子和脚“听”，而不是（或者说不只是）用耳朵。

sentences.en: The elephant trunk may be the most versatile appendage in nature: it is used for drinking, bathing, smelling, feeding and scratching.
sentences.zh: 象鼻可能是自然界中用途最广的附肢：它可用于饮水、洗澡、嗅闻、进食和抓挠。

sentences.en: Both trunk and feet contain two types of nerve endings that are sensitive to pressure—one detects infrasonic vibration and the other responds to vibrations of slightly higher frequencies.
sentences.zh: 象鼻和脚都含有两类对压力敏感的神经末梢——一类探测次声振动，另一类则对频率略高的振动作出反应。

sentences.en: As O’ Connell-Rodwell sees it, this research has a boundless and unpredictable future.
sentences.zh: 在奥康奈尔-罗德韦尔看来，这项研究有着无限且难以预料的前景。

sentences.en: ‘Our work is really at the interface of geophysics, neurophysiology and ecology,’ she says.
sentences.zh: “我们的工作真正处在地球物理学、神经生理学和生态学的交界处，”她说。

sentences.en: ‘We’re raising questions that have never even been considered before.’
sentences.zh: “我们提出的这些问题，此前甚至无人考虑过。”

sentences.en: (E) Scientists have long known that seismic communication is widespread among small animals such as spiders, scorpions, insects and many vertebrates, including white-lipped frogs, blind mole-rats, kangaroo rats and golden moles.
sentences.zh: 科学家早就知道，地震波交流在蜘蛛、蝎子、昆虫以及包括白唇蛙、盲鼹鼠、更格卢鼠和金毛鼹在内的许多脊椎动物等小型动物中十分普遍。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, O’ Connell-Rodwell was the first to argue that a giant land animal is also sending and receiving seismic signals.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，奥康奈尔-罗德韦尔仍是第一个提出巨型陆生动物也在发送和接收地震波信号的人。

sentences.en: ‘I used to lay a male planthopper on a stem and replay the calling sound of a female; the male would exhibit the same kind of behaviour that happens in elephants: he would freeze, press down on his legs, move forward a little, then stay still again.
sentences.zh: “我过去常把一只雄性飞虱放在茎秆上，再播放雌虫的求偶声；这只雄虫会表现出与大象身上相同的那类行为：它会僵住，用腿向下压，向前挪一点，然后再次静止不动。

sentences.en: I found it fascinating, and it made me think that perhaps auditory communication is not the only thing going on.’
sentences.zh: 我觉得这非常迷人，也让我想到，或许发生的并不只是听觉交流。”

sentences.en: (F) Scientists have confirmed that an elephant’s capacity to communicate over long distances is essential for survival, especially in places like Etosha, where more than 2,400 savanna elephants range over an area larger than New Jersey.
sentences.zh: 科学家已经确认，大象远距离交流的能力对生存至关重要，在埃托沙这样的地方尤其如此——那里有 2400 多头草原象，活动范围比新泽西州还大。

sentences.en: It is already difficult for an elephant to find a mate in such a vast wilderness, and elephant reproductive biology only complicates matters.
sentences.zh: 在如此辽阔的荒野中，大象本就难以找到配偶，而大象的生殖生物学特性更让事情复杂。

sentences.en: Breeding herds also adopt low-frequency sounds to warn of predators.
sentences.zh: 繁殖象群还会用低频声来预警捕食者。

sentences.en: Even though adult elephants have no enemies other than human beings, calves are vulnerable and susceptible to attacks from lions and hyenas.
sentences.zh: 尽管成年大象除人类之外没有天敌，幼象却很脆弱，容易受到狮子和鬣狗的攻击。

sentences.en: At the sight of a predator, older herd members clump together to protect the young before running away.
sentences.zh: 一看到捕食者，年长的象群成员就会聚拢起来保护幼象，然后再逃走。

sentences.en: (G) We now know that elephants can respond to warning calls in the air, but can they detect signals transmitted solely through the ground?
sentences.zh: 我们现在知道大象能对空气中传播的警报声作出反应，但它们能否探测到仅通过地面传播的信号呢？

sentences.en: To investigate, the research team designed an experiment in 2002 that used electronic devices to send signals through the ground at Mushara.
sentences.zh: 为了探究这一点，研究团队于 2002 年设计了一项实验，使用电子设备在穆沙拉把信号送入地下。

sentences.en: ‘The outcomes of our 2002 study revealed that elephants could indeed sense warning signals through the ground,’ O’ Connell-Rodwell observes.
sentences.zh: “我们 2002 年研究的结果显示，大象确实能够通过地面感知警报信号，”奥康奈尔-罗德韦尔评述道。

sentences.en: (H) Last year, an experiment was set up to pursue the problem further.
sentences.zh: 去年，又设立了一项实验来进一步追查这个问题。

sentences.en: It used three different recordings: the 1994 warning call from Mushara, an anti-predator call recorded by scientist Joyce Poole in Kenya, and a made-up warble tone.
sentences.zh: 实验使用了三段不同的录音：1994 年来自穆沙拉的警报声、科学家乔伊斯·普尔在肯尼亚录下的一段防捕食者叫声，以及一段人工合成的颤音。

sentences.en: ‘The data I’ve observed so far imply that the elephants responded exactly as I expected.
sentences.zh: “我目前观察到的数据表明，大象的反应与我的预期完全一致。

sentences.en: However, the fascinating finding is that the anti-predator call from Kenya—unfamiliar to them—caused them to gather, tense up and rumble aggressively as well; but they didn’t always flee.
sentences.zh: 不过，最引人入胜的发现是：那段来自肯尼亚、它们并不熟悉的防捕食者叫声，同样让它们聚拢、紧绷并发出具有攻击性的低沉隆隆声；但它们并不总是逃走。

sentences.en: I didn’t expect the results to be that clear-cut.’
sentences.zh: 我没有料到结果会如此明确。”

sentences.en: A Many plants emit a smell.
sentences.zh: 许多植物会散发气味。

sentences.en: This may come from the flower of the plant, from the leaves, stem, or even, in some cases, from the root.
sentences.zh: 这种气味可能来自植物的花，来自叶、茎，某些情况下甚至来自根。

sentences.en: What humans may perceive as a fragrant perfume is actually a tool used by plants to entice pollinators, discourage bacteria, or fend off predators.
sentences.zh: 人类可能感知为芬芳香气的东西，实际上是植物用来引诱传粉者、抑制细菌或抵御捕食者的工具。

sentences.en: Fragrances consist of small organic particles with high vapor pressures, so that a scent compound evaporates easily if exposed to the air; chemicals which evaporate in this way are described as ‘volatile compounds’.
sentences.zh: 香气由蒸气压高的有机小颗粒构成，因此香味化合物一旦暴露在空气中就很容易挥发；以这种方式挥发的化学物质被称为“挥发性化合物”。

sentences.en: B Although we generally think of plant odors as pleasant, many volatile compounds in plants are toxic when eaten.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们通常认为植物气味令人愉悦，植物中许多挥发性化合物食用后却是有毒的。

sentences.en: These compounds are used by plants to protect themselves from bacterial attack.
sentences.zh: 植物用这些化合物保护自己免受细菌侵袭。

sentences.en: Humans have recognized and taken advantage of these plant-derived antibacterials since antiquity, when they were used to slow the spoilage of food.
sentences.zh: 自古以来，人类就认识并利用了这些源自植物的抗菌物质，当时用它们来延缓食物腐败。

sentences.en: For example, the spice clove could be used in baked goods and prepared meats to slow the growth of mould and bacteria, because a small amount was not dangerous to humans.
sentences.zh: 例如，丁香这种香料可用于烘焙食品和加工肉类以延缓霉菌和细菌生长，因为少量食用对人无害。

sentences.en: Before the development of modern food preservation techniques, European civilization was heavily dependent on cloves and other tropical spices to ensure a long-lasting supply of food.
sentences.zh: 在现代食品保存技术出现之前，欧洲文明严重依赖丁香和其他热带香料来确保长期的食物供应。

sentences.en: However, the long distance from Europe to South-east Asia made these spices extremely expensive and was part of the motivation behind the search for a shorter route to Asia, which resulted in the discovery of the Americas.
sentences.zh: 然而，从欧洲到东南亚路途遥远，使这些香料极其昂贵，这也是人们寻找通往亚洲更短航路的部分动因，并最终促成了美洲的发现。

sentences.en: C Although volatile compounds in plants probably originally evolved to repel herbivorous (plant-eating) animals of all kinds, they now perform a remarkable range of functions.
sentences.zh: 尽管植物中的挥发性化合物最初演化出来很可能是为了驱避各类食草（以植物为食）动物，它们如今却承担着范围惊人的多种功能。

sentences.en: An important one common to many plants is to attract animals which will spread that plant’s pollen.
sentences.zh: 其中一项许多植物共有的重要功能，是吸引那些能替该植物传播花粉的动物。

sentences.en: Insects are the most common animals to interact with plants in this way, and most insects detect volatile compounds through the extremely sensitive antennae on their heads.
sentences.zh: 以这种方式与植物互动的动物中最常见的是昆虫，而多数昆虫通过头部极其灵敏的触角来探测挥发性化合物。

sentences.en: Some antennae can detect an airborne volatile compound at concentrations of just a few parts per billion.
sentences.zh: 有些触角能在仅十亿分之几的浓度下探测到空气中的挥发性化合物。

sentences.en: D Other plants emit volatile compounds which function as toxins against invading insects, and still others emit such compounds when they have been injured, in order to deter insects from laying eggs on them and thus injuring them further.
sentences.zh: 另一些植物释放的挥发性化合物可作为毒素对付入侵昆虫，还有一些植物在受伤时释放这类化合物，以阻止昆虫在其上产卵而造成进一步伤害。

sentences.en: Volatile compounds released by plants in response to herbivore egg-laying, for example, can attract parasites of the eggs, thereby preventing them from hatching.
sentences.zh: 例如，植物为应对食草动物产卵而释放的挥发性化合物，能够吸引这些卵的寄生者，从而阻止卵孵化。

sentences.en: In this way the plant can avoid the attack of the hungry young herbivores that would have emerged from the eggs.
sentences.zh: 植物由此得以避开那些本会从卵中孵出的饥饿幼虫的侵害。

sentences.en: E Volatile compounds in plants can also be used as a kind of currency in some very indirect defensive systems.
sentences.zh: 在某些非常间接的防御体系中，植物的挥发性化合物还能充当一种通货。

sentences.en: In the rainforest tree Leonardoxa africana, for example, ants of the species Petalomyrmex phylax are attracted to young leaves because they emit high levels of the volatile compound methyl salicylate, a substance that ants need to use as an antiseptic in their nests; coincidentally, the ants attack any herbivorous insects that they encounter.
sentences.zh: 例如，在雨林树种 Leonardoxa africana 上，Petalomyrmex phylax 蚂蚁被幼叶所吸引，因为幼叶大量释放挥发性化合物水杨酸甲酯，而蚂蚁需要用这种物质作巢中的抗菌剂；碰巧的是，这些蚂蚁会攻击遇到的任何食草昆虫。

sentences.en: It appears that methyl salicylate both attracts ants and rewards them for performing their valuable role in deterring herbivores.
sentences.zh: 看来水杨酸甲酯既吸引蚂蚁，也犒赏它们在阻遏食草动物方面所发挥的宝贵作用。

sentences.en: The web of interactions among plants and animals can become so complicated that it is difficult to detect what the outcome of the release of volatile compounds is.
sentences.zh: 植物与动物之间的互动之网可能变得极其复杂，以至于难以判断释放挥发性化合物究竟带来了什么结果。

sentences.en: But it is clear that the system can have a defensive purpose, as many experiments have shown that the deactivation of a plant’s volatile emission system makes it more vulnerable to herbivores.
sentences.zh: 但可以肯定的是，这一体系可以有防御目的，因为许多实验表明，让植物的挥发物释放系统失效会使其更易受食草动物侵害。

sentences.en: F Floral scent has a strong impact on the economic success of many agricultural crops that rely on insect pollinators, including fruit trees such as the bee-pollinated cherry, apple, apricot, and peach, as well as vegetables and tropical plants such as the papaya.
sentences.zh: 花香对许多依赖昆虫传粉的农作物的经济效益影响巨大，其中包括樱桃、苹果、杏和桃等靠蜜蜂传粉的果树，也包括番木瓜等蔬菜和热带植物。

sentences.en: A decrease in fragrance emission, due to crossbreeding for fruit size or other characteristics, reduces the ability of plants to attract pollinators and may result in considerable losses for growers.
sentences.zh: 为了果实大小或其他性状而进行杂交育种导致香气释放减少，削弱了植物吸引传粉者的能力，可能给种植者带来相当大的损失。

sentences.en: This problem has been made worse in the United States by recent epidemics that have infected and killed many honeybees, the major insect pollinator.
sentences.zh: 在美国，近年来的疫病感染并杀死了大量作为主要传粉昆虫的蜜蜂，使这一问题更加严重。

sentences.en: G Some plant breeders have tried to solve this pollination problem by spraying scent compounds on orchard trees to enhance honeybee foraging, but this approach was costly and, in the end, proved to be inefficient.
sentences.zh: 一些植物育种者试图通过在果园树木上喷洒香味化合物来促进蜜蜂采食，以解决这一传粉难题，但这种做法成本高昂，最终被证明效率低下。

sentences.en: One of the reasons for its ineffectiveness was that general spraying of the crop could not tell insects exactly where the blossoms were.
sentences.zh: 其无效的原因之一是，对作物全面喷洒无法告诉昆虫花朵究竟在哪里。

sentences.en: Clearly, a more refined strategy is needed; genetic manipulation of scents, for example, would allow growers to regulate the types of insect pollinators and the frequency of their visits.
sentences.zh: 显然需要一种更精细的策略；例如，对香气进行基因操控可以让种植者调控传粉昆虫的种类及其造访频率。

sentences.en: H Such manipulation of scent will also benefit people who grow flowers commercially.
sentences.zh: 这样的香气操控也将惠及以商业方式种花的人。

sentences.en: Cut flowers and potted plants play an important aesthetic part in human life.
sentences.zh: 切花和盆栽植物在人类生活中发挥着重要的审美作用。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, traditional breeding has produced varieties with improved vase life, color, and shape, while perfume has been sacrificed.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，传统育种培育出了瓶插期更长、颜色和形状更好的品种，却牺牲了香味。

sentences.en: The loss of scent among ornamental flowers, which have a worldwide annual value of more than US$30 billion, makes them important targets for the genetic manipulation of flower fragrance.
sentences.zh: 观赏花卉全球年产值超过 300 亿美元，其香味的丧失使它们成为花香基因操控的重要目标。

sentences.en: Some preliminary experiments have already been carried out, but for technical reasons the scent was present in every part of the plant, rather than being localized in the flower, and the level of intensity of fragrance was below the threshold of detection for the human nose.
sentences.zh: 一些初步实验已经开展，但由于技术原因，香味存在于植物的每一个部位而非局限于花中，且香气强度低于人类鼻子的察觉阈值。

sentences.en: The next generation of experiments, already in progress, will include more sophisticated schemes that target the expression of scent specifically to flowers or other organs, such as special glands that can store antibacterial or herbivore-repellent compounds.
sentences.zh: 下一代实验已在进行中，将包含更为精巧的方案，使香味的表达专门定位于花或其他器官，例如能够储存抗菌或驱避食草动物化合物的特殊腺体。

sentences.en: (A) When scientists began the first substantial exploration of the islands 30 years ago, they found a fascinating collection of unusual plants and animals - a unique combination of 'relict' populations (organisms that have become extinct elsewhere) and species that have evolved to cope with the island's harsh conditions.
sentences.zh: 30 年前科学家首次对这些岛屿展开实质性考察时，发现了一批引人入胜的奇特动植物——那是“残遗”种群（在别处已经灭绝的生物）与为适应岛上严酷环境而演化出来的物种的独特组合。

sentences.en: In fact, almost a third of its plant species and up to 80 percent of its terrestrial animals are found nowhere else.
sentences.zh: 事实上，岛上近三分之一的植物物种和多达 80% 的陆生动物在其他任何地方都找不到。

sentences.en: (B) Life in the arid conditions is harsh for the people living there too.
sentences.zh: 干旱的环境对生活在那里的人们同样严酷。

sentences.en: Isolated from the mainland by hundreds of kilometres, and with monsoons that rage for several months every year, the islanders were historically self-sufficient - relying only on what they themselves could produce to survive.
sentences.zh: 这些岛屿与大陆相隔数百公里，每年又有连续数月肆虐的季风，岛民历来自给自足——只靠自己所能生产的东西维生。

sentences.en: There are floods and droughts, and many islanders lack adequate water resources and nutrition.
sentences.zh: 这里有洪水也有干旱，许多岛民缺乏足够的水资源和营养。

sentences.en: Medical care and education are limited.
sentences.zh: 医疗和教育也很有限。

sentences.en: (C) However, the main island, Socotra, is experiencing significant change.
sentences.zh: 然而，主岛索科特拉正在经历显著的变化。

sentences.en: A rapid development programme has been instituted that will have far-reaching impacts on the island's people and the environment for decades to come.
sentences.zh: 岛上已启动一项快速发展计划，将在未来数十年对岛上居民和环境产生深远影响。

sentences.en: In the past, the only way to get to Socotra was by travelling for several days on a boat, but irregular flights began touching down on dirt landing strips during the late 1960s.
sentences.zh: 过去，前往索科特拉的唯一办法是乘船航行数日，但从 20 世纪 60 年代末起，已有不定期航班降落在土质跑道上。

sentences.en: By 1999, a runway had been constructed on Socotra that was capable of taking larger aircraft all year round, and since 2000 the capital, Hadibo, has seen huge expansion.
sentences.zh: 到 1999 年，索科特拉建成了一条全年可起降更大型飞机的跑道；自 2000 年以来，首府哈迪博也经历了大规模扩张。

sentences.en: New schools have been built, and a modern terminal was added to the airport, through which an increasing number of tourists are beginning to pass.
sentences.zh: 新学校陆续建成，机场还增建了一座现代化航站楼，越来越多的游客开始由此进出。

sentences.en: And there are plans to construct new harbour facilities that will enable fishermen to sell their catch more easily, and also make it simpler for local people to have food, and bricks and timber for construction projects brought to the island.
sentences.zh: 此外还计划兴建新的港口设施，让渔民更方便地出售渔获，也让当地人更容易把食物以及建筑工程所需的砖木运上岛来。

sentences.en: (D) However, although these improvements are significant, it’s the continuing development of Socotra’s road system that is having the greatest impact on the islanders.
sentences.zh: 然而，尽管这些改善意义重大，对岛民影响最大的还是索科特拉道路系统的持续建设。

sentences.en: Until 1991, a few dirt tracks, navigable only by four-wheel drive, gave access to part of the island.
sentences.zh: 直到 1991 年，只有几条仅四驱车能通行的土路可通往岛上部分地区。

sentences.en: Otherwise it was only possible to reach most areas on foot, or with a donkey.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，多数地方只能步行或靠驴子抵达。

sentences.en: By 2001, however, there was an extensive network of unpaved car tracks, and the following year a tarmac road, the first of its kind on Socotra, connecting the airport to Hadibo, was completed.
sentences.zh: 不过到 2001 年，已经形成了一张四通八达的未铺装车行道网络；次年，索科特拉岛上第一条柏油路——连接机场与哈迪博的公路——竣工。

sentences.en: Now, a road traverses the Diksam plateau and continues on to the south coast, making essential services more accessible to a large number of villagers.
sentences.zh: 如今，一条公路横穿迪克萨姆高原并继续通往南部海岸，使大量村民更容易获得基本服务。

sentences.en: (E) There is no doubt that the development of Socotra’s infrastructure has brought many benefits to the island's inhabitants, but there is growing concern that the speed with which it is taking place is so rapid that it will be difficult for local people to maintain certain traditions.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，索科特拉基础设施的发展给岛上居民带来了诸多益处，但人们越来越担心，其推进速度之快会让当地人难以维系某些传统。

sentences.en: There is also the fear that the developments will threaten the island's unique ecosystems.
sentences.zh: 人们还担心这些开发会威胁到岛上独特的生态系统。

sentences.en: Building new roads and harbours may lead to the introduction of alien species to Socotra Island (as has already happened with the Indian house crow), damage to the sea's biodiversity through the increased collection and sale of coral, and tourist developments on an inappropriate and unsustainable scale.
sentences.zh: 修建新的道路和港口可能导致外来物种被引入索科特拉岛（印度家鸦的情况就已经发生），可能因珊瑚采集和买卖增加而损害海洋生物多样性，也可能带来规模不当且不可持续的旅游开发。

sentences.en: (F) Problems were also caused by increasing access to sensitive areas.
sentences.zh: 敏感区域日益便于抵达也带来了问题。

sentences.en: For example, cutting the road along the coast caused considerable damage to the stunning scenery.
sentences.zh: 例如，沿海岸开辟道路对壮丽的景观造成了相当大的破坏。

sentences.en: However, some steps were then taken to limit the damage caused by further development.
sentences.zh: 不过，随后也采取了一些措施来限制进一步开发所造成的破坏。

sentences.en: For example, biodiversity project officers were consulted in the planning stages of the road that crosses the centre of Socotra, so it avoids some of the most scenic areas and sites that contain plants only found in a limited number of locations.
sentences.zh: 例如，在规划横穿索科特拉中部的那条公路时征询了生物多样性项目官员的意见，因此这条路避开了一些最具景观价值的区域，以及只在少数地点才有的植物所在的地点。

sentences.en: It is an area which is also home to the greatest concentrations of dragon's blood trees and supports many endemic animals.
sentences.zh: 那里也是龙血树最密集的地区，还养育着许多特有动物。

sentences.en: (G) An agreement has now been reached about all future construction of roads.
sentences.zh: 目前已就今后所有道路建设达成一项协议。

sentences.en: To protect the island's ecologically sensitive areas, any proposed road will be subject to a report assessing its environmental impact prior to construction.
sentences.zh: 为保护岛上生态敏感区域，任何拟建道路在动工前都必须提交一份评估其环境影响的报告。

sentences.en: The challenge has been to bring the benefits of development to Socotra without damaging the environment, which supports the people's way of life and will form the basis of future development on the island.
sentences.zh: 挑战在于既让索科特拉获得发展的益处，又不损害环境，因为环境支撑着当地人的生活方式，也将构成岛上未来发展的基础。

records.title: The Rise And Fall Of Detective Stories

sentences.en: (A) The detective story is normally said to have begun in the fertile brain of the great American writer Edgar Allan Poe (1809–49), especially in his stories featuring the detective C.
sentences.zh: 通常认为，侦探小说诞生于美国大作家埃德加·爱伦·坡（1809–49）富于想象力的头脑，尤其是他笔下那些以侦探 C.

sentences.en: Auguste Dupin.
sentences.zh: 奥古斯特·杜邦为主角的故事。

sentences.en: From 1859, Dupin had a counterpart in Monsieur Lecoq, created by the French author Emile Gaboriau.
sentences.zh: 从 1859 年起，杜邦有了一位对应人物——法国作家埃米尔·加博里约笔下的勒科克先生。

sentences.en: Despite these American and French origins, it was to Britain that detective fiction migrated, where it took root and flourished, becoming a characteristically British genre.
sentences.zh: 尽管起源于美国和法国，侦探小说却迁入了英国，并在那里扎根繁盛，成为一种典型的英国文类。

sentences.en: (B) This transition occurred because of one author and his great detective.
sentences.zh: 这一转变的发生，要归功于一位作家和他笔下伟大的侦探。

sentences.en: The most famous of all fictional detectives, Sherlock Holmes, was introduced by Sir Arthur Conan Doyle in A Study in Scarlet, first published in 1887, and later became the subject of four novels and 56 short stories.
sentences.zh: 所有虚构侦探中最著名的夏洛克·福尔摩斯，由阿瑟·柯南·道尔爵士在 1887 年首次出版的《血字的研究》中引入，此后又成为四部长篇和 56 篇短篇小说的主角。

sentences.en: Nearly all of the Holmes stories are narrated by his friend Dr Watson.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有福尔摩斯故事都由他的朋友华生医生叙述。

sentences.en: Watson is constantly amazed and stupefied by Holmes’s genius, but despite years of working with him, Watson is never able to produce these brilliant insights himself.
sentences.zh: 华生始终为福尔摩斯的天才所惊叹、所折服，但共事多年之后，他自己却从来无法作出那些精彩的推断。

sentences.en: Holmes is memorably eccentric, with a range of endearing and less endearing habits.
sentences.zh: 福尔摩斯的古怪令人印象深刻，既有讨人喜欢的习惯，也有不那么讨喜的。

sentences.en: He is a brilliant private detective, categorically better than the plodding and mediocre officials of Scotland Yard, who constantly turn to him when they are baffled.
sentences.zh: 他是一位杰出的私家侦探，明显胜过苏格兰场那些迟钝平庸的官员，而后者一旦束手无策就不断向他求助。

sentences.en: This in itself is pure fiction: in real life there were never any brilliant private detectives to whom Scotland Yard turned when they failed, and the Yard’s Criminal Investigation Department (CID) had a remarkable clear-up rate and was highly competent.
sentences.zh: 这本身纯属虚构：现实中从来没有哪位出色的私家侦探会在苏格兰场失手时被求助，而苏格兰场的刑事调查部（CID）破案率很高，能力也很强。

sentences.en: (C) Most of the Holmes stories are set among the higher levels of 19th-century British society, a world inhabited by professional men, retired army officers and country gentlemen, as well as members of royalty and cabinet ministers.
sentences.zh: 多数福尔摩斯故事都设定在 19 世纪英国社会的上层，那是一个由专业人士、退役军官和乡绅，以及王室成员和内阁大臣构成的世界。

sentences.en: Few take place among the working classes or the very poor, whereas in fact much crime was a product of the poverty and gangs in London’s underworld.
sentences.zh: 很少有故事发生在工人阶级或极度贫困者之中，而事实上大量犯罪正是伦敦下层社会的贫困与帮派所催生的。

sentences.en: (D) In the 20th century detective stories became increasingly popular.
sentences.zh: 进入 20 世纪，侦探小说越来越受欢迎。

sentences.en: Reading these stories was one of the characteristic aspects of the British middle classes in the ‘golden age’ of British detective fiction—the 1920s and 30s.
sentences.zh: 在英国侦探小说的“黄金时代”——20 世纪二三十年代——阅读这类故事是英国中产阶级的典型特征之一。

sentences.en: Their emphasis on rationality, the inevitable triumph of justice, and the existence of an unofficial super-detective tells us much about the society of the time.
sentences.zh: 它们强调理性、强调正义必然获胜、强调存在一位非官方的超级侦探，这些都在很大程度上折射出当时的社会。

sentences.en: So, too, do the stock characters and unstated prejudices in these works: country folk and domestic servants were almost always depicted as unintelligent, and women were often depicted in a simplistic, two-dimensional way, although a few female detective writers would present female characters in a more realistic manner.
sentences.zh: 这些作品中的定型人物和未言明的偏见同样如此：乡下人和家仆几乎总被描绘得头脑简单，女性也常被写得单薄而扁平，尽管少数女性侦探小说作家会以更真实的方式塑造女性角色。

sentences.en: (E) Most of the well-known British authors of ‘golden age’ detective stories were drawn from the middle classes, like their audience.
sentences.zh: “黄金时代”英国侦探小说的知名作家大多和他们的读者一样出身中产阶级。

sentences.en: Conan Doyle was a doctor who turned to writing fiction while he awaited his patients; Freeman Wills Crofts was a railway engineer in Northern Ireland; Gilbert Keith Chesterton and Anthony Berkeley were journalists; Cecil Street a career army officer.
sentences.zh: 柯南·道尔是一名医生，在等候病人时转而写起了小说；弗里曼·威尔斯·克罗夫茨是北爱尔兰的铁路工程师；吉尔伯特·基思·切斯特顿和安东尼·伯克利是记者；塞西尔·斯特里特则是职业军官。

sentences.en: Apart from a few superstars such as Agatha Christie, financial rewards for these interwar authors were rather meagre; a few hundred pounds per book—a useful income, but nothing princely.
sentences.zh: 除阿加莎·克里斯蒂等少数巨星之外，这些两战之间的作家所得报酬相当微薄；每本书几百英镑——算是一笔有用的收入，却谈不上丰厚。

sentences.en: (F) US writers such as Rex Stout and Ellery Queen attempted to recreate the ‘golden age’ of British detective fiction.
sentences.zh: 雷克斯·斯托特和埃勒里·奎因等美国作家曾试图重现英国侦探小说的“黄金时代”。

sentences.en: For the most part their books were mere imitations of the British models, although they were seldom wholly successful.
sentences.zh: 他们的书大多只是对英国范本的模仿，而且很少完全成功。

sentences.en: But in the 1920s and 1930s, America also saw the rise of the ‘hard-boiled’ genre and its detective type: the tough private cop who appeared in the works of Dashiell Hammett and Raymond Chandler.
sentences.zh: 但在 20 世纪二三十年代，美国也兴起了“硬汉派”文类及其侦探形象：达希尔·哈米特和雷蒙德·钱德勒笔下那种强悍的私家警探。

sentences.en: Apart from the violence that appeared throughout their works, Hammett’s and Chandler’s novels were often marked by a political agenda that sought to expose the inequality they saw at the heart of American life.
sentences.zh: 除了贯穿作品的暴力之外，哈米特和钱德勒的小说往往还带有一种政治意图，试图揭露他们眼中美国生活核心处的不平等。

sentences.en: Britain had no real parallel either to their outlook on the world or (until much later) to their violence, but upheld the belief that the authorities should punish criminals regardless of their circumstances.
sentences.zh: 英国既没有与之对应的世界观，也（直到很久以后）没有与之对应的暴力，而是坚持认为当局应当惩罚罪犯，不论其境遇如何。

sentences.en: (G) By around 1960, the classic British detective story was in serious decline.
sentences.zh: 到 1960 年前后，经典英国侦探小说已严重衰落。

sentences.en: It seemed that writers had simply run out of ingenious plots and puzzles for their detectives to solve.
sentences.zh: 似乎作家们再也想不出精巧的情节和谜题供笔下侦探破解了。

sentences.en: The best-known crime fiction writers, such as P.
sentences.zh: 最知名的犯罪小说作家，例如 P.

sentences.en: D.
sentences.zh: D.

sentences.en: James, eschewed private detectives for police inspectors, and straightforward puzzles for stories that were full of unexpected twists.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯，舍弃私家侦探而改写警探，舍弃直白的谜题而写出充满意外转折的故事。

sentences.en: (H) Today the detective story no longer exists in Britain, at least in its old form.
sentences.zh: 今天，侦探小说在英国已不复存在，至少其旧有形式已不复存在。

sentences.en: Arguably this mirrors the transformation of that society as a whole.
sentences.zh: 可以说，这映照出整个英国社会的转变。

sentences.en: The belief that scientific developments were invariably beneficial possibly reached its height during the period when the classic detective story flourished, as did the belief in putting rationality at the heart of Britain’s education system.
sentences.zh: 相信科学发展必然有益的观念，很可能正是在经典侦探小说繁盛的那段时期达到顶点，把理性置于英国教育体系核心的信念亦然。

sentences.en: And finally, the central belief that evil-doers would inevitably get their just deserts through the incorruptibility of the judicial system was replaced by a questioning of some of the procedures and decisions associated with that system.
sentences.zh: 最后，那种认为作恶者必将因司法体系的清廉而受到应得惩罚的核心信念，已被对该体系某些程序与裁决的质疑所取代。

sentences.en: (A) Humans are born to trade and we don’t need shops or money to do it—the heart of commerce is an instinctive ability for what anthropologists call “reciprocity”.
sentences.zh: 人类天生就会交易，而且不需要商店或货币就能做到——商业的核心是一种本能的能力，人类学家称之为“互惠”。

sentences.en: This is an ability to exchange goods of equal worth, and it evolved as the brains of our ancient ancestors and societies became more complex, allowing individuals to keep a running tally of their interactions with others.
sentences.zh: 这是一种交换等值物品的能力，它随着我们远古祖先的大脑和社会日益复杂而演化出来，使个体能够持续记下自己与他人往来的账。

sentences.en: Evidence from modern hunter-gatherers leaves little doubt that the exchange of food and favours is innate, as is the ability to keep track of the credits and debits that accrue as a result.
sentences.zh: 来自现代狩猎采集者的证据几乎无可置疑地表明，食物与人情的交换是天生的，而记录由此累积的人情盈亏的能力同样是天生的。

sentences.en: Combine this skill for mental book-keeping with even the most basic material culture, and trade inevitably follows.
sentences.zh: 把这种心算记账的本领与哪怕最基本的物质文化结合起来，交易便必然随之而来。

sentences.en: (B) Once trade gets off the ground, the economic benefits quickly make it irresistible.
sentences.zh: 交易一旦起步，其经济收益很快就让人无法抗拒。

sentences.en: But exchanging tools, food and other essentials of life in a barter economy is a far cry from the shopping mall.
sentences.zh: 但在以物易物的经济中交换工具、食物和其他生活必需品，与购物中心相去甚远。

sentences.en: Modern consumerism extends beyond subsistence and utilitarianism to encompass everything from Gucci handbags and BMW convertibles to valuable paintings.
sentences.zh: 现代消费主义超越了维生与实用，涵盖了从古驰手袋、宝马敞篷车到名贵画作的一切。

sentences.en: Clearly, the worth of such goods is not inherent but resides in certain intangible qualities that we invest in them.
sentences.zh: 显然，这类物品的价值并非其固有，而在于我们赋予它们的某些无形特质。

sentences.en: When did humans start holding these goods in such high esteem?
sentences.zh: 人类是从什么时候开始如此看重这类物品的呢？

sentences.en: (C) All the archaeological evidence for the flowering of consumer culture has up to now pointed to a date of around 40,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 迄今为止，关于消费文化兴盛的所有考古证据都指向大约四万年前这个时间点。

sentences.en: That’s when early modern humans started making increasingly intricate bone and stone tools, carving patterns into rocks and creating representational art such as carved figurines, jewellery and cave paintings.
sentences.zh: 那时早期现代人开始制作日益精巧的骨器和石器，在岩石上刻画纹样，并创作雕刻小像、饰品和洞穴壁画等具象艺术。

sentences.en: However, discoveries in Africa are pushing the origins of consumerism much further back into human prehistory.
sentences.zh: 然而，非洲的发现正把消费主义的源头推向人类史前更为久远的时期。

sentences.en: A few years ago, reports began to emerge of discoveries made at the Blombos Cave, a site of ancient human habitation in South Africa.
sentences.zh: 几年前，开始有报告披露在南非古人类居住遗址布隆伯斯洞穴所取得的发现。

sentences.en: Christopher Henshilwood and colleagues from the University of Bergen in Norway dated thousands of pieces of ochre from the cave, and many of them proved to be more than 100,000 years old — before the time that early humans moved out of Africa.
sentences.zh: 挪威卑尔根大学的克里斯托弗·亨希尔伍德及其同事对洞中数千块赭石进行了年代测定，其中许多被证明有十万年以上的历史——早于早期人类走出非洲的时间。

sentences.en: Ochre, a coloured clay that comes in various shades from red to black, does not occur naturally around Blombos and must have been imported from quarries at least 30 kilometres away, either directly by Blombos residents or through trade.
sentences.zh: 赭石是一种颜色从红到黑深浅不一的有色黏土，在布隆伯斯周边并不天然存在，必定是从至少 30 公里外的矿场运来的，或由布隆伯斯居民直接取得，或通过交易获得。

sentences.en: Although ochre can be used to dry and preserve (cure) animal hides, the researchers are convinced the Blombos ochre had a symbolic purpose.
sentences.zh: 尽管赭石可用来使兽皮干燥并加以保存（鞣制），研究者仍确信布隆伯斯的赭石具有象征性用途。

sentences.en: For a start, it is predominantly red—any of the other colours available would have done for curing—and the surfaces of the clay had been scraped in a way that indicates they were used to yield pigment for dyes.
sentences.zh: 首先，它以红色为主——现有的其他任何颜色本来都可用于鞣制——而且黏土表面被刮擦的方式表明，它们被用来取得染料所需的颜料。

sentences.en: (D) An even more intriguing discovery from Blombos was of 41 beads dating from 76,000 years ago, found in clusters and made from the shells of a tiny mollusc.
sentences.zh: 布隆伯斯更加耐人寻味的一项发现，是 41 颗距今 76000 年的珠子，它们成簇出土，由一种微小软体动物的贝壳制成。

sentences.en: These cannot be natural deposits, argue the researchers, as each cluster contains shells of a similar size and colour with consistently placed holes.
sentences.zh: 研究者认为这些不可能是自然沉积，因为每一簇中的贝壳大小和颜色相近，钻孔位置也始终一致。

sentences.en: What’s more, all the beads display a pattern of wear suggesting friction from rubbing against thread, clothes or other beads.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，所有珠子都呈现出一种磨损痕迹，显示它们曾与线、衣物或其他珠子摩擦。

sentences.en: The previous oldest find of beads in Africa dates back to just 45,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 此前非洲发现的最古老珠子仅可追溯到四万五千年前。

sentences.en: And it seems the Blombos people’s taste for beautiful items was not an isolated phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 而且看来，布隆伯斯人对美物的偏好并非孤立现象。

sentences.en: Jessica Thompson of Arizona State University in Tempe has described finding shell fragments from a site in Tanzania that she believes may represent debris from bead manufacture.
sentences.zh: 位于坦佩的亚利桑那州立大学的杰西卡·汤普森描述过在坦桑尼亚一处遗址发现的贝壳碎片，她认为那可能是制珠留下的废料。

sentences.en: They are at least 45,000—and possibly 280,000—years old.
sentences.zh: 它们至少有四万五千年——也可能有二十八万年——的历史。

sentences.en: Although there is no evidence of how the ancient beads were used, their modern counterparts are often traded.
sentences.zh: 尽管没有证据表明这些古代珠子如何使用，但它们的现代对应物常被用于交易。

sentences.en: So it looks as though our taste for jewellery and art is much older than we thought.
sentences.zh: 因此看来，我们对首饰与艺术的偏好，要比我们原先以为的古老得多。

sentences.en: (E) But why did we come to value these objects in the first place?
sentences.zh: 但我们当初为什么会看重这些物件呢？

sentences.en: In many animal species, individuals signal their genetic fitness by showing off with attention-grabbing adornment.
sentences.zh: 在许多动物物种中，个体通过炫耀引人注目的装饰来彰显自身的遗传适应度。

sentences.en: Some researchers think that in humans, consumer products play a similar role.
sentences.zh: 有些研究者认为，在人类身上，消费品也扮演着类似的角色。

sentences.en: Archaeologist Aimee Plourde, from the University of California, also argues that even in egalitarian societies, some people are more successful than others.
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚大学的考古学家艾梅·普卢德还提出，即便在平等主义社会里，也有些人比别人更成功。

sentences.en: Among our ancestors, superior skills in areas such as hunting, crafts, environmental knowledge and contact with neighbouring groups would have brought respect—in other words, prestige.
sentences.zh: 在我们的祖先中，狩猎、手工、环境知识以及与邻近群体往来等方面的高超技能会赢得尊重——换句话说，赢得声望。

sentences.en: And because prestige brings social benefits, people would want to show off their talents.
sentences.zh: 而由于声望能带来社会性好处，人们便会想要炫耀自己的才能。

sentences.en: The best way to do this would be through demonstrating possession of material items that are hard to fake.
sentences.zh: 做到这一点的最佳方式，就是展示自己拥有难以造假的实物。

sentences.en: ‘A good hunter, for instance, could advertise his skills by wearing the tooth of an animal that is elusive or dangerous,’ says Plourde.
sentences.zh: “比如说，一名优秀的猎手可以佩戴一颗难以捕获或危险动物的牙齿来彰显本领，”普卢德说。

sentences.en: The benefits of prestige would also lead to competition to acquire it.
sentences.zh: 声望带来的好处也会引发对声望的争夺。

sentences.en: As a result, the value and variety of prestige goods would spiral and there would be a parallel increase in the ranking of social systems.
sentences.zh: 其结果是，声望物品的价值和种类会螺旋上升，社会体系的等级化也会随之加剧。

sentences.en: If Plourde is correct, prestige goods form a direct link between our innate drive for trade and the development of structured, hierarchical societies.
sentences.zh: 如果普卢德是对的，那么声望物品就在我们与生俱来的交易冲动和结构化等级社会的形成之间架起了一座直接的桥梁。

sentences.en: They are arguably the first step on the road to modern civilisation, paving the way for agriculture and urbanisation.
sentences.zh: 可以说，它们是通往现代文明之路的第一步，为农业和城市化铺平了道路。

sentences.en: We may not be impressed by beads any more, but their modern equivalents have the same fascination.
sentences.zh: 我们也许不再为珠子所动，但它们的现代对应物同样令人着迷。

sentences.en: Nobody believes the guy who spends €670,000 on a Bugatti Veyron car does so because he needs to travel at 250 mph.
sentences.zh: 没有人会相信，那个花 67 万欧元买布加迪威龙的人这么做是因为他需要以每小时 250 英里的速度赶路。

sentences.en: We all know in today’s consumer society he’s buying an exclusive status symbol.
sentences.zh: 我们都清楚，在今天的消费社会里，他买的是一个专属的身份象征。

sentences.en: (A) Are the climatic changes the world is seeing now really unprecedented, or have there been other times when change was just as swift?
sentences.zh: 当今世界所见的气候变化真的前所未有吗，还是说过去也曾有过同样迅速的变化？

sentences.en: ‘If we go back to the past and find there really hasn’t been anything like this before, then that strengthens the case that human activity is responsible for the rapid changes we are seeing today,’ says climatologist Dennis Wheeler of the University of Sunderland, UK.
sentences.zh: “如果我们回到过去，发现此前确实不曾有过类似情形，那就会强化这样一种论点：我们今天所见的快速变化是人类活动造成的，”英国桑德兰大学气候学家丹尼斯·惠勒说。

sentences.en: (B) But the past is tricky territory for climatologists.
sentences.zh: 但对气候学家来说，过去是一片棘手的领域。

sentences.en: While tree rings and ice cores chart annual changes in climate going back millennia, they cannot show what happened on a month-to-month basis.
sentences.zh: 树轮和冰芯虽然记录了上溯数千年的逐年气候变化，却无法显示逐月发生了什么。

sentences.en: There are some long-running chronicles of temperature and air pressure over land dating back to the 17th century, but systematic records of air movements over the oceans — which govern most of our weather — were almost non-existent before the mid-19th century, by which time the Industrial Revolution was already well under way, and factory chimneys were pouring carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 确实有一些关于陆地气温和气压的长期记录可上溯到 17 世纪，但关于海洋上空气流的系统记录——而正是这些气流主宰着我们的大部分天气——在 19 世纪中叶以前几乎不存在，而那时工业革命早已全面展开，工厂烟囱正把二氧化碳排入大气。

sentences.en: In order to establish whether today’s climate changes indeed had any precedent in the past, what Wheeler needed was detailed information from earlier times, and he soon became convinced that the multitude of jottings in old ships’ records could provide just that.
sentences.zh: 为了确定今天的气候变化在过去是否真有先例，惠勒需要的是来自更早年代的详细信息，而他很快就确信，旧船舶记录中大量的随手记载正能提供这些信息。

sentences.en: (C) By the late 17th century, the seafaring nations of Europe had fleets of ships criss-crossing the seas, all keeping meticulous accounts of their voyages, including regular observations of weather conditions.
sentences.zh: 到 17 世纪晚期，欧洲各航海国家已有成队的船只往来穿梭于各海域，全都细致地记录航程，其中包括对天气状况的定期观测。

sentences.en: In 1731, it became obligatory for British naval vessels to keep a detailed logbook, and by 1750 the practice was universal.
sentences.zh: 1731 年，英国海军舰船被强制要求保存详细的航海日志，到 1750 年这一做法已经普及。

sentences.en: A vast number of such records survive to this day.
sentences.zh: 大量这样的记录留存至今。

sentences.en: Despite initial reluctance among climatologists to use these historical documents for scientific research, Wheeler and his team secured funding for a project to sift through two thousand old logbooks.
sentences.zh: 尽管气候学家起初不愿把这些历史文献用于科学研究，惠勒和他的团队还是为一个筛查两千本旧航海日志的项目争取到了经费。

sentences.en: They pored over records of English, Dutch, French and Spanish fleets, with the aim of creating a climatological database for the world’s oceans between 1750 and 1850.
sentences.zh: 他们钻研英国、荷兰、法国和西班牙舰队的记录，目标是建立一个涵盖 1750 至 1850 年间全球海洋的气候数据库。

sentences.en: (D) In order to reconstruct air pressure fields as they move across the sea, climate ‘modellers’ need details of wind strength and direction at as many locations as possible.
sentences.zh: 为了重建气压场在海上移动的情形，气候“建模者”需要尽可能多的地点上的风力和风向细节。

sentences.en: The team’s research produced the equivalent of two million days of information but, plentiful as this data was, much of it needed translation.
sentences.zh: 团队的研究产出了相当于两百万天的信息，但数据虽多，其中大部分还需要转译。

sentences.en: Until 1805, even a day wasn’t a day as we know it, but a nautical day, which started at noon.
sentences.zh: 直到 1805 年，一天甚至都不是我们今天所理解的一天，而是从正午开始的航海日。

sentences.en: Before 1752, the year began on 25 March, and until September of that year the English calendar lagged 10 days behind the one used in the rest of Europe.
sentences.zh: 1752 年之前，一年从 3 月 25 日开始；而直到那一年的 9 月，英国历法都比欧洲其他地区所用的历法晚 10 天。

sentences.en: (E) Even the wind’s direction posed a problem.
sentences.zh: 就连风向也是个问题。

sentences.en: It took a long time to work out if the direction noted in the log was based on magnetic north or true north.
sentences.zh: 要弄清日志中记下的方向是以磁北还是真北为准，花了很长时间。

sentences.en: Get it wrong and the data could be out by as much as 30 degrees.
sentences.zh: 一旦搞错，数据的偏差可能高达 30 度。

sentences.en: ‘On British vessels, most observations were magnetic.
sentences.zh: “在英国船只上，多数观测采用的是磁向。

sentences.en: Once a day, officers would convert the readings to true north — but the logbooks don’t tell you that,’ says Wheeler.
sentences.zh: 军官们每天会把读数换算成真北——但航海日志里并不会告诉你这一点，”惠勒说。

sentences.en: ‘It took some detective work to find out what was going on.’
sentences.zh: “要弄明白究竟是怎么回事，得下一番侦查功夫。”

sentences.en: (F) Harder still was interpreting observations on the strength of the wind.
sentences.zh: 更难的是解读关于风力强弱的观测记录。

sentences.en: It was 1850 before most ships were equipped with accurate instruments to collect climatic data, previous to which officers had to rely on judgement and experience.
sentences.zh: 直到 1850 年，多数船只才配备了采集气候数据的精确仪器，在此之前军官只能依靠判断和经验。

sentences.en: And, as the numerical Beaufort scale of wind strength did not become official until 1838, most of the logbooks in Wheeler’s archives describe weather conditions using words alone — and often archaic or peculiar ones.
sentences.zh: 而且，由于用数字表示风力的蒲福风级直到 1838 年才正式启用，惠勒所藏的多数日志都只用文字描述天气状况——而且往往是古旧或独特的措辞。

sentences.en: A sample of English logs from 1685 to 1700 produced 73 different ways of describing the wind’s force.
sentences.zh: 一份 1685 至 1700 年的英国日志样本中，就出现了 73 种描述风力的不同说法。

sentences.en: To everyone’s relief, closer scrutiny showed that many terms were used just once or twice: most log-keepers stuck to a similar set of terms.
sentences.zh: 令所有人松一口气的是，更仔细的审视表明许多措辞只出现过一两次：多数记录者用的其实是一套相近的词。

sentences.en: (G) So how strong was a wind described as ‘moderate’, or a gale described as ‘fine’?
sentences.zh: 那么，被描述为“中等”的风究竟有多强，被描述为“不错”的大风又有多强呢？

sentences.en: And did all seafarers have the same thing in mind when they used them?
sentences.zh: 而且所有航海者在使用这些词时想的都是同一回事吗？

sentences.en: This was tested by checking how far the ships sailed each day, another fact carefully recorded in the logbook.
sentences.zh: 对此的检验办法是核查船只每天航行了多远——这也是航海日志中仔细记录的另一项事实。

sentences.en: The speed a sailing ship travelled was directly linked to the force of the wind, at least up to Beaufort force 7.
sentences.zh: 帆船航行的速度与风力直接相关，至少在蒲福 7 级以内如此。

sentences.en: ‘If you have a large enough sample you can pick out all the days when officers described, for example, a “fine breeze”, and check the sea-miles covered,’ says Wheeler.
sentences.zh: “只要样本足够大，你就能挑出军官们描述为‘不错的微风’的所有日子，再核对航行的海里数，”惠勒说。

sentences.en: ‘That gives a measure of the relative wind strength.’
sentences.zh: “这就给出了相对风力的一个量度。”

sentences.en: (H) Having to deal with logs from four nations, from both naval and merchant vessels, made the task of translating archaic terms into hard numbers doubly daunting.
sentences.zh: 由于要处理来自四个国家、既有军舰又有商船的日志，把古旧措辞转译成确切数字的任务难上加难。

sentences.en: Toughest of all was unravelling the terms used aboard trading ships.
sentences.zh: 其中最棘手的是厘清商船上使用的术语。

sentences.en: These had their own complex vocabulary of gales, trade winds, and monsoons, each in several grades, Wheeler discovered.
sentences.zh: 惠勒发现，商船有自己一套复杂的词汇来指称大风、信风和季风，每一种还分若干等级。

sentences.en: But, by checking sea-miles covered, and cross-checking with the logs of occasional naval escorts, the team eventually worked out which terms meant what.
sentences.zh: 但通过核对航行海里数，并与偶尔随行的海军护航舰日志相互印证，团队最终弄清了各个词的含义。

sentences.en: Pairs of ships in convoy, or squadrons in the same locality, should have the same records, so allowing the researchers to check for consistency.
sentences.zh: 结伴同行的两艘船，或同一海域的分舰队，记录应当一致，这样研究者就能据此检验一致性。

sentences.en: (I) The wealth of data Wheeler was able to call on enabled him to show statistically that the expressions used in the logbooks were not vague approximations, but precise terms falling into distinct categories.
sentences.zh: 惠勒所能调用的丰富数据使他得以从统计上证明，日志中所用的表述并非含糊的近似说法，而是可归入不同类别的精确用语。

sentences.en: The researchers have now fitted nearly all the terms used into the Beaufort scale, and have high hopes that the seafarers of the pre-instrumental age will, in time, give today’s scientists a valuable insight into the causes of global climate change.
sentences.zh: 研究者如今已把几乎所有用语都对应到蒲福风级中，并寄予厚望：仪器时代之前的航海者终将为今天的科学家提供有关全球气候变化成因的宝贵洞见。

records.title: Introduction To A Book About The Assessment Of Carbon Footprints
records.titleZh: 关于碳足迹评估的书籍导论

sentences.en: A As this book is about ways of measuring the carbon footprint of particular things, I should start by making it clear what I mean.
sentences.zh: 由于本书讲的是衡量特定事物碳足迹的方法，我应当先把自己的意思说清楚。

sentences.en: I am using the word ‘carbon’ as shorthand for all the different global-warming greenhouse gases, and I am using the word ‘footprint’ as a metaphor for the total impact that something has.
sentences.zh: 我用“碳”一词作为所有各类造成全球变暖的温室气体的简称，用“足迹”一词作为某事物全部影响的隐喻。

sentences.en: So I am using the phrase ‘carbon footprint’ as shorthand to mean the full climate-change impact of something.
sentences.zh: 因此，我用“碳足迹”这个说法作为简称，指某事物对气候变化的全部影响。

sentences.en: That something could be anything – an activity, an item, a lifestyle, a company, a country, or even the whole world.
sentences.zh: 这个“某事物”可以是任何东西——一项活动、一件物品、一种生活方式、一家公司、一个国家，甚至整个世界。

sentences.en: B Measuring carbon footprints is a long way from being an exact process, whatever the claims, or whatever numbers you might see written on the side of products in some shops.
sentences.zh: 无论有怎样的说法，也无论你在某些商店的产品侧面看到怎样的数字，衡量碳足迹都远算不上一个精确的过程。

sentences.en: All my numbers are best estimates, and nothing more, even though I have reached them as carefully as I can.
sentences.zh: 我给出的所有数字都只是最佳估计，仅此而已，尽管我已尽可能审慎地得出它们。

sentences.en: C I have used a variety of different methods and sources.
sentences.zh: 我使用了多种不同的方法和来源。

sentences.en: I have drawn on a range of data sets and models taken from publicly available reports of life-cycle* studies.
sentences.zh: 我借助了一系列数据集和模型，取自公开发表的生命周期*研究报告。

sentences.en: I have also used studies carried out for businesses across different industries by my own company, Small World Consulting, using models that we are developing all the time.
sentences.zh: 我还使用了我自己的公司“小世界咨询”为不同行业的企业所做的研究，所用模型我们一直在不断完善。

sentences.en: Often I have arrived at numbers by a couple of different routes, to check that the results agree with each other.
sentences.zh: 我常常通过两三条不同的路径得出数字，以核对结果是否彼此吻合。

sentences.en: Occasionally, it has been more a case of putting my finger in the air and guessing, but when that has been the case I have tried to make it clear.
sentences.zh: 偶尔更像是凭空估摸着猜，但每逢这种情况，我都尽量说明清楚。

sentences.en: D The publicly available data sets I have used were arrived at by two main methods.
sentences.zh: 我所使用的公开数据集是由两种主要方法得出的。

sentences.en: The first of these, process-based life-cycle analysis, is the most common approach to carbon footprint calculations.
sentences.zh: 其中第一种是基于过程的生命周期分析，也是碳足迹计算最常用的方法。

sentences.en: It is often referred to as ‘bottom-up’ because you start off identifying, one by one, all the processes that have had to happen in order for, say, a product to be created.
sentences.zh: 它常被称为“自下而上”，因为你要先逐一识别出为了让某样东西——比如一件产品——得以问世而必须发生的所有过程。

sentences.en: Then you add up the emissions from each process, and that is the footprint of the product.
sentences.zh: 然后把各个过程的排放加总起来，那就是该产品的足迹。

sentences.en: It may sound simple, but it is not at all.
sentences.zh: 这听上去也许简单，其实根本不然。

sentences.en: It is back-breaking work, and since the number of processes you really need to include is always infinite, the job is never quite complete, so you end up with an underestimate.
sentences.zh: 这是极其费神的工作，而且由于你真正需要纳入的过程数量总是无穷无尽，这项工作永远不算完成，最终你得到的只是一个偏低的估计。

sentences.en: In fact, the omissions from the calculation are often shocking: they can be fifty per cent or more.
sentences.zh: 事实上，计算中的遗漏往往令人吃惊：可能达到五成甚至更多。

sentences.en: To make matters worse, these problems are commonly overlooked, even in the development of government-backed and government-funded guidelines, such as the UK’s PAS 2050 standard.
sentences.zh: 更糟的是，即便在制定由政府支持和资助的准则时，例如英国的 PAS 2050 标准，这些问题通常也被忽视了。

sentences.en: But for all the problems, process-based life-cycle analysis is still an essential source of detailed information that can’t be gathered any other way.
sentences.zh: 但尽管存在种种问题，基于过程的生命周期分析仍是一个不可或缺的详细信息来源，这类信息用别的办法根本无法收集。

sentences.en: E The other method is environmental input-output analysis.
sentences.zh: 另一种方法是环境投入产出分析。

sentences.en: This is a neat alternative to process-based life-cycle analysis.
sentences.zh: 这是基于过程的生命周期分析之外一个巧妙的替代办法。

sentences.en: It is not as popular, perhaps because it is a bit less easy to understand, but it is at least as robust as anything else in the dim world of measuring carbon footprints.
sentences.zh: 它不那么流行，或许是因为它稍微不那么容易理解，但在衡量碳足迹这个含混的领域里，它至少和其他任何方法一样稳健。

sentences.en: It is sometimes called a ‘top-down’ approach because it begins by looking at the whole economy.
sentences.zh: 它有时被称为“自上而下”的方法，因为它从考察整个经济体入手。

sentences.en: It uses macroeconomic modelling to understand the way in which the activities of one industry trigger activities and emissions in every other industry.
sentences.zh: 它运用宏观经济建模来理解一个行业的活动如何引发其他所有行业的活动与排放。

sentences.en: Input-output analysis’ key ‘trick’ is a piece of ingenious maths (for which a man called Wassily Leontief got a Nobel Prize) that succeeds in capturing the endless ripple effects in a way that is one hundred per cent complete.
sentences.zh: 投入产出分析的关键“诀窍”是一套精巧的数学（一位名叫瓦西里·列昂惕夫的人因此获得了诺贝尔奖），它成功地以百分之百完整的方式捕捉到无穷无尽的涟漪效应。

sentences.en: It has the further advantage that if you know how much something costs, you can get an instant crude estimate of its carbon footprint.
sentences.zh: 它还有一个好处：只要你知道某样东西的价钱，就能立刻粗略估算出它的碳足迹。

sentences.en: It is like a magic trick.
sentences.zh: 这就像变魔术。

sentences.en: And just like all the best magic it is also a bit too good to be true – in many cases the results can be ridiculously general and of little value.
sentences.zh: 而正如所有最精彩的魔术一样，它也好得有点不真实——在许多情况下，结果可能笼统得可笑，价值不大。

sentences.en: F Input-output analysis is nevertheless a natural method, both because it does not omit things, and because once a specific model has been built it is often easy to use: the basic technique is well established.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，投入产出分析仍是一种自然的方法，既因为它不会遗漏东西，也因为一旦建成某个具体模型往往就很好用：其基本技术已相当成熟。

sentences.en: The specific model I have used is one that was developed at Small World Consulting in collaboration with Lancaster University in the UK, and draws mainly on data obtained from government sources.
sentences.zh: 我所使用的具体模型，是“小世界咨询”与英国兰卡斯特大学合作开发的，主要取用来自政府来源的数据。

sentences.en: It was based on a 2007 picture of the UK economy.
sentences.zh: 它以 2007 年的英国经济图景为基础。

sentences.en: It deals with all the greenhouse gases, and employs a weighting factor for gases emitted at a high altitude, which have a greater impact than ground-level emissions.
sentences.zh: 它涵盖所有温室气体，并对高空排放的气体采用加权系数，因为这些气体的影响比地面排放更大。

sentences.en: A key weakness, which I sometimes adjust for, is that it treats imported products as though they had the same carbon intensity as products from within the UK, whereas in reality imports are usually more carbon-intensive.
sentences.zh: 一个关键弱点是它把进口产品当作与英国本土产品具有相同的碳强度来处理，而现实中进口品通常碳强度更高；对此我有时会作出调整。

sentences.en: G Most of the time I have used a combination of life-cycle analysis and input-output analysis to get my numbers.
sentences.zh: 多数时候，我把生命周期分析和投入产出分析结合起来得出数字。

sentences.en: At its best, life-cycle analysis can be more precise, but input-output analysis is often able to get at information that life-cycle analysis is unable to reach.
sentences.zh: 生命周期分析在最理想的情况下可以更精确，但投入产出分析往往能触及生命周期分析无法触及的信息。

sentences.en: Putting the two methods together is sometimes called a hybrid approach, and the result is a bit like looking through both a microscope and a telescope at the same time.
sentences.zh: 把两种方法放在一起有时被称为混合方法，其效果有点像同时透过显微镜和望远镜观看。

sentences.en: They each show you different things, and between them, if the lenses are clean, you end up with a passable understanding of whatever it is you are looking at.
sentences.zh: 它们各自向你展示不同的东西，而如果镜片干净，两者合起来就能让你对所观察的对象获得一种说得过去的理解。

sentences.en: A Alfred Marshall, one of the fathers of modern economics, was asked why firms in the same industry were often geographically located near each other.
sentences.zh: 现代经济学之父之一Alfred Marshall曾被问及，为什么同一行业的企业在地理位置上往往彼此靠近。

sentences.en: Proximity, he replied, created something ‘in the air’.
sentences.zh: 他回答说，邻近造就了某种“弥漫在空气中”的东西。

sentences.en: He went on to explain, ‘If one man starts a new idea, it is taken up by others and combined with suggestions of their own, and thus it becomes a source of further new ideas.’
sentences.zh: 他接着解释道：“如果一个人提出一个新想法，其他人就会把它接过去，并结合自己的一些建议，于是它就成为更多新想法的源泉。”

sentences.en: Marshall was thinking about traditional 19th-century manufacturing companies, but the same is true of IT companies of the 21st century.
sentences.zh: Marshall当时想的是传统的19世纪制造企业，但21世纪的IT公司也是如此。

sentences.en: Silicon Valley, an area near San Francisco in the USA, is home to many of the industry’s giants, and hopeful founders of young start-up companies still head there.
sentences.zh: Silicon Valley是位于美国San Francisco附近的一个地区，那里是许多行业巨头的大本营，年轻初创公司满怀希望的创始人们至今仍纷纷奔向那里。

sentences.en: B Economic theory suggests several main reasons why historically firms from the same industry—for example, steel makers or clothing manufacturers—have ended up in the same place.
sentences.zh: 经济理论给出了几个主要原因，解释为什么历史上来自同一行业的企业——例如钢铁制造商或服装制造商——最终都聚集在同一个地方。

sentences.en: Some may depend on the availability of natural resources such as coal or being close to a harbour or river for shipping goods.
sentences.zh: 有些原因可能取决于煤等自然资源的可得性，或是靠近便于货运的港口或河流。

sentences.en: A concentration of firms also creates a pool of specialized workers, and this benefits both employees and employers: the former are likely to find jobs and the latter are likely to find staff.
sentences.zh: 企业的集中还会造就一个专业工人储备库，这对雇员和雇主双方都有利：前者更容易找到工作，后者更容易招到员工。

sentences.en: Yet another reason is that subsidiary trades spring up to supply specialised inputs required by the primary industry.
sentences.zh: 还有一个原因是，辅助性行业会应运而生，为主要行业提供所需的专门投入品。

sentences.en: And inevitably, industries cluster together because ideas spill over from one firm to the next.
sentences.zh: 而且不可避免的是，各行业会聚集在一起，因为想法会从一家企业外溢到另一家企业。

sentences.en: C But there are also forces that encourage companies to spread out.
sentences.zh: 但也有促使公司分散布局的力量。

sentences.en: One is the cost of transporting products to widely dispersed customers.
sentences.zh: 其一是把产品运送给分散各地的客户的成本。

sentences.en: Another is that rents tend to rise when firms cluster together.
sentences.zh: 其二是企业聚集在一起时，租金往往会上涨。

sentences.en: You might imagine that the dramatic fall in the cost of computing would have pushed firms in the IT industry farther apart.
sentences.zh: 你可能以为，计算成本的大幅下降会促使IT行业的企业分散得更开。

sentences.en: Natural resources do not matter to them as they do to many traditional manufacturing industries, and the ease of online communication should reduce the need for staff to be close together to deal with customers and suppliers or to swap ideas.
sentences.zh: 自然资源对它们不像对许多传统制造业那样重要，而且便捷的线上沟通本应降低员工为对接客户和供应商或交流想法而聚在一起的必要性。

sentences.en: But none of this seems to count against Silicon Valley, where commercial property prices are high, and against other IT centres like London and New York, which are not only expensive, but also lack California’s high-tech history.
sentences.zh: 但这一切似乎都无碍于Silicon Valley——那里的商业地产价格很高——也无碍于London和New York等其他IT中心，这些城市不仅成本高昂，而且缺乏California那样的高科技历史。

sentences.en: There are plenty of other places in Europe where costs are lower, but they currently lack sufficient appeal.
sentences.zh: 欧洲还有许多成本更低的地方，但它们目前缺乏足够的吸引力。

sentences.en: D Although you can find high-tech companies of all shapes and sizes in these IT centres, the smaller ones especially have a fondness for clustering together.
sentences.zh: 虽然在这些IT中心里能找到各种形态与规模的高科技公司，但规模较小的公司尤其偏爱聚集在一起。

sentences.en: As Jed Kolko, an economist for an international property company, explains, the less an industry needs to be near its suppliers or its customers, the more likely it is to locate where the jobs are already, such as Silicon Valley, or in major cities like London or New York.
sentences.zh: 正如一家国际房地产公司的经济学家Jed Kolko所解释的，一个行业越是无需靠近它的供应商或客户，它就越有可能选址在就业岗位已经存在的地方，例如Silicon Valley，或者London和New York这样的大城市。

sentences.en: In Russia, says one knowledgeable observer of the IT scene, for a university kid studying in the regions, moving to Moscow sounds smart.
sentences.zh: 一位熟悉IT界情况的人士说，在Russia，对一个在外地省市上学的大学生来说，搬到Moscow听起来是明智之举。

sentences.en: E The area around Silicon Valley now has clusters inside clusters—that is, specific smaller geographic areas where similar IT companies are located.
sentences.zh: Silicon Valley周边地区现在有了集群中的集群，也就是说，在更小的一些特定地理区域内坐落着类似的IT公司。

sentences.en: Within the borders of the Valley, makers of semiconductors and network equipment are found mostly around the city of San Jose, while search engine and social network companies are located farther to the north.
sentences.zh: 在Valley范围之内，半导体和网络设备制造商大多分布在San Jose市周围，而搜索引擎和社交网络公司则位于更北的地方。

sentences.en: Even in San Francisco there are divisions with similar companies located in specific city districts.
sentences.zh: 就连在San Francisco市内也有类似的划分，同类公司集中在特定的城区。

sentences.en: F Young IT companies need more than a workforce; they also need access to money and expert advice.
sentences.zh: 年轻的IT公司需要的不只是劳动力；它们还需要有渠道获得资金和专业建议。

sentences.en: If a company is located in a cluster with other IT companies, staff can have more face-to-face communication with like-minded people from other companies, which is often more productive than phone calls or emails.
sentences.zh: 如果一家公司坐落在与其他IT公司共处的集群中，员工就能与其他公司里志同道合的人进行更多面对面的交流，这通常比打电话或发电子邮件更有效率。

sentences.en: Also, there is a better chance of making contact with someone with money and an interest in potentially profitable ideas.
sentences.zh: 此外，也更有机会接触到既有钱又对可能有盈利前景的点子感兴趣的人。

sentences.en: Even in industries which are built around virtual relationships, physical contact can be invaluable.
sentences.zh: 即使在围绕虚拟关系建立起来的行业中，面对面的接触也可能极为宝贵。

sentences.en: The recycling of people is important, too.
sentences.zh: 人员的循环流动也很重要。

sentences.en: As people move from company to company in Silicon Valley, and as one company buys or merges with another, a whole network of people who know each other develops, and these people are able to communicate easily with each other, and hire each other.
sentences.zh: 随着人们在Silicon Valley从一家公司流动到另一家公司，以及一家公司收购或兼并另一家公司，一张由彼此相识的人构成的大型网络逐渐形成，这些人能够轻松地相互交流，并且相互雇用。

sentences.en: G In places like Silicon Valley, people are also close to the latest ideas.
sentences.zh: 在Silicon Valley这样的地方，人们还能贴近最新的想法。

sentences.en: ‘New ideas become known in that tiny region perhaps years ahead of the rest of the world,’ argues one Valley entrepreneur.
sentences.zh: 一位Valley的创业者断言：“新想法在那个小小区域内为人所知的时间，也许比世界其他地方早好几年。”

sentences.en: ‘You are always building on the idea that came immediately before.
sentences.zh: “你总是在紧接着前一个想法的基础上进行构建。

sentences.en: If you are trying to build the thing that comes next, being aware of information about innovations that are already out there helps you.’
sentences.zh: 如果你想要构建接下来的那个东西，了解已经存在的种种创新的信息会对你有所帮助。”

sentences.en: This sounds very much like the point Marshall was trying to make.
sentences.zh: 这听起来与Marshall想要表达的观点非常相似。

sentences.en: H Will other IT hubs ever catch up with Silicon Valley?
sentences.zh: 其他IT中心究竟有没有可能赶上Silicon Valley？

sentences.en: Berlin and perhaps some other international cities like Beijing have several things going for them.
sentences.zh: Berlin以及Beijing等其他一些国际城市或许有几个方面的优势。

sentences.en: One is size: they are big and lively and act as magnets for young, creative people in search of opportunities.
sentences.zh: 其一是规模：它们又大又有活力，像磁铁一样吸引着寻求机会的年轻而有创造力的人。

sentences.en: The other advantage of these cities is that many other types of industries are located there, and hence they offer various skills on which IT companies can draw.

sentences.en: To many, this variety may prove invaluable.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，这种多样性也许会被证明是无价的。
